Hence $\left\lvert 2\vec{a} + k\left(\vec{b} + \vec{c}\right) \right\rvert \;=\; \left\lvert 2\vec{a} - k\vec{a} \right\rvert \;=\; \left\lvert 2 - k \right\rvert \;=\; 3$. So $k \;=\; 5$ or $k \;=\; -1$, and the positive value is $k \;=\; 5$.
questions.topic: Unit vectors with zero vector sum (expansion of squares)

questions.text: The set of all $\alpha$, for which the vectors $\vec{a}\;=\;\alpha t\hat{i}\;+\;6\hat{j}\;-\;3\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}\;=\;t\hat{i}\;-\;2\hat{j}\;-\;2\alpha t\hat{k}$ are inclined at an obtuse angle for all $t\;\in\;\mathbb{R}$, is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: An obtuse angle means $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}\;<\;0$, giving a quadratic in $t$ that must stay negative for every real $t$. // 📝 Solution: $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}\;=\;\alpha t^2\;-\;12\;+\;6\alpha t\;<\;0$ for all $t\;\in\;\mathbb{R}$, i.e. $\alpha t^2\;+\;6\alpha t\;-\;12\;<\;0$. If $\alpha\;=\;0$ this is $-12\;<\;0$, which holds. If $\alpha\;\ne\;0$ we need $\alpha\;<\;0$ and discriminant $D\;<\;0$: $36\alpha^2\;+\;48\alpha\;<\;0\;\implies\;12\alpha\left(3\alpha\;+\;4\right)\;<\;0\;\implies\;-\frac{4}{3}\;<\;\alpha\;<\;0$. Combining both cases, $\alpha\;\in\;\left(-\frac{4}{3},\;0\right]$.
questions.topic: Obtuse angle condition (dot product with quadratic in parameter)

questions.text: Let $\vec{a} \;=\; 2\hat{i} \;-\; \hat{j} \;-\; \hat{k}$, $\vec{b} \;=\; \hat{i} \;+\; 3\hat{j} \;-\; \hat{k}$ and $\vec{c} \;=\; 2\hat{i} \;+\; \hat{j} \;+\; 3\hat{k}$. Let $\vec{v}$ be a vector in the plane of $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ whose projection on $\vec{c}$ is of length $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{14}}$. Then $\left\lvert\vec{v}\right\rvert$ is equal to
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Write $\vec{v} \;=\; \lambda\vec{a} + \mu\vec{b}$ and note that $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} \;=\; 0$. // 📝 Solution: $\vec{v} \;=\; \lambda\vec{a} + \mu\vec{b} \;=\; \left(2\lambda + \mu\right)\hat{i} + \left(-\lambda + 3\mu\right)\hat{j} - \left(\lambda + \mu\right)\hat{k}$. $\vec{v} \cdot \vec{c} \;=\; 2\mu$ and $\left\lvert\vec{c}\right\rvert \;=\; \sqrt{14}$, so $\dfrac{\left\lvert 2\mu \right\rvert}{\sqrt{14}} \;=\; \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{14}} \;\implies\; \left\lvert\mu\right\rvert \;=\; \dfrac{1}{2}$. Since $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} \;=\; 2 - 3 + 1 \;=\; 0$, $\left\lvert\vec{v}\right\rvert^{2} \;=\; 6\lambda^{2} + 11\mu^{2}$. The answer key takes $\lambda^{2} \;=\; 1$ (the statement does not fix $\lambda$ on its own): $\left\lvert\vec{v}\right\rvert^{2} \;=\; 6 + \dfrac{11}{4} \;=\; \dfrac{35}{4}$, so $\left\lvert\vec{v}\right\rvert \;=\; \dfrac{\sqrt{35}}{2}$.
questions.topic: Vector in the plane of two vectors and projection

questions.text: Let $\vec{a}\;=\;\hat{i}\;-\;3\hat{j}\;+\;7\hat{k}$, $\vec{b}\;=\;2\hat{i}\;-\;\hat{j}\;+\;\hat{k}$ and $\vec{c}$ be a vector such that $\left(\vec{a}\;+\;2\vec{b}\right)\times\vec{c}\;=\;3\left(\vec{c}\times\vec{a}\right)$. If $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c}\;=\;130$, then $\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c}$ is equal to ____.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $\vec{c}\times\vec{a}\;=\;-\left(\vec{a}\times\vec{c}\right)$ to combine everything into one cross product with $\vec{c}$ equal to zero. // 📝 Solution: $\left(\vec{a}\;+\;2\vec{b}\right)\times\vec{c}\;+\;3\left(\vec{a}\times\vec{c}\right)\;=\;\vec{0}\;\implies\;\left(4\vec{a}\;+\;2\vec{b}\right)\times\vec{c}\;=\;\vec{0}$. So $\vec{c}\;=\;\lambda\left(4\vec{a}\;+\;2\vec{b}\right)\;=\;\lambda\left(8,\;-14,\;30\right)$. $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c}\;=\;\lambda\left(8\;+\;42\;+\;210\right)\;=\;260\lambda\;=\;130\;\implies\;\lambda\;=\;\frac{1}{2}$. Hence $\vec{c}\;=\;\left(4,\;-7,\;15\right)$ and $\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c}\;=\;8\;+\;7\;+\;15\;=\;30$.
questions.topic: Vector equation with cross product (parallel vectors)

questions.text: Consider three vectors $\vec{a},\;\vec{b},\;\vec{c}$. Let $\left\lvert\vec{a}\right\rvert\;=\;2$, $\left\lvert\vec{b}\right\rvert\;=\;3$ and $\vec{a}\;=\;\vec{b}\times\vec{c}$. If $\alpha\;\in\;\left[0,\;\frac{\pi}{3}\right]$ is the angle between the vectors $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$, then the minimum value of $27\left\lvert\vec{c}\;-\;\vec{a}\right\rvert^2$ is equal to:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\vec{a}\;=\;\vec{b}\times\vec{c}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{c}$, so $\left\lvert\vec{c}-\vec{a}\right\rvert^2\;=\;\left\lvert\vec{c}\right\rvert^2\;+\;\left\lvert\vec{a}\right\rvert^2$. // 📝 Solution: $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c}\;=\;0$, so $\left\lvert\vec{c}\;-\;\vec{a}\right\rvert^2\;=\;\left\lvert\vec{c}\right\rvert^2\;+\;4$. From $\left\lvert\vec{a}\right\rvert\;=\;\left\lvert\vec{b}\right\rvert\left\lvert\vec{c}\right\rvert\sin\alpha$: $2\;=\;3\left\lvert\vec{c}\right\rvert\sin\alpha\;\implies\;\left\lvert\vec{c}\right\rvert\;=\;\frac{2}{3}\csc\alpha$. For $\alpha\;\in\;\left(0,\;\frac{\pi}{3}\right]$ (note $\alpha\;\ne\;0$ since $\vec{a}\;\ne\;\vec{0}$), $\csc\alpha\;\ge\;\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$, so $\left\lvert\vec{c}\right\rvert_{\min}\;=\;\frac{2}{3}\cdot\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}$ and $\left\lvert\vec{c}\right\rvert_{\min}^2\;=\;\frac{16}{27}$. Therefore $27\left\lvert\vec{c}\;-\;\vec{a}\right\rvert^2_{\min}\;=\;27\left(\frac{16}{27}\;+\;4\right)\;=\;16\;+\;108\;=\;124$.
questions.topic: Magnitude of cross product with minimisation

questions.text: Let $\vec{a} \;=\; \sqrt{2}\hat{i} \;-\; \hat{j} \;+\; \lambda\hat{k}$, $\lambda > 0$, make an obtuse angle with the vector $\vec{b} \;=\; -\lambda^{2}\hat{i} \;+\; 4\sqrt{2}\hat{j} \;+\; 4\sqrt{2}\hat{k}$ and an angle $\theta$, $\dfrac{\pi}{6} < \theta < \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, with the positive z-axis. If the set of all possible values of $\lambda$ is $\left(\alpha, \beta\right) - \left\{\gamma\right\}$, then $\alpha + \beta + \gamma$ is equal to
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Obtuse angle means $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} < 0$; the angle with the z-axis gives bounds on $\cos\theta \;=\; \dfrac{\lambda}{\left\lvert\vec{a}\right\rvert}$. // 📝 Solution: $\cos\theta \;=\; \dfrac{\lambda}{\sqrt{3 + \lambda^{2}}}$ and $\dfrac{\pi}{6} < \theta < \dfrac{\pi}{2} \;\implies\; 0 < \cos\theta < \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$. This gives $\lambda > 0$ and $4\lambda^{2} < 9 + 3\lambda^{2} \;\implies\; \lambda < 3$, so $\lambda \in \left(0, 3\right)$. $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} \;=\; -\sqrt{2}\lambda^{2} - 4\sqrt{2} + 4\sqrt{2}\lambda \;<\; 0 \;\implies\; \lambda^{2} - 4\lambda + 4 > 0 \;\implies\; \left(\lambda - 2\right)^{2} > 0 \;\implies\; \lambda \neq 2$. The set is $\left(0, 3\right) - \left\{2\right\}$, so $\alpha = 0$, $\beta = 3$, $\gamma = 2$ and $\alpha + \beta + \gamma \;=\; 5$.
questions.topic: Obtuse angle condition and direction cosine with an axis

questions.text: Let $\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}$ be vectors such that $\vec{a} \times \vec{b} \;=\; 2\left(\vec{a} \times \vec{c}\right)$, $\left\lvert\vec{a}\right\rvert \;=\; 1$, $\left\lvert\vec{b}\right\rvert \;=\; 4$ and $\left\lvert\vec{c}\right\rvert \;=\; 2$. If the angle between $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ is $60^{\circ}$, then $\left\lvert\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c}\right\rvert$ is equal to
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Rewrite as $\vec{a} \times \left(\vec{b} - 2\vec{c}\right) \;=\; \vec{0}$, so $\vec{b} - 2\vec{c} \;=\; k\vec{a}$, then take magnitudes and dot products. // 📝 Solution: $\vec{b} - 2\vec{c} \;=\; k\vec{a}$. $\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c} \;=\; 4 \cdot 2 \cdot \cos 60^{\circ} \;=\; 4$. Taking the square of the magnitude: $\left\lvert\vec{b}\right\rvert^{2} - 4\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c} + 4\left\lvert\vec{c}\right\rvert^{2} \;=\; 16 - 16 + 16 \;=\; 16 \;=\; k^{2}\left\lvert\vec{a}\right\rvert^{2} \;=\; k^{2}$, so $k \;=\; \pm 4$. Dot with $\vec{c}$: $\vec{b} \cdot \vec{c} - 2\left\lvert\vec{c}\right\rvert^{2} \;=\; 4 - 8 \;=\; -4 \;=\; k\left(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c}\right)$. So $\left\lvert\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c}\right\rvert \;=\; \dfrac{4}{\left\lvert k\right\rvert} \;=\; 1$.
questions.topic: Cross product equation (parallel vectors) and dot product

questions.text: Let $\vec{a}\;=\;\hat{i}\;+\;2\hat{j}\;+\;3\hat{k}$, $\vec{b}\;=\;2\hat{i}\;+\;3\hat{j}\;-\;5\hat{k}$ and $\vec{c}\;=\;3\hat{i}\;-\;\hat{j}\;+\;\lambda\hat{k}$ be three vectors. Let $\vec{r}$ be a unit vector along $\vec{b}\;+\;\vec{c}$. If $\vec{r}\cdot\vec{a}\;=\;3$, then $3\lambda$ is equal to:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Write $\vec{r}\;=\;k\left(\vec{b}+\vec{c}\right)$ and use both $\vec{r}\cdot\vec{a}\;=\;3$ and $\left\lvert\vec{r}\right\rvert\;=\;1$ to eliminate $k$. // 📝 Solution: $\vec{b}\;+\;\vec{c}\;=\;\left(5,\;2,\;\lambda\;-\;5\right)$ and $\vec{r}\;=\;k\left(\vec{b}\;+\;\vec{c}\right)$. $\vec{r}\cdot\vec{a}\;=\;k\left(5\;+\;4\;+\;3\lambda\;-\;15\right)\;=\;k\left(3\lambda\;-\;6\right)\;=\;3\;\implies\;k\;=\;\frac{1}{\lambda\;-\;2}$. $\left\lvert\vec{r}\right\rvert\;=\;1\;\implies\;k^2\left(25\;+\;4\;+\;\left(\lambda\;-\;5\right)^2\right)\;=\;1\;\implies\;\left(\lambda\;-\;2\right)^2\;=\;29\;+\;\left(\lambda\;-\;5\right)^2$. So $\lambda^2\;-\;4\lambda\;+\;4\;=\;\lambda^2\;-\;10\lambda\;+\;54\;\implies\;6\lambda\;=\;50\;\implies\;3\lambda\;=\;25$.
questions.topic: Unit vector along a given direction with dot product condition

questions.text: Between the following two statements: Statement I : Let $\vec{a}\;=\;\hat{i}\;+\;2\hat{j}\;-\;3\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}\;=\;2\hat{i}\;+\;\hat{j}\;-\;\hat{k}$. Then the vector $\vec{r}$ satisfying $\vec{a}\times\vec{r}\;=\;\vec{a}\times\vec{b}$ and $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{r}\;=\;0$ is of magnitude $\sqrt{10}$. Statement II : In a triangle $ABC$, $\cos2A\;+\;\cos2B\;+\;\cos2C\;\ge\;-\frac{3}{2}$.

options.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For I, $\vec{a}\times\left(\vec{r}-\vec{b}\right)\;=\;\vec{0}$; for II, use $A+B+C\;=\;\pi$ and $\cos A\cos B\cos C\;\le\;\frac{1}{8}$. // 📝 Solution: Statement I: $\vec{a}\times\left(\vec{r}\;-\;\vec{b}\right)\;=\;\vec{0}\;\implies\;\vec{r}\;-\;\vec{b}\;=\;\mu\vec{a}$. Dot with $\vec{a}$: $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{r}\;-\;\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}\;=\;\mu\left\lvert\vec{a}\right\rvert^2\;\implies\;0\;-\;7\;=\;14\mu\;\implies\;\mu\;=\;-\frac{1}{2}$. So $\vec{r}\;=\;\vec{b}\;-\;\frac{\vec{a}}{2}\;=\;\frac{3\hat{i}\;+\;\hat{k}}{2}$ and $\left\lvert\vec{r}\right\rvert\;=\;\frac{\sqrt{10}}{2}\;\ne\;\sqrt{10}$, so Statement I is incorrect. Statement II: since $2A\;+\;2B\;+\;2C\;=\;2\pi$, $\cos2A\;+\;\cos2B\;+\;\cos2C\;=\;-1\;-\;4\cos A\cos B\cos C\;\ge\;-1\;-\;4\cdot\frac{1}{8}\;=\;-\frac{3}{2}$, so Statement II is correct.
questions.topic: Vector equation with cross product; trigonometric inequality in a triangle

questions.text: Let $\vec{a} \;=\; 2\hat{i} \;-\; 5\hat{j} \;+\; 5\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b} \;=\; \hat{i} \;-\; \hat{j} \;+\; 3\hat{k}$. Let $\vec{c}$ be a vector such that $2\left(\vec{a} \times \vec{c}\right) \;+\; 3\left(\vec{b} \times \vec{c}\right) \;=\; \vec{0}$ and $\left(\vec{a} \;-\; \vec{b}\right) \cdot \vec{c} \;=\; -97$. Then $\left\lvert\vec{c} \times \hat{k}\right\rvert^{2}$ is equal to
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Combine the two cross products into $\left(2\vec{a} + 3\vec{b}\right) \times \vec{c} \;=\; \vec{0}$, so $\vec{c}$ is parallel to $2\vec{a} + 3\vec{b}$. // 📝 Solution: $2\vec{a} + 3\vec{b} \;=\; 7\hat{i} - 13\hat{j} + 19\hat{k}$, so $\vec{c} \;=\; t\left(7\hat{i} - 13\hat{j} + 19\hat{k}\right)$. $\vec{a} - \vec{b} \;=\; \hat{i} - 4\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$, so $\left(\vec{a} - \vec{b}\right) \cdot \vec{c} \;=\; t\left(7 + 52 + 38\right) \;=\; 97t \;=\; -97 \;\implies\; t \;=\; -1$. Then $\vec{c} \;=\; -7\hat{i} + 13\hat{j} - 19\hat{k}$. $\vec{c} \times \hat{k} \;=\; 13\hat{i} + 7\hat{j}$, so $\left\lvert\vec{c} \times \hat{k}\right\rvert^{2} \;=\; 169 + 49 \;=\; 218$.
questions.topic: Vector equation with cross product (parallel vectors)

questions.text: Let $\vec{a}\;=\;2\hat{i}\;+\;\alpha\hat{j}\;+\;\hat{k}$, $\vec{b}\;=\;-\hat{i}\;+\;\hat{k}$, $\vec{c}\;=\;\beta\hat{j}\;-\;\hat{k}$, where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are integers and $\alpha\beta\;=\;-6$. Let the values of the ordered pair $\left(\alpha,\;\beta\right)$, for which the area of the parallelogram of diagonals $\vec{a}\;+\;\vec{b}$ and $\vec{b}\;+\;\vec{c}$ is $\frac{\sqrt{21}}{2}$, be $\left(\alpha_1,\;\beta_1\right)$ and $\left(\alpha_2,\;\beta_2\right)$. Then $\alpha_1^2\;+\;\beta_1^2\;-\;\alpha_2\beta_2$ is equal to
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Area of a parallelogram with diagonals $\vec{d}_1$ and $\vec{d}_2$ is $\frac{1}{2}\left\lvert\vec{d}_1\times\vec{d}_2\right\rvert$. // 📝 Solution: $\vec{a}\;+\;\vec{b}\;=\;\left(1,\;\alpha,\;2\right)$ and $\vec{b}\;+\;\vec{c}\;=\;\left(-1,\;\beta,\;0\right)$. Their cross product is $\left(-2\beta,\;-2,\;\alpha\;+\;\beta\right)$. Area $\;=\;\frac{\sqrt{21}}{2}\;\implies\;4\beta^2\;+\;4\;+\;\left(\alpha\;+\;\beta\right)^2\;=\;21\;\implies\;\alpha^2\;+\;5\beta^2\;+\;2\alpha\beta\;=\;17$. With $\alpha\beta\;=\;-6$: $\alpha^2\;+\;5\beta^2\;=\;29$. The integer solutions are $\left(\alpha,\;\beta\right)\;=\;\left(-3,\;2\right)$ and $\left(3,\;-2\right)$. Whichever is labelled first, $\alpha_1^2\;+\;\beta_1^2\;=\;13$ and $\alpha_2\beta_2\;=\;-6$, so the value is $13\;+\;6\;=\;19$.
questions.topic: Area of a parallelogram using its diagonals

questions.text: Let $\vec{a}\;=\;2\hat{i}\;+\;5\hat{j}\;-\;\hat{k}$, $\vec{b}\;=\;2\hat{i}\;-\;2\hat{j}\;+\;2\hat{k}$ and $\vec{c}$ be three vectors such that $\left(\vec{c}\;+\;\hat{i}\right)\times\left(\vec{a}\;+\;\vec{b}\;+\;\hat{i}\right)\;=\;\vec{a}\times\left(\vec{c}\;+\;\hat{i}\right)$. If $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c}\;=\;-29$, then $\vec{c}\cdot\left(-2\hat{i}\;+\;\hat{j}\;+\;\hat{k}\right)$ is equal to:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Put $\vec{p}\;=\;\vec{c}+\hat{i}$ and reduce the equation to $\vec{p}\times\vec{w}\;=\;\vec{0}$ so that $\vec{p}$ is parallel to $\vec{w}$. // 📝 Solution: Let $\vec{p}\;=\;\vec{c}\;+\;\hat{i}$ and $\vec{v}\;=\;\vec{a}\;+\;\vec{b}\;+\;\hat{i}\;=\;\left(5,\;3,\;1\right)$. The condition $\vec{p}\times\vec{v}\;=\;\vec{a}\times\vec{p}$ gives $\vec{p}\times\vec{v}\;+\;\vec{p}\times\vec{a}\;=\;\vec{0}\;\implies\;\vec{p}\times\left(\vec{v}\;+\;\vec{a}\right)\;=\;\vec{0}$. Since $\vec{v}\;+\;\vec{a}\;=\;\left(7,\;8,\;0\right)$, $\vec{c}\;+\;\hat{i}\;=\;\lambda\left(7\hat{i}\;+\;8\hat{j}\right)$. Dot with $\vec{a}$: $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c}\;+\;\vec{a}\cdot\hat{i}\;=\;\lambda\left(14\;+\;40\right)\;\implies\;-29\;+\;2\;=\;54\lambda\;\implies\;\lambda\;=\;-\frac{1}{2}$. Dot with $\vec{w}\;=\;-2\hat{i}\;+\;\hat{j}\;+\;\hat{k}$: $\vec{c}\cdot\vec{w}\;+\;\hat{i}\cdot\vec{w}\;=\;\lambda\left(-14\;+\;8\right)\;=\;3$. Since $\hat{i}\cdot\vec{w}\;=\;-2$, $\vec{c}\cdot\vec{w}\;=\;3\;+\;2\;=\;5$.

questions.text: Let $\vec{a}\;=\;\hat{i}\;+\;\hat{j}\;+\;\hat{k}$, $\vec{b}\;=\;2\hat{i}\;+\;4\hat{j}\;-\;5\hat{k}$ and $\vec{c}\;=\;x\hat{i}\;+\;2\hat{j}\;+\;3\hat{k}$, $x\;\in\;\mathbb{R}$. If $\vec{d}$ is the unit vector in the direction of $\vec{b}\;+\;\vec{c}$ such that $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{d}\;=\;1$, then $\left(\vec{a}\times\vec{b}\right)\cdot\vec{c}$ is equal to
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\vec{d}\;=\;\frac{\vec{b}+\vec{c}}{\left\lvert\vec{b}+\vec{c}\right\rvert}$, so $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{d}\;=\;1$ fixes $x$; then expand the scalar triple product. // 📝 Solution: $\vec{b}\;+\;\vec{c}\;=\;\left(x\;+\;2,\;6,\;-2\right)$. $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{d}\;=\;1\;\implies\;\left(x\;+\;2\right)\;+\;6\;-\;2\;=\;\left\lvert\vec{b}\;+\;\vec{c}\right\rvert\;\implies\;x\;+\;6\;=\;\left\lvert\vec{b}\;+\;\vec{c}\right\rvert$. Squaring: $\left(x\;+\;6\right)^2\;=\;\left(x\;+\;2\right)^2\;+\;36\;+\;4\;\implies\;8x\;=\;8\;\implies\;x\;=\;1$. Now $\left(\vec{a}\times\vec{b}\right)\cdot\vec{c}\;=\;1\left(12\;+\;10\right)\;-\;1\left(6\;+\;5x\right)\;+\;1\left(4\;-\;4x\right)\;=\;20\;-\;9x\;=\;20\;-\;9\;=\;11$.
questions.topic: Scalar triple product with unit vector condition

questions.text: Let $\vec{a} \;=\; 2\hat{i} \;+\; \hat{j} \;-\; 2\hat{k}$, $\vec{b} \;=\; \hat{i} \;+\; \hat{j}$ and $\vec{c} \;=\; \vec{a} \times \vec{b}$. If $\vec{d}$ is a vector such that $\left\lvert\vec{d} - \vec{a}\right\rvert \;=\; \sqrt{11}$, $\left\lvert\vec{c} \times \vec{d}\right\rvert \;=\; 3$ and the angle between $\vec{c}$ and $\vec{d}$ is $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$, then $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{d}$ is equal to
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $\left\lvert\vec{c} \times \vec{d}\right\rvert \;=\; \left\lvert\vec{c}\right\rvert\left\lvert\vec{d}\right\rvert\sin\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ to find $\left\lvert\vec{d}\right\rvert$, then expand $\left\lvert\vec{d} - \vec{a}\right\rvert^{2}$. // 📝 Solution: $\vec{c} \;=\; \vec{a} \times \vec{b} \;=\; 2\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}$, so $\left\lvert\vec{c}\right\rvert \;=\; 3$, and $\left\lvert\vec{a}\right\rvert \;=\; 3$. $\left\lvert\vec{c} \times \vec{d}\right\rvert \;=\; 3\left\lvert\vec{d}\right\rvert \cdot \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \;=\; 3 \;\implies\; \left\lvert\vec{d}\right\rvert \;=\; \sqrt{2}$. $\left\lvert\vec{d} - \vec{a}\right\rvert^{2} \;=\; \left\lvert\vec{d}\right\rvert^{2} - 2\vec{a} \cdot \vec{d} + \left\lvert\vec{a}\right\rvert^{2} \;=\; 2 - 2\vec{a} \cdot \vec{d} + 9 \;=\; 11$. So $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{d} \;=\; 0$.
questions.topic: Cross product magnitude and dot product

questions.text: Let a unit vector which makes an angle of $60^\circ$ with $2\hat{i}\;+\;2\hat{j}\;-\;\hat{k}$ and an angle $45^\circ$ with $\hat{i}\;-\;\hat{k}$ be $\vec{C}$. Then $\vec{C}\;+\;\left(-\frac{1}{2}\hat{i}\;+\;\frac{1}{3\sqrt{2}}\hat{j}\;-\;\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}\hat{k}\right)$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $\vec{C}\cdot\vec{u}\;=\;\left\lvert\vec{u}\right\rvert\cos\theta$ for each given vector together with $\left\lvert\vec{C}\right\rvert\;=\;1$. // 📝 Solution: Let $\vec{C}\;=\;C_1\hat{i}\;+\;C_2\hat{j}\;+\;C_3\hat{k}$ with $C_1^2\;+\;C_2^2\;+\;C_3^2\;=\;1$. Since $\left\lvert2\hat{i}\;+\;2\hat{j}\;-\;\hat{k}\right\rvert\;=\;3$, we get $2C_1\;+\;2C_2\;-\;C_3\;=\;3\cos60^\circ\;=\;\frac{3}{2}$. Since $\left\lvert\hat{i}\;-\;\hat{k}\right\rvert\;=\;\sqrt{2}$, we get $C_1\;-\;C_3\;=\;\sqrt{2}\cos45^\circ\;=\;1$. Subtracting, $C_1\;+\;2C_2\;=\;\frac{1}{2}$. Put $C_3\;=\;C_1\;-\;1$ and $C_2\;=\;\frac{1}{4}\;-\;\frac{C_1}{2}$ in the unit condition: $36C_1^2\;-\;36C_1\;+\;1\;=\;0\;\implies\;C_1\;=\;\frac{1}{2}\;\pm\;\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}$. Take $C_1\;=\;\frac{1}{2}\;+\;\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}$ (the other root gives a vector that matches none of the options). Then $C_2\;=\;-\frac{1}{3\sqrt{2}}$ and $C_3\;=\;\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}\;-\;\frac{1}{2}$. Hence $\vec{C}\;+\;\left(-\frac{1}{2}\hat{i}\;+\;\frac{1}{3\sqrt{2}}\hat{j}\;-\;\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}\hat{k}\right)\;=\;\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}\hat{i}\;-\;\frac{1}{2}\hat{k}$.
questions.topic: Unit vector with given angles (dot product)

questions.text: Let three vectors $\vec{a}\;=\;\alpha\hat{i}\;+\;4\hat{j}\;+\;2\hat{k}$, $\vec{b}\;=\;5\hat{i}\;+\;3\hat{j}\;+\;4\hat{k}$, $\vec{c}\;=\;x\hat{i}\;+\;y\hat{j}\;+\;z\hat{k}$ form a triangle such that $\vec{c}\;=\;\vec{a}\;-\;\vec{b}$ and the area of the triangle is $5\sqrt{6}$. If $\alpha$ is a positive real number, then $\left\lvert\vec{c}\right\rvert^2$ is equal to:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Area of the triangle $\;=\;\frac{1}{2}\left\lvert\vec{a}\times\vec{c}\right\rvert$ since $\vec{a}\;=\;\vec{b}+\vec{c}$. // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] Triangle with sides $\vec{a}$, $\vec{b}$, $\vec{c}$ where $\vec{c}\;=\;\vec{a}\;-\;\vec{b}$. $\vec{c}\;=\;\left(\alpha\;-\;5,\;1,\;-2\right)$. $\vec{a}\times\vec{c}\;=\;\left(-10,\;4\alpha\;-\;10,\;20\;-\;3\alpha\right)$. Area $\;=\;5\sqrt{6}\;\implies\;\left\lvert\vec{a}\times\vec{c}\right\rvert^2\;=\;600$, so $100\;+\;\left(4\alpha\;-\;10\right)^2\;+\;\left(20\;-\;3\alpha\right)^2\;=\;600\;\implies\;25\alpha^2\;-\;200\alpha\;=\;0\;\implies\;\alpha\;=\;8$ (as $\alpha\;>\;0$). Then $\vec{c}\;=\;\left(3,\;1,\;-2\right)$ and $\left\lvert\vec{c}\right\rvert^2\;=\;9\;+\;1\;+\;4\;=\;14$.
questions.topic: Area of a triangle using cross product

questions.text: Let $\vec{a} \;=\; -\hat{i} \;+\; 2\hat{j} \;+\; 2\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b} \;=\; 8\hat{i} \;+\; 7\hat{j} \;-\; 3\hat{k}$. Let $\vec{c}$ be a vector such that $\vec{a} \times \vec{c} \;=\; \vec{b}$ and $\vec{c} \cdot \left(\hat{i} \;+\; \hat{j} \;+\; \hat{k}\right) \;=\; 4$. Then $\left\lvert\vec{a} \;+\; \vec{c}\right\rvert^{2}$ is equal to
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Put $\vec{c} \;=\; x\hat{i} + y\hat{j} + z\hat{k}$, expand $\vec{a} \times \vec{c}$ and match components with $\vec{b}$. // 📝 Solution: $\vec{a} \times \vec{c} \;=\; \left(2z - 2y\right)\hat{i} + \left(2x + z\right)\hat{j} + \left(-y - 2x\right)\hat{k} \;=\; 8\hat{i} + 7\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}$. So $z - y \;=\; 4$, $2x + z \;=\; 7$ and $2x + y \;=\; 3$. With $x + y + z \;=\; 4$: $z \;=\; 7 - 2x$ and $y \;=\; 3 - 2x$, so $x + 3 - 2x + 7 - 2x \;=\; 4 \;\implies\; x \;=\; 2$, $y \;=\; -1$, $z \;=\; 3$. $\vec{a} + \vec{c} \;=\; \hat{i} + \hat{j} + 5\hat{k}$, so $\left\lvert\vec{a} + \vec{c}\right\rvert^{2} \;=\; 1 + 1 + 25 \;=\; 27$.
questions.topic: Vector equation with cross product and dot product

questions.text: Let $\overrightarrow{OA}\;=\;2\vec{a}$, $\overrightarrow{OB}\;=\;6\vec{a}\;+\;5\vec{b}$ and $\overrightarrow{OC}\;=\;3\vec{b}$, where $O$ is the origin. If the area of the parallelogram with adjacent sides $\overrightarrow{OA}$ and $\overrightarrow{OC}$ is $15$ sq. units, then the area (in sq. units) of the quadrilateral $OABC$ is equal to :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Area of quadrilateral $OABC\;=\;\frac{1}{2}\left\lvert\overrightarrow{AC}\times\overrightarrow{OB}\right\rvert$ (half the cross product of the diagonals). // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] Quadrilateral $OABC$ with diagonals $OB$ and $AC$. Parallelogram area: $\left\lvert2\vec{a}\times3\vec{b}\right\rvert\;=\;6\left\lvert\vec{a}\times\vec{b}\right\rvert\;=\;15\;\implies\;\left\lvert\vec{a}\times\vec{b}\right\rvert\;=\;\frac{5}{2}$. Now $\overrightarrow{AC}\;=\;3\vec{b}\;-\;2\vec{a}$ and $\overrightarrow{OB}\;=\;6\vec{a}\;+\;5\vec{b}$, so $\overrightarrow{AC}\times\overrightarrow{OB}\;=\;18\left(\vec{b}\times\vec{a}\right)\;-\;10\left(\vec{a}\times\vec{b}\right)\;=\;-28\left(\vec{a}\times\vec{b}\right)$. Area $\;=\;\frac{1}{2}\cdot28\left\lvert\vec{a}\times\vec{b}\right\rvert\;=\;14\cdot\frac{5}{2}\;=\;35$.
questions.topic: Area of a quadrilateral using cross product of diagonals

questions.text: Let $\vec{a}\;=\;2\hat{i}\;-\;3\hat{j}\;+\;4\hat{k}$, $\vec{b}\;=\;3\hat{i}\;+\;4\hat{j}\;-\;5\hat{k}$ and a vector $\vec{c}$ be such that $\vec{a}\times\left(\vec{b}\;+\;\vec{c}\right)\;+\;\vec{b}\times\vec{c}\;=\;\hat{i}\;+\;8\hat{j}\;+\;13\hat{k}$. If $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c}\;=\;13$, then $\left(24\;-\;\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c}\right)$ is equal to ____.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Cross the equation with $\vec{a}$, expand using $\vec{a}\times\left(\vec{u}\times\vec{v}\right)\;=\;\left(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{v}\right)\vec{u}-\left(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{u}\right)\vec{v}$, then dot with $\vec{b}$. // 📝 Solution: Let $\vec{s}\;=\;\hat{i}\;+\;8\hat{j}\;+\;13\hat{k}$. The condition is $\vec{a}\times\vec{b}\;+\;\vec{a}\times\vec{c}\;+\;\vec{b}\times\vec{c}\;=\;\vec{s}$. Cross with $\vec{a}$ from the left: $\vec{a}\times\left(\vec{a}\times\vec{b}\right)\;+\;\vec{a}\times\left(\vec{a}\times\vec{c}\right)\;+\;\vec{a}\times\left(\vec{b}\times\vec{c}\right)\;=\;\vec{a}\times\vec{s}$. With $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}\;=\;-26$, $\left\lvert\vec{a}\right\rvert^2\;=\;29$, $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c}\;=\;13$: $\left(-26\vec{a}\;-\;29\vec{b}\right)\;+\;\left(13\vec{a}\;-\;29\vec{c}\right)\;+\;\left(13\vec{b}\;+\;26\vec{c}\right)\;=\;-13\vec{a}\;-\;16\vec{b}\;-\;3\vec{c}\;=\;\vec{a}\times\vec{s}$. Dot with $\vec{b}$: $-13\left(-26\right)\;-\;16\left(50\right)\;-\;3\,\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c}\;=\;\left[\vec{a}\;\vec{s}\;\vec{b}\right]$. The triple product is $2\left(-92\right)\;+\;3\left(-44\right)\;+\;4\left(-20\right)\;=\;-396$. So $338\;-\;800\;-\;3\,\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c}\;=\;-396\;\implies\;\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c}\;=\;-22$. Hence $24\;-\;\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c}\;=\;24\;+\;22\;=\;46$.

questions.text: Let $\vec{a}\;=\;9\hat{i}\;-\;13\hat{j}\;+\;25\hat{k}$, $\vec{b}\;=\;3\hat{i}\;+\;7\hat{j}\;-\;13\hat{k}$ and $\vec{c}\;=\;17\hat{i}\;-\;2\hat{j}\;+\;\hat{k}$ be three given vectors. If $\vec{r}$ is a vector such that $\vec{r}\times\vec{a}\;=\;\left(\vec{b}\;+\;\vec{c}\right)\times\vec{a}$ and $\vec{r}\cdot\left(\vec{b}\;-\;\vec{c}\right)\;=\;0$, then $\frac{\left\lvert593\vec{r}\;+\;67\vec{a}\right\rvert^2}{\left(593\right)^2}$ is equal to ____.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\left(\vec{r}-\vec{b}-\vec{c}\right)\times\vec{a}\;=\;\vec{0}$ means $\vec{r}\;=\;\vec{b}+\vec{c}+\lambda\vec{a}$; then apply $\vec{r}\cdot\left(\vec{b}-\vec{c}\right)\;=\;0$. // 📝 Solution: $\vec{r}\;=\;\vec{b}\;+\;\vec{c}\;+\;\lambda\vec{a}$. From $\vec{r}\cdot\left(\vec{b}\;-\;\vec{c}\right)\;=\;0$: $\left\lvert\vec{b}\right\rvert^2\;-\;\left\lvert\vec{c}\right\rvert^2\;+\;\lambda\left(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}\;-\;\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c}\right)\;=\;0$. Here $\left\lvert\vec{b}\right\rvert^2\;=\;227$, $\left\lvert\vec{c}\right\rvert^2\;=\;294$, $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}\;=\;-389$, $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c}\;=\;204$, so $-67\;-\;593\lambda\;=\;0\;\implies\;\lambda\;=\;-\frac{67}{593}$. Then $593\vec{r}\;+\;67\vec{a}\;=\;593\left(\vec{b}\;+\;\vec{c}\right)$, and the required ratio is $\left\lvert\vec{b}\;+\;\vec{c}\right\rvert^2\;=\;\left\lvert\left(20,\;5,\;-12\right)\right\rvert^2\;=\;400\;+\;25\;+\;144\;=\;569$.
questions.topic: Vector equation with cross product and dot product

questions.text: Let $\overrightarrow{AB} \;=\; 2\hat{i} \;+\; 4\hat{j} \;-\; 5\hat{k}$ and $\overrightarrow{AD} \;=\; \hat{i} \;+\; 2\hat{j} \;+\; \lambda\hat{k}$, $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$, be adjacent sides of a parallelogram ABCD. If the projection of $\vec{v} \;=\; \hat{i} \;+\; \hat{j} \;+\; \hat{k}$ on the diagonal $\overrightarrow{AC}$ is of length 1 and $\alpha > \beta$ are the roots of $\lambda^{2}x^{2} \;-\; 6\lambda x \;+\; 5 \;=\; 0$, then $2\alpha \;-\; \beta$ is equal to
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\overrightarrow{AC} \;=\; \overrightarrow{AB} + \overrightarrow{AD}$; set $\dfrac{\left\lvert\vec{v} \cdot \overrightarrow{AC}\right\rvert}{\left\lvert\overrightarrow{AC}\right\rvert} \;=\; 1$ to find $\lambda$. // 📝 Solution: $\overrightarrow{AC} \;=\; 3\hat{i} + 6\hat{j} + \left(\lambda - 5\right)\hat{k}$. $\vec{v} \cdot \overrightarrow{AC} \;=\; \lambda + 4$ and $\left\lvert\overrightarrow{AC}\right\rvert \;=\; \sqrt{45 + \left(\lambda - 5\right)^{2}}$. Projection $= 1 \;\implies\; \left(\lambda + 4\right)^{2} \;=\; 45 + \left(\lambda - 5\right)^{2} \;\implies\; 18\lambda \;=\; 54 \;\implies\; \lambda \;=\; 3$. The equation becomes $9x^{2} - 18x + 5 \;=\; 0$, with roots $x \;=\; \dfrac{5}{3}$ and $\dfrac{1}{3}$. So $\alpha \;=\; \dfrac{5}{3}$, $\beta \;=\; \dfrac{1}{3}$ and $2\alpha - \beta \;=\; \dfrac{10}{3} - \dfrac{1}{3} \;=\; 3$.
questions.topic: Parallelogram diagonal and projection of a vector

questions.text: For $\lambda\;>\;0$, let $\theta$ be the angle between the vectors $\vec{a}\;=\;\hat{i}\;+\;\lambda\hat{j}\;-\;3\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}\;=\;3\hat{i}\;-\;\hat{j}\;+\;2\hat{k}$. If the vectors $\vec{a}\;+\;\vec{b}$ and $\vec{a}\;-\;\vec{b}$ are mutually perpendicular, then the value of $\left(14\cos\theta\right)^2$ is equal to
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\left(\vec{a}+\vec{b}\right)\cdot\left(\vec{a}-\vec{b}\right)\;=\;\left\lvert\vec{a}\right\rvert^2\;-\;\left\lvert\vec{b}\right\rvert^2$. // 📝 Solution: Perpendicular vectors give $\left\lvert\vec{a}\right\rvert^2\;=\;\left\lvert\vec{b}\right\rvert^2\;\implies\;1\;+\;\lambda^2\;+\;9\;=\;9\;+\;1\;+\;4\;\implies\;\lambda^2\;=\;4\;\implies\;\lambda\;=\;2$ (as $\lambda\;>\;0$). Then $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}\;=\;3\;-\;\lambda\;-\;6\;=\;-5$ and $\left\lvert\vec{a}\right\rvert\left\lvert\vec{b}\right\rvert\;=\;\sqrt{14}\cdot\sqrt{14}\;=\;14$. So $14\cos\theta\;=\;\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}\;=\;-5$ and $\left(14\cos\theta\right)^2\;=\;25$.

questions.text: Let $\vec{a} \;=\; -\hat{i} \;+\; \hat{j} \;+\; 2\hat{k}$, $\vec{b} \;=\; \hat{i} \;-\; \hat{j} \;-\; 3\hat{k}$, $\vec{c} \;=\; \vec{a} \times \vec{b}$ and $\vec{d} \;=\; \vec{c} \times \vec{a}$. Then $\left(\vec{a} \;-\; \vec{b}\right) \cdot \vec{d}$ is equal to
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Compute $\vec{c}$, then $\vec{d}$, then take the dot product with $\vec{a} - \vec{b}$. // 📝 Solution: $\vec{c} \;=\; \vec{a} \times \vec{b} \;=\; \left(-3 + 2\right)\hat{i} - \left(3 - 2\right)\hat{j} + \left(1 - 1\right)\hat{k} \;=\; -\hat{i} - \hat{j}$. $\vec{d} \;=\; \vec{c} \times \vec{a} \;=\; \left(-2\right)\hat{i} - \left(-2\right)\hat{j} + \left(-1 - 1\right)\hat{k} \;=\; -2\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 2\hat{k}$. $\vec{a} - \vec{b} \;=\; -2\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 5\hat{k}$. $\left(\vec{a} - \vec{b}\right) \cdot \vec{d} \;=\; 4 + 4 - 10 \;=\; -2$.
questions.topic: Cross product and dot product of explicit vectors

questions.text: Let P be a point in the plane of $\overrightarrow{AB} \;=\; 3\hat{i} \;+\; \hat{j} \;-\; \hat{k}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC} \;=\; \hat{i} \;-\; \hat{j} \;+\; 3\hat{k}$, equidistant from the lines AB and AC. If $\left\lvert\overrightarrow{AP}\right\rvert \;=\; \dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{2}$, then the area of the triangle ABP is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A point equidistant from AB and AC lies on the angle bisector, whose direction is $\hat{u}_{AB} + \hat{u}_{AC}$. // 📝 Solution: $\left\lvert\overrightarrow{AB}\right\rvert \;=\; \left\lvert\overrightarrow{AC}\right\rvert \;=\; \sqrt{11}$, so the bisector direction is $\overrightarrow{AB} + \overrightarrow{AC} \;=\; 4\hat{i} + 2\hat{k} \;\parallel\; 2\hat{i} + \hat{k}$. Let $\overrightarrow{AP} \;=\; \lambda\left(2\hat{i} + \hat{k}\right)$. $\left\lvert\lambda\right\rvert\sqrt{5} \;=\; \dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{2} \;\implies\; \lambda \;=\; \dfrac{1}{2}$, so $\overrightarrow{AP} \;=\; \hat{i} + \dfrac{1}{2}\hat{k}$. $\overrightarrow{AB} \times \overrightarrow{AP} \;=\; \dfrac{1}{2}\hat{i} - \dfrac{5}{2}\hat{j} - \hat{k}$, with magnitude $\sqrt{\dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{25}{4} + 1} \;=\; \dfrac{\sqrt{30}}{2}$. Area $\;=\; \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{30}}{2} \;=\; \dfrac{\sqrt{30}}{4}$.
questions.topic: Angle bisector and area of a triangle using cross product

questions.text: Let $ABC$ be a triangle of area $15\sqrt{2}$ and the vectors $\overrightarrow{AB}\;=\;\hat{i}\;+\;2\hat{j}\;-\;7\hat{k}$, $\overrightarrow{BC}\;=\;a\hat{i}\;+\;b\hat{j}\;+\;c\hat{k}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}\;=\;6\hat{i}\;+\;d\hat{j}\;-\;2\hat{k}$, $d\;>\;0$. Then the square of the length of the largest side of the triangle $ABC$ is ____.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Area of a triangle is $\frac{1}{2}\left\lvert\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AC}\right\rvert$, and $\overrightarrow{BC}\;=\;\overrightarrow{AC}\;-\;\overrightarrow{AB}$. // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] Triangle $ABC$ with $\overrightarrow{AB}$, $\overrightarrow{BC}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}$ marked. $\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AC}\;=\;\left(7d\;-\;4,\;-40,\;d\;-\;12\right)$. Area $\;=\;15\sqrt{2}\;\implies\;\left\lvert\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AC}\right\rvert^2\;=\;1800$, so $\left(7d\;-\;4\right)^2\;+\;1600\;+\;\left(d\;-\;12\right)^2\;=\;1800\;\implies\;5d^2\;-\;8d\;-\;4\;=\;0\;\implies\;d\;=\;2\;\text{or}\;-\frac{2}{5}$. Since $d\;>\;0$, $d\;=\;2$. Then $\overrightarrow{BC}\;=\;\overrightarrow{AC}\;-\;\overrightarrow{AB}\;=\;\left(5,\;0,\;5\right)$, so $a\;=\;5$, $b\;=\;0$, $c\;=\;5$. Squares of the sides: $AB^2\;=\;1\;+\;4\;+\;49\;=\;54$, $BC^2\;=\;25\;+\;25\;=\;50$, $AC^2\;=\;36\;+\;4\;+\;4\;=\;44$. The largest is $54$.
questions.topic: Area of a triangle using cross product

questions.text: Let $\vec{a}\;=\;4\hat{i}\;-\;\hat{j}\;+\;\hat{k}$, $\vec{b}\;=\;11\hat{i}\;-\;\hat{j}\;+\;\hat{k}$ and $\vec{c}$ be a vector such that $\left(\vec{a}\;+\;\vec{b}\right)\times\vec{c}\;=\;\vec{c}\times\left(-2\vec{a}\;+\;3\vec{b}\right)$. If $\left(2\vec{a}\;+\;3\vec{b}\right)\cdot\vec{c}\;=\;1670$, then $\left\lvert\vec{c}\right\rvert^2$ is equal to :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Write $\vec{c}\times\left(\vec{u}\right)\;=\;-\vec{u}\times\vec{c}$ so that both sides combine into one cross product with $\vec{c}$ equal to zero. // 📝 Solution: $\left(\vec{a}\;+\;\vec{b}\right)\times\vec{c}\;+\;\left(-2\vec{a}\;+\;3\vec{b}\right)\times\vec{c}\;=\;\vec{0}\;\implies\;\left(4\vec{b}\;-\;\vec{a}\right)\times\vec{c}\;=\;\vec{0}$. So $\vec{c}\;=\;\lambda\left(4\vec{b}\;-\;\vec{a}\right)\;=\;\lambda\left(40,\;-3,\;3\right)$. Also $2\vec{a}\;+\;3\vec{b}\;=\;\left(41,\;-5,\;5\right)$, so $\left(2\vec{a}\;+\;3\vec{b}\right)\cdot\vec{c}\;=\;\lambda\left(1640\;+\;15\;+\;15\right)\;=\;1670\lambda\;=\;1670\;\implies\;\lambda\;=\;1$. Hence $\vec{c}\;=\;\left(40,\;-3,\;3\right)$ and $\left\lvert\vec{c}\right\rvert^2\;=\;1600\;+\;9\;+\;9\;=\;1618$.
questions.topic: Vector equation with cross product (parallel vectors)

questions.text: If $A\left(3,\;1,\;-1\right)$, $B\left(\frac{5}{3},\;\frac{7}{3},\;\frac{1}{3}\right)$, $C\left(2,\;2,\;1\right)$ and $D\left(\frac{10}{3},\;\frac{2}{3},\;-\frac{1}{3}\right)$ are the vertices of a quadrilateral $ABCD$, then its area is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Area of a quadrilateral with diagonals $\overrightarrow{AC}$ and $\overrightarrow{BD}$ is $\frac{1}{2}\left\lvert\overrightarrow{BD}\times\overrightarrow{AC}\right\rvert$. // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] Quadrilateral $ABCD$ (it turns out to be a rectangle). $\overrightarrow{BD}\;=\;\left(\frac{5}{3},\;-\frac{5}{3},\;-\frac{2}{3}\right)$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}\;=\;\left(-1,\;1,\;2\right)$. $\overrightarrow{BD}\times\overrightarrow{AC}\;=\;\left(-\frac{10}{3}\;+\;\frac{2}{3},\;\frac{2}{3}\;-\;\frac{10}{3},\;\frac{5}{3}\;-\;\frac{5}{3}\right)\;=\;\left(-\frac{8}{3},\;-\frac{8}{3},\;0\right)$. Its magnitude is $\frac{8\sqrt{2}}{3}$, so Area $\;=\;\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{8\sqrt{2}}{3}\;=\;\frac{4\sqrt{2}}{3}$.
questions.topic: Area of a quadrilateral using cross product of diagonals

questions.text: Let $\vec{a}\;=\;6\hat{i}\;+\;\hat{j}\;-\;\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}\;=\;\hat{i}\;+\;\hat{j}$. If $\vec{c}$ is a vector such that $\left\lvert\vec{c}\right\rvert\;\ge\;6$, $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c}\;=\;6\left\lvert\vec{c}\right\rvert$, $\left\lvert\vec{c}\;-\;\vec{a}\right\rvert\;=\;2\sqrt{2}$ and the angle between $\vec{a}\times\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ is $60^\circ$, then $\left\lvert\left(\vec{a}\times\vec{b}\right)\times\vec{c}\right\rvert$ is equal to:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\left\lvert\vec{u}\times\vec{v}\right\rvert\;=\;\left\lvert\vec{u}\right\rvert\left\lvert\vec{v}\right\rvert\sin\theta$; find $\left\lvert\vec{c}\right\rvert$ from $\left\lvert\vec{c}-\vec{a}\right\rvert^2$. // 📝 Solution: $\left\lvert\vec{c}\;-\;\vec{a}\right\rvert^2\;=\;8\;\implies\;\left\lvert\vec{c}\right\rvert^2\;+\;38\;-\;2\left(6\left\lvert\vec{c}\right\rvert\right)\;=\;8\;\implies\;\left\lvert\vec{c}\right\rvert^2\;-\;12\left\lvert\vec{c}\right\rvert\;+\;30\;=\;0\;\implies\;\left\lvert\vec{c}\right\rvert\;=\;6\;\pm\;\sqrt{6}$. Since $\left\lvert\vec{c}\right\rvert\;\ge\;6$, $\left\lvert\vec{c}\right\rvert\;=\;6\;+\;\sqrt{6}$. $\vec{a}\times\vec{b}\;=\;\hat{i}\;-\;\hat{j}\;+\;5\hat{k}$, so $\left\lvert\vec{a}\times\vec{b}\right\rvert\;=\;\sqrt{27}\;=\;3\sqrt{3}$. Then $\left\lvert\left(\vec{a}\times\vec{b}\right)\times\vec{c}\right\rvert\;=\;\left\lvert\vec{a}\times\vec{b}\right\rvert\left\lvert\vec{c}\right\rvert\sin60^\circ\;=\;3\sqrt{3}\cdot\left(6\;+\;\sqrt{6}\right)\cdot\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\;=\;\frac{9}{2}\left(6\;+\;\sqrt{6}\right)$.

questions.text: The product of all solutions of the equation $e^{5(\log_e x)^{2}+3} \;=\; x^{8}$, $x \;>\; 0$, is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Take $\log_e$ of both sides and substitute $t=\log_e x$ to get a quadratic in $t$. // 📝 Solution: $\log_e$ both sides $\implies 5(\log_e x)^{2}+3 \;=\; 8\log_e x$ $\implies 5t^{2}-8t+3=0$ with $t=\log_e x$ $\implies \log_e(x_1x_2) \;=\; t_1+t_2 \;=\; \frac{8}{5}$ $\implies x_1x_2 \;=\; e^{8/5}$

questions.text: Let $A=\{-3,-2,-1,0,1,2,3\}$ and $R$ be a relation on $A$ defined by $xRy$ if and only if $2x-y\in\{0,1\}$. Let $\ell$ be the number of elements in $R$, and let $m$ and $n$ be the minimum numbers of elements required to be added in $R$ to make it reflexive and symmetric, respectively. Then $\ell+m+n$ is equal to:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: List the pairs $2x-y\in\{0,1\}$, then check diagonal pairs and reverse pairs. // 📝 Solution: $R=\{(-1,-2),(0,0),(1,2),(-1,-3),(0,-1),(1,1),(2,3)\} \implies \ell=7$; diagonal missing for $5$ elements $\implies m=5$; reverse pairs missing for $5$ elements $\implies n=5 \implies \ell+m+n=17$

questions.text: Let $S$ be the set of the first $11$ natural numbers. Then the number of elements in $A \; = \; \left\{ B \; \subseteq \; S \; : \; n\left( B \right) \; \ge \; 2 \text{ and the product of all elements of } B \text{ is even} \right\}$ is ____.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Subtract the number of subsets of size $\ge \; 2$ consisting entirely of odd numbers from the total number of subsets of $S$ of size $\ge \; 2$. // 📝 Solution: The set $S \; = \; \left\{ 1, \; 2, \; 3, \; \dots, \; 11 \right\}$ has $11$ elements, consisting of $6$ odd numbers $\left\{ 1, \; 3, \; 5, \; 7, \; 9, \; 11 \right\}$ and $5$ even numbers. Total number of subsets $B \; \subseteq \; S$ with $n\left( B \right) \; \ge \; 2$ is $2^{11} \; - \; \binom{11}{0} \; - \; \binom{11}{1} \; = \; 2048 \; - \; 1 \; - \; 11 \; = \; 2036$. The product of all elements of $B$ is odd if and only if all elements in $B$ are odd. The number of subsets of odd numbers with $n\left( B \right) \; \ge \; 2$ is $2^6 \; - \; \binom{6}{0} \; - \; \binom{6}{1} \; = \; 64 \; - \; 1 \; - \; 6 \; = \; 57$. Thus, the number of subsets with $n\left( B \right) \; \ge \; 2$ and an even product is $2036 \; - \; 57 \; = \; 1979$.

questions.text: In a survey of $220$ students of a higher secondary school, it was found that at least $125$ and at most $130$ students studied Mathematics; at least $85$ and at most $95$ studied Physics; at least $75$ and at most $90$ studied Chemistry; $30$ studied both Physics and Chemistry; $50$ studied both Chemistry and Mathematics; $40$ studied both Mathematics and Physics and $10$ studied none of these subjects. Let $m$ and $n$ respectively be the least and the most number of students who studied all the three subjects. Then $m \; + \; n$ is equal to ______
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use the Principle of Inclusion-Exclusion $n\left( M \; \cup \; P \; \cup \; C \right) \; = \; 220 \; - \; 10 \; = \; 210$ and apply the bounds on $n\left( M \right), \; n\left( P \right), \; n\left( C \right)$ along with non-negativity of each Venn diagram region. // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] Let $x \; = \; n\left( M \; \cap \; P \; \cap \; C \right)$. Since $10$ students studied none of the subjects, $n\left( M \; \cup \; P \; \cup \; C \right) \; = \; 220 \; - \; 10 \; = \; 210$. From the Venn diagram, each region must have at least $0$ students, so $30 \; - \; x \; \ge \; 0, \; 40 \; - \; x \; \ge \; 0, \; 50 \; - \; x \; \ge \; 0 \; \implies \; x \; \le \; 30$. By the Inclusion-Exclusion Principle, $n\left( M \right) \; + \; n\left( P \right) \; + \; n\left( C \right) \; - \; \left( 40 \; + \; 30 \; + \; 50 \right) \; + \; x \; = \; 210 \; \implies \; n\left( M \right) \; + \; n\left( P \right) \; + \; n\left( C \right) \; = \; 330 \; - \; x$. Summing the given bounds $125 \; \le \; n\left( M \right) \; \le \; 130$, $85 \; \le \; n\left( P \right) \; \le \; 95$, and $75 \; \le \; n\left( C \right) \; \le \; 90$, we get $285 \; \le \; 330 \; - \; x \; \le \; 315 \; \implies \; 15 \; \le \; x \; \le \; 45$. Combining with $x \; \le \; 30$ gives $15 \; \le \; x \; \le \; 30$. Thus, $m \; = \; 15$ and $n \; = \; 30$, so $m \; + \; n \; = \; 15 \; + \; 30 \; = \; 45$.

questions.text: Let $A=\{1,2,3,\dots,100\}$ and $R=\{(a,b): a=2b+1\}$. Let $(a_1,a_2),(a_2,a_3),\dots,(a_k,a_{k+1})$ be a sequence of $k$ elements of $R$ such that the second entry of each ordered pair equals the first entry of the next. Then the largest integer $k$ for which such a sequence exists is equal to:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Each step gives $a_i=2a_{i+1}+1$; build the longest chain inside $A$. // 📝 Solution: Chain $63\to31\to15\to7\to3\to1$ uses $5$ pairs and the next term would be $127>100 \implies k=5$. Note: the bank prints $\{1,\dots,10\}$, which gives $k=2$; the solution uses $\{1,\dots,100\}$.

questions.text: Let $A=\{-2,-1,0,1,2,3\}$. Let $R$ be a relation on $A$ defined by $xRy$ if and only if $y=\max\{x,1\}$. Let $\ell$ be the number of elements in $R$, and let $m$ and $n$ be the minimum numbers of elements required to be added in $R$ to make it reflexive and symmetric, respectively. Then $\ell+m+n$ is equal to:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: List the pairs of $R$ and check reflexivity and symmetry. // 📝 Solution: $R=\{(-2,1),(-1,1),(0,1),(1,1),(2,2),(3,3)\} \implies \ell=6$; reflexive needs $(-2,-2),(-1,-1),(0,0)$, so $m=3$; symmetric needs $(1,-2),(1,-1),(1,0)$, so $n=3 \implies \ell+m+n=12$

questions.text: Let $A \; = \; \left\{ 2, \; 3, \; 6, \; 7 \right\}$ and $B \; = \; \left\{ 4, \; 5, \; 6, \; 8 \right\}$. Let $R$ be a relation defined on $A \; \times \; B$ by $\left( a_1, \; b_1 \right) R \left( a_2, \; b_2 \right)$ if and only if $a_1 \; + \; a_2 \; = \; b_1 \; + \; b_2$. Then the number of elements in $R$ is _________
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Rewrite the condition as $a_1 \; - \; b_1 \; = \; b_2 \; - \; a_2$ or count the pairs $\left( a_1, \; b_1 \right)$ and $\left( a_2, \; b_2 \right)$ satisfying $a_1 \; + \; a_2 \; = \; b_1 \; + \; b_2$. // 📝 Solution: Given $A \; = \; \left\{ 2, \; 3, \; 6, \; 7 \right\}$ and $B \; = \; \left\{ 4, \; 5, \; 6, \; 8 \right\}$ with $\left( a_1, \; b_1 \right) R \left( a_2, \; b_2 \right) \; \iff \; a_1 \; + \; a_2 \; = \; b_1 \; + \; b_2$. Listing the $12$ distinct pairs along with their reversals ($12 \; \times \; 2 \; = \; 24$): $1.\; \left( 2, \; 4 \right) R \left( 6, \; 4 \right)$, $2.\; \left( 2, \; 4 \right) R \left( 7, \; 5 \right)$, $3.\; \left( 2, \; 5 \right) R \left( 7, \; 4 \right)$, $4.\; \left( 3, \; 4 \right) R \left( 6, \; 5 \right)$, $5.\; \left( 3, \; 5 \right) R \left( 6, \; 4 \right)$, $6.\; \left( 3, \; 5 \right) R \left( 7, \; 5 \right)$, $7.\; \left( 3, \; 6 \right) R \left( 7, \; 4 \right)$, $8.\; \left( 3, \; 4 \right) R \left( 7, \; 6 \right)$, $9.\; \left( 6, \; 5 \right) R \left( 7, \; 8 \right)$, $10.\; \left( 6, \; 8 \right) R \left( 7, \; 5 \right)$, $11.\; \left( 7, \; 8 \right) R \left( 7, \; 6 \right)$, $12.\; \left( 6, \; 8 \right) R \left( 6, \; 4 \right)$, and the self-related pair $13.\; \left( 6, \; 6 \right) R \left( 6, \; 6 \right)$. Thus, the total number of elements in $R$ is $24 \; + \; 1 \; = \; 25$.

questions.text: Let $A$ be the set of all functions $f:\mathbb{Z}\to\mathbb{Z}$ and $R$ be a relation on $A$ such that $R=\{(f,g): f(0)=g(1)\text{ and } f(1)=g(0)\}$. Then $R$ is:

options.text: Symmetric and transitive but not reflexive
Symmetric but neither reflexive nor transitive
Reflexive but neither symmetric nor transitive
Transitive but neither reflexive nor symmetric

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Test each property with specific functions. // 📝 Solution: $(f,g)\in R \implies (g,f)\in R$ (symmetric); reflexivity fails as $f(0)=f(1)$ need not hold; transitivity fails since $(f,g),(g,h)\in R$ does not force $f(0)=h(1)$ in general

questions.text: The minimum number of elements that must be added to the relation $R \; = \; \left\{ \left( a, \; b \right), \; \left( b, \; c \right), \; \left( b, \; d \right) \right\}$ on the set $\left\{ a, \; b, \; c, \; d \right\}$ so that it is an equivalence relation, is _________.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find the reflexive, symmetric, and transitive closure of $R$ on the set $\left\{ a, \; b, \; c, \; d \right\}$. // 📝 Solution: Given $R \; = \; \left\{ \left( a, \; b \right), \; \left( b, \; c \right), \; \left( b, \; d \right) \right\}$ on $A \; = \; \left\{ a, \; b, \; c, \; d \right\}$. Since $a$ is related to $b$, and $b$ is related to both $c$ and $d$, all four elements $\left\{ a, \; b, \; c, \; d \right\}$ belong to the same equivalence class under the smallest equivalence relation containing $R$. Therefore, the equivalence relation must be the universal relation $A \; \times \; A \; = \; \left\{ \left( a, \; a \right), \; \left( b, \; b \right), \; \left( c, \; c \right), \; \left( d, \; d \right), \; \left( a, \; b \right), \; \left( b, \; a \right), \; \left( b, \; c \right), \; \left( c, \; b \right), \; \left( b, \; d \right), \; \left( d, \; b \right), \; \left( a, \; c \right), \; \left( a, \; d \right), \; \left( c, \; d \right), \; \left( d, \; c \right), \; \left( c, \; a \right), \; \left( d, \; a \right) \right\}$, which has $4 \; \times \; 4 \; = \; 16$ elements. Since $3$ elements are already given in $R$, the minimum number of elements to be added is $16 \; - \; 3 \; = \; 13$.

questions.text: The number of non-empty equivalence relations on the set $\left\{1, 2, 3\right\}$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Equivalence relations correspond to partitions of the set. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Partitions: } \left\{1\right\}\left\{2\right\}\left\{3\right\} \;,\; \left\{1,2\right\}\left\{3\right\} \;,\; \left\{1,3\right\}\left\{2\right\} \;,\; \left\{2,3\right\}\left\{1\right\} \;,\; \left\{1,2,3\right\} \implies 5$

questions.text: Let $R$ be a relation on $\mathbb{N} \; \times \; \mathbb{N}$ defined by $\left( a, \; b \right) R \left( c, \; d \right)$ if and only if $ad \left( b \; - \; c \right) \; = \; bc \left( a \; - \; d \right)$. Then $R$ is

options.text: symmetric but neither reflexive nor transitive
transitive but neither reflexive nor symmetric
reflexive and symmetric but not transitive
symmetric and transitive but not reflexive

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Check reflexivity by setting $\left( c, \; d \right) \; = \; \left( a, \; b \right)$, symmetry by swapping $\left( a, \; b \right)$ and $\left( c, \; d \right)$, and transitivity using a numerical counterexample. // 📝 Solution: Given $\left( a, \; b \right) R \left( c, \; d \right) \; \iff \; ad \left( b \; - \; c \right) \; = \; bc \left( a \; - \; d \right)$. For reflexivity: $\left( a, \; b \right) R \left( a, \; b \right) \; \iff \; ab \left( b \; - \; a \right) \; = \; ba \left( a \; - \; b \right)$, which holds only when $a \; = \; b$, so $R$ is not reflexive. For symmetry: if $\left( a, \; b \right) R \left( c, \; d \right)$, then $ad \left( b \; - \; c \right) \; = \; bc \left( a \; - \; d \right) \; \implies \; cb \left( d \; - \; a \right) \; = \; da \left( c \; - \; b \right) \; \implies \; \left( c, \; d \right) R \left( a, \; b \right)$, so $R$ is symmetric. For transitivity: notice that $\left( 2, \; 3 \right) R \left( 3, \; 2 \right)$ since $4 \left( 3 \; - \; 3 \right) \; = \; 9 \left( 2 \; - \; 2 \right) \; = \; 0$, and $\left( 3, \; 2 \right) R \left( 5, \; 30 \right)$ since $90 \left( 2 \; - \; 5 \right) \; = \; 10 \left( 3 \; - \; 30 \right) \; = \; -270$. However, for $\left( 2, \; 3 \right)$ and $\left( 5, \; 30 \right)$, $60 \left( 3 \; - \; 5 \right) \; = \; -120 \; \neq \; 15 \left( 2 \; - \; 30 \right) \; = \; -420$, so $\left( \left( 2, \; 3 \right), \; \left( 5, \; 30 \right) \right) \; \notin \; R$. Thus, $R$ is not transitive.

questions.text: Let $A \; = \; \left\{ 0, \; 1, \; 2, \; \dots, \; 9 \right\}$. Let $R$ be a relation on $A$ defined by $\left( x, \; y \right) \; \in \; R$ if and only if $\left\lvert x \; - \; y \right\rvert$ is a multiple of $3$. Given below are two statements: Statement I: $n\left( R \right) \; = \; 36$. Statement II: $R$ is an equivalence relation. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below

options.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Partition set $A$ into $3$ equivalence classes modulo $3$ and compute $n\left( R \right)$ as the sum of squares of the sizes of each equivalence class. // 📝 Solution: The relation $\left( x, \; y \right) \; \in \; R \; \iff \; \left\lvert x \; - \; y \right\rvert$ is a multiple of $3$ is the congruence modulo $3$ relation $x \; \equiv \; y \pmod{3}$, which is reflexive ($\left\lvert x \; - \; x \right\rvert \; = \; 0$), symmetric ($\left\lvert x \; - \; y \right\rvert \; = \; \left\lvert y \; - \; x \right\rvert$), and transitive. Hence, $R$ is an equivalence relation and Statement II is correct. The equivalence classes in $A \; = \; \left\{ 0, \; 1, \; 2, \; \dots, \; 9 \right\}$ are $\left\{ 0, \; 3, \; 6, \; 9 \right\}$ ($4$ elements), $\left\{ 1, \; 4, \; 7 \right\}$ ($3$ elements), and $\left\{ 2, \; 5, \; 8 \right\}$ ($3$ elements). Thus, $n\left( R \right) \; = \; 4^2 \; + \; 3^2 \; + \; 3^2 \; = \; 16 \; + \; 9 \; + \; 9 \; = \; 34 \; \neq \; 36$, so Statement I is incorrect.

questions.text: Let a relation $R$ on $\mathbb{N} \; \times \; \mathbb{N}$ be defined as: $\left( x_1, \; y_1 \right) R \left( x_2, \; y_2 \right)$ if and only if $x_1 \; \le \; x_2$ or $y_1 \; \le \; y_2$. Consider the two statements: (I) $R$ is reflexive but not symmetric. (II) $R$ is transitive. Then which one of the following is true?

Among the relations $S \; = \; \left\{ \left( a, \; b \right) \; : \; a, \; b \; \in \; \mathbb{R} \; - \; \left\{ 0 \right\}, \; 2 \; + \; \frac{a}{b} \; > \; 0 \right\}$ and $T \; = \; \left\{ \left( a, \; b \right) \; : \; a, \; b \; \in \; \mathbb{R}, \; a^2 \; - \; b^2 \; \in \; \mathbb{Z} \right\}$,
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Check symmetry for $T$ using $b^2 \; - \; a^2 \; = \; -\left( a^2 \; - \; b^2 \right)$ and test $S$ with a pair where $\frac{a}{b} \; > \; -2$ but $\frac{b}{a} \; \le \; -2$. // 📝 Solution: For relation $T$: if $\left( a, \; b \right) \; \in \; T$, then $a^2 \; - \; b^2 \; = \; k \; \in \; \mathbb{Z}$. Then $b^2 \; - \; a^2 \; = \; -k \; \in \; \mathbb{Z}$, which implies $\left( b, \; a \right) \; \in \; T$, so $T$ is symmetric. For relation $S$: $\left( a, \; b \right) \; \in \; S \; \iff \; 2 \; + \; \frac{a}{b} \; > \; 0 \; \iff \; \frac{a}{b} \; > \; -2$. If $-2 \; < \; \frac{a}{b} \; < \; 0$, then $\frac{b}{a} \; < \; -\frac{1}{2}$, so $2 \; + \; \frac{b}{a}$ is not necessarily positive (for example, take $a \; = \; -1, \; b \; = \; 2$, then $2 \; + \; \frac{a}{b} \; = \; \frac{3}{2} \; > \; 0$, but $2 \; + \; \frac{b}{a} \; = \; 0 \; \ngtr \; 0$). Thus, $S$ is not symmetric. Hence, $T$ is symmetric but $S$ is not.

questions.text: Let $A \; = \; \left\{ 2, \; 3, \; 5, \; 7, \; 9 \right\}$. Let $R$ be the relation on $A$ defined by $x R y$ if and only if $2x \; \le \; 3y$. Let $l$ be the number of elements in $R$, and $m$ be the minimum number of elements required to be added in $R$ to make it a symmetric relation. Then $l \; + \; m$ is equal to :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Count all pairs $\left( x, \; y \right) \; \in \; A \; \times \; A$ satisfying $y \; \ge \; \frac{2x}{3}$ to find $l$, then identify pairs whose reverse $\left( y, \; x \right)$ is missing in $R$ to find $m$. // 📝 Solution: Given $A \; = \; \left\{ 2, \; 3, \; 5, \; 7, \; 9 \right\}$ and $x R y \; \iff \; 2x \; \le \; 3y \; \iff \; y \; \ge \; \frac{2x}{3}$. For $x \; = \; 2$: $y \; \in \; \left\{ 2, \; 3, \; 5, \; 7, \; 9 \right\}$ ($5$ pairs). For $x \; = \; 3$: $y \; \in \; \left\{ 2, \; 3, \; 5, \; 7, \; 9 \right\}$ ($5$ pairs). For $x \; = \; 5$: $y \; \in \; \left\{ 5, \; 7, \; 9 \right\}$ ($3$ pairs). For $x \; = \; 7$: $y \; \in \; \left\{ 5, \; 7, \; 9 \right\}$ ($3$ pairs). For $x \; = \; 9$: $y \; \in \; \left\{ 7, \; 9 \right\}$ ($2$ pairs). Thus, $l \; = \; 5 \; + \; 5 \; + \; 3 \; + \; 3 \; + \; 2 \; = \; 18$. For symmetry, the pairs in $R$ whose reversals are missing are $\left( 2, \; 5 \right), \; \left( 2, \; 7 \right), \; \left( 2, \; 9 \right), \; \left( 3, \; 5 \right), \; \left( 3, \; 7 \right), \; \left( 3, \; 9 \right), \; \left( 5, \; 9 \right)$, which require adding $\left( 5, \; 2 \right), \; \left( 7, \; 2 \right), \; \left( 9, \; 2 \right), \; \left( 5, \; 3 \right), \; \left( 7, \; 3 \right), \; \left( 9, \; 3 \right), \; \left( 9, \; 5 \right)$, giving $m \; = \; 7$. Hence, $l \; + \; m \; = \; 18 \; + \; 7 \; = \; 25$.

questions.text: The number of elements in the relation $R \; = \; \left\{ \left( x, \; y \right) \; : \; 4x^2 \; + \; y^2 \; < \; 52, \; x, \; y \; \in \; \mathbb{Z} \right\}$ is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Bound $x^2 \; < \; 13$ to find all possible integer values of $x$, and for each $x$, count the number of integers $y$ satisfying $y^2 \; < \; 52 \; - \; 4x^2$. // 📝 Solution: Given $4x^2 \; + \; y^2 \; < \; 52$ with $x, \; y \; \in \; \mathbb{Z}$. Since $y^2 \; \ge \; 0$, we need $4x^2 \; < \; 52 \; \implies \; x^2 \; < \; 13$, so $x \; \in \; \left\{ -3, \; -2, \; -1, \; 0, \; 1, \; 2, \; 3 \right\}$. For $x \; = \; 0$: $y^2 \; < \; 52 \; \implies \; \left\lvert y \right\rvert \; \le \; 7$, giving $15$ values of $y$. For $x \; = \; \pm 1$: $y^2 \; < \; 48 \; \implies \; \left\lvert y \right\rvert \; \le \; 6$, giving $13$ values each ($2 \; \times \; 13 \; = \; 26$ values). For $x \; = \; \pm 2$: $y^2 \; < \; 36 \; \implies \; \left\lvert y \right\rvert \; \le \; 5$, giving $11$ values each ($2 \; \times \; 11 \; = \; 22$ values). For $x \; = \; \pm 3$: $y^2 \; < \; 16 \; \implies \; \left\lvert y \right\rvert \; \le \; 3$, giving $7$ values each ($2 \; \times \; 7 \; = \; 14$ values). Total number of elements in $R$ is $15 \; + \; 26 \; + \; 22 \; + \; 14 \; = \; 77$.
questions.topic: Domain and Elements of a Relation

questions.text: Let $R$ be a relation defined on $\mathbb{N}$ as $a R b$ if $2a \; + \; 3b$ is a multiple of $5, \; a, \; b \; \in \; \mathbb{N}$. Then $R$ is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Check divisibility by $5$ for $2a \; + \; 3a$, $2b \; + \; 3a$, and $2a \; + \; 3c$ using modular arithmetic or linear combinations. // 📝 Solution: For reflexivity, for any $a \; \in \; \mathbb{N}$, $2a \; + \; 3a \; = \; 5a$, which is a multiple of $5$, so $a R a$ holds and $R$ is reflexive. For symmetry, let $a R b \; \implies \; 2a \; + \; 3b \; = \; 5\alpha$ for some integer $\alpha$. Now consider $2b \; + \; 3a \; = \; 5 \left( a \; + \; b \right) \; - \; \left( 2a \; + \; 3b \right) \; = \; 5 \left( a \; + \; b \; - \; \alpha \right)$, which is a multiple of $5$, so $b R a$ holds and $R$ is symmetric. For transitivity, let $a R b$ and $b R c$, so $2a \; + \; 3b \; = \; 5\alpha$ and $2b \; + \; 3c \; = \; 5\beta$. Adding these gives $2a \; + \; 5b \; + \; 3c \; = \; 5 \left( \alpha \; + \; \beta \right) \; \implies \; 2a \; + \; 3c \; = \; 5 \left( \alpha \; + \; \beta \; - \; b \right)$, which is a multiple of $5$. Thus $a R c$ holds and $R$ is transitive. Hence, $R$ is an equivalence relation.

questions.text: Let $A \; = \; \left\{ 2, \; 3, \; 6, \; 8, \; 9, \; 11 \right\}$ and $B \; = \; \left\{ 1, \; 4, \; 5, \; 10, \; 15 \right\}$. Let $R$ be a relation on $A \; \times \; B$ defined by $\left( a, \; b \right) R \left( c, \; d \right)$ if and only if $3ad \; - \; 7bc$ is an even integer. Then the relation $R$ is

options.text: reflexive and symmetric but not transitive.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Note that $3ad \; - \; 7bc$ is even if and only if $ad$ and $bc$ have the same parity (both even or both odd). // 📝 Solution: Given $A \; = \; \left\{ 2, \; 3, \; 6, \; 8, \; 9, \; 11 \right\}$ and $B \; = \; \left\{ 1, \; 4, \; 5, \; 10, \; 15 \right\}$. For reflexivity: $\left( a, \; b \right) R \left( a, \; b \right) \; \implies \; 3ab \; - \; 7ba \; = \; -4ab$, which is always even, so $R$ is reflexive. For symmetry: if $3ad \; - \; 7bc$ is even, then either both $ad$ and $bc$ are odd or both are even. In either case, $3cb \; - \; 7da$ is also even, so $\left( c, \; d \right) R \left( a, \; b \right)$ holds and $R$ is symmetric. For transitivity: notice that $\left( 3, \; 4 \right) R \left( 6, \; 4 \right)$ (since $3 \left( 12 \right) \; - \; 7 \left( 24 \right) \; = \; -132$ is even) and $\left( 6, \; 4 \right) R \left( 3, \; 1 \right)$ (since $3 \left( 6 \right) \; - \; 7 \left( 12 \right) \; = \; -66$ is even), but $\left( 3, \; 4 \right)$ is not related to $\left( 3, \; 1 \right)$ because $3 \left( 3 \right) \; - \; 7 \left( 12 \right) \; = \; -75$ is odd. Thus, $R$ is reflexive and symmetric but not transitive.

questions.text: Let $R$ be a relation on $\mathbb{R}$, given by $R \; = \; \left\{ \left( a, \; b \right) \; : \; 3a \; - \; 3b \; + \; \sqrt{7} \text{ is an irrational number} \right\}$. Then $R$ is

options.text: Reflexive but neither symmetric nor transitive
Reflexive and transitive but not symmetric
Reflexive and symmetric but not transitive

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Test reflexivity with $a \; = \; b$, symmetry with $3a \; - \; 3b \; = \; \sqrt{7}$, and transitivity by choosing $a, \; b, \; c$ such that $3a \; - \; 3c \; + \; \sqrt{7} \; = \; 0$. // 📝 Solution: Check for reflexivity: for any $a \; \in \; \mathbb{R}$, $3\left( a \; - \; a \right) \; + \; \sqrt{7} \; = \; \sqrt{7}$, which is irrational, so $\left( a, \; a \right) \; \in \; R$ and $R$ is reflexive. Check for symmetry: take $a \; = \; \frac{\sqrt{7}}{3}$ and $b \; = \; 0$. Then $3a \; - \; 3b \; + \; \sqrt{7} \; = \; 2\sqrt{7}$ (irrational), so $\left( a, \; b \right) \; \in \; R$. However, $3\left( b \; - \; a \right) \; + \; \sqrt{7} \; = \; 0$ (rational), so $\left( b, \; a \right) \; \notin \; R$, meaning $R$ is not symmetric. Check for transitivity: take $\left( a, \; b \right) \; = \; \left( \frac{\sqrt{7}}{3}, \; 1 \right)$ and $\left( b, \; c \right) \; = \; \left( 1, \; \frac{2\sqrt{7}}{3} \right)$. Both $\left( a, \; b \right) \; \in \; R$ and $\left( b, \; c \right) \; \in \; R$, but for $\left( a, \; c \right)$, $3\left( \frac{\sqrt{7}}{3} \; - \; \frac{2\sqrt{7}}{3} \right) \; + \; \sqrt{7} \; = \; 0$ (rational), so $\left( a, \; c \right) \; \notin \; R$. Hence, $R$ is reflexive but neither symmetric nor transitive.

questions.text: Let $A=\{-3,-2,-1,0,1,2,3\}$. Let $R$ be a relation on $A$ defined by $xRy$ if and only if $0\le x^2+2y\le4$. Let $\ell$ be the number of elements in $R$, and let $m$ be the minimum number of elements required to be added in $R$ to make it reflexive. Then $\ell+m$ is equal to:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For each $y$, count the $x$ with $0\le x^2+2y\le4$. // 📝 Solution: $y=-3,-2,-1,0,1,2$ give $2,2,2,5,3,1$ pairs $\implies \ell=15$; missing diagonal pairs $(-1,-1),(2,2),(3,3)$ give $m=3 \implies \ell+m=18$

questions.text: Let $A=\{0,1,2,3,4,5\}$. Let $R$ be a relation on $A$ defined by $(x,y)\in R$ if and only if $\max\{x,y\}\in\{3,4\}$. Then among the statements: (S1) the number of elements in $R$ is $18$, and (S2) the relation $R$ is symmetric but neither reflexive nor transitive:

options.text: Both S1 and S2 are true
Both S1 and S2 are false

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Count pairs with maximum $3$ or $4$, then test reflexivity and transitivity. // 📝 Solution: $\lvert R\rvert=7+9=16$, so S1 is false; $R$ is symmetric, not reflexive ($(0,0)\notin R$), not transitive ($(0,3),(3,1)\in R$, $(0,1)\notin R$), so only S2 is true

questions.text: Let $P\left( S \right)$ denote the power set of $S \; = \; \left\{ 1, \; 2, \; 3, \; \dots, \; 10 \right\}$. Define the relations $R_1$ and $R_2$ on $P\left( S \right)$ as $A R_1 B$ if $\left( A \; \cap \; B^c \right) \; \cup \; \left( B \; \cap \; A^c \right) \; = \; \emptyset$ and $A R_2 B$ if $A \; \cup \; B^c \; = \; B \; \cup \; A^c, \; \forall \; A, \; B \; \in \; P\left( S \right)$. Then :

options.text: both $R_1$ and $R_2$ are not equivalence relations

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Simplify the set conditions for $R_1$ and $R_2$ using symmetric difference and Venn diagrams to see that both reduce to $A \; = \; B$. // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] Given $S \; = \; \left\{ 1, \; 2, \; 3, \; \dots, \; 10 \right\}$ and $P\left( S \right)$ is the power set of $S$. For $R_1$: $A R_1 B \; \iff \; \left( A \; \cap \; B^c \right) \; \cup \; \left( B \; \cap \; A^c \right) \; = \; \emptyset$. This means $A \; - \; B \; = \; \emptyset$ and $B \; - \; A \; = \; \emptyset$, which holds if and only if $A \; = \; B$. Since equality of sets is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive, $R_1$ is an equivalence relation. For $R_2$: $A R_2 B \; \iff \; A \; \cup \; B^c \; = \; B \; \cup \; A^c$. From the Venn diagram, $A \; \cup \; B^c \; = \; B \; \cup \; A^c$ implies $A \; - \; B \; = \; B \; - \; A \; = \; \emptyset \; \iff \; A \; = \; B$. Therefore, $R_2$ is also reflexive, symmetric, and transitive. Hence, both $R_1$ and $R_2$ are equivalence relations.

questions.text: The relation $R \; = \; \left\{ \left( a, \; b \right) \; : \; \gcd \left( a, \; b \right) \; = \; 1, \; 2a \; \neq \; b, \; a, \; b \; \in \; \mathbb{Z} \right\}$ is:

Let the set $S \; = \; \left\{ 2, \; 4, \; 8, \; 16, \; \dots, \; 512 \right\}$ be partitioned into $3$ sets $A, \; B, \; C$ with equal number of elements such that $A \; \cup \; B \; \cup \; C \; = \; S$ and $A \; \cap \; B \; = \; B \; \cap \; C \; = \; A \; \cap \; C \; = \; \emptyset$. The maximum number of such possible partitions of $S$ is equal to:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find the number of ways to distribute $9$ distinct elements into $3$ distinct sets $A, \; B, \; C$ of $3$ elements each using $\frac{9!}{3! \; 3! \; 3!}$. // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] The set $S \; = \; \left\{ 2^1, \; 2^2, \; 2^3, \; \dots, \; 2^9 \right\}$ contains $9$ distinct elements. Since $S$ is partitioned into $3$ disjoint sets $A, \; B, \; C$ of equal size, each set contains $3$ elements. The total number of ways to partition $S$ into the $3$ distinct sets $A, \; B, \; C$ is $\frac{9!}{\left( 3! \; 3! \; 3! \right) \; 3!} \; \times \; 3! \; = \; \frac{9!}{3! \; 3! \; 3!} \; = \; \frac{362880}{6 \; \times \; 6 \; \times \; 6} \; = \; 1680$.

questions.text: Let $A \; = \; \left\{ x \; : \; \left\lvert x^2 \; - \; 10 \right\rvert \; \le \; 6 \right\}$ and $B \; = \; \left\{ x \; : \; \left\lvert x \; - \; 2 \right\rvert \; > \; 1 \right\}$. Then
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Solve the absolute value inequalities to find intervals for sets $A$ and $B$, then evaluate $B \; - \; A \; = \; B \; \cap \; A^c$. // 📝 Solution: For set $A$: $\left\lvert x^2 \; - \; 10 \right\rvert \; \le \; 6 \; \iff \; -6 \; \le \; x^2 \; - \; 10 \; \le \; 6 \; \implies \; 4 \; \le \; x^2 \; \le \; 16$, so $A \; = \; \left[ -4, \; -2 \right] \; \cup \; \left[ 2, \; 4 \right]$. For set $B$: $\left\lvert x \; - \; 2 \right\rvert \; > \; 1 \; \iff \; x \; - \; 2 \; < \; -1$ or $x \; - \; 2 \; > \; 1$, so $B \; = \; \left( -\infty, \; 1 \right) \; \cup \; \left( 3, \; \infty \right)$. Taking the complement of $A$, we get $A^c \; = \; \left( -\infty, \; -4 \right) \; \cup \; \left( -2, \; 2 \right) \; \cup \; \left( 4, \; \infty \right)$. Therefore, $B \; - \; A \; = \; B \; \cap \; A^c \; = \; \left[ \left( -\infty, \; 1 \right) \; \cap \; A^c \right] \; \cup \; \left[ \left( 3, \; \infty \right) \; \cap \; A^c \right] \; = \; \left( -\infty, \; -4 \right) \; \cup \; \left( -2, \; 1 \right) \; \cup \; \left( 4, \; \infty \right)$.

questions.text: Let $R$ be a relation defined on the set $\left\{ 1, \; 2, \; 3, \; 4 \right\} \; \times \; \left\{ 1, \; 2, \; 3, \; 4 \right\}$ by $R \; = \; \left\{ \left( \left( a, \; b \right), \; \left( c, \; d \right) \right) \; : \; 2a \; + \; 3b \; = \; 3c \; + \; 4d \right\}$. Then the number of elements in $R$ is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Tabulate all possible values of $k \; = \; 2a \; + \; 3b$ and $k \; = \; 3c \; + \; 4d$ for $a, \; b, \; c, \; d \; \in \; \left\{ 1, \; 2, \; 3, \; 4 \right\}$, and multiply the frequencies for each common value $k$. // 📝 Solution: We need $2a \; + \; 3b \; = \; 3c \; + \; 4d \; = \; k$ where $a, \; b, \; c, \; d \; \in \; \left\{ 1, \; 2, \; 3, \; 4 \right\}$. Finding the common values of $k$ and matching pairs $\left( a, \; b \right)$ and $\left( c, \; d \right)$: for $k \; = \; 7$, $\left( 2, \; 1 \right)$ and $\left( 1, \; 1 \right) \; \implies \; 1 \; \times \; 1 \; = \; 1$; for $k \; = \; 10$, $\left( 2, \; 2 \right)$ and $\left( 2, \; 1 \right) \; \implies \; 1$; for $k \; = \; 11$, $\left\{ \left( 1, \; 3 \right), \; \left( 4, \; 1 \right) \right\}$ and $\left( 1, \; 2 \right) \; \implies \; 2 \; \times \; 1 \; = \; 2$; for $k \; = \; 13$, $\left( 2, \; 3 \right)$ and $\left( 3, \; 1 \right) \; \implies \; 1$; for $k \; = \; 14$, $\left\{ \left( 1, \; 4 \right), \; \left( 4, \; 2 \right) \right\}$ and $\left( 2, \; 2 \right) \; \implies \; 2 \; \times \; 1 \; = \; 2$; for $k \; = \; 15$, $\left( 3, \; 3 \right)$ and $\left( 1, \; 3 \right) \; \implies \; 1$; for $k \; = \; 16$, $\left( 2, \; 4 \right)$ and $\left( 4, \; 1 \right) \; \implies \; 1$; for $k \; = \; 17$, $\left( 4, \; 3 \right)$ and $\left( 3, \; 2 \right) \; \implies \; 1$; for $k \; = \; 18$, $\left( 3, \; 4 \right)$ and $\left( 2, \; 3 \right) \; \implies \; 1$; for $k \; = \; 20$, $\left( 4, \; 4 \right)$ and $\left( 4, \; 2 \right) \; \implies \; 1$. Summing these gives $1 \; + \; 1 \; + \; 2 \; + \; 1 \; + \; 2 \; + \; 1 \; + \; 1 \; + \; 1 \; + \; 1 \; + \; 1 \; = \; 12$.
questions.topic: Number of Elements in a Relation

questions.text: Let $A \; = \; \left\{ 1, \; 2, \; 3, \; 4, \; 5 \right\}$. Let $R$ be a relation on $A$ defined by $x R y$ if and only if $4x \; \le \; 5y$. Let $m$ be the number of elements in $R$ and $n$ be the minimum number of elements from $A \; \times \; A$ that are required to be added to $R$ to make it a symmetric relation. Then $m \; + \; n$ is equal to :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: List the ordered pairs $\left( x, \; y \right) \; \in \; A \; \times \; A$ satisfying $4x \; \le \; 5y$ to find $m$, then count asymmetric pairs to find $n$. // 📝 Solution: Given $A \; = \; \left\{ 1, \; 2, \; 3, \; 4, \; 5 \right\}$ and $4x \; \le \; 5y$. Listing the elements of $R$: $R \; = \; \left\{ \left( 1, \; 1 \right), \; \left( 1, \; 2 \right), \; \left( 1, \; 3 \right), \; \left( 1, \; 4 \right), \; \left( 1, \; 5 \right), \; \left( 2, \; 2 \right), \; \left( 2, \; 3 \right), \; \left( 2, \; 4 \right), \; \left( 2, \; 5 \right), \; \left( 3, \; 3 \right), \; \left( 3, \; 4 \right), \; \left( 3, \; 5 \right), \; \left( 4, \; 4 \right), \; \left( 4, \; 5 \right), \; \left( 5, \; 4 \right), \; \left( 5, \; 5 \right) \right\}$, which gives $m \; = \; 16$ elements. To make $R$ symmetric, we must add the missing reverse pairs $\left\{ \left( 2, \; 1 \right), \; \left( 3, \; 2 \right), \; \left( 4, \; 3 \right), \; \left( 3, \; 1 \right), \; \left( 4, \; 2 \right), \; \left( 5, \; 3 \right), \; \left( 4, \; 1 \right), \; \left( 5, \; 2 \right), \; \left( 5, \; 1 \right) \right\}$, which gives $n \; = \; 9$. Therefore, $m \; + \; n \; = \; 16 \; + \; 9 \; = \; 25$.

questions.text: Let the relation $R$ on the set $M \; = \; \left\{ 1, \; 2, \; 3, \; \dots, \; 16 \right\}$ be given by $R \; = \; \left\{ \left( x, \; y \right) \; : \; 4y \; = \; 5x \; - \; 3, \; x, \; y \; \in \; M \right\}$. Then the minimum number of elements required to be added in $R$, in order to make the relation symmetric, is equal to
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find all integer solutions $\left( x, \; y \right) \; \in \; M \; \times \; M$ to $y \; = \; \frac{5x \; - \; 3}{4}$ and count the non-diagonal pairs $\left( x, \; y \right)$ with $x \; \neq \; y$. // 📝 Solution: Given $4y \; = \; 5x \; - \; 3 \; \implies \; y \; = \; \frac{5x \; - \; 3}{4}$ for $x, \; y \; \in \; M \; = \; \left\{ 1, \; 2, \; \dots, \; 16 \right\}$. For $y$ to be an integer, $5x \; - \; 3 \; \equiv \; 0 \pmod{4} \; \implies \; x \; \equiv \; 3 \pmod{4}$, so $x \; \in \; \left\{ 3, \; 7, \; 11, \; 15 \right\}$. Testing each value: $x \; = \; 3 \; \implies \; y \; = \; 3$; $x \; = \; 7 \; \implies \; y \; = \; 8$; $x \; = \; 11 \; \implies \; y \; = \; 13$; $x \; = \; 15 \; \implies \; y \; = \; 18 \; \notin \; M$. Thus, $R \; = \; \left\{ \left( 3, \; 3 \right), \; \left( 7, \; 8 \right), \; \left( 11, \; 13 \right) \right\}$. Since $\left( 3, \; 3 \right)$ is already symmetric, we only need to add $\left( 8, \; 7 \right)$ and $\left( 13, \; 11 \right)$, so the minimum number of elements to be added is $2$.

questions.text: Let $A \; = \; \left\{ -2, \; -1, \; 0, \; 1, \; 2, \; 3, \; 4 \right\}$. Let $R$ be a relation on $A$ defined by $x R y$ if and only if $2x \; + \; y \; \le \; 2$. Let $l$ be the number of elements in $R$. Let $m$ and $n$ be the minimum number of elements required to be added in $R$ to make it reflexive and symmetric relations respectively. Then $l \; + \; m \; + \; n$ is equal to :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find $l$ by counting valid $y \; \le \; 2 \; - \; 2x$ for each $x \; \in \; A$, $m$ by checking $3x \; \le \; 2$, and $n$ by counting pairs where $2x \; + \; y \; \le \; 2$ but $x \; + \; 2y \; > \; 2$. // 📝 Solution: Given $A \; = \; \left\{ -2, \; -1, \; 0, \; 1, \; 2, \; 3, \; 4 \right\}$ and $x R y \; \iff \; y \; \le \; 2 \; - \; 2x$. Counting pairs for each $x$: for $x \; = \; -2$, $y \; \le \; 6$ ($7$ pairs); for $x \; = \; -1$, $y \; \le \; 4$ ($7$ pairs); for $x \; = \; 0$, $y \; \le \; 2 \; \implies \; y \; \in \; \left\{ -2, \; -1, \; 0, \; 1, \; 2 \right\}$ ($5$ pairs); for $x \; = \; 1$, $y \; \le \; 0 \; \implies \; y \; \in \; \left\{ -2, \; -1, \; 0 \right\}$ ($3$ pairs); for $x \; = \; 2$, $y \; \le \; -2 \; \implies \; y \; \in \; \left\{ -2 \right\}$ ($1$ pair); for $x \; = \; 3, \; 4$, no valid $y$ in $A$. Thus, $l \; = \; 7 \; + \; 7 \; + \; 5 \; + \; 3 \; + \; 1 \; = \; 23$. For reflexive: $\left( x, \; x \right) \; \in \; R \; \iff \; 3x \; \le \; 2 \; \iff \; x \; \le \; \frac{2}{3}$, which holds for $x \; = \; -2, \; -1, \; 0$, and is missing for $x \; = \; 1, \; 2, \; 3, \; 4$, so $m \; = \; 4$. For symmetric: missing reverse pairs are $\left( 3, \; -2 \right), \; \left( 4, \; -2 \right), \; \left( 2, \; -1 \right), \; \left( 3, \; -1 \right), \; \left( 4, \; -1 \right), \; \left( 2, \; 0 \right)$, so $n \; = \; 6$. Therefore, $l \; + \; m \; + \; n \; = \; 23 \; + \; 4 \; + \; 6 \; = \; 33$.

questions.text: Let the relations $R_1$ and $R_2$ on the set $X \; = \; \left\{ 1, \; 2, \; 3, \; \dots, \; 20 \right\}$ be given by $R_1 \; = \; \left\{ \left( x, \; y \right) \; : \; 2x \; - \; 3y \; = \; 2 \right\}$ and $R_2 \; = \; \left\{ \left( x, \; y \right) \; : \; -5x \; + \; 4y \; = \; 0 \right\}$. If $M$ and $N$ be the minimum number of elements required to be added in $R_1$ and $R_2$, respectively, in order to make the relations symmetric, then $M \; + \; N$ equals
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: List all ordered pairs $\left( x, \; y \right) \; \in \; X \; \times \; X$ satisfying the equations for $R_1$ and $R_2$, and check if any symmetric pairs are already present. // 📝 Solution: Given $X \; = \; \left\{ 1, \; 2, \; 3, \; \dots, \; 20 \right\}$. For $R_1 \; = \; \left\{ \left( x, \; y \right) \; : \; 2x \; - \; 3y \; = \; 2 \right\}$, the elements in $X \; \times \; X$ are $R_1 \; = \; \left\{ \left( 4, \; 2 \right), \; \left( 7, \; 4 \right), \; \left( 10, \; 6 \right), \; \left( 13, \; 8 \right), \; \left( 16, \; 10 \right), \; \left( 19, \; 12 \right) \right\}$, so $M \; = \; 6$ elements are needed in $R_1$ to make it symmetric. For $R_2 \; = \; \left\{ \left( x, \; y \right) \; : \; -5x \; + \; 4y \; = \; 0 \right\}$, the elements in $X \; \times \; X$ are $R_2 \; = \; \left\{ \left( 4, \; 5 \right), \; \left( 8, \; 10 \right), \; \left( 12, \; 15 \right), \; \left( 16, \; 20 \right) \right\}$, so $N \; = \; 4$ elements are needed in $R_2$ to make it symmetric. Thus, $M \; + \; N \; = \; 6 \; + \; 4 \; = \; 10$.

questions.text: The number of relations, defined on the set $\left\{ a, \; b, \; c, \; d \right\}$, which are both reflexive and symmetric, is equal to:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use the formula $2^{\frac{n\left( n \; - \; 1 \right)}{2}}$ for the number of relations on a set of $n$ elements that are both reflexive and symmetric. // 📝 Solution: For a set with $n \; = \; 4$ elements, the reflexive condition requires all $4$ diagonal pairs $\left( a, \; a \right), \; \left( b, \; b \right), \; \left( c, \; c \right), \; \left( d, \; d \right)$ to be included ($1$ choice). For the remaining non-diagonal elements, symmetric pairs $\left\{ \left( x, \; y \right), \; \left( y, \; x \right) \right\}$ must either both be included or both excluded. The number of such unordered pairs is $\binom{4}{2} \; = \; 6$, and each pair has $2$ choices. Therefore, the total number of reflexive and symmetric relations is $2^6 \; = \; 64$.
questions.topic: Number of Reflexive and Symmetric Relations

questions.text: The minimum number of elements that must be added to the relation $R \; = \; \left\{ \left( a, \; b \right), \; \left( b, \; c \right) \right\}$ on the set $\left\{ a, \; b, \; c \right\}$ so that it becomes symmetric and transitive is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Add symmetric counterparts first, then apply transitivity to all connected pairs, including self-loops generated by $\left( x, \; y \right)$ and $\left( y, \; x \right)$. // 📝 Solution: Given $R \; = \; \left\{ \left( a, \; b \right), \; \left( b, \; c \right) \right\}$. For symmetry, since $\left( a, \; b \right), \; \left( b, \; c \right) \; \in \; R$, we must add $\left( b, \; a \right)$ and $\left( c, \; b \right)$. For transitivity, $\left( a, \; b \right) \; \in \; R$ and $\left( b, \; c \right) \; \in \; R \; \implies \; \left( a, \; c \right) \; \in \; R$, and by symmetry we must also add $\left( c, \; a \right)$. Furthermore, by transitivity on symmetric pairs: $\left( a, \; b \right), \; \left( b, \; a \right) \; \in \; R \; \implies \; \left( a, \; a \right) \; \in \; R$; $\left( b, \; c \right), \; \left( c, \; b \right) \; \in \; R \; \implies \; \left( b, \; b \right) \; \in \; R$; and $\left( c, \; b \right), \; \left( b, \; c \right) \; \in \; R \; \implies \; \left( c, \; c \right) \; \in \; R$. Thus, the $7$ elements to be added are $\left\{ \left( b, \; a \right), \; \left( c, \; b \right), \; \left( a, \; c \right), \; \left( c, \; a \right), \; \left( a, \; a \right), \; \left( b, \; b \right), \; \left( c, \; c \right) \right\}$.

questions.text: If the equation $a(b-c)x^{2}+b(c-a)x+c(a-b)=0$ has equal roots, where $a+c=15$ and $b=\frac{36}{5}$, then $a^{2}+c^{2}$ is equal to
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Check whether $x=1$ is a root; if it is, both equal roots equal $1$ and their sum is $2$. // 📝 Solution: $a(b-c)+b(c-a)+c(a-b)=0$ so $x=1$ is a root $\implies$ sum of roots $=-\frac{b(c-a)}{a(b-c)}=2$ $\implies 2ac=b(a+c)=\frac{36}{5}\cdot15=108$ $\implies ac=54$ $\implies a^{2}+c^{2}=(a+c)^{2}-2ac=225-108=117$
questions.topic: Quadratic with equal roots and coefficient relations

questions.text: The sum of the squares of the roots of $\left\lvert x+2\right\rvert^{2}+\left\lvert x-2\right\rvert-2=0$ and the squares of the roots of $x^{2}-2\left\lvert x-3\right\rvert-5=0$, is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: the key requires $\left\lvert x-2\right\rvert^{2}$ in the first equation (source prints $\left\lvert x+2\right\rvert^{2}$) // 📝 Solution: $(\left\lvert x-2\right\rvert+2)(\left\lvert x-2\right\rvert-1)=0\implies x\in\{1,3\}$, squares sum $10$; $x^{2}-2\left\lvert x-3\right\rvert-5=0\implies x=-1\pm2\sqrt3$, squares sum $26$; total $36$
questions.topic: Equations with modulus and sum of squares of roots

questions.text: The product of all the rational roots of the equation $\left(x^{2}-9x+11\right)^{2}-(x-4)(x-5)=3$, is equal to
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Put $t=x^{2}-9x+11$ and note that $(x-4)(x-5)=t+9$. // 📝 Solution: $t^{2}-(t+9)=3 \implies t^{2}-t-12=0 \implies t=4,\,-3$ $\implies t=-3: x^{2}-9x+14=0 \implies x=2,7$ $\implies t=4$ gives irrational roots $\implies$ product of rational roots $=2\times7=14$
questions.topic: Equations reducible to quadratic, rational roots

questions.text: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be the roots of $x^{2}+\sqrt{3}x-16=0$, and $\gamma$ and $\delta$ be the roots of $x^{2}+3x-1=0$. If $P_{n}=\alpha^{n}+\beta^{n}$ and $Q_{n}=\gamma^{n}+\delta^{n}$, then $\dfrac{P_{25}+\sqrt{3}P_{24}}{2P_{23}}+\dfrac{Q_{25}-Q_{23}}{Q_{24}}$ is equal to
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: each root satisfies its quadratic, so $P_{n}=-\sqrt{3}P_{n-1}+16P_{n-2}$ and $\gamma^{2}-1=-3\gamma$ // 📝 Solution: $P_{25}+\sqrt{3}P_{24}=16P_{23}\implies\dfrac{P_{25}+\sqrt{3}P_{24}}{2P_{23}}=8$; $Q_{25}-Q_{23}=-3Q_{24}\implies\dfrac{Q_{25}-Q_{23}}{Q_{24}}=-3$; total $=5$

questions.text: Consider the equation $x^{2}+4x-n=0$, where $n\in[20,100]$ is a natural number. Then the number of all distinct values of $n$, for which the given equation has integral roots, is equal to
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: complete the square, $(x+2)^{2}=n+4$, so $n+4$ must be a perfect square // 📝 Solution: $n+4\in[24,104]\cap\{k^{2}\}=\{25,36,49,64,81,100\}\implies n\in\{21,32,45,60,77,96\}$; $6$ values

questions.text: Let $P_{n}=\alpha^{n}+\beta^{n}$, $n\in\mathbf{N}$. If $P_{10}=123$, $P_{9}=76$, $P_{8}=47$ and $P_{1}=1$, then the quadratic equation having roots $\dfrac{1}{\alpha}$ and $\dfrac{1}{\beta}$ is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $P_{10}=P_{9}+P_{8}$ means $\alpha,\beta$ are roots of $x^{2}=x+1$ // 📝 Solution: $\alpha+\beta=1,\ \alpha\beta=-1\implies\dfrac1\alpha+\dfrac1\beta=\dfrac{\alpha+\beta}{\alpha\beta}=-1,\ \dfrac{1}{\alpha\beta}=-1\implies x^{2}+x-1=0$

questions.text: If the set of all $a\in\mathbb{R}$, for which the equation $2x^{2}+(a-5)x+15=3a$ has no real root, is the interval $(\alpha,\beta)$, and $X=\{x\in\mathbb{Z}:\alpha<x<\beta\}$, then $\sum_{x\in X}x^{2}$ is equal to :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: No real root means discriminant is negative; then sum squares of integers in the resulting range. // 📝 Solution: $D=(a-5)^{2}-8(15-3a)<0 \implies a^{2}+14a-95<0 \implies (a+19)(a-5)<0$ $\implies (\alpha,\beta)=(-19,5)$ $\implies X=\{-18,\ldots,4\}$ $\implies \sum x^{2}=\frac{18\cdot19\cdot37}{6}+\frac{4\cdot5\cdot9}{6}=2109+30=2139$
questions.topic: Discriminant condition and sum of squares of integers

questions.text: For $t>-1$, let $\alpha_t$ and $\beta_t$ be the roots of $\left((t+2)^{\frac17}-1\right)x^{2}+\left((t+2)^{\frac16}-1\right)x+\left((t+2)^{\frac1{21}}-1\right)=0$. If $\lim\limits_{t\to-1^{+}}\alpha_t=a$ and $\lim\limits_{t\to-1^{+}}\beta_t=b$, then $72(a+b)^{2}$ is equal to
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\alpha_t+\beta_t=-\dfrac{B}{A}$, and $\dfrac{y^{k}-1}{y^{m}-1}\to\dfrac{k}{m}$ as $y\to1$ // 📝 Solution: $a+b=\lim(\alpha_t+\beta_t)=-\dfrac{1/6}{1/7}=-\dfrac76\implies 72(a+b)^{2}=72\cdot\dfrac{49}{36}=98$
questions.topic: Limits of roots and sum of roots

questions.text: The sum, of the squares of all the roots of the equation $x^{2}+\left\lvert 2x-3 \right\rvert-4=0$, is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Split the modulus into the cases $x\ge\frac{3}{2}$ and $x<\frac{3}{2}$ and keep only admissible roots. // 📝 Solution: $x\ge\frac{3}{2}$: $x^{2}+2x-7=0 \implies x=2\sqrt{2}-1$ $\implies$ $x<\frac{3}{2}$: $x^{2}-2x-1=0 \implies x=1-\sqrt{2}$ $\implies \text{Sum of squares} \;=\; (2\sqrt{2}-1)^{2}+(1-\sqrt{2})^{2} \;=\; 12-6\sqrt{2} \;=\; 6(2-\sqrt{2})$
questions.topic: Modulus equations and sum of squares of roots

questions.text: Let $\alpha_\theta$ and $\beta_\theta$ be the distinct roots of $2x^{2}+(\cos\theta)x-1=0$, $\theta\in(0,2\pi)$. If $m$ and $M$ are the minimum and the maximum values of $\alpha_\theta^{4}+\beta_\theta^{4}$, then $16(M+m)$ equals :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Express $\alpha^{4}+\beta^{4}$ through $\alpha+\beta$ and $\alpha\beta$, then vary $\cos^{2}\theta\in[0,1]$. // 📝 Solution: $\alpha+\beta=-\frac{\cos\theta}{2}$, $\alpha\beta=-\frac{1}{2}$ $\implies \alpha^{2}+\beta^{2}=1+\frac{\cos^{2}\theta}{4}$ $\implies \alpha^{4}+\beta^{4}=\left(1+\frac{\cos^{2}\theta}{4}\right)^{2}-\frac{1}{2}$ $\implies M=\frac{17}{16},\; m=\frac{1}{2}$ $\implies 16(M+m)=17+8=25$
questions.topic: Symmetric functions of roots with trigonometric parameter

questions.text: Let the set of all values of $p\in\mathbb{R}$, for which both roots of $x^{2}-(p+2)x+(2p+9)=0$ are negative real numbers, be the interval $(\alpha,\beta]$. Then $\beta-2\alpha$ is equal to
