questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Lower (more negative) the standard reduction potential, stronger is the reducing agent. // 📝 Solution: Since $E^\circ_{\text{red}}$ increases in the order $\text{Al}^{3+}/\text{Al}\;\left(-1.66\;\text{V}\right) \;<\; \text{Cr}^{3+}/\text{Cr}\;\left(-0.74\;\text{V}\right) \;<\; \text{Fe}^{3+}/\text{Fe}^{2+}\;\left(+0.77\;\text{V}\right) \;<\; \text{Co}^{3+}/\text{Co}^{2+}\;\left(+1.81\;\text{V}\right)$, the reducing power of the reduced species decreases as $\text{Al} \;>\; \text{Cr} \;>\; \text{Fe}^{2+} \;>\; \text{Co}^{2+}$.

questions.text: For a closed circuit Daniell cell, which of the following plots is the accurate one at a given temperature?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Standard cell potential $\left(E^\circ_{\text{cell}}\right)$ is a constant thermodynamic property at a given temperature. // 📝 Solution: $E^\circ_{\text{cell}} \;=\; E^\circ_{\text{Cu}^{2+}/\text{Cu}} \;-\; E^\circ_{\text{Zn}^{2+}/\text{Zn}}$ depends only on temperature and the nature of species, remaining constant with time. Thus, the plot of $E^\circ_{\text{cell}}$ vs time is a horizontal straight line parallel to the time axis.

questions.text: For the cell reaction $Fe^{2+}\left(aq\right)+Ag^{+}\left(aq\right)\;\rightarrow\;Fe^{3+}\left(aq\right)+Ag\left(s\right)$, the standard cell potential is [Given: $Ag^{+}+e^-\rightarrow Ag$, $E^{\theta}=x\,V$; $Fe^{2+}+2e^-\rightarrow Fe$, $E^{\theta}=y\,V$; $Fe^{3+}+3e^-\rightarrow Fe$, $E^{\theta}=z\,V$]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Get $E^{\circ}\left(Fe^{3+}/Fe^{2+}\right)$ from Gibbs energies of the two Fe half reactions. // 📝 Solution: $-3Fz+2Fy\;=\;-FE\;\implies\;E_{Fe^{3+}/Fe^{2+}}\;=\;3z-2y\;\implies\;E^{\circ}_{cell}\;=\;x-\left(3z-2y\right)\;=\;x+2y-3z$

questions.text: Match List - I with List - II. List - I (Applications): (A) Transistors (B) Hearing aids (C) Invertors (D) Apollo space ship. List - II (Batteries/Cell): (I) Anode - $Zn/Hg$; Cathode - $HgO+C$ (II) Hydrogen fuel cell (III) Anode - $Zn$; Cathode - Carbon (IV) Anode - $Pb$; Cathode - $Pb\mid PbO_2$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall the practical battery used in each device. // 📝 Solution: Transistors $\implies$ dry cell $Zn$/C (III); hearing aids $\implies$ mercury cell (I); invertors $\implies$ lead storage (IV); Apollo $\implies$ $H_2$-$O_2$ fuel cell (II)

questions.text: One Faraday of electricity liberates $x \;\times\; 10^{-1}$ gram atom of copper from copper sulphate, $x$ is _______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $1\;\text{Faraday}$ deposits $1\;\text{gram equivalent}$ of an ion; for $\text{Cu}^{2+}$, $1\;\text{eq} \;=\; 0.5\;\text{mol}$. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Cu}^{2+} \;+\; 2\text{e}^- \;\rightarrow\; \text{Cu} \;\implies\; 2\;\text{F}$ liberates $1\;\text{mol}$ (gram atom) of $\text{Cu} \;\implies\; 1\;\text{F}$ liberates $0.5\;\text{gram atom} \;=\; 5 \;\times\; 10^{-1}\;\text{gram atom} \;\implies\; x \;=\; 5$.

questions.text: Molar ionic conductivities of divalent cation and anion are $57\;\text{S}\;\text{cm}^2\;\text{mol}^{-1}$ and $73\;\text{S}\;\text{cm}^2\;\text{mol}^{-1}$ respectively. The molar conductivity of solution of an electrolyte with the above cation and anion will be:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For a $1:1$ divalent electrolyte $\left(\text{C}^{2+}\text{A}^{2-}\right)$, $\Lambda_m \;=\; \lambda^\circ_{\text{C}^{2+}} \;+\; \lambda^\circ_{\text{A}^{2-}}$. // 📝 Solution: $\Lambda_m \;=\; \lambda^{2+}_{\text{C}} \;+\; \lambda^{2-}_{\text{A}} \;=\; 57 \;+\; 73 \;=\; 130\;\text{S}\;\text{cm}^2\;\text{mol}^{-1}$.

questions.text: Based on the data: $E^{\circ}_{Cr_2O_7^{2-}/Cr^{3+}}\;=\;1.33\;V$, $E^{\circ}_{Cl_2/Cl^-}\;=\;1.36\;V$, $E^{\circ}_{MnO_4^-/Mn^{2+}}\;=\;1.51\;V$, $E^{\circ}_{Cr^{3+}/Cr}\;=\;-0.74\;V$, the strongest reducing agent is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The strongest reducing agent has the most negative reduction potential. // 📝 Solution: $E^{\circ}_{Cr^{3+}/Cr}\;=\;-0.74\;V\;$ is the lowest $\implies\;Cr$ is the strongest reducing agent
questions.topic: Reducing and oxidising strength from E°

questions.text: Molar conductivity of a weak acid $\text{HQ}$ of concentration $0.18\;\text{M}$ was found to be $1/30$ of the molar conductivity of another weak acid $\text{HZ}$ with concentration of $0.02\;\text{M}$. If $\lambda^\circ_{\text{Q}^-}$ happened to be equal with $\lambda^\circ_{\text{Z}^-}$, then the difference of the $\text{p}K_a$ values of the two weak acids $\left(\text{p}K_a\left(\text{HQ}\right) \;-\; \text{p}K_a\left(\text{HZ}\right)\right)$ is _______ (Nearest integer). [Given: degree of dissociation $\left(\alpha\right) \;\ll\; 1$ for both weak acids, $\lambda^\circ$: limiting molar conductivity of ions]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Since $\lambda^\circ_{\text{Q}^-} \;=\; \lambda^\circ_{\text{Z}^-}$, both acids have the same $\Lambda^\circ_m$, so $\frac{\Lambda_m\left(\text{HQ}\right)}{\Lambda_m\left(\text{HZ}\right)} \;=\; \frac{\alpha_{\text{HQ}}}{\alpha_{\text{HZ}}}$; then use $K_a \;=\; C\alpha^2$. // 📝 Solution: $\Lambda^\circ_m\left(\text{HQ}\right) \;=\; \Lambda^\circ_m\left(\text{HZ}\right) \;\implies\; \frac{\alpha_{\text{HQ}}}{\alpha_{\text{HZ}}} \;=\; \frac{\Lambda_m\left(\text{HQ}\right)}{\Lambda_m\left(\text{HZ}\right)} \;=\; \frac{1}{30} \;\implies\; \frac{K_a\left(\text{HZ}\right)}{K_a\left(\text{HQ}\right)} \;=\; \frac{C_{\text{HZ}}\;\alpha_{\text{HZ}}^2}{C_{\text{HQ}}\;\alpha_{\text{HQ}}^2} \;=\; \frac{0.02}{0.18} \;\times\; \left(30\right)^2 \;=\; \frac{1}{9} \;\times\; 900 \;=\; 100 \;\implies\; \text{p}K_a\left(\text{HQ}\right) \;-\; \text{p}K_a\left(\text{HZ}\right) \;=\; \log\left(100\right) \;=\; 2$.

questions.text: Given below is the plot of molar conductivity $\Lambda_m$ vs $\sqrt{c}$ for $KCl$ in aqueous solution. [FIGURE] If, for the higher concentration of $KCl$ solution, the resistance of the conductivity cell is $100\;\Omega$, then the resistance of the same cell with the dilute solution is $x\;\Omega$. The value of $x$ is ______ (nearest integer).
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Same cell constant gives $\frac{R_d}{R_c}\;=\;\frac{\kappa_c}{\kappa_d}$ with $\kappa\;\propto\;\Lambda_m\,c$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{R_d}{R_c}\;=\;\frac{\Lambda_c\,c_c}{\Lambda_d\,c_d}\;=\;\frac{100\times0.15^2}{150\times0.1^2}\;=\;1.5\;\implies\;R_d\;=\;150\;\Omega$
questions.topic: Conductivity cell and molar conductivity graph

questions.text: A conductivity cell with two electrodes (dark side) are half filled with infinitely dilute aqueous solution of a weak electrolyte. If volume is doubled by adding more water at constant temperature, the molar conductivity of the cell will - [FIGURE]

options.text: remain same or can not be measured accurately

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: At infinite dilution, an electrolyte is already $100\%$ dissociated and $\Lambda_m$ has reached its maximum limiting value $\Lambda^\circ_m$. // 📝 Solution: Since the solution is already infinitely dilute, further addition of water causes no change in molar conductivity (or cannot be measured accurately due to extremely low specific conductance).

questions.text: Which of the following statements is not correct about rusting of iron?

options.text: Coating of iron surface by tin prevents rusting, even if the tin coating is peeling off.
When $\text{pH}$ lies above $9$ or $10$, rusting of iron does not take place.
Dissolved acidic oxides $\text{SO}_2,\; \text{NO}_2$ in water act as catalyst in the process of rusting.
Rusting of iron is envisaged as setting up of electrochemical cell on the surface of iron object.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Compare the standard reduction potentials of iron and tin to see which corrodes if the coating breaks. // 📝 Solution: Tin ($\text{Sn}$) is less electropositive (has higher $E^\circ_{\text{red}}$) than iron ($\text{Fe}$). If the tin coating peels off, iron is exposed to the atmosphere and acts as the anode, rusting even faster.

questions.text: Electrolysis of $600\;mL$ aqueous solution of $NaCl$ for $5\;min$ changes the pH of the solution to $12$. The current in amperes used for the given electrolysis is ______ (nearest integer).
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $OH^-$ formed at the cathode equals the charge passed divided by $F$. // 📝 Solution: $\left[OH^-\right]\;=\;10^{-2}\;\implies\;n\;=\;10^{-2}\times0.6\;=\;6\times10^{-3}\;mol\;\implies\;I\;=\;\frac{6\times10^{-3}\times96500}{300}\;=\;1.93\;\approx\;2\;A$
questions.topic: Electrolysis of brine and pH change

questions.text: The molar conductivity of a weak electrolyte when plotted against the square root of its concentration, which of the following is expected to be observed?

options.text: A small decrease in molar conductivity is observed at infinite dilution
Molar conductivity decreases sharply with increase in concentration
A small increase in molar conductivity is observed at infinite dilution
Molar conductivity increases sharply with increase in concentration

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Dilution increases the degree of dissociation of a weak electrolyte. // 📝 Solution: $\alpha\;\uparrow$ as $c\;\downarrow\;\implies\;\Lambda_m$ rises steeply on dilution, i.e. $\Lambda_m$ falls sharply with increasing $\sqrt{c}$

questions.text: Following figure shows dependence of molar conductance of two electrolytes on concentration. $\Lambda^\circ_m$ is the limiting molar conductivity. [FIGURE] The number of Incorrect statement(s) from the following is _______: (A) $\Lambda^\circ_m$ for electrolyte $\text{A}$ is obtained by extrapolation (B) For electrolyte $\text{B}$, $\Lambda_m$ vs $\sqrt{c}$ graph is a straight line with intercept equal to $\Lambda^\circ_m$ (C) At infinite dilution, the value of degree of dissociation approaches zero for electrolyte $\text{B}$. (D) $\Lambda^\circ_m$ for any electrolyte $\text{A}$ or $\text{B}$ can be calculated using $\lambda^\circ$ for individual ions.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Identify $\text{A}$ as a weak electrolyte and $\text{B}$ as a strong electrolyte from the Debye-Huckel-Onsager plot. // 📝 Solution: Electrolyte $\text{A}$ is a weak electrolyte, so its $\Lambda^\circ_m$ cannot be obtained by extrapolation (Statement A is incorrect). At infinite dilution, the degree of dissociation $\left(\alpha\right)$ approaches $1$, not zero (Statement C is incorrect). Thus, $2$ statements (A and C) are incorrect.

questions.text: For a strong electrolyte, a plot of molar conductivity against $\left(\text{concentration}\right)^{1/2}$ is a straight line, with a negative slope, the correct unit for the slope is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: From $\Lambda_m \;=\; \Lambda^\circ_m \;-\; A\sqrt{C}$, the unit of $A\sqrt{C}$ must match the unit of $\Lambda_m$. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Unit of } A \;=\; \frac{\text{Unit of }\Lambda_m}{\text{Unit of }C^{1/2}} \;=\; \frac{\text{S}\;\text{cm}^2\;\text{mol}^{-1}}{\left(\text{mol}\;\text{L}^{-1}\right)^{1/2}} \;=\; \text{S}\;\text{cm}^2\;\text{mol}^{-3/2}\;\text{L}^{1/2}$.

questions.text: Identify the factor from the following that does not affect electrolytic conductance of a solution.

options.text: The nature of the electrolyte added.
The nature of the electrode used.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Electrolytic conductance depends on ion mobility and ion concentration, not on the metallic electrodes. // 📝 Solution: Electrolytic conductance of a solution depends on the nature and concentration of the electrolyte, nature of the solvent (viscosity, dielectric constant), and temperature, but does not depend on the nature of the electrode used.

questions.text: The number of pairs of solutions having the same value of osmotic pressure from the following is ____. (Assume 100% ionization) A. $0.500\;\text{M}$ $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$ (aq) and $0.25\;\text{M}$ KBr (aq). B. $0.100\;\text{M}$ $\text{K}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]$ (aq) and $0.100\;\text{M}$ $\text{FeSO}_4(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4$ (aq). C. $0.05\;\text{M}$ $\text{K}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]$ (aq) and $0.25\;\text{M}$ NaCl (aq). D. $0.15\;\text{M}$ NaCl (aq) and $0.1\;\text{M}$ $\text{BaCl}_2$ (aq). E. $0.02\;\text{M}$ KCl$\cdot$MgCl$_2\cdot$6H$_2$O (aq) and $0.05\;\text{M}$ KCl (aq).
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Osmotic pressure is $\pi = iCRT$, so compare the total ion concentration $iC$ of each solution. // 📝 Solution: $\pi \propto iC$; solutions A, B, D and E share the same osmotic pressure $\implies$ count of pairs = 4 (as per official NTA key).
questions.topic: Van't Hoff factor and osmotic pressure

questions.text: The total pressure of a mixture of non-reacting gases X ($0.6\;\text{g}$) and Y ($0.45\;\text{g}$) in a vessel is $740\;\text{mm Hg}$. The partial pressure of gas X is ____ mm Hg (nearest integer). Given molar mass of X $= 20\;\text{g mol}^{-1}$ and of Y $= 45\;\text{g mol}^{-1}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Partial pressure $P_X = x_X P_{\text{total}}$ with $x_X$ the mole fraction. // 📝 Solution: $n_X = \dfrac{0.6}{20} = 0.03$, $n_Y = \dfrac{0.45}{45} = 0.01$ $\implies x_X = \dfrac{0.03}{0.04} = 0.75 \implies P_X = 0.75 \times 740 = 555\;\text{mm Hg}$.

questions.text: The solution from the following with highest depression in freezing point / lowest freezing point is:

options.text: 180 g of acetic acid dissolved in water
180 g of acetic acid dissolved in benzene
180 g of benzoic acid dissolved in benzene
180 g of glucose dissolved in water

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The largest depression needs the largest $i\,K_f\,m$ // 📝 Solution: $\Delta T_f = i\,K_f\,m \implies$ option A gives the largest depression (key answer)

questions.text: A solution is prepared by adding $1$ mole of ethyl alcohol in $9$ moles of water. The mass percent of solute in the solution is ____ (integer). Given molar masses: ethyl alcohol $= 46\;\text{g mol}^{-1}$, water $= 18\;\text{g mol}^{-1}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Mass percent equals mass of solute divided by total mass of solution, times 100. // 📝 Solution: $\dfrac{1 \times 46}{1 \times 46 + 9 \times 18} \times 100 = \dfrac{4600}{208} \approx 22.1 \implies 22$.

questions.text: One mole of volatile liquid A is mixed with 3 moles of volatile liquid B. The vapour pressure of pure A is 200 mm Hg and that of the solution is 500 mm Hg. The vapour pressure of pure B and the least volatile component of the solution, respectively, are:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Apply Raoult's law: $P_s = P_A^\circ x_A + P_B^\circ x_B$. // 📝 Solution: $x_A=\tfrac14$, $x_B=\tfrac34$ $\implies$ $500 = 200\left(\tfrac14\right) + P_B^\circ\left(\tfrac34\right)$ $\implies$ $P_B^\circ = 600\,\text{mmHg}$; the lower $P^\circ$ (A) is least volatile $\implies$ D.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (A) Solution of chloroform and acetone, (B) Solution of ethanol and water, (C) Solution of benzene and toluene, (D) Solution of acetic acid in benzene. List-II: (I) Minimum boiling azeotrope, (II) Dimerizes, (III) Maximum boiling azeotrope, (IV) $\Delta V_{mix}=0$. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Chloroform–acetone shows negative deviation (maximum boiling); ethanol–water shows positive deviation (minimum boiling). // 📝 Solution: (A)→III, (B)→I; benzene–toluene is ideal so $\Delta V_{mix}=0$ (C)→IV; acetic acid dimerises in benzene (D)→II $\implies$ option (1).

questions.text: The total pressure of a mixture of two liquids A and B is $350\;\text{mm Hg}$ when their mole fractions are $0.7$ and $0.3$ respectively. It becomes $410\;\text{mm Hg}$ when the mole fractions are changed to $0.2$ and $0.8$ respectively for A and B. The vapour pressure of pure A is ____ mm Hg (nearest integer). Consider ideal behaviour.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Apply Raoult's law for an ideal binary solution, $P_{\text{total}} = P_A^0 x_A + P_B^0 x_B$. // 📝 Solution: $0.7P_A^0 + 0.3P_B^0 = 350$ and $0.2P_A^0 + 0.8P_B^0 = 410$ $\implies$ $P_A^0 = 314\;\text{mm Hg}$ and $P_B^0 = 434\;\text{mm Hg}$.

questions.text: At $T\;\text{K}$, $100\;\text{g}$ of $98\%$ $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ (w/w) aqueous solution is mixed with $100\;\text{g}$ of $49\%$ $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ (w/w) aqueous solution. What is the mole fraction of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ in the resultant solution? (Atomic mass H = 1 u, S = 32 u, O = 16 u; assume temperature remains constant after mixing)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Total moles of acid and water are needed after mixing // 📝 Solution: $n_{\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4} = \dfrac{98}{98} + \dfrac{49}{98} = 1.5$, $n_{\text{water}} = \dfrac{2 + 51}{18} = 2.944 \implies x = \dfrac{1.5}{1.5 + 2.944} = 0.337$
questions.topic: Mole fraction after mixing acid solutions

questions.text: Considering acetic acid dissociates in water, its dissociation constant is $6.25 \times 10^{-5}$. If $5\;\text{mL}$ of acetic acid is dissolved in $1$ litre of water, the solution will freeze at $-x \times 10^{-2}\;^\circ\text{C}$, provided pure water freezes at $0\;^\circ\text{C}$. $x = $ ____ (nearest integer). Given $K_f$ of water $= 1.86\;\text{K kg mol}^{-1}$, density of acetic acid $= 1.2\;\text{g mL}^{-1}$, molar mass of water $= 18\;\text{g mol}^{-1}$, molar mass of acetic acid $= 60\;\text{g mol}^{-1}$, density of water $= 1\;\text{g cm}^{-3}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For a weak acid, $\alpha = \sqrt{K_a/C}$ and $i = 1 + \alpha(n-1)$. // 📝 Solution: $C = \dfrac{6/60}{1} = 0.1\;\text{M} \implies \alpha = \sqrt{\dfrac{6.25 \times 10^{-5}}{0.1}} = 0.025 \implies i = 1.025$ $\implies \Delta T_f = 1.025 \times 1.86 \times 0.1 = 0.19\;^\circ\text{C} = 19 \times 10^{-2}\;^\circ\text{C}$.
questions.topic: Depression of freezing point of weak acid

questions.text: Two liquids A and B form an ideal solution at temperature $T\;\text{K}$. At $T\;\text{K}$, the vapour pressures of pure A and B are $55$ and $15\;\text{kN m}^{-2}$ respectively. What is the mole fraction of A in solution of A and B in equilibrium with a vapour in which the mole fraction of A is $0.8$?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Apply Raoult's law to both components and set $y_A = 0.8$ // 📝 Solution: $0.8 = \dfrac{55x_A}{55x_A + 15(1 - x_A)} \implies 12 = 23x_A \implies x_A = 0.5217$

questions.text: The osmotic pressure of a living cell is $12\;\text{atm}$ at $300\;\text{K}$. The strength of sodium chloride solution that is isotonic with the living cell at this temperature is ____ $\text{g L}^{-1}$ (nearest integer). [Given: $R = 0.08\;\text{L atm K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$; assume complete dissociation of NaCl; molar masses Na $= 23$, Cl $= 35.5\;\text{g mol}^{-1}$]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For NaCl, $i = 2$ under complete dissociation // 📝 Solution: $\pi = i\,M\,R\,T \implies 12 = 2 \times M \times 0.08 \times 300 \implies M = 0.25 \implies 0.25 \times 58.5 = 14.6 \approx 15\;\text{g L}^{-1}$

questions.text: A solution is prepared by dissolving $0.3\;\text{g}$ of a non-volatile non-electrolyte solute 'A' of molar mass $60\;\text{g mol}^{-1}$ and $0.9\;\text{g}$ of a non-volatile non-electrolyte solute 'B' of molar mass $180\;\text{g mol}^{-1}$ in $100\;\text{mL}$ $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ at $27\;^\circ\text{C}$. Osmotic pressure of the solution will be: [Given: $R = 0.082\;\text{L atm K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Total moles of solute add up for non-electrolytes // 📝 Solution: $n_{\text{total}} = 0.005 + 0.005 = 0.01 \implies \pi = \dfrac{0.01 \times 0.082 \times 300}{0.1} = 2.46\;\text{atm}$

questions.text: The vapour pressure of pure benzene and methylbenzene at $27\;^\circ\text{C}$ is $80$ Torr and $24$ Torr respectively. The mole fraction of methylbenzene in the vapour phase, in equilibrium with an equimolar mixture of those two liquids (ideal solution) at the same temperature, is ____ $\times 10^{-2}$ (nearest integer).
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use Raoult's law for each component and Dalton's law for the vapour phase mole fraction. // 📝 Solution: $P_{\text{total}} = 0.5 \times 80 + 0.5 \times 24 = 52\;\text{Torr} \implies y_{\text{methylbenzene}} = \dfrac{0.5 \times 24}{52} = 0.23 = 23 \times 10^{-2}$.
questions.topic: Raoult's law and vapour phase composition

questions.text: Statement I: The Henry's law constant $K_H$ is constant with respect to variations in solution's concentration over the range for which the solution is ideally dilute. Statement II: $K_H$ does not differ for the same solute in different solvents. Choose the correct answer.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $K_H$ depends on the solute, solvent and temperature // 📝 Solution: Statement I holds for dilute solutions; Statement II fails because $K_H$ varies with solvent $\implies$ option C

questions.text: Evaluate the following statements for their correctness. A. The elevation in boiling point of water will be same for $0.1\;\text{M}$ NaCl and $0.1\;\text{M}$ urea. B. Azeotropic mixtures boil without change in their composition. C. Osmosis always takes place from hypertonic to hypotonic solution. D. The density of $32\%$ $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ solution having molarity $4.09\;\text{M}$ is approximately $1.26\;\text{g mL}^{-1}$. E. A negatively charged sol is obtained when KI solution is added to silver nitrate solution. Choose the correct answer.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Check each statement against colligative properties, azeotropes, osmosis, molarity-density relation and colloid charge. // 📝 Solution: A is false (NaCl has $i \approx 2$), B is true, C is false (osmosis goes hypotonic to hypertonic), D is true ($M \approx 10 \times 1.26 \times 32/98 \approx 4.1\;\text{M}$), E is false (positive sol with excess AgNO$_3$) $\implies$ B and D only.

questions.text: A solution of two miscible liquids showing negative deviation from Raoult's law will have:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Negative deviation means stronger solute-solvent attraction, which lowers vapour pressure. // 📝 Solution: $P_{\text{total}} < P_A^0 x_A + P_B^0 x_B \implies$ vapour pressure decreases $\implies$ boiling point increases $\implies$ option D.

questions.text: The molarity of an aqueous solution containing $5.85\;\text{g}$ of NaCl in $500\;\text{mL}$ water is: (Given molar mass of Na $= 23$ and Cl $= 35.5\;\text{g mol}^{-1}$).
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Molarity equals moles of solute per litre of solution. // 📝 Solution: $n = \dfrac{5.85}{58.5} = 0.1 \implies M = \dfrac{0.1}{0.5} = 0.2\;\text{M}$.

questions.text: The freezing point depression of a 0.1 m aqueous solution of a monobasic weak acid HA is 0.20 °C. The dissociation constant of the acid is (Given $K_f(\text{H}_2\text{O}) = 1.8\,\text{K kg mol}^{-1}$; molality $\equiv$ molarity):
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\Delta T_f = i\,K_f\,m$ gives $i$, and then $\alpha = i-1$. // 📝 Solution: $i = \dfrac{0.2}{1.8\times0.1} = \dfrac{10}{9}$ $\implies$ $\alpha = \dfrac{1}{9}$ $\implies$ $K_a = \dfrac{C\alpha^2}{1-\alpha} = \dfrac{0.1/81}{8/9} = \dfrac{1}{720}\approx1.38\times10^{-3}$.

questions.text: An artificial cell is made by encapsulating $0.2\;\text{M}$ glucose solution within a semipermeable membrane. The osmotic pressure developed when the artificial cell is placed within a $0.05\;\text{M}$ NaCl solution at $300\;\text{K}$ is ____ $\times 10^{-1}$ bar (nearest integer). Given $R = 0.083\;\text{L bar K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$. Assume complete dissociation of NaCl.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Net osmotic pressure equals the difference of total particle concentrations times $RT$. // 📝 Solution: $C_{\text{NaCl, ions}} = 2 \times 0.05 = 0.1\;\text{M} \implies \Delta\pi = (0.2 - 0.1) \times 0.083 \times 300 = 2.49\;\text{bar} = 24.9 \times 10^{-1}\;\text{bar} \approx 25 \times 10^{-1}\;\text{bar}$.

questions.text: A $300\;\text{mL}$ bottle of soft drink has $0.2\;\text{M}$ $\text{CO}_2$ dissolved in it. Assuming $\text{CO}_2$ behaves as an ideal gas, the volume of the dissolved $\text{CO}_2$ at STP is ____ mL (nearest integer). Given molar volume of an ideal gas at STP is $22.7\;\text{L mol}^{-1}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Moles equal molarity times volume in litres; volume at STP equals moles times molar volume. // 📝 Solution: $n = 0.2 \times 300 \times 10^{-3} = 0.06\;\text{mol} \implies V = 0.06 \times 22.7 = 1.362\;\text{L} = 1362\;\text{mL}$.
questions.topic: Molarity and gas volume at STP

questions.text: At $298\;\text{K}$, the mole percentage of $\text{N}_2(g)$ in air is $80\%$. Water is in equilibrium with air at a pressure of $10\;\text{atm}$. What is the mole fraction of $\text{N}_2(g)$ in water at $298\;\text{K}$? ($K_H$ for $\text{N}_2$ is $6.5 \times 10^7\;\text{mmHg}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use Henry's law with the partial pressure of $\text{N}_2$ // 📝 Solution: $p = 0.8 \times 10\;\text{atm} = 6080\;\text{mmHg} \implies x = \dfrac{6080}{6.5 \times 10^7} = 9.35 \times 10^{-5}$
questions.topic: Henry's law mole fraction of a gas in water

questions.text: The osmotic pressure of solutions of PVC in cyclohexanone at $300\;\text{K}$ is plotted on the graph shown, with concentration $C$ in $\text{g L}^{-1}$ on the x-axis. The molar mass of PVC is ____ $\text{g mol}^{-1}$ (nearest integer). Given $R = 0.083\;\text{L atm K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Osmotic pressure of a polymer solution gives $\dfrac{\pi}{C} = \dfrac{RT}{M}$, so the slope gives molar mass. // 📝 Solution: $\pi = \dfrac{W}{V}\cdot\dfrac{RT}{M} = CRT/M \implies \text{slope} = \dfrac{RT}{M} = \dfrac{0.083 \times 300}{M} = 6 \times 10^{-4} \implies M = 41500\;\text{g mol}^{-1}$.
questions.topic: Osmotic pressure and molar mass of polymers

questions.text: When $x \times 10^{-2}\;\text{mL}$ of methanol (molar mass $= 32\;\text{g mol}^{-1}$, density $= 0.792\;\text{g cm}^{-3}$) is added to $100\;\text{mL}$ of water (density $= 1\;\text{g cm}^{-3}$), the diagram shown is obtained. $x = $ ____ (nearest integer). Given molal freezing point depression constant of water is $1.86\;\text{K kg mol}^{-1}$. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: From the diagram, $\Delta T_f = 273.15 - 270.65$; use $\Delta T_f = K_f m$ to get moles of methanol. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta T_f = 2.5\;\text{K} \implies m = \dfrac{2.5}{1.86} \implies n = 0.1344\;\text{mol} \implies w = 0.1344 \times 32 = 4.3\;\text{g} \implies V = \dfrac{4.3}{0.792} = 5.43\;\text{mL} = 543 \times 10^{-2}\;\text{mL}$.
questions.topic: Freezing point depression and volume of solution

questions.text: $W\;\text{g}$ of a non-volatile electrolyte solid solute of molar mass $M\;\text{g mol}^{-1}$, when dissolved in $100\;\text{mL}$ water, decreases vapour pressure of water from $640\;\text{mmHg}$ to $600\;\text{mmHg}$. If the aqueous solution boils at $375\;\text{K}$ and $K_b$ for water is $0.52\;\text{K kg mol}^{-1}$, the mole fraction of the electrolyte solute ($x_2$) can be expressed as: [Given: density of water $= 1\;\text{g mL}^{-1}$; boiling point of water $= 373\;\text{K}$]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use relative lowering for $i\,x_2$ and boiling elevation for $i$ // 📝 Solution: $i\,x_2 = \dfrac{40}{640} = \dfrac{1}{16}$, $\Delta T_b = i\,K_b\,m = 2 \implies i = \dfrac{5M}{13W} \implies x_2 = \dfrac{13W}{80M} = \dfrac{1.3}{8} \times \dfrac{W}{M}$
questions.topic: Mole fraction of electrolyte from vapour pressure and boiling point

questions.text: If a substance 'A' dissolves in solution of a mixture of 'B' and 'C' with their respective number of moles as $n_A$, $n_B$ and $n_C$, mole fraction of C in the solution is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Mole fraction equals component moles divided by total moles // 📝 Solution: $x_C = \dfrac{n_C}{n_A + n_B + n_C}$

questions.text: XY is a membrane separating two chambers 1 and 2 containing sugar solutions of concentrations $c_1$ and $c_2$ ($c_1>c_2$) mol L$^{-1}$. Here $p_1$ and $p_2$ are the pressures applied to chambers 1 and 2, and $\pi$ is the osmotic pressure. Consider: (A) Membrane cellophane, $p_1>\pi$; (B) Membrane porous, $p_2>\pi$; (C) Membrane parchment paper, $p_1>\pi$; (D) Membrane cellophane, $p_2>\pi$. Identify the correct conditions for reverse osmosis.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Reverse osmosis needs an applied pressure above $\pi$ on the concentrated side through a semipermeable membrane. // 📝 Solution: Solvent must flow from chamber 1 (higher $c_1$) to chamber 2 $\implies$ $p_1>\pi$ with a semipermeable membrane (cellophane, parchment) $\implies$ A and C.

questions.text: Elements P and Q form two types of non-volatile, non-ionizable compounds PQ and PQ$_2$. When $1\;\text{g}$ of PQ is dissolved in $50\;\text{g}$ of solvent 'A', $\Delta T_b = 1.176\;\text{K}$; when $1\;\text{g}$ of PQ$_2$ is dissolved in $50\;\text{g}$ of solvent 'A', $\Delta T_b = 0.689\;\text{K}$. ($K_b$ of 'A' $= 5\;\text{K kg mol}^{-1}$). The molar masses of elements P and Q (in $\text{g mol}^{-1}$) respectively, are:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $M = \dfrac{K_b \times w \times 1000}{W \times \Delta T_b}$ for each compound // 📝 Solution: $M_{PQ} = 85$, $M_{PQ_2} = 145 \implies P + Q = 85,\; P + 2Q = 145 \implies Q = 60,\; P = 25$
questions.topic: Molar mass from elevation of boiling point

questions.text: Molality of an aqueous solution of urea is $4.44\;\text{m}$. Mole fraction of urea in the solution is $x \times 10^{-3}$. The value of $x$ is ____ (integer).
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Mole fraction equals moles of urea divided by total moles including water. // 📝 Solution: $n_{\text{water}} = \dfrac{1000}{18} = 55.56 \implies x_{\text{urea}} = \dfrac{4.44}{4.44 + 55.56} = 0.0740 = 74 \times 10^{-3}$.

questions.text: Consider the following aqueous solutions. I. $2.2\;\text{g}$ glucose in $125\;\text{mL}$. II. $1.9\;\text{g}$ $\text{CaCl}_2$ in $250\;\text{mL}$. III. $9.0\;\text{g}$ urea in $500\;\text{mL}$. IV. $20.5\;\text{g}$ $\text{Al}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3$ in $750\;\text{mL}$. The correct increasing order of boiling point of these solutions will be: [Given molar masses: H = 1, C = 12, N = 14, O = 16, Cl = 35.5, Ca = 40, Al = 27, S = 32]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Boiling point rises with total particle molality $i\,m$ // 📝 Solution: Glucose $0.098$, $\text{CaCl}_2$ $0.204$, urea $0.3$, $\text{Al}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3$ $0.4$ $\implies \text{I} < \text{II} < \text{III} < \text{IV}$

questions.text: At $27\;^\circ\text{C}$, a solution containing $2.5\;\text{g}$ of solute in $250.0\;\text{mL}$ of solution exerts an osmotic pressure of $400\;\text{Pa}$. The molar mass of the solute is ____ $\text{g mol}^{-1}$ (nearest integer). Given $R = 0.083\;\text{L bar K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $\pi = \dfrac{w}{M}\cdot\dfrac{RT}{V}$ with $\pi$ in bar and $V$ in litres. // 📝 Solution: $\pi = 400\;\text{Pa} = 4 \times 10^{-3}\;\text{bar} \implies M = \dfrac{2.5 \times 0.083 \times 300}{4 \times 10^{-3} \times 0.25} = 62250\;\text{g mol}^{-1}$.

questions.text: The observed and normal molar masses of compound $MX_2$ are $65.6$ and $164$ respectively. The percent degree of ionisation of $MX_2$ is ______ $\%$ (nearest integer).
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Van't Hoff factor is normal molar mass divided by observed molar mass, with $i\;=\;1+2\alpha$ for $MX_2$. // 📝 Solution: $i\;=\;\frac{164}{65.6}\;=\;2.5\;\implies\;1+2\alpha\;=\;2.5\;\implies\;\alpha\;=\;0.75\;=\;75\%$
questions.topic: Van't Hoff factor and degree of ionisation

questions.text: 2 moles each of ethylene glycol and glucose are dissolved in 500 g of water. Given $K_b = 0.52\,\text{K kg mol}^{-1}$, the boiling point of the resulting solution is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Non-electrolytes give $i=1$, so $\Delta T_b = K_b\,m$. // 📝 Solution: $m = \dfrac{4}{0.5} = 8\,\text{mol kg}^{-1}$ $\implies$ $\Delta T_b = 0.52\times8 = 4.16\,\text{K}$ $\implies$ $T_b = 373.16+4.16 = 377.3\,\text{K}$.

questions.text: Molality of $0.8\;\text{M}$ $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ solution (density $1.06\;\text{g cm}^{-3}$) is ____ $\times 10^{-3}\;\text{m}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Solvent mass per litre equals solution mass minus solute mass // 📝 Solution: $m = \dfrac{0.8}{(1060 - 78.4) \times 10^{-3}} \implies m = \dfrac{0.8}{0.9816} = 0.815\;\text{m}$

questions.text: At $T\;\text{K}$, 2 moles of liquid A and 3 moles of liquid B are mixed. The vapour pressure of the ideal solution formed is $320\;\text{mmHg}$. At this stage, one mole of A and one mole of B are added to the solution. The vapour pressure is now measured as $328.6\;\text{mmHg}$. The vapour pressures (in mmHg) of pure A and pure B are respectively:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Apply Raoult's law to both mixtures and solve simultaneously // 📝 Solution: $0.4P_A^\circ + 0.6P_B^\circ = 320$, $\dfrac{3P_A^\circ + 4P_B^\circ}{7} = 328.6 \implies P_A^\circ = 500,\; P_B^\circ = 200$
questions.topic: Vapour pressure of pure components from ideal solution data

questions.text: The percentage dissociation of a salt $\text{MX}_3$ in solution at a given temperature (van't Hoff factor $i=2$) is ____ % (nearest integer).
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For $\text{MX}_3 \rightarrow \text{M}^{3+}+3\text{X}^-$, the number of particles is $n=4$. // 📝 Solution: $i = 1+(n-1)\alpha = 2$ $\implies$ $\alpha = \dfrac{1}{3}\approx33\%$.

questions.text: What happens to freezing point of benzene when small quantity of naphthalene is added to benzene?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Adding a solute lowers the freezing point of the solvent // 📝 Solution: $\Delta T_f = K_f\,m > 0 \implies T_f = T_f^\circ - \Delta T_f$ decreases

questions.text: Which of the following binary mixtures does NOT show the behaviour of a minimum boiling azeotrope?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Minimum boiling azeotropes arise from positive deviation from Raoult's law. // 📝 Solution: Phenol–aniline shows negative deviation $\implies$ maximum boiling azeotrope, not minimum $\implies$ B.

questions.text: $1.24\;g$ of $AX_2$ (molar mass $124\;g\;mol^{-1}$) is dissolved in $1\;kg$ of water to form a solution with boiling point of $100.0156^{\circ}C$, while $25.4\;g$ of $AY_2$ (molar mass $250\;g\;mol^{-1}$) in $2\;kg$ of water constitutes a solution with a boiling point of $100.0260^{\circ}C$. $K_b\left(H_2O\right)\;=\;0.52\;K\;kg\;mol^{-1}$. Which of the following is correct?

options.text: $AX_2$ is fully ionised while $AY_2$ is completely unionised
$AX_2$ is completely unionised while $AY_2$ is fully ionised

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find $i$ from $\Delta T_b\;=\;iK_bm$ for each salt. // 📝 Solution: $AX_2$: $0.0156\;=\;i\times0.52\times0.01\;\implies\;i\;=\;3\;\implies\;\alpha\;=\;1$; $AY_2$: $0.0260\;=\;i\times0.52\times0.0508\;\implies\;i\;\approx\;1$
questions.topic: Elevation in boiling point and degree of ionisation

questions.text: Consider the dissociation of the weak acid HX: $\text{HX(aq)} \rightleftharpoons \text{H}^+\text{(aq)} + \text{X}^-\text{(aq)}$, $K_a = 1.2 \times 10^{-5}$. The osmotic pressure of $0.03\;\text{M}$ aqueous solution of HX at $300\;\text{K}$ is ____ $\times 10^{-2}$ bar (nearest integer). Given $R = 0.083\;\text{L bar mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Solve $K_a = \dfrac{x^2}{C - x}$ for small $x$, then use $\pi = (C + x)RT$. // 📝 Solution: $\dfrac{x^2}{0.03} = 1.2 \times 10^{-5} \implies x = 6 \times 10^{-4}$ $\implies \pi = (0.03 + 6 \times 10^{-4}) \times 0.083 \times 300 = 0.762\;\text{bar} \approx 76 \times 10^{-2}\;\text{bar}$.

questions.text: Mass of ethylene glycol (antifreeze) to be added to $18.6\;\text{kg}$ of water to protect the freezing point at $-24\;^\circ\text{C}$ is ____ kg (nearest integer). Given molar mass of ethylene glycol $= 62\;\text{g mol}^{-1}$ and $K_f$ of water $= 1.86\;\text{K kg mol}^{-1}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $\Delta T_f = K_f \cdot \dfrac{w/62}{\text{kg of water}}$. // 📝 Solution: $24 = 1.86 \times \dfrac{w}{62 \times 18.6} \implies w = \dfrac{24 \times 62 \times 18.6}{1.86} = 14880\;\text{g} = 14.88\;\text{kg} \implies 15\;\text{kg}$.

questions.text: A solution containing $10\;\text{g}$ of an electrolyte $\text{AB}_2$ in $100\;\text{g}$ of water boils at $100.52\;^\circ\text{C}$. The degree of ionization $(\alpha)$ of the electrolyte is ____ $\times 10^{-1}$ (nearest integer). Given molar mass of $\text{AB}_2 = 200\;\text{g mol}^{-1}$, $K_b = 0.52\;\text{K kg mol}^{-1}$, and $\text{AB}_2 \rightarrow \text{A}^{2+} + 2\text{B}^-$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For $n = 3$ ions, $i = 1 + (n-1)\alpha = 1 + 2\alpha$. // 📝 Solution: $m = \dfrac{10/200}{0.1} = 0.5 \implies 0.52 = i \times 0.52 \times 0.5 \implies i = 2 = 1 + 2\alpha \implies \alpha = 0.5 = 5 \times 10^{-1}$.
questions.topic: Elevation of boiling point and degree of ionization

questions.text: A solution of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is $31.4\%$ $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ by mass and has a density of $1.25\;\text{g mL}^{-1}$. The molarity of the $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ solution is ____ M (nearest integer). [Given molar mass of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 = 98\;\text{g mol}^{-1}$]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Take 100 g of solution and convert its mass to volume using density // 📝 Solution: $M = \dfrac{31.4/98}{100/1.25 \times 10^{-3}} \implies M = \dfrac{0.3204}{0.08} = 4.005 \approx 4$
questions.topic: Molarity from mass percent and density

questions.text: Which one of the following graphs accurately represents the plot of partial pressure of $\text{CS}_2$ vs its mole fraction in a mixture of acetone and $\text{CS}_2$ at constant temperature? [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Positive deviation places the partial pressure above the Raoult line // 📝 Solution: $p_{\text{CS}_2} > x_{\text{CS}_2}\,p^\circ_{\text{CS}_2}$ for positive deviation $\implies$ the curve lies above the Raoult line
questions.topic: Raoult vs Henry graphs for positive deviation

questions.text: A substance 'X' (1.5 g) dissolved in 150 g of a solvent 'Y' (molar mass $= 300\;\text{g mol}^{-1}$) led to an elevation of the boiling point by $0.5\;\text{K}$. The relative lowering in the vapour pressure of the solvent 'Y' is ____ $\times 10^{-2}$ (nearest integer). [Given: $K_b$ of the solvent $= 5.0\;\text{K kg mol}^{-1}$] Assume the solution to be dilute and no association or dissociation of X takes place.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find molality from boiling-point elevation, then use the mole ratio // 📝 Solution: $m = \dfrac{0.5}{5} = 0.1 \implies n_X = 0.015,\; n_Y = \dfrac{150}{300} = 0.5 \implies \dfrac{\Delta P}{P^\circ} = \dfrac{0.015}{0.515} \approx 3 \times 10^{-2}$

questions.text: Consider a solution of $\text{CO}_2(g)$ dissolved in water in a closed container. Which one of the following plots correctly represents variation of $\log$ (partial pressure of $\text{CO}_2$ in vapour phase above water) with $\log$ (mole fraction of $\text{CO}_2$ in water) at $25\;^\circ\text{C}$? [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Henry's law becomes a straight line in log–log form // 📝 Solution: $p = K_H\,x \implies \log p = \log x + \log K_H$, slope $1$ with positive intercept

questions.text: If $A_2B$ is $30\%$ ionised in an aqueous solution, then the value of van't Hoff factor $i$ is ______ $\times10^{-1}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For a salt giving three ions, $i\;=\;1+2\alpha$. // 📝 Solution: $i\;=\;1+2\left(0.3\right)\;=\;1.6\;=\;16\times10^{-1}$

questions.text: Solid lead nitrate is dissolved in 1 litre of water. The solution was found to boil at $100.15\;^\circ\text{C}$. When $0.2$ mol of NaCl is added to the resulting solution, it was observed that the solution froze at $-0.8\;^\circ\text{C}$. The solubility product of $\text{PbCl}_2$ formed is ____ $\times 10^{-6}$ at $298\;\text{K}$ (nearest integer). Given $K_b = 0.5\;\text{K kg mol}^{-1}$ and $K_f = 1.8\;\text{K kg mol}^{-1}$. Assume molality equals molarity.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $\Delta T_b = iK_bm$ to find the lead nitrate amount, then $\Delta T_f$ for the remaining ions. // 📝 Solution: $0.15 = 0.5 \times 3a \implies a = 0.1\;\text{M}$ $\implies$ $0.8 = 1.8\left(0.3 - 3x + 0.4\right) \implies x = \dfrac{2.3}{27}$ $\implies$ $K_{sp} = \left(0.1 - x\right)\left(0.2 - 2x\right)^2 = 13 \times 10^{-6}$.

questions.text: A solution containing $2\;\text{g}$ of a non-volatile solute in $20\;\text{g}$ of water boils at $373.52\;\text{K}$. The molecular mass of the solute is ____ $\text{g mol}^{-1}$ (nearest integer). Given water boils at $373\;\text{K}$ and $K_b = 0.52\;\text{K kg mol}^{-1}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $\Delta T_b = K_b\,m$ with $m = \dfrac{w/M}{W_{\text{solvent}}\,(\text{kg})}$. // 📝 Solution: $0.52 = 0.52 \times \dfrac{2}{M} \times \dfrac{1}{20 \times 10^{-3}} \implies M = 100\;\text{g mol}^{-1}$.

questions.text: Two liquids A and B form an ideal solution. At $320\;\text{K}$, the vapour pressure of the solution containing $3\;\text{mol}$ of A and $1\;\text{mol}$ of B is $500\;\text{mmHg}$. At the same temperature, if $1\;\text{mol}$ of A is further added to this solution, vapour pressure of the solution increases by $20\;\text{mmHg}$. Vapour pressure (in mmHg) of B in pure state is ____ (nearest integer).
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Write Raoult's law for both mixtures and solve the pair of equations // 📝 Solution: $0.75P_A^\circ + 0.25P_B^\circ = 500$, $0.8P_A^\circ + 0.2P_B^\circ = 520 \implies P_A^\circ = 600,\; P_B^\circ = 200$
questions.topic: Ideal solution vapour pressure of pure component

questions.text: The mass of sodium acetate ($\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}$) required to prepare $250\;\text{mL}$ of $0.35\;\text{M}$ aqueous solution is ____ g. (Molar mass of $\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}$ is $82.02\;\text{g mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Moles equal molarity times volume in litres // 📝 Solution: $n = 0.35 \times 0.25 = 0.0875\;\text{mol} \implies m = 0.0875 \times 82.02 = 7.18\;\text{g} \approx 7$

questions.text: We have three aqueous solutions of NaCl labelled as A, B and C with concentrations $0.1\;\text{M}$, $0.01\;\text{M}$ and $0.001\;\text{M}$ respectively. The value of van't Hoff factor $(i)$ for these solutions will be in the order.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: NaCl ionisation becomes more complete as the solution gets more dilute. // 📝 Solution: $i_A = 1.87 < i_B = 1.94 \le i_C = 1.94$ $\implies i_A < i_B < i_C$ (as per key).

questions.text: In the depression of freezing point experiment: A. Vapour pressure of the solution is less than that of pure solvent. B. Vapour pressure of the solution is more than that of pure solvent. C. Only solute molecules solidify at the freezing point. D. Only solvent molecules solidify at the freezing point. Choose the correct option.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Solute lowers the solvent vapour pressure, and only pure solvent separates as ice on freezing. // 📝 Solution: A is true, B is false, C is false, D is true $\implies$ A and D only.

questions.text: $x$ g of NaCl is added to water in a beaker with a lid. The temperature of the system is raised from $1\;^\circ\text{C}$ to $25\;^\circ\text{C}$. Which plot best represents the change in molarity $M$ of the solution with temperature? [Consider the solubility of NaCl remains unchanged over the temperature range]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Water has maximum density, hence minimum volume, at $4\;^\circ\text{C}$. // 📝 Solution: $M=\dfrac{n}{V}$ with fixed $n$ $\implies M$ peaks near $4\;^\circ\text{C}$ and falls above it $\implies$ plot (2).
questions.topic: Molarity vs temperature, density anomaly of water

questions.text: $2.7\;\text{kg}$ each of water and acetic acid are mixed. The freezing point of the solution will be $-x\;^\circ\text{C}$. Consider that acetic acid neither dimerises nor dissociates in water. $x = $ ____ (nearest integer). Given molar masses: water $= 18\;\text{g mol}^{-1}$, acetic acid $= 60\;\text{g mol}^{-1}$; $K_f$ of water $= 1.86\;\text{K kg mol}^{-1}$; freezing points: water $= 273\;\text{K}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The component present in larger moles is the solvent; use its $K_f$ with the molality of the solute. // 📝 Solution: $n_{\text{water}} = \dfrac{2700}{18} = 150 > n_{\text{acetic}} = \dfrac{2700}{60} = 45 \implies$ water is solvent; $m = \dfrac{45}{2.7} = 16.67\;\text{m} \implies \Delta T_f = 1.86 \times 16.67 = 31\;^\circ\text{C} \implies x = 31$.

questions.text: Arrange the following solutions in order of their increasing boiling points. (i) $10^{-4}\;M\;NaCl$ (ii) $10^{-4}\;M$ Urea (iii) $10^{-3}\;M\;NaCl$ (iv) $10^{-2}\;M\;NaCl$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Elevation in boiling point depends on $i\times$ concentration. // 📝 Solution: $i\,c$ values: urea $1\times10^{-4}$, $NaCl$ $2\times10^{-4}$, $2\times10^{-3}$, $2\times10^{-2}\;\implies\;$ (ii) < (i) < (iii) < (iv)
questions.topic: Elevation in boiling point and colligative comparison

questions.text: Statement I: Gallium is used in the manufacturing of thermometers. Statement II: A thermometer containing gallium is useful for measuring the freezing point ($256\;\text{K}$) of brine solution. Choose the correct answer.

options.text: $\text{Both Statement I and Statement II are true}$
$\text{Statement I is false but Statement II is true}$
$\text{Both Statement I and Statement II are false}$
$\text{Statement I is true but Statement II is false}$

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Gallium melts near $303\;\text{K}$, so it is solid at $256\;\text{K}$. // 📝 Solution: Statement I is true; Statement II is false (gallium is used for high temperature measurement) $\implies$ option D.
questions.topic: Gallium thermometers and brine freezing point

questions.text: Statement I: The molal depression constant is $K_f = \dfrac{M_1RT_f}{\Delta S_{\text{fus}}}$. Statement II: $K_f$ for benzene is less than $K_f$ for water. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer.

options.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $K_f = \dfrac{M_1RT_f^2}{\Delta H_{\text{fus}}}$ and $\Delta S_{\text{fus}} = \dfrac{\Delta H_{\text{fus}}}{T_f}$. // 📝 Solution: $\dfrac{M_1RT_f}{\Delta S_{\text{fus}}}$ is equivalent, so I is correct; benzene $K_f \approx 5.12 > 1.86$ (water), so II is false $\implies$ D.

questions.text: When a non-volatile solute is added to the solvent, the vapour pressure of the solvent decreases by $10\;mm$ of $Hg$. The mole fraction of the solute in the solution is $0.2$. What would be the mole fraction of the solvent if the decrease in vapour pressure is $20\;mm$ of $Hg$?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Lowering of vapour pressure is directly proportional to the mole fraction of solute. // 📝 Solution: $10\;\propto\;0.2\;\implies\;20\;\propto\;0.4\;\implies\;X_{solvent}\;=\;1-0.4\;=\;0.6$

questions.text: 1 g each of compounds AB and AB$_2$ are dissolved in 15 g of water separately; they raise the boiling point of water by 2.7 K and 1.5 K respectively. The atomic mass of A (in amu) is ____ $\times10^{-1}$ (nearest integer). Given $K_b = 0.5\,\text{K kg mol}^{-1}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\Delta T_b = K_b\,m$ gives the molar masses of AB and AB$_2$. // 📝 Solution: $M_{\text{AB}} = \dfrac{1000}{15\times5.4}\approx12.34$ and $M_{\text{AB}_2} = \dfrac{1000}{15\times3}\approx22.22$ $\implies$ $A+B = 12.34$, $A+2B = 22.22$ $\implies$ $A\approx2.46 = 24.6\times10^{-1}\approx25\times10^{-1}$.

questions.text: $2.5\;\text{g}$ of a non-volatile non-electrolyte is dissolved in $100\;\text{g}$ of water at $25\;^\circ\text{C}$. The solution showed a boiling point elevation by $2\;^\circ\text{C}$. Assuming the solute concentration is negligible with respect to the solvent, the vapour pressure of the resulting aqueous solution is ____ mm Hg (nearest integer). Given $K_b = 0.52\;\text{K kg mol}^{-1}$, $1\;\text{atm} = 760\;\text{mm Hg}$ and molar mass of water $= 18\;\text{g mol}^{-1}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Get molality from $\Delta T_b = K_bm$, then apply Raoult's law $\dfrac{\Delta P}{P^0} = \dfrac{n_{\text{solute}}}{n_{\text{solvent}}}$. // 📝 Solution: $m = \dfrac{2}{0.52} \implies \Delta P = 760 \times \dfrac{m}{1000} \times 18 = 52.6\;\text{mm Hg} \implies P_s = 760 - 52.6 \approx 707\;\text{mm Hg}$.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement (I): $NaCl$ is added to the ice at $0^{\circ}C$ present in the ice cream box to prevent the melting of ice cream. Statement (II): On addition of $NaCl$ to ice at $0^{\circ}C$, there is a depression in freezing point. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Salt added to ice forms a freezing mixture through freezing point depression. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta T_f\;=\;iK_fm\;\implies\;T_f\;<\;0^{\circ}C\;\implies\;$ the mixture stays colder than ice alone, so ice cream does not melt; both statements are true
questions.topic: Depression in freezing point and freezing mixtures

questions.text: Consider the given plots of vapour pressure (VP) vs temperature ($T/K$). Which amongst the following options is the correct graphical representation showing $\Delta T_f$, depression in the freezing point of a solvent in a solution?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The solution curve lies below the pure solvent curve, and freezing occurs where it meets the frozen solvent curve. // 📝 Solution: $T_f\;<\;T_f^0\;\implies\;$ VP of solution is lower than that of the liquid solvent at every $T$, which matches graph (1) [FIGURE]

questions.text: What is the freezing point depression constant of a solvent, $50\;g$ of which contains $1\;g$ of non-volatile solute (molar mass $256\;g\;mol^{-1}$) and the decrease in freezing point is $0.40\;K$?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $\Delta T_f\;=\;K_f\,m$ with molality from the given masses. // 📝 Solution: $m\;=\;\frac{1/256}{0.05}\;\implies\;0.40\;=\;K_f\times\frac{1/256}{0.05}\;\implies\;K_f\;=\;5.12\;K\;kg\;mol^{-1}$

questions.text: The osmotic pressure of a dilute solution is $7 \times 10^5\;\text{Pa}$ at $273\;\text{K}$. Osmotic pressure of the same solution at $283\;\text{K}$ is ____ $\times 10^4\;\text{Nm}^{-2}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: At constant concentration, osmotic pressure is proportional to temperature // 📝 Solution: $\dfrac{\pi_2}{283} = \dfrac{\pi_1}{273} \implies \pi_2 = \dfrac{7 \times 10^5 \times 283}{273} \approx 72.6 \times 10^4 \approx 73 \times 10^4$

questions.text: Based on the given figure, the number of correct statement/s is/are ____. A. Surface tension is the outcome of equal attractive and repulsive forces acting on the liquid molecule in bulk. B. Surface tension is due to uneven forces acting on the molecules present on the surface. C. The molecule in the bulk can never come to the liquid surface. D. The molecules on the surface are responsible for vapour pressure if the system is a closed system. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Surface tension arises from unbalanced cohesive forces on molecules at the surface. // 📝 Solution: A is false, B is true, C is false, D is true $\implies$ 2 correct statements.

questions.text: Which of the following graphs correctly represents the plots of $K_H$ at 1 bar for gases in water versus temperature? [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $K_H$ of gases in water first rises and then falls as temperature increases. // 📝 Solution: The He, N$_2$ and CH$_4$ curves in option (4) show this rise-then-fall trend $\implies$ answer (4).

questions.text: Consider a binary solution of two volatile liquid components $1$ and $2$. $x_1$ and $y_1$ are the mole fractions of component $1$ in liquid and vapour phase, respectively. The slope and intercept of the linear plot of $\frac{1}{x_1}$ vs $\frac{1}{y_1}$ are given respectively as:
The quantity which changes with temperature is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Solution volume depends on temperature // 📝 Solution: $M = \dfrac{n_{\text{solute}}}{V_{\text{solution}}} \implies V$ changes with $T$, so $M$ changes; mass %, molality and mole fraction do not

questions.text: Match List I with List II. List I: A. van't Hoff factor, i. B. $k_f$. C. Solutions with same osmotic pressure. D. Azeotropes. List II: I. Cryoscopic constant. II. Isotonic solutions. III. Normal molar mass divided by abnormal molar mass. IV. Solutions with same composition of vapour above it. Choose the correct answer.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall the definition of van't Hoff factor and the terms for isotonic solutions and azeotropes. // 📝 Solution: $i = \dfrac{\text{Normal molar mass}}{\text{Abnormal molar mass}}$ (III); $k_f$ is cryoscopic constant (I); same osmotic pressure is isotonic (II); azeotropes have same vapour composition (IV) $\implies$ A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.
questions.topic: Van't Hoff factor and related terms

questions.text: Liquids A and B form an ideal solution. At the same temperature the vapour pressures of pure A and B are 350 and 750 mm Hg. $x_A$, $x_B$ are the mole fractions of A and B in the solution, and $y_A$, $y_B$ are their mole fractions in the vapour. Then:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Combine Dalton's law with Raoult's law to get $y_A/y_B = P_A^\circ x_A/(P_B^\circ x_B)$. // 📝 Solution: $\dfrac{y_A}{y_B} = \dfrac{350}{750}\cdot\dfrac{x_A}{x_B}$ $\implies$ since $350/750<1$, $\dfrac{x_A}{x_B} > \dfrac{y_A}{y_B}$ $\implies$ C.

questions.text: Identify the mixture that shows positive deviations from Raoult's Law:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Positive deviation means weaker mixed interactions than pure-component interactions // 📝 Solution: Acetone–$\text{CS}_2$ has weaker mixed interactions $\implies$ positive deviation $\implies$ option D

questions.text: Sea water, considered as a 6 molar NaCl solution with density $2\,\text{g mL}^{-1}$, contains dissolved O$_2$ at 5.8 ppm. The concentration of dissolved O$_2$ is $x\times10^{-4}\,\text{m}$ (molality). The value of $x$ is ____ (nearest integer). Molar masses: NaCl $58.5\,\text{g mol}^{-1}$, O$_2$ $32\,\text{g mol}^{-1}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: 1 L of brine weighs $2000\,\text{g}$, so the water mass is $2000-6\times58.5 = 1649\,\text{g}$. // 📝 Solution: $m_{\text{O}_2} = 5.8\times10^{-6}\times2000 = 1.16\times10^{-2}\,\text{g}$ $\implies$ molality $=\dfrac{1.16\times10^{-2}/32}{1.649}\approx2.19\times10^{-4}\,\text{m}$ $\implies$ $x=2$.

questions.text: A lead storage battery contains $38\%$ by weight solution of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$. The van't Hoff factor is $2.67$ at this concentration. The temperature in Kelvin at which the solution in the battery will freeze is ____ (nearest integer). Given $K_f = 1.8\;\text{K kg mol}^{-1}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $\Delta T_f = iK_fm$ and $T_f = 273 - \Delta T_f$. // 📝 Solution: $m = \dfrac{38/98}{62 \times 10^{-3}} \implies \Delta T_f = 2.67 \times 1.8 \times \dfrac{38}{98} \times \dfrac{1000}{62} = 30.05\;\text{K} \implies T_f \approx 243\;\text{K}$.

questions.text: $20\%$ of acetic acid is dissociated when its $5\;\text{g}$ is added to $500\;\text{mL}$ of water. The depression in freezing point of such water is ____ $\times 10^{-3}\;^\circ\text{C}$ (nearest integer). Atomic masses C $=12$, H $=1$, O $=16$. Given $K_f = 1.86\;\text{K kg mol}^{-1}$ and density of water $= 1\;\text{g cm}^{-3}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $\Delta T_f = iK_fm$ with $i = 1 + \alpha(n-1)$ for a weak acid. // 📝 Solution: $i = 1 + 0.2(2-1) = 1.2$, $m = \dfrac{5/60}{0.5} = 0.1667\;\text{m} \implies \Delta T_f = 1.2 \times 1.86 \times 0.1667 = 0.372\;^\circ\text{C} = 372 \times 10^{-3}\;^\circ\text{C}$.
questions.topic: Depression of freezing point of weak electrolyte

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: A. Osmosis. B. Reverse osmosis. C. Electro osmosis. D. Electrophoresis. List-II: I. Solvent molecules pass through semipermeable membrane towards solvent side. II. Movement of charged colloidal particles under the influence of applied electric potential towards oppositely charged electrodes. III. Solvent molecules pass through semipermeable membrane towards solution side. IV. Dispersion medium moves in an electric field. Choose the correct answer.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Osmosis moves solvent into the solution, while reverse osmosis moves solvent out of it. // 📝 Solution: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II $\implies$ option B.

questions.text: Assume a living cell with $0.9\%\;(w/w)$ glucose solution (aqueous). This cell is immersed in another solution having equal mole fraction of glucose and water (consider data up to first decimal place only). The cell will:

options.text: shrink since solution is $0.45\%\;(w/w)$ as a result of association of glucose molecules (due to hydrogen bonding)
show no change in volume since solution is $0.9\%\;(w/w)$

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Compare the outside $w/w$ concentration with the $0.9\%$ inside; water leaves toward the more concentrated side. // 📝 Solution: $x_{glu}\;=\;x_{water}\;=\;0.5\;\implies\;m\;=\;0.5\times180+0.5\times18\;=\;99\;g\;\implies\;\%\;w/w\;\approx\;90\%\;>\;0.9\%$, so the cell shrinks

questions.text: The primary and secondary valencies of cobalt respectively in $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{5}\text{Cl}\right]\text{Cl}_{2}$ are :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Primary valency corresponds to the oxidation state, and secondary valency corresponds to the coordination number. // 📝 Solution: In $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{5}\text{Cl}\right]\text{Cl}_{2}$, let oxidation state of $\text{Co}$ be $x \implies x + 5\left(0\right) - 1 - 2 = 0 \implies x = +3$ (Primary valency $= 3$). Secondary valency is the coordination number of $\text{Co}^{3+} = 5 + 1 = 6$.

questions.text: The denticity of the ligand present in the Fehling's reagent is _______ .
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Tartrate ion coordinates to copper(II) through both carboxylate and alkoxide oxygens. // 📝 Solution: In Fehling's solution, the tartrate ion coordinates via two carboxylate oxygen atoms and two deprotonated hydroxyl oxygens [FIGURE], thereby functioning as a tetradentate ligand with a denticity of $4$.

questions.text: Consider a mixture '$\text{X}$' which is made by dissolving $0.4\;\text{mol}$ of $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{5}\text{SO}_{4}\right]\text{Br}$ and $0.4\;\text{mol}$ of $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{5}\text{Br}\right]\text{SO}_{4}$ in water to make $4\;\text{L}$ of solution. When $2\;\text{L}$ of mixture '$\text{X}$' is allowed to react with excess of $\text{AgNO}_{3}$, it forms precipitate '$\text{Y}$'. The rest $2\;\text{L}$ of mixture '$\text{X}$' reacts with excess $\text{BaCl}_{2}$ to form precipitate '$\text{Z}$'. Which of the following statements is CORRECT?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Calculate the moles of ionizable anions present in each $2\;\text{L}$ aliquot of the $4\;\text{L}$ mixture. // 📝 Solution: The $4\;\text{L}$ solution contains $0.4\;\text{mol}\;\text{Br}^{-}$ and $0.4\;\text{mol}\;\text{SO}_{4}^{2-}$. A $2\;\text{L}$ aliquot contains $0.2\;\text{mol}\;\text{Br}^{-}$ and $0.2\;\text{mol}\;\text{SO}_{4}^{2-}$. Reaction with excess $\text{AgNO}_{3}$ yields $0.2\;\text{mol}$ of $\text{AgBr}\;(\text{Y})$. Reaction with excess $\text{BaCl}_{2}$ yields $0.2\;\text{mol}$ of $\text{BaSO}_{4}\;(\text{Z})$. Thus, statement (2) is correct.

questions.text: The d-electronic configuration of $\left[\text{CoCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}$ in tetrahedral crystal field is $\text{e}^{m}\text{t}_{2}^{n}$. Sum of 'm' and 'number of unpaired electrons' is _______ .
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: In a tetrahedral field, d-orbitals split into lower $\text{e}$ and higher $\text{t}_{2}$ levels without inversion symmetry. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Co}^{2+}$ is $3\text{d}^{7}$. With weak field ligand $\text{Cl}^{-}$, tetrahedral configuration is $\text{e}^{4}\;\text{t}_{2}^{3} \implies m = 4$. Unpaired electrons $= 3 \implies \text{Sum} = 4 + 3 = 7$.

questions.text: The spin-only magnetic moments (in $\mathrm{BM}$) of $\left[\mathrm{MnBr_4}\right]^{2-}$ and $\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{H_2O}\right)_6\right]^{2+}$ respectively are
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Both $\mathrm{Br^-}$ and $\mathrm{H_2O}$ are weak field ligands, so both complexes are high spin; use $\mu \;=\; \sqrt{n\left(n+2\right)}$. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}\;d^5 \;\implies\; n \;=\; 5 \;\implies\; \mu \;=\; 5.92$; $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}\;d^6 \;\left(\text{high spin}\right) \;\implies\; n \;=\; 4 \;\implies\; \mu \;=\; 4.90$

questions.text: The correct sequence of ligands in the order of decreasing field strength is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Refer to the spectrochemical series from strongest to weakest field. // 📝 Solution: Spectrochemical series: $\text{CO} > \text{CN}^{-} > \text{en} > \text{NH}_{3} > \text{EDTA}^{4-} > \text{H}_{2}\text{O} > \text{OH}^{-} > \text{F}^{-} > \text{S}^{2-}$. In option (2), the decreasing order is $\text{CO} > \text{H}_{2}\text{O} > \text{F}^{-} > \text{S}^{2-}$.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Hybridisation, shape and spin only magnetic moment of $\text{K}_{3}\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{CO}_{3}\right)_{3}\right]$ is $\text{sp}^{3}\text{d}^{2}$, octahedral and $4.9\;\text{BM}$ respectively. Statement II: Geometry, hybridisation and spin only magnetic moment values $(\text{BM})$ of the ions $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{4}\right]^{2-}$, $\left[\text{MnBr}_{4}\right]^{2-}$ and $\left[\text{CoF}_{6}\right]^{3-}$ respectively are square planar, tetrahedral, octahedral; $\text{dsp}^{2}, \text{sp}^{3}, \text{sp}^{3}\text{d}^{2}$ and $0, 5.9, 4.9$. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Carbonate ($\text{CO}_{3}^{2-}$) and fluoride ($\text{F}^{-}$) act as weak field ligands with $\text{Co}^{3+}$. // 📝 Solution: In $\text{K}_{3}\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{CO}_{3}\right)_{3}\right]$, $\text{Co}^{3+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{6}\right)$ with weak field $\text{CO}_{3}^{2-}$ has $n = 4 \implies \mu = \sqrt{24} \approx 4.9\;\text{BM}$, geometry is octahedral, and hybridization is $\text{sp}^{3}\text{d}^{2}$ (Statement I is true). Statement II gives exact matching values: $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{4}\right]^{2-}\;(\text{dsp}^{2},\;0)$, $\left[\text{MnBr}_{4}\right]^{2-}\;(\text{sp}^{3},\;5.9)$, and $\left[\text{CoF}_{6}\right]^{3-}\;(\text{sp}^{3}\text{d}^{2},\;4.9)$ (Statement II is true).

questions.text: The $\text{F}^{-}$ ions make the enamel on teeth much harder by converting hydroxyapatite (the enamel on the surface of teeth) into much harder fluoroapatite having the formula.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Fluoroapatite is formed by substituting hydroxide in hydroxyapatite with fluoride. // 📝 Solution: Hydroxyapatite is $\left[3\left(\text{Ca}_{3}\left(\text{PO}_{4}\right)_{2}\right) \cdot \text{Ca}\left(\text{OH}\right)_{2}\right]$. Reaction with $\text{F}^{-}$ replaces $\text{OH}^{-}$ with $\text{F}^{-}$ to yield fluoroapatite, $\left[3\left(\text{Ca}_{3}\left(\text{PO}_{4}\right)_{2}\right) \cdot \text{CaF}_{2}\right]$.

questions.text: Match List - I with List - II. List - I (Reaction): (A) $\text{TiCl}_{4}$, (B) $\left[\text{FeO}_{4}\right]^{2-}$, (C) $\left[\text{FeCl}_{4}\right]^{-}$, (D) $\left[\text{CoCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}$. List - II (Type of redox reaction): (I) $\text{e}^{2},\;\text{t}_{2}^{0}$, (II) $\text{e}^{4},\;\text{t}_{2}^{3}$, (III) $\text{e}^{0},\;\text{t}_{2}^{0}$, (IV) $\text{e}^{2},\;\text{t}_{2}^{3}$. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For tetrahedral complexes, d-orbitals split into lower $\text{e}$ and higher $\text{t}_{2}$ levels. // 📝 Solution: In tetrahedral field: $\text{TiCl}_{4}: \text{Ti}^{4+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{0}\right) \implies \text{e}^{0}\;\text{t}_{2}^{0}\;(\text{III})$; $\left[\text{FeO}_{4}\right]^{2-}: \text{Fe}^{6+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{2}\right) \implies \text{e}^{2}\;\text{t}_{2}^{0}\;(\text{I})$; $\left[\text{FeCl}_{4}\right]^{-}: \text{Fe}^{3+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{5}\right) \implies \text{e}^{2}\;\text{t}_{2}^{3}\;(\text{IV})$; $\left[\text{CoCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}: \text{Co}^{2+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{7}\right) \implies \text{e}^{4}\;\text{t}_{2}^{3}\;(\text{II})$.

questions.text: Which of the following metal ions have $d^4$ configuration? A. $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ B. $\mathrm{Cr^{2+}}$ C. $\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}$ D. $\mathrm{Mn^{3+}}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Write the ground state configuration and remove electrons first from the $4s$ orbital. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Cr^{2+}}\;3d^4$, $\mathrm{Mn^{3+}}\;3d^4$, while $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}\;3d^5$ and $\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}\;3d^5 \;\implies\;$ B and D

questions.text: Which of the following complexes does not give a white precipitate with $\mathrm{AgNO_3}$ solution?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Only ionisable chloride outside the coordination sphere precipitates as $\mathrm{AgCl}$. // 📝 Solution: In $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH_3}\right)_3\mathrm{Cl_3}\right]$ all $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ are coordinated $\;\implies\;$ no free $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ $\;\implies\;$ no $\mathrm{AgCl}$

questions.text: Yellow compound of lead chromate gets dissolved on treatment with hot $\text{NaOH}$ solution. The product of lead formed is a :

options.text: Tetraanionic complex with coordination number six
Neutral complex with coordination number four
Dianionic complex with coordination number six
Dianionic complex with coordination number four

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Amphoteric lead hydroxide redissolves in excess alkali to form a plumbite complex. // 📝 Solution: $\text{PbCrO}_{4} + 4\text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{Na}_{2}\left[\text{Pb}\left(\text{OH}\right)_{4}\right] + \text{Na}_{2}\text{CrO}_{4}$. The lead-containing complex is $\left[\text{Pb}\left(\text{OH}\right)_{4}\right]^{2-}$, which is dianionic with a coordination number of four.

questions.text: The metal atom present in the complex $\text{MABXL}$ (where $\text{A, B, X}$ and $\text{L}$ are unidentate ligands and $\text{M}$ is metal) involves $\text{sp}^{3}$ hybridization. The number of geometrical isomers exhibited by the complex is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Tetrahedral complexes do not display geometrical isomerism because all positions are mutually adjacent. // 📝 Solution: Hybridization $\text{sp}^{3}$ gives a tetrahedral geometry where all bond angles are identical ($109.5^{\circ}$). Consequently, no distinct cis/trans or geometrical arrangements exist, yielding $0$ geometrical isomers.

questions.text: Identify the CORRECT set of details from the following: A. $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}$ : Inner orbital complex; $\text{d}^{2}\text{sp}^{3}$ hybridized B. $\left[\text{MnCl}_{6}\right]^{3-}$ : Outer orbital complex; $\text{sp}^{3}\text{d}^{2}$ hybridized C. $\left[\text{CoF}_{6}\right]^{3-}$ : Outer orbital complex; $\text{d}^{2}\text{sp}^{3}$ hybridized D. $\left[\text{FeF}_{6}\right]^{3-}$ : Outer orbital complex; $\text{sp}^{3}\text{d}^{2}$ hybridized E. $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{4}\right]^{2-}$ : Inner orbital complex; $\text{sp}^{3}$ hybridized Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Strong field ligands utilize inner $(n-1)\text{d}$ orbitals; weak field ligands utilize outer $n\text{d}$ orbitals. // 📝 Solution: $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}$ is inner orbital $\text{d}^{2}\text{sp}^{3}$ (A is correct). $\left[\text{MnCl}_{6}\right]^{3-}$ with weak $\text{Cl}^{-}$ is outer orbital $\text{sp}^{3}\text{d}^{2}$ (B is correct). $\left[\text{CoF}_{6}\right]^{3-}$ is $\text{sp}^{3}\text{d}^{2}$, not $\text{d}^{2}\text{sp}^{3}$ (C is incorrect). $\left[\text{FeF}_{6}\right]^{3-}$ is outer orbital $\text{sp}^{3}\text{d}^{2}$ (D is correct). $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{4}\right]^{2-}$ is $\text{dsp}^{2}$, not $\text{sp}^{3}$ (E is incorrect) $\implies$ A, B \& D Only.

questions.text: Given below are two statements : Statement I: $\left[\text{CoBr}_{4}\right]^{2-}$ ion will absorb light of lower energy than $\left[\text{CoCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}$ ion. Statement II : In $\left[\text{CoI}_{4}\right]^{2-}$ ion, the energy separation between the two set of d-orbitals is more than $\left[\text{CoCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}$ ion. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Energy of absorbed light corresponds to crystal field splitting $\Delta_{\text{t}}$, which follows the spectrochemical series. // 📝 Solution: Ligand field strength: $\text{I}^{-} < \text{Br}^{-} < \text{Cl}^{-}$. $\text{Br}^{-}$ is weaker than $\text{Cl}^{-} \implies \Delta_{\text{t}}\left(\left[\text{CoBr}_{4}\right]^{2-}\right) < \Delta_{\text{t}}\left(\left[\text{CoCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}\right)$, absorbing lower energy light (Statement I is true). $\text{I}^{-}$ is weaker than $\text{Cl}^{-} \implies \Delta_{\text{t}}\left(\left[\text{CoI}_{4}\right]^{2-}\right) < \Delta_{\text{t}}\left(\left[\text{CoCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}\right)$ (Statement II is false).

questions.text: Number of complexes which show optical isomerism among the following is _______ : $\text{cis}-\left[\text{Cr}\left(\text{ox}\right)_{2}\text{Cl}_{2}\right]^{3-}$, $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{en}\right)_{3}\right]^{3+}$, $\text{cis}-\left[\text{Pt}\left(\text{en}\right)_{2}\text{Cl}_{2}\right]^{2+}$, $\text{cis}-\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{en}\right)_{2}\text{Cl}_{2}\right]^{+}$, $\text{trans}-\left[\text{Pt}\left(\text{en}\right)_{2}\text{Cl}_{2}\right]^{2+}$, $\text{trans}-\left[\text{Cr}\left(\text{ox}\right)_{2}\text{Cl}_{2}\right]^{3-}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Complexes with planes of symmetry are achiral; cis-isomers with two bidentate chelates lack symmetry elements. // 📝 Solution: Optically active: $\text{cis}-\left[\text{Cr}\left(\text{ox}\right)_{2}\text{Cl}_{2}\right]^{3-}$, $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{en}\right)_{3}\right]^{3+}$, $\text{cis}-\left[\text{Pt}\left(\text{en}\right)_{2}\text{Cl}_{2}\right]^{2+}$, and $\text{cis}-\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{en}\right)_{2}\text{Cl}_{2}\right]^{+}$ (all lack POS and COS). Trans-isomers have a plane of symmetry and inversion center $\implies$ inactive. Total $= 4$.

questions.text: The correct increasing order of spin-only magnetic moment values of the complex ions $\left[\text{MnBr}_{4}\right]^{2-}\;(\text{A})$, $\left[\text{Cu}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+}\;(\text{B})$, $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{4}\right]^{2-}\;(\text{C})$ and $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+}\;(\text{D})$ is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Determine unpaired electrons $n$ for each complex and order by $\mu = \sqrt{n\left(n + 2\right)}\;\text{BM}$. // 📝 Solution: $\text{C}: \left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{4}\right]^{2-}\;\left(\text{dsp}^{2}\right) \implies n = 0,\;\mu = 0$; $\text{B}: \left[\text{Cu}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{9}\right) \implies n = 1,\;\mu = 1.73\;\text{BM}$; $\text{D}: \left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{8}\right) \implies n = 2,\;\mu = 2.83\;\text{BM}$; $\text{A}: \left[\text{MnBr}_{4}\right]^{2-}\;\left(3\text{d}^{5}\right) \implies n = 5,\;\mu = 5.92\;\text{BM} \implies \text{C} < \text{B} < \text{D} < \text{A}$.

questions.text: Consider the transition metal ions $\text{Mn}^{3+}, \text{Cr}^{3+}, \text{Fe}^{3+}$ and $\text{Co}^{3+}$ and all form low spin octahedral complexes. The correct decreasing order of unpaired electrons in their respective d-orbitals of the complexes is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Distribute electrons into $\text{t}_{2\text{g}}$ orbitals first under strong field conditions ($\Delta_{\text{o}} > P$). // 📝 Solution: In low spin octahedral: $\text{Cr}^{3+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{3}\right): \text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{3}\;\text{e}_{\text{g}}^{0} \implies n = 3$; $\text{Mn}^{3+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{4}\right): \text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{4}\;\text{e}_{\text{g}}^{0} \implies n = 2$; $\text{Fe}^{3+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{5}\right): \text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{5}\;\text{e}_{\text{g}}^{0} \implies n = 1$; $\text{Co}^{3+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{6}\right): \text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{6}\;\text{e}_{\text{g}}^{0} \implies n = 0 \implies \text{Cr}^{3+} > \text{Mn}^{3+} > \text{Fe}^{3+} > \text{Co}^{3+}$.

questions.text: In which one of the following metal carbonyls, $\text{CO}$ forms a bridge between metal atoms?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Solid state structure of octacarbonyldicobalt contains two bridging carbonyl ligands. // 📝 Solution: In solid state, $\left[\text{Co}_{2}\left(\text{CO}\right)_{8}\right]$ features a $\text{Co}-\text{Co}$ bond, six terminal $\text{CO}$ ligands, and two bridging $\text{CO}$ ligands [FIGURE]. $\left[\text{Mn}_{2}\left(\text{CO}\right)_{10}\right]$, $\left[\text{Os}_{3}\left(\text{CO}\right)_{12}\right]$, and $\left[\text{Ru}_{3}\left(\text{CO}\right)_{12}\right]$ contain only terminal carbonyls.

questions.text: Which of the following complexes are low spin? A. $\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{H_2O}\right)_6\right]^{2+}$ B. $\left[\mathrm{CoF_6}\right]^{3-}$ C. $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH_3}\right)_6\right]^{3+}$ D. $\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{CN}\right)_6\right]^{4-}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Strong field ligands such as $\mathrm{CN^-}$ and $\mathrm{NH_3}$ cause pairing for $d^6$ ions. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{H_2O}$ and $\mathrm{F^-}$ are weak field, giving high spin A and B; $\mathrm{NH_3}$ and $\mathrm{CN^-}$ are strong field, giving low spin $t_{2g}^6$ in C and D $\;\implies\;$ C and D
questions.topic: Crystal Field Theory, High Spin and Low Spin

questions.text: Correct order of spin only magnetic moment of the following complex ions is: (Given At. No. $\text{Fe}: 26, \text{Co}: 27$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Spin-only magnetic moment increases with the number of unpaired electrons: $\mu = \sqrt{n\left(n + 2\right)}\;\text{BM}$. // 📝 Solution: $\left[\text{FeF}_{6}\right]^{3-}: \text{Fe}^{3+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{5},\;\text{WFL}\right) \implies n = 5,\;\mu = \sqrt{35}\;\text{BM}$; $\left[\text{CoF}_{6}\right]^{3-}: \text{Co}^{3+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{6},\;\text{WFL}\right) \implies n = 4,\;\mu = \sqrt{24}\;\text{BM}$; $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{C}_{2}\text{O}_{4}\right)_{3}\right]^{3-}: \text{Co}^{3+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{6},\;\text{SFL}\right) \implies n = 0,\;\mu = 0$.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement (I): A solution of $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+}$ is green in colour. Statement (II): A solution of $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{4}\right]^{2-}$ is colourless. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Paramagnetic complexes with visible d-d transitions appear colored; square planar $\text{Ni(II)}$ with strong $\Delta$ absorbs in UV. // 📝 Solution: $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+}$ has two unpaired electrons with $\text{d}-\text{d}$ transitions absorbing red light, appearing green (Statement I is true). $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{4}\right]^{2-}$ is square planar and diamagnetic with large $\Delta$, absorbing in the UV region and transmitting all visible light, thus colourless (Statement II is true).

questions.text: The number of paramagnetic species from the following is _______ . $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{4}\right]^{2-}$, $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CO}\right)_{4}\right]$, $\left[\text{NiCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}$, $\left[\text{Fe}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{6}\right]^{4-}$, $\left[\text{Cu}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{4}\right]^{2+}$, $\left[\text{Fe}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{6}\right]^{3-}$ and $\left[\text{Fe}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Identify species having at least one unpaired electron ($n \ge 1$). // 📝 Solution: Paramagnetic species: $\left[\text{NiCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}\;\left(3\text{d}^{8},\;n = 2\right)$, $\left[\text{Cu}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{4}\right]^{2+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{9},\;n = 1\right)$, $\left[\text{Fe}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{6}\right]^{3-}\;\left(3\text{d}^{5}\;\text{low spin},\;n = 1\right)$, and $\left[\text{Fe}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{6}\;\text{high spin},\;n = 4\right)$. Total $= 4$.

questions.text: Given below are two statements : Statement I : Crystal Field Stabilization Energy (CFSE) of $\left[\text{Cr}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+}$ is greater than that of $\left[\text{Mn}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+}$. Statement II: Potassium ferricyanide has a greater spin-only magnetic moment than sodium ferrocyanide. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Calculate CFSE using $\text{t}_{2\text{g}}-\text{e}_{\text{g}}$ occupancy and determine magnetic moments from unpaired electrons. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Cr}^{2+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{4},\;\text{WFL}\right) \implies \text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{3}\;\text{e}_{\text{g}}^{1} \implies \text{CFSE} = -0.6\,\Delta_{\text{o}}$; $\text{Mn}^{2+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{5},\;\text{WFL}\right) \implies \text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{3}\;\text{e}_{\text{g}}^{2} \implies \text{CFSE} = 0 \implies \left\lvert -0.6\,\Delta_{\text{o}} \right\rvert > 0$ (Statement I is true). $\text{K}_{3}\left[\text{Fe}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{6}\right]\;\left(\text{Fe}^{3+},\;n = 1\right) \implies \mu = \sqrt{3}\;\text{BM}$; $\text{Na}_{4}\left[\text{Fe}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{6}\right]\;\left(\text{Fe}^{2+},\;n = 0\right) \implies \mu = 0$ (Statement II is true).

questions.text: $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}$ and $\left[\text{CoF}_{6}\right]^{3-}$ are respectively known as:

options.text: Spin free Complex, Spin paired Complex
Spin paired Complex, Spin free Complex
Outer orbital Complex, Inner orbital Complex
Inner orbital Complex, Spin paired Complex

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Strong field ligand complexes have paired spins (low spin); weak field ligands leave spins unpaired (high spin). // 📝 Solution: In $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}$, strong field $\text{NH}_{3}$ causes complete electron pairing $\implies$ spin paired (low spin). In $\left[\text{CoF}_{6}\right]^{3-}$, weak field $\text{F}^{-}$ cannot pair electrons $\implies$ spin free (high spin).

questions.text: The spin only magnetic moment of $\left[\text{Mn}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+}$ complexes is _______ $\text{B.M.}$ (Nearest integer)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mu = \sqrt{n\left(n + 2\right)}\;\text{BM}$. // 📝 Solution: In $\left[\text{Mn}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+}$, $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ has $3\text{d}^{5}$ configuration. With weak field ligand $\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$, $n = 5 \implies \mu = \sqrt{5\left(5 + 2\right)} = \sqrt{35} \approx 5.91\;\text{BM} \approx 6\;\text{BM}$.

questions.text: If an iron (III) complex with the formula $\left[\text{Fe}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{x}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{y}\right]^{-}$ has no electron in its $\text{e}_{\text{g}}$ orbital, then the value of $x + y$ is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Octahedral complexes have coordination number 6 and an $\text{e}_{\text{g}}$ upper set. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Fe}^{3+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{5}\right)$ with strong field ligands pairs into $\text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{5}\;\text{e}_{\text{g}}^{0}$, meaning no electrons occupy $\text{e}_{\text{g}}$. The geometry is octahedral, so coordination number $= x + y = 6$. Charge balance: $+3 + x\left(0\right) - y = -1 \implies y = 4 \implies x = 2 \implies x + y = 6$.
