questions.text: The correct IUPAC name of $\text{K}_{2}\text{MnO}_{4}$ is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For an anionic complex, add suffix '-ate' to the metal name followed by oxidation state in Roman numerals. // 📝 Solution: In $\text{K}_{2}\text{MnO}_{4}$, oxidation state of $\text{Mn}$ is $x \implies 2\left(+1\right) + x + 4\left(-2\right) = 0 \implies x = +6$. The oxide ligands are named 'oxido' $\implies$ Potassium tetraoxidomanganate(VI).

questions.text: The crystal field splitting energy of $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{oxalate}\right)_{3}\right]^{3-}$ complex is '$n$' times that of the $\left[\text{Cr}\left(\text{oxalate}\right)_{3}\right]^{3-}$ complex. Here '$n$' is _______ . (Assume $\Delta_{0} \gg P$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\text{CFSE} = \left[-0.4 \times n\left(\text{t}_{2\text{g}}\right) + 0.6 \times n\left(\text{e}_{\text{g}}\right)\right]\Delta_{\text{o}}$. // 📝 Solution: For $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{ox}\right)_{3}\right]^{3-}: \text{Co}^{3+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{6},\;\text{low spin}\right) \implies \text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{6}\;\text{e}_{\text{g}}^{0} \implies \text{CFSE} = 6\left(-0.4\,\Delta_{\text{o}}\right) = -2.4\,\Delta_{\text{o}}$. For $\left[\text{Cr}\left(\text{ox}\right)_{3}\right]^{3-}: \text{Cr}^{3+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{3}\right) \implies \text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{3}\;\text{e}_{\text{g}}^{0} \implies \text{CFSE} = 3\left(-0.4\,\Delta_{\text{o}}\right) = -1.2\,\Delta_{\text{o}} \implies n = \frac{2.4\,\Delta_{\text{o}}}{1.2\,\Delta_{\text{o}}} = 2$.

questions.text: Chiral complex from the following is [Here $\text{en} = \text{ethylene diamine}$]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A chiral complex lacks plane of symmetry (POS) and centre of inversion (COS). // 📝 Solution: $\text{cis}-\left[\text{PtCl}_{2}\left(\text{en}\right)_{2}\right]^{2+}$ lacks both plane of symmetry and centre of inversion [FIGURE], making it non-superimposable on its mirror image and optically active. Trans-isomers and square planar complexes possess a plane of symmetry.

questions.text: The complex cation which has two isomers is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Ambidentate ligands give rise to linkage isomerism. // 📝 Solution: $\text{NO}_{2}^{-}$ is an ambidentate ligand that coordinates via $\text{N}$ ($-\text{NO}_{2}$, nitro) or $\text{O}$ ($-\text{ONO}$, nitrito), producing two linkage isomers: $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{5}\left(\text{NO}_{2}\right)\right]^{2+}$ and $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{5}\left(\text{ONO}\right)\right]^{2+}$.

questions.text: Aluminium chloride in acidified aqueous solution forms an ion having geometry
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\text{Al}^{3+}$ expands its coordination number to six in water. // 📝 Solution: In acidified aqueous solution, $\text{AlCl}_{3}$ dissolves to form the hexaaqua complex ion $\left[\text{Al}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}$ involving $\text{d}^{2}\text{sp}^{3}$ hybridization and an octahedral geometry.

questions.text: $1\;\text{L},\;0.02\;\text{M}$ solution of $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{5}\text{SO}_{4}\right]\text{Br}$ is mixed with $1\;\text{L},\;0.02\;\text{M}$ solution of $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{5}\text{Br}\right]\text{SO}_{4}$. The resulting solution is divided into two equal parts $(\text{X})$ and treated with excess $\text{AgNO}_{3}$ solution and $\text{BaCl}_{2}$ solution respectively as shown below: $1\;\text{L Solution (X)} + \text{AgNO}_{3}\;\text{solution (excess)} \rightarrow \text{Y}$; $1\;\text{L Solution (X)} + \text{BaCl}_{2}\;\text{solution (excess)} \rightarrow \text{Z}$. The number of moles of $\text{Y}$ and $\text{Z}$ respectively are
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Equal volume division halves the total moles of free $\text{Br}^{-}$ and $\text{SO}_{4}^{2-}$ in the mixture. // 📝 Solution: Total solution ($2\;\text{L}$) contains $0.02\;\text{mol}\;\text{Br}^{-}$ and $0.02\;\text{mol}\;\text{SO}_{4}^{2-}$. Half portion ($1\;\text{L}$) has $0.01\;\text{mol}\;\text{Br}^{-}$ and $0.01\;\text{mol}\;\text{SO}_{4}^{2-} \implies \text{Moles of Y}\;(\text{AgBr}) = 0.01$ and $\text{Moles of Z}\;(\text{BaSO}_{4}) = 0.01$.

questions.text: $\text{X}$ is the number of geometrical isomers exhibited by $\left[\text{Pt}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)\text{BrCl}\right]$. $\text{Y}$ is the number of optically inactive isomer(s) exhibited by $\left[\text{CrCl}_{2}\left(\text{ox}\right)_{2}\right]^{3-}$. $\text{Z}$ is the number of geometrical isomers exhibited by $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{3}\left(\text{NO}_{2}\right)_{3}\right]$. The value of $\text{X} + \text{Y} + \text{Z}$ is _______ .
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Square planar $\left[\text{Mabcd}\right]$ has 3 geometrical isomers; octahedral $\left[\text{M}\left(\text{AA}\right)_{2}\text{b}_{2}\right]$ has an inactive trans isomer; $\left[\text{Ma}_{3}\text{b}_{3}\right]$ has $\text{fac}$ and $\text{mer}$ isomers. // 📝 Solution: $\text{X} = 3$ for square planar $\left[\text{Mabcd}\right]$. $\text{Y} = 1$ for $\left[\text{CrCl}_{2}\left(\text{ox}\right)_{2}\right]^{3-}$ as the trans isomer has a plane of symmetry (optically inactive). $\text{Z} = 2$ for $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{3}\left(\text{NO}_{2}\right)_{3}\right]$ ($\text{fac}$ and $\text{mer}$). $\text{X} + \text{Y} + \text{Z} = 3 + 1 + 2 = 6$.

questions.text: The number of isoelectronic species among $\text{Sc}^{3+}, \text{Cr}^{2+}, \text{Mn}^{3+}, \text{Co}^{3+}$ and $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ is '$n$'. If '$n$' moles of $\text{AgCl}$ is formed during the reaction of complex with formula $\text{CoCl}_{3}\left(\text{en}\right)_{2}\text{NH}_{3}$ with excess of $\text{AgNO}_{3}$ solution, then the number of electrons present in the $\text{t}_{2\text{g}}$ orbital of the complex is _______ .
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Electron counts: $\text{Cr}^{2+}$ and $\text{Mn}^{3+}$ have $22$ electrons ($n = 2$); write the Werner coordination formula. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Cr}^{2+}\;\left(22\text{e}^{-}\right)$ and $\text{Mn}^{3+}\;\left(22\text{e}^{-}\right)$ are isoelectronic $\implies n = 2$. $2\;\text{mol}\;\text{AgCl}$ indicates formula $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{en}\right)_{2}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)\text{Cl}\right]\text{Cl}_{2}$ with central $\text{Co}^{3+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{6}\right)$. Strong field ligands induce a low spin state $\text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{6}\;\text{e}_{\text{g}}^{0} \implies$ electrons in $\text{t}_{2\text{g}} = 6$.

questions.text: The coordination environment of $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ ion in its complex with $\text{EDTA}^{4-}$ is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\text{EDTA}^{4-}$ acts as a hexadentate chelate ligand towards metal ions. // 📝 Solution: $\text{EDTA}^{4-}$ coordinates to $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ through two nitrogen donor atoms and four oxygen atoms from carboxylate groups, forming a six-coordinate $\left[\text{Ca}\left(\text{EDTA}\right)\right]^{2-}$ complex with an octahedral coordination geometry.

questions.text: Number of Complexes with even number of electrons in $\text{t}_{2\text{g}}$ orbitals is - $\left[\text{Fe}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+}$, $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+}$, $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}$, $\left[\text{Cu}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+}$, $\left[\text{Cr}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Distribute d-electrons into $\text{t}_{2\text{g}}$ and $\text{e}_{\text{g}}$ based on weak/strong field nature of $\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$. // 📝 Solution: $\left[\text{Fe}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+}: 3\text{d}^{6}\;(\text{WFL}) \implies \text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{4}\;\text{e}_{\text{g}}^{2}$ (4 is even); $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+}: 3\text{d}^{7}\;(\text{WFL}) \implies \text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{5}\;\text{e}_{\text{g}}^{2}$ (5 is odd); $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}: 3\text{d}^{6}\;(\text{SFL}) \implies \text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{6}\;\text{e}_{\text{g}}^{0}$ (6 is even); $\left[\text{Cu}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+}: 3\text{d}^{9} \implies \text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{6}\;\text{e}_{\text{g}}^{3}$ (6 is even); $\left[\text{Cr}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+}: 3\text{d}^{4}\;(\text{WFL}) \implies \text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{3}\;\text{e}_{\text{g}}^{1}$ (3 is odd). Total complexes $= 3$.

questions.text: The following complexes: $\left[\text{CoCl}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{5}\right]^{2+}\;(\text{A})$, $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{6}\right]^{3-}\;(\text{B})$, $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{5}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)\right]^{3+}\;(\text{C})$, $\left[\text{Cu}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{4}\right]^{2+}\;(\text{D})$. The correct order of $\text{A, B, C}$ and $\text{D}$ in terms of wavenumber of light absorbed is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Wavenumber of absorbed light is directly proportional to crystal field splitting ($\bar{\nu} \propto \Delta$). // 📝 Solution: For $\text{Co}^{3+}$, ligand field strength: $\text{CN}^{-} > \text{NH}_{3}/\text{H}_{2}\text{O} > \text{NH}_{3}/\text{Cl}^{-} \implies \Delta(\text{B}) > \Delta(\text{C}) > \Delta(\text{A})$. $\text{Cu}^{2+}\;(\text{D})$ has a lower oxidation state and fewer ligands, giving the lowest $\Delta \implies \text{D} < \text{A} < \text{C} < \text{B}$.

questions.text: The correct IUPAC name of $\left[\text{PtBr}_{2}\left(\text{PMe}_{3}\right)_{2}\right]$ is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Alphabetical order of ligands determines naming; complex neutral ligands take the prefix 'bis'. // 📝 Solution: In $\left[\text{PtBr}_{2}\left(\text{PMe}_{3}\right)_{2}\right]$, ligands are bromo and trimethylphosphine. Alphabetically: 'bromo' precedes 'trimethylphosphine'. Platinum has oxidation state $+2 \implies$ dibromobis(trimethylphosphine)platinum(II).

questions.text: The number of hydrogen atoms in the red precipitate formed when $\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}$ reacts with dimethylglyoxime in ammoniacal medium is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Dimethylglyoxime $\left(\mathrm{C_4H_8N_2O_2}\right)$ loses one H per ligand on forming $\left[\mathrm{Ni}\left(\mathrm{dmg}\right)_2\right]$. // 📝 Solution: $2\left(8 \;-\; 1\right) \;=\; 14$ hydrogen atoms

questions.text: The coordination geometry around the manganese in decacarbonyldimanganese(0) is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Count the $\text{Mn}-\text{CO}$ bonds plus the $\text{Mn}-\text{Mn}$ metal-metal single bond. // 📝 Solution: In $\text{Mn}_{2}\left(\text{CO}\right)_{10}$, each manganese atom is bonded to five terminal carbonyl ligands and one other manganese atom via an $\text{Mn}-\text{Mn}$ bond [FIGURE], completing an octahedral coordination geometry around each $\text{Mn}$ center.

questions.text: Cobalt chloride when dissolved in water forms pink colored complex $\text{X}$ which has octahedral geometry. This solution on treating with conc $\text{HCl}$ forms deep blue complex, $\text{Y}$ which has a $\text{Z}$ geometry. $\text{X}$, $\text{Y}$ and $\text{Z}$, respectively, are
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+} + 4\text{Cl}^{-} \rightleftharpoons \left[\text{CoCl}_{4}\right]^{2-} + 6\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$. // 📝 Solution: In water, cobalt chloride forms pink octahedral $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+}\;(\text{X})$. Upon reaction with conc. $\text{HCl}$, tetrahedral deep blue $\left[\text{CoCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}\;(\text{Y})$ is formed with tetrahedral geometry $(\text{Z})$.

questions.text: The molecule/ion with square pyramidal shape is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A steric number of 6 with 5 bonding pairs and 1 lone pair gives a square pyramidal shape. // 📝 Solution: $\text{BrF}_{5}$ has 5 bond pairs and 1 lone pair on bromine ($5 + 1 = 6 \implies \text{sp}^{3}\text{d}^{2}$) [FIGURE], producing a square pyramidal geometry. $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{4}\right]^{2-}$ is square planar; $\text{PCl}_{5}$ and $\text{PF}_{5}$ are trigonal bipyramidal.

questions.text: Select the option with correct property -
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Strong field $\text{CO}$ forces pairing of 4s electrons into 3d; weak field $\text{Cl}^{-}$ leaves unpaired electrons in tetrahedral geometry. // 📝 Solution: In $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CO}\right)_{4}\right]$, $\text{Ni}^{0}\;\left(3\text{d}^{8}4\text{s}^{2}\right)$ rearranges to fully paired $3\text{d}^{10}\;(\text{sp}^{3}) \implies n = 0$ (diamagnetic). In $\left[\text{NiCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}$, $\text{Ni}^{2+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{8}\right)$ forms a high-spin tetrahedral complex with $\text{e}^{4}\;\text{t}_{2}^{4} \implies n = 2$ (paramagnetic).

questions.text: Identity the incorrect pair from the following:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Identify the metal chloride catalyst used in the commercial Wacker oxidation of alkenes. // 📝 Solution: The Wacker process for the oxidation of ethene to ethanal uses palladium(II) chloride ($\text{PdCl}_{2}$) as catalyst in the presence of $\text{CuCl}_{2}$, not $\text{PtCl}_{2}$. Thus, pair (4) is incorrect.

questions.text: Which one of the following complexes will exhibit the least paramagnetic behaviour? [Atomic number, $\text{Cr} = 24, \text{Mn} = 25, \text{Fe} = 26, \text{Co} = 27$]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Least paramagnetic behavior corresponds to the minimum number of unpaired electrons $n$. // 📝 Solution: Unpaired electrons with weak field $\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$: $\text{Cr}^{2+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{4}\right) \implies n = 4$; $\text{Fe}^{2+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{6}\right) \implies n = 4$; $\text{Mn}^{2+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{5}\right) \implies n = 5$; $\text{Co}^{2+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{7}\right) \implies n = 3$. Smallest $n = 3$ belongs to $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+}$ ($\mu = 3.87\;\text{BM}$).

questions.text: A chromium complex with a formula $\text{CrCl}_{3} \cdot 6\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$ has a spin only magnetic moment value of $3.87\;\text{BM}$ and its solution conductivity corresponds to $1 : 2$ electrolyte. $2.75\;\text{g}$ of the complex solution was initially passed through a cation exchanger. The solution obtained after the process was reacted with excess of $\text{AgNO}_{3}$. The amount of $\text{AgCl}$ formed in the above process is _______ $\text{g}$. (Nearest integer) [Given: Molar mass in $\text{g}\cdot\text{mol}^{-1}$: $\text{Cr} : 52; \text{Cl} : 35.5, \text{Ag} : 108, \text{O} : 16, \text{H} : 1$]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $1:2$ electrolyte corresponds to $\left[\text{Cr}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{5}\text{Cl}\right]\text{Cl}_{2} \cdot \text{H}_{2}\text{O}$ having $2$ ionizable $\text{Cl}^{-}$ per formula unit. // 📝 Solution: Complex is $\left[\text{Cr}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{5}\text{Cl}\right]\text{Cl}_{2} \cdot \text{H}_{2}\text{O}\;(M = 285.5\;\text{g}/\text{mol})$. $\text{Moles} = \frac{2.75}{285.5} \approx 0.00963\;\text{mol} \implies n(\text{Cl}^{-}) = 2 \times 0.00963 = 0.01926\;\text{mol}$. $\text{Mass of AgCl} = 0.01926 \times 143.5 \approx 2.76\;\text{g} \approx 3\;\text{g}$.

questions.text: The correct statement among the following is: (1) $\text{Ni}\left(\text{CO}\right)_{4}$ and $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{4}\right]^{2-}$ are diamagnetic and $\left[\text{NiCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}$ is paramagnetic. (2) $\text{Ni}\left(\text{CO}\right)_{4}$ and $\left[\text{NiCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}$ are diamagnetic and $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{4}\right]^{2-}$ is paramagnetic. (3) $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{4}\right]^{2-}$ and $\left[\text{NiCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}$ are diamagnetic and $\text{Ni}\left(\text{CO}\right)_{4}$ is paramagnetic. (4) $\text{Ni}\left(\text{CO}\right)_{4}$ is diamagnetic and $\left[\text{NiCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}$ and $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{4}\right]^{2-}$ are paramagnetic.

options.text: $\text{Ni}\left(\text{CO}\right)_{4}$ and $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{4}\right]^{2-}$ are diamagnetic and $\left[\text{NiCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}$ is paramagnetic.
$\text{Ni}\left(\text{CO}\right)_{4}$ and $\left[\text{NiCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}$ are diamagnetic and $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{4}\right]^{2-}$ is paramagnetic.
$\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{4}\right]^{2-}$ and $\left[\text{NiCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}$ are diamagnetic and $\text{Ni}\left(\text{CO}\right)_{4}$ is paramagnetic.
$\text{Ni}\left(\text{CO}\right)_{4}$ is diamagnetic and $\left[\text{NiCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}$ and $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{4}\right]^{2-}$ are paramagnetic.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Strong field ligands pair d-electrons in $\text{Ni(0)}$ and $\text{Ni(II)}$; weak field halide ligands preserve unpaired spins in tetrahedral geometry. // 📝 Solution: In $\text{Ni}\left(\text{CO}\right)_{4}$, $\text{Ni}^{0}$ pairs into $3\text{d}^{10}\;(\text{sp}^{3},\;n = 0)$. In $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{4}\right]^{2-}$, $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ pairs into square planar $\text{dsp}^{2}\;(n = 0)$. Both are diamagnetic. In $\left[\text{NiCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}$, $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ forms high-spin tetrahedral $\text{sp}^{3}\;(n = 2)$, which is paramagnetic.

questions.text: Which of the following complex will show largest splitting of d-orbitals?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Crystal field splitting $\Delta_{\text{o}}$ increases with ligand field strength according to the spectrochemical series. // 📝 Solution: $\text{CN}^{-}$ is the strongest field ligand among the choices ($\text{CN}^{-} > \text{NH}_{3} > \text{C}_{2}\text{O}_{4}^{2-} > \text{F}^{-}$), causing the maximum splitting $\Delta_{\text{o}}$ in $\left[\text{Fe}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{6}\right]^{3-}$.

questions.text: Which of the following cannot be explained by crystal field theory?

options.text: Magnetic properties of transition metal complexes

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Crystal field theory assumes purely electrostatic interactions and cannot theoretically justify certain empirical properties. // 📝 Solution: CFT treats ligands as point charges and fails to explain the spectrochemical series theoretically, though thermodynamic stability is also an empirical result of chelation and CFSE. Per official answer key, option (4) is given.

questions.text: The number of unpaired d-electrons in $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}$ is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\text{Co}^{3+}$ has high charge density, rendering water a strong field ligand ($\Delta_{\text{o}} > P$). // 📝 Solution: In $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}$, $\text{Co}^{3+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{6}\right)$ is in a low-spin configuration: $\text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{6}\;\text{e}_{\text{g}}^{0}$ [FIGURE]. All d-electrons are paired, so the number of unpaired electrons is $0$.

questions.text: Which of the following complex is homoleptic?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Homoleptic complexes have central metal bonded to only one kind of donor group/ligand. // 📝 Solution: In $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{4}\right]^{2-}$, all four ligands are identical cyanide ions ($\text{CN}^{-}$), so it is homoleptic. The other complexes have two different ligands and are heteroleptic.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The number of paramagnetic species among $\left[\text{CoF}_{6}\right]^{3-}$, $\left[\text{TiF}_{6}\right]^{3-}$, $\text{V}_{2}\text{O}_{5}$ and $\left[\text{Fe}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{6}\right]^{3-}$ is 3. Statement II: $\text{K}_{4}\left[\text{Fe}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{6}\right] < \text{K}_{3}\left[\text{Fe}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{6}\right] < \left[\text{Fe}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]\text{SO}_{4} \cdot \text{H}_{2}\text{O} < \left[\text{Fe}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]\text{Cl}_{3}$ is the correct order in terms of number of unpaired electron(s) present in the complexes. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Evaluate unpaired electrons $n$ for each complex based on metal oxidation state and ligand field strength. // 📝 Solution: In Statement I: $\left[\text{CoF}_{6}\right]^{3-}\;(n = 4)$, $\left[\text{TiF}_{6}\right]^{3-}\;(n = 1)$, and $\left[\text{Fe}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{6}\right]^{3-}\;(n = 1)$ are paramagnetic; $\text{V}_{2}\text{O}_{5}\;(3\text{d}^{0},\;n = 0)$ is diamagnetic $\implies 3$ paramagnetic species (True). In Statement II: Unpaired electrons are $0 < 1 < 4 < 5$, which matches the given sequence (True).

questions.text: Total number of unpaired electrons in the complex ions $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}$ and $\left[\text{NiCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}$ is _______ .
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Strong field ligand causes pairing in $\text{Co}^{3+}$; tetrahedral $\left[\text{NiCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}$ retains high spin. // 📝 Solution: In $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}$, $\text{Co}^{3+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{6}\right)$ with $\text{SFL}\;\text{NH}_{3}$ pairs into $\text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{6}\;\text{e}_{\text{g}}^{0} \implies n_{1} = 0$. In $\left[\text{NiCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}$, $\text{Ni}^{2+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{8}\right)$ in tetrahedral geometry has configuration $\text{e}^{4}\;\text{t}_{2}^{4} \implies n_{2} = 2$. Total unpaired electrons $= 0 + 2 = 2$.

questions.text: Match List - I with List - II. List - I (Complex ion): (A) $\left[\text{Cr}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}$, (B) $\left[\text{NiCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}$, (C) $\left[\text{CoF}_{6}\right]^{3-}$, (D) $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{4}\right]^{2-}$. List - II (Spin only magnetic moment in B.M.): (I) 4.90, (II) 3.87, (III) 0.0, (IV) 2.83. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Calculate number of unpaired electrons $n$ and use $\mu = \sqrt{n\left(n + 2\right)}\;\text{BM}$. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Cr}^{3+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{3}\right) \implies n = 3,\;\mu = \sqrt{15} \approx 3.87\;\text{BM}\;(\text{II})$; $\left[\text{NiCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}\;\left(3\text{d}^{8},\;\text{Td}\right) \implies n = 2,\;\mu = \sqrt{8} \approx 2.83\;\text{BM}\;(\text{IV})$; $\left[\text{CoF}_{6}\right]^{3-}\;\left(3\text{d}^{6},\;\text{WFL}\right) \implies n = 4,\;\mu = \sqrt{24} \approx 4.90\;\text{BM}\;(\text{I})$; $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{4}\right]^{2-}\;\left(3\text{d}^{8},\;\text{sq. pl.}\right) \implies n = 0,\;\mu = 0.0\;\text{BM}\;(\text{III})$.

questions.text: Identify the metal ions among $\text{Co}^{2+}, \text{Ni}^{2+}, \text{Fe}^{2+}, \text{V}^{3+}$ and $\text{Ti}^{2+}$ having a spin-only magnetic moment value more than $3.0\;\text{BM}$. The sum of unpaired electrons present in the high spin octahedral complexes formed by those metal ions is _______ .
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For $\mu > 3.0\;\text{BM}$, the number of unpaired electrons must satisfy $n \ge 3$. // 📝 Solution: For high spin octahedral: $\text{Co}^{2+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{7}\right) \implies n = 3\;(\mu = 3.87\;\text{BM})$; $\text{Ni}^{2+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{8}\right) \implies n = 2$; $\text{Fe}^{2+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{6}\right) \implies n = 4\;(\mu = 4.90\;\text{BM})$; $\text{V}^{3+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{2}\right) \implies n = 2$; $\text{Ti}^{2+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{2}\right) \implies n = 2$. Ions with $\mu > 3.0\;\text{BM}$ are $\text{Co}^{2+}$ and $\text{Fe}^{2+} \implies \text{Sum} = 3 + 4 = 7$.

questions.text: $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{PPh}_{3}\right)_{2}\text{Cl}_{2}\right]$ is a paramagnetic complex. Identify the INCORRECT statements about this complex. A. The complex exhibits geometrical isomerism. B. The complex is white in colour. C. The calculated spin-only magnetic moment of the complex is $2.84\;\text{BM}$. D. The calculated CFSE (Crystal Field Stabilization Energy) of $\text{Ni}$ in this complex is $-0.8\,\Delta_{\text{o}}$. E. The geometrical arrangement of ligands in this complex is similar to that in $\text{Ni}\left(\text{CO}\right)_{4}$. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: 4-coordinate paramagnetic $\text{Ni(II)}$ is tetrahedral ($\text{sp}^{3}$); tetrahedral complexes do not show geometrical isomerism. // 📝 Solution: Paramagnetic $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{PPh}_{3}\right)_{2}\text{Cl}_{2}\right]$ is tetrahedral ($n = 2,\;\mu = \sqrt{8} \approx 2.83\;\text{BM}$). Tetrahedral complexes do not show geometrical isomerism (A is incorrect). It is colored blue/green, not white (B is incorrect). Its CFSE is $-0.8\,\Delta_{\text{t}}$, not $-0.8\,\Delta_{\text{o}}$ (D is incorrect). Incorrect statements: A, B, and D.

questions.text: Number of complexes from the following with even number of unpaired "d" electrons is _______ $\left[\text{V}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}$, $\left[\text{Cr}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+}$, $\left[\text{Fe}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}$, $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}$, $\left[\text{Cu}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+}$ [Given atomic numbers : $\text{V} = 23, \text{Cr} = 24, \text{Fe} = 26, \text{Ni} = 28, \text{Cu} = 29$]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Count unpaired electrons for each metal ion in the high-spin octahedral state with $\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$. // 📝 Solution: $\text{V}^{3+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{2}\right) \implies n = 2$ (even); $\text{Cr}^{2+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{4}\right) \implies n = 4$ (even); $\text{Fe}^{3+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{5}\right) \implies n = 5$ (odd); $\text{Ni}^{3+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{7}\right) \implies n = 3$ (odd); $\text{Cu}^{2+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{9}\right) \implies n = 1$ (odd). Thus, exactly $2$ complexes have an even number of unpaired electrons.

questions.text: Total number of moles of $\text{AgCl}$ precipitated on addition of excess of $\text{AgNO}_{3}$ to one mole each of the following complexes $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{4}\text{Cl}_{2}\right]\text{Cl}$, $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]\text{Cl}_{2}$, $\left[\text{Pt}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{2}\text{Cl}_{2}\right]$ and $\left[\text{Pd}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{4}\right]\text{Cl}_{2}$ is _______ .
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Only chloride ions present in the outer ionization sphere are precipitated by $\text{AgNO}_{3}$. // 📝 Solution: Ionizable chloride ions: $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{4}\text{Cl}_{2}\right]\text{Cl} \implies 1\;\text{mol}$, $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]\text{Cl}_{2} \implies 2\;\text{mol}$, $\left[\text{Pt}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{2}\text{Cl}_{2}\right] \implies 0\;\text{mol}$, $\left[\text{Pd}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{4}\right]\text{Cl}_{2} \implies 2\;\text{mol}$. Total moles $= 1 + 2 + 0 + 2 = 5$.

questions.text: The wavelength of light absorbed for the following complexes are in the order $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}\;(\text{I})$; $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}\;(\text{II})$; $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{6}\right]^{3-}\;(\text{III})$; $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{5}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)\right]^{3+}\;(\text{IV})$; $\left[\text{CoF}_{6}\right]^{3-}\;(\text{V})$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\lambda_{\text{absorbed}} \propto \frac{1}{\Delta_{\text{o}}}$; ligand field strength determines $\Delta_{\text{o}}$. // 📝 Solution: Ligand field strength: $\text{CN}^{-} > \text{NH}_{3} > \text{H}_{2}\text{O} > \text{F}^{-} \implies \Delta_{\text{o}}(\text{III}) > \Delta_{\text{o}}(\text{I}) > \Delta_{\text{o}}(\text{IV}) > \Delta_{\text{o}}(\text{II}) > \Delta_{\text{o}}(\text{V})$. Since $\lambda \propto \frac{1}{\Delta_{\text{o}}} \implies \text{III} < \text{I} < \text{IV} < \text{II} < \text{V}$.

questions.text: Identify from the following species in which $\text{d}^{2}\text{sp}^{3}$ hybridization is shown by central atom:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: An octahedral complex with vacant inner (n-1)d orbitals shows $\text{d}^{2}\text{sp}^{3}$ hybridization. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Co}^{3+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{6}\right)$ with strong field ligand $\text{NH}_{3}$ pairs completely into $\text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{6}\;\text{e}_{\text{g}}^{0}$, providing two inner $3\text{d}$ orbitals $\implies \text{d}^{2}\text{sp}^{3}$. $\text{BrF}_{5}$ and $\text{SF}_{6}$ are $\text{sp}^{3}\text{d}^{2}$; $\left[\text{PtCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}$ is $\text{dsp}^{2}$.

questions.text: If the $\text{CFSE}$ of $\left[\text{Ti}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}$ is $-96.0\;\text{kJ}/\text{mol}$, this complex will absorb maximum at wavelength _______ $\text{nm}$. (nearest integer) Assume Planck's constant $(h) = 6.4 \times 10^{-34}\;\text{J}\cdot\text{s}$, Speed of light $(c) = 3.0 \times 10^{8}\;\text{m}/\text{s}$ and Avogadro's constant $(N_{\text{A}}) = 6 \times 10^{23}/\text{mol}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\text{CFSE} = -0.4\,\Delta_{\text{o}}$ for a $\text{d}^{1}$ ion; $\Delta_{\text{o}} = \frac{N_{\text{A}}hc}{\lambda}$. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Ti}^{3+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{1}\right) \implies \text{CFSE} = -0.4\,\Delta_{\text{o}} = -96.0 \times 10^{3}\;\text{J}/\text{mol} \implies \Delta_{\text{o}} = 240 \times 10^{3}\;\text{J}/\text{mol}$. Thus, $\lambda = \frac{N_{\text{A}}hc}{\Delta_{\text{o}}} = \frac{6 \times 10^{23} \times 6.4 \times 10^{-34} \times 3 \times 10^{8}}{240 \times 10^{3}} = 4.8 \times 10^{-7}\;\text{m} = 480\;\text{nm}$.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: LIST - I (Complex ion): A. $\left[\text{Cr}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}$, B. $\left[\text{Fe}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}$, C. $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+}$, D. $\left[\text{V}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}$. LIST - II (Electronic Configuration): I. $\text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{2}\;\text{e}_{\text{g}}^{0}$, II. $\text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{3}\;\text{e}_{\text{g}}^{0}$, III. $\text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{3}\;\text{e}_{\text{g}}^{2}$, IV. $\text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{6}\;\text{e}_{\text{g}}^{2}$. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: High spin octahedral electronic configurations depend on metal oxidation state and d-electron count. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Cr}^{3+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{3}\right) \implies \text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{3}\;\text{e}_{\text{g}}^{0}\;(\text{II})$; $\text{Fe}^{3+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{5}\right) \implies \text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{3}\;\text{e}_{\text{g}}^{2}\;(\text{III})$; $\text{Ni}^{2+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{8}\right) \implies \text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{6}\;\text{e}_{\text{g}}^{2}\;(\text{IV})$; $\text{V}^{3+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{2}\right) \implies \text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{2}\;\text{e}_{\text{g}}^{0}\;(\text{I})$.

questions.text: An octahedral complex with the formula $\text{CoCl}_{3} \cdot n\text{NH}_{3}$ upon reaction with excess of $\text{AgNO}_{3}$ solution gives $2$ moles of $\text{AgCl}$. Consider the oxidation state of $\text{Co}$ in the complex is '$x$'. The value of "$x + n$" is _______
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Precipitation of $2$ moles of $\text{AgCl}$ means $2$ chloride ions are outside the coordination sphere. // 📝 Solution: Complex giving $2\;\text{mol}\;\text{AgCl}$ has the formula $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{n}\text{Cl}\right]\text{Cl}_{2}$. Since coordination number $= 6 \implies n + 1 = 6 \implies n = 5$. Oxidation state of $\text{Co}$ is $x = +3 \implies x + n = 3 + 5 = 8$.

questions.text: Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A) : The total number of geometrical isomers shown by $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{en}\right)_{2}\text{Cl}_{2}\right]^{+}$ complex ion is three. Reason (R): $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{en}\right)_{2}\text{Cl}_{2}\right]^{+}$ complex ion has an octahedral geometry. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\left[\text{M}\left(\text{AA}\right)_{2}\text{B}_{2}\right]$ complexes display only cis and trans geometrical forms. // 📝 Solution: Octahedral complex $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{en}\right)_{2}\text{Cl}_{2}\right]^{+}$ exhibits only two geometrical isomers: cis and trans [FIGURE] $\implies$ (A) is false. Its coordination number is $6 \implies$ geometry is octahedral $\implies$ (R) is true.

questions.text: The number of complexes from the following with no electrons in the $\text{t}_{2}$ orbital is _______ $\text{TiCl}_{4}$, $\left[\text{MnO}_{4}\right]^{-}$, $\left[\text{FeO}_{4}\right]^{2-}$, $\left[\text{FeCl}_{4}\right]^{-}$, $\left[\text{CoCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: In tetrahedral splitting, orbitals split into lower $\text{e}$ and higher $\text{t}_{2}$. // 📝 Solution: Configurations: $\text{TiCl}_{4}\;\left(\text{Ti}^{4+},\;3\text{d}^{0}\right): \text{e}^{0}\;\text{t}_{2}^{0}$; $\left[\text{MnO}_{4}\right]^{-}\;\left(\text{Mn}^{7+},\;3\text{d}^{0}\right): \text{e}^{0}\;\text{t}_{2}^{0}$; $\left[\text{FeO}_{4}\right]^{2-}\;\left(\text{Fe}^{6+},\;3\text{d}^{2}\right): \text{e}^{2}\;\text{t}_{2}^{0}$; $\left[\text{FeCl}_{4}\right]^{-}\;\left(\text{Fe}^{3+},\;3\text{d}^{5}\right): \text{e}^{2}\;\text{t}_{2}^{3}$; $\left[\text{CoCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}\;\left(\text{Co}^{2+},\;3\text{d}^{7}\right): \text{e}^{4}\;\text{t}_{2}^{3}$. Number of complexes with zero $\text{t}_{2}$ electrons $= 3$.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List - I (Compound): A. Iodoform, B. Carbon tetrachloride, C. CFC, D. DDT. List - II (Uses): I. Fire extinguisher, II. Insecticide, III. Antiseptic, IV. Refrigerants. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Match compounds with their primary industrial and medical applications. // 📝 Solution: Iodoform is an antiseptic (A-III); $\text{CCl}_{4}$ is a fire extinguisher (B-I); CFCs are refrigerants (C-IV); DDT is an insecticide (D-II).

questions.text: Choose the correct Statements from the following: (A) Ethane-1,2-diamine is a chelating ligand. (B) Metallic aluminium is produced by electrolysis of aluminium oxide in presence of cryolite. (C) Cyanide ion is used as ligand for leaching of silver. (D) Phosphine act as a ligand in Wilkinson catalyst. (E) The stability constants of $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ and $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ are similar with $\text{EDTA}$ complexes. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Triphenylphosphine ($\text{PPh}_{3}$), not phosphine ($\text{PH}_{3}$), is present in Wilkinson's catalyst. // 📝 Solution: Statements (A), (B), and (C) are correct facts. (D) is incorrect as Wilkinson catalyst is $\left[\text{RhCl}\left(\text{PPh}_{3}\right)_{3}\right]$ with $\text{PPh}_{3}$, not $\text{PH}_{3}$. (E) is incorrect because $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ and $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ complexes with $\text{EDTA}$ have significantly different formation constants.

questions.text: Given below are two statements : Statement I : Among $\left[\text{Cu}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{4}\right]^{2+}$, $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{en}\right)_{3}\right]^{2+}$, $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+}$ and $\left[\text{Mn}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+}$, $\left[\text{Mn}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+}$ has the maximum number of unpaired electrons. Statement II : The number of pairs among $\left\{\left[\text{NiCl}_{4}\right]^{2-},\;\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CO}\right)_{4}\right]\right\}$, $\left\{\left[\text{NiCl}_{4}\right]^{2-},\;\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{4}\right]^{2-}\right\}$ and $\left\{\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CO}\right)_{4}\right],\;\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{4}\right]^{2-}\right\}$ that contain only diamagnetic species is two. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.text: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Count unpaired electrons for each complex and determine which species are diamagnetic ($n = 0$). // 📝 Solution: In Statement I: $\text{Cu}^{2+}\;\left(n = 1\right)$, $\text{Ni}^{2+}\;\left(n = 2\right)$, $\text{Mn}^{2+}\;\left(n = 5\right) \implies \left[\text{Mn}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{6}\right]^{2+}$ has maximum (True). In Statement II: $\left[\text{NiCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}$ is paramagnetic ($n = 2$), while $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CO}\right)_{4}\right]$ and $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{4}\right]^{2-}$ are diamagnetic. Only $\left\{\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CO}\right)_{4}\right],\;\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{4}\right]^{2-}\right\}$ contains only diamagnetic species (Count $= 1 \ne 2$, False).

questions.text: The statements that are incorrect about the nickel(II) complex of dimethylglyoxime are : A. It is red in colour. B. It has a high solubility in water at $\text{pH} = 9$. C. The $\text{Ni}$ ion has two unpaired d-electrons. D. The $\text{N}-\text{Ni}-\text{N}$ bond angle is almost close to $90^{\circ}$. E. The complex contains four five-membered metallacycles (metal containing rings). Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{dmg}\right)_{2}\right]$ is a square planar, neutral, red precipitate with two 5-membered chelate rings and two 6-membered H-bonded rings. // 📝 Solution: $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{dmg}\right)_{2}\right]$ is insoluble in water at $\text{pH} \approx 9$ (B is incorrect). $\text{Ni}^{2+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{8}\right)$ is square planar and diamagnetic ($n = 0$, C is incorrect). The structure contains two five-membered chelate rings, not four (E is incorrect). Thus, B, C, and E are incorrect.

questions.text: The hybridization and magnetic behaviour of cobalt ion in $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}$ complex, respectively is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\text{NH}_{3}$ acts as a strong field ligand for $\text{Co}^{3+}$, forcing electron pairing. // 📝 Solution: For $\text{Co}^{3+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{6}\right)$, strong ligand $\text{NH}_{3}$ causes pairing $\implies \text{t}_{2\text{g}}^{6}\;\text{e}_{\text{g}}^{0} \implies n = 0$ (diamagnetic). Two $3\text{d}$ orbitals are vacant $\implies \text{d}^{2}\text{sp}^{3}$ hybridization.

questions.text: The $\text{Cl}-\text{Co}-\text{Cl}$ bond angle values in a $\text{fac}-\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{3}\text{Cl}_{3}\right]$ complex is/are:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: In a facial ($\text{fac}$) isomer, identical donor atoms occupy adjacent positions on one octahedral triangular face. // 📝 Solution: In $\text{fac}-\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{3}\text{Cl}_{3}\right]$, all three $\text{Cl}^{-}$ ligands are mutually cis to one another [FIGURE] $\implies$ all $\text{Cl}-\text{Co}-\text{Cl}$ bond angles are $90^{\circ}$.

questions.text: Number of ambidentate ligands among the following is _______ : $\text{NO}_{2}^{-}$, $\text{SCN}^{-}$, $\text{C}_{2}\text{O}_{4}^{2-}$, $\text{NH}_{3}$, $\text{CN}^{-}$, $\text{SO}_{4}^{2-}$, $\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Ambidentate ligands possess two different donor atoms capable of coordinating independently. // 📝 Solution: $\text{NO}_{2}^{-}$ (donors $\text{N}$ or $\text{O}$), $\text{SCN}^{-}$ (donors $\text{S}$ or $\text{N}$), and $\text{CN}^{-}$ (donors $\text{C}$ or $\text{N}$) are ambidentate ligands. $\text{C}_{2}\text{O}_{4}^{2-}$, $\text{NH}_{3}$, $\text{SO}_{4}^{2-}$, and $\text{H}_{2}\text{O}$ are not $\implies$ count $= 3$.

questions.text: To inhibit the growth of tumours, identify the compounds used from the following: (A) $\text{EDTA}$, (B) Coordination Compounds of $\text{Pt}$, (C) $\text{D}-\text{Penicillamine}$, (D) $\text{Cis}-\text{Platin}$. Choose the correct answer from the option given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Platinum coordination complexes such as cisplatin are widely used in cancer chemotherapy. // 📝 Solution: Cis-platin ($\text{cis}-\left[\text{PtCl}_{2}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{2}\right]$) and related coordination compounds of platinum are effective antitumor agents. EDTA is used for lead poisoning, and D-penicillamine is used for copper poisoning.

questions.text: Given below are two statements : Statement (I) : Dimethyl glyoxime forms a sixmembered covalent chelate when treated with $\text{NiCl}_{2}$ solution in presence of $\text{NH}_{4}\text{OH}$. Statement (II) : Prussian blue precipitate contains iron both in (+2) and (+3) oxidation states. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Analyze the ring size of the nickel dimethylglyoxime complex and the formula of Prussian blue. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ reacts with $\text{dmg}^{-}$ to form $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{dmg}\right)_{2}\right]$ stabilized by two 5-membered rings and intramolecular hydrogen bonds [FIGURE], not 6-membered covalent chelate $\implies$ Statement I is false. Prussian blue is $\text{Fe}_{4}\left[\text{Fe}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{6}\right]_{3}$ containing $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ and $\text{Fe}^{2+} \implies$ Statement II is true.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I (Coordination entity): A. $\left[\text{CoCl}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{5}\right]^{2+}$, B. $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}$, C. $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{6}\right]^{3-}$, D. $\left[\text{Cu}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{4}\right]^{2+}$. List II (Wavelength of light absorbed in nm): I. 310, II. 475, III. 535, IV. 600. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Crystal field splitting $\Delta \propto \text{ligand field strength} \propto \frac{1}{\lambda_{\text{absorbed}}}$. // 📝 Solution: Ligand field strength order: $\text{CN}^{-} > \text{NH}_{3} > \text{H}_{2}\text{O} > \text{Cl}^{-} \implies$ highest $\Delta$ absorbs lowest $\lambda$. Thus, $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{6}\right]^{3-} \rightarrow 310\;\text{nm}\;(\text{C-I})$, $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right]^{3-} \rightarrow 475\;\text{nm}\;(\text{B-II})$, $\left[\text{CoCl}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{5}\right]^{2+} \rightarrow 535\;\text{nm}\;(\text{A-III})$, and $\left[\text{Cu}\left(\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\right)_{4}\right]^{2+} \rightarrow 600\;\text{nm}\;(\text{D-IV})$.

questions.text: Given below are two statements : Statement I : $\text{PF}_{5}$ and $\text{BrF}_{5}$ both exhibit $\text{sp}^{3}\text{d}$ hybridisation. Statement II : Both $\text{SF}_{6}$ and $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}$ exhibit $\text{sp}^{3}\text{d}^{2}$ hybridisation. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.text: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Determine hybridization using steric number and crystal field splitting for inner vs outer orbital complexes. // 📝 Solution: $\text{PF}_{5}$ has steric number $5\;(\text{sp}^{3}\text{d})$ while $\text{BrF}_{5}$ has steric number $6\;(\text{sp}^{3}\text{d}^{2}) \implies$ Statement I is false. $\text{SF}_{6}$ has outer $\text{sp}^{3}\text{d}^{2}$ hybridization, whereas $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}$ has inner $\text{d}^{2}\text{sp}^{3}$ hybridization $\implies$ Statement II is false.

questions.text: The Spin only magnetic moment value of square planar complex $\left[\text{Pt}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{2}\text{Cl}\left(\text{NH}_{2}\text{CH}_{3}\right)\right]\text{Cl}$ is _______ $\text{B.M.}$ (Nearest integer) (Given atomic number for $\text{Pt} = 78$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Second and third row transition metal ions with $\text{d}^{8}$ configuration are diamagnetic square planar. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Pt}^{2+}$ is a $5\text{d}^{8}$ ion. Heavy transition metals exhibit large ligand field splitting $\Delta$, ensuring complete pairing of all 8 electrons in square planar geometry $\implies n = 0 \implies \mu = 0\;\text{BM}$.

questions.text: The correct order of ligands arranged in increasing field strength.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Refer to the spectrochemical series from weakest to strongest. // 📝 Solution: In spectrochemical series: $\text{I}^{-} < \text{Br}^{-} < \text{Cl}^{-} < \text{F}^{-} < \text{OH}^{-} < \text{H}_{2}\text{O} < \text{NH}_{3} < \text{CN}^{-} \implies \text{Br}^{-} < \text{F}^{-} < \text{H}_{2}\text{O} < \text{NH}_{3}$.

questions.text: Which of the following is correct order of ligand field strength?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Refer to the standard spectrochemical series of ligands. // 📝 Solution: Spectrochemical series: $\text{I}^{-} < \text{Br}^{-} < \text{S}^{2-} < \text{Cl}^{-} < \text{F}^{-} < \text{OH}^{-} < \text{C}_{2}\text{O}_{4}^{2-} < \text{H}_{2}\text{O} < \text{NH}_{3} < \text{en} < \text{CN}^{-} < \text{CO} \implies \text{S}^{2-} < \text{C}_{2}\text{O}_{4}^{2-} < \text{NH}_{3} < \text{en} < \text{CO}$.

questions.text: The oxidation state and geometry of nickel in $\left[\mathrm{NiCl_4}\right]^{2-}$ and $\left[\mathrm{Ni}\left(\mathrm{CO}\right)_4\right]$ respectively are
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Cl⁻ is a weak field ligand and CO is a strong field ligand; both give $sp^3$ hybridisation here. // 📝 Solution: $\left[\mathrm{NiCl_4}\right]^{2-}\;:\;\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}\;3d^8$, $sp^3$ tetrahedral; $\left[\mathrm{Ni}\left(\mathrm{CO}\right)_4\right]\;:\;\mathrm{Ni}\left(0\right)\;3d^{10}$, $sp^3$ tetrahedral

questions.text: The sum of bridging carbonyls in $\text{W}\left(\text{CO}\right)_{6}$ and $\text{Mn}_{2}\left(\text{CO}\right)_{10}$ is _______ .
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Both complexes contain only terminal carbonyl ligands. // 📝 Solution: $\text{W}\left(\text{CO}\right)_{6}$ is a mononuclear octahedral complex with $0$ bridging carbonyls. $\text{Mn}_{2}\left(\text{CO}\right)_{10}$ consists of two $\text{Mn}\left(\text{CO}\right)_{5}$ units connected by an $\text{Mn}-\text{Mn}$ single bond with $0$ bridging carbonyls [FIGURE] $\implies \text{Sum} = 0 + 0 = 0$.

questions.text: Identify the diamagnetic species among the following. A. $\left[\mathrm{Fe}\left(\mathrm{H_2O}\right)_6\right]^{2+}$ B. $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH_3}\right)_6\right]^{3+}$ C. $\left[\mathrm{NiCl_4}\right]^{2-}$ D. $\left[\mathrm{Ni}\left(\mathrm{CO}\right)_4\right]$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Diamagnetic species have no unpaired electrons; count them using the ligand field strength. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Co^{3+}}\;d^6$ with $\mathrm{NH_3}$ is low spin $t_{2g}^6$ and $\mathrm{Ni}\left(0\right)\;d^{10}$ is paired, while A and C are paramagnetic $\;\implies\;$ B and D

questions.text: The correct statements from following are: A. The strength of anionic ligands can be explained by crystal field theory. B. Valence bond theory does not give a quantitative interpretation of kinetic stability of coordination compounds. C. The hybridization involved in formation of $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{4}\right]^{2-}$ complex is $\text{dsp}^{2}$. D. The number of possible isomer(s) of $\text{cis}-\left[\text{PtCl}_{2}\left(\text{en}\right)_{2}\right]^{2+}$ is one. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: CFT treats ligands as point charges, failing to justify spectrochemical order of halides; cis-chelated octahedral complexes are chiral. // 📝 Solution: A is incorrect (CFT cannot explain spectrochemical series). B is correct (VBT provides no quantitative kinetic/thermodynamic stability data). C is correct ($\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{4}\right]^{2-}$ is $\text{dsp}^{2}$). D is incorrect ($\text{cis}-\left[\text{PtCl}_{2}\left(\text{en}\right)_{2}\right]^{2+}$ is chiral and exists as a pair of enantiomers, so it has 2 isomers). Correct: B, C only.

questions.text: Total number of unpaired electrons present in the central metal atoms/ions of $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CO}\right)_{4}\right]$, $\left[\text{NiCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}$, $\left[\text{PtCl}_{2}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{2}\right]$, $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{4}\right]^{2-}$ and $\left[\text{Pt}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{4}\right]^{2-}$ is _______ .
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Tetrahedral $\left[\text{NiCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}$ has $2$ unpaired electrons; square planar $\text{d}^{8}$ and $\text{Ni(0)}$ carbonyl are diamagnetic. // 📝 Solution: $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CO}\right)_{4}\right]\;\left(3\text{d}^{10}\right) \implies n = 0$; $\left[\text{NiCl}_{4}\right]^{2-}\;\left(3\text{d}^{8},\;\text{Td}\right) \implies n = 2$; $\left[\text{PtCl}_{2}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{2}\right]\;\left(5\text{d}^{8},\;\text{sq. pl.}\right) \implies n = 0$; $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{4}\right]^{2-}\;\left(3\text{d}^{8},\;\text{sq. pl.}\right) \implies n = 0$; $\left[\text{Pt}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{4}\right]^{2-}\;\left(5\text{d}^{8},\;\text{sq. pl.}\right) \implies n = 0$. Total $= 0 + 2 + 0 + 0 + 0 = 2$.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List - I: A. $\text{K}_{2}\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{4}\right]$, B. $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CO}\right)_{4}\right]$, C. $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right]\text{Cl}_{3}$, D. $\text{Na}_{3}\left[\text{CoF}_{6}\right]$. List - II: I. $\text{sp}^{3}$, II. $\text{sp}^{3}\text{d}^{2}$, III. $\text{dsp}^{2}$, IV. $\text{d}^{2}\text{sp}^{3}$. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Strong field ligands pair electrons to allow inner d-orbital hybridization. // 📝 Solution: $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CN}\right)_{4}\right]^{2-}: \text{Ni}^{2+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{8}\right)$ with $\text{SFL} \implies \text{dsp}^{2}\;(\text{III})$; $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{CO}\right)_{4}\right]: \text{Ni}^{0}\;\left(3\text{d}^{10}\right) \implies \text{sp}^{3}\;(\text{I})$; $\left[\text{Co}\left(\text{NH}_{3}\right)_{6}\right]^{3+}: \text{Co}^{3+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{6}\right)$ with $\text{SFL} \implies \text{d}^{2}\text{sp}^{3}\;(\text{IV})$; $\left[\text{CoF}_{6}\right]^{3-}: \text{Co}^{3+}\;\left(3\text{d}^{6}\right)$ with $\text{WFL} \implies \text{sp}^{3}\text{d}^{2}\;(\text{II})$.

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: The correct increasing order of the ionic radii is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For isoelectronic species, size $\propto \dfrac{1}{Z}$. // 📝 Solution: All have 18 electrons, with $Z$: $\mathrm{Ca^{2+}} \;=\; 20$, $\mathrm{K^+} \;=\; 19$, $\mathrm{Cl^-} \;=\; 17$, $\mathrm{S^{2-}} \;=\; 16$ $\implies$ $\mathrm{Ca^{2+}} \;<\; \mathrm{K^+} \;<\; \mathrm{Cl^-} \;<\; \mathrm{S^{2-}}$.

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Match List I with List II. List I: (A) $Al^{3+} < Mg^{2+} < Na^{+} < F^{-}$; (B) $B < C < O < N$; (C) $B < Al < Mg < K$; (D) $Si < P < S < Cl$. List II: (I) Ionisation enthalpy; (II) Metallic character; (III) Electronegativity; (IV) Ionic radii.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Identify which periodic property increases along each given series. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Isoelectronic ions} \;\implies\; \text{radii increase with fewer protons (A-IV)};\; B<C<O<N \;\implies\; \text{IE (B-I)};\; \text{metals increasing} \;\implies\; \text{C-II};\; \text{Si to Cl} \;\implies\; \text{EN (D-III)}$

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Fluorine has most negative electron gain enthalpy in its group. Statement II: Oxygen has least negative electron gain enthalpy in its group. Choose the most appropriate from the options given below.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Chlorine, not fluorine, has the most negative $\Delta_{eg}H$ among halogens. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Cl}$ has the most negative electron gain enthalpy in group 17 $\implies$ I false; oxygen has the least negative in group 16 (due to small size and repulsion) $\implies$ II true.
questions.topic: Electron gain enthalpy of groups 16 and 17

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The correct order of first ionization enthalpy values of $\mathrm{Li}, \mathrm{Na}, \mathrm{F}$ and $\mathrm{Cl}$ is $\mathrm{Na} \;<\; \mathrm{Li} \;<\; \mathrm{Cl} \;<\; \mathrm{F}$. Statement II: The correct order of negative electron gain enthalpy values of $\mathrm{Li}, \mathrm{Na}, \mathrm{F}$ and $\mathrm{Cl}$ is $\mathrm{Na} \;<\; \mathrm{Li} \;<\; \mathrm{F} \;<\; \mathrm{Cl}$. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Compare standard IE and electron gain enthalpy data, noting Cl has the most negative $\Delta_{eg}H$. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{IE_1}$ (kJ/mol): $\mathrm{Na} \;496 \;<\; \mathrm{Li} \;520 \;<\; \mathrm{Cl} \;1256 \;<\; \mathrm{F} \;1681$; $\Delta_{eg}H$: $\mathrm{Na} \;-53$, $\mathrm{Li} \;-60$, $\mathrm{F} \;-328$, $\mathrm{Cl} \;-349$ $\implies$ both true.
questions.topic: IE and electron gain enthalpy comparison

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement (I): The oxidation state of an element in a particular compound is the charge acquired by its atom on the basis of electron gain enthalpy consideration from other atoms in the molecule. Statement (II): $p\pi - p\pi$ bond formation is more prevalent in second period elements over other periods. Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Oxidation state is defined using electronegativity, not electron gain enthalpy. // 📝 Solution: Oxidation state is based on electronegativity $\implies$ I incorrect; second period elements are small, so $p\pi - p\pi$ bonding is prevalent $\implies$ II correct.

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: The successive ionisation enthalpies of an element are $800$, $2427$, $3658$, $25024$ and $32824\text{ kJ/mol}$. The element belongs to the group:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A very large jump in successive ionisation energies marks the removal of a core electron. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Large jump between } IE_3 \text{ and } IE_4 \;\implies\; 3 \text{ valence electrons} \;\implies\; \text{group 13}$

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: The correct order of $\mathrm{C}, \mathrm{N}, \mathrm{O}$ and $\mathrm{F}$ in terms of second ionisation potential is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Consider the configuration of the monopositive ions, where $\mathrm{O^+}$ is $2p^3$. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{C^+} \;2p^1$ (easiest), $\mathrm{N^+} \;2p^2$, $\mathrm{F^+} \;2p^4$, $\mathrm{O^+} \;2p^3$ half-filled (hardest to ionize) $\implies$ $\mathrm{C} \;<\; \mathrm{N} \;<\; \mathrm{F} \;<\; \mathrm{O}$.

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Along the period, the chemical reactivity of the element gradually increases from group 1 to group 18. Statement II: The nature of oxides formed by group 1 element is basic while that of group 17 elements is acidic. Choose the most appropriate from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Reactivity is high at both extremes of a period and lowest for group 18. // 📝 Solution: Reactivity first decreases then increases, and it is lowest for noble gases $\implies$ I false; group 1 oxides are basic and group 17 oxides are acidic $\implies$ II true.
questions.topic: Chemical reactivity and nature of oxides

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: The electron affinity value are negative for A. $\mathrm{Be} \to \mathrm{Be^-}$ B. $\mathrm{N} \to \mathrm{N^-}$ C. $\mathrm{O} \to \mathrm{O^{2-}}$ D. $\mathrm{Na} \to \mathrm{Na^-}$ E. $\mathrm{Al} \to \mathrm{Al^-}$. Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: A, B, D and E only

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Filled or half-filled subshells and anion repulsion make electron addition unfavourable. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Be}$ (filled $2s$), $\mathrm{N}$ (half-filled $2p$) and $\mathrm{O^-} \to \mathrm{O^{2-}}$ (repulsion) have E.A. $\;=\;$ negative; $\mathrm{Na}$, $\mathrm{Al}$ have positive E.A. $\implies$ A, B, C only.

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: From the given list, the number of compounds with $+4$ oxidation state of Sulphur is: $\mathrm{SO_3}, \mathrm{H_2 SO_3}, \mathrm{SOCl_2}, \mathrm{SF_4}, \mathrm{BaSO_4}, \mathrm{H_2 S_2 O_7}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Calculate the oxidation state of $\mathrm{S}$ in each compound. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{SO_3} \;=\; +6$, $\mathrm{H_2 SO_3} \;=\; +4$, $\mathrm{SOCl_2} \;=\; +4$, $\mathrm{SF_4} \;=\; +4$, $\mathrm{BaSO_4} \;=\; +6$, $\mathrm{H_2 S_2 O_7} \;=\; +6$ $\implies$ count $\;=\; 3$.

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: In group 13, the stability of $+1$ oxidation state increases down the group. Statement II: The atomic size of gallium is greater than that of aluminium. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Inert pair effect increases down the group, and Ga follows Al only after the d-block contraction. // 📝 Solution: Poor shielding by $d$ and $f$ electrons $\implies$ stability of $+1$ increases down the group (I correct); atomic radius of $\mathrm{Al} \;\ge\; \mathrm{Ga}$ (II incorrect) $\implies$ option (4).
questions.topic: Group 13 oxidation states and atomic size

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Among the elements Iridium, Platinum, Osmium and Palladium, the element which does not belong to the same period as the others is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Identify the period from the valence shell of each transition metal. // 📝 Solution: $Ir,\, Pt,\, Os \;\implies\; 5d \;\implies\; \text{period 6}$; $Pd \;\implies\; 4d \;\implies\; \text{period 5}$
questions.topic: Position of elements in the periodic table

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: $\mathrm{C} \;<\; \mathrm{O} \;<\; \mathrm{N} \;<\; \mathrm{F}$ is the correct order in terms of first ionization enthalpy values. Statement II: $\mathrm{S} \;>\; \mathrm{Se} \;>\; \mathrm{Te} \;>\; \mathrm{Po} \;>\; \mathrm{O}$ is the correct order in terms of the magnitude of electron gain enthalpy values. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: N has half-filled $2p^3$, and O has an anomalously low $\Delta_{eg}H$ among group 16. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{IE_1}$: $\mathrm{C} \;<\; \mathrm{O} \;<\; \mathrm{N} \;<\; \mathrm{F}$ true; $\Delta_{eg}H$ magnitude: $\mathrm{S} \;200 \;>\; \mathrm{Se} \;195 \;>\; \mathrm{Te} \;190 \;>\; \mathrm{Po} \;183 \;>\; \mathrm{O} \;141$ true $\implies$ both true.
questions.topic: IE and electron gain enthalpy trends

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Elements X and Y belong to Group 15. The difference between the electronegativity values of 'X' and phosphorus is higher than that of the difference between phosphorus and 'Y'. 'X' and 'Y' are respectively
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use Pauling electronegativity values for group 15. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{N} \;3.04$, $\mathrm{P} \;2.19$, $\mathrm{As} \;2.18$, $\mathrm{Sb} \;2.05$, $\mathrm{Bi} \;2.02$; for N and As: $\left\lvert 3.04 - 2.19 \right\rvert \;=\; 0.85 \;>\; \left\lvert 2.19 - 2.18 \right\rvert \;=\; 0.01$ $\implies$ option (1).

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Given below are two statements: Assertion A: $\mathrm{H_2 Te}$ is more acidic than $\mathrm{H_2 S}$. Reason R: Bond dissociation enthalpy of $\mathrm{H_2 Te}$ is lower than $\mathrm{H_2 S}$. Choose the most appropriate from the options given below.

options.text: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
A is true but R is false

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A weaker $\mathrm{H-E}$ bond releases $\mathrm{H^+}$ more easily. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{H-Te}$ bond dissociation enthalpy is lower than $\mathrm{H-S}$ $\implies$ $\mathrm{H_2 Te}$ ionizes to give $\mathrm{H^+}$ more easily $\implies$ both true with R explaining A.

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Among Li, Na, Be, Mg, B and Al, the element with the smallest atomic radius forms an oxide of the type (A is the element):
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find the smallest atom by period and group trends, then use its common valence. // 📝 Solution: $r:\; B \;<\; Be \;<\; Li \;\implies\; \text{smallest is B (valence 3)} \;\implies\; B_2O_3$

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Statement I: An element in the extreme left of the periodic table forms acidic oxides. Statement II: An acid is formed when the oxide of a reactive element at the extreme right of the periodic table reacts with water. Choose the correct option.

options.text: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Metals on the left form basic oxides, non-metals on the right form acidic oxides. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Left oxides} \;\implies\; \text{basic}$; $\text{Right oxides} + H_2O \;\implies\; \text{acid}$, so I is false and II is true
questions.topic: Periodic trends in nature of oxides

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: The bond dissociation energy is highest for
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mathrm{F_2}$ has an anomalously low bond energy because of lone pair–lone pair repulsion. // 📝 Solution: Bond energy order $\;\mathrm{Cl_2} \;>\; \mathrm{Br_2} \;>\; \mathrm{F_2} \;>\; \mathrm{I_2}$ $\implies$ highest is $\mathrm{Cl_2}$.

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Lowest Oxidation number of an atom in a compound $\mathrm{A_2 B}$ is $-2$. The number of electron in its valence shell is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Lowest oxidation state equals valence electrons minus 8. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{A_2 B} \to 2\mathrm{A^+} + \mathrm{B^{2-}}$ $\implies$ $\mathrm{B^{2-}}$ has a complete octet $\implies$ $\mathrm{B}$ has $8 \;-\; 2 \;=\; 6$ valence electrons.

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The correct order in terms of atomic/ionic radii is $\mathrm{Al} \;>\; \mathrm{Mg} \;>\; \mathrm{Mg^{2+}} \;>\; \mathrm{Al^{3+}}$. Statement II: The correct order in terms of the magnitude of electron gain enthalpy is $\mathrm{Cl} \;>\; \mathrm{Br} \;>\; \mathrm{S} \;>\; \mathrm{O}$. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Atomic radius decreases across a period, so Mg is larger than Al. // 📝 Solution: Correct radii: $\mathrm{Mg} \;>\; \mathrm{Al} \;>\; \mathrm{Mg^{2+}} \;>\; \mathrm{Al^{3+}}$ so I false; $\mathrm{Cl} \;349 \;>\; \mathrm{Br} \;325 \;>\; \mathrm{S} \;200 \;>\; \mathrm{O} \;141$ so II true.
questions.topic: Atomic radii and electron gain enthalpy

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Which of the following is an incorrect order of electronegativity?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Compare Pauling values across periods and diagonally related elements. // 📝 Solution: $\chi_{Mg} \;=\; 1.31 \;<\; \chi_{Al} \;=\; 1.61 \;\implies\; Al < Mg \;\text{ is wrong}$

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Which of the following represents the correct order of metallic character of the given elements ?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Metallic character increases down a group and decreases along a period. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Si}$ (non-metal/metalloid) $\;<\;$ $\mathrm{Be}$ $\;<\;$ $\mathrm{Mg}$ (below Be) $\;<\;$ $\mathrm{K}$ (group 1) $\implies$ option (1).

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: The correct order of first ionization enthalpy values of the following elements is: (A) $\mathrm{O}$ (B) $\mathrm{N}$ (C) $\mathrm{Be}$ (D) $\mathrm{F}$ (E) $\mathrm{B}$. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: IE generally increases across a period, with exceptions at Be to B and N to O. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Li} \;<\; \mathrm{B} \;<\; \mathrm{Be} \;<\; \mathrm{C} \;<\; \mathrm{O} \;<\; \mathrm{N} \;<\; \mathrm{F} \;<\; \mathrm{Ne}$ $\implies$ $\mathrm{B} \;<\; \mathrm{Be} \;<\; \mathrm{O} \;<\; \mathrm{N} \;<\; \mathrm{F}$ $\implies$ E < C < A < B < D.

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Match LIST-I (Family) with LIST-II (Symbol of element). LIST-I: (A) Pnicogen (group 15), (B) Chalcogen, (C) Halogen, (D) Noble gas. LIST-II: (I) Ts, (II) Og, (III) Lv, (IV) Mc. Choose the correct answer.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The period-7 members of groups 15–18 are Mc, Lv, Ts and Og. // 📝 Solution: Mc ($Z=115$, pnicogen), Lv ($Z=116$, chalcogen), Ts ($Z=117$, halogen), Og ($Z=118$, noble gas) $\implies$ A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Which of the following elements have half-filled f-orbitals in their ground state? (Given: atomic number $\mathrm{Sm} \;=\; 62$, $\mathrm{Eu} \;=\; 63$, $\mathrm{Tb} \;=\; 65$, $\mathrm{Gd} \;=\; 64$, $\mathrm{Pm} \;=\; 61$) A. Sm B. Eu C. Tb D. Gd E. Pm
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Half-filled f-subshell means $4f^7$. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Sm} \;=\; 4f^6 6s^2$, $\mathrm{Eu} \;=\; 4f^7 6s^2$, $\mathrm{Gd} \;=\; 4f^7 5d^1 6s^2$, $\mathrm{Tb} \;=\; 4f^9 6s^2$, $\mathrm{Pm} \;=\; 4f^5 6s^2$ $\implies$ Eu and Gd $\implies$ option (1).

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Given below are two statements. Statement (I): The metallic radius of Al is less than that of Ga. Statement (II): The ionic radius of $\mathrm{Al^{3+}}$ is less than that of $\mathrm{Ga^{3+}}$. In the light of the statements, choose the most appropriate answer.

options.text: Both statements I and II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Both statements I and II are correct

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Poor d-subshell shielding makes Ga smaller than expected. // 📝 Solution: Metallic radius order is $\mathrm{Ga}<\mathrm{Al}$, so I is false; $\mathrm{Al^{3+}}<\mathrm{Ga^{3+}}$, so II is true $\implies$ option (2).
questions.topic: Atomic and ionic radii, d-block contraction

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: For electron gain enthalpies of the elements denoted as $\Delta_{eg}H$, the incorrect option is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Compare the actual signed values of $\Delta_{eg}H$ (more negative means smaller). // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Cl} \;(-345) \;<\; \mathrm{F} \;(-328)$ correct; $\mathrm{Se} \;(-195) \;<\; \mathrm{S} \;(-200)$ is incorrect; $\mathrm{I} \;(-295) \;<\; \mathrm{At} \;(-270)$ correct; $\mathrm{Te} \;(-190) \;<\; \mathrm{Po} \;(-183)$ correct $\implies$ option (2).

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Melting Point [K]; B. Ionic Radius $\left[ \mathrm{M^{+3}} / \mathrm{pm} \right]$; C. $\Delta_i H_1 \left[ \mathrm{kJ \, mol^{-1}} \right]$; D. Atomic Radius [pm]. List II: I. $\mathrm{Tl} \;>\; \mathrm{In} \;>\; \mathrm{Ga} \;>\; \mathrm{Al} \;>\; \mathrm{B}$; II. $\mathrm{B} \;>\; \mathrm{Tl} \;>\; \mathrm{Al} \;\approx\; \mathrm{Ga} \;>\; \mathrm{In}$; III. $\mathrm{Tl} \;>\; \mathrm{In} \;>\; \mathrm{Al} \;>\; \mathrm{Ga} \;>\; \mathrm{B}$; IV. $\mathrm{B} \;>\; \mathrm{Al} \;>\; \mathrm{Tl} \;>\; \mathrm{In} \;>\; \mathrm{Ga}$. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use the group 13 trends of melting point, ionic radius, IE and atomic radius. // 📝 Solution: M.P.: $\mathrm{B} \;>\; \mathrm{Al} \;>\; \mathrm{Tl} \;>\; \mathrm{In} \;>\; \mathrm{Ga}$ (IV); ionic radius: $\mathrm{Tl} \;>\; \mathrm{In} \;>\; \mathrm{Ga} \;>\; \mathrm{Al} \;>\; \mathrm{B}$ (I); IE: II; atomic radius: III $\implies$ A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Statement I: The Law of Octaves arranged the elements in increasing order of atomic number. Statement II: Lothar Meyer plotted physical properties of elements against atomic numbers. Choose the correct option.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Early classifications used atomic weights, not atomic numbers. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Newlands (octaves)} \;\implies\; \text{atomic weight};\; \text{Meyer curves} \;\implies\; \text{atomic weight} \;\implies\; \text{both statements false}$

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Inert gases have positive electron gain enthalpy. Its correct order is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use the NCERT values of $\Delta_{eg}H$ for the noble gases. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta_{eg}H \;(\mathrm{kJ/mol})$: $\mathrm{He} \;=\; +48$, $\mathrm{Ne} \;=\; +116$, $\mathrm{Kr} \;=\; +96$, $\mathrm{Xe} \;=\; +77$ $\implies$ $\mathrm{Ne} \;>\; \mathrm{Kr} \;>\; \mathrm{Xe} \;>\; \mathrm{He}$ $\implies$ option (3).
questions.topic: Electron gain enthalpy of noble gases

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: The correct trend in the first ionization enthalpies of the elements in the $3^{rd}$ period of periodic table is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: IE rises across the period except P exceeds S because of half-filled $3p^3$. // 📝 Solution: IE (kJ/mol): $\mathrm{Al} \;578 \;<\; \mathrm{Si} \;787 \;<\; \mathrm{S} \;1000 \;<\; \mathrm{P} \;1012 \;<\; \mathrm{Cl} \;1251$ $\implies$ option (3).

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Consider the elements $\mathrm{N}, \mathrm{P}, \mathrm{O}, \mathrm{S}, \mathrm{Cl}$ and $\mathrm{F}$. The number of valence electrons present in the elements with most and least metallic character from the above list is respectively.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Metallic character increases down a group and decreases along a period. // 📝 Solution: Most metallic is $\mathrm{P}$ with $5$ valence electrons; least metallic is $\mathrm{F}$ with $7$ valence electrons $\implies$ 5 and 7.

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Given below are two statements: Assertion A: The first ionisation enthalpy decreases across a period. Reason R: The increasing nuclear charge outweighs the shielding across the period. Choose the most appropriate from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: IE increases across a period because $Z_{eff}$ rises. // 📝 Solution: First IE increases along a period $\implies$ A false; $Z$ increases and outweighs shielding $\implies$ R true.
questions.topic: Ionization enthalpy trend across a period

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Which of the following represents the correct trend for the mentioned property? A. $\mathrm{F} \;>\; \mathrm{P} \;>\; \mathrm{S} \;>\; \mathrm{B}$ - First Ionization Energy B. $\mathrm{Cl} \;>\; \mathrm{F} \;>\; \mathrm{S} \;>\; \mathrm{P}$ - Electron Affinity C. $\mathrm{K} \;>\; \mathrm{Al} \;>\; \mathrm{Mg} \;>\; \mathrm{B}$ - Metallic character D. $\mathrm{K_2 O} \;>\; \mathrm{Na_2 O} \;>\; \mathrm{MgO} \;>\; \mathrm{Al_2 O_3}$ - Basic character. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Mg is more metallic than Al in the same period. // 📝 Solution: A correct (P exceeds S due to half-filled $3p^3$); B correct; C incorrect since correct order is $\mathrm{K} \;>\; \mathrm{Mg} \;>\; \mathrm{Al} \;>\; \mathrm{B}$; D correct $\implies$ A, B and D only.
questions.topic: Periodic trends: IE, EA, metallic and basic character

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: The statement(s) that are correct about the species $\mathrm{O^{2-}}, \mathrm{F^-}, \mathrm{Na^+}$ and $\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}$. (A) All are isoelectronic (B) All have the same nuclear charge (C) $\mathrm{O^{2-}}$ has the largest ionic radii (D) $\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}$ has the smallest ionic radii. Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Isoelectronic species differ in nuclear charge, and size $\propto \dfrac{1}{Z}$. // 📝 Solution: All have $10$ electrons (A true); $Z \;=\; 8, 9, 11, 12$ so (B false); radius $\mathrm{O^{2-}} \;>\; \mathrm{F^-} \;>\; \mathrm{Na^+} \;>\; \mathrm{Mg^{2+}}$ $\implies$ A, C, D.

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: If IUPAC name of an element is "Unununnium" then the element belongs to $n^{th}$ group of periodic table. The value of $n$ is ______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Un-un-un stands for digits 1-1-1, giving $Z \;=\; 111$ with the suffix -ium. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Un} \;=\; 1$ so $Z \;=\; 111$ $\implies$ the element belongs to group $11$ $\implies$ $n \;=\; 11$.

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The halogen that makes longest bond with hydrogen in $\mathrm{HX}$, has the smallest covalent radius in its group. Statement II: A group 15 element's hydride $\mathrm{EH_3}$ has the lowest boiling point among corresponding hydrides of other group 15 elements. The maximum covalency of that element E is 4. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Longest H–X bond belongs to the largest halogen, and the lowest boiling hydride is PH3. // 📝 Solution: Longest bond is $\mathrm{HI}$ and $\mathrm{I}$ has the largest radius, so I false; lowest b.p. is $\mathrm{PH_3}$ and $\mathrm{P}$ has maximum covalency $6$, so II false $\implies$ both false.
questions.topic: Bond length, boiling point and covalency

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The second ionisation enthalpy of $\mathrm{Na}$ is larger than the corresponding ionisation enthalpy of $\mathrm{Mg}$. Statement II: The ionic radius of $\mathrm{O^{2-}}$ is larger than that of $\mathrm{F^-}$. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Removing an electron from a noble gas core is very difficult, and for isoelectronic ions size $\propto \dfrac{1}{Z}$. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Na^+}$ has $2p^6$ core while $\mathrm{Mg^+}$ has $3s^1$ $\implies$ $\mathrm{IE_2}(\mathrm{Na}) \;\gg\; \mathrm{IE_2}(\mathrm{Mg})$ true; $\mathrm{O^{2-}}$ ($Z=8$) $\;>\;$ $\mathrm{F^-}$ ($Z=9$) true.
questions.topic: Second ionization enthalpy and ionic radii

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: In case of isoelectronic species the size of $\mathrm{F^-}$, $\mathrm{Ne}$ and $\mathrm{Na^+}$ is affected by:

options.text: None of the factors because their size is the same
Electron-electron interaction in the outer orbitals

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Isoelectronic species have the same $n$ and number of electrons. // 📝 Solution: All have $1s^2 2s^2 2p^6$ $\implies$ size differs only because of nuclear charge $Z$.

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I (Atomic number): (A) $37$, (B) $78$, (C) $52$, (D) $65$. List-II (Block of periodic table): (I) p-block, (II) d-block, (III) f-block, (IV) s-block. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Identify each element from its atomic number and find its block. // 📝 Solution: $37 \;\to\; \mathrm{Rb}$ (s-block), $78 \;\to\; \mathrm{Pt}$ (d-block), $52 \;\to\; \mathrm{Te}$ (p-block), $65 \;\to\; \mathrm{Tb}$ (f-block) $\implies$ A–IV, B–II, C–I, D–III.

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
