questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement (I): Both metal and non-metal exist in p and d-block elements. Statement (II): Non-metals have higher ionisation enthalpy and higher electronegativity than the metals. Choose the most appropriate answer from the option given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The d-block contains only metals. // 📝 Solution: p-block has metals and non-metals but d-block has only metals $\implies$ I false; non-metals have higher IE and EN than metals $\implies$ II true.

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Given below are the pairs of group 13 elements in terms of atomic radius: $\mathrm{B<Al}$, $\mathrm{Al<Ga}$, $\mathrm{Ga<In}$ and $\mathrm{In<Tl}$. Identify the elements in the incorrect pair. In that pair, the element (X) has the higher ionic radius $\mathrm{M^{3+}}$ than the other. The atomic number of X is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Ga is smaller than Al due to poor d-shielding, so the pair Al–Ga is incorrect. // 📝 Solution: Incorrect pair $=$ Al–Ga; $\mathrm{Ga^{3+}}>\mathrm{Al^{3+}}$ in ionic radius $\implies X=\text{Ga}$, $Z=31$ $\implies$ option (1).

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: The first ionisation enthalpies of the first four group 15 elements are given in $\text{kJ/mol}$. The first ionisation enthalpy of the element which is the main component of apatite is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Apatite is a phosphate mineral; recall the IE order down group 15. // 📝 Solution: $IE_1:\; N\left(1402\right) > P\left(1012\right) > As\left(947\right) > Sb\left(834\right) \;\implies\; P \;=\; 1012\text{ kJ/mol}$

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Match List I with List II. List I (Elements): A. $\mathrm{Cl}, \mathrm{S}$; B. $\mathrm{Ge}, \mathrm{As}$; C. $\mathrm{Fr}, \mathrm{Ra}$; D. $\mathrm{F}, \mathrm{O}$. List II (Properties in their respective groups): I. Elements with highest electronegativity; II. Elements with largest atomic size; III. Elements which show properties of both metals and non-metals; IV. Elements with highest negative electron gain enthalpy. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall the extreme-property elements and metalloids of the periodic table. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Cl}, \mathrm{S}$ $\to$ highest negative $\Delta_{eg}H$ (IV); $\mathrm{Ge}, \mathrm{As}$ $\to$ metalloids (III); $\mathrm{Fr}, \mathrm{Ra}$ $\to$ largest size (II); $\mathrm{F}, \mathrm{O}$ $\to$ highest EN (I).

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The metallic radius of $\mathrm{Na}$ is $1.86 \, \mathring{A}$ and the ionic radius of $\mathrm{Na^+}$ is lesser than $1.86 \, \mathring{A}$. Statement II: Ions are always smaller in size than the corresponding elements. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Cations are smaller and anions are larger than their parent atoms. // 📝 Solution: $r_{\mathrm{Na}} \;>\; r_{\mathrm{Na^+}}$ so I is correct; anions are larger than neutral atoms so II is incorrect $\implies$ option (4).

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Which of the following statements are NOT true about the periodic table? A. The properties of elements are a function of their atomic weights. B. The properties of elements are a function of their atomic numbers. C. Elements in the same period have similar outer electronic configuration. D. The location of an element reflects the quantum numbers of the last filled orbital. E. The number of elements in a period is the same as the number of atomic orbitals available in the energy level that is being filled.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall the modern periodic law and what actually repeats within a group versus a period. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Modern law} \;\implies\; \text{atomic number}$ (A false); $\text{similar outer configuration} \;\implies\; \text{same group}$ (C false); $\text{elements per period} \;=\; 2\times\text{orbitals}$ (E false)

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Which of the following material is not a semiconductor.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall which common materials are semiconductors and which are conductors. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Si}$, $\mathrm{Ge}$ and $\mathrm{Cu_2O}$ are semiconductors $\implies$ graphite is a conductor, so it is not a semiconductor.

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Given below are the two statements: Assertion (A): There is a considerable increase in covalent radius from $\mathrm{N}$ to $\mathrm{P}$. However from $\mathrm{As}$ to $\mathrm{Bi}$ only a small increase in covalent radius is observed. Reason (R): Covalent and ionic radii in a particular oxidation state increases down the group. Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Filled $d$ and $f$ orbitals shield poorly in heavier members. // 📝 Solution: (A) is NCERT factual data and (R) is true, but the actual explanation is the presence of completely filled $d$ and $f$ orbitals in heavier members $\implies$ option (2).

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: The first ionisation enthalpy of element E is $374\text{ kJ/mol}$. The electron gain enthalpies of elements A, B, C and D are $-328$, $-349$, $-325$ and $-295\text{ kJ/mol}$ respectively. The correct order of ionic character of the compounds formed by E with A, B, C and D is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Ease of forming the anion (more negative electron gain enthalpy) favours greater ionic character. // 📝 Solution: $\left\lvert\Delta_{eg}H\right\rvert:\; B\left(349\right) > A\left(328\right) > C\left(325\right) > D\left(295\right) \;\implies\; EB > EA > EC > ED$
questions.topic: Electron gain enthalpy and ionic character

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: The strongest reducing agent among the following is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Lower bond dissociation energy of $\mathrm{E-H}$ means stronger reducing power. // 📝 Solution: Down group 15 the $\mathrm{E-H}$ bond weakens $\implies$ $\mathrm{BiH_3}$ is the strongest reducing agent.

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R). Assertion (A): The first ionization enthalpy of 3d series elements is more than that of group 2 metals. Reason (R): In 3d series of elements successive filling of d-orbitals takes place. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Poor shielding by d-electrons raises $Z_{eff}$ across the 3d series. // 📝 Solution: Successive d-electrons shield poorly $\implies$ $Z_{eff}$ increases $\implies$ IE of 3d elements (Sc to Zn) $\;>\;$ IE of the group 2 metal $\mathrm{Ca}$ $\implies$ (A) true and (R) explains it, as per the official key, option (1).
questions.topic: Ionization enthalpy of d-block vs s-block

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: The correct sequence of electron gain enthalpy of the elements listed below is A. $\mathrm{Ar}$ B. $\mathrm{Br}$ C. $\mathrm{F}$ D. $\mathrm{S}$. Choose the most appropriate from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Compare signed $\Delta_{eg}H$ values, where the least negative or positive is largest. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta_{eg}H$ (kJ/mol): $\mathrm{F} \;-333$, $\mathrm{S} \;-200$, $\mathrm{Br} \;-325$, $\mathrm{Ar} \;+96$ $\implies$ $\mathrm{Ar} \;>\; \mathrm{S} \;>\; \mathrm{Br} \;>\; \mathrm{F}$ $\implies$ A > D > B > C.

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: The element having the highest first ionization enthalpy is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: IE increases across a period, and N has a stable half-filled $2p^3$. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Al} \;<\; \mathrm{Si} \;<\; \mathrm{C} \;<\; \mathrm{N}$ in $\mathrm{IE_1}$ $\implies$ highest is $\mathrm{N}$.

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: In period 4 of the periodic table, the elements with highest and lowest atomic radii are respectively.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Atomic radius decreases from left to right in a period (excluding noble gases). // 📝 Solution: In period 4, $\mathrm{K}$ is at the extreme left (largest) and $\mathrm{Br}$ is near the right end (smallest, excluding noble gas) $\implies$ K and Br.

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Which of the following is the incorrect decreasing order of atomic radii?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Radius decreases across a period and increases down a group. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Mg is below Be} \;\implies\; r_{Mg} \;>\; r_{Be} \;\implies\; Be \;>\; Mg \;\text{ is incorrect}$

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Consider the following elements. [FIGURE] Which of the following is/are true about $\mathrm{A'}, \mathrm{B'}, \mathrm{C'}$ and $\mathrm{D'}$? A. Order of atomic radii: $\mathrm{B'} \;<\; \mathrm{A'} \;<\; \mathrm{D'} \;<\; \mathrm{C'}$ B. Order of metallic character: $\mathrm{B'} \;<\; \mathrm{A'} \;<\; \mathrm{D'} \;<\; \mathrm{C'}$ C. Size of the element: $\mathrm{D'} \;<\; \mathrm{C'} \;<\; \mathrm{B'} \;<\; \mathrm{A'}$ D. Order of ionic radii: $\mathrm{B'^+} \;<\; \mathrm{A'^+} \;<\; \mathrm{D'^+} \;<\; \mathrm{C'^+}$. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Size and metallic character decrease along a period and increase down a group. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{B'} \;<\; \mathrm{A'}$ and $\mathrm{D'} \;<\; \mathrm{C'}$ in size and metallic character, $\mathrm{C'} \;>\; \mathrm{A'}$, $\mathrm{D'} \;>\; \mathrm{B'}$ $\implies$ A, B, D correct and C incorrect.
questions.topic: Periodic trends in a group-period grid

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: The correct order of the first ionization enthalpy is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Think of lanthanide and scandide (d-block) contraction in group 13. // 📝 Solution: Due to lanthanide contraction $\mathrm{Tl}$ has higher IE than $\mathrm{Ga}$ and $\mathrm{Al}$; due to scandide contraction $\mathrm{Ga}$ has higher IE than $\mathrm{Al}$ $\implies$ $\mathrm{Tl} \;>\; \mathrm{Ga} \;>\; \mathrm{Al}$.

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Number of elements from the following that CANNOT form compounds with valencies which match with their respective group valencies is ______. $\mathrm{B}, \mathrm{C}, \mathrm{N}, \mathrm{S}, \mathrm{O}, \mathrm{F}, \mathrm{P}, \mathrm{Al}, \mathrm{Si}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Second-period elements N, O, F have no vacant d-orbitals to expand valency. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{N}$, $\mathrm{O}$, $\mathrm{F}$ cannot extend valency up to group number because $2d$ orbitals are unavailable $\implies$ count $\;=\; 3$.

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Write the configuration of $\mathrm{Nd}$ ($Z = 60$) and remove the 6s electrons first. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Nd} \;=\; [\mathrm{Xe}] \, 4f^4 \, 6s^2$ $\implies$ $\mathrm{Nd^{2+}} \;=\; [\mathrm{Xe}] \, 4f^4$ $\implies$ option (2).

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Anomalous behaviour of oxygen is due to its
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Anomalous behaviour of second period elements comes from small size and high EN. // 📝 Solution: Oxygen is small and highly electronegative $\implies$ option (3).

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The electronegativity of group 14 elements from $\mathrm{Si}$ to $\mathrm{Pb}$ gradually decreases. Statement II: Group 14 contains non-metallic, metallic, as well as metalloid elements. Choose the most appropriate from the options given below:

options.text: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Check the electronegativity values of Si, Ge, Sn, Pb. // 📝 Solution: EN: $\mathrm{Si} \;1.8$, $\mathrm{Ge} \;1.8$, $\mathrm{Sn} \;1.8$, $\mathrm{Pb} \;1.9$ $\implies$ almost the same, so I false; group 14 has C (non-metal), Si and Ge (metalloids), Sn and Pb (metals) $\implies$ II true.

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: $\mathrm{K} \;>\; \mathrm{Mg} \;>\; \mathrm{Al} \;>\; \mathrm{B}$ is the correct order in terms of metallic character. Statement II: Atomic radius is always greater than the ionic radius for any element. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Anions are larger than their parent atoms. // 📝 Solution: Metallic character decreases left to right and increases down, so $\mathrm{K} \;>\; \mathrm{Mg} \;>\; \mathrm{Al} \;>\; \mathrm{B}$ is true; $\mathrm{Cl} \;<\; \mathrm{Cl^-}$ so II false $\implies$ option (4).
questions.topic: Metallic character and atomic vs ionic radius

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Identify the correct statements about p-block elements and their compounds. (A) Non metals have higher electronegativity than metals. (B) Non metals have lower ionisation enthalpy than metals. (C) Compounds formed between highly reactive nonmetals and highly reactive metals are generally ionic. (D) The non-metal oxides are generally basic in nature. (E) The metal oxides are generally acidic or neutral in nature. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Non-metals have high EN and IE, and their oxides are acidic. // 📝 Solution: (A) true; (B) false as non-metals have higher IE; (C) true as large EN difference gives ionic bonds; (D) false as non-metal oxides are acidic; (E) false as metal oxides are basic $\implies$ (A) and (C) only.

questions.chapterName: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.text: Choose the INCORRECT statement

options.text: $\mathrm{CO_2}$ is the most acidic oxide among the dioxides of group of 14 elements.
Carbon exhibits negative oxidation states along with $+4$ and $+2$.
Carbon cannot exceed its covalency more than four.
Among the isotopes of carbon, $\mathrm{^{13}C}$ is a radioactive isotope.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall which carbon isotope is radioactive. // 📝 Solution: Statements (1) to (3) are correct; $\mathrm{^{13}C}$ is stable and $\mathrm{^{14}C}$ is radioactive $\implies$ statement (4) is incorrect.

questions.text: The product $\mathrm{C}$ in the following sequence of reactions has ______ $\pi$ bonds. [FIGURE] propylbenzene $\xrightarrow{\;\mathrm{KMnO_4-KOH},\;\Delta\;}\;\mathrm{A}\;\xrightarrow{\;\mathrm{H_3O^+}\;}\;\mathrm{B}\;\xrightarrow{\;\mathrm{Br_2}/\mathrm{FeBr_3}\;}\;\mathrm{C}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Alkylbenzene gives benzoate on side-chain oxidation; the COOH group is meta-directing in bromination. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{A}\;=\;\mathrm{PhCOOK}\;\implies\;\mathrm{B}\;=\;\mathrm{PhCOOH}\;\implies\;\mathrm{C}\;=\;\text{3-bromobenzoic acid}\;\implies\;\pi\;\text{bonds}\;=\;3\;(\text{ring})\;+\;1\;(\mathrm{C=O})\;=\;4$
questions.topic: Side-chain oxidation and electrophilic substitution of benzoic acid

questions.text: In a reaction, [FIGURE] salicylic acid gives methyl salicylate with reagent $\mathrm{Y}$ and acetylsalicylic acid (aspirin) with reagent $\mathrm{X}$. Reagents $\mathrm{X}$ and $\mathrm{Y}$ respectively are :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Acetylation of phenolic OH uses acetic anhydride; esterification of COOH uses alcohol with acid. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Phenolic}\;\mathrm{OH}\;\xrightarrow{\;\left(\mathrm{CH_3CO}\right)_2\mathrm{O}/\mathrm{H^+}\;}\;\mathrm{OCOCH_3}\;\text{(aspirin)}\;\implies\;\mathrm{X}\;=\;\left(\mathrm{CH_3CO}\right)_2\mathrm{O}/\mathrm{H^+}\;;\;\mathrm{COOH}\;\xrightarrow{\;\mathrm{CH_3OH}/\mathrm{H^+},\;\Delta\;}\;\mathrm{COOCH_3}\;\implies\;\mathrm{Y}\;=\;\mathrm{CH_3OH}/\mathrm{H^+},\;\Delta$
questions.topic: Esterification and acetylation of salicylic acid

questions.text: $\mathrm{A}$ in the given reaction is : [FIGURE] $\left(\mathrm{CH_3}\right)_3\mathrm{C}\mathrm{CHO}\;+\;\mathrm{HO}\mathrm{C}\left(\mathrm{CH_3}\right)_2\mathrm{COOH}\;\xrightarrow{\;\mathrm{H^+}\;}\;\mathrm{A}\;\text{(Major)}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Aldehyde with a hydroxy acid under acid catalysis forms a cyclic acetal, here a 1,3-dioxolan-4-one. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{OH}\;\text{attacks protonated}\;\mathrm{C=O}\;\implies\;\text{hemiacetal}\;\implies\;\mathrm{COOH}\;\text{esterifies intramolecularly with loss of}\;\mathrm{H_2O}\;\implies\;\text{1,3-dioxolan-4-one (option 2)}$
questions.topic: Cyclic acetal formation from hydroxy acid

questions.text: The azo-dye $\left(\mathrm{Y}\right)$ formed in the following reactions is : Sulphanilic acid $+\;\mathrm{NaNO_2}\;+\;\mathrm{CH_3COOH}\;\to\;\mathrm{X}$ ; [FIGURE] $\mathrm{X}\;+\;\text{1-naphthylamine}\;\to\;\mathrm{Y}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Diazotisation followed by azo coupling at the para position of the aromatic amine (Griess-Ilosvay test). // 📝 Solution: $\text{Sulphanilic acid}\;\xrightarrow{\;\mathrm{NaNO_2}/\mathrm{CH_3COOH}\;}\;\text{diazonium acetate}\;\mathrm{X}\;\implies\;\text{coupling at para (C-4) of 1-naphthylamine}\;\implies\;\mathrm{HO_3S}\mathrm{C_6H_4}\mathrm{N=N}\text{-(4-amino-1-naphthyl)}\;\text{(option 4)}$

questions.text: [FIGURE] benzene $+$ succinic anhydride $\xrightarrow{\;\mathrm{AlCl_3}\;}\;\mathrm{A}\;\xrightarrow{\;\mathrm{Zn-Hg}/\mathrm{HCl}\;}\;\mathrm{B}\;\xrightarrow{\;\mathrm{Conc.\;H_2SO_4}\;}\;\mathrm{C}$ . What is the structure of $\mathrm{C}$ ?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Friedel-Crafts acylation, then Clemmensen reduction, then intramolecular cyclic acylation. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{A}\;=\;\text{4-oxo-4-phenylbutanoic acid}\;\implies\;\mathrm{B}\;=\;\text{4-phenylbutanoic acid}\;\implies\;\mathrm{Conc.\;H_2SO_4}\;\text{cyclises}\;\implies\;\mathrm{C}\;=\;\text{1-tetralone (option 1)}$
questions.topic: Friedel-Crafts acylation with anhydride and Clemmensen reduction

questions.text: Compound $\mathrm{X}$ undergoes the following sequence of reactions to give the lactone $\mathrm{Y}$. Reagents: (i) $\mathrm{HCHO,\;KOH}$ ; (ii) $\mathrm{KCN\;(alc)}$ ; (iii) $\mathrm{H_3O^+}$ . [FIGURE] Compound $\mathrm{X}$ is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Crossed aldol with HCHO, then cyanohydrin formation, then hydrolysis and lactonisation. // 📝 Solution: $\left(\mathrm{CH_3}\right)_2\mathrm{CH}\mathrm{CHO}\;+\;\mathrm{HCHO}\;\xrightarrow{\;\mathrm{KOH}\;}\;\mathrm{HOCH_2}\mathrm{C}\left(\mathrm{CH_3}\right)_2\mathrm{CHO}\;\implies\;\mathrm{KCN}\;\text{gives cyanohydrin}\;\implies\;\mathrm{H_3O^+}\;\text{hydrolysis and lactonisation gives}\;\alpha\text{-hydroxy-}\gamma\text{-lactone}\;\implies\;\mathrm{X}\;=\;\left(\mathrm{CH_3}\right)_2\mathrm{CH}\mathrm{CHO}$

questions.text: Number of compounds from the following which will not dissolve in cold $\mathrm{NaHCO_3}$ and $\mathrm{NaOH}$ solutions but will dissolve in hot $\mathrm{NaOH}$ solution is ______ . [FIGURE] (seven compounds: p-toluic acid, methyl benzoate, p-tolyl acetate, 2-hydroxyacetophenone, 3-hydroxy-5-methylbenzaldehyde, isopropyl methoxybenzene, phenyl acetate)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Esters are insoluble in cold base but get hydrolysed and dissolve in hot NaOH; acids and phenols dissolve in cold base. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Acid dissolves in}\;\mathrm{NaHCO_3}\;;\;\text{phenols dissolve in cold}\;\mathrm{NaOH}\;;\;\text{ether is insoluble in hot}\;\mathrm{NaOH}\;\implies\;\text{only esters (compounds 2, 3, 7) qualify}\;\implies\;3$
questions.topic: Hydrolysis of esters and solubility tests

questions.text: Identify major product $\mathrm{P}$ formed in the following reaction. [FIGURE] benzene $+$ benzoyl chloride $\xrightarrow{\;\mathrm{Anhydrous\;AlCl_3}\;}\;\mathrm{P}\;\text{(Major Product)}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Friedel-Crafts acylation with an acyl chloride gives an aromatic ketone. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{PhCOCl}\;+\;\mathrm{AlCl_3}\;\implies\;\mathrm{PhCO^+}\;\text{acylium ion}\;\implies\;\text{electrophilic attack on benzene}\;\implies\;\mathrm{PhCOPh}\;\text{(benzophenone, option 4)}$

questions.text: The correct order of acidic strength of the major products formed in the given reactions, is : A. $\mathrm{PhNH_2}\;\xrightarrow{\;\left(1\right)\;\mathrm{NaNO_2}\;+\;\mathrm{HCl}\;\left(<5^\circ\mathrm{C}\right)\;;\;\left(2\right)\;\mathrm{CuCN}\;;\;\left(3\right)\;\mathrm{H_3O^+}/\Delta\;}\;\left[\mathrm{A}\right]$ B. $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CHO}\;\xrightarrow{\;\left[\mathrm{Ag}\left(\mathrm{NH_3}\right)_2\right]^+,\;\mathrm{OH^-},\;\Delta\;}\;\left[\mathrm{B}\right]$ C. $\mathrm{CH_4}\;+\;\mathrm{O_2}\;\xrightarrow{\;\left(\mathrm{i}\right)\;;\;\left(\mathrm{ii}\right)\;\mathrm{Na_2Cr_2O_7}/\mathrm{H^+}\;}\;\left[\mathrm{C}\right]$ D. $\mathrm{PhCH_2MgBr}\;+\;\mathrm{CO_2}\;\xrightarrow{\;\text{Dry ether};\;\mathrm{H_3O^+}\;}\;\left[\mathrm{D}\right]$ Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Lower pKa means stronger acid; identify each carboxylic acid formed and compare pKa. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{A}\;=\;\mathrm{PhCOOH}\;\left(\mathrm{pK_a}\;\approx\;4.2\right)\;,\;\mathrm{B}\;=\;\mathrm{CH_3CH_2COOH}\;\text{per key reasoning}\;\left(\mathrm{pK_a}\;\approx\;4.8\right)\;,\;\mathrm{C}\;=\;\mathrm{HCOOH}\;\left(3.8\right)\;,\;\mathrm{D}\;=\;\mathrm{PhCH_2COOH}\;\left(4.3\right)\;\implies\;C\;>\;A\;>\;D\;>\;B$
questions.topic: Acidic strength of carboxylic acids and their preparation

questions.text: Identify the product $\mathrm{P}$ in the following reaction: [FIGURE] cyclopentanecarboxylic acid $\xrightarrow{\;\mathrm{i)\;Br_2/Red\;P\;\;\;ii)\;H_2O}\;}\;\mathrm{P}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction brominates the alpha carbon of a carboxylic acid. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Br_2}/\mathrm{Red\;P}\;\implies\;\alpha\text{-bromination at ring carbon bearing}\;\mathrm{COOH}\;\implies\;\mathrm{H_2O}\;\text{hydrolyses acyl bromide}\;\implies\;\text{1-bromocyclopentanecarboxylic acid (option 1)}$

questions.text: [FIGURE] $\mathrm{P}\;\xrightarrow{\;?\;}\;\mathrm{PhCOOH}\;+\;\mathrm{PhCH_2OH}$ , where $\mathrm{P}$ is the open-chain alkane shown, $\mathrm{Q}\;=\;\mathrm{PhCOOH}$ and $\mathrm{R}\;=\;\mathrm{PhCH_2OH}$ . The correct sequence of reagents for the preparation of $\mathrm{Q}$ and $\mathrm{R}$ is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Aromatization, then Etard oxidation, then Cannizzaro reaction. // 📝 Solution: $\text{n-Heptane}\;\xrightarrow{\;\mathrm{Cr_2O_3,\;770\;K,\;20\;atm}\;}\;\text{Toluene}\;\xrightarrow{\;\mathrm{CrO_2Cl_2,\;H_3O^+}\;}\;\mathrm{PhCHO}\;\implies\;\mathrm{NaOH}\;\text{(Cannizzaro)}\;\implies\;\mathrm{PhCOONa}\;+\;\mathrm{PhCH_2OH}\;\xrightarrow{\;\mathrm{H_3O^+}\;}\;\mathrm{PhCOOH}\;+\;\mathrm{PhCH_2OH}$
questions.topic: Aromatization, Etard reaction and Cannizzaro reaction

questions.text: Major product $B$ of the following reaction has ______ $\pi$-bond. [FIGURE] ethylbenzene $\xrightarrow{\;\mathrm{KMnO_4-KOH},\;\Delta\;}\;\left(\mathrm{A}\right)\;\xrightarrow{\;\mathrm{HNO_3}/\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\;}\;\left(\mathrm{B}\right)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Side-chain oxidation gives benzoate; nitration occurs at the meta position; count ring, C=O and N=O pi bonds. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{A}\;=\;\mathrm{PhCOOK}\;\implies\;\mathrm{B}\;=\;\text{3-nitrobenzoic acid}\;\implies\;\pi\;\text{bonds}\;=\;3\;(\text{ring})\;+\;1\;(\mathrm{C=O})\;+\;1\;(\mathrm{N=O})\;=\;5$
questions.topic: Side-chain oxidation and nitration of benzoate

questions.text: The most stable carbocation for the following is: [FIGURE] (a) (b) (c) (d)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The +M effect of $\text{NH}_2$ stabilises a carbocation when its lone pair delocalises onto the positive carbon. // 📝 Solution: $\text{NH}_2$ lone pair delocalisation is possible only in structure $(c)$ $\implies$ most stable $\implies$ option $(1)$.

questions.text: Compound that will give positive Lassaigne's test for both nitrogen and halogen is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Positive Lassaigne's test needs C, N and X in one molecule to form NaCN and NaX. // 📝 Solution: $\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2\cdot\text{HCl}\xrightarrow{\text{Na fusion}}\text{NaCN}+\text{NaCl}\implies$ both tests positive $\implies$ option $(2)$.

questions.text: Which of the following conformations will be the most stable? (1) [FIGURE] (2) [FIGURE] (3) [FIGURE] (4) [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The most stable Newman conformer minimises van der Waals and torsional strain. // 📝 Solution: Conformer $(1)$ has the lowest van der Waals and torsional strain $\implies$ most stable $\implies$ option $(1)$.

questions.text: Resonance in carbonate ion $(\text{CO}_3^{2-})$ is [FIGURE]. Which of the following is true?

options.text: (1) It is possible to identify each structure individually by some physical or chemical method.
(2) All these structures are in dynamic equilibrium with each other.
(3) Each structure exists for equal amount of time.
(4) $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$ has a single structure i.e., resonance hybrid of the above three structures.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Resonance structures are hypothetical; only the resonance hybrid is real. // 📝 Solution: Resonance contributors are not separately observable $\implies$ $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$ is one resonance hybrid $\implies$ option $(4)$.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I : Sulphanilic acid gives esterification test for carboxyl group. Statement II : Sulphanilic acid gives red colour in Lassaigne's test for extra element detection. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer.

options.text: (1) Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
(2) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
(3) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
(4) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Sulphanilic acid contains $-\text{SO}_3\text{H}$, not $-\text{COOH}$, and both S and N. // 📝 Solution: No $-\text{COOH}$ $\implies$ no esterification (I false); S and N together give red colour (II true) $\implies$ option $(4)$.

questions.text: What is the correct order of acidity of the protons marked A–D in the given compounds? [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Acidity follows the stability of the conjugate base (resonance with COO⁻, sp carbanion, benzylic anion). // 📝 Solution: $H_C$ (COOH) $\implies$ $H_D$ (α to COOH) $\implies$ $H_A$ (alkyne C–H) $\implies$ $H_B$ (benzylic CH anion least stable) $\implies$ option $(2)$.

questions.text: Match items of Column I and Column II. Column I (Mixture of compounds): A. $\text{H}_2\text{O}/\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2$; B. [FIGURE]; C. Kerosene/Naphthalene; D. $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6$/NaCl. Column II (Separation technique): i. Crystallization; ii. Differential solvent extraction; iii. Column chromatography; iv. Fractional distillation. Correct match is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Match each technique to the property difference (solubility, polarity, boiling point, ionic crystallinity). // 📝 Solution: A (immiscible solvents) $\implies$ ii; B (polarity difference) $\implies$ iii; C (boiling point) $\implies$ iv; D (ionic solid) $\implies$ i $\implies$ option $(3)$.

questions.text: Match List I with List II. List I (Isomeric pairs): A. Propanamine and N-Methylethanamine; B. Hexan-2-one and Hexan-3-one; C. Ethanamide and Hydroxyethanimine; D. o-Nitrophenol and p-Nitrophenol. List II (Type of isomers): I. Metamers; II. Positional isomers; III. Functional isomers; IV. Tautomers. Choose the correct answer.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Compare functional groups, alkyl groups around the same group, and proton shift (tautomerism). // 📝 Solution: A: functional $\implies$ III; B: metamers $\implies$ I; C: tautomers $\implies$ IV; D: positional $\implies$ II $\implies$ option $(4)$.

questions.text: The isomeric deuterated bromide with molecular formula $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{DBr}$ having two chiral carbon atoms is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A chiral carbon carries four different groups; test each C–Br and C–D candidate. // 📝 Solution: In $\text{CH}_3\text{-}C^*\text{HBr-}C^*\text{HD-CH}_3$ both starred carbons have four different groups $\implies$ two chiral centres $\implies$ option $(3)$.

questions.text: The total number of chiral compound/s from the following is ____. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A compound is chiral if it has neither a plane (POS) nor a centre (COS) of symmetry. // 📝 Solution: Among the listed structures exactly two lack POS and COS $\implies$ total chiral $=2$.

questions.text: All structures given below are of vitamin C. Most stable of them is : [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Conjugated enediol and intramolecular H-bonding stabilise a structure. // 📝 Solution: Structure $(1)$ has a conjugated $\text{C=C}$ enediol with H-bonding $\implies$ most stable $\implies$ option $(1)$.

questions.text: In the following halogenated organic compounds, the one with maximum number of chlorine atoms in its structure is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Count Cl atoms in each structure. // 📝 Solution: Chloral $\text{Cl}_3\text{CCHO}\to3$; Gammaxene $\text{C}_6\text{H}_6\text{Cl}_6\to6$; chloropicrin $\text{CCl}_3\text{NO}_2\to3$; Freon-12 $\text{CCl}_2\text{F}_2\to2$ $\implies$ option $(2)$.

questions.text: An organic compound $[\text{A}]\,(\text{C}_4\text{H}_{11}\text{N})$ shows optical activity and gives $\text{N}_2$ gas on treatment with $\text{HNO}_2$. The compound $[\text{A}]$ reacts with $\text{PhSO}_2\text{Cl}$ producing a compound soluble in KOH. The structure of A is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\text{N}_2$ evolution with $\text{HNO}_2$ indicates a primary amine; Hinsberg product soluble in KOH confirms it. // 📝 Solution: $\text{HNO}_2\implies\text{N}_2$ $\implies$ primary amine; sulphonamide of $\text{PhSO}_2\text{Cl}$ soluble in KOH $\implies$ chiral primary amine $\implies$ option $(4)$.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Sublimation is used for the separation and purification of compounds with low melting point. Statement II: The boiling point of a liquid increases as the external pressure is reduced. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer.

options.text: (1) Both Statement I and Statement II are true
(2) Statement I is true but Statement II is false
(3) Both Statement I and Statement II are false
(4) Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Sublimation depends on vapour pressure; boiling point falls as external pressure falls. // 📝 Solution: Sublimation is not based on low melting point (I false); $T_b$ decreases with reduced pressure (II false) $\implies$ option $(3)$.
questions.topic: Purification by sublimation and boiling point

questions.text: Following chromatogram was developed by adsorption of compound A on a 6 cm TLC glass plate. Retardation factor of compound A is ____ $\times 10^{-1}$. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $R_f=\dfrac{\text{distance moved by substance from base line}}{\text{distance moved by solvent from base line}}$. // 📝 Solution: $R_f=\dfrac{3.0\;\text{cm}}{5.0\;\text{cm}}=0.6=6\times10^{-1}\implies x=6$.

questions.text: Assertion A : Benzene is more stable than hypothetical cyclohexatriene. Reason R : The delocalized $\pi$ electron cloud is attracted more strongly by nuclei of carbon atoms. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer.

options.text: (1) A is true but R is false
(2) A is false but R is true
(3) Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
(4) Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Delocalisation lowers the energy of the $\pi$ system; check whether R explains A. // 📝 Solution: Benzene is more stable than cyclohexatriene (A true) $\implies$ delocalised $\pi$ cloud is attracted by all carbon nuclei, lowering energy (R true, correct explanation).

questions.text: Given below are four compounds: (a) n-propyl chloride (b) iso-propyl chloride (c) sec-butyl chloride (d) neo-pentyl chloride. Percentage of carbon in the one which exhibits optical isomerism is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Optical isomerism requires one chiral carbon with four different groups. // 📝 Solution: Only sec-butyl chloride is chiral $\implies$ $\%\text{C}=\dfrac{48}{92.5}\times100\implies51.9\implies52$ $\implies$ option $(3)$.

questions.text: Increasing order of stability of the resonance structures (A) [FIGURE] (B) [FIGURE] (C) [FIGURE] (D) [FIGURE] is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Rank resonance forms by covalent bonds, octet completion and charge on electronegative atoms. // 📝 Solution: Analysis gives $C \;<\; A \;<\; B \;<\; D$ $\implies$ no option matches exactly; NTA key marks option $(2)$.

questions.text: In Dumas method for the estimation of $\text{N}_2$, the sample is heated with copper oxide and the gas evolved is passed over :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Traces of nitrogen oxides must be reduced to $\text{N}_2$ before measurement. // 📝 Solution: $\text{NO}_x$ traces are reduced to $\text{N}_2$ over hot copper gauze $\implies$ option $(2)$.

questions.text: Consider the following reaction: Propanal $+$ Methanal $\xrightarrow[\text{(iii) NaCN}]{\text{(i) dil. NaOH, (ii) }\Delta}$ Product B $(\text{C}_5\text{H}_8\text{O}_3)$ ; then (iv) $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$. The correct statement for product B is :

options.text: (1) optically active and adds one mole of bromine
(3) racemic mixture and gives a gas with saturated NaHCO3 solution
(4) optically active alcohol and is neutral

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Aldol condensation, cyanohydrin formation and hydrolysis give a hydroxy acid. // 📝 Solution: Aldol $\implies$ $\text{CH}_2=\text{C(CH}_3)\text{CHO}$ $\implies$ $\text{CH}_2=\text{C(CH}_3)\text{CH(OH)COOH}$ (racemic acid) $\implies$ releases $\text{CO}_2$ with $\text{NaHCO}_3$ $\implies$ option $(3)$.

questions.text: Identify the correct order for the given property for the following compounds. (A) Boiling point: [FIGURE] (B) Density: [FIGURE] (C) Boiling point: [FIGURE] (D) Density: [FIGURE] (E) Boiling point: [FIGURE] Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Boiling point rises with chain length and falls with branching; density rises Cl < Br < I. // 📝 Solution: (A), (C), (E) follow these trends $\implies$ correct; (B) and (D) violate density order $\implies$ option $(2)$.
questions.topic: Boiling point and density of haloalkanes

questions.text: The total number of asymmetric carbon atom/s in testosterone is ____. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: An asymmetric carbon bears four different groups; mark each stereogenic sp³ carbon. // 📝 Solution: Testosterone has six stereocentres (marked with asterisks) $\implies$ answer $6$. [FIGURE]

questions.text: In sulphur estimation, $0.471$ g of an organic compound gave $1.4439$ g of barium sulphate. The percentage of sulphur in the compound is ____ (Nearest Integer). Given: Ba $=137$, S $=32$, O $=16$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\%\,\text{S}=\dfrac{32}{233}\times\dfrac{\text{mass of BaSO}_4}{\text{mass of compound}}\times100$. // 📝 Solution: $\%\,\text{S}=\dfrac{32}{233}\times\dfrac{1.4439}{0.471}\times100\implies 42.10\implies 42$.

questions.text: Total number of essential amino acids among the given list is ____. Arginine, Phenylalanine, Aspartic acid, Cysteine, Histidine, Valine, Proline
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall the standard list of essential amino acids (obtained from diet). // 📝 Solution: Essential $\implies$ Arginine, Phenylalanine, Histidine, Valine $\implies$ count $=\;4$

questions.text: From the given following (A to D) cyclic structures, those which will not react with Tollen's reagent are: [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Tollen's reagent needs a free aldehyde, which comes from the open-chain form of a hemiacetal. // 📝 Solution: A and D are hemiacetals $\implies$ react; B and C are acetal/glycoside-type $\implies$ no free CHO $\implies$ B and C
questions.topic: Carbohydrates – cyclic forms and Tollen's test

questions.text: A protein 'X' with molecular weight of 70,000 u, on hydrolysis gives amino acids. One of these amino acids is: [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Protein hydrolysis yields $\alpha$-amino acids, with $\text{NH}_2$ on the carbon next to COOH. // 📝 Solution: Official key marks option (1) $\implies$ Correct A; verify the structure against the source paper
questions.topic: Amino acids – identification of αα-amino acid

questions.text: DNA molecule contains 4 bases whose structures are shown below. One of the structures is not correct. Identify the incorrect base structure. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: DNA bases are adenine, guanine, cytosine and thymine; match each ring pattern. // 📝 Solution: Structures (1) thymine, (3) cytosine and (4) adenine are DNA bases $\implies$ structure (2) is not a DNA base $\implies$ option (2)

questions.text: Sugar which does not give reddish brown precipitate with Fehling's reagent is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Reducing sugars possess a free hemiacetal or aldehyde group. // 📝 Solution: Sucrose $\implies$ both anomeric carbons in glycosidic bond $\implies$ non-reducing $\implies$ no Fehling test

questions.text: A student is given one compound among the following compounds that gives positive test with Tollen's reagent. [FIGURE] The compound is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Tollen's test requires a free aldehyde or a ring-opening hemiacetal. // 📝 Solution: A and B are acetal/ether-type $\implies$ no CHO; D has no hemiacetal $\implies$ no test; C is a cyclic hemiacetal $\implies$ open-chain CHO $\implies$ option (4) = C

questions.text: Match items of Row I with those of Row II. Row I: (P), (Q), (R), (S) [FIGURE]. Row II: (i) $\alpha$-D-(−) Fructofuranose, (ii) $\beta$-D-(−) Fructofuranose, (iii) $\alpha$-D-(+) Glucopyranose, (iv) $\beta$-D-(+) Glucopyranose. Correct match is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Ring size (5 = furanose, 6 = pyranose) and C1 OH orientation (α/β) decide the match. // 📝 Solution: P (pyranose, α) $\implies$ iii; Q (pyranose, β) $\implies$ iv; R $\implies$ i; S $\implies$ ii $\implies$ option (4)

questions.text: The correct statements are: A. Activation energy for enzyme catalysed hydrolysis of sucrose is lower than that of acid catalysed hydrolysis. B. During denaturation, secondary and tertiary structures are destroyed but primary structure remains intact. C. Nucleotides are joined by glycosidic linkage between $C_1$ and $C_4$ carbons of the pentose sugar. D. Quaternary structure of proteins represents overall folding of the polypeptide chain.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Check enzyme catalysis, denaturation, nucleotide linkage and levels of protein structure. // 📝 Solution: A true; B true; C false (3′–5′ phosphodiester); D false (tertiary structure) $\implies$ A and B only
questions.topic: Mixed – enzymes, proteins and nucleic acids

questions.text: Match List I with List II. List I: A. $\alpha$-Glucose and $\alpha$-Galactose, B. $\alpha$-Glucose and $\beta$-Glucose, C. $\alpha$-Glucose and $\alpha$-Fructose, D. $\alpha$-Glucose and $\alpha$-Ribose. List II: I. Functional isomers, II. Homologous, III. Anomers, IV. Epimers. Choose the correct answer.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Epimers differ at one stereocentre; anomers differ only at C1. // 📝 Solution: Glc/Gal differ at C4 $\implies$ IV; Glc/Glc differ at C1 $\implies$ III; Glc/Fru $\implies$ I; Glc/Ribose $\implies$ II $\implies$ A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II

questions.text: The number of possible tripeptides formed involving alanine (ala), glycine (gly) and valine (val), where no amino acid has been used more than once is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Each tripeptide must use all three distinct amino acids once. // 📝 Solution: Number of arrangements $=\;3!\;=\;6$

questions.text: Coagulation of egg on heating is because of:

options.text: The secondary structure of protein remains unchanged
Biological property of protein remains unchanged
Breaking of the peptide linkage in the primary structure of protein occurs

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Heat disrupts the non-covalent bonds that hold the folded structure. // 📝 Solution: Heating $\implies$ unfolding of secondary and tertiary structure $\implies$ denaturation $\implies$ coagulation $\implies$ option (2)

questions.text: Question text is blank in the uploaded PDF. Answer key: option (3).
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Source question missing from PDF. // 📝 Solution: Official answer key gives option (3) $\implies$ Correct C; verify question text from the original paper

questions.text: The number of tripeptides formed by three different amino acids using each amino acid once is ____.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Count the arrangements of three distinct amino acids in three positions. // 📝 Solution: $3!\;=\;3\;\times\;2\;\times\;1\;=\;6$

questions.text: Assertion (A): Ketoses give Seliwanoff's test faster than aldoses. Reason (R): Ketoses undergo $\beta$-elimination followed by formation of furfural. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Seliwanoff's test depends on rapid dehydration of ketoses to 5-hydroxymethylfurfural. // 📝 Solution: Ketoses dehydrate faster $\implies$ faster coloured complex (A true); this dehydration pathway is R $\implies$ option (2)

questions.text: The incorrect statements regarding enzymes are: (A) Enzymes are biocatalysts. (B) Enzymes are non-specific and can catalyse different kinds of reactions. (C) Most enzymes are globular proteins. (D) Enzyme oxidase catalyses the hydrolysis of maltose into glucose.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Enzymes are highly specific, and maltose hydrolysis is catalysed by maltase. // 📝 Solution: A and C true; B false (specific); D false (maltase, not oxidase) $\implies$ incorrect statements are (B) and (D)

questions.text: Number of cyclic tripeptides formed with 2 amino acids A and B is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Count distinct cyclic arrangements, treating rotations as identical. // 📝 Solution: AAA, BBB, AAB, ABB $\implies$ 4 distinct cyclic tripeptides

questions.text: Which of the following gives a positive test with ninhydrin?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Ninhydrin detects free $\alpha$-amino groups. // 📝 Solution: Egg albumin is a protein $\implies$ free $\alpha$-amino groups $\implies$ positive test $\implies$ option (2)

questions.text: Following tetrapeptide can be represented as: [FIGURE] (F, L, D, Y, I, Q, P are one letter codes for amino acids)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Read the chain from the free NH2 (N-terminus) and match side chains. // 📝 Solution: Benzyl side chain $\implies$ F; isobutyl $\implies$ L; $\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$ $\implies$ D; p-hydroxybenzyl $\implies$ Y $\implies$ FLDY

questions.text: Compound A, $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_5$, gives a tetraacetate with $\text{Ac}_2\text{O}$. Oxidation of A with $\text{Br}_2-\text{H}_2\text{O}$ gives an acid, $\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_6$. Reduction of A with HI gives isopentane. The possible structure of A is: [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Tetraacetate indicates four OH groups; HI reduction to isopentane indicates a five-carbon chain. // 📝 Solution: Four OH groups $\implies$ tetraacetate; C5 skeleton $\implies$ isopentane; oxidation to acid $\implies$ option (2)

questions.text: Both human DNA and RNA are chiral molecules. The chirality in DNA and RNA arises due to the presence of:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Look at the sugar units in the nucleotide backbone. // 📝 Solution: Deoxyribose (DNA) and ribose (RNA) are D-sugars $\implies$ source of chirality $\implies$ option (4)
questions.topic: Nucleic acids – chirality of sugar units

questions.text: Given below are two statements. Statement I: Sucrose is dextrorotatory. However, sucrose upon hydrolysis gives a solution having a mixture of products, and this solution shows laevorotation. Statement II: Hydrolysis of sucrose gives glucose and fructose. Since the laevorotation of glucose is more than the dextrorotation of fructose, the resulting solution becomes laevorotatory. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer.

options.text: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall the specific rotations of sucrose, glucose and fructose. // 📝 Solution: Sucrose $\left(+66.5^{\circ}\right)$ $\implies$ glucose $\left(+52.5^{\circ}\right)$ + fructose $\left(-92.4^{\circ}\right)$ $\implies$ laevorotation $\implies$ I true; II false (glucose is dextro, fructose is laevo)
questions.topic: Carbohydrates – optical rotation and inversion of sugar

questions.text: In the given pentapeptide, find out an essential amino acid (Y) and the sequence present in the pentapeptide: [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Identify the essential residue and read the chain from N-terminus to C-terminus. // 📝 Solution: Only Threonine is essential $\implies$ Y = Threonine; N $\to$ C sequence $\implies$ Thr-Ser-Asp-Gly-Ala $\implies$ option (4)

questions.text: The incorrect statement about glucose is:

options.text: Glucose is soluble in water because of having aldehyde functional group
Glucose remains in multiple isomeric forms in its aqueous solution
Glucose is one of the monomer units in sucrose

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Water solubility arises from polar OH groups forming hydrogen bonds. // 📝 Solution: Solubility $\implies$ multiple OH groups (H-bonding), not the CHO group $\implies$ statement (1) incorrect $\implies$ option (1)

questions.text: Structures of four disaccharides are given below. Among the given disaccharides, the non-reducing sugar is: [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A non-reducing sugar has no free hemiacetal (anomeric) OH group. // 📝 Solution: Both anomeric carbons are engaged in the glycosidic bond (sucrose type) $\implies$ no free CHO $\implies$ option (3)

questions.text: Match List I (Bio Polymer) with List II (Monomer). List I: A. Starch, B. Cellulose, C. Nucleic acid, D. Protein. List II: I. Nucleotide, II. $\alpha$-glucose, III. $\beta$-glucose, IV. $\alpha$-amino acid. Choose the correct answer.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Identify the monomer unit of each biopolymer. // 📝 Solution: Starch $\implies$ $\alpha$-glucose; Cellulose $\implies$ $\beta$-glucose; Nucleic acid $\implies$ nucleotide; Protein $\implies$ $\alpha$-amino acid $\implies$ A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV

questions.text: Match List I with List II. List I (Reaction of glucose with): A. Hydroxylamine, B. $\mathrm{Br}_2$ water, C. Excess acetic anhydride, D. Concentrated $\mathrm{HNO}_3$. List II (Product formed): I. Gluconic acid, II. Glucose pentacetate, III. Saccharic acid, IV. Glucoxime. Choose the correct answer.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Identify which group (CHO, all OH groups, or both ends) each reagent attacks. // 📝 Solution: $\text{NH}_2\text{OH}$ $\implies$ oxime (IV); $\mathrm{Br}_2$/water $\implies$ gluconic acid (I); $\text{Ac}_2\text{O}$ $\implies$ pentacetate (II); conc. $\mathrm{HNO}_3$ $\implies$ saccharic acid (III) $\implies$ A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III

questions.text: The total number of correct statements regarding nucleic acids is: A. RNA is regarded as the reserve of genetic information. B. DNA molecule self-duplicates during cell division. C. DNA synthesizes proteins in the cell. D. The message for the synthesis of particular proteins is present in DNA. E. Identical DNA strands are transferred to daughter cells.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Check each statement against DNA replication and the central dogma. // 📝 Solution: A false; B true; C false (RNA synthesises proteins); D true; E true $\implies$ correct count $=3$
questions.topic: Nucleic acids – roles of DNA and RNA

questions.text: Assertion (A): $\alpha$-halocarboxylic acid on reaction with dil. $\text{NH}_3$ gives good yield of $\alpha$-amino carboxylic acid, whereas the yield of amines is very low when prepared from alkyl halides. Reason (R): Amino acids exist in zwitter ion form in aqueous medium. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Consider the ammonolysis yield issue and the stability of zwitter ions. // 📝 Solution: Dil. $\text{NH}_3$ gives good $\alpha$-amino acid yield (A true); zwitter ion form (R true) $\implies$ official key option (1)
questions.topic: Amino acids – preparation and zwitter ion

questions.text: Type of amino acids obtained by hydrolysis of proteins is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Peptide bonds link the carboxyl group of one amino acid to the $\alpha$-amino group of the next. // 📝 Solution: Proteins $\implies$ polymers of $\alpha$-amino acids $\implies$ acidic hydrolysis $\implies$ $\alpha$-amino acids

questions.text: The total number of carbon atoms present in tyrosine, an amino acid, is ____.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Count carbons in the benzene ring, side-chain CH2, $\alpha$-carbon and COOH. // 📝 Solution: $6+1+1+1\;=\;9$

questions.text: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Ziegler catalyst, B. Blood pigment, C. Wilkinson catalyst, D. Vitamin $\mathrm{B}_{12}$. List II: I. Rhodium, II. Cobalt, III. Iron, IV. Titanium. Choose the correct answer.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall the metal centre present in each catalyst or biomolecule. // 📝 Solution: Ziegler $\implies$ Ti (IV); Blood pigment $\implies$ Fe (III); Wilkinson $\implies$ Rh (I); $\mathrm{B}_{12}$ $\implies$ Co (II) $\implies$ A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II
questions.topic: Bioinorganic chemistry – metals in catalysts and biomolecules

questions.text: Identify the correct statements. A. Arginine and Tryptophan are essential amino acids. B. Histidine does not contain a heterocyclic ring in its structure. C. Proline is a six membered cyclic ring amino acid. D. Glycine does not have a chiral centre. E. Cysteine has characteristic side chain $\text{MeS}\;-\;\text{CH}_2\;-\;\text{CH}_2\;-$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Check essential amino acids, proline ring size, glycine structure and side-chain identity. // 📝 Solution: B false (imidazole ring); C false (five-membered ring); D true (CH2 α-carbon); E false ($\text{–CH}_2\text{SH}$ is cysteine) $\implies$ A and D as per key

questions.text: Which structure of protein remains intact after coagulation of egg white on boiling?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Heat breaks non-covalent bonds, while covalent peptide bonds survive. // 📝 Solution: Boiling $\implies$ denaturation $\implies$ loss of secondary, tertiary and quaternary structure $\implies$ primary structure intact

questions.text: Total number of tripeptides possible by mixing of valine and proline is ____.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Each of the three positions can be filled by either amino acid. // 📝 Solution: $2^{3}\;=\;8$

questions.text: Uracil is a base present in RNA with the following structure: [FIGURE]. % of N in uracil is ____. Given: molar mass N = 14 g mol$^{-1}$, O = 16 g mol$^{-1}$, C = 12 g mol$^{-1}$, H = 1 g mol$^{-1}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\%\text{N}\;=\;\dfrac{\text{mass of N}}{\text{molar mass}}\times100$. // 📝 Solution: $M(\text{C}_4\text{H}_4\text{N}_2\text{O}_2)\;=\;48+4+28+32\;=\;112$ $\implies$ $\%\text{N}\;=\;\dfrac{28}{112}\times100\;=\;25\%$

questions.text: A short peptide on complete hydrolysis produces 3 moles of glycine (G), 2 moles of leucine (L) and 2 moles of valine (V) per mole of peptide. The number of peptide linkages in it is ____.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Peptide linkages $=$ total residues $-\;1$. // 📝 Solution: Total residues $=\;3+2+2\;=\;7$ $\implies$ linkages $=\;7-1\;=\;6$

questions.text: Number of compounds among the following which contain sulphur as heteroatom is ____. Furan, Thiophene, Pyridine, Pyrrole, Cysteine, Tyrosine
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Look for S in a ring or in a side chain. // 📝 Solution: Thiophene (ring S) and Cysteine ($\text{–SH}$) $\implies$ count $=2$

questions.text: If one strand of a DNA has the sequence $\mathrm{ATGCTTCA}$, the sequence of bases in the complementary strand is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Pair A with T and G with C; the complementary strand runs antiparallel. // 📝 Solution: $\text{A}\;\leftrightarrow\;\text{T}$, $\text{G}\;\leftrightarrow\;\text{C}$ $\implies$ $\mathrm{ATGCTTCA}\;\implies\;\mathrm{TACGAAGT}$
questions.topic: Nucleic acids – base pairing in DNA

questions.text: Vanillin compound obtained from vanilla beans has total sum of oxygen atoms and $\pi$ electrons equal to ____. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Count O atoms, then count $\pi$ bonds (each double bond gives two $\pi$ electrons). // 📝 Solution: $\text{C}_8\text{H}_8\text{O}_3$ $\implies$ O $=\;3$; $\pi$-bonds $=\;4$ $\implies$ $\pi$-electrons $=\;8$ $\implies$ $3+8\;=\;11$

questions.text: A compound (x) with molar mass $108\;\text{g mol}^{-1}$ undergoes acetylation to give a product with molar mass $192\;\text{g mol}^{-1}$. The number of amino groups in compound (x) is ____.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Each $\text{–NH}_2$ acetylation replaces H by $\text{COCH}_3$, adding 42 u. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta M\;=\;192\;-\;108\;=\;84$ $\implies$ $n\;=\;\dfrac{84}{42}\;=\;2$
questions.topic: Amines – acetylation and functional group counting

questions.text: Match List I (Test) and List II (Functional group / Class of compound). List I: A. Molisch's Test, B. Biuret Test, C. Carbylamine Test, D. Schiff's Test. List II: I. Peptide, II. Carbohydrate, III. Primary amine, IV. Aldehyde. Choose the correct answer.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Match each colour test to the functional group it detects. // 📝 Solution: Molisch $\implies$ carbohydrate (II); Biuret $\implies$ peptide (I); Carbylamine $\implies$ primary amine (III); Schiff $\implies$ aldehyde (IV) $\implies$ A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV

questions.text: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Glucose / $\mathrm{NaHCO}_3$ / $\Delta$, B. Glucose / $\mathrm{HNO}_3$, C. Glucose / HI / $\Delta$, D. Glucose / Bromine water. List II: I. Gluconic acid, II. No reaction, III. n-hexane, IV. Saccharic acid. Choose the correct answer.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Mild oxidants act only on CHO; $\mathrm{HNO}_3$ oxidises both ends; HI reduces fully. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{NaHCO}_3$ $\implies$ II; $\mathrm{HNO}_3$ $\implies$ IV; HI/$\Delta$ $\implies$ III; $\mathrm{Br}_2$/water $\implies$ I $\implies$ A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I

questions.text: Which of the following is the correct structure of L-Glucose? [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: L-glucose is the mirror image of D-glucose, so every stereocentre is inverted. // 📝 Solution: D-glucose has OH right at C2, C4, C5 and left at C3 $\implies$ L-glucose has OH left at C2, C4, C5 and right at C3 $\implies$ option (1)

questions.text: Two nucleotides are joined together by a linkage known as:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The bond joins the 3′-OH of one sugar to the 5′-phosphate of the next. // 📝 Solution: Nucleotide $\implies$ $3'\text{–}5'$ bond via phosphate $\implies$ phosphodiester linkage

questions.text: From the vitamins A, B1, B6, B12, C, D, E and K, the number of vitamins that can be stored in our body is ____.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall which vitamins are fat-soluble or stored in the liver. // 📝 Solution: Storable vitamins $\implies$ A, D, E, K and B12 $\implies$ count $=5$

questions.text: The incorrect statement regarding the given structure is: [FIGURE]

options.text: Can be oxidized to a dicarboxylic acid with $\mathrm{Br}_2$ water
Will coexist in equilibrium with 2 other cyclic structures
Despite the presence of $\text{–CHO}$ does not give Schiff's test

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mathrm{Br}_2$ water oxidises only the CHO group of an aldose. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Br}_2$/$\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$ $\implies$ CHO to COOH only $\implies$ monocarboxylic (gluconic) acid, not dicarboxylic $\implies$ option (1)

questions.text: For a reaction, $N_2O_{5(g)} \to 2NO_{2(g)} + \frac{1}{2}O_{2(g)}$ in a constant volume container, no products were present initially. The final pressure of the system when $50\%$ of reaction gets completed is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: At constant $V$ and $T$, $P \propto n$; build a pressure table with extent $x$ // 📝 Solution: $x \;=\; \frac{P_0}{2} \implies P_{total} \;=\; (P_0 - x) + 2x + \frac{x}{2} \;=\; P_0 + 1.5x \;=\; P_0 + 0.75P_0 \;=\; \frac{7}{4}P_0$
questions.topic: Partial pressure and gaseous reaction extent

questions.text: At sea level, the dry air mass percentage composition is nitrogen gas $70.0$, oxygen gas $27.0$ and argon gas $3.0$. If total pressure is $1.15\;\mathrm{atm}$, calculate (i) $P_{\mathrm{N_2}}/P_{\mathrm{O_2}}$ and (ii) $P_{\mathrm{O_2}}/P_{\mathrm{Ar}}$. Given molar mass of N, O and Ar are 14, 16 and $40\;\mathrm{g\;mol^{-1}}$ respectively.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For ideal gas mixtures $P_i \propto n_i$ (Dalton's law); use mole ratios from mass percentages // 📝 Solution: $n_{\mathrm{N_2}} = 70/28 = 2.5$, $n_{\mathrm{O_2}} = 27/32 \approx 0.844$, $n_{\mathrm{Ar}} = 3/40 = 0.075$ $\implies$ $\dfrac{P_{\mathrm{N_2}}}{P_{\mathrm{O_2}}} = \dfrac{2.5}{0.844} \approx 2.96$ and $\dfrac{P_{\mathrm{O_2}}}{P_{\mathrm{Ar}}} = \dfrac{0.844}{0.075} \approx 11.2$

questions.text: A sample of $n$-octane ($1.14\,\text{g}$, molar mass $114\,\text{g mol}^{-1}$) is completely burnt in excess oxygen in a bomb calorimeter of heat capacity $5\,\text{kJ K}^{-1}$. The temperature rises by $5\,\text{K}$. The magnitude of the heat of combustion of octane at constant volume is ____ $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ (nearest integer).
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $q = C_{\text{cal}}\,\Delta T$, then scale to one mole. // 📝 Solution: $q = 5\times5 = 25\,\text{kJ}$ and $n = \dfrac{1.14}{114} = 0.01\,\text{mol}$ $\implies$ $\left\lvert\Delta_c U\right\rvert = \dfrac{25}{0.01} = 2500\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$.
questions.topic: Bomb calorimetry and heat of combustion

questions.text: Consider the following standard enthalpies of reaction (in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$): $\text{C}_2\text{H}_6\left(g\right)+\frac{7}{2}\text{O}_2\left(g\right)\to 2\text{CO}_2\left(g\right)+3\text{H}_2\text{O}\left(l\right)$, $\Delta H_1^\circ\;=\;-1550$; $\text{C}\left(\text{graphite}\right)+\text{O}_2\left(g\right)\to\text{CO}_2\left(g\right)$, $\Delta H_2^\circ\;=\;-393.5$; $\text{H}_2\left(g\right)+\frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2\left(g\right)\to\text{H}_2\text{O}\left(l\right)$, $\Delta H_3^\circ\;=\;-286$. The magnitude of $\Delta H_f^\circ\left(\text{C}_2\text{H}_6\right)$ is ______ $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ (nearest integer).
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Apply Hess's law to $2\text{C}+3\text{H}_2\to\text{C}_2\text{H}_6$. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta H_f\;=\;2\Delta H_2\;+\;3\Delta H_3\;-\;\Delta H_1\implies\;-787\;-\;858\;+\;1550\;=\;-95\implies\;\left\lvert\Delta H_f\right\rvert\;=\;95$
questions.topic: Hess's law and enthalpy of formation

questions.text: The bond dissociation enthalpy of $\text{X}_2$ ($\Delta H_{\text{bond}}$) calculated from the given data is ______ $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ (nearest integer). Given: $\text{M}^+\text{X}^-\left(s\right)\to\text{M}^+\left(g\right)+\text{X}^-\left(g\right)$, $\Delta H_{\text{lattice}}\;=\;800$; $\text{M}\left(s\right)\to\text{M}\left(g\right)$, $\Delta H_{\text{sub}}\;=\;100$; $\text{M}\left(g\right)\to\text{M}^+\left(g\right)+e^-$, $\Delta H_i\;=\;500$; $\text{X}\left(g\right)+e^-\to\text{X}^-\left(g\right)$, $\Delta H_{eg}\;=\;-300$; $\text{M}\left(s\right)+\frac{1}{2}\text{X}_2\left(g\right)\to\text{M}^+\text{X}^-\left(s\right)$, $\Delta H_f\;=\;-400$ (all in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$).
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Construct the Born–Haber cycle for $\text{M}^+\text{X}^-$. // 📝 Solution: $-400\;=\;100\;+\;500\;+\;\frac{1}{2}\text{BE}\;-\;300\;-\;800\implies\;\frac{1}{2}\text{BE}\;=\;100\implies\;\text{BE}\;=\;200\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$

questions.text: The total enthalpy change for freezing 1 mol of water at $10^\circ\text{C}$ to ice at $-10^\circ\text{C}$ is ____. Given: $\Delta_{\text{fus}}H = x\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, $C_p[\text{H}_2\text{O(l)}] = y\,\text{J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$, $C_p[\text{H}_2\text{O(s)}] = z\,\text{J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use a path: cool the liquid to $0^\circ\text{C}$, freeze it, then cool the solid to $-10^\circ\text{C}$. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta H = y(0-10) - x\times1000 + z(-10-0)$ $\implies$ $\Delta H = -10(100x+y+z)\,\text{J}$.
questions.topic: Hess's law and temperature dependence of enthalpy

questions.text: Vessels A (filled with a gas at a certain pressure) and B (evacuated) are connected by a stopcock and immersed in water in thermal equilibrium. After opening the stopcock, the gas expands from A into B and no change in the thermometer reading is observed. Which statement is true?

options.text: The pressure in vessel B before opening the stopcock is zero

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Free expansion into a vacuum has $P_{\text{ext}}=0$, so no work, no heat, and no temperature change. // 📝 Solution: Thermometer unchanged $\implies$ $q=0$, $w=0$, $\Delta U=0$; expansion into an evacuated $B$ needs $P_B=0$ before opening $\implies$ D (A–C also hold for free expansion, the key selects D).

questions.text: Consider the following data: heat of formation of $\text{CO}_2\left(g\right)\;=\;-393.5\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$; heat of formation of $\text{H}_2\text{O}\left(l\right)\;=\;-286.0\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$; heat of combustion of benzene $=\;-3267.0\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. The heat of formation of benzene is ______ $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ (nearest integer).
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\Delta H_c\;=\;\sum\Delta H_f\left(\text{products}\right)\;-\;\sum\Delta H_f\left(\text{reactants}\right)$ for $\text{C}_6\text{H}_6+\frac{15}{2}\text{O}_2\to 6\text{CO}_2+3\text{H}_2\text{O}$. // 📝 Solution: $-3267\;=\;6\left(-393.5\right)\;+\;3\left(-286\right)\;-\;\Delta H_f\left(\text{C}_6\text{H}_6\right)\implies\;\Delta H_f\;=\;48\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$

questions.text: Statement I: When ice in equilibrium with liquid water is heated, heat is absorbed and the temperature stays constant until all the ice melts. Statement II: At the melting point, the absorbed heat overcomes intermolecular attraction and the kinetic energy of the molecules does not increase. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer.

options.text: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Latent heat at a phase change goes into breaking intermolecular forces, not raising temperature. // 📝 Solution: Heat absorbed at the melting point overcomes intermolecular attraction $\implies$ $T$ stays constant $\implies$ both statements are true.

questions.text: A liquid when kept inside a thermally insulated closed vessel at $25^{\circ}C$ was mechanically stirred from outside. What will be the correct option for the following thermodynamic parameters ?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: First law: $\Delta U \;=\; q + w$ // 📝 Solution: Insulated $\implies q \;=\; 0$; stirring is work done on the liquid $\implies w > 0 \implies \Delta U \;=\; w > 0$

questions.text: Ice at $-5^\circ\text{C}$ is heated to become vapour at $110^\circ\text{C}$ at atmospheric pressure. The entropy change associated with this process can be obtained from:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Add $\int C_p\,dT/T$ for each heating step and $\Delta H/T$ for each phase change. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta S_{\text{total}}\;=\;\Delta S_1\;+\;\Delta S_2\;+\;\Delta S_3\;+\;\Delta S_4\;+\;\Delta S_5$ with heating steps as $\int\frac{C_{p,m}}{T}dT$ and phase changes as $\frac{\Delta H}{T}$

questions.text: Standard entropies of $X_2$, $Y_2$ and $XY_5$ are $70, 50$ and $110\;J\;K^{-1}\;mol^{-1}$ respectively. The temperature in Kelvin at which the reaction $\frac{1}{2}X_2 + \frac{5}{2}Y_2 \rightleftharpoons XY_5$, $\Delta H^{\Theta} \;=\; -35\;kJ\;mol^{-1}$ will be at equilibrium is _______. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: At equilibrium $\Delta G^{\circ} \;=\; 0 \implies T \;=\; \frac{\Delta H^{\circ}}{\Delta S^{\circ}}$ // 📝 Solution: $\Delta S^{\circ} \;=\; 110 - \left( 35 + 125 \right) \;=\; -50 \implies T \;=\; \frac{-35000}{-50} \;=\; 700\;K$

questions.text: Consider an endothermic reaction which is non-spontaneous at the freezing point of water. However, the reaction is spontaneous at the boiling point of water. Choose the correct option.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Spontaneity requires $\Delta G\;=\;\Delta H\;-\;T\Delta S\;<\;0$. // 📝 Solution: Endothermic $\implies\;\Delta H\;>\;0$; spontaneous only at high $T$ $\implies\;T\Delta S\;>\;\Delta H\implies\;\Delta S\;>\;0$

questions.text: Resonance in $\text{X}_2\text{Y}$ is represented as [FIGURE]. The enthalpy of formation of $\text{X}_2\text{Y}$ from $\text{X}\equiv\text{X(g)} + \tfrac12\text{Y}=\text{Y(g)}$ is $80\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. Bond energies (kJ mol$^{-1}$): $\text{X}\equiv\text{X}$ = 940, $\text{X}=\text{X}$ = 410, $\text{Y}=\text{Y}$ = 500, $\text{X}=\text{Y}$ = 602. The magnitude of the resonance energy of $\text{X}_2\text{Y}$ is ____ kJ mol$^{-1}$ (nearest integer).
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\Delta H_{\text{RE}} = \Delta H_{f(\text{exp})} - \Delta H_{f(\text{theo})}$, where the theoretical value comes from bond energies. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta H_{f(\text{theo})} = \left(940 + \tfrac12\times500\right) - (410+602) = 178$ $\implies$ $\Delta H_{\text{RE}} = 80-178 = -98$ $\implies$ magnitude $98$.

questions.text: Which of the following graphs correctly represents the variation of thermodynamic properties of Haber's process, $\text{N}_2 + 3\text{H}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3$ ($\Delta H^\circ<0$, $\Delta S^\circ<0$), with temperature? [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\Delta G^\circ = \Delta H^\circ - T\Delta S^\circ$, and $\Delta H^\circ$, $\Delta S^\circ$ are nearly constant with $T$. // 📝 Solution: $-\dfrac{\Delta G^\circ}{T} = -\dfrac{\Delta H^\circ}{T} + \Delta S^\circ$ $\implies$ only graph 1 shows flat $\Delta H^\circ$, $\Delta S^\circ$ with the correct $-\Delta G^\circ/T$ trend $\implies$ A.

questions.text: Which of the following mixing of $1\;\text{M}$ base and $1\;\text{M}$ acid leads to the largest increase in temperature?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Largest heat from the most moles of strong acid–strong base neutralised in the smallest final volume. // 📝 Solution: Options A and B use a weak acid $\implies$ lower heat; D neutralises only $20\;\text{mmol}$ in $70\;\text{mL}$ $\implies$ C ($30\;\text{mmol}$ in $60\;\text{mL}$) is largest

questions.text: An ideal gas undergoes a cyclic transformation starting from point $A$ and returning to the same point by tracing the path $A \to B \to C \to D \to A$ as shown in the three cases [FIGURE]. Choose the correct option regarding $\Delta U$:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Internal energy is a state function. // 📝 Solution: Cyclic process $\implies\;\oint dU\;=\;0\implies\;\Delta U$ is the same (zero) in all three cases

questions.text: The formation enthalpies $\Delta_f H^\ominus$ for $\text{H}\left(g\right)$ and $\text{O}\left(g\right)$ are $220.0$ and $250.0\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ respectively at $298.15\;\text{K}$, and $\Delta_f H^\ominus$ for $\text{H}_2\text{O}\left(g\right)$ is $-242.0\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ at the same temperature. The average bond enthalpy of the $\text{O-H}$ bond in water at $298.15\;\text{K}$ is ______ $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ (nearest integer).
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Atomise $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ into $2\text{H}+\text{O}$ and equate with $2\times$ BE(O–H). // 📝 Solution: $-242\;=\;2\left(220\right)\;+\;250\;-\;2\,\text{BE}\left(\text{O-H}\right)\implies\;\text{BE}\left(\text{O-H}\right)\;=\;466\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$

questions.text: Given: $\text{S}\left(g\right)+\frac{3}{2}\text{O}_2\left(g\right)\to\text{SO}_3\left(g\right)+2x\;\text{kcal}$ and $\text{SO}_2\left(g\right)+\frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2\left(g\right)\to\text{SO}_3\left(g\right)+y\;\text{kcal}$. The heat of formation of $\text{SO}_2\left(g\right)$ is given by:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Subtract the second reaction from the first to get $\text{S}+\text{O}_2\to\text{SO}_2$. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta H\;=\;\Delta H_1\;-\;\Delta H_2\implies\;-2x\;-\;\left(-y\right)\;=\;\left(y\;-\;2x\right)\;\text{kcal}$

questions.text: $500\;\text{J}$ of energy is transferred as heat to $0.5\;\text{mol}$ of Argon gas at $298\;\text{K}$ and $1.00\;\text{atm}$. The final temperature and the change in internal energy respectively are: (Given $R\;=\;8.3\;\text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: At constant pressure $q_p\;=\;nC_p\Delta T$ and $\Delta U\;=\;nC_v\Delta T$. // 📝 Solution: $500\;=\;0.5\times\frac{5}{2}\times 8.3\times\left(T_f-298\right)\implies T_f\;\approx\;348\;\text{K}\implies\Delta U\;=\;\frac{3}{5}\times 500\;=\;300\;\text{J}$
questions.topic: Heat, internal energy and enthalpy of ideal gas

questions.text: The standard enthalpy and standard entropy of decomposition of N$_2$O$_4$ to NO$_2$ are $55.0\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ and $175.0\;\text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$ respectively. The standard free energy change for this reaction at $25^\circ\text{C}$ in $\text{J mol}^{-1}$ is ______ (nearest integer).
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $\Delta G^\circ\;=\;\Delta H^\circ\;-\;T\Delta S^\circ$ with consistent units. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta G^\circ\;=\;55000\;-\;298\times 175\implies\;55000\;-\;52150\;=\;2850\;\text{J mol}^{-1}$

questions.text: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: The term standard state implies a temperature of $0^\circ\text{C}$
The standard state of a pure gas is the pure gas at 1 bar and 273 K

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Standard state fixes pressure at 1 bar only; elements in their reference form have zero $\Delta_f H^\circ$. // 📝 Solution: $\text{O}_2\text{(g)}$ is the reference form of oxygen $\implies$ $\Delta_f H^\circ = 0$ at the specified temperature $\implies$ D; atomic $\text{O(g)}$ has nonzero $\Delta_f H^\circ$.
questions.topic: Standard states and enthalpy of formation

questions.text: Match List-I (Partial Derivatives) with List-II (Thermodynamic Quantity): (A) $\left(\frac{\partial G}{\partial T}\right)_P$ (B) $\left(\frac{\partial H}{\partial T}\right)_P$ (C) $\left(\frac{\partial G}{\partial P}\right)_T$ (D) $\left(\frac{\partial U}{\partial T}\right)_V$ ; (I) $C_p$ (II) $-S$ (III) $C_v$ (IV) $V$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $dG\;=\;V\,dP\;-\;S\,dT$, $dH\;=\;C_p\,dT$ at constant $P$ and $dU\;=\;C_v\,dT$ at constant $V$. // 📝 Solution: $\left(\frac{\partial G}{\partial T}\right)_P\;=\;-S$, $\left(\frac{\partial H}{\partial T}\right)_P\;=\;C_p$, $\left(\frac{\partial G}{\partial P}\right)_T\;=\;V$, $\left(\frac{\partial U}{\partial T}\right)_V\;=\;C_v$

questions.text: Given: $\text{HCl(g)} + 10\,\text{H}_2\text{O(l)} \rightarrow \text{HCl}\cdot10\,\text{H}_2\text{O}$, $\Delta H = -69.01\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ and $\text{HCl(g)} + 40\,\text{H}_2\text{O(l)} \rightarrow \text{HCl}\cdot40\,\text{H}_2\text{O}$, $\Delta H = -72.79\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. Choose the correct statement.

options.text: Dissolution of HCl(g) in water is an endothermic process
The heat of solution depends on the amount of solvent
The heat of dilution from $\text{HCl}\cdot10\,\text{H}_2\text{O}$ to $\text{HCl}\cdot40\,\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is $3.78\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$
The heat of formation of HCl solution is represented by both (a) and (b)

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Compare the two solution enthalpies for different amounts of solvent. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta H$ differs with solvent amount ($-69.01$ vs $-72.79$) $\implies$ heat of solution depends on solvent; dilution is $-3.78\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ (not $+3.78$), so C is wrong.

questions.text: If $C$ (diamond) $\to$ $C$ (graphite) $+ X\;kJ\;mol^{-1}$, $C$(diamond) $+ O_2(g) \to CO_2(g) + Y\;kJ\;mol^{-1}$, $C$ (graphite) $+ O_2(g) \to CO_2(g) + Z\;kJ\;mol^{-1}$ at constant temperature. Then
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Hess's law: diamond $\to$ graphite $=$ (diamond combustion) $-$ (graphite combustion) // 📝 Solution: Heat released: $X \;=\; Y - Z$ (diamond $+ O_2 \to CO_2 + Y$, then $CO_2 \to$ graphite $+ O_2 - Z$)

questions.text: Ice and water are placed in a closed container at a pressure of $1\;\text{atm}$ and temperature $273.15\;\text{K}$. If the pressure of the system is increased $2$ times keeping temperature constant, identify the correct observation.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The solid–liquid line in the phase diagram of water has a negative slope. // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] $P\;\uparrow\;\implies$ ice $\to$ water (denser phase favoured) $\implies$ only the liquid phase remains

questions.text: The effect of temperature on spontaneity of reactions are represented as : (A) $\Delta H \;=\; +$, $\Delta S \;=\; -$, any T, Non spontaneous (B) $\Delta H \;=\; +$, $\Delta S \;=\; +$, low T, spontaneous (C) $\Delta H \;=\; -$, $\Delta S \;=\; -$, low T, Non spontaneous (D) $\Delta H \;=\; -$, $\Delta S \;=\; +$, any T, spontaneous. The incorrect combinations are :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\Delta G \;=\; \Delta H - T\Delta S$; spontaneous when $\Delta G < 0$ // 📝 Solution: (A) and (D) are correct; (B) $+,+$ is spontaneous only at high T; (C) $-,-$ is spontaneous at low T $\implies$ (B) and (C) are incorrect

questions.text: Which of the following statements are TRUE about Haloform reaction?: A. Sodium hypochlorite reacts with KI to give KOI. B. KOI is a reducing agent. C. $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated methylketone $\left(\mathrm{CH_3-CH=CH-CO-CH_3}\right)$ will give iodoform reaction. D. Isopropyl alcohol will not give iodoform test. E. Methanoic acid will give positive iodoform test. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: KOI is an oxidising agent; $\mathrm{CH_3CO-}$ and $\mathrm{CH_3CH\left(OH\right)-}$ give iodoform. // 📝 Solution: A true $\;;\;$ B false (oxidant) $\;;\;$ C true (methyl ketone) $\;;\;$ D false ($\mathrm{\left(CH_3\right)_2CHOH}$ gives iodoform) $\;;\;$ E false $\implies$ A & C only

questions.text: This reduction reaction is known as: [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mathrm{H_2,\;Pd\text{-}BaSO_4}$ converts an acid chloride to an aldehyde. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{PhCOCl}\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{H_2,\;Pd\text{-}BaSO_4}}\;\mathrm{PhCHO}\;\implies$ Rosenmund reduction

questions.text: $x$ is the product which is obtained from propanenitrile and stannous chloride in the presence of hydrochloric acid followed by hydrolysis. $y$ is the product which is obtained from the but-2-ene by the ozonolysis followed by hydrolysis. From the following, which product is not obtained when one mole of $x$ and one mole of $y$ react with each other in the presence of alkali followed by heating?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Stephen reduction gives an aldehyde; ozonolysis of but-2-ene gives ethanal; then cross aldol. // 📝 Solution: $x\;=\;\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CHO}$, $y\;=\;\mathrm{CH_3CHO}$ $\implies$ products: 2-methylpent-2-enal, but-2-enal, pent-2-enal, 2-methylbut-2-enal $\implies$ 3-methylbut-2-enal is not formed

questions.text: Identify the name reaction. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mathrm{CO,\;HCl,\;AlCl_3/CuCl}$ formylates benzene. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{C_6H_6}\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{CO,\;HCl,\;AlCl_3/CuCl}}\;\mathrm{C_6H_5CHO}\;\implies$ Gattermann-Koch reaction

questions.text: Identify the product in the following reaction : [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Zn-Hg/HCl is Clemmensen reduction and reduces both $\mathrm{C=O}$ groups to $\mathrm{CH_2}$. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{-CHO}\;\to\;\mathrm{-CH_3}$ and $\mathrm{-COCH_3}\;\to\;\mathrm{-CH_2CH_3}\;\implies$ 1-ethyl-3-methylbenzene $\implies$ option (1)

questions.text: The structures of major products A, B and C in the following reaction are sequence. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Cyanohydrin formation, then LiAlH4 reduces CN to CH2NH2, and acid hydrolysis converts CN to COOH. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{A}\;=\;$ cyanohydrin $\;;\;$ $\mathrm{LiAlH_4}\;\implies\;\mathrm{B}\;=\;\mathrm{-CH_2NH_2}$ $\;;\;$ $\mathrm{HCl/H_2O},\;\Delta\;\implies\;\mathrm{C}\;=\;\mathrm{-COOH}$ $\implies$ option (4)

questions.text: The product of the following reaction is $P$. [FIGURE] The number of hydroxyl groups present in the product $P$ is _______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Grignard reagent first deprotonates the acidic phenolic OH. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{PhMgBr}\;+\;\mathrm{ArOH}\;\to\;\mathrm{C_6H_6}\;+\;\mathrm{ArOMgBr}\;\implies$ $P\;=\;$ benzene $\implies$ $0$ hydroxyl groups

questions.text: The compound A, $\mathrm{C_8H_8O_2}$ reacts with acetophenone to form a single product via cross-Aldol condensation. The compound A on reaction with conc. $\mathrm{NaOH}$ forms a substituted benzyl alcohol as one of the two products. The compound A is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: No $\alpha\mathrm{-H}$ aldehyde undergoes both Claisen-Schmidt and Cannizzaro reactions. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{C_8H_8O_2}$ aldehyde without $\alpha\mathrm{-H}$ $\implies$ $\mathrm{4\text{-}CH_3OC_6H_4CHO}$; Cannizzaro gives 4-methoxybenzyl alcohol and 4-methoxybenzoate

questions.text: Given below are two statements : Statement I : Acidity of $\alpha$-hydrogens of aldehydes and ketones is responsible for Aldol reaction. Statement II : Reaction between benzaldehyde and ethanal will NOT give Cross-Aldol product. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer.

options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
