questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Cross aldol needs one partner with an acidic $\alpha$-hydrogen. // 📝 Solution: Aldol needs acidic $\alpha\mathrm{-H}$ $\implies$ I correct $\;;\;$ $\mathrm{PhCHO}$ (no $\alpha\mathrm{-H}$) $+\;\mathrm{CH_3CHO}$ gives cinnamaldehyde (cross aldol) $\implies$ II incorrect

questions.text: Match List - I with List - II. List-I (Reactions): (A) $\mathrm{CH_3\left(CH_2\right)_5COOC_2H_5\;\to\;CH_3\left(CH_2\right)_5CHO}$ (B) $\mathrm{C_6H_5COC_6H_5\;\to\;C_6H_5CH_2C_6H_5}$ (C) $\mathrm{C_6H_5CHO\;\to\;C_6H_5CH\left(OH\right)CH_3}$ (D) $\mathrm{CH_3COCH_2COOC_2H_5\;\to\;CH_3CH\left(OH\right)CH_2COOC_2H_5}$. List-II (Reagents): (I) $\mathrm{CH_3MgBr,\;H_2O}$ (II) $\mathrm{Zn\left(Hg\right)\;and\;conc.\;HCl}$ (III) $\mathrm{NaBH_4,\;H^+}$ (IV) $\mathrm{DIBAL\text{-}H,\;H_2O}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: DIBAL-H reduces an ester to an aldehyde; Clemmensen reduces a carbonyl to CH2. // 📝 Solution: A $\;\to\;$ DIBAL-H (IV) $\;;\;$ B $\;\to\;$ Zn(Hg)/HCl (II) $\;;\;$ C $\;\to\;$ $\mathrm{CH_3MgBr}$ (I) $\;;\;$ D $\;\to\;$ $\mathrm{NaBH_4}$ (III)

questions.text: Find out the major products from the following reaction sequence. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Cyanohydrin, then hydrolysis and esterification; excess Grignard converts the ester into a tertiary alcohol. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{A}$: $\mathrm{NaCN}$ then $\mathrm{EtOH/H_3O^+}\;\implies\;$ hydroxy ester $\mathrm{ArC\left(OH\right)\left(CH_3\right)CO_2Et}$ $\;;\;$ $\mathrm{B}$: excess $\mathrm{MeMgBr}\;\implies\;$ diol $\implies$ option (2)
questions.topic: Cyanohydrin and Grignard reaction on ester

questions.text: Which among the following aldehydes is most reactive towards nucleophilic addition reactions?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Less steric hindrance and fewer +I groups give higher reactivity. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{HCHO}$ has the least steric hindrance and the highest partial positive charge on carbonyl C $\implies$ most reactive

questions.text: Match List - I with List - II. List-I (Test): (A) Bayer's test (B) Ceric ammonium nitrate test (C) Phthalein dye test (D) Schiff's test. List-II (Identification): (I) Phenol (II) Aldehyde (III) Alcoholic-OH group (IV) Unsaturation
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall what each qualitative test detects. // 📝 Solution: Bayer's $\;\to\;$ unsaturation $\;;\;$ CAN $\;\to\;$ alcoholic $\mathrm{-OH}$ $\;;\;$ phthalein dye $\;\to\;$ phenol $\;;\;$ Schiff's $\;\to\;$ aldehyde $\implies$ A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II

questions.text: Iodoform test can differentiate between A. Methanol and Ethanol B. $\mathrm{CH_3COOH}$ and $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2COOH}$ C. Cyclohexene and cyclohexanone D. Diethyl ether and Pentan-3-one E. Anisole and acetone. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Only one member of the pair must contain $\mathrm{CH_3CO-}$ or $\mathrm{CH_3CH\left(OH\right)-}$. // 📝 Solution: A: ethanol positive, methanol negative $\;;\;$ E: acetone positive, anisole negative $\;;\;$ B, C, D: both negative $\implies$ A & E only

questions.text: Number of isomeric compounds with molecular formula $\mathrm{C_9H_{10}O}$ which (i) do not dissolve in $\mathrm{NaOH}$ (ii) do not dissolve in $\mathrm{HCl}$ (iii) do not give orange precipitate with 2, 4 $-$ DNP (iv) on hydrogenation give identical compound with molecular formula $\mathrm{C_9H_{12}O}$ is ______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: No phenol, no amine, no carbonyl means an ether; hydrogenation must give the same product. // 📝 Solution: The compound is $\mathrm{Ph-CH=CH-O-CH_3}$ $\implies$ cis and trans isomers $\implies$ total $\;=\;2$

questions.text: From the compounds given below, number of compounds which give positive Fehling's test is _______ Benzaldehyde, Acetaldehyde, Acetone, Acetophenone, Methanal, 4-nitrobenzaldehyde, cyclohexane carbaldehyde.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Only aliphatic aldehydes respond to Fehling's solution. // 📝 Solution: Acetaldehyde, methanal and cyclohexane carbaldehyde are aliphatic aldehydes $\implies$ count $\;=\;3$

questions.text: A trisubstituted compound 'A', $\mathrm{C_{10}H_{12}O_2}$ gives neutral $\mathrm{FeCl_3}$ test positive. Treatment of compound 'A' with $\mathrm{NaOH}$ and $\mathrm{CH_3Br}$ gives $\mathrm{C_{11}H_{14}O_2}$, with hydroiodic acid gives methyl iodide and with hot conc. $\mathrm{NaOH}$ gives a compound B, $\mathrm{C_{10}H_{12}O_2}$. Compound 'A' also decolorises alkaline $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$. The number of $\pi$ bond/s present in the compound 'A' is _______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use the degree of unsaturation and identify phenol, aldehyde/alkene functional groups. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{DBE}\;=\;\frac{2\times 10\;+\;2\;-\;12}{2}\;=\;5\;\implies$ benzene ring ($3\;\pi$ and one ring) plus one more $\pi$ bond ($\mathrm{C=O}$) $\implies$ total $\pi\;=\;3\;+\;1\;=\;4$

questions.text: $\mathrm{R}$ formed in the following sequence of reaction is: [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Cyanohydrin formation, then acid hydrolysis and esterification, then Grignard addition to the ester. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{ArCOCH_3}\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{NaCN/HOAc}}\;\mathrm{ArC\left(OH\right)\left(CH_3\right)CN}\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{EtOH/H^+}}\;\mathrm{ArC\left(OH\right)\left(CH_3\right)CO_2Et}\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{2MeMgBr,\;H_3O^+}}\;\mathrm{ArC\left(OH\right)\left(CH_3\right)C\left(OH\right)\left(CH_3\right)_2}\;\implies$ option (2)
questions.topic: Cyanohydrin and Grignard reaction on ester

questions.text: The number of molecules which gives haloform test among the following molecules is ______ . [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Haloform test is given by $\mathrm{CH_3CO-}$ and $\mathrm{CH_3CH\left(OH\right)-}$ groups. // 📝 Solution: Count the molecules that contain a methyl ketone or a $\mathrm{CH_3CH\left(OH\right)-}$ group $\implies$ total $\;=\;4$

questions.text: Match List - I with List - II. List - I (Reagents): A. $\mathrm{H_2,\;Pd-BaSO_4}$ B. $\mathrm{SnCl_2,\;HCl}$ C. $\mathrm{CrO_2Cl_2,\;CS_2}$ D. $\mathrm{CO,\;HCl,\;Anhyd.\;AlCl_3}$. List - II (Reaction Name, involving aldehydes): I. Etard Reaction II. Rosenmund Reduction III. Gatterman - Koch Reaction IV. Stephen Reaction
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Match each reagent with its aldehyde-forming named reaction. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{H_2/Pd\text{-}BaSO_4}\;\to\;$ Rosenmund $\;;\;$ $\mathrm{SnCl_2/HCl}\;\to\;$ Stephen $\;;\;$ $\mathrm{CrO_2Cl_2}\;\to\;$ Etard $\;;\;$ $\mathrm{CO/HCl/AlCl_3}\;\to\;$ Gattermann-Koch $\implies$ A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III

questions.text: Which of the following compounds would give the following set of qualitative analysis? (i) Fehling's Test : Positive (ii) Na fusion extract upon treatment with sodium nitroprusside gives a blood red colour but not [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Aromatic aldehydes do not give Fehling's test; blood red colour with nitroprusside needs both N and S. // 📝 Solution: Options (1), (2), (3) are heteroaryl aldehydes $\implies$ Fehling's negative $\;;\;$ option (4) has an aliphatic $\mathrm{-CHO}$ and both N and S $\implies$ option (4)

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I (Reaction): (A) Hoffmann Degradation (B) Clemenson reduction (C) Cannizaro reaction (D) Reimer-Tiemann reaction. List-II (Reagents): (I) Conc. $\mathrm{KOH}$, $\Delta$ (II) $\mathrm{CHCl_3}$, $\mathrm{NaOH/H_3O^+}$ (III) $\mathrm{Br_2}$, $\mathrm{NaOH}$ (IV) $\mathrm{Zn\text{-}Hg/HCl}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall the reagent of each named reaction. // 📝 Solution: Hoffmann $\;\to\;\mathrm{Br_2/NaOH}$ $\;;\;$ Clemmensen $\;\to\;\mathrm{Zn\text{-}Hg/HCl}$ $\;;\;$ Cannizzaro $\;\to\;$ conc. $\mathrm{KOH}$, $\Delta$ $\;;\;$ Reimer-Tiemann $\;\to\;\mathrm{CHCl_3/NaOH}$ $\implies$ A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II

questions.text: Cyclohexylamine when treated with nitrous acid yields (P). On treating (P) with PCC results in (Q). When (Q) is heated with dil. $\mathrm{NaOH}$ we get (R). The final product (R) is : [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Amine to alcohol with $\mathrm{HNO_2}$, alcohol to ketone with PCC, then aldol condensation. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{C_6H_{11}NH_2}\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{HNO_2}}\;\mathrm{C_6H_{11}OH}\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{PCC}}\;\mathrm{cyclohexanone}\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{NaOH},\;\Delta}\;$ 2-cyclohexylidenecyclohexanone $\implies$ option (2)

questions.text: Which of the following compounds will give silver mirror with ammoniacal silver nitrate? A. Formic acid B. Formaldehyde C. Benzaldehyde D. Acetone. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Tollens' test is given by aldehydes and formic acid. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{HCOOH}$, $\mathrm{HCHO}$ and $\mathrm{PhCHO}$ reduce Tollens' reagent; acetone does not $\implies$ A, B and C only

questions.text: Assertion A : Acetal/Ketal is stable in basic medium. Reason R : The high leaving tendency of alkoxide ion gives the stability to acetal/ketal in basic medium. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer.

options.text: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Acetals are ethers, and the alkoxide ion is a poor leaving group. // 📝 Solution: Acetals/ketals are stable to bases and break down in acid $\implies$ A true $\;;\;$ $\mathrm{RO^-}$ is a poor leaving group $\implies$ R false $\implies$ option (1)

questions.text: Match the LIST-I with LIST-II. List-I (Reagents): A. $\mathrm{NH_2-NH_2,\;KOH}$ B. $\mathrm{Ag\left(NH_3\right)_2OH}$ C. Aq. $\mathrm{CuSO_4}$, Sodium potassium tartarate, $\mathrm{KOH}$ D. $\mathrm{Zn-Hg,\;HCl}$. List-II (Name of reaction involving carbonyl compounds): I. Tollen's Test II. Clemmensen Reduction III. Wolff-Kishner Reduction IV. Fehling's Test
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall the reagent of each named reaction/test. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{NH_2NH_2/KOH}\;\to\;$ Wolff-Kishner $\;;\;$ $\mathrm{Ag\left(NH_3\right)_2OH}\;\to\;$ Tollens $\;;\;$ $\mathrm{CuSO_4/tartrate/KOH}\;\to\;$ Fehling $\;;\;$ $\mathrm{Zn\text{-}Hg/HCl}\;\to\;$ Clemmensen
questions.topic: Named reactions and tests of carbonyl compounds

questions.text: The number of molecules which gives haloform test among the following molecules is ______. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Haloform test is given by $\mathrm{CH_3CO-}$ and $\mathrm{CH_3CH\left(OH\right)-}$ groups. // 📝 Solution: Count molecules having a methyl ketone or a $\mathrm{CH_3CH\left(OH\right)-}$ unit $\implies$ total $\;=\;3$

questions.text: Which of the following compound can give positive iodoform test when treated with aqueous $\mathrm{KOH}$ solution followed by potassium hypoiodite. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: gem-Dihalide hydrolyses to a carbonyl compound. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CCl_2CH_3}\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{aq.\;KOH}}\;\mathrm{CH_3CH_2COCH_3}\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{KOI}}\;\mathrm{CH_3CH_2COOK}\;+\;\mathrm{CHI_3}\downarrow$

questions.text: m-chlorobenzaldehyde on treatment with $50\%\;\mathrm{KOH}$ solution yields [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Aldehydes without $\alpha$-hydrogen undergo Cannizzaro reaction. // 📝 Solution: $2\;\mathrm{m\text{-}ClC_6H_4CHO}\;\xrightarrow{50\%\;\mathrm{KOH}}\;\mathrm{m\text{-}ClC_6H_4COO^-}\;+\;\mathrm{m\text{-}ClC_6H_4CH_2OH}\;\implies$ option (2)

questions.text: Identify $\mathrm{A}$ in the following reaction: [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mathrm{N_2H_4}$ followed by ethylene glycol/KOH is Wolff-Kishner reduction. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{CH_3COCH_2CH_3}\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{N_2H_4,\;KOH/glycol}}\;\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2CH_3}$ (butane) $\implies$ option (4)

questions.text: Match List I with List II. List-I (Test): A. $\mathrm{Br_2}$ water test B. Ceric ammonium nitrate test C. Ferric chloride test D. 2, 4 - DNP test. List-II (Observation): I. Yellow orange or orange red precipitate formed II. Reddish orange colour disappears III. Red colour appears IV. Blue, Green, Violet or Red colour appear
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall the observation for each qualitative test. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Br_2}$ water $\to$ colour disappears (II) $\;;\;$ CAN $\to$ red colour (III) $\;;\;$ $\mathrm{FeCl_3}\to$ violet/blue/green (IV) $\;;\;$ 2,4-DNP $\to$ orange precipitate (I)

questions.text: Number of compounds giving (i) red colouration with ceric ammonium nitrate and also (ii) positive iodoform test from the following is ______ [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Ceric ammonium nitrate (CAN) test is given by alcohols; the iodoform test needs $\mathrm{CH_3CH\left(OH\right)-}$ or $\mathrm{CH_3CO-}$. // 📝 Solution: Alcohols with $\mathrm{CH_3CH\left(OH\right)-}$ are 1-phenylpropan-2-ol, butan-2-ol and 1-cyclohexylpropan-2-ol $\implies$ count $\;=\;3$

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Cross aldol condensation between two different aldehydes will always produce four different products. Statement II: When semicarbazide reacts with a mixture of benzaldehyde and acetophenone under optimum pH, it forms a condensation product with acetophenone only. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below

options.text: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Four products need both aldehydes to have $\alpha$-hydrogen; aldehydes are more reactive than ketones. // 📝 Solution: I: if one aldehyde lacks $\alpha\mathrm{-H}$, fewer products form $\implies$ false $\;;\;$ II: $\mathrm{PhCHO}$ reacts faster than acetophenone $\implies$ false

questions.text: The compound formed by the reaction of ethanal with semicarbazide contains _______ number of nitrogen atoms.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Semicarbazone formation retains all N atoms of semicarbazide. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{CH_3CHO}\;+\;\mathrm{H_2N-NH-CO-NH_2}\;\to\;\mathrm{CH_3CH=N-NH-CO-NH_2}\;\implies$ $3$ N atoms

questions.text: Assertion A : [FIGURE] can be easily reduced using $\mathrm{Zn\text{-}Hg/HCl}$ to [FIGURE]. Reason R : $\mathrm{Zn\text{-}Hg/HCl}$ is used to reduce carbonyl group to $\mathrm{-CH_2-}$ group. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer.

options.text: A is false but R is true
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Clemmensen reduction uses strong acid, so it is unsuitable for acid-sensitive groups. // 📝 Solution: The tertiary alcohol is acid sensitive and reacts with $\mathrm{HCl}$ to give an alkyl chloride $\implies$ A false $\;;\;$ R is a true statement $\implies$ option (1)

questions.text: Identify major product $\mathrm{X}$ formed in the following reaction : [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mathrm{CO,\;HCl,\;AlCl_3/CuCl}$ is the Gattermann-Koch reaction. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{C_6H_6}\;+\;\mathrm{CO}\;+\;\mathrm{HCl}\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{AlCl_3/CuCl}}\;\mathrm{C_6H_5CHO}\;\implies$ option (3)

questions.text: In the Claisen-Schmidt reaction to prepare $351\;\mathrm{g}$ of dibenzalacetone using $87\;\mathrm{g}$ of acetone, the amount of benzaldehyde required is ______ g. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $2\;\mathrm{PhCHO}\;+\;\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3}\;\to\;$ dibenzalacetone; use mole ratio. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Moles}\;=\;\frac{351}{234}\;=\;1.5\;\implies\;\mathrm{PhCHO}\;=\;3\;\mathrm{mol}\;\implies\;3\;\times\;106\;=\;318\;\mathrm{g}$

questions.text: Identify the reagents used for the following conversion [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: DIBAL-H selectively reduces an ester to an aldehyde; alc. NaOH gives intramolecular aldol; Clemmensen removes C=O. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{A}$: DIBAL-H (ester to $\mathrm{CHO}$) $\implies$ $\mathrm{B}$: $\mathrm{NaOH_{\left(alc\right)}}$ (intramolecular aldol) $\implies$ $\mathrm{C}$: $\mathrm{Zn/HCl}$ (Clemmensen)

questions.text: An organic compound P of molecular formula $\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_3}$ gives positive Iodoform test but negative Tollen's test. When P is treated with dilute acid, it produces Q. Q gives positive Tollen's test and also iodoform test. The structure of P is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: An acetal hides the aldehyde and hydrolyses in acid to a free $\mathrm{-CHO}$. // 📝 Solution: P has $\mathrm{CH_3CO-}$ and an acetal $\mathrm{-CH\left(OCH_3\right)_2}$ $\implies$ $\mathrm{H^+/H_2O}$ gives $\mathrm{CH_3COCH_2CHO}$ (Tollens and iodoform positive) $\implies$ option (1)

questions.text: The number of the correct reaction(s) among the following is ______ [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Check each named reaction: Friedel-Crafts acylation, Rosenmund, Gattermann-Koch, amide hydrolysis. // 📝 Solution: (A) gives benzophenone, not diphenylmethane $\implies$ wrong $\;;\;$ (B) Rosenmund gives $\mathrm{PhCHO}$ $\implies$ wrong $\;;\;$ (C) Gattermann-Koch is correct $\;;\;$ (D) gives $\mathrm{PhCOOH}$ $\implies$ wrong $\implies$ only $1$

questions.text: Two moles of benzaldehyde and one mole of acetone under alkaline conditions using aqueous $\mathrm{NaOH}$ after heating gives $x$ as the major product. The number of $\pi$ bonds in the product $x$ is _______
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The product is dibenzalacetone $\mathrm{PhCH=CH-CO-CH=CHPh}$. // 📝 Solution: $\pi\;=\;2\times 3\;(\mathrm{rings})\;+\;2\;(\mathrm{C=C})\;+\;1\;(\mathrm{C=O})\;=\;9$

questions.text: The correct statements from the following are: (A) The decreasing order of atomic radii of group 13 elements is $\text{Tl}>\text{In}>\text{Ga}>\text{Al}>\text{B}$. (B) Down group 13, electronegativity decreases from top to bottom. (C) Al dissolves in dil. HCl and liberates $\text{H}_2$ but conc. $\text{HNO}_3$ renders Al passive by forming a protective oxide layer. (D) All group 13 elements exhibit highly stable +1 oxidation state. (E) Hybridisation of Al in $[\text{Al(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+}$ is $sp^3d^2$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Check periodic trends in radius and electronegativity, and the passivation of Al. // 📝 Solution: (A) $\text{Al}>\text{Ga}$ in size $\;\implies\;$ false; (B) EN not monotonic ($\text{Ga}>\text{Al}$) $\;\implies\;$ false; (C) true; (D) +3 is stable $\;\implies\;$ false; (E) octahedral $\;\implies\;$ $sp^3d^2$ true $\;\implies\;$ option C.
questions.topic: Trends and reactions of group 13 elements

questions.text: Assertion A: The stability order of +1 oxidation state of Ga, In and Tl is $\text{Ga}^{+}\;<\;\text{In}^{+}\;<\;\text{Tl}^{+}$. Reason R: The inert pair effect stabilizes the lower oxidation state down the group. Choose the correct answer.

options.text: A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Think about how $ns^2$ electrons behave down group 13. // 📝 Solution: Inert pair effect $\;\implies\;$ $\text{M}^{+}$ stability rises down group $\;\implies\;$ $\text{Ga}^{+}<\text{In}^{+}<\text{Tl}^{+}$ $\;\implies\;$ R explains A.

questions.text: Lithium aluminium hydride can be prepared from the reaction of:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Hydride transfer from LiH to a Lewis acidic aluminium halide. // 📝 Solution: $8\text{LiH}\;+\;\text{Al}_2\text{Cl}_6\;\rightarrow\;2\text{LiAlH}_4\;+\;6\text{LiCl}$

questions.text: The number of ions from the following that are expected to behave as oxidising agents is: $\text{Sn}^{4+},\;\text{Sn}^{2+},\;\text{Pb}^{2+},\;\text{Tl}^{3+},\;\text{Pb}^{4+},\;\text{Tl}^{+}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Inert pair effect makes the higher oxidation state of heavier elements unstable. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Tl}^{3+}\;\rightarrow\;\text{Tl}^{+}$ and $\text{Pb}^{4+}\;\rightarrow\;\text{Pb}^{2+}$ favourable $\;\implies\;$ 2 oxidising ions.
questions.topic: Inert pair effect and oxidising ions

questions.text: Statement I: $\text{SiO}_2$ and $\text{GeO}_2$ are acidic while SnO and PbO are amphoteric in nature. Statement II: Allotropic forms of carbon are due to the property of catenation and $p\pi-d\pi$ bond formation. Choose the most appropriate answer.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Carbon has no d-orbitals in its valence shell. // 📝 Solution: $\text{SiO}_2,\;\text{GeO}_2$ acidic; SnO, PbO amphoteric $\;\implies\;$ I true. Carbon lacks d-orbitals $\;\implies\;$ $p\pi-d\pi$ invalid; allotropy from catenation and $p\pi-p\pi\;\implies\;$ II false.

questions.text: Consider the oxides of group 14 elements $\text{SiO}_2$, $\text{GeO}_2$, $\text{SnO}_2$, $\text{PbO}_2$, CO and GeO. The amphoteric oxides are:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Amphoteric oxides react with both acids and bases. // 📝 Solution: $\text{SiO}_2$, $\text{GeO}_2$ acidic; CO neutral; $\text{SnO}_2$, $\text{PbO}_2$ amphoteric $\;\implies\;$ option C.

questions.text: The correct order of bond enthalpy $(\text{kJ mol}^{-1})$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Bond enthalpy falls as atomic size and bond length increase down the group. // 📝 Solution: $\text{C}-\text{C}\;>\;\text{Si}-\text{Si}\;>\;\text{Ge}-\text{Ge}\;>\;\text{Sn}-\text{Sn}$ $\;\implies\;$ option D.

questions.text: Consider the following reactions: $\text{PbCl}_2+\text{K}_2\text{CrO}_4\rightarrow\text{A}+2\text{KCl}$; $\text{A}+\text{NaOH}\rightleftharpoons\text{B}+\text{Na}_2\text{CrO}_4$ (hot solution); $\text{PbSO}_4+4\text{CH}_3\text{COONH}_4\rightarrow(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{SO}_4+\text{X}$. In the above reactions, A, B and X are respectively:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\text{PbCrO}_4$ is an insoluble chromate; excess alkali dissolves amphoteric Pb(II). // 📝 Solution: $\text{PbCl}_2+\text{K}_2\text{CrO}_4\rightarrow\text{PbCrO}_4$ (A); $\text{PbCrO}_4+4\text{NaOH}\rightarrow\text{Na}_2[\text{Pb(OH)}_4]$ (B); $\text{PbSO}_4+4\text{CH}_3\text{COONH}_4\rightarrow(\text{NH}_4)_2[\text{Pb(CH}_3\text{COO)}_4]$ (X).

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Amphoteric oxides react with both acids and bases; $\text{BF}_3$ is $sp^2$ hybridised. // 📝 Solution: $[\text{SnO},\text{SnO}_2]$ and $[\text{GeO},\text{GeO}_2]$ both amphoteric $\;\implies\;$ 2 pairs $\;\implies\;$ I true. $\text{BF}_3$ electron deficient, $sp^2$, trigonal planar $\;\implies\;$ II true.

questions.text: Boron trihalides are arranged in order of increasing Lewis acid character. Choose the correct order of Lewis acidity of boron trihalides.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Lewis acidity is inversely related to extent of $p\pi-p\pi$ back bonding. // 📝 Solution: Back bonding decreases down the group $\;\implies\;$ $\text{BF}_3\;<\;\text{BCl}_3\;<\;\text{BBr}_3\;<\;\text{BI}_3$ (acidity).

questions.text: Consider the following reactions: $\text{Na}_2\text{B}_4\text{O}_7\xrightarrow{\Delta}2\text{X}+\text{Y}$; $\text{CuSO}_4+\text{Y}\xrightarrow{\text{Non-Luminous flame}}\text{Z}+\text{SO}_3$; $2\text{Z}+2\text{X}+\text{Carbon}\xrightarrow{\text{Luminous flame}}2\text{Q}+\text{Na}_2\text{B}_4\text{O}_7+\text{CO}$. The oxidation states of Cu in Z and Q, respectively, are:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Borax bead test: oxidising flame gives Cu(II) metaborate, reducing flame gives Cu(I). // 📝 Solution: $\text{Z}=\text{Cu(BO}_2)_2$: $x\;+\;2(-1)\;=\;0\;\implies\;x=+2$; $\text{Q}=\text{CuBO}_2$: $x\;-\;1\;=\;0\;\implies\;x=+1$.

questions.text: Evaluate the following statements related to group 14 elements: (A) Covalent radius decreases down the group from C to Pb in a regular manner. (B) Electronegativity decreases from C to Pb gradually. (C) Maximum covalency of C is 4, whereas other elements can expand covalency due to d orbitals. (D) Heavier elements do not form $p\pi-p\pi$ bonds. (E) Carbon can exhibit negative oxidation states.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Atomic size increases down the group; $p\pi-p\pi$ bonding is weak for heavier atoms. // 📝 Solution: (A) radius increases $\;\implies\;$ false; (B) not gradual $\;\implies\;$ false; (C), (D), (E) true $\;\implies\;$ option B.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (A) Carbon tetrachloride, (B) Methylene chloride, (C) DDT, (D) Freons. List-II: (I) Paint remover, (II) Refrigerators and air conditioners, (III) Fire extinguisher, (IV) Non-biodegradable insecticide. Choose the correct answer.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall the common industrial uses of each chlorocarbon. // 📝 Solution: $\text{CCl}_4\;\rightarrow\;$ (III), $\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2\;\rightarrow\;$ (I), Freons $\rightarrow$ (II), DDT $\rightarrow$ (IV) $\;\implies\;$ option B.

questions.text: Statement I: Elements X and Y are the most and least electronegative elements, respectively, among N, As, Sb and P. The nature of the oxides $\text{X}_2\text{O}_3$ and $\text{Y}_2\text{O}_3$ is acidic and amphoteric, respectively. Statement II: $\text{BCl}_3$ is covalent in nature and gets hydrolysed in water, producing $[\text{B(OH)}_4]^{-}$ and $[\text{B(H}_2\text{O)}_6]^{3+}$ in aqueous medium. Choose the correct answer.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Electronegativity decreases down the group; check the products of $\text{BCl}_3$ hydrolysis. // 📝 Solution: $X=\text{N}$, $Y=\text{Sb}$; $\text{N}_2\text{O}_3$ acidic, $\text{Sb}_2\text{O}_3$ amphoteric $\;\implies\;$ I true. $\text{BCl}_3+3\text{H}_2\text{O}\rightarrow\text{B(OH)}_3+3\text{HCl}$ $\;\implies\;$ II false.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Match each mineral with its chemical formula. // 📝 Solution: Fluorspar is $\text{CaF}_2$, not $\text{BF}_3\;\implies\;$ pair (1) is incorrect.

questions.text: Assertion A: Carbon forms two important oxides, CO and $\text{CO}_2$. CO is neutral whereas $\text{CO}_2$ is acidic in nature. Reason R: $\text{CO}_2$ combines with water in a limited way to form carbonic acid, while CO is sparingly soluble in water. Choose the most appropriate answer.

Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
A is not correct but R is correct.
A is correct but R is not correct.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Acidity of an oxide arises from the acid it forms with water. // 📝 Solution: $\text{CO}_2\;+\;\text{H}_2\text{O}\;\rightleftharpoons\;\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3\;\implies\;$ acidic, CO neutral $\;\implies\;$ R explains A.

questions.text: Assertion A: Beryllium has less negative value of reduction potential compared to the other alkaline earth metals. Reason R: Beryllium has large hydration energy due to small size of $\text{Be}^{2+}$ but relatively large value of atomization enthalpy. Choose the most appropriate answer.

options.text: A is correct but R is not correct.
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
A is not correct but R is correct.
Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Reduction potential depends on sublimation, ionisation and hydration enthalpies. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Be}$ has less negative $E^\circ\;\implies\;$ large $\Delta_{\text{hyd}}H$ of small $\text{Be}^{2+}$ with large $\Delta_{\text{at}}H\;\implies\;$ R explains A.

questions.text: The number of neutrons in the more abundant isotope of boron is $x$. Amorphous boron upon heating with air forms a product in which the oxidation state of boron is $y$. The value of $x\;+\;y$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Neutrons equal mass number minus atomic number; oxidation state from the oxide formula. // 📝 Solution: $^{11}\text{B}$ abundant $\;\implies\;$ $x\;=\;11\;-\;5\;=\;6$; $\text{B}_2\text{O}_3$ $\;\implies\;$ $y\;=\;+3$ $\;\implies\;$ $x\;+\;y\;=\;9$.

questions.text: The correct statements from the following are: A. Ionic radii of trivalent cations of group 13 elements decrease down the group. B. Electronegativity of group 13 elements decreases down the group. C. Among group 13 elements, Boron has the highest first ionisation enthalpy. D. The trichloride and triiodide of group 13 elements are covalent in nature.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Ionic radius increases down a group; check ionisation trends and covalent character of halides. // 📝 Solution: A false (radii increase); B false (Ga $>$ Al in EN); C true (B has highest $\text{IE}_1$); D true $\;\implies\;$ option A.

questions.text: It is noticed that $\text{Pb}^{2+}$ is more stable than $\text{Pb}^{4+}$ but $\text{Sn}^{2+}$ is less stable than $\text{Sn}^{4+}$. Observe: $\text{PbO}_2+\text{Pb}\rightarrow2\text{PbO}$; $\Delta_r G^\circ(1)$. $\text{SnO}_2+\text{Sn}\rightarrow2\text{SnO}$; $\Delta_r G^\circ(2)$. Identify the correct set.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A reaction is spontaneous if it moves toward the more stable oxidation state. // 📝 Solution: Reaction (1) gives stable $\text{Pb}^{2+}$ $\;\implies\;$ $\Delta_r G^\circ(1)<0$; Reaction (2) moves $\text{Sn}^{4+}\rightarrow\text{Sn}^{2+}$ (unstable) $\;\implies\;$ $\Delta_r G^\circ(2)>0$.

questions.text: Assertion (A): Melting point of Boron (2453 K) is unusually high in group 13 elements. Reason (R): Solid Boron has very strong crystalline lattice. Choose the most appropriate answer.

Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Melting point depends on the strength of the crystal lattice. // 📝 Solution: Boron forms a covalent network lattice $\;\implies\;$ very high $m.p.$ $\;\implies\;$ R explains A.

questions.text: Statement I: The decrease in first ionisation enthalpy from B to Al is much larger than that from Al to Ga. Statement II: The d orbitals in Ga are completely filled. Choose the most appropriate answer.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Compare the successive $\text{IE}_1$ differences in group 13. // 📝 Solution: $801\;-\;577\;=\;224\;\gg\;577\;-\;579\;=\;-2\;\implies\;$ I correct. $\text{Ga}$ $3d^{10}$ is full, but official key marks II incorrect $\;\implies\;$ option C.

questions.text: A student has been given a compound x of molecular formula $\mathrm{C_6H_7N}$. x is sparingly soluble in water; on addition of dilute mineral acid, x becomes soluble. x when treated with $\mathrm{CHCl_3}$ and $\mathrm{KOH\;(alc)}$, y is produced. y has a specific unpleasant smell. On treatment with benzenesulphonyl chloride, x gives a compound z which is soluble in alkali. The number of different H atoms present in z is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Carbylamine and Hinsberg tests identify x as aniline; count distinct H in z. // 📝 Solution: x $=$ aniline $\;\implies\;$ z $=\mathrm{C_6H_5NHSO_2C_6H_5}$ $\;\implies\;$ $1\;(\mathrm{NH})\;+\;3\;(\text{ring on N})\;+\;3\;(\text{ring on S})\;=\;7$.

questions.text: The product A formed in the following reaction is: aniline $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{NaNO_2,\;HCl,\;0^\circ C;\;then\;Cu_2Cl_2}}\;$ A [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Sandmeyer reaction replaces $\mathrm{-N_2^+}$ by $\mathrm{-Cl}$. // 📝 Solution: Aniline $\;\to\;$ benzenediazonium chloride $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{Cu_2Cl_2}}\;$ chlorobenzene $\;\implies\;$ Option (3).

questions.text: The mass of benzanilide obtained from the benzoylation reaction of $5.8$ g of aniline, if the yield of product is $82\%$, is ______ g. (nearest integer) (Given molar mass in $\mathrm{g\;mol^{-1}}$: H: 1, C: 12, N: 14, O: 16)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Mass $=$ moles of aniline $\times$ M(benzanilide) $\times$ yield. // 📝 Solution: $n\;=\;\frac{5.8}{93}\;=\;0.0624$ $\;\implies\;$ theoretical $\;=\;0.0624\times 197\;=\;12.29\;\mathrm{g}$ $\;\implies\;$ actual $\;=\;12.29\times 0.82\;\approx\;10\;\mathrm{g}$.

questions.text: From $6.55$ g of aniline, the maximum amount of acetanilide that can be prepared will be ______ $\times 10^{-1}$ g.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Mole-to-mole conversion: aniline (93) to acetanilide (135). // 📝 Solution: $93\;\mathrm{g}\;\to\;135\;\mathrm{g}$ $\;\implies\;$ $6.55\;\mathrm{g}\;\to\;\frac{135}{93}\times 6.55\;=\;9.5\;\mathrm{g}\;=\;95\times 10^{-1}\;\mathrm{g}$.

questions.text: Match List I with List II. List I: (A) chlorobenzene $\;+\;\mathrm{CH_3Cl}\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{Na}}\;$ toluene, (B) chlorobenzene $\;+\;2\mathrm{Na}\;\to\;$ biphenyl, (C) benzenediazonium chloride $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{Cu_2Cl_2}}\;$ chlorobenzene $\;+\;\mathrm{N_2}$, (D) $\mathrm{C_2H_5Cl\;+\;NaI\;\to\;C_2H_5I\;+\;NaCl}$. List II: (I) Fittig reaction, (II) Wurtz-Fittig reaction, (III) Finkelstein reaction, (IV) Sandmeyer reaction. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Aryl halide + alkyl halide + Na is Wurtz-Fittig; two aryl halides + Na is Fittig. // 📝 Solution: A $\;=\;$ Wurtz-Fittig (II), B $\;=\;$ Fittig (I), C $\;=\;$ Sandmeyer (IV), D $\;=\;$ Finkelstein (III) $\;\implies\;$ Option (4).

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: o-phenylenediamine can be synthesized from o-dipropylbenzene (o-di-n-propylbenzene) using simpler reagents in the order i) acidic $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$, ii) ammonia, iii) bromine and alkali. Statement II: p-toluidine can be converted into 3,5-dibromotoluene using reagents in the order i) bromine-$\mathrm{H_2O}$, ii) $\mathrm{NaNO_2/HCl\;(0-5^\circ C)}$, iii) aq. $\mathrm{H_3PO_2}$. Choose the correct answer. [FIGURE]

options.text: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Trace each route through oxidation, amidation, Hoffmann degradation and diazonium removal. // 📝 Solution: I: phthalic acid $\;\to\;$ phthalamide $\;\to\;$ o-phenylenediamine (true) $\;\implies\;$ II: 2,6-dibromo-4-methylaniline $\;\to\;$ diazonium $\;\to\;$ 3,5-dibromotoluene (true) $\;\implies\;$ Option (2).

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The dipole moment of R-CN is greater than R-NC and R-NC can undergo hydrolysis under acidic medium to produce $\mathrm{R{-}COOH}$. Statement II: R-CN hydrolyses under acidic medium to produce a compound which on treatment with $\mathrm{SOCl_2}$, followed by the addition of $\mathrm{NH_3}$ gives another compound (x). This compound (x) on treatment with $\mathrm{NaOCl/NaOH}$ gives a product, that on treatment with $\mathrm{CHCl_3/KOH/\Delta}$ produces R-NC. Choose the correct answer.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Acidic hydrolysis of isocyanides gives amine and formic acid. // 📝 Solution: R-NC $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{H^+/H_2O}}\;\mathrm{RNH_2}\;+\;\mathrm{HCOOH}$ $\;\implies\;$ Statement I false $\;\implies\;$ $\mathrm{RCN\to RCOOH\to RCOCl\to RCONH_2\to RNH_2\to RNC}$ $\;\implies\;$ Statement II true.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Pure aniline and other arylamines are usually colourless. Statement II: Arylamines get coloured on storage due to atmospheric reduction. Choose the most appropriate answer.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Aniline darkens on exposure to air and light. // 📝 Solution: Pure aniline is a colourless liquid $\;\implies\;$ Statement I true $\;\implies\;$ Colouring is due to atmospheric oxidation, not reduction $\;\implies\;$ Statement II false $\;\implies\;$ Option (3).

questions.text: How many of the transformations given below would result in aromatic amines? (1) benzamide $\;+\;\mathrm{Br_2}\;+\;\mathrm{NaOH}$ (2) potassium phthalimide $\;+\;$ chlorobenzene (3) nitrobenzene $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{H_2,\;Pd/C}}$ (4) acetanilide $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{dil.\;H_2SO_4,\;\Delta}}$ [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Check which reactions yield aniline; aryl halides fail in Gabriel synthesis. // 📝 Solution: (1) Hoffmann gives aniline $\;\implies\;$ (2) no reaction, since aryl halide is a poor $S_N2$ substrate $\;\implies\;$ (3) gives aniline $\;\implies\;$ (4) gives aniline $\;+\;\mathrm{CH_3COOH}$ $\;\implies\;$ total $\;=\;3$.

questions.text: Reaction of propanamide with $\mathrm{Br_2\;/\;KOH\;(aq)}$ produces:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Hoffmann bromamide degradation gives an amine with one carbon less. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CONH_2}\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{Br_2/KOH}}\;\mathrm{CH_3CH_2NH_2}$ $\;\implies\;$ Ethylamine $\;\implies\;$ Option (4).

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Griss-Ilosvay test is used for the detection of nitrite ion, which involves the use of sulphanilic acid and $\alpha$-naphthylamine reagent. Statement II: In the above test, sulphanilic acid is diazotized by the acidified nitrite ion, which on further coupling with $\alpha$-naphthylamine forms an azo-dye. Choose the correct answer.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Griss-Ilosvay test is based on diazotisation then azo coupling. // 📝 Solution: Nitrite diazotises sulphanilic acid $\;\implies\;$ coupling with $\alpha$-naphthylamine gives a red azo dye $\;\implies\;$ both statements true $\;\implies\;$ Option (1).

questions.text: Phenetole ($\mathrm{C_6H_5OC_2H_5}$) $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{HNO_3,\;H_2SO_4}}\;$ P (major) $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{2Br_2,\;Fe}}\;$ Q (major). The ratio of number of oxygen atoms to bromine atoms in the product Q is ______ $\times 10^{-1}$. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mathrm{-OEt}$ is a stronger activator than $\mathrm{-NO_2}$ is a director; bromine enters ortho to $\mathrm{-OEt}$. // 📝 Solution: P $\;=\;$ 4-nitrophenetole $\;\implies\;$ Q $\;=\;$ 2,6-dibromo-4-nitrophenetole $\;\implies\;$ O atoms $\;=\;3$, Br atoms $\;=\;2$ $\;\implies\;$ ratio $\;=\;1.5\;=\;15\times 10^{-1}$.

questions.text: Cyclohexylmethanamine $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{C_6H_5COCl,\;NaOH}}\;$ [A] $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{LiAlH_4;\;H_2O}}\;$ [B]. The final product [B] is: [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Benzoylation gives an amide; $\mathrm{LiAlH_4}$ reduces amide $\mathrm{C{=}O}$ to $\mathrm{CH_2}$. // 📝 Solution: A $\;=\;$ N-(cyclohexylmethyl)benzamide $\;\implies\;$ $\mathrm{LiAlH_4}$ gives $\mathrm{C_6H_{11}CH_2{-}NH{-}CH_2C_6H_5}$ $\;\implies\;$ Option (4).

questions.text: Find out the major product formed from the following reaction: 3,5-dibromocyclopentene $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{Me_2NH\;(2\;equiv)}}\;$ ? [Me: $\mathrm{-CH_3}$] [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Neighbouring-group participation via an aziridinium ion gives the same 1,2-diamine for cis or trans. // 📝 Solution: First $S_N2$ by $\mathrm{Me_2NH}$ $\;\implies\;$ aziridinium ion forms $\;\implies\;$ second $\mathrm{Me_2NH}$ opens it $\;\implies\;$ vicinal bis(dimethylamino)cyclopentene $\;\implies\;$ Option (3).

questions.text: A is a neutral organic compound (M.F: $\mathrm{C_8H_9ON}$). On treatment with aqueous $\mathrm{Br_2/HO^{(-)}}$, A forms a compound B which is soluble in dilute acid. B on treatment with aqueous $\mathrm{NaNO_2/HCl\;(0-5^\circ C)}$ produces a compound C which on treatment with $\mathrm{CuCN/NaCN}$ produces D. Hydrolysis of D produces E which is also obtainable from the hydrolysis of A. E on treatment with acidified $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ produces F. F contains two different types of hydrogen atoms. The structure of A is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: F with only two types of H is terephthalic acid, so the substituents are para. // 📝 Solution: A (Hoffmann) gives p-toluidine (B) $\;\to\;$ diazonium (C) $\;\to\;$ p-tolunitrile (D) $\;\to\;$ p-toluic acid (E) $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{KMnO_4}}\;$ terephthalic acid (F) $\;\implies\;$ A $=$ 4-methylbenzamide $\;\implies\;$ Option (3).

questions.text: Consider the reaction sequence: benzene $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{conc.\;HNO_3+conc.\;H_2SO_4,\;333\;K}}\;$ P $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{1.\;Sn/HCl/\Delta;\;2.\;pH\;neutralised}}\;$ Q $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{(CH_3CO)_2O}}\;$ R $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{conc.\;HNO_3+conc.\;H_2SO_4}}\;$ S (major) $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{1.\;HCl/EtOH,\;\Delta;\;2.\;pH\;neutralised}}\;$ T. The percentage of nitrogen in product T formed is ______ %. (Nearest integer) (Given molar mass in $\mathrm{g\;mol^{-1}}$: H: 1, C: 12, N: 14, O: 16) [FIGURE]
questions.topic: Protection of Amino Group, Percentage Composition

questions.text: An amine (X) is prepared by ammonolysis of benzyl chloride. On adding p-toluenesulphonyl chloride to it the solution remains clear. Molar mass of the amine (X) formed is ______ $\mathrm{g\;mol^{-1}}$. (C: 12, H: 1, O: 16, N: 14)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A clear solution means no reaction with TsCl, so X is a tertiary amine. // 📝 Solution: X $\;=\;\mathrm{(PhCH_2)_3N}\;=\;\mathrm{C_{21}H_{21}N}$ $\;\implies\;$ $M\;=\;252\;+\;21\;+\;14\;=\;287\;\mathrm{g\;mol^{-1}}$.

questions.text: Nitrobenzene is treated successively with: (1) $\mathrm{Br_2/FeBr_3/\Delta}$ (2) $\mathrm{Sn/HCl/\Delta}$ (3) pH neutralisation (4) $\mathrm{Br_2/H_2O}$ (5) $\mathrm{NaNO_2/HBr,\;0-5^\circ C}$ (6) $\mathrm{CuBr/NaBr}$ to give the major product (P). The number of bromine atom(s) in the final product (P) will be:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Track the Br atoms through meta-bromination, tribromination of the aniline and Sandmeyer. // 📝 Solution: Step 1 gives m-bromonitrobenzene (1 Br) $\;\implies\;$ m-bromoaniline $\;\implies\;$ $\mathrm{Br_2/H_2O}$ adds 3 Br (total $4$) $\;\implies\;$ Sandmeyer replaces $\mathrm{-N_2^+}$ by Br (total $5$).

questions.text: Following is a confirmatory test for aromatic primary amines: aniline $\;\xrightarrow{(A)}\;$ benzenediazonium chloride $\;\xrightarrow[\mathrm{NaOH}]{(B)}\;$ scarlet red dye. Identify reagents (A) and (B). [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The azo dye test uses diazotisation then coupling with beta-naphthol. // 📝 Solution: A $=\mathrm{NaNO_2/HCl}$ at $0-5^\circ C$ gives diazonium salt $\;\implies\;$ coupling with $\beta$-naphthol in NaOH gives scarlet red dye $\;\implies\;$ Option (4).
questions.topic: Azo Dye Test for Primary Aromatic Amines

questions.text: $9.3$ g of pure aniline upon diazotisation followed by coupling with phenol gives an orange dye. The mass of orange dye produced (assume $100\%$ yield) is ______ g. (nearest integer)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $1$ mol aniline gives $1$ mol p-hydroxyazobenzene (M $=$ 198 to 199). // 📝 Solution: $n\;=\;\frac{9.3}{93}\;=\;0.1$ $\;\implies\;$ mass $\;=\;0.1\times 199\;=\;19.9\;\approx\;20\;\mathrm{g}$.

questions.text: An organic compound (P) on treatment with aqueous ammonia under hot condition forms compound (Q) which on heating with $\mathrm{Br_2}$ and KOH forms compound (R) having molecular formula $\mathrm{C_6H_7N}$. Names of P, Q and R respectively are:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mathrm{C_6H_7N}$ is aniline, formed by Hoffmann degradation of benzamide. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{C_6H_5COOH}\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{NH_3,\;\Delta}}\;\mathrm{C_6H_5CONH_2}\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{Br_2/KOH}}\;\mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2}$ $\;\implies\;$ Option (4).

questions.text: A hydrocarbon P ($\mathrm{C_4H_8}$) on reaction with HCl gives an optically active compound Q ($\mathrm{C_4H_9Cl}$) which on reaction with one mole of ammonia gives compound R ($\mathrm{C_4H_{11}N}$). R on diazotization followed by hydrolysis gives S. Identify P, Q, R and S.

options.text: P $=$ methylcyclopropane, Q $=\mathrm{ClCH_2}$-cyclopropane, R $=\mathrm{H_2NCH_2}$-cyclopropane, S $=$ cyclopropylmethanol [FIGURE]

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Optical activity of Q requires a chiral carbon, so Q is 2-chlorobutane. // 📝 Solution: 2-butene $\;+\;\mathrm{HCl}\;\to\;$ 2-chlorobutane (chiral) $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{NH_3}}\;$ 2-aminobutane $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{NaNO_2/HCl;\;H_2O}}\;$ butan-2-ol $\;\implies\;$ Option (4).
questions.topic: Optical Activity, Amines from Alkyl Halides

questions.text: Compound P undergoes the following sequence of reactions: P $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{(i)\;NH_3,\;(ii)\;\Delta}}\;$ Q $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{(i)\;KOH,\;Br_2;\;(ii)\;CHCl_3,\;KOH\;(alc),\;\Delta}}\;$ cyclohexyl isocyanide. P is: [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Work backwards: carbylamine, then Hoffmann degradation, then amide formation. // 📝 Solution: Isocyanide $\;\leftarrow\;$ $\mathrm{C_6H_{11}NH_2}$ $\;\leftarrow\;$ $\mathrm{C_6H_{11}CONH_2}$ (Q) $\;\leftarrow\;$ $\mathrm{C_6H_{11}COOH}$ (P) $\;\implies\;$ Option (4).

questions.text: In the following reaction, A is the major product: the amino alcohol $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CH{-}CH(NH_2){-}CH_2OH}$ $\;+\;$ diethyl carbonate $\;\longrightarrow\;$ A [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The amine attacks the carbonyl first, then the $\mathrm{-OH}$ attacks intramolecularly, losing EtOH. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{-NH_2}$ attacks the electrophilic carbon of the carbonate $\;\implies\;$ the lone pair of O attacks the carbamate carbon with loss of EtOH $\;\implies\;$ cyclic carbamate (oxazolidinone) $\;\implies\;$ Option (2).

questions.text: A student performed analysis of an aliphatic organic compound X which gave $\mathrm{C}=61.01\%$, $\mathrm{H}=15.25\%$, $\mathrm{N}=23.74\%$. This compound on treatment with $\mathrm{HNO_2/H_2O}$ produced another compound Y which did not contain any nitrogen atom. However, Y upon controlled oxidation produced another compound Z that responded to the iodoform test. The structure of X is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find the empirical formula, then use the iodoform test to locate the amino group. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{C:H:N}\;=\;\frac{61.01}{12}:15.25:\frac{23.74}{14}\;=\;3:9:1$ $\;\implies\;$ $\mathrm{C_3H_9N}$ (aliphatic) $\;\implies\;$ isopropylamine $\;\to\;$ propan-2-ol $\;\to\;$ acetone (iodoform positive) $\;\implies\;$ Option (2).

questions.text: Number of amine compounds from the following giving solids which are soluble in $\mathrm{NaOH}$ upon reaction with Hinsberg's reagent is ______. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Only primary amines give sulphonamides soluble in NaOH. // 📝 Solution: Count the primary amines (aniline, 4-aminodiphenylamine, 2-methoxyaniline, propylamine, cyclohexylamine) $\;\implies\;$ $5$ (amide, hydrazine and urea are not amines of this type; secondary gives insoluble, tertiary gives none).

questions.text: Identify the product formed (A and E) in the sequence: p-nitrotoluene $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{Br_2}}\;$ A $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{Sn/HCl}}\;$ B $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{NaNO_2/HCl,\;273-278\;K}}\;$ C $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{H_3PO_2/H_2O}}\;$ D $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{(i)\;KMnO_4/KOH,\;(ii)\;H_3O^+}}\;$ E [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Br enters ortho to the activating $\mathrm{-CH_3}$ (meta to $\mathrm{-NO_2}$); $\mathrm{H_3PO_2}$ removes the diazonium group. // 📝 Solution: A $\;=\;$ 2-bromo-4-nitrotoluene $\;\implies\;$ B $\;=\;$ amine $\;\implies\;$ C $\;=\;$ diazonium salt $\;\implies\;$ D $\;=\;$ 2-bromotoluene $\;\implies\;$ E $\;=\;$ 2-bromobenzoic acid $\;\implies\;$ Option (2).

questions.text: Benzyl isocyanide can be obtained by: (A) $\mathrm{PhCH_2Br}\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{AgCN}}$ (B) $\mathrm{PhCH_2NH_2}\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{CHCl_3,\;aq.\;KOH}}$ (C) $\mathrm{PhCH_2NHCH_3}\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{CHCl_3,\;aq.\;KOH}}$ (D) $\mathrm{PhCH_2OTs}\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{KCN}}$. Choose the correct answer. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: AgCN gives isocyanides (covalent); the carbylamine reaction needs a primary amine. // 📝 Solution: A gives $\mathrm{PhCH_2NC}$ $\;\implies\;$ B (carbylamine) gives $\mathrm{PhCH_2NC}$ $\;\implies\;$ C is a secondary amine, no reaction $\;\implies\;$ D gives $\mathrm{PhCH_2CN}$ $\;\implies\;$ A and B $\;\implies\;$ Option (3).

questions.text: $X$ g of ethylamine is subjected to reaction with $\mathrm{NaNO_2/HCl}$ followed by water; the evolved dinitrogen gas occupied $2.24\;\mathrm{L}$ volume at STP. $X$ is ______ $\times 10^{-1}$ g.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Aliphatic primary amine $\;+\;\mathrm{HNO_2}$ releases $1$ mol $\mathrm{N_2}$ per mol amine. // 📝 Solution: $n(\mathrm{N_2})\;=\;\frac{2.24}{22.4}\;=\;0.1\;\mathrm{mol}$ $\;\implies\;$ $n(\mathrm{C_2H_5NH_2})\;=\;0.1$ $\;\implies\;$ $X\;=\;0.1\times 45\;=\;4.5\;\mathrm{g}\;=\;45\times 10^{-1}\;\mathrm{g}$.
questions.topic: Reaction of Aliphatic Amines with Nitrous Acid

questions.text: Match List I with List II. List I: (A) aniline $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{(i)\;NaNO_2+HCl,\;(ii)\;H_2O,\;warm}}$ (B) phenol $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{Na_2Cr_2O_7/H_2SO_4}}$ (C) phenol $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{(i)\;CHCl_3+aq\;NaOH,\;(ii)\;H^+}}$ (D) phenol $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{(i)\;NaOH,\;(ii)\;CO_2,\;(iii)\;H^+}}$. List II: (I) salicylaldehyde, (II) phenol, (III) salicylic acid, (IV) benzoquinone. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall diazonium hydrolysis, oxidation of phenol, Reimer-Tiemann and Kolbe reactions. // 📝 Solution: A gives phenol (II) $\;\implies\;$ B gives benzoquinone (IV) $\;\implies\;$ C Reimer-Tiemann gives salicylaldehyde (I) $\;\implies\;$ D Kolbe gives salicylic acid (III) $\;\implies\;$ Option (4).
questions.topic: Reactions of Phenol and Diazonium Salts

questions.text: The correct stability order of the following diazonium salts is: (A) 4-methoxybenzenediazonium chloride, (B) 4-nitrobenzenediazonium chloride, (C) benzenediazonium chloride, (D) 4-cyanobenzenediazonium chloride. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Electron-donating groups stabilise the diazonium cation; electron-withdrawing groups destabilise it. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{-OCH_3}$ ($+M$) stabilises $\;\implies\;$ $\mathrm{-H}$ baseline $\;\implies\;$ $\mathrm{-CN}$ ($-M,\;-I$) destabilises $\;\implies\;$ $\mathrm{-NO_2}$ destabilises most $\;\implies\;$ $\mathrm{A}\;>\;\mathrm{C}\;>\;\mathrm{D}\;>\;\mathrm{B}$.

questions.text: Total number of alkali insoluble solid sulphonamides obtained by reaction of the given amines with Hinsberg's reagent is ______. Aniline, N-Methylaniline, Methanamine, N,N-Dimethylmethanamine, N-Methylmethanamine, Phenylmethanamine, N-propylaniline, N-phenylaniline, N,N-Dimethylaniline, Allyl amine, Isopropyl amine
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Secondary amines give alkali-insoluble sulphonamides. // 📝 Solution: Secondary amines: N-methylaniline, N-methylmethanamine, N-propylaniline, N-phenylaniline $\;\implies\;$ $4$ (primary give soluble products; tertiary do not react).

questions.text: The correct order in aqueous medium of basic strength in case of methyl substituted amines is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: In water, basicity depends on both the +I effect and solvation of the cation. // 📝 Solution: Electron density and solvation of the cation both matter $\;\implies\;$ $\mathrm{Me_2NH}\;>\;\mathrm{MeNH_2}\;>\;\mathrm{Me_3N}\;>\;\mathrm{NH_3}$ $\;\implies\;$ Option (1).

questions.text: Phthalimide is made to undergo the following sequence of reactions: Phthalimide $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{(i)\;KOH,\;(ii)\;Benzyl\;chloride}}\;$ P. Total number of $\pi$ bonds present in product P is ______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Gabriel synthesis gives N-benzylphthalimide; count the C=O and aromatic $\pi$ bonds. // 📝 Solution: P $\;=\;$ N-benzylphthalimide $\;\implies\;$ $2\;(\mathrm{C{=}O})\;+\;3\;(\text{phthalimide ring})\;+\;3\;(\text{benzyl ring})\;=\;8$.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Aniline reacts with conc. $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ followed by heating at $453-473\;\mathrm{K}$ to give p-aminobenzene sulphonic acid, which gives blood red colour in the Lassaigne's test. Statement II: In Friedel-Crafts alkylation and acylation reactions, aniline forms salt with the $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$ catalyst. Due to this, nitrogen of aniline acquires a positive charge and acts as a deactivating group. Choose the correct answer.

options.text: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Sulphanilic acid contains both N and S, giving $\mathrm{[Fe(SCN)]^{2+}}$ in Lassaigne's test. // 📝 Solution: Sulphanilic acid gives blood red $\mathrm{[Fe(SCN)]^{2+}}$ $\;\implies\;$ Statement I true $\;\implies\;$ aniline forms a salt with $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$ giving $\mathrm{-NH_2^+}$ which deactivates the ring $\;\implies\;$ Statement II true $\;\implies\;$ Option (4).

questions.text: $X$ g of ethanamine was subjected to reaction with $\mathrm{NaNO_2/HCl}$ followed by hydrolysis to liberate $\mathrm{N_2}$ and $\mathrm{HCl}$. The $\mathrm{HCl}$ generated was completely neutralised by $0.2$ moles of $\mathrm{NaOH}$. $X$ is ______ g.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: One mole of amine releases one mole of $\mathrm{HCl}$. // 📝 Solution: $n(\mathrm{HCl})\;=\;n(\mathrm{NaOH})\;=\;0.2$ $\;\implies\;$ $n(\mathrm{amine})\;=\;0.2$ $\;\implies\;$ $X\;=\;0.2\times 45\;=\;9\;\mathrm{g}$.
questions.topic: Reaction of Aliphatic Amines with Nitrous Acid

questions.text: Major product of the following reaction is: 4-cyanobenzoic acid methyl ester $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{(i)\;CH_3MgBr\;(excess),\;(ii)\;H_3O^+}}\;$ ? [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Grignard converts a nitrile to a ketone (after hydrolysis) and an ester to a tertiary alcohol. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{-CN}\;\to\;\mathrm{-C(=NMgBr)CH_3}\;\to\;\mathrm{-COCH_3}$ $\;\implies\;$ $\mathrm{-CO_2CH_3}\;\to\;\mathrm{-C(OH)(CH_3)_2}$ $\;\implies\;$ Option (4).
questions.topic: Grignard Reaction with Nitriles and Esters

questions.text: In the conversion of compound (X), p-nitrotoluene, to product (Y), 3,5-dibromotoluene, the sequence of reagents to be used will be: [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Convert $\mathrm{-NO_2}$ to $\mathrm{-NH_2}$, brominate ortho to it, then remove the amino group via diazonium and $\mathrm{H_3PO_2}$. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Fe/H^+}$ gives p-toluidine $\;\implies\;$ $\mathrm{Br_2(aq)}$ gives 2,6-dibromo-4-methylaniline $\;\implies\;$ $\mathrm{HNO_2}$ gives diazonium salt $\;\implies\;$ $\mathrm{H_3PO_2}$ gives 3,5-dibromotoluene $\;\implies\;$ Option (4).

questions.text: Identify the product (A) in the following reaction: aniline $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{(i)\;NaNO_2+HCl,\;(ii)\;Cu_2Cl_2,\;(iii)\;NaOH,\;623\;K,\;300\;atm,\;(iv)\;H^+}}\;$ (A) [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Sandmeyer gives chlorobenzene; Dow process converts it to phenol. // 📝 Solution: Aniline $\;\to\;$ diazonium chloride $\;\to\;$ chlorobenzene $\;\to\;$ sodium phenoxide $\;\to\;$ phenol $\;\implies\;$ Option (4).

questions.text: Consider the following reactions giving major product. Identify the correct reaction.

options.text: Benzanilide $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{HNO_3:H_2SO_4\;(1:2)}}\;$ nitro on the benzoyl ring [FIGURE]

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Check each: aryl halides fail in Gabriel; isocyanide reduction gives an N-methylamine; nitration goes on the N-ring. // 📝 Solution: (1) aryl halide is a poor $S_N2$ substrate, so wrong $\;\implies\;$ (2) $\mathrm{R{-}NC\to R{-}NHCH_3}$, so wrong $\;\implies\;$ (3) Hoffmann degradation gives ethanamine, correct $\;\implies\;$ (4) nitration occurs on the N-attached ring, so wrong.

questions.text: If $279$ g of aniline is reacted with one equivalent of benzenediazonium chloride, the maximum amount of aniline yellow formed will be ______ g. (nearest integer) (consider complete conversion)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Aniline yellow is p-aminoazobenzene (M $=$ 197), formed $1:1$. // 📝 Solution: $n\;=\;\frac{279}{93}\;=\;3$ $\;\implies\;$ mass $\;=\;3\times 197\;=\;591\;\mathrm{g}$.

questions.text: A student has planned to prepare acetanilide from aniline using acetic anhydride. The student started from $9.3$ g of aniline and managed to obtain $11$ g of dry acetanilide. The percentage yield of this reaction is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Percentage yield $=$ actual yield $\div$ theoretical yield $\times 100$. // 📝 Solution: $n\;=\;\frac{9.3}{93}\;=\;0.1$ $\;\implies\;$ theoretical mass $\;=\;0.1\times 135\;=\;13.5\;\mathrm{g}$ $\;\implies\;$ yield $\;=\;\frac{11}{13.5}\times 100\;=\;81.5\%$.

questions.text: Choose the correct colour of the product for the following reaction. [FIGURE] (4-sulphobenzenediazonium acetate $\;+\;$ 1-naphthylamine $\;\longrightarrow\;$ ?)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Diazonium salts couple with aromatic amines to give coloured azo dyes. // 📝 Solution: Coupling at the para position of 1-naphthylamine $\;\implies\;$ azo dye bearing $\mathrm{-SO_3H}$ $\;\implies\;$ Red dye $\;\implies\;$ Option (3).

questions.text: Which of the following reaction is correct?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Check Markovnikov addition and the carbon count in Hoffmann degradation. // 📝 Solution: (1) gives propan-1-ol or a mixture, not ethanol $\;\implies\;$ (2) Markovnikov addition is correct $\;\implies\;$ (3) UV light gives substitution, not addition $\;\implies\;$ (4) should give $\mathrm{C_2H_5NH_2}$ $\;\implies\;$ Option (2).

questions.text: The products A and B formed in the following reaction scheme are respectively: benzene $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{(i)\;conc.\;HNO_3/conc.\;H_2SO_4,\;323-333\;K;\;(ii)\;Sn/HCl}}\;$ A $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{(i)\;NaNO_2,\;HCl,\;273-278\;K;\;(ii)\;Phenol}}\;$ B [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Nitration, reduction, diazotisation and then coupling at para of phenol. // 📝 Solution: Benzene $\;\to\;$ nitrobenzene $\;\to\;$ aniline (A) $\;\to\;$ diazonium salt $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{phenol}}\;$ p-hydroxyazobenzene (B) $\;\implies\;$ Option (3).

questions.text: Consider the sequence: 4-nitrotoluene $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{(i)\;Sn,\;HCl/\Delta;\;(ii)\;pH\;neutralisation}}\;$ (A) $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{(i)\;(H_3CCO)_2O;\;(ii)\;Br_2/AcOH}}\;$ (B). Assuming the reaction proceeds to completion, $137$ mg of 4-nitrotoluene will produce ______ mg of B. (Given molar mass in $\mathrm{g\;mol^{-1}}$: H: 1, C: 12, N: 14, O: 16, Br: 80) [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: B is mono-bromo N-(4-methylphenyl)acetamide; use mole-to-mole conversion. // 📝 Solution: $n\;=\;\frac{137}{137}\;=\;1\;\mathrm{mmol}$ $\;\implies\;$ B $=\mathrm{C_9H_{10}BrNO}$, $M\;=\;228$ $\;\implies\;$ mass $\;=\;228\;\mathrm{mg}$.
questions.topic: Acetylation and Bromination of Aromatic Amines, Stoichiometry

questions.text: Number of compounds which give reaction with Hinsberg's reagent is ______. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Only primary and secondary amines react with benzenesulfonyl chloride. // 📝 Solution: Reacting: benzylamine-type $\mathrm{-NH-}$, aniline, ethylenediamine-type $\mathrm{-NH_2}$, piperidine, propylamine $\;\implies\;$ total $\;=\;5$ (diazonium salt, amide, tertiary amines, pyridine and urea do not react).

questions.text: Nitrobenzene $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{H_2/Pd,\;C_2H_5OH}}\;$ [A] $\;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{(CH_3CO)_2O,\;Pyridine}}\;$ [B]. Identify [B]. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Catalytic hydrogenation reduces $\mathrm{-NO_2}$ to $\mathrm{-NH_2}$; acetic anhydride acetylates it. // 📝 Solution: A $\;=\;$ aniline $\;\implies\;$ B $\;=\;$ acetanilide $\;\mathrm{C_6H_5NHCOCH_3}$ $\;\implies\;$ Option (4).

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement (I): All the following compounds react with p-toluenesulfonyl chloride: $\mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2}$, $\mathrm{(C_6H_5)_2NH}$, $\mathrm{(C_6H_5)_3N}$. Statement (II): Their products in the above reaction are soluble in aqueous $\mathrm{NaOH}$. Choose the correct answer.

options.text: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Tertiary amines do not react in the Hinsberg test, and secondary amine products are insoluble in alkali. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{(C_6H_5)_3N}$ does not react $\;\implies\;$ Statement I false $\;\implies\;$ the product of $\mathrm{(C_6H_5)_2NH}$ is insoluble in NaOH $\;\implies\;$ Statement II false $\;\implies\;$ Option (4).

questions.text: The number of moles of methane required to produce 11 g $\mathrm{CO_2(g)}$ after complete combustion is : (Given molar mass of methane in $\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$ : 16)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mathrm{CH_4} + 2\mathrm{O_2} \to \mathrm{CO_2} + 2\mathrm{H_2O}$ gives a 1 : 1 mole ratio of $\mathrm{CH_4}$ to $\mathrm{CO_2}$. // 📝 Solution: $n_{\mathrm{CO_2}} \; = \; \frac{11}{44} \; = \; 0.25$ $\implies$ $n_{\mathrm{CH_4}} \; = \; 0.25 \;\text{mol}$.

questions.text: Zinc reacts with hydrochloric acid to give hydrogen and zinc chloride. The volume of hydrogen gas produced at STP from the reaction of 11.5 g of zinc with excess HCl is ______ L (Nearest integer) (Given : Molar mass of Zn is 65.4 g $\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$ and Molar volume of $\mathrm{H_2}$ at STP $\; = \;$ 22.7 L)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mathrm{Zn} + 2\mathrm{HCl} \to \mathrm{ZnCl_2} + \mathrm{H_2}$ gives 1 mol $\mathrm{H_2}$ per mol Zn. // 📝 Solution: Moles of Zn $\; = \; \frac{11.5}{65.4}$ $\; = \;$ moles of $\mathrm{H_2}$ $\implies$ $V \; = \; \frac{11.5}{65.4} \times 22.7 \; = \; 3.99 \;\text{L} \; \approx \; 4 \;\text{L}$.
questions.topic: Stoichiometry and gas volume at STP

questions.text: Volume of 3 M NaOH (formula weight 40 g $\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$) which can be prepared from 84 g of NaOH is ______ $\times 10^{-1} \;\mathrm{dm^3}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $M \; = \; \frac{n_{\text{solute}}}{V \;(\text{in L})}$. // 📝 Solution: $3 \; = \; \frac{84 / 40}{V} \implies V \; = \; 0.7 \;\text{L} \; = \; 7 \times 10^{-1} \;\mathrm{dm^3}$.

questions.text: Among $10^{-9}\;\mathrm{g}$ (each) of the following elements, which one will have the highest number of atoms? Elements: $\mathrm{Pb}$, $\mathrm{Po}$, $\mathrm{Pr}$ and $\mathrm{Pt}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For a fixed mass, number of atoms is inversely proportional to molar mass // 📝 Solution: $N = \dfrac{m}{M} \times N_A$ $\implies$ least $M$ gives most atoms; $M_{\mathrm{Pr}} = 141 < M_{\mathrm{Pt}} = 195 < M_{\mathrm{Pb}} = 207 < M_{\mathrm{Po}} = 209$ $\implies$ $\mathrm{Pr}$
questions.topic: Number of atoms from mass and molar mass

questions.text: When $81.0\;g$ of aluminium is allowed to react with $128.0\;g$ of oxygen gas, the mass of aluminium oxide produced in grams is _______ (Nearest integer). Given : Molar mass of Al is $27.0\;g\;mol^{-1}$, Molar mass of O is $16.0\;g\;mol^{-1}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find the limiting reagent from $4Al + 3O_2 \to 2Al_2O_3$ // 📝 Solution: $n_{Al} \;=\; 3,\; n_{O_2} \;=\; 4 \implies \text{Al is limiting} \implies n_{Al_2O_3} \;=\; 1.5 \implies m \;=\; 1.5 \times 102 \;=\; 153\;g$

questions.text: Consider the sequence: 2-bromopentane $\xrightarrow{\text{alc. KOH}}$ P (major product, $80\%$ yield) $\xrightarrow{\mathrm{Br_2}}$ Q ($100\%$ yield). $151\;\mathrm{g}$ of 2-bromopentane is made to react. The mass of Q obtained is ______ g. Given molar mass (g mol$^{-1}$): H $=1$, C $=12$, O $=16$, Br $=80$. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Apply the percentage yields step by step, then multiply by the molar mass of Q // 📝 Solution: $n_{\text{2-bromopentane}} = 151/151 = 1\;\mathrm{mol}$ $\implies$ $n_P = 0.8\;\mathrm{mol}$ $\implies$ $n_Q = 0.8\;\mathrm{mol}$ with $M_Q = \mathrm{C_5H_{10}Br_2} = 230\;\mathrm{g\;mol^{-1}}$ $\implies$ $m_Q = 0.8 \times 230 = 184\;\mathrm{g}$

questions.text: A sample of $\mathrm{CaCO_3}$ and $\mathrm{MgCO_3}$ weighed 2.21 g is ignited to constant weight of 1.152 g. The composition of mixture is : (Given molar mass in $\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$ $\mathrm{CaCO_3}$ : 100, $\mathrm{MgCO_3}$ : 84)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Let $\mathrm{CaCO_3}$ be $x$ g; the residue is CaO (M $\; = \;$ 56) plus MgO (M $\; = \;$ 40), formed mole for mole. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{x}{100} \times 56 + \frac{2.21 - x}{84} \times 40 \; = \; 1.152$ $\implies$ $x \; = \; 1.1886 \;\text{g}$ $\implies$ $\mathrm{CaCO_3} \; = \; 1.187 \;\text{g}$, $\mathrm{MgCO_3} \; = \; 2.21 - 1.1886 \; \approx \; 1.023 \;\text{g}$.

questions.text: 1 mole of PbS is oxidised by " X " moles of $\mathrm{O_3}$ to get " Y " moles of $\mathrm{O_2}$. $X + Y \; = \;$ ______
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Balance by electron change: S$^{2-}$ to S$^{6+}$ loses 8 electrons, and each $\mathrm{O_3}$ gains 2 electrons. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{PbS} + 4\mathrm{O_3} \to \mathrm{PbSO_4} + 4\mathrm{O_2}$ $\implies$ $X \; = \; 4$, $Y \; = \; 4$ $\implies$ $X + Y \; = \; 8$.

questions.text: Consider the following reaction occurring in the blast furnace: $Fe_3O_{4(s)} + 4CO_{(g)} \to 3Fe_{(l)} + 4CO_{2(g)}$. $'x'$ kg of iron is produced when $2.32 \times 10^{3}\;kg\;Fe_3O_4$ and $2.8 \times 10^{2}\;kg\;CO$ are brought together in the furnace. The value of $'x'$ is _____. (nearest integer) Given: molar mass of $Fe_3O_4 \;=\; 232\;g\;mol^{-1}$, $CO \;=\; 28\;g\;mol^{-1}$, $Fe \;=\; 56\;g\;mol^{-1}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Compare mole ratio $Fe_3O_4 : CO \;=\; 1 : 4$ to find the limiting reagent // 📝 Solution: $n_{Fe_3O_4} \;=\; 10^4,\; n_{CO} \;=\; 10^4 \implies \text{CO limiting} \implies n_{Fe} \;=\; \frac{3}{4} \times 10^4 \implies m \;=\; \frac{3}{4} \times 10^4 \times 56\;g \;=\; 420\;kg$

questions.text: When 0.01 mol of an organic compound containing 60% carbon was burnt completely, 4.4 g of $\mathrm{CO_2}$ was produced. The molar mass of compound is _______ g $\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$ (Nearest integer)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Moles of C in the compound $\; = \;$ moles of $\mathrm{CO_2}$ produced. // 📝 Solution: Let molar mass be $M$ $\implies$ $\frac{0.01\,M}{12} \times \frac{60}{100} \; = \; \frac{4.4}{44}$ $\implies$ $M \; = \; \frac{4.4}{44} \times \frac{100}{60} \times \frac{12}{0.01} \; = \; 200 \;\text{g/mol}$.

questions.text: The number of units, which are used to express concentration of solutions from the following is _______. Mass percent, Mole, Mole fraction, Molarity, ppm, Molality.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Mole is a quantity of substance, not a concentration unit. // 📝 Solution: Concentration units $\implies$ mass percent, mole fraction, molarity, ppm, molality $\implies$ $5$ units.

questions.text: On complete combustion $1.0\;\mathrm{g}$ of an organic compound (X) gave $1.46\;\mathrm{g}$ of $\mathrm{CO_2}$ and $0.567\;\mathrm{g}$ of $\mathrm{H_2O}$. The empirical formula mass of X is ______ g. Given molar mass (g mol$^{-1}$): C $=12$, H $=1$, O $=16$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Convert masses to moles of C, H, O and find the simplest whole-number ratio // 📝 Solution: $n_C = 1.46/44 = 0.033$ $\implies$ $n_H = 2 \times 0.567/18 = 0.063$ $\implies$ $m_O = 1 - (0.033 \times 12 + 0.063) = 0.541\;\mathrm{g}$ $\implies$ $n_O = 0.541/16 = 0.033$ $\implies$ ratio $1:2:1$ $\implies$ $\mathrm{CH_2O}$, mass $= 30\;\mathrm{g}$

questions.text: 9.3 g of aniline is subjected to reaction with excess of acetic anhydride to prepare acetanilide. The mass of acetanilide produced if the reaction is 100% completed is ______ $\times 10^{-1}$ g. (Given molar mass in $\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$ N : 14, O : 16, C : 12, H : 1)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Aniline (M $\; = \;$ 93) and acetanilide (M $\; = \;$ 135) react in a 1 : 1 mole ratio. // 📝 Solution: $n_{\text{acetanilide}} \; = \; n_{\text{aniline}}$ $\implies$ $\frac{m}{135} \; = \; \frac{9.3}{93}$ $\implies$ $m \; = \; 13.5 \;\text{g} \; = \; 135 \times 10^{-1} \;\text{g}$.

questions.text: Choose the correct statements. (A) Weight of a substance is the amount of matter present in it. (B) Mass is the force exerted by gravity on an object. (C) Volume is the amount of space occupied by a substance. (D) Temperatures below $0^{\circ}C$ are possible in Celsius scale, but in Kelvin scale negative temperature is not possible. (E) Precision refers to the closeness of various measurements for the same quantity. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Mass is the amount of matter; weight is the gravitational force // 📝 Solution: (A) and (B) are interchanged, so both are false $\implies$ (C), (D) and (E) are true

questions.text: For $\mathrm{CaCO_3(s) + 2HCl(aq) \to CaCl_2(aq) + CO_2(g) + H_2O(l)}$, what mass of $\mathrm{CaCl_2}$ will be formed if $250\;\mathrm{mL}$ of $0.76\;\mathrm{M}$ HCl reacts with $1000\;\mathrm{g}$ of $\mathrm{CaCO_3}$? Given molar mass (g mol$^{-1}$): Ca $=40$, C $=12$, O $=16$, H $=1$, Cl $=35.5$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find the limiting reagent first, then use the mole ratio $\mathrm{HCl}:\mathrm{CaCl_2} = 2:1$ // 📝 Solution: $n_{\mathrm{HCl}} = 0.76 \times 0.25 = 0.19\;\mathrm{mol}$ (L.R.) $\implies$ $n_{\mathrm{CaCl_2}} = 0.19/2 = 0.095\;\mathrm{mol}$ $\implies$ $m = 0.095 \times 111 = 10.545\;\mathrm{g}$

questions.text: Mass of methane required to produce 22 g of $\mathrm{CO_2}$ after complete combustion is ______ g. (Given Molar mass in g $\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$ C $\; = \;$ 12.0, H $\; = \;$ 1.0, O $\; = \;$ 16.0)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mathrm{CH_4} + 2\mathrm{O_2} \to \mathrm{CO_2} + 2\mathrm{H_2O}$ gives a 1 : 1 mole ratio. // 📝 Solution: $n_{\mathrm{CO_2}} \; = \; \frac{22}{44} \; = \; 0.5$ $\implies$ $n_{\mathrm{CH_4}} \; = \; 0.5$ $\implies$ mass $\; = \; 0.5 \times 16 \; = \; 8 \;\text{g}$.

questions.text: $2.8 \times 10^{-3}\;mol$ of $CO_2$ is left after removing $10^{21}$ molecules from its $'x'$ mg sample. The mass of $CO_2$ taken initially is. Given: $N_A \;=\; 6.02 \times 10^{23}\;mol^{-1}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Moles $\;=\; \frac{\text{molecules}}{N_A}$; add removed moles to remaining moles // 📝 Solution: $n_{removed} \;=\; \frac{10^{21}}{6.02 \times 10^{23}} \;=\; 1.66 \times 10^{-3} \implies n_{total} \;=\; 4.46 \times 10^{-3} \implies m \;=\; 4.46 \times 10^{-3} \times 44 \;=\; 196.2\;mg$

questions.text: When $\mathrm{Fe_{0.93}O}$ is heated in presence of oxygen, it converts to $\mathrm{Fe_2O_3}$. The number of correct statement/s from the following is _______. A. The equivalent weight of $\mathrm{Fe_{0.93}O}$ is $\frac{\text{Molecular weight}}{0.79}$. B. The number of moles of $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ and $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ in 1 mole of $\mathrm{Fe_{0.93}O}$ is 0.79 and 0.14 respectively. C. $\mathrm{Fe_{0.93}O}$ is metal deficient with lattice comprising of cubic closed packed arrangement of $\mathrm{O^{2-}}$ ions. D. The % composition of $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ and $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ in $\mathrm{Fe_{0.93}O}$ is 85% and 15% respectively.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use charge balance for $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ and $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ and the n-factor from the change in average oxidation state. // 📝 Solution: $n_f \; = \; 0.93 \times \left( 3 - \frac{200}{93} \right) \; = \; 0.79$ $\implies$ A is true $\implies$ $2x + 3\left( 0.93 - x \right) \; = \; 2 \implies x \; = \; 0.79$, so $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}} \; = \; 0.14$ $\implies$ B is true $\implies$ C is a fact (true) $\implies$ $\%\,\mathrm{Fe^{2+}} \; = \; \frac{0.79}{0.93} \times 100 \; = \; 85\%$, so D is true $\implies$ all 4 are correct.

questions.text: Density of $3\;M$ $NaCl$ solution is $1.25\;g/mL$. The molality of the solution is :
Number of moles of methane required to produce 22 g $\mathrm{CO_{2(g)}}$ after combustion is $x \times 10^{-2}$ moles. The value of $x$ is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mathrm{CH_4} + 2\mathrm{O_2} \to \mathrm{CO_2} + 2\mathrm{H_2O}$ gives a 1 : 1 mole ratio. // 📝 Solution: $n_{\mathrm{CO_2}} \; = \; \frac{22}{44} \; = \; 0.5$ $\implies$ $n_{\mathrm{CH_4}} \; = \; 0.5 \; = \; 50 \times 10^{-2}$ $\implies$ $x \; = \; 50$.

questions.text: The molarity of a $70\%$ (mass / mass) aqueous solution of a monobasic acid $(X)$ is _____ $\times 10^{-1}\;M$ (Nearest integer) [Given: Density of aqueous solution of $(X)$ is $1.25\;g\;mL^{-1}$, Molar mass of the acid is $70\;g\;mol^{-1}$]
When a hydrocarbon A undergoes combustion in the presence of air, it requires 9.5 equivalents of oxygen and produces 3 equivalents of water. What is the molecular formula of A?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mathrm{C_xH_y} + \left( x + \frac{y}{4} \right) \mathrm{O_2} \to x\,\mathrm{CO_2} + \frac{y}{2}\,\mathrm{H_2O}$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{y}{2} \; = \; 3 \implies y \; = \; 6$ $\implies$ $x + \frac{6}{4} \; = \; 9.5 \implies x \; = \; 8$ $\implies$ $\mathrm{C_8H_6}$.

questions.text: On combustion of $0.210\;\mathrm{g}$ of an organic compound containing C, H and O, $0.127\;\mathrm{g}$ of $\mathrm{H_2O}$ and $0.307\;\mathrm{g}$ of $\mathrm{CO_2}$ were obtained. The percentages of hydrogen and oxygen in the compound, respectively, are:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Mass of H $= \dfrac{2}{18} \times m_{\mathrm{H_2O}}$; mass of O is obtained by difference // 📝 Solution: $m_C = \dfrac{12}{44} \times 0.307 \approx 0.0837\;\mathrm{g}$ $\implies$ $m_H = \dfrac{2}{18} \times 0.127 \approx 0.0141\;\mathrm{g}$ $\implies$ $\%\;H = \dfrac{0.0141}{0.210} \times 100 \approx 6.72\%$ $\implies$ $m_O = 0.210 - 0.0978 = 0.1122\;\mathrm{g}$ $\implies$ $\%\;O \approx 53.41\%$

questions.text: Mass of magnesium required to produce $220\;\mathrm{mL}$ of hydrogen gas at STP on reaction with excess of dilute HCl is (molar mass of Mg $=24\;\mathrm{g\;mol^{-1}}$).
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mathrm{Mg} + 2\mathrm{HCl} \to \mathrm{MgCl_2} + \mathrm{H_2}$ gives 1:1 mole ratio; use $22.4\;\mathrm{L}$ per mole at STP // 📝 Solution: $n_{\mathrm{H_2}} = 0.220/22.4 \approx 9.82 \times 10^{-3}\;\mathrm{mol}$ $\implies$ $n_{\mathrm{Mg}} = n_{\mathrm{H_2}}$ $\implies$ $m_{\mathrm{Mg}} = 9.82 \times 10^{-3} \times 24 \approx 0.2357\;\mathrm{g} \approx 236\;\mathrm{mg}$
questions.topic: Gas volume at STP and metal stoichiometry

questions.text: Concentrated nitric acid is labelled as $75\%$ by mass. The volume in mL of the solution which contains $30\;g$ of nitric acid is ____. Given : Density of nitric acid solution is $1.25\;g/mL$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $V \;=\; \frac{m_{solution}}{d}$ // 📝 Solution: $m_{sol} \;=\; \frac{30 \times 100}{75} \;=\; 40\;g \implies V \;=\; \frac{40}{1.25} \;=\; 32\;mL$

questions.text: An organic compound has 42.1% carbon, 6.4% hydrogen and remainder is oxygen. If its molecular weight is 342, then its molecular formula is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Number of atoms of an element $\; = \; \frac{\%\;\times\;M}{100 \times \text{atomic mass}}$. // 📝 Solution: $\%\,\mathrm{O} \; = \; 100 - 42.1 - 6.4 \; = \; 51.5$ $\implies$ $\mathrm{C} : \frac{0.421 \times 342}{12} \; = \; 12$, $\mathrm{H} : 0.064 \times 342 \; \approx \; 22$, $\mathrm{O} : \frac{0.515 \times 342}{16} \; = \; 11$ $\implies$ $\mathrm{C_{12}H_{22}O_{11}}$.

questions.text: Number of hydrogen atoms per molecule of a hydrocarbon A having 85.8% carbon is _______. (Given : Molar mass of A $\; = \;$ 84 g $\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find the empirical formula from the mole ratio, then scale it by $\frac{\text{molar mass}}{\text{empirical formula mass}}$. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{C} : \frac{85.8}{12} \; = \; 7.15$, $\mathrm{H} : \frac{14.2}{1} \; = \; 14.2 \implies$ ratio $1 : 2 \implies$ empirical formula $\mathrm{CH_2}$ $\implies$ $14 \times n \; = \; 84 \implies n \; = \; 6$ $\implies$ $\mathrm{C_6H_{12}}$, so $12$ H atoms.

questions.text: Molality ( m ) of 3M aqueous solution of NaCl is : (Given : Density of solution $\; = \; 1.25 \;\mathrm{g\,mL^{-1}}$, Molar mass in $\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$ : Na $-$ 23, Cl $-$ 35.5)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Molality $\; = \; \frac{\text{moles of solute}}{\text{mass of solvent in kg}}$, taking 1 L of solution. // 📝 Solution: Mass of solution $\; = \; 1250 \;\text{g}$, mass of NaCl $\; = \; 3 \times 58.5 \; = \; 175.5 \;\text{g}$ $\implies$ $m \; = \; \frac{3 \times 1000}{1250 - 175.5} \; = \; 2.79 \;\text{m}$.

questions.text: Butane reacts with oxygen as $\mathrm{C_4H_{10}(g) + \dfrac{13}{2}O_2(g) \to 4CO_2(g) + 5H_2O(l)}$. If $174.0\;\mathrm{kg}$ of butane is mixed with $320.0\;\mathrm{kg}$ of $\mathrm{O_2}$, the volume of water formed in litres is ______ (nearest integer). Given molar mass: C $=12$, H $=1$, O $=16$ g mol$^{-1}$; density of water $=1\;\mathrm{g\;mL^{-1}}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Identify the limiting reagent using stoichiometry, then convert mass of water to volume using density // 📝 Solution: $n_{\mathrm{C_4H_{10}}} = 174000/58 = 3000\;\mathrm{mol}$, $n_{\mathrm{O_2}} = 320000/32 = 10000\;\mathrm{mol}$ $\implies$ $\mathrm{O_2}$ is L.R. $\implies$ $n_{\mathrm{H_2O}} = 10000 \times \dfrac{5}{6.5} \approx 7692\;\mathrm{mol}$ $\implies$ $m = 7692 \times 18 \approx 1.3846 \times 10^{5}\;\mathrm{g}$ $\implies$ $V \approx 138.46\;\mathrm{L}$

questions.text: The amount of calcium oxide produced on heating $150\;\mathrm{kg}$ of limestone ($75\%$ pure) is ______ kg (nearest integer). Given molar mass (g mol$^{-1}$): Ca $=40$, O $=16$, C $=12$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Moles of $\mathrm{CaO}$ formed equal moles of $\mathrm{CaCO_3}$ decomposed // 📝 Solution: $m_{\mathrm{CaCO_3}} = 150 \times 0.75 = 112.5\;\mathrm{kg}$ $\implies$ $n = 112500/100 = 1125\;\mathrm{mol}$ $\implies$ $m_{\mathrm{CaO}} = 1125 \times 56 = 63000\;\mathrm{g} = 63\;\mathrm{kg}$

questions.text: On complete combustion, 0.492 g of an organic compound gave 0.792 g of $\mathrm{CO_2}$. The % of carbon in the organic compound is _____ (Nearest integer)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Mass of C $\; = \; \frac{12}{44} \times$ mass of $\mathrm{CO_2}$. // 📝 Solution: Mass of C $\; = \; \frac{12}{44} \times 0.792 \; = \; 0.216 \;\text{g}$ $\implies$ $\%\,\mathrm{C} \; = \; \frac{0.216}{0.492} \times 100 \; = \; 43.90\% \; \approx \; 44$.
questions.topic: Percentage of carbon by combustion analysis

questions.text: Fortification of food with iron is done using $\mathrm{FeSO_4 \cdot 7H_2O}$. The mass in grams of $\mathrm{FeSO_4 \cdot 7H_2O}$ required to achieve $12\;\mathrm{ppm}$ of iron in $150\;\mathrm{kg}$ of wheat is ______ (nearest integer). Given molar mass: Fe $=56$, S $=32$, O $=16$, H $=1$ g mol$^{-1}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: ppm $= \dfrac{\text{mass of solute}}{\text{mass of solution}} \times 10^{6}$ // 📝 Solution: $m_{\mathrm{Fe}} = 12 \times 10^{-6} \times 150 \times 10^{3}\;\mathrm{g} = 1.8\;\mathrm{g}$ $\implies$ $n_{\mathrm{Fe}} = 1.8/56 \approx 0.0321$ $\implies$ $m_{\text{salt}} = 0.0321 \times (56 + 96 + 126) \approx 8.94\;\mathrm{g} \approx 9\;\mathrm{g}$
questions.topic: ppm concentration and hydrated salt stoichiometry

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I (Mixture): (A) $\mathrm{CHCl_3} + \mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2}$, (B) $\mathrm{C_6H_{14}} + \mathrm{C_5H_{12}}$, (C) $\mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2} + \mathrm{H_2O}$, (D) Organic compound in $\mathrm{H_2O}$. List II (Separation Technique): (I) Steam distillation, (II) Differential extraction, (III) Distillation, (IV) Fractional distillation.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Think about boiling point differences and which liquids are immiscible with water. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{CHCl_3} + \mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2}$ (large boiling point difference) $\implies$ simple distillation $\implies$ $\mathrm{C_6H_{14}} + \mathrm{C_5H_{12}}$ (close boiling points) $\implies$ fractional distillation $\implies$ aniline + water $\implies$ steam distillation $\implies$ organic compound in water $\implies$ differential extraction $\implies$ A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

questions.text: When a hydrocarbon A undergoes complete combustion it requires 11 equivalents of oxygen and produces 4 equivalents of water. What is the molecular formula of A ?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mathrm{C_xH_y} + \left( x + \frac{y}{4} \right) \mathrm{O_2} \to x\,\mathrm{CO_2} + \frac{y}{2}\,\mathrm{H_2O}$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{y}{2} \; = \; 4 \implies y \; = \; 8$ $\implies$ $x + \frac{8}{4} \; = \; 11 \implies x \; = \; 9$ $\implies$ $\mathrm{C_9H_8}$.

questions.text: [FIGURE] Some amount of dichloromethane $\left( \mathrm{CH_2Cl_2} \right)$ is added to 671.141 mL of chloroform $\left( \mathrm{CHCl_3} \right)$ to prepare $2.6 \times 10^{-3}$ M solution of $\mathrm{CH_2Cl_2}$ (DCM). The concentration of DCM is _______ ppm (by mass). Given: Atomic mass : C $\; = \;$ 12; H : 1; Cl $\; = \;$ 35.5; density of $\mathrm{CHCl_3} \; = \; 1.49 \;\mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$
