questions.solution: 💡 Hint: ppm $\; = \; \frac{\text{mass of solute}}{\text{mass of solution}} \times 10^6$. // 📝 Solution: $2.6 \times 10^{-3} \; = \; \frac{x / 85}{0.671141} \implies x \; = \; 0.148 \;\text{g}$ $\implies$ mass of $\mathrm{CHCl_3} \; = \; 1.49 \times 671.141 \; \approx \; 1000 \;\text{g}$ $\implies$ ppm $\; = \; \frac{0.148}{1000} \times 10^6 \; = \; 148$.

questions.text: Quantitative analysis of an organic compound (X) shows following % composition. C : $14.5\%$, Cl : $64.46\%$, H: $1.8\%$ (rest oxygen). Empirical formula mass of the compound $(X)$ is __________ $\times 10^{-1}$ (Given molar mass in $g\;mol^{-1}$ of $C : 12, H : 1, O : 16, Cl : 35.5$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Convert percentages to mole ratio and find the simplest whole-number ratio // 📝 Solution: $O \;=\; 19.24\%;\; C : Cl : H : O \;=\; 1.2 : 1.8 : 1.8 : 1.2 \;=\; 2 : 3 : 3 : 2 \implies C_2H_3Cl_3O_2 \implies 165.5 \;=\; 1655 \times 10^{-1}$

questions.text: 0.05 cm thick coating of silver is deposited on a plate of $0.05 \;\mathrm{m^2}$ area. The number of silver atoms deposited on plate are _______ $\times 10^{23}$. (At mass Ag $\; = \;$ 108, d $\; = \;$ 7.9 g $\mathrm{cm^{-3}}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Volume $\; = \;$ thickness $\times$ area; then mass $\to$ moles $\to$ atoms using $N_A$. // 📝 Solution: $V \; = \; 0.05 \times 0.05 \times 10^4 \; = \; 25 \;\mathrm{cm^3}$ $\implies$ mass $\; = \; 25 \times 7.9 \;\text{g}$ $\implies$ atoms $\; = \; \frac{25 \times 7.9}{108} \times 6.023 \times 10^{23} \; = \; 11.01 \times 10^{23}$.

questions.text: The density of 'x' M solution ('X' molar) of NaOH is 1.12 g $\mathrm{mL^{-1}}$, while in molality, the concentration of the solution is 3 m (3 molal). Then $x$ is (Given : Molar mass of NaOH is 40 g/mol)
10 mL of gaseous hydrocarbon on combustion gives 40 mL of $\mathrm{CO_2(g)}$ and 50 mL of water vapour. Total number of carbon and hydrogen atoms in the hydrocarbon is _______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: By Gay-Lussac's law, gas volumes are in the same ratio as the mole coefficients. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{C_xH_y} + \left( x + \frac{y}{4} \right) \mathrm{O_2} \to x\,\mathrm{CO_2} + \frac{y}{2}\,\mathrm{H_2O}$ $\implies$ $10x \; = \; 40 \implies x \; = \; 4$, $5y \; = \; 50 \implies y \; = \; 10$ $\implies$ $\mathrm{C_4H_{10}}$, total atoms $\; = \; 4 + 10 \; = \; 14$.

questions.text: Molarity (M) of an aqueous solution containing $x$ g of anhyd. $\mathrm{CuSO_4}$ in 500 mL solution at $32^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$ is $2 \times 10^{-1}$ M. Its molality will be ______ $\times 10^{-3}$ m. (nearest integer). [Given density of the solution $\; = \; 1.25 \;\mathrm{g/mL}$]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Molality $\; = \; \frac{n_{\text{solute}}}{\text{mass of solvent in kg}}$, where solvent mass $\; = \;$ solution mass $-$ solute mass. // 📝 Solution: $n \; = \; 0.2 \times 0.5 \; = \; 0.1$ mol, solute mass $\; = \; 0.1 \times 159.5 \; = \; 15.95 \;\text{g}$, solution mass $\; = \; 500 \times 1.25 \; = \; 625 \;\text{g}$ $\implies$ solvent $\; = \; 609.05 \;\text{g}$ $\implies$ $m \; = \; \frac{0.1 \times 1000}{609.05} \; = \; 0.164 \; = \; 164 \times 10^{-3}$.

questions.text: $0.1\;\mathrm{mol}$ of the antiviral compound (P) shown in the figure will weigh ______ $\times 10^{-1}\;\mathrm{g}$. Given molar mass (g mol$^{-1}$): H $=1$, C $=12$, N $=14$, O $=16$, F $=19$, I $=127$. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Mass $= n \times M$, with $M$ from the molecular formula of the nucleoside // 📝 Solution: Formula $\mathrm{C_9H_{10}FIN_2O_5}$ $\implies$ $M = 108 + 10 + 19 + 127 + 28 + 80 = 372\;\mathrm{g\;mol^{-1}}$ $\implies$ mass $= 0.1 \times 372 = 37.2\;\mathrm{g} = 372 \times 10^{-1}\;\mathrm{g}$

questions.text: $X\;g$ of benzoic acid on reaction with aq $NaHCO_3$ released $CO_2$ that occupied $11.2\;L$ volume at STP. $X$ is _____ g.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $1$ mol benzoic acid gives $1$ mol $CO_2$; $1$ mol gas $=$ $22.4\;L$ at STP // 📝 Solution: $n_{CO_2} \;=\; \frac{11.2}{22.4} \;=\; 0.5 \implies n_{acid} \;=\; 0.5 \implies X \;=\; 0.5 \times 122 \;=\; 61\;g$
questions.topic: Stoichiometry with gas volume at STP

questions.text: Combustion of glucose $\left( \mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6} \right)$ produces $\mathrm{CO_2}$ and water. The amount of oxygen (in g) required for the complete combustion of 900 g of glucose is : [Molar mass of glucose in $\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}} \; = \; 180$ ]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6} + 6\mathrm{O_2} \to 6\mathrm{CO_2} + 6\mathrm{H_2O}$ gives a 1 : 6 mole ratio of glucose to $\mathrm{O_2}$. // 📝 Solution: $n_{\text{glucose}} \; = \; \frac{900}{180} \; = \; 5$ $\implies$ $n_{\mathrm{O_2}} \; = \; 30$ mol $\implies$ mass $\; = \; 30 \times 32 \; = \; 960 \;\text{g}$.

questions.text: An organic compound weighing $500\;\mathrm{mg}$ produced $220\;\mathrm{mg}$ of $\mathrm{CO_2}$ on complete combustion. The percentage of carbon in the compound is ______ \% (nearest integer). Given molar mass (g mol$^{-1}$): C $=12$, O $=16$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: All carbon of the compound converts into $\mathrm{CO_2}$; carbon mass is $\dfrac{12}{44}$ of $\mathrm{CO_2}$ mass // 📝 Solution: $n_{\mathrm{CO_2}} = 220/44 = 5\;\mathrm{mmol}$ $\implies$ $m_C = 5 \times 12 = 60\;\mathrm{mg}$ $\implies$ $\%\;C = \dfrac{60}{500} \times 100 = 12\%$

questions.text: The density of 3 M solution of NaCl is 1.0 g $\mathrm{mL^{-1}}$. Molality of the solution is __________ $\times 10^{-2}$ m. (Nearest integer). Given: Molar mass of Na and Cl is 23 and 35.5 g $\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$ respectively.

Assume carbon burns according to following equation : $2\mathrm{C_{(s)}} + \mathrm{O_{2(g)}} \to 2\mathrm{CO(g)}$. When 12 g carbon is burnt in 48 g of oxygen, the volume of carbon monoxide produced is ______ $\times 10^{-1}$ L at STP [nearest integer] [Given : Assume CO as ideal gas, Mass of C is 12 g $\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$, Mass of O is 16 g $\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$ and molar volume of an ideal gas at STP is 22.7 L $\mathrm{mol^{-1}}$ ]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find the limiting reagent first, then use mole ratio from the balanced equation. // 📝 Solution: $n_{\mathrm{C}} \; = \; \frac{12}{12} \; = \; 1$ mol, $n_{\mathrm{O_2}} \; = \; \frac{48}{32} \; = \; 1.5$ mol $\implies$ C needs only $0.5$ mol $\mathrm{O_2}$, so C is limiting $\implies$ $n_{\mathrm{CO}} \; = \; 1$ mol $\implies$ $V \; = \; 22.7 \;\text{L} \; = \; 227 \times 10^{-1} \;\text{L}$.

questions.text: 9.3 g of pure aniline is treated with bromine water at room temperature to give a white precipitate of the product 'P'. The mass of product 'P' obtained is 26.4 g. The percentage yield is _______ %.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Aniline gives 2,4,6-tribromoaniline (molar mass 330) with bromine water; yield $\; = \; \frac{\text{actual}}{\text{theoretical}} \times 100$. // 📝 Solution: $93 \;\text{g}$ aniline $\to$ $330 \;\text{g}$ product $\implies$ $9.3 \;\text{g}$ aniline $\to$ $33 \;\text{g}$ $\implies$ $\%\;\text{yield} \; = \; \frac{26.4}{33} \times 100 \; = \; 80\%$.

questions.text: The molality of a 10% (v/v) solution of di-bromine solution in $\mathrm{CCl_4}$ (carbon tetrachloride) is 'x'. $x \; = \;$ ________ $\times 10^{-2}$ M. (Nearest integer) [Given : molar mass of $\mathrm{Br_2} \; = \; 160 \;\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$, atomic mass of C $\; = \; 12 \;\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$, atomic mass of Cl $\; = \; 35.5 \;\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$, density of dibromine $\; = \; 3.2 \;\mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$, density of $\mathrm{CCl_4} \; = \; 1.6 \;\mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: 10% v/v means 10 mL solute in 90 mL solvent; convert volumes to masses using densities. // 📝 Solution: Mass of $\mathrm{Br_2} \; = \; 10 \times 3.2 \; = \; 32 \;\text{g}$, mass of $\mathrm{CCl_4} \; = \; 90 \times 1.6 \; = \; 144 \;\text{g}$ $\implies$ $m \; = \; \frac{32 \times 1000}{160 \times 144} \; = \; 1.388 \; \approx \; 139 \times 10^{-2}$.

questions.text: $0.01$ mole of an organic compound $(X)$ containing $10\%$ hydrogen, on complete combustion produced $0.9\;g\;H_2O$. Molar mass of $(X)$ is _____ $g\;mol^{-1}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Mass of H per mole of compound from water formed; then use $\%H$ // 📝 Solution: $n_{H_2O} \;=\; 0.05 \implies n_H \;=\; 0.1\;\text{in}\;0.01\;mol \implies 10\;g\;H\;\text{per mol} \implies 10 \;=\; \frac{10}{M} \times 100 \implies M \;=\; 100$

questions.text: $20\;mL$ of $2\;M\;\text{NaOH}$ solution is added to $400\;mL$ of $0.5\;M\;\text{NaOH}$ solution. The final concentration of the solution is $\_\_\_\_\_ \times 10^{-2}\;M$. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Mixing of same solute: $M_f \;=\; \frac{M_1 V_1 + M_2 V_2}{V_1 + V_2}$ // 📝 Solution: $M_f \;=\; \frac{2 \times 20 + 0.5 \times 400}{420} \;=\; 0.571\;M \;=\; 57.1 \times 10^{-2}\;M \implies 57$

questions.text: The hydrocarbon $(X)$ with molar mass $80\;g\;mol^{-1}$ and $90\%$ carbon has ...... degree of unsaturation.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find the molecular formula from the mass percentages, then $DoU \;=\; \frac{2C + 2 - H}{2}$ // 📝 Solution: $C \;=\; \frac{72}{12} \;=\; 6,\; H \;=\; 8 \implies C_6H_8 \implies DoU \;=\; \frac{12 + 2 - 8}{2} \;=\; 3$
questions.topic: Molecular formula and degree of unsaturation

questions.text: Consider the following reaction: $3\mathrm{PbCl_2} + 2\left( \mathrm{NH_4} \right)_3\mathrm{PO_4} \to \mathrm{Pb_3}\left( \mathrm{PO_4} \right)_2 + 6\mathrm{NH_4Cl}$. If 72 mmol of $\mathrm{PbCl_2}$ is mixed with 50 mmol of $\left( \mathrm{NH_4} \right)_3\mathrm{PO_4}$, then amount of $\mathrm{Pb_3}\left( \mathrm{PO_4} \right)_2$ formed is ______ mmol. (nearest integer)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Divide the mmol of each reactant by its stoichiometric coefficient; the smaller value is the limiting reagent. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{72}{3} \; = \; 24$, $\frac{50}{2} \; = \; 25$ $\implies$ $\mathrm{PbCl_2}$ is limiting $\implies$ $\mathrm{Pb_3}\left( \mathrm{PO_4} \right)_2 \; = \; \frac{72}{3} \; = \; 24 \;\text{mmol}$.

questions.text: What is the mass ratio of ethylene glycol ($\mathrm{C_2H_6O_2}$, molar mass $\; = \;$ 62 g/mol) required for making 500 g of 0.25 molal aqueous solution and 250 mL of 0.25 molar aqueous solution ?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Molality $\; = \;$ moles of solute per kg of solvent; molarity $\; = \;$ moles of solute per litre of solution. // 📝 Solution: Assume mass of solvent $\approx$ mass of solution $\implies$ $0.25 \; = \; \frac{W_1}{62} \times \frac{1000}{500} \implies W_1 \; = \; 7.75 \;\text{g}$ $\implies$ $0.25 \; = \; \frac{W_2}{62} \times \frac{1000}{250} \implies W_2 \; = \; 3.875 \;\text{g}$ $\implies$ $\frac{W_1}{W_2} \; = \; 2 : 1$.

questions.text: $20\;\mathrm{mL}$ of sodium iodide solution gave $4.74\;\mathrm{g}$ of silver iodide when treated with excess silver nitrate. The molarity of the sodium iodide solution is ______ M (nearest integer). Given Na $=23$, I $=127$, Ag $=108$, N $=14$, O $=16$ g mol$^{-1}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Moles of $\mathrm{I^-}$ in NaI equal moles of AgI precipitated // 📝 Solution: $M_{\mathrm{AgI}} = 235$ $\implies$ $n = 4.74/235 \approx 0.0202\;\mathrm{mol}$ $\implies$ $[\mathrm{NaI}] = 0.0202/0.020 \approx 1.008\;\mathrm{M} \approx 1\;\mathrm{M}$

questions.text: The elemental composition of a compound is $54.2\%\;C$, $9.2\%\;H$ and $36.6\%\;O$. If the molar mass of the compound is $132\;g\;mol^{-1}$, the molecular formula of the compound is : [Given : The relative atomic mass of $C : H : O \;=\; 12 : 1 : 16$]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Mole ratio gives the empirical formula; $n \;=\; \frac{\text{molar mass}}{\text{EF mass}}$ // 📝 Solution: $C : H : O \;=\; 4.52 : 9.2 : 2.28 \;=\; 2 : 4 : 1 \implies C_2H_4O\;(44) \implies n \;=\; \frac{132}{44} \;=\; 3 \implies C_6H_{12}O_3$

questions.text: Which of the following statements about $\mathrm{SO_2}$ is incorrect?

options.text: $\mathrm{SO_2}$ dissolves in water to give sulphurous acid
$\mathrm{SO_2}$ can act as an oxidising agent but not as a reducing agent

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Sulphur in $\mathrm{SO_2}$ is in the $+4$ state, intermediate between $-2$ and $+6$. // 📝 Solution: S can go to $+6$ (reducing action) or to lower states (oxidising action) $\;\implies\;$ $\mathrm{SO_2}$ acts as both $\;\implies\;$ statement B is incorrect
questions.topic: Oxides of Sulphur, Redox Behaviour of SO2

questions.text: A group 15 element exists as the tetra-atomic molecule $\mathrm{E_4}$ in its white allotrope and forms the oxides $\mathrm{E_4O_6}$ and $\mathrm{E_4O_{10}}$. The atomic number of the element is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: White phosphorus is $\mathrm{P_4}$ and its oxides are $\mathrm{P_4O_6}$ and $\mathrm{P_4O_{10}}$. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{E} \;=\; \mathrm{P} \;\implies\; Z \;=\; 15$

questions.text: The atomicities of oxygen and sulphur in their stable forms at room temperature are respectively
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Oxygen forms strong $p\pi-p\pi$ double bonds, while sulphur prefers single-bonded rings. // 📝 Solution: Oxygen is $\mathrm{O_2}$ and rhombic sulphur is $\mathrm{S_8}$ $\;\implies\;$ atomicities $2$ and $8$

questions.text: Among the group 15 elements, the element whose covalency cannot exceed $4$ is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Expansion of covalency needs vacant d-orbitals in the valence shell. // 📝 Solution: N has no d-orbitals in the second shell $\;\implies\;$ maximum covalency is $4$ $\;\implies\;$ N

questions.text: Electrolysis of cold, concentrated sulphuric acid at high current density gives which of the following at the anode?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Anodic oxidation of hydrogen sulphate ions joins two $\mathrm{HSO_4^-}$ units through a peroxo linkage. // 📝 Solution: $2\mathrm{HSO_4^-} \;\to\; \mathrm{HO_3SOOSO_3H} \;+\; 2e^-$ $\;\implies\;$ peroxodisulphuric acid $\mathrm{H_2S_2O_8}$

questions.text: Alkaline oxidative fusion of $\text{MnO}_2$ gives A, which on electrolytic oxidation in alkaline solution gives B. A and B, respectively, are:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Follow the two-step preparation of $\text{KMnO}_4$: fusion first, electrolytic oxidation second. // 📝 Solution: $\text{MnO}_2\;\xrightarrow{\text{KOH},\;\text{O}_2}\;\text{MnO}_4^{2-}\;(\text{A})\;\implies\;\text{MnO}_4^{2-}\;\xrightarrow{\text{electrolytic oxidation}}\;\text{MnO}_4^{-}\;(\text{B})$

questions.text: Which one amongst the following are good oxidizing agents? A. $\mathrm{Sm^{2+}}$ B. $\mathrm{Ce^{2+}}$ C. $\mathrm{Ce^{4+}}$ D. $\mathrm{Tb^{4+}}$ Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Lanthanoid ions revert to the stable $+3$ state. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Ce^{4+}} \;\to\; \mathrm{Ce^{3+}}$ and $\mathrm{Tb^{4+}} \;\to\; \mathrm{Tb^{3+}}$ are oxidising, while $\mathrm{Sm^{2+}}$ and $\mathrm{Ce^{2+}}$ are reducing $\implies$ C and D only
questions.topic: Lanthanoids: oxidation states and redox behaviour

questions.text: Statement I: The first ionisation enthalpy of Cr is lower than that of Mn. Statement II: The second and third ionisation enthalpies of Cr are higher than those of Mn. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Compare the actual $IE_1$, $IE_2$ and $IE_3$ values of Cr and Mn, keeping in mind the stability of $\text{Cr}^{+}\;(3d^5)$ and $\text{Mn}^{2+}\;(3d^5)$. // 📝 Solution: $IE_1:\;653\;<\;717\;\implies\;\text{I true};\;IE_2:\;1592\;>\;1509,\;IE_3:\;2987\;<\;3248\;\implies\;\text{II false}$

questions.text: Consider the following statements about manganate and permanganate ions. A. Both are tetrahedral. B. The oxidation states of Mn are $+7$ in manganate and $+6$ in permanganate. C. Oxidation of a Mn(II) salt by peroxodisulphate gives manganate as the final product. D. Manganate is paramagnetic and permanganate is diamagnetic. E. Acidified permanganate reduces oxalate, nitrite and iodide ions. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find the oxidation state and d-electron count of Mn in each ion, and note whether permanganate acts as an oxidant or a reductant. // 📝 Solution: $\text{MnO}_4^{2-}\;(\text{Mn}^{6+},\;d^1)\;\text{paramagnetic};\;\text{MnO}_4^{-}\;(\text{Mn}^{7+},\;d^0)\;\text{diamagnetic}\;\implies\;\text{B false; C gives }\text{MnO}_4^{-}\;\text{(false); E false (oxidises)}\;\implies\;\text{A and D}$

questions.text: A first row transition metal in its $+2$ oxidation state has a spin-only magnetic moment value of $3.86\;\mathrm{BM}$. The atomic number of the metal is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mu \;=\; \sqrt{n\left(n+2\right)}$ gives the number of unpaired electrons. // 📝 Solution: $3.86 \;\approx\; \sqrt{15} \implies n \;=\; 3 \implies M^{2+} \;=\; 3d^{3} \implies \mathrm{V}\;\left(Z \;=\; 23\right)$

questions.text: The oxidation state of vanadium in the orthovanadate ion $\mathrm{VO_4^{3-}}$ is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The sum of the oxidation states equals the net charge on the ion. // 📝 Solution: $x \;+\; 4\left(-2\right) \;=\; -3 \;\implies\; x \;=\; +5$

questions.text: Which of the following statements about $\mathrm{Zn}$, $\mathrm{Cd}$ and $\mathrm{Hg}$ are correct? A. They have completely filled $d$-orbitals in the ground state and in common oxidation states. B. They have lower melting points than other $d$-block metals. C. $\mathrm{Hg}$ is a liquid at room temperature. D. They show variable oxidation states like $\mathrm{Fe}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Group 12 elements have $\left(n-1\right)d^{10}ns^2$ configuration, with weak metallic bonding. // 📝 Solution: $d^{10}$ is retained and metallic bonding is weak, so low melting points and Hg is liquid, but there is no variable oxidation state like Fe $\;\implies\;$ A, B and C

questions.text: The spin-only magnetic moment value of the ion among $\mathrm{Ti^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{V^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{Co^{3+}}$ and $\mathrm{Cr^{2+}}$, that acts as strong oxidising agent in aqueous solution is _______ BM (Near integer). (Given atomic numbers : Ti : 22, V : 23, Cr : 24, Co : 27)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mathrm{Co^{3+}}$ is strongly oxidising ($\mathrm{Co^{3+}} \;\to\; \mathrm{Co^{2+}}$). // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Co^{3+}} \;=\; 3d^{6}$ (weak field in water) $\implies n \;=\; 4 \implies \mu \;=\; \sqrt{24} \;=\; 4.9 \;\approx\; 5\;\mathrm{BM}$

questions.text: On heating common salt and $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ in equal amounts with conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, a gas is evolved. The formula of the gas and the oxidation state of the central metal atom in it are, respectively:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: This is the chromyl chloride test, and the central metal keeps its dichromate oxidation state. // 📝 Solution: $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7\;+\;4\text{NaCl}\;+\;6\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\;\to\;2\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2\;+\;\ldots\;\implies\;x\;+\;2\left(-2\right)\;+\;2\left(-1\right)\;=\;0\;\implies\;x\;=\;+6$

questions.text: Identify the correct statements. A. $\text{Mn}_2\text{O}_7$ is an oil at room temperature. B. $\text{V}_2\text{O}_4$ reacts with acid to give $\text{VO}_2^{2+}$. C. $\text{CrO}$ is a basic oxide. D. $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5$ does not react with acid. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall the nature of lower and higher oxides of V, Cr and Mn (lower oxides basic, higher oxides acidic or amphoteric). // 📝 Solution: $\text{V}_2\text{O}_4\;\to\;\text{VO}^{2+}\;\text{salts}\;\implies\;\text{B false};\;\text{V}_2\text{O}_5\;\text{is amphoteric}\;\implies\;\text{D false};\;\text{A and C true}$

questions.text: The difference in the 'spin-only' magnetic moment values of $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ and the manganese product formed during titration of $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ against oxalic acid in acidic medium is _______ BM. (nearest integer)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: In acidic medium $\mathrm{MnO_4^-}$ is reduced to $\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}$. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{KMnO_4}\;\left(\mathrm{Mn^{7+}},\,d^0\right) \;=\; 0$; $\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}\;\left(d^5\right) \;=\; \sqrt{35} \;=\; 5.92 \implies$ difference $\approx 6$

questions.text: Match List I with List II. List I (Species): A. $\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}}$ B. $\mathrm{MnO_4^-}$ C. $\mathrm{CrO_4^{2-}}$ D. $\mathrm{MnO_4^{2-}}$. List II (Feature): I. Yellow colour II. Green colour, paramagnetic III. Purple colour, $d^0$ IV. Orange colour, two $\mathrm{Cr}$ atoms joined by an oxo bridge
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall the colour, oxidation state and structure of chromate, dichromate and manganate/permanganate ions. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}}$ orange with oxo bridge, $\mathrm{MnO_4^-}$ purple $d^0$, $\mathrm{CrO_4^{2-}}$ yellow, $\mathrm{MnO_4^{2-}}$ green $d^1$ $\;\implies\;$ A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II

questions.text: A first-row transition metal M does not liberate $\text{H}_2$ from dilute HCl. One mole of aqueous $\text{MSO}_4$ is treated with excess aqueous KCN, and then $\text{H}_2\text{S}\left(g\right)$ is passed through the solution. The amount of MS formed is ___ mol.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A metal that does not react with dilute HCl has a positive $E^{\circ}$, and excess cyanide forms a very stable complex that keeps the free metal ion concentration negligible. // 📝 Solution: $\text{M}\;=\;\text{Cu}\;\implies\;\text{Cu}^{2+}\;+\;\text{excess CN}^{-}\;\to\;\text{K}_3\left[\text{Cu}\left(\text{CN}\right)_4\right]\;\implies\;\text{no CuS precipitates}\;\implies\;0\;\text{mol}$

questions.text: The number of mixed oxides among $\text{Ti}_2\text{O}_3$, $\text{V}_2\text{O}_4$, $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_3$, $\text{Mn}_3\text{O}_4$, $\text{Fe}_3\text{O}_4$, $\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3$ and $\text{Co}_3\text{O}_4$ is ___.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A mixed oxide contains the metal in two different oxidation states, usually with the formula $\text{M}_3\text{O}_4$. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Mn}_3\text{O}_4\;(\text{MnO}\cdot\text{Mn}_2\text{O}_3),\;\text{Fe}_3\text{O}_4\;(\text{FeO}\cdot\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3),\;\text{Co}_3\text{O}_4\;(\text{CoO}\cdot\text{Co}_2\text{O}_3)\;\implies\;3$

questions.text: Identify A and B in the following reactions: $\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2\;+\;4\text{NaOH}\;\to\;\text{A}\;+\;2\text{NaCl}\;+\;2\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{A}\;+\;2\text{HCl}\;+\;2\text{H}_2\text{O}_2\;\to\;\text{B}\;+\;3\text{H}_2\text{O}$ (the $2\text{NaCl}$ is not shown in the second reaction).
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Chromyl chloride hydrolyses in alkali to chromate, and acidified chromate with $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ gives the blue peroxide. // 📝 Solution: $\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2\;+\;4\text{NaOH}\;\to\;\text{Na}_2\text{CrO}_4\;+\;2\text{NaCl}\;+\;2\text{H}_2\text{O}\;\implies\;\text{Na}_2\text{CrO}_4\;+\;2\text{HCl}\;+\;2\text{H}_2\text{O}_2\;\to\;\text{CrO}_5\;+\;2\text{NaCl}\;+\;3\text{H}_2\text{O}$

questions.text: Which of the following are the example of double salt? (A) $\mathrm{FeSO_4 \cdot \left(NH_4\right)_2SO_4 \cdot 6H_2O}$ (B) $\mathrm{CuSO_4 \cdot 4NH_3 \cdot H_2O}$ (C) $\mathrm{K_2SO_4 \cdot Al_2\left(SO_4\right)_3 \cdot 24H_2O}$ (D) $\mathrm{Fe\left(CN\right)_2 \cdot 4KCN}$ Choose the correct answer.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Double salts lose identity in solution, whereas complexes do not. // 📝 Solution: A is Mohr's salt and C is potash alum (double salts) $\implies$ B and D are complex compounds $\implies$ A and C only

questions.text: Which of the following compounds shows colour due to d–d transition?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: d–d transitions need a partly filled d subshell, whereas $d^0$ species are coloured by charge transfer. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Cu}^{2+}\;(3d^9)\;\implies\;d\text{–}d\;\text{transition}\;\implies\;\text{CuSO}_4\cdot 5\text{H}_2\text{O};\;\text{Cr}^{6+},\;\text{Mn}^{7+}\;(d^0)\;\implies\;\text{charge transfer}$

questions.text: A solution of $\mathrm{FeCl_3}$ when treated with $\mathrm{K_4\left[Fe\left(CN\right)_6\right]}$ gives a prussian blue precipitate due to the formation of
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Balance charge between $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ and $\left[\mathrm{Fe\left(CN\right)_6}\right]^{4-}$. // 📝 Solution: $4\,\mathrm{Fe^{3+}} \;+\; 3\left[\mathrm{Fe\left(CN\right)_6}\right]^{4-} \;\to\; \mathrm{Fe_4\left[Fe\left(CN\right)_6\right]_3}$ (Prussian blue)

questions.text: Which of the following is a strong reducing agent? (Given atomic numbers: Ce = 58, Eu = 63, Gd = 64, Lu = 71)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Look for the ion that readily loses one electron to reach the stable +3 state. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Eu}^{2+}\;(4f^7)\;\to\;\text{Eu}^{3+}\;(4f^6)\;+\;e^{-}\;\implies\;\text{Eu}^{2+}\;\text{is a strong reductant};\;\text{Ce}^{4+}\;\text{is an oxidant}$

questions.text: Statement I: In lanthanoids, the formation of $\text{Ce}^{4+}$ is favoured by its noble gas configuration. Statement II: $\text{Ce}^{4+}$ is a strong oxidant, reverting to the common +3 state. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.

options.text: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Compare the electronic configuration of $\text{Ce}^{4+}$ with a noble gas and recall its reduction potential. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Ce}^{4+}\;(4f^0)\;\text{is isoelectronic with Xe}\;\implies\;E^{\circ}_{\text{Ce}^{4+}/\text{Ce}^{3+}}\;=\;+1.74\;\text{V}\;\implies\;\text{both true}$

questions.text: Which lanthanoid ion in the $+4$ oxidation state has the $4f^7$ configuration?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Count the $4f$ electrons left after removing four electrons from the neutral atom. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Tb}\;\left[\mathrm{Xe}\right]4f^96s^2 \;\to\; \mathrm{Tb^{4+}}\;4f^7$, while $\mathrm{Ce^{4+}}\;4f^0$, $\mathrm{Pr^{4+}}\;4f^1$, $\mathrm{Dy^{4+}}\;4f^6 \;\implies\; \mathrm{Tb^{4+}}$

questions.text: The spin-only magnetic moment of the $\mathrm{Mn^{3+}}$ ion in $\mathrm{BM}$, rounded off to the nearest integer, is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $\mu \;=\; \sqrt{n\left(n+2\right)}$ with $n$ the number of unpaired electrons. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Mn^{3+}}\;:\;d^4 \;\implies\; n \;=\; 4 \;\implies\; \mu \;=\; \sqrt{24} \;\approx\; 4.89 \;\approx\; 5\;\mathrm{BM}$

questions.text: Strong heating of $\mathrm{FeSO_4\cdot 7H_2O}$ leaves a brown residue of an iron oxide. The molar mass of this oxide in $\mathrm{g\;mol^{-1}}$ is (Fe $\;=\; 56$, O $\;=\; 16$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Ferrous sulphate decomposes on heating to ferric oxide, $\mathrm{SO_2}$ and $\mathrm{SO_3}$. // 📝 Solution: $2\mathrm{FeSO_4} \;\xrightarrow{\;\Delta\;}\; \mathrm{Fe_2O_3} \;+\; \mathrm{SO_2} \;+\; \mathrm{SO_3} \;\implies\; 2\left(56\right) \;+\; 3\left(16\right) \;=\; 160$

questions.text: The correct order of basicity of oxides of vanadium is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Higher oxidation state gives a more acidic and less basic oxide. // 📝 Solution: $+3 \;<\; +4 \;<\; +5 \implies$ acidic nature $\mathrm{V_2O_3} \;<\; \mathrm{V_2O_4} \;<\; \mathrm{V_2O_5} \implies$ basicity $\mathrm{V_2O_3} \;>\; \mathrm{V_2O_4} \;>\; \mathrm{V_2O_5}$

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (A) $\text{Cr}^{2+}$ (B) $\text{Mn}^{+}$ (C) $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ (D) $\text{V}^{+}$. List-II: (I) $3d^8$ (II) $3d^3 4s^1$ (III) $3d^4$ (IV) $3d^5 4s^1$. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Write the neutral atom configuration, then remove electrons from 4s first. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Cr}^{2+}\;(3d^4),\;\text{Mn}^{+}\;(3d^5 4s^1),\;\text{Ni}^{2+}\;(3d^8),\;\text{V}^{+}\;(3d^3 4s^1)\;\implies\;\text{A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II}$

questions.text: In the chromyl chloride test for $\text{Cl}^{-}$, the yellow solution containing $\text{CrO}_4^{2-}$ is acidified, and amyl alcohol and 10% $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ are added to give a blue organic layer (chromium pentoxide). The oxidation state of Cr in the blue compound is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The blue compound contains two peroxide (O–O) linkages, so $\text{CrO}_5$ is $\text{CrO}\left(\text{O}_2\right)_2$. // 📝 Solution: $\text{CrO}\left(\text{O}_2\right)_2\;\implies\;x\;+\;\left(-2\right)\;+\;2\left(-2\right)\;=\;0\;\implies\;x\;=\;+6$

questions.text: Which element is not present in Nessler's reagent ?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall the formula of Nessler's reagent. // 📝 Solution: Nessler's reagent $\;=\; \mathrm{K_2\left[HgI_4\right]}$ contains K, Hg and I but no oxygen $\implies$ oxygen

questions.text: In alkaline medium, $\text{MnO}_4^{-}$ oxidises $\text{I}^{-}$ to:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: In alkaline or neutral medium, permanganate is reduced to $\text{MnO}_2$ and iodide goes to a higher oxidation state than $\text{I}_2$. // 📝 Solution: $2\text{MnO}_4^{-}\;+\;\text{H}_2\text{O}\;+\;\text{I}^{-}\;\to\;2\text{MnO}_2\;+\;2\text{OH}^{-}\;+\;\text{IO}_3^{-}$

questions.text: Which of the following ions have two unpaired electrons? A. $\mathrm{Ti^{2+}}$ B. $\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}$ C. $\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}$ D. $\mathrm{V^{3+}}$ E. $\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Write the $d^n$ configuration of each ion and count the unpaired electrons. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Ti^{2+}}\;d^2$, $\mathrm{V^{3+}}\;d^2$, $\mathrm{Ni^{2+}}\;d^8$ each have $n \;=\; 2$, while $\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}\;d^3$ has $3$ and $\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}\;d^5$ has $5 \;\implies\;$ A, D and E
questions.topic: Unpaired Electrons in Transition Metal Ions

questions.text: Choose the correct colours of the hydrated ions $\mathrm{Zn^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{V^{3+}}$ and $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ respectively.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Colour arises from $d-d$ transitions, so a $d^{10}$ ion is colourless. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Zn^{2+}}\left(d^{10}\right)$ colourless, $\mathrm{V^{3+}}\left(d^2\right)$ green, $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}\left(d^5\right)$ yellow $\;\implies\;$ option B

questions.text: Among $\text{Sc}$, $\text{Ti}$, $\text{V}$, $\text{Cr}$, $\text{Mn}$ and $\text{Fe}$, the transition metal M that has the highest second ionisation enthalpy gives $\text{M}^{+}$ whose spin-only magnetic moment is ___ BM (nearest integer).
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Removing an electron from the stable half-filled $3d^5$ configuration of $\text{Cr}^{+}$ is very difficult; use $\mu\;=\;\sqrt{n\left(n+2\right)}$. // 📝 Solution: $\text{M}\;=\;\text{Cr}\;\implies\;\text{Cr}^{+}\;(3d^5)\;\implies\;n\;=\;5\;\implies\;\mu\;=\;\sqrt{35}\;\approx\;5.92\;\approx\;6\;\text{BM}$

questions.text: The orange colour of $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ and the purple colour of $\text{KMnO}_4$ are due to:

options.text: $d\to d$ transition in $\text{KMnO}_4$ and charge transfer transition in $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$
$d\to d$ transition in $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ and charge transfer transition in $\text{KMnO}_4$

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Check the d-electron count of the central metal ion in each compound. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Cr}^{6+}\;(d^0),\;\text{Mn}^{7+}\;(d^0)\;\implies\;\text{no d–d transition}\;\implies\;\text{ligand}\to\text{metal charge transfer in both}$

questions.text: A solution of $\mathrm{CrO_5}$ in amyl alcohol has a ...... colour
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Chromium pentoxide is the blue peroxo compound. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{CrO_5}$ in amyl alcohol $\implies$ blue colour

questions.text: Consider the following statements about Mn and $\text{Mn}_2\text{O}_7$. A. Mn forms $\text{Mn}_2\text{O}_7$, in which Mn is in its highest oxidation state. B. Oxygen stabilises Mn in higher oxidation states by forming multiple bonds. C. $\text{Mn}_2\text{O}_7$ is an ionic oxide. D. The structure of $\text{Mn}_2\text{O}_7$ consists of one bridged oxygen. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Mn in a high oxidation state forms covalent oxides, and the structure has two $\text{MnO}_3$ units joined through oxygen. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Mn}_2\text{O}_7:\;\text{Mn}\;=\;+7\;\text{(group number)}\;\implies\;\text{covalent oil, }\text{O}_3\text{Mn}\text{–O–}\text{MnO}_3\;\implies\;\text{C false; A, B, D true}$

questions.text: What will be the decreasing order of basic strength of the following conjugate bases? $\mathrm{^-OH}$, $\mathrm{RO^-}$, $\mathrm{CH_3COO^-}$, $\mathrm{Cl^-}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Stronger acid gives weaker conjugate base. // 📝 Solution: Acidity $\mathrm{HCl} \;>\; \mathrm{CH_3COOH} \;>\; \mathrm{H_2O} \;>\; \mathrm{ROH} \implies$ basicity $\mathrm{Cl^-} \;<\; \mathrm{CH_3COO^-} \;<\; \mathrm{^-OH} \;<\; \mathrm{RO^-}$
questions.topic: Acid strength and conjugate base strength

questions.text: The oxidation state of chromium in the final product formed by the reaction between KI and acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ solution is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Dichromate is a strong oxidant in acidic medium and is reduced to the stable aqua ion of Cr. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}\;+\;14\text{H}^{+}\;+\;6\text{I}^{-}\;\to\;2\text{Cr}^{3+}\;+\;3\text{I}_2\;+\;7\text{H}_2\text{O}\;\implies\;\text{Cr}\;=\;+3$

questions.text: Arrange the following elements in the increasing order of number of unpaired electrons: $A\;=\;\text{Sc}$, $B\;=\;\text{Cr}$, $C\;=\;\text{V}$, $D\;=\;\text{Ti}$, $E\;=\;\text{Mn}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Write the ground-state configuration of each element and count the half-filled and singly filled orbitals. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Sc}\;(3d^1)\;=\;1,\;\text{Ti}\;(3d^2)\;=\;2,\;\text{V}\;(3d^3)\;=\;3,\;\text{Mn}\;(3d^5)\;=\;5,\;\text{Cr}\;(3d^5 4s^1)\;=\;6\;\implies\;A\;<\;D\;<\;C\;<\;E\;<\;B$

questions.text: $\text{NaCl}\;+\;\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7\;+\;\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\;\to\;\text{A}\;+\;\text{KHSO}_4\;+\;\text{NaHSO}_4\;+\;\text{H}_2\text{O}$; $\text{A}\;+\;\text{NaOH}\;\to\;\text{B}\;+\;\text{NaCl}\;+\;\text{H}_2\text{O}$; $\text{B}\;+\;\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\;+\;\text{H}_2\text{O}_2\;\to\;\text{C}\;+\;\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4\;+\;\text{H}_2\text{O}$. In the product C, X is the number of $\text{O}_2^{2-}$ units, Y is the total number of oxygen atoms and Z is the oxidation state of Cr. The value of $X\;+\;Y\;+\;Z$ is ___.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Identify A, B and C from the chromyl chloride test followed by the blue peroxide test, then count peroxide units in C. // 📝 Solution: $\text{A}\;=\;\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2,\;\text{B}\;=\;\text{Na}_2\text{CrO}_4,\;\text{C}\;=\;\text{CrO}\left(\text{O}_2\right)_2\;\implies\;X\;=\;2,\;Y\;=\;5,\;Z\;=\;+6\;\implies\;X\;+\;Y\;+\;Z\;=\;13$

questions.text: Fe(III) catalyses the reaction between iodide and persulphate ions. A. $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ oxidises the iodide ion. B. $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ oxidises the persulphate ion. C. $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ reduces the iodide ion. D. $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ reduces the persulphate ion. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A catalyst is consumed in one step and regenerated in the next, so write the two-step mechanism. // 📝 Solution: $2\text{Fe}^{3+}\;+\;2\text{I}^{-}\;\to\;2\text{Fe}^{2+}\;+\;\text{I}_2\;\implies\;2\text{Fe}^{2+}\;+\;\text{S}_2\text{O}_8^{2-}\;\to\;2\text{Fe}^{3+}\;+\;2\text{SO}_4^{2-}\;\implies\;\text{A and D}$

questions.text: Which of the following sulphides is not precipitated when $\mathrm{H_2S}$ is passed through a solution containing dilute $\mathrm{HCl}$?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Compare $K_{sp}$ values; Group II sulphides precipitate in acidic medium while Group IV sulphides need basic medium. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{CuS}$, $\mathrm{PbS}$ and $\mathrm{CdS}$ have low $K_{sp}$ and precipitate in acid, whereas $\mathrm{CoS}$ ($\text{Group IV}$) precipitates only in $\mathrm{NH_4OH}$ medium $\;\implies\;$ CoS

questions.text: The number of colourless lanthanoid ions among $\text{Eu}^{3+}$, $\text{Lu}^{3+}$, $\text{Nd}^{3+}$, $\text{La}^{3+}$ and $\text{Sm}^{3+}$ is ___.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Lanthanoid ions with $4f^0$ or $4f^{14}$ configuration have no f–f transitions and are colourless. // 📝 Solution: $\text{La}^{3+}\;(4f^0),\;\text{Lu}^{3+}\;(4f^{14})\;\implies\;\text{colourless ions}\;=\;2$

questions.text: Statement I: The number of pairs in which both ions are coloured in aqueous solution is 3: $\left[\text{Sc}^{3+},\;\text{Ti}^{3+}\right]$, $\left[\text{Mn}^{2+},\;\text{Cr}^{2+}\right]$, $\left[\text{Cu}^{2+},\;\text{Zn}^{2+}\right]$, $\left[\text{Ni}^{2+},\;\text{Ti}^{4+}\right]$. Statement II: $\text{Th}^{4+}$ is the strongest reducing agent among $\text{Th}^{4+}$, $\text{Ce}^{4+}$, $\text{Gd}^{3+}$ and $\text{Eu}^{2+}$. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: An ion is coloured only if it has a partly filled d or f subshell, and a strong reductant readily loses an electron to reach a stable state. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Sc}^{3+}\;(d^0),\;\text{Zn}^{2+}\;(d^{10}),\;\text{Ti}^{4+}\;(d^0)\;\text{colourless}\;\implies\;\text{only 1 pair, I false};\;\text{Eu}^{2+}\;(4f^7\to4f^6)\;\text{is the strongest reductant}\;\implies\;\text{II false}$
questions.topic: Colour of Ions and Reducing Strength

questions.text: Consider the following reaction $\mathrm{MnO_2} \;+\; \mathrm{KOH} \;+\; \mathrm{O_2} \;\to\; \mathrm{A} \;+\; \mathrm{H_2O}$. Product 'A' in neutral or acidic medium disproportionate to give products 'B' and 'C' along with water. The sum of spin-only magnetic moment values of B and C is ______ BM. (nearest integer) (Given atomic number of Mn is 25)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mathrm{K_2MnO_4}$ disproportionates to $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ and $\mathrm{MnO_2}$. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{A} \;=\; \mathrm{K_2MnO_4} \implies \mathrm{B} \;=\; \mathrm{KMnO_4}\;\left(d^0,\; \mu \;=\; 0\right)$, $\mathrm{C} \;=\; \mathrm{MnO_2}\;\left(d^3,\; \mu \;=\; \sqrt{15} \;=\; 3.87\right) \implies$ sum $\approx 4$
questions.topic: Disproportionation of manganate and magnetic moment

questions.text: $0.05\;\text{M}$ $\text{CuSO}_4$ solution on treatment with $0.01\;\text{M}$ $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ gives green $\text{Cu}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$. The two solutions are separated by a semipermeable membrane (SPM) as shown: [FIGURE]. Which of the following is correct due to osmosis?

options.text: Green colour is observed on side Y
Green colour is observed on side X

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Osmosis moves only solvent, from the dilute solution to the concentrated solution, through the SPM. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Solvent}\;:\;0.01\;\text{M}\;\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7\;\to\;0.05\;\text{M}\;\text{CuSO}_4\;\implies\;\text{CuSO}_4\;\text{gets diluted}\;\implies\;\text{molarity of }\text{CuSO}_4\;\text{is lowered}$

questions.text: Highest oxidation state of Mn is exhibited in $\mathrm{Mn_2O_7}$. The correct statements about $\mathrm{Mn_2O_7}$ are (A) Mn is tetrahedrally surrounded by oxygen atoms (B) Mn is octahedrally surrounded by oxygen atoms (C) Contains Mn-O-Mn bridge (D) Contains Mn-Mn bond. Choose the correct answer from the options given below
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall the structure of $\mathrm{Mn_2O_7}$: two $\mathrm{MnO_3}$ units joined by one oxygen. // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] $\implies$ each Mn is tetrahedral and the two Mn atoms are linked through a Mn-O-Mn bridge, with no Mn-Mn bond $\implies$ A and C

questions.text: Statement I: The 4f and 5f series of elements are placed separately in the periodic table to preserve the principle of classification. Statement II: s-block elements can be found in pure form in nature. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.

options.text: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Consider how reactive the s-block metals are. // 📝 Solution: $\text{s-block metals are highly reactive}\;\implies\;\text{occur only in the combined state}\;\implies\;\text{Statement II false, Statement I true}$

questions.text: Which pair of sulphides are both yellow in colour?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall the colours of metal sulphide precipitates in qualitative analysis. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{CuS}$ and $\mathrm{PbS}$ are black, $\mathrm{ZnS}$ is white, $\mathrm{HgS}$ is black or red, while $\mathrm{As_2S_3}$ and $\mathrm{As_2S_5}$ are yellow $\;\implies\;$ option B

questions.text: When $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ ion is treated with KI, a white precipitate, X appears in solution. The solution is titrated with sodium thiosulphate, the compound Y is formed. X and Y respectively are
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mathrm{I^-}$ reduces $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ to $\mathrm{Cu^+}$ and liberates $\mathrm{I_2}$, which thiosulphate converts to tetrathionate. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}} \;+\; 2\,\mathrm{KI} \;\to\; \mathrm{CuI_2}$ (unstable) $\implies 2\,\mathrm{CuI_2} \;\to\; \mathrm{Cu_2I_2} \;+\; \mathrm{I_2}$; $\mathrm{I_2}\;+\;\mathrm{Na_2S_2O_3} \;\to\; \mathrm{Na_2S_4O_6}$

questions.text: Identify the option in which all the given elements have $d^{10}$ configuration.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Write the outer configuration of each element and look for a completely filled d subshell. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Cu}\;3d^{10}4s^1,\;\text{Zn}\;3d^{10}4s^2,\;\text{Cd}\;4d^{10}5s^2,\;\text{Ag}\;4d^{10}5s^1\;\implies\;\text{option B}$

questions.text: "X" is an oxoanion of the lightest element of group 7. The metal in X is in the $+6$ oxidation state. The colour of the potassium salt of X is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The lightest group 7 element is Mn, and the oxoanion with Mn in +6 is the manganate ion. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Mn}\;\implies\;\text{MnO}_4^{2-}\;(\text{Mn}\;=\;+6)\;\implies\;\text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4\;\text{is dark green}$

questions.text: $\mathrm{K_2Cr_2O_7}$ paper acidified with dilute $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ turns green when exposed to
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mathrm{SO_2}$ reduces orange dichromate to green $\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}$. // 📝 Solution: $3\,\mathrm{SO_2} \;+\; \mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}} \;+\; 2\,\mathrm{H^+} \;\to\; 3\,\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}} \;+\; 2\,\mathrm{Cr^{3+}} \;+\; \mathrm{H_2O}$ (green) $\implies$ sulphur dioxide
questions.topic: Reactions of potassium dichromate (test for SO2)

questions.text: In the reaction of potassium dichromate, potassium chloride and conc. sulfuric acid, the oxidation state of chromium in the product is $\left(+\right)$ ___.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: This is the chromyl chloride test, so identify the volatile red product and find Cr in it. // 📝 Solution: $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7\;+\;4\text{KCl}\;+\;6\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\;\to\;2\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2\;+\;\ldots\;\implies\;x\;+\;2\left(-2\right)\;+\;2\left(-1\right)\;=\;0\;\implies\;x\;=\;+6$

questions.text: The set of correct statements is: (i) Manganese exhibits $+7$ oxidation state in its oxide. (ii) Ruthenium and Osmium exhibit $+8$ oxidation in their oxides. (iii) Sc shows $+4$ oxidation state which is oxidizing in nature. (iv) Cr shows oxidising nature in $+6$ oxidation state.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Check the highest oxidation states of Mn, Ru, Os, Sc and Cr. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Mn_2O_7}\;\left(+7\right)$, $\mathrm{RuO_4},\,\mathrm{OsO_4}\;\left(+8\right)$ and $\mathrm{Cr\left(VI\right)}$ oxidising are true; Sc does not show $+4 \implies$ (i), (ii), (iv)

questions.text: Which of the following compounds contains manganese in the $+6$ oxidation state?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Assign the oxidation state of Mn using the charges on the other ions. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{K_2MnO_4}$: $2\left(+1\right) \;+\; x \;+\; 4\left(-2\right) \;=\; 0 \;\implies\; x \;=\; +6$

questions.text: An ammoniacal metal salt solution gives a brilliant red precipitate on addition of dimethylglyoxime. The metal ion is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Dimethylglyoxime (DMG) is the specific reagent for nickel. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Ni^{2+}} \;+\; 2\,\mathrm{DMG} \;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{NH_3}}\; \left[\mathrm{Ni\left(DMG\right)_2}\right] \implies$ rosy red complex

questions.text: Statement I: In the transition elements, the higher oxidation states of the heavier elements become more stable down the group, unlike in the p-block elements. Statement II: Cu cannot liberate hydrogen from weak acids. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Compare the standard reduction potential of $\text{Cu}^{2+}/\text{Cu}$ with that of $\text{H}^{+}/\text{H}_2$. // 📝 Solution: $E^{\circ}_{\text{Cu}^{2+}/\text{Cu}}\;=\;+0.34\;\text{V}\;>\;E^{\circ}_{\text{H}^{+}/\text{H}_2}\;=\;0\;\implies\;\text{Cu does not liberate }\text{H}_2\;\implies\;\text{both true}$
questions.topic: Oxidation State Trends and Electrode Potential

questions.text: During the qualitative analysis of $\mathrm{SO_3^{2-}}$ using dilute $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$, $\mathrm{SO_2}$ gas is evolved which turns $\mathrm{K_2Cr_2O_7}$ solution (acidified with dilute $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$) :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mathrm{SO_2}$ reduces $\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}}$ to $\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}$. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}} \;+\; \mathrm{SO_3^{2-}} \;\xrightarrow{\mathrm{H^+}}\; \mathrm{Cr^{3+}} \;+\; \mathrm{SO_4^{2-}} \implies$ green

questions.text: Which transition metal has the highest third ionisation enthalpy among the following?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The third ionisation removes an electron from the $M^{2+}$ ion, so look for the most stable $d^5$ configuration in $M^{2+}$. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Mn}^{2+}\;(3d^5)\;\text{half-filled}\;\implies\;IE_3\;(\text{Mn})\;=\;3260\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\;>\;\text{Fe, Cr, V}$

questions.text: Among $\mathrm{CrO}$, $\mathrm{Cr_2O_3}$ and $\mathrm{CrO_3}$, the sum of spin-only magnetic moment values of basic and amphoteric oxides is _______ $10^{-2}\;\mathrm{BM}$ (nearest integer). (Given atomic number of Cr is 24)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mathrm{CrO}$ is basic, $\mathrm{Cr_2O_3}$ is amphoteric and $\mathrm{CrO_3}$ is acidic. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Cr^{2+}}\;\left(d^4\right) \;=\; \sqrt{24} \;=\; 4.90$, $\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}\;\left(d^3\right) \;=\; \sqrt{15} \;=\; 3.87 \implies$ sum $\;=\; 8.77 \;=\; 877 \times 10^{-2}$
questions.topic: Nature of chromium oxides and magnetic moment

questions.text: Assertion A: In aqueous solution, $\text{Cr}^{2+}$ is reducing while $\text{Mn}^{3+}$ is oxidising in nature. Reason R: Extra stability to half-filled configuration is greater than that of incompletely filled configuration. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
A is true but R is false

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Check the configuration each ion reaches after losing or gaining one electron. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Cr}^{2+}\;(d^4)\;\to\;\text{Cr}^{3+}\;(d^3,\;t_{2g}^3)\;\text{and}\;\text{Mn}^{3+}\;(d^4)\;\to\;\text{Mn}^{2+}\;(d^5)\;\implies\;\text{A and R true, R explains A}$
questions.topic: Reducing and Oxidising Nature of Ions

questions.text: A first row transition metal with highest enthalpy of atomisation, upon reaction with oxygen at high temperature forms oxides of formula $\mathrm{M_2O_n}$ (where $n \;=\; 3,\,4,\,5$). The 'spin-only' magnetic moment value of the amphoteric oxide from the above oxides is ______ BM (near integer) (Given atomic number: Sc : 21, Ti : 22, V : 23, Cr : 24, Mn : 25, Fe : 26, Co : 27, Ni : 28, Cu : 29, Zn : 30)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: V has the highest enthalpy of atomisation ($515\;\mathrm{kJ/mol}$) and its amphoteric oxide is $\mathrm{V_2O_5}$. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{M} \;=\; \mathrm{V} \implies \mathrm{V_2O_5}$ amphoteric, $\mathrm{V^{5+}} \;=\; 3d^{0} \implies \mu \;=\; 0$
questions.topic: Enthalpy of atomisation and vanadium oxides

questions.text: Statement I: Fusion of $\text{MnO}_2$ with KOH in the presence of an oxidising agent gives dark green $\text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4$. Statement II: Manganate ion on electrolytic oxidation in alkaline medium gives permanganate ion. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.

options.text: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall the two-stage preparation of $\text{KMnO}_4$ from pyrolusite. // 📝 Solution: $2\text{MnO}_2\;+\;4\text{KOH}\;+\;\text{O}_2\;\to\;2\text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4\;+\;2\text{H}_2\text{O}\;\implies\;\text{MnO}_4^{2-}\;\xrightarrow{\text{electrolytic oxidation}}\;\text{MnO}_4^{-}\;\implies\;\text{both true}$

questions.text: The metal that shows highest and maximum number of oxidation state is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Mn in the 3d series reaches $+7$. // 📝 Solution: Mn shows oxidation states from $+2$ to $+7$ $\implies$ Mn

questions.text: In acidic medium, $\text{MnO}_4^{2-}$ undergoes disproportionation to give:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Mn(VI) simultaneously oxidises to Mn(VII) and reduces to the more stable Mn(IV). // 📝 Solution: $3\text{MnO}_4^{2-}\;+\;4\text{H}^{+}\;\to\;2\text{MnO}_4^{-}\;+\;\text{MnO}_2\;+\;2\text{H}_2\text{O}\;\implies\;\text{MnO}_4^{-}\;\text{and}\;\text{MnO}_2$

questions.text: The number of element from the following that do not belong to lanthanoids is $\mathrm{Eu}$, $\mathrm{Cm}$, $\mathrm{Er}$, $\mathrm{Tb}$, $\mathrm{Yb}$ and $\mathrm{Lu}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Lanthanoids are $\mathrm{Ce}$ to $\mathrm{Lu}$; $\mathrm{Cm}$ is in the actinoid series. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Eu},\,\mathrm{Er},\,\mathrm{Tb},\,\mathrm{Yb},\,\mathrm{Lu}$ are lanthanoids and only $\mathrm{Cm}$ is an actinoid $\implies 1$

questions.text: Identify the correct statements. A. Chromate ion is square planar. B. Dichromates are generally prepared from chromates. C. The green manganate ion is diamagnetic. D. Dark green $\text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4$ disproportionates in neutral or acidic medium to give permanganate. E. With increasing oxidation number of the transition metal, the ionic character of the oxides decreases. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Check the geometry of $\text{CrO}_4^{2-}$ and the number of unpaired electrons in $\text{MnO}_4^{2-}$ ($\text{Mn}^{6+}$). // 📝 Solution: $\text{CrO}_4^{2-}\;\text{is tetrahedral}\;\implies\;\text{A false};\;\text{MnO}_4^{2-}\;(d^1)\;\text{is paramagnetic}\;\implies\;\text{C false};\;\text{B, D, E true}$

questions.text: The spin-only magnetic moment value of $\left[\text{Ni}\left(\text{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{2+}$ is ___ $\times\;10^{-1}$ BM. (Given: atomic number of Ni is 28)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find the d-electron count of Ni in the complex and use $\mu\;=\;\sqrt{n\left(n+2\right)}$ BM. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Ni}^{2+}\;(3d^8)\;\implies\;n\;=\;2\;\implies\;\mu\;=\;\sqrt{8}\;=\;2.82\;\text{BM}\;=\;28.2\;\times\;10^{-1}\;\text{BM}\;\approx\;28\;\times\;10^{-1}\;\text{BM}$

questions.text: Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A) : $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ in water is more stable than $\mathrm{Cu^{+}}$. Reason (R) : Enthalpy of hydration for $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ is much less than that of $\mathrm{Cu^{+}}$. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $2\,\mathrm{Cu^+} \;\to\; \mathrm{Cu^{2+}} \;+\; \mathrm{Cu}$, so check the hydration enthalpy of $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta_{hyd}H$ of $\mathrm{Cu^{2+}}$ is much more negative than that of $\mathrm{Cu^+}$ and more than compensates the second ionisation enthalpy $\implies$ (A) and (R) correct and (R) explains (A)
questions.topic: Stability of Cu2+ in aqueous solution

questions.text: The fusion of chromite ore with sodium carbonate in the presence of air leads to the formation of products A and B along with the evolution of $\mathrm{CO_2}$. The sum of spin-only magnetic moment values of $A$ and $B$ is ______ B.M. (Nearest integer) [Given atomic number : C : 6, Na : 11, O : 8, Fe : 26, Cr : 24]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Write the chromite fusion reaction and find $d$-electron count of the metal in each product. // 📝 Solution: $4\,\mathrm{FeCr_2O_4} \;+\; 8\,\mathrm{Na_2CO_3} \;+\; 7\,\mathrm{O_2} \;\to\; 8\,\mathrm{Na_2CrO_4} \;+\; 2\,\mathrm{Fe_2O_3} \;+\; 8\,\mathrm{CO_2} \implies 0 \;+\; 5.9 \;\approx\; 6$
questions.topic: Chromite ore processing and magnetic moment

questions.text: $\text{NaCl}$ reacts with conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ and $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ to give reddish fumes (B), which react with NaOH to give a yellow solution (C). B and C, respectively, are:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: This is the chromyl chloride test for chloride ions. // 📝 Solution: $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7\;+\;4\text{NaCl}\;+\;6\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\;\to\;2\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2\;+\;\ldots\;\implies\;\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2\;+\;4\text{NaOH}\;\to\;\text{Na}_2\text{CrO}_4\;(\text{yellow})\;+\;2\text{NaCl}\;+\;2\text{H}_2\text{O}$

questions.text: During the borax bead test with $\mathrm{CuSO_4}$, a blue green colour of the bead was observed in oxidising flame due to the formation of
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: In oxidising flame, the metal oxide combines with $\mathrm{B_2O_3}$ to give the metaborate. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{CuSO_4} \;\xrightarrow{\Delta}\; \mathrm{CuO} \;+\; \mathrm{SO_3}$ and $\mathrm{CuO} \;+\; \mathrm{B_2O_3} \;\to\; \mathrm{Cu\left(BO_2\right)_2}$ (blue green)

questions.text: Choose the correct statements about Zn, Cd and Hg. A. They have high enthalpy of atomisation as the d subshell is full. B. Zn and Cd do not show variable oxidation state while Hg shows +I and +II. C. Compounds of Zn, Cd and Hg are paramagnetic in nature. D. Zn, Cd and Hg are called soft metals. Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Group 12 elements have a completely filled $d^{10}$ subshell, so weak metallic bonding and no unpaired electrons. // 📝 Solution: $\text{lowest enthalpy of atomisation}\;\implies\;\text{A false};\;d^{10}\;\implies\;\text{diamagnetic}\;\implies\;\text{C false};\;\text{B and D true}$

questions.text: Diamagnetic lanthanoid ions are:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Diamagnetism needs no unpaired electrons, so check the 4f configuration of each ion. // 📝 Solution: $\text{La}^{3+}\;(4f^0),\;\text{Ce}^{4+}\;(4f^0)\;\implies\;n\;=\;0\;\implies\;\text{diamagnetic};\;\text{Nd}^{3+}\;(4f^3),\;\text{Eu}^{3+}\;(4f^6)\;\text{paramagnetic}$

questions.text: The spin-only magnetic moment value of $\text{MO}_4^{2-}$ is ___ BM, where M is the metal having the lowest metallic radius among $\text{Sc}$, $\text{Ti}$, $\text{V}$, $\text{Cr}$, $\text{Mn}$ and $\text{Zn}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Metallic radius is smallest near the middle of the 3d series; find the oxidation state of M in $\text{MO}_4^{2-}$. // 📝 Solution: $\text{M}\;=\;\text{Cr}\;\implies\;\text{CrO}_4^{2-}:\;\text{Cr}^{6+}\;(3d^0)\;\implies\;n\;=\;0\;\implies\;\mu\;=\;0\;\text{BM}$

questions.text: The sum of the number of $d$ electrons in the ground state electronic configurations of $\mathrm{Nb}$ and $\mathrm{Ru}$ is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Both Nb and Ru are exceptions to the Aufbau filling order in the 4d series. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Nb}\;:\;\left[\mathrm{Kr}\right]4d^4\,5s^1$, $\mathrm{Ru}\;:\;\left[\mathrm{Kr}\right]4d^7\,5s^1 \;\implies\; 4 \;+\; 7 \;=\; 11$

questions.text: The potassium salts of chromium that are yellow in basic medium and orange in acidic medium are respectively
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Chromate and dichromate are interconverted by changing the pH. // 📝 Solution: $2\mathrm{CrO_4^{2-}} \;+\; 2\mathrm{H^+} \;\rightleftharpoons\; \mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}} \;+\; \mathrm{H_2O} \;\implies\;$ yellow $\mathrm{K_2CrO_4}$ in base, orange $\mathrm{K_2Cr_2O_7}$ in acid

questions.text: Cu(II) is $3d^9$ and Cu(I) is $3d^{10}$. Which of the following is correct?

options.text: Stability of Cu(I) and Cu(II) depends on the nature of the copper salts
Cu(I) and Cu(II) are equally stable

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Compare the large hydration enthalpy of $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ with the second ionisation enthalpy of Cu in aqueous medium. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta_{hyd}H\left(\text{Cu}^{2+}\right)\;\text{compensates}\;IE_2\;\implies\;\text{Cu}^{2+}\left(aq\right)\;\text{is more stable than}\;\text{Cu}^{+}\left(aq\right)$

questions.text: Which pair of lanthanoid ions has a half-filled $4f$ subshell?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Half-filled means $4f^7$ configuration. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Eu}\;\left[\mathrm{Xe}\right]4f^76s^2 \;\to\; \mathrm{Eu^{2+}}\;4f^7$ and $\mathrm{Gd}\;\left[\mathrm{Xe}\right]4f^75d^16s^2 \;\to\; \mathrm{Gd^{3+}}\;4f^7$ $\;\implies\;$ option C

questions.text: Potassium dichromate acts as a strong oxidizing agent in acidic solution. During this process, the oxidation state of chromium changes from
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Acidic dichromate is reduced to $\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}$. // 📝 Solution: $14\,\mathrm{H^+} \;+\; 6\,e^- \;+\; \mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}} \;\to\; 2\,\mathrm{Cr^{3+}} \;+\; 7\,\mathrm{H_2O} \implies +6 \;\to\; +3$

questions.text: While preparing crystals of Mohr's salt, dil $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ is added to a mixture of ferrous sulphate and ammonium sulphate, before dissolving this mixture in water, dil $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ is added here to :

options.text: prevent the hydrolysis of ferrous sulphate
prevent the hydrolysis of ammonium sulphate
increase the rate of formation of crystals

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ undergoes hydrolysis in water. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Fe^{2+}}$ hydrolyses in aqueous solution $\implies$ dilute $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ suppresses the hydrolysis of ferrous sulphate

questions.text: The element which shows only one oxidation state other than its elemental form is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Sc has only one stable ionic state. // 📝 Solution: Co, Ti and Ni show $+2$, $+3$, $+4$ states, but Sc shows only $+3 \implies$ Scandium

questions.text: The number of ions from the following that have the ability to liberate hydrogen from a dilute acid is _____. $\mathrm{Ti^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{Cr^{2+}}$ and $\mathrm{V^{2+}}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Strong reducing ions can reduce $\mathrm{H^+}$ to $\mathrm{H_2}$. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Ti^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{V^{2+}}$ and $\mathrm{Cr^{2+}}$ are strong reducing agents, e.g. $2\,\mathrm{Cr^{2+}} \;+\; 2\,\mathrm{H^+} \;\to\; 2\,\mathrm{Cr^{3+}} \;+\; \mathrm{H_2} \implies 3$

questions.text: The magnetic moment of a transition metal compound has been calculated to be $3.87\;\mathrm{B.M.}$ The metal ion is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Spin-only formula $\mu \;=\; \sqrt{n\left(n+2\right)}$ // 📝 Solution: $3.87 \;=\; \sqrt{15} \implies n \;=\; 3 \implies \mathrm{V^{2+}}\;\left(3d^{3}\right)$ while $\mathrm{Cr^{2+}} \;=\; 4.89$, $\mathrm{Mn^{2+}} \;=\; 5.92$, $\mathrm{Ti^{2+}} \;=\; 2.82\;\mathrm{BM}$
questions.topic: Magnetic moment of transition metal ions

questions.text: When $\mathrm{MnO_2}$ and $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ is added to a salt (A), the greenish yellow gas liberated as salt (A) is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Greenish yellow gas is $\mathrm{Cl_2}$, so the salt must be a chloride. // 📝 Solution: $2\,\mathrm{NH_4Cl} \;+\; \mathrm{MnO_2} \;+\; 2\,\mathrm{H_2SO_4} \;\xrightarrow{\Delta}\; \mathrm{MnSO_4} \;+\; \left(\mathrm{NH_4}\right)_2\mathrm{SO_4} \;+\; 2\,\mathrm{H_2O} \;+\; \mathrm{Cl_2}\uparrow$
questions.topic: Preparation and test of chlorine (MnO2 test)

questions.text: The number of moles of $\text{H}^{+}$ required by 1 mole of $\text{MnO}_4^{-}$ to oxidise oxalate ion to $\text{CO}_2$ is ___.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Balance the ionic equation in acidic medium and scale to 1 mole of $\text{MnO}_4^{-}$. // 📝 Solution: $2\text{MnO}_4^{-}\;+\;5\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-}\;+\;16\text{H}^{+}\;\to\;2\text{Mn}^{2+}\;+\;10\text{CO}_2\;+\;8\text{H}_2\text{O}\;\implies\;\dfrac{16}{2}\;=\;8$
questions.topic: Redox Titration of KMnO4 with Oxalate

questions.text: Number of species from the following in which the central atom uses $\text{sp}^2$ hybrid orbitals in its bonding is ___: $\text{NH}_3$, $\text{SO}_2$, $\text{SiO}_2$, $\text{BeCl}_2$, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_2$, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4$, $\text{BCl}_3$, $\text{HCHO}$, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_6$, $\text{BF}_3$, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\text{Cl}_2$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: sp² hybridisation corresponds to steric number 3 (bond pairs plus lone pairs on the central atom). // 📝 Solution: $\text{SO}_2,\;\text{C}_2\text{H}_4,\;\text{BCl}_3,\;\text{HCHO},\;\text{C}_6\text{H}_6,\;\text{BF}_3\;\implies\;\text{sp}^2\;\implies\;6$

questions.text: Choose the correct option for free expansion of an ideal gas under adiabatic condition from the following :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: In free expansion, external pressure $P_{\text{ext}} \;=\; 0$, and in an adiabatic process, $q \;=\; 0$. // 📝 Solution: Since $P_{\text{ext}} \;=\; 0 \;\implies\; w \;=\; 0$, and for an adiabatic process $q \;=\; 0 \;\implies\; \Delta U \;=\; q \;+\; w \;=\; 0 \;\implies\; \Delta T \;=\; 0$ for an ideal gas.

questions.text: Combustion of $1\;\text{mole}$ of benzene is expressed at $\text{C}_6\text{H}_6\left(\text{l}\right) \;+\; \frac{15}{2}\text{O}_2\left(\text{g}\right) \;\to\; 6\text{CO}_2\left(\text{g}\right) \;+\; 3\text{H}_2\text{O}\left(\text{l}\right)$. The standard enthalpy of combustion of $2\;\text{mol}$ of benzene is $-'x'\;\text{kJ}$. $x \;=\;$ ______. Given: 1. standard Enthalpy of formation of $1\;\text{mol}$ of $\text{C}_6\text{H}_6\left(\text{l}\right)$, for the reaction $6\text{C}\left(\text{graphite}\right) \;+\; 3\text{H}_2\left(\text{g}\right) \;\to\; \text{C}_6\text{H}_6\left(\text{l}\right)$ is $48.5\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. 2. Standard Enthalpy of formation of $1\;\text{mol}$ of $\text{CO}_2\left(\text{g}\right)$, for the reaction $\text{C}\left(\text{graphite}\right) \;+\; \text{O}_2\left(\text{g}\right) \;\to\; \text{CO}_2\left(\text{g}\right)$ is $-393.5\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. 3. Standard and Enthalpy of formation of $1\;\text{mol}$ of $\text{H}_2\text{O}\left(\text{l}\right)$, for the reaction $\text{H}_2\left(\text{g}\right) \;+\; \frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2\left(\text{g}\right) \;\to\; \text{H}_2\text{O}\left(\text{l}\right)$ is $-286\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Calculate $\Delta_c H^\circ$ for $1\;\text{mol}$ of $\text{C}_6\text{H}_6\left(\text{l}\right)$ using $\Delta_c H^\circ \;=\; 6\Delta_f H^\circ\left(\text{CO}_2\right) \;+\; 3\Delta_f H^\circ\left(\text{H}_2\text{O}\right) \;-\; \Delta_f H^\circ\left(\text{C}_6\text{H}_6\right)$, then multiply by $2$. // 📝 Solution: For $1\;\text{mol}$, $\Delta_c H^\circ \;=\; 6\left(-393.5\right) \;+\; 3\left(-286\right) \;-\; 48.5 \;=\; -3267.5\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1} \;\implies\; \text{for } 2\;\text{mol}, \; \Delta H \;=\; 2 \;\times\; \left(-3267.5\right) \;=\; -6535\;\text{kJ} \;\implies\; x \;=\; 6535$.

questions.text: When $\Delta H_{\text{vap}} \;=\; 30\;\text{kJ/mol}$ and $\Delta S_{\text{vap}} \;=\; 75\;\text{J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$, then the temperature of vapour, at one atmosphere is ______ $\text{K}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: At phase equilibrium (boiling at $1\;\text{atm}$), $\Delta G_{\text{vap}} \;=\; 0 \;\implies\; T \;=\; \frac{\Delta H_{\text{vap}}}{\Delta S_{\text{vap}}}$. // 📝 Solution: $T \;=\; \frac{30 \;\times\; 1000\;\text{J mol}^{-1}}{75\;\text{J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}} \;=\; 400\;\text{K}$.

questions.text: Which of the following properties will change when the system containing solution 1 becomes solution 2? [FIGURE: 10 mol solute x in 10 L water to 1 L of solution 1 + 1 mol solute x + 1 L water]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Intensive properties depend only on composition; extensive properties depend on amount present // 📝 Solution: Both systems have the same composition $\implies$ molar heat capacity, density and concentration (intensive) remain same $\implies$ Gibbs free energy (extensive) changes $\implies$ option (4)
questions.topic: Intensive vs extensive properties of solutions

questions.text: [FIGURE] Consider the figure provided. $1\;\text{mol}$ of an ideal gas is kept in a cylinder, fitted with a piston, at the position A, at $18^\circ\text{C}$. If the piston is moved to position B, keeping the temperature unchanged, then $'x'\;\text{L atm}$ work is done in this reversible process. $x \;=\;$ ______ $\text{L atm}$. (nearest integer) [Given : Absolute temperature $= \;^\circ\text{C} \;+\; 273.15, \; R \;=\; 0.08206\;\text{L atm mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For a reversible isothermal expansion from $V_1 \;=\; 10\;\text{L}$ to $V_2 \;=\; 10 \;+\; 90 \;=\; 100\;\text{L}$, $w \;=\; -nRT\ln\left(\frac{V_2}{V_1}\right)$. // 📝 Solution: $w \;=\; -1 \;\times\; 0.08206 \;\times\; 291.15 \;\times\; \ln\left(\frac{100}{10}\right) \;=\; -55.01\;\text{L atm} \;\implies\; \left\lvert w \right\rvert \;\approx\; 55\;\text{L atm}$.

questions.text: $1\;\text{mole}$ of ideal gas is allowed to expand reversibly and adiabatically from a temperature of $27^\circ\text{C}$. The work done is $3\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. The final temperature of the gas is ______ $\text{K}$ (Nearest integer). Given $C_V \;=\; 20\;\text{J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For an adiabatic process, $q \;=\; 0$, so $\Delta U \;=\; w \;=\; n C_V \left(T_2 \;-\; T_1\right)$. // 📝 Solution: Since expansion work is done by the gas, $w \;=\; -3000\;\text{J} \;\implies\; 1 \;\times\; 20 \;\times\; \left(T_2 \;-\; 300\right) \;=\; -3000 \;\implies\; T_2 \;-\; 300 \;=\; -150 \;\implies\; T_2 \;=\; 150\;\text{K}$.

questions.text: Three moles of an ideal gas are compressed isothermally from $60\;\text{L}$ to $20\;\text{L}$ using constant pressure of $5\;\text{atm}$. Heat exchange $Q$ for the compression is $-$ ______ $\text{Lit. atm}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For an isothermal process of an ideal gas, $\Delta U \;=\; 0 \;\implies\; Q \;=\; -W \;=\; P_{\text{ext}}\left(V_2 \;-\; V_1\right)$. // 📝 Solution: $Q \;=\; 5 \;\times\; \left(20 \;-\; 60\right) \;=\; -200\;\text{L atm}$, so the magnitude is $200\;\text{L atm}$.

questions.text: For a certain thermochemical reaction $\text{M} \;\to\; \text{N}$ at $T \;=\; 400\;\text{K}, \; \Delta H^\ominus \;=\; 77.2\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}, \; \Delta S \;=\; 122\;\text{J K}^{-1}$, $\log$ equilibrium constant $\left(\log K\right)$ is $-$ ______ $\times\; 10^{-1}$.

Given below are two statements : One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A) : Enthalpy of neutralisation of strong monobasic acid with strong monoacidic base is always $-57\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. Reason (R) : Enthalpy of neutralisation is the amount of heat liberated when one mole of $\text{H}^+$ ions furnished by acid combine with one mole of $\text{OH}^-$ ions furnished by base to form one mole of water. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Strong acids and strong bases are completely ionized in dilute aqueous solutions. // 📝 Solution: The net neutralization reaction between any strong monobasic acid and strong monoacidic base is $\text{H}^+\left(\text{aq}\right) \;+\; \text{OH}^-\left(\text{aq}\right) \;\to\; \text{H}_2\text{O}\left(\text{l}\right)$ with $\Delta H \;=\; -57\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$; hence both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

questions.text: Match the LIST-I (Thermodynamic Process) with LIST-II (Magnitude in $\text{kJ}$): A. Work done in reversible, isothermal expansion of $2\;\text{mol}$ ideal gas from $2\;\text{dm}^3$ to $20\;\text{dm}^3$ at $300\;\text{K}$; B. Work done in irreversible isothermal expansion of $1\;\text{mol}$ ideal gas from $1\;\text{m}^3$ to $3\;\text{m}^3$ at $300\;\text{K}$ against constant pressure $3\;\text{kPa}$; C. Change in internal energy for adiabatic expansion of $1\;\text{mol}$ ideal gas, $\Delta T \;=\; 320\;\text{K}, \; \bar{C}_V \;=\; \frac{3}{2}R$; D. Change in enthalpy at constant pressure of $1\;\text{mol}$ ideal gas, $\Delta T \;=\; 337\;\text{K}, \; \bar{C}_P \;=\; \frac{5}{2}R$. List-II: I. $4$, II. $11.5$, III. $6$, IV. $7$. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $\left\lvert w_{\text{rev}} \right\rvert \;=\; 2.303 nRT \log_{10}\left(\frac{V_2}{V_1}\right)$, $\left\lvert w_{\text{irrev}} \right\rvert \;=\; P_{\text{ext}}\Delta V$, $\left\lvert \Delta U \right\rvert \;=\; n\bar{C}_V\left\lvert \Delta T \right\rvert$, and $\left\lvert \Delta H \right\rvert \;=\; n\bar{C}_P\left\lvert \Delta T \right\rvert$. // 📝 Solution: A: $\left\lvert w \right\rvert \;=\; 2 \;\times\; 8.314 \;\times\; 300 \;\times\; 2.303 \log_{10}\left(10\right) \;\approx\; 11.5\;\text{kJ}$ (II); B: $\left\lvert w \right\rvert \;=\; 3\;\text{kPa} \;\times\; \left(3 \;-\; 1\right)\;\text{m}^3 \;=\; 6\;\text{kJ}$ (III); C: $\left\lvert \Delta U \right\rvert \;=\; 1 \;\times\; \frac{3}{2} \;\times\; 8.314 \;\times\; 320 \;\approx\; 4\;\text{kJ}$ (I); D: $\left\lvert \Delta H \right\rvert \;=\; 1 \;\times\; \frac{5}{2} \;\times\; 8.314 \;\times\; 337 \;\approx\; 7\;\text{kJ}$ (IV).

questions.text: When $2\;\text{litre}$ of ideal gas expands isothermally into vacuum to a total volume of $6\;\text{litre}$, the change in internal energy is ______ $\text{J}$. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Internal energy of an ideal gas is a function of temperature only: $U \;=\; f\left(T\right)$. // 📝 Solution: Since the expansion of the ideal gas is isothermal ($\Delta T \;=\; 0$), the change in internal energy is $\Delta U \;=\; n C_V \Delta T \;=\; 0\;\text{J}$.

questions.text: The enthalpy of formation of ethane $\left(\text{C}_2\text{H}_6\right)$ from ethylene by addition of hydrogen where the bond-energies of $\text{C}-\text{H}, \; \text{C}-\text{C}, \; \text{C}=\text{C}, \; \text{H}-\text{H}$ are $414\;\text{kJ}, \; 347\;\text{kJ}, \; 615\;\text{kJ}$ and $435\;\text{kJ}$ respectively is $-$ ______ $\text{kJ}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\left(\text{g}\right) \;+\; \text{H}_2\left(\text{g}\right) \;\to\; \text{C}_2\text{H}_6\left(\text{g}\right)$, $\Delta H \;=\; \sum \text{BE}_{\text{reactants}} \;-\; \sum \text{BE}_{\text{products}}$. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta H \;=\; \text{BE}\left(\text{C}=\text{C}\right) \;+\; \text{BE}\left(\text{H}-\text{H}\right) \;-\; \text{BE}\left(\text{C}-\text{C}\right) \;-\; 2\text{BE}\left(\text{C}-\text{H}\right) \;\implies\; \Delta H \;=\; 615 \;+\; 435 \;-\; 347 \;-\; 2 \;\times\; 414 \;=\; -125\;\text{kJ}$.

questions.text: Given: $\Delta H^\circ_{\mathrm{sub}}[\mathrm{C(graphite)}] = 710\;\mathrm{kJ\;mol^{-1}}$, $\Delta H^\circ_{\mathrm{C-H}} = 414\;\mathrm{kJ\;mol^{-1}}$, $\Delta H^\circ_{\mathrm{H-H}} = 436\;\mathrm{kJ\;mol^{-1}}$, $\Delta H^\circ_{\mathrm{C=C}} = 611\;\mathrm{kJ\;mol^{-1}}$. The $\Delta H^\circ_f$ of $\mathrm{CH_2=CH_2}$ is ______ $\mathrm{kJ\;mol^{-1}}$ (nearest integer).
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\Delta H_f = \sum \text{bonds broken} - \sum \text{bonds formed}$, including atomisation of carbon // 📝 Solution: $\Delta H_f = 2(710) + 2(436) - 611 - 4(414) = 1420 + 872 - 611 - 1656 = 25\;\mathrm{kJ\;mol^{-1}}$
questions.topic: Bond enthalpy and enthalpy of formation

questions.text: Which of the following is not correct?

options.text: $\Delta G$ is negative for a spontaneous reaction
$\Delta G$ is positive for a spontaneous reaction
$\Delta G$ is zero for a reversible reaction
$\Delta G$ is positive for a non-spontaneous reaction

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall the Gibbs free energy criteria for spontaneity at constant temperature and pressure. // 📝 Solution: At constant $T$ and $P$, a reaction is spontaneous when $\Delta G \;<\; 0$ and non-spontaneous when $\Delta G \;>\; 0$; hence stating $\Delta G$ is positive for a spontaneous reaction is incorrect.

questions.text: If the enthalpy of sublimation of $\text{Li}$ is $155\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, enthalpy of dissociation of $\text{F}_2$ is $150\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, ionization enthalpy of $\text{Li}$ is $520\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, electron gain enthalpy of $\text{F}$ is $-313\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, standard enthalpy of formation of $\text{LiF}$ is $-594\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. The magnitude of lattice enthalpy of $\text{LiF}$ is ______ $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. (Nearest Integer)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Apply the Born-Haber cycle for $\text{LiF}\left(\text{s}\right)$: $\Delta_f H^\circ \;=\; \Delta_{\text{sub}} H^\circ \;+\; \frac{1}{2}\Delta_{\text{diss}} H^\circ \;+\; \Delta_{\text{i}} H^\circ \;+\; \Delta_{\text{eg}} H^\circ \;-\; U_{\text{lattice}}$. // 📝 Solution: $-594 \;=\; 155 \;+\; \frac{1}{2}\left(150\right) \;+\; 520 \;+\; \left(-313\right) \;-\; U_{\text{lattice}} \;\implies\; -594 \;=\; 437 \;-\; U_{\text{lattice}} \;\implies\; U_{\text{lattice}} \;=\; 437 \;+\; 594 \;=\; 1031\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$.

questions.text: The enthalpy change for the conversion of $\frac{1}{2}\text{Cl}_2\left(\text{g}\right)$ to $\text{Cl}^-\left(\text{aq}\right)$ is $\left(-\right)$ ______ $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ (Nearest integer). Given : $\Delta_{\text{dis}} H^\circ_{\text{Cl}_2\left(\text{g}\right)} \;=\; 240\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}, \; \Delta_{\text{eg}} H^\circ_{\text{Cl}\left(\text{g}\right)} \;=\; -350\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}, \; \Delta_{\text{hyd}} H^\circ_{\text{Cl}^-\left(\text{g}\right)} \;=\; -380\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Apply Hess's law for the sequence $\frac{1}{2}\text{Cl}_2\left(\text{g}\right) \;\to\; \text{Cl}\left(\text{g}\right) \;\to\; \text{Cl}^-\left(\text{g}\right) \;\to\; \text{Cl}^-\left(\text{aq}\right)$. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta H^\circ \;=\; \frac{1}{2}\Delta_{\text{dis}} H^\circ \;+\; \Delta_{\text{eg}} H^\circ \;+\; \Delta_{\text{hyd}} H^\circ \;\implies\; \Delta H^\circ \;=\; \frac{1}{2}\left(240\right) \;+\; \left(-350\right) \;+\; \left(-380\right) \;=\; -610\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$.

questions.text: The heat of combustion of solid benzoic acid at constant volume is $-321.30\;\text{kJ}$ at $27^\circ\text{C}$. The heat of combustion at constant pressure is $\left(-321.30 \;-\; x R\right)\;\text{kJ}$, the value of $x$ is _______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $\Delta H \;=\; \Delta U \;+\; \Delta n_g R T$ for the combustion of $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOH}\left(\text{s}\right)$. // 📝 Solution: For $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOH}\left(\text{s}\right) \;+\; \frac{15}{2}\text{O}_2\left(\text{g}\right) \;\to\; 7\text{CO}_2\left(\text{g}\right) \;+\; 3\text{H}_2\text{O}\left(\text{l}\right)$, $\Delta n_g \;=\; 7 \;-\; \frac{15}{2} \;=\; -\frac{1}{2} \;\implies\; \Delta H \;=\; -321.30 \;-\; \frac{1}{2} \;\times\; 300 R \;=\; \left(-321.30 \;-\; 150 R\right)\;\text{kJ} \;\implies\; x \;=\; 150$.
questions.topic: Relation Between Delta H and Delta U

questions.text: An ideal gas, $\bar{C}_V \;=\; \frac{5}{2}R$, is expanded adiabatically against a constant pressure of $1\;\text{atm}$ until it doubles in volume. If the initial temperature and pressure is $298\;\text{K}$ and $5\;\text{atm}$, respectively then the final temperature is _______ $\text{K}$ (nearest integer). [$\bar{C}_V$ is the molar heat capacity at constant volume]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For an irreversible adiabatic expansion, $\Delta U \;=\; w \;\implies\; n\bar{C}_V\left(T_2 \;-\; T_1\right) \;=\; -P_{\text{ext}}\left(V_2 \;-\; V_1\right)$. // 📝 Solution: Since $V_2 \;=\; 2V_1$, $n \;\times\; \frac{5}{2}R\left(T_2 \;-\; T_1\right) \;=\; -P_{\text{ext}}\left(2V_1 \;-\; V_1\right) \;=\; -P_{\text{ext}}\left(\frac{nRT_1}{P_1}\right) \;\implies\; \frac{5}{2}\left(T_2 \;-\; 298\right) \;=\; -1 \;\times\; \frac{298}{5} \;\implies\; T_2 \;=\; 274.16\;\text{K} \;\approx\; 274\;\text{K}$.

questions.text: One mole of an ideal gas expands isothermally and reversibly from $10\;\mathrm{dm^3}$ to $20\;\mathrm{dm^3}$ at $300\;\mathrm{K}$. $\Delta U$, $q$ and work done $w$ respectively are: Given $R = 8.3\;\mathrm{J\;K^{-1}\;mol^{-1}}$, $\ln 10 = 2.3$, $\log 2 = 0.30$, $\log 3 = 0.48$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For isothermal ideal gas, $\Delta U = 0$ and $w = -nRT\ln(V_2/V_1)$, with $q = -w$ // 📝 Solution: $\Delta U = 0$ $\implies$ $w = -(1)(8.3)(300)\ln 2 \approx -1718\;\mathrm{J} = -1.718\;\mathrm{kJ}$ $\implies$ $q = +1.718\;\mathrm{kJ}$
questions.topic: Isothermal reversible expansion of ideal gas

questions.text: $28.0\;\text{L}$ of $\text{CO}_2$ is produced on complete combustion of $16.8\;\text{L}$ gaseous mixture of ethene and methane at $25^\circ\text{C}$ and $1\;\text{atm}$. Heat evolved during the combustion process is ______ $\text{kJ}$. Given : $\Delta H_{\text{c}}\left(\text{CH}_4\right) \;=\; -900\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}, \; \Delta H_{\text{c}}\left(\text{C}_2\text{H}_4\right) \;=\; -1400\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use stoichiometry of $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4 \;+\; 3\text{O}_2 \;\to\; 2\text{CO}_2 \;+\; 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{CH}_4 \;+\; 2\text{O}_2 \;\to\; \text{CO}_2 \;+\; 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$ to find volumes of gases. // 📝 Solution: Let volume of $\text{C}_2\text{H}_4 \;=\; x\;\text{L}$, then $2x \;+\; \left(16.8 \;-\; x\right) \;=\; 28 \;\implies\; x \;=\; 11.2\;\text{L}$ and $V_{\text{CH}_4} \;=\; 5.6\;\text{L}$. Taking molar volume $= 22.4\;\text{L}$, $n_{\text{C}_2\text{H}_4} \;=\; 0.5\;\text{mol}, \; n_{\text{CH}_4} \;=\; 0.25\;\text{mol} \;\implies\; \text{Heat evolved} \;=\; 0.5 \;\times\; 1400 \;+\; 0.25 \;\times\; 900 \;=\; 925\;\text{kJ}$ (or $847.3\;\text{kJ}$ using $RT \;=\; 24.46\;\text{L atm mol}^{-1}$).

questions.text: Two reactions are given below: $2\text{Fe}_{\left(\text{s}\right)} \;+\; \frac{3}{2}\text{O}_{2\left(\text{g}\right)} \;\to\; \text{Fe}_2\text{O}_{3\left(\text{s}\right)}, \; \Delta H^\circ \;=\; -822\;\text{kJ/mol}$; $\text{C}_{\left(\text{s}\right)} \;+\; \frac{1}{2}\text{O}_{2\left(\text{g}\right)} \;\to\; \text{CO}_{\left(\text{g}\right)}, \; \Delta H^\circ \;=\; -110\;\text{kJ/mol}$. Then enthalpy change for following reaction $3\text{C}_{\left(\text{s}\right)} \;+\; \text{Fe}_2\text{O}_{3\left(\text{s}\right)} \;\to\; 2\text{Fe}_{\left(\text{s}\right)} \;+\; 3\text{CO}_{\left(\text{g}\right)}$ is ______ $\text{kJ/mol}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Apply Hess's law by multiplying the second reaction by $3$ and subtracting the first reaction. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta H^\circ \;=\; 3\Delta H_2^\circ \;-\; \Delta H_1^\circ \;=\; 3\left(-110\right) \;-\; \left(-822\right) \;=\; -330 \;+\; 822 \;=\; 492\;\text{kJ/mol}$.

questions.text: Use the following data : For $\text{AB}\left(\text{g}\right)$: $\Delta_f H^\ominus\left(500\;\text{K}\right) \;=\; 32\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}, \; S^\ominus\left(500\;\text{K}\right) \;=\; 222\;\text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$; For $\text{A}_2\left(\text{g}\right)$: $\Delta_f H^\ominus\left(500\;\text{K}\right) \;=\; 6\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}, \; S^\ominus\left(500\;\text{K}\right) \;=\; 146\;\text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$; For $\text{B}_2\left(\text{g}\right)$: $\Delta_f H^\ominus\left(500\;\text{K}\right) \;=\; x\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}, \; S^\ominus\left(500\;\text{K}\right) \;=\; 280\;\text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$.
