One mole each of $\text{A}_2\left(\text{g}\right)$ and $\text{B}_2\left(\text{g}\right)$ are taken in a $1\;\text{L}$ closed flask and allowed to establish the equilibrium at $500\;\text{K}$. $\text{A}_2\left(\text{g}\right) \;+\; \text{B}_2\left(\text{g}\right) \;\rightleftharpoons\; 2\text{AB}\left(\text{g}\right)$. The value of $x$ (in $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$) is ______. (Nearest integer) (Given : $\log K \;=\; 2.2, \; R \;=\; 8.3\;\text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $\Delta_r G^\ominus \;=\; -2.303 R T \log_{10} K$ and $\Delta_r G^\ominus \;=\; \Delta_r H^\ominus \;-\; T\Delta_r S^\ominus$. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta_r G^\ominus \;=\; -2.303 \;\times\; 8.3 \;\times\; 500 \;\times\; 2.2 \;=\; -21.03\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, $\Delta_r S^\ominus \;=\; 2\left(222\right) \;-\; \left(146 \;+\; 280\right) \;=\; 18\;\text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$, and $\Delta_r H^\ominus \;=\; 2\left(32\right) \;-\; \left(6 \;+\; x\right) \;=\; 58 \;-\; x \;\implies\; -21.03 \;=\; \left(58 \;-\; x\right) \;-\; 500\left(0.018\right) \;\implies\; x \;=\; 70.03 \;\approx\; 70\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$.

questions.text: Consider the following reaction at $298\;\text{K}$. $\frac{3}{2}\text{O}_{2\left(\text{g}\right)} \;\rightleftharpoons\; \text{O}_{3\left(\text{g}\right)}, \; K_{\text{P}} \;=\; 2.47 \;\times\; 10^{-29}$. $\Delta_r G^\ominus$ for the reaction is ______ $\text{kJ}$. (Given $R \;=\; 8.314\;\text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use the standard Gibbs energy relation $\Delta_r G^\ominus \;=\; -R T \ln K_{\text{P}}$. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta_r G^\ominus \;=\; -8.314 \;\times\; 10^{-3}\;\text{kJ K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1} \;\times\; 298\;\text{K} \;\times\; \ln\left(2.47 \;\times\; 10^{-29}\right) \;\implies\; \Delta_r G^\ominus \;=\; -2.4776 \;\times\; \left(-65.87\right) \;=\; 163.19\;\text{kJ} \;\approx\; 163\;\text{kJ}$.

questions.text: Enthalpies of formation of $\text{CCl}_4\left(\text{g}\right), \; \text{H}_2\text{O}\left(\text{g}\right), \; \text{CO}_2\left(\text{g}\right)$ and $\text{HCl}\left(\text{g}\right)$ are $-105, \; -242, \; -394$ and $-92\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ respectively. The magnitude of enthalpy of the reaction given below is ______ $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ (nearest integer) $\text{CCl}_4\left(\text{g}\right) \;+\; 2\text{H}_2\text{O}\left(\text{g}\right) \;\to\; \text{CO}_2\left(\text{g}\right) \;+\; 4\text{HCl}\left(\text{g}\right)$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $\Delta_r H^\circ \;=\; \sum \Delta_f H^\circ\left(\text{products}\right) \;-\; \sum \Delta_f H^\circ\left(\text{reactants}\right)$. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta_r H^\circ \;=\; \left[-394 \;+\; 4\left(-92\right)\right] \;-\; \left[-105 \;+\; 2\left(-242\right)\right] \;=\; -762 \;-\; \left(-589\right) \;=\; -173\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1} \;\implies\; \left\lvert \Delta_r H^\circ \right\rvert \;=\; 173\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$.

questions.text: $20.0\;\text{dm}^3$ of an ideal gas $'X'$ at $600\;\text{K}$ and $0.5\;\text{MPa}$ undergoes isothermal reversible expansion until pressure of the gas is $0.2\;\text{MPa}$. Which of the following option is correct? (Given: $\log 2 \;=\; 0.3010$ and $\log 5 \;=\; 0.6989$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For an isothermal reversible expansion of an ideal gas, $\Delta U \;=\; \Delta H \;=\; 0$ and $w \;=\; -2.303 P_1 V_1 \log_{10}\left(\frac{P_1}{P_2}\right)$. // 📝 Solution: $w \;=\; -2.303 \;\times\; \left(0.5 \;\times\; 10^6\;\text{Pa}\right) \;\times\; \left(20 \;\times\; 10^{-3}\;\text{m}^3\right) \;\times\; \log_{10}\left(\frac{0.5}{0.2}\right) \;=\; -23030 \;\times\; \left(0.6989 \;-\; 0.3010\right) \;\approx\; -9.16\;\text{kJ} \;\approx\; -9.1\;\text{kJ}$ and $q \;=\; -w \;=\; 9.1\;\text{kJ}$.

questions.text: Standard enthalpy of vapourisation for $\text{CCl}_4$ is $30.5\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. Heat required for vapourisation of $284\;\text{g}$ of $\text{CCl}_4$ at constant temperature is _______ $\text{kJ}$. (Given molar mass in $\text{g mol}^{-1}$; $\text{C} \;=\; 12, \; \text{Cl} \;=\; 35.5$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find the number of moles of $\text{CCl}_4$ and multiply by $\Delta_{\text{vap}} H^\circ$. // 📝 Solution: Molar mass of $\text{CCl}_4 \;=\; 12 \;+\; 4 \;\times\; 35.5 \;=\; 154\;\text{g mol}^{-1} \;\implies\; n \;=\; \frac{284}{154} \;=\; 1.844\;\text{mol} \;\implies\; q \;=\; 1.844 \;\times\; 30.5 \;=\; 56.24\;\text{kJ} \;\approx\; 56\;\text{kJ}$.

questions.text: Consider the following data: $\Delta_f H^\ominus\left(\text{methane, g}\right) \;=\; -X\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, Enthalpy of sublimation of graphite $= Y\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, Dissociation enthalpy of $\text{H}_2 \;=\; Z\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. The bond enthalpy of $\text{C}-\text{H}$ bond is given by :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For $\text{C}\left(\text{graphite}\right) \;+\; 2\text{H}_2\left(\text{g}\right) \;\to\; \text{CH}_4\left(\text{g}\right)$, $\Delta_f H^\ominus \;=\; \Delta_{\text{sub}} H^\ominus\left(\text{C}\right) \;+\; 2\Delta_{\text{diss}} H^\ominus\left(\text{H}_2\right) \;-\; 4\text{BE}\left(\text{C}-\text{H}\right)$. // 📝 Solution: $-X \;=\; Y \;+\; 2Z \;-\; 4\text{BE}\left(\text{C}-\text{H}\right) \;\implies\; 4\text{BE}\left(\text{C}-\text{H}\right) \;=\; X \;+\; Y \;+\; 2Z \;\implies\; \text{BE}\left(\text{C}-\text{H}\right) \;=\; \frac{X \;+\; Y \;+\; 2Z}{4}$.

questions.text: If three moles of an ideal gas at $300\;\text{K}$ expand isothermally from $30\;\text{dm}^3$ to $45\;\text{dm}^3$ against a constant opposing pressure of $80\;\text{kPa}$, then the amount of heat transferred is ______ $\text{J}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For an isothermal expansion of an ideal gas, $\Delta U \;=\; 0 \;\implies\; q \;=\; -w \;=\; P_{\text{ext}}\left(V_2 \;-\; V_1\right)$. // 📝 Solution: $w \;=\; -80 \;\times\; 10^3\;\text{Pa} \;\times\; \left(45 \;-\; 30\right) \;\times\; 10^{-3}\;\text{m}^3 \;=\; -1200\;\text{J} \;\implies\; q \;=\; -w \;=\; 1200\;\text{J}$.

questions.text: For a certain reaction at $300\;\text{K}, \; K \;=\; 10$, then $\Delta G^\circ$ for the same reaction is $-$ ______ $\times\; 10^{-1}\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. (Given $R \;=\; 8.314\;\text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use the relation $\Delta G^\circ \;=\; -2.303 R T \log_{10} K$. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta G^\circ \;=\; -2.303 \;\times\; 8.314 \;\times\; 300 \;\times\; \log_{10}\left(10\right) \;=\; -5744.14\;\text{J mol}^{-1} \;=\; -57.44 \;\times\; 10^{-1}\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1} \;\implies\; 57$.

questions.text: Consider the two different first order reactions given below $\text{A} \;+\; \text{B} \;\to\; \text{C}$ (Reaction 1), $\text{P} \;\to\; \text{Q}$ (Reaction 2). The ratio of the half life of Reaction 1 : Reaction 2 is $5 : 2$. If $t_1$ and $t_2$ represent the time taken to complete $2/3^{\text{rd}}$ and $4/5^{\text{th}}$ of Reaction 1 and Reaction 2, respectively, then the value of the ratio $t_1 : t_2$ is ______ $\times\; 10^{-1}$ (nearest integer). [Given : $\log_{10}\left(3\right) \;=\; 0.477$ and $\log_{10}\left(5\right) \;=\; 0.699$]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For a first-order reaction, $t \;=\; \frac{t_{1/2}}{\log_{10} 2}\log_{10}\left(\frac{1}{1 \;-\; f}\right)$ where $f$ is the fraction completed. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{\left(t_{1/2}\right)_1}{\left(t_{1/2}\right)_2} \;=\; \frac{k_2}{k_1} \;=\; \frac{5}{2}$, $k_1 t_1 \;=\; \ln\left(\frac{1}{1 \;-\; 2/3}\right) \;=\; \ln 3$ and $k_2 t_2 \;=\; \ln\left(\frac{1}{1 \;-\; 4/5}\right) \;=\; \ln 5 \;\implies\; \frac{t_1}{t_2} \;=\; \frac{k_2}{k_1} \;\times\; \frac{\log_{10} 3}{\log_{10} 5} \;=\; \frac{5}{2} \;\times\; \frac{0.477}{0.699} \;=\; 1.7 \;=\; 17 \;\times\; 10^{-1}$.

questions.text: If $5\;\text{moles}$ of an ideal gas expands from $10\;\text{L}$ to a volume of $100\;\text{L}$ at $300\;\text{K}$ under isothermal and reversible condition then work, $w$, is $-x\;\text{J}$. The value of $x$ is _______. (Given $R \;=\; 8.314\;\text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For an isothermal reversible expansion of an ideal gas, $w \;=\; -2.303 n R T \log_{10}\left(\frac{V_2}{V_1}\right)$. // 📝 Solution: $w \;=\; -2.303 \;\times\; 5 \;\times\; 8.314 \;\times\; 300 \;\times\; \log_{10}\left(\frac{100}{10}\right) \;=\; -28720.7\;\text{J} \;\approx\; -28721\;\text{J} \;\implies\; x \;=\; 28721$.

questions.text: $\text{A} \;\to\; \text{D}$ is an endothermic reaction occurring in three steps (elementary). (i) $\text{A} \;\to\; \text{B}, \; \Delta H_{\text{i}} \;=\; +\text{ve}$ (ii) $\text{B} \;\to\; \text{C}, \; \Delta H_{\text{ii}} \;=\; -\text{ve}$ (iii) $\text{C} \;\to\; \text{D}, \; \Delta H_{\text{iii}} \;=\; -\text{ve}$. Which of the following graphs between potential energy ($y$-axis) vs reaction coordinate ($x$-axis) correctly represents the reaction profile of $\text{A} \;\to\; \text{D}$ ?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Compare the potential energy levels of intermediates $\text{B}, \; \text{C}$ and product $\text{D}$ relative to reactant $\text{A}$. // 📝 Solution: Since $\Delta H_{\text{i}} \;>\; 0, \; \Delta H_{\text{ii}} \;<\; 0, \; \Delta H_{\text{iii}} \;<\; 0$ and the overall reaction $\text{A} \;\to\; \text{D}$ is endothermic ($\Delta H_{\text{overall}} \;>\; 0$), the potential energy order must satisfy $E_{\text{B}} \;>\; E_{\text{C}} \;>\; E_{\text{D}} \;>\; E_{\text{A}}$ with three transition-state peaks, which is shown in graph (1).

questions.text: A perfect gas having $\overline{C}_v = 1.50R$ (independent of temperature) undergoes the transformation from point 1 to point 4 as shown in the P–V diagram. If each step is reversible, the total work done ($w$) from point 1 to point 4 is $(-)$ ______ J (nearest integer). Given $R = 0.082\;\mathrm{L\;atm\;K^{-1}\;mol^{-1}}$. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Isochoric steps do no work; only the isobaric step contributes $w = -P\Delta V$ // 📝 Solution: $w_{1\to2} = 0$, $w_{2\to3} = -3\;\mathrm{atm} \times (2-1)\;\mathrm{L} = -3\;\mathrm{atm\;L}$, $w_{3\to4} = 0$ $\implies$ $w = -3 \times 101.3 \approx -304\;\mathrm{J}$

questions.text: Which of the following graphs between pressure $'p'$ versus volume $'V'$ represents the maximum work done?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The magnitude of work done on a $p-V$ graph is equal to the net area under the curve bounded by the volume axis. // 📝 Solution: Graph (1) shows a single expansion from $22.4\;\text{L}$ to $44.8\;\text{L}$ whose total area under the curve down to the $V$-axis is greater than the enclosed loop areas of the cyclic processes in (2) and (4) and zero work in the isochoric process (3).

questions.text: One mole of an ideal monoatomic gas is subjected to changes as shown in the graph. The magnitude of the work done (by the system or on the system) is ______ $\text{J}$ (nearest integer). [FIGURE] Given : $\log 2 \;=\; 0.3, \; \ln 10 \;=\; 2.3$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Total work done in the cyclic process is $W \;=\; W_{1 \to 2} \;+\; W_{2 \to 3} \;+\; W_{3 \to 1}$ where $1 \to 2$ is isobaric, $2 \to 3$ is isochoric, and $3 \to 1$ is isothermal. // 📝 Solution: $W \;=\; -P\left(V_2 \;-\; V_1\right) \;+\; 0 \;-\; P_1 V_1 \ln\left(\frac{V_1}{V_2}\right) \;\implies\; W \;=\; -1 \;\times\; \left(40 \;-\; 20\right) \;-\; 1 \;\times\; 20 \ln\left(\frac{20}{40}\right) \;=\; -20 \;+\; 20 \ln 2 \;\implies\; W \;=\; -20 \;+\; 20 \;\times\; 2.3 \;\times\; 0.3 \;=\; -6.2\;\text{bar L} \;\implies\; \left\lvert W \right\rvert \;=\; 6.2 \;\times\; 100\;\text{J} \;=\; 620\;\text{J}$.

questions.text: [FIGURE] An ideal gas undergoes a cyclic transformation starting from the point A and coming back to the same point by tracing the path $\text{A} \;\to\; \text{B} \;\to\; \text{C} \;\to\; \text{A}$ as shown in the diagram. The total work done in the process is _______ $\text{J}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Magnitude of work done in a cyclic process equals the area enclosed by the loop on the $V$ vs $P$ diagram. // 📝 Solution: $\left\lvert W \right\rvert \;=\; \frac{1}{2} \;\times\; \left(30 \;-\; 10\right)\;\text{dm}^3 \;\times\; \left(30 \;-\; 10\right)\;\text{kPa} \;=\; \frac{1}{2} \;\times\; 20 \;\times\; 20\;\text{J} \;=\; 200\;\text{J}$.

questions.text: Which of the following relations are correct? (A) $\Delta U \;=\; q \;+\; p\Delta V$ (B) $\Delta G \;=\; \Delta H \;-\; T\Delta S$ (C) $\Delta S \;=\; \frac{q_{\text{rev}}}{T}$ (D) $\Delta H \;=\; \Delta U \;-\; \Delta n R T$ Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Check the standard thermodynamic relations at constant temperature and pressure. // 📝 Solution: At constant $T$ and $P$, $\Delta G \;=\; \Delta H \;-\; T\Delta S$ (B is correct) and $\Delta S \;=\; \frac{q_{\text{rev}}}{T}$ (C is correct), while $\Delta U \;=\; q \;-\; p\Delta V$ and $\Delta H \;=\; \Delta U \;+\; \Delta n_g R T$ make A and D incorrect.

questions.text: Match the LIST-I (Isothermal process for ideal gas system) with LIST-II (Work done, $V_f \;>\; V_i$): A. Reversible expansion, B. Free expansion, C. Irreversible expansion, D. Irreversible compression. List-II: I. $w \;=\; 0$, II. $w \;=\; -nRT\ln\left(\frac{V_f}{V_i}\right)$, III. $w \;=\; -p_{\text{ex}}\left(V_f \;-\; V_i\right)$, IV. $w \;=\; -p_{\text{ex}}\left(V_i \;-\; V_f\right)$. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Match each isothermal process with its standard work formula given $V_f \;>\; V_i$. // 📝 Solution: A (Reversible expansion) $\to$ II: $w \;=\; -nRT\ln\left(\frac{V_f}{V_i}\right)$; B (Free expansion, $p_{\text{ex}} \;=\; 0$) $\to$ I: $w \;=\; 0$; C (Irreversible expansion) $\to$ III: $w \;=\; -p_{\text{ex}}\left(V_f \;-\; V_i\right)$; D (Irreversible compression, positive work) $\to$ IV: $w \;=\; -p_{\text{ex}}\left(V_i \;-\; V_f\right)$.

questions.text: The heat of atomisation of methane and ethane are $'x'\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ and $'y'\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ respectively. The longest wavelength $\left(\lambda\right)$ of light capable of breaking the $\text{C}-\text{C}$ bond can be expressed in SI unit as:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Express $\text{BE}\left(\text{C}-\text{C}\right)$ per bond in Joules using $\text{CH}_4$ ($4\;\text{C}-\text{H}$ bonds) and $\text{C}_2\text{H}_6$ ($1\;\text{C}-\text{C}$ and $6\;\text{C}-\text{H}$ bonds), then equate to $\frac{hc}{\lambda}$. // 📝 Solution: $\text{BE}\left(\text{C}-\text{H}\right) \;=\; \frac{x}{4}\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1} \;\implies\; \text{BE}\left(\text{C}-\text{C}\right) \;=\; y \;-\; 6\left(\frac{x}{4}\right) \;=\; \frac{4y \;-\; 6x}{4}\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1} \;=\; 250\left(4y \;-\; 6x\right)\;\text{J mol}^{-1} \;\implies\; \frac{N_{\text{A}} h c}{\lambda} \;=\; 250\left(4y \;-\; 6x\right) \;\implies\; \lambda \;=\; \frac{N_{\text{A}} h c}{250\left(4y \;-\; 6x\right)}$.
questions.topic: Enthalpy of Atomization and Bond Energy

questions.text: When equal volume of $1\;\text{M HCl}$ and $1\;\text{M H}_2\text{SO}_4$ are separately neutralised by excess volume of $1\;\text{M NaOH}$ solution, $x$ and $y\;\text{kJ}$ of heat is liberated respectively. The value of $y/x$ is _______
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Heat liberated during neutralization of a strong acid with excess strong base is directly proportional to the moles of $\text{H}^+$ ions furnished. // 📝 Solution: Equal volumes of $1\;\text{M HCl}$ and $1\;\text{M H}_2\text{SO}_4$ furnish $\text{H}^+$ ions in the molar ratio $1 : 2 \;\implies\; y \;=\; 2x \;\implies\; \frac{y}{x} \;=\; 2$.

questions.text: Let us consider a reversible reaction at temperature $T$. In this reaction both $\Delta H$ and $\Delta S$ are observed to have positive values. If the equilibrium temperature is $T_e$, then the reaction becomes spontaneous at:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Spontaneity requires $\Delta G < 0$ with $\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$ // 📝 Solution: $\Delta H - T\Delta S < 0 \implies T > \dfrac{\Delta H}{\Delta S} = T_e$ $\implies$ spontaneous at $T > T_e$

questions.text: A cup of water at $5^\circ\text{C}$ (system) is placed in a microwave oven and the oven is turned on for one minute during which the water begins to boil. Which of the following option is true ?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Determine the signs of heat absorbed, expansion work during boiling, and net internal energy change as temperature increases. // 📝 Solution: Water absorbs energy from the microwave ($q \;=\; +\text{ve}$), expands against atmospheric pressure upon boiling ($w \;=\; -\text{ve}$), and its temperature increases from $5^\circ\text{C}$ to $100^\circ\text{C}$ with $\left\lvert q \right\rvert \;>\; \left\lvert w \right\rvert$ ($\Delta U \;=\; q \;+\; w \;=\; +\text{ve}$).

questions.text: The plot of $\log_{10} K$ vs $\frac{1}{T}$ gives a straight line. The intercept and slope respectively are (where $K$ is equilibrium constant).
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Equate $\Delta G^\circ \;=\; -2.303 R T \log_{10} K$ and $\Delta G^\circ \;=\; \Delta H^\circ \;-\; T\Delta S^\circ$. // 📝 Solution: $\log_{10} K \;=\; \left(-\frac{\Delta H^\circ}{2.303 R}\right)\frac{1}{T} \;+\; \frac{\Delta S^\circ}{2.303 R}$, which is of the form $y \;=\; mx \;+\; c$ with intercept $c \;=\; \frac{\Delta S^\circ}{2.303 R}$ and slope $m \;=\; -\frac{\Delta H^\circ}{2.303 R}$.

questions.text: $0.3\;\text{g}$ of ethane undergoes combustion at $27^\circ\text{C}$ in a bomb calorimeter. The temperature of calorimeter system (including the water) is found to rise by $0.5^\circ\text{C}$. The heat evolved during combustion of ethane at constant pressure is ______ $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. (Nearest integer) [Given : The heat capacity of the calorimeter system is $20\;\text{kJ K}^{-1}, \; R \;=\; 8.3\;\text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$. Assume ideal gas behaviour. Atomic mass of $\text{C}$ and $\text{H}$ are $12$ and $1\;\text{g mol}^{-1}$ respectively]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Bomb calorimeter measures $\Delta U$ at constant volume, and $\Delta H \;=\; \Delta U \;+\; \Delta n_g R T$. // 📝 Solution: For $1\;\text{mol}$ of $\text{C}_2\text{H}_6\left(\text{g}\right) \;+\; \frac{7}{2}\text{O}_2\left(\text{g}\right) \;\to\; 2\text{CO}_2\left(\text{g}\right) \;+\; 3\text{H}_2\text{O}\left(\text{l}\right)$, $\Delta U \;=\; -\frac{20 \;\times\; 0.5}{0.3 / 30} \;=\; -1000\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ and $\Delta n_g \;=\; -\frac{5}{2} \;\implies\; \Delta H \;=\; -1000 \;-\; \frac{5}{2} \;\times\; \frac{8.3 \;\times\; 300}{1000} \;=\; -1006.225\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1} \;\implies\; 1006\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$.

questions.text: For the reaction at $298\;\text{K}, \; 2\text{A} \;+\; \text{B} \;\to\; \text{C}$. $\Delta H \;=\; 400\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ and $\Delta S \;=\; 0.2\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$. The reaction will become spontaneous above ______ $\text{K}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A reaction with $\Delta H \;>\; 0$ and $\Delta S \;>\; 0$ becomes spontaneous ($\Delta G \;<\; 0$) above $T \;=\; \frac{\Delta H}{\Delta S}$. // 📝 Solution: At equilibrium $\Delta G \;=\; 0 \;\implies\; T \;=\; \frac{\Delta H}{\Delta S} \;=\; \frac{400}{0.2} \;=\; 2000\;\text{K}$.

questions.text: Arrange the following in order of magnitude of work done by the system or on the system at constant temperature: (a) $\lvert w_{\mathrm{rev}} \rvert$ for expansion in infinite stage. (b) $\lvert w_{\mathrm{irr}} \rvert$ for expansion in single stage. (c) $\lvert w_{\mathrm{rev}} \rvert$ for compression in infinite stage. (d) $\lvert w_{\mathrm{irr}} \rvert$ for compression in single stage.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Reversible work is maximum; compression against a higher opposing pressure requires more work // 📝 Solution: $\lvert w_{\mathrm{rev}} \rvert_{\mathrm{exp}} = \lvert w_{\mathrm{rev}} \rvert_{\mathrm{comp}}$ $\implies$ $a = c$; $\lvert w_{\mathrm{irr}} \rvert_{\mathrm{exp}} < \lvert w_{\mathrm{irr}} \rvert_{\mathrm{comp}}$ $\implies$ $d > c = a > b$

questions.text: An athlete is given $100\;\text{g}$ of glucose $\left(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6\right)$ for energy. This is equivalent to $1800\;\text{kJ}$ of energy. The $50\%$ of this energy gained is utilized by the athlete for sports activities at the event. In order to avoid storage of energy, the weight of extra water he would need to perspire is ______ $\text{g}$ (Nearest integer). Assume that there is no other way of consuming stored energy. Given : The enthalpy of evaporation of water is $45\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. Molar mass of $\text{C}, \; \text{H}$ & $\text{O}$ are $12, \; 1$ and $16\;\text{g mol}^{-1}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The unused $50\%$ energy is used to evaporate water via $\text{H}_2\text{O}\left(\text{l}\right) \;\to\; \text{H}_2\text{O}\left(\text{g}\right)$. // 📝 Solution: Extra energy to be consumed $= \frac{1800}{2} \;=\; 900\;\text{kJ} \;\implies\; n_{\text{H}_2\text{O}} \;=\; \frac{900}{45} \;=\; 20\;\text{mol} \;\implies\; W_{\text{H}_2\text{O}} \;=\; 20 \;\times\; 18 \;=\; 360\;\text{g}$.

questions.text: The heat of solution of anhydrous $\text{CuSO}_4$ and $\text{CuSO}_4 \cdot 5\text{H}_2\text{O}$ are $-70\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ and $+12\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ respectively. The heat of hydration of $\text{CuSO}_4$ to $\text{CuSO}_4 \cdot 5\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is $-x\;\text{kJ}$. The value of $x$ is ______ (nearest integer).
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: By Hess's Law, $\Delta_{\text{sol}} H\left(\text{CuSO}_4\right) \;=\; \Delta_{\text{hyd}} H\left(\text{CuSO}_4\right) \;+\; \Delta_{\text{sol}} H\left(\text{CuSO}_4 \cdot 5\text{H}_2\text{O}\right)$. // 📝 Solution: $-70 \;=\; \Delta_{\text{hyd}} H \;+\; 12 \;\implies\; \Delta_{\text{hyd}} H \;=\; -82\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1} \;\implies\; x \;=\; 82$.

questions.text: The hydration energies of $\mathrm{K^+}$ and $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ are $-x$ and $-y$ kJ mol$^{-1}$ respectively. If the lattice energy of KCl is $-z$ kJ mol$^{-1}$, then the heat of solution of KCl is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\Delta H_{\mathrm{sol}} = \text{lattice dissociation enthalpy} + \sum \Delta H_{\mathrm{hyd}}$ // 📝 Solution: $\Delta H_{\mathrm{sol}} = z + (-x) + (-y) = z - (x + y)$
questions.topic: Enthalpy of solution via Born-Haber-type cycle

questions.text: $\Delta_{\text{vap}} H^\ominus$ for water is $+40.79\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ at $1\;\text{bar}$ and $100^\circ\text{C}$. Change in internal energy for this vapourisation under same condition is ______ $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. (Integer answer) (Given $R \;=\; 8.3\;\text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For $\text{H}_2\text{O}\left(\text{l}\right) \;\rightleftharpoons\; \text{H}_2\text{O}\left(\text{g}\right)$, $\Delta n_g \;=\; 1$ and $\Delta_{\text{vap}} H^\ominus \;=\; \Delta_{\text{vap}} U^\ominus \;+\; \Delta n_g R T$. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta_{\text{vap}} U^\ominus \;=\; 40.79 \;-\; \frac{1 \;\times\; 8.3 \;\times\; 373.15}{1000} \;=\; 40.79 \;-\; 3.097 \;=\; 37.69\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1} \;\approx\; 38\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$.

questions.text: The number of non-polar molecules from the following is ____. [Species list is not legible in the source PDF; the official solution identifies the non-polar species as $\mathrm{CO_2}$, $\mathrm{H_2}$, $\mathrm{CH_4}$ and $\mathrm{BF_3}$.]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Non-polar molecules have zero net dipole moment. // 📝 Solution: Non-polar: $\mathrm{CO_2}$, $\mathrm{H_2}$, $\mathrm{CH_4}$, $\mathrm{BF_3}$ $\implies 4$.

questions.text: Match List I (molecules/ions) with List II (No. of lone pairs of e$^-$ on central atom): (A) $\mathrm{IF_7}$, (B) $\mathrm{ICl_4^-}$, (C) $\mathrm{XeF_6}$, (D) $\mathrm{XeF_2}$. List II: I. Three, II. One, III. Two, IV. Zero. Choose the correct answer.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Count lone pairs on the central atom for each species. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{IF_7}$ zero (IV); $\mathrm{ICl_4^-}$ two (III); $\mathrm{XeF_6}$ one (II); $\mathrm{XeF_2}$ three (I) $\implies$ option (2).

questions.text: Number of molecules having bond order 2 from the following is ____. $\mathrm{C_2}$, $\mathrm{O_2}$, $\mathrm{Be_2}$, $\mathrm{Li_2}$, $\mathrm{Ne_2}$, $\mathrm{N_2}$, $\mathrm{He_2}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: BO $= (\text{bonding} - \text{antibonding})/2$. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{C_2}$: 2; $\mathrm{O_2}$: 2; $\mathrm{Be_2}$: 0; $\mathrm{Li_2}$: 1; $\mathrm{Ne_2}$: 0; $\mathrm{N_2}$: 3; $\mathrm{He_2}$: 0 $\implies 2$.

questions.text: Match List I (hybridization) with List II (orientation in space): A. $\mathrm{sp^3}$; B. $\mathrm{dsp^2}$; C. $\mathrm{sp^3d}$; D. $\mathrm{sp^3d^2}$. I. Trigonal bipyramidal; II. Octahedral; III. Tetrahedral; IV. Square planar. Choose the correct answer.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Match each hybrid set to its electron-domain geometry. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{sp^3}$ tetrahedral (III); $\mathrm{dsp^2}$ square planar (IV); $\mathrm{sp^3d}$ TBP (I); $\mathrm{sp^3d^2}$ octahedral (II) $\implies$ option (2).

questions.text: The number of sp and sp$^2$ hybridised carbon atoms in the given structure [FIGURE] are respectively:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Carbon with a triple bond or two double bonds is sp; carbon with one double bond is sp$^2$. // 📝 Solution: $\text{count by bond type} \;\implies\; sp \;=\; 3,\; sp^2 \;=\; 5$

questions.text: Number of compounds with one lone pair of electrons on central atom amongst the following is ____. $\mathrm{O_3}$, $\mathrm{H_2O}$, $\mathrm{SF_4}$, $\mathrm{ClF_3}$, $\mathrm{NH_3}$, $\mathrm{BrF_5}$, $\mathrm{XeF_4}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Count lone pairs on the central atom from VSEPR. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{O_3}$ (1), $\mathrm{SF_4}$ (1), $\mathrm{NH_3}$ (1), $\mathrm{BrF_5}$ (1); $\mathrm{H_2O}$ (2), $\mathrm{ClF_3}$ (2), $\mathrm{XeF_4}$ (2) $\implies 4$.

questions.text: What is the number of unpaired electron(s) in the highest occupied molecular orbital of the following species: $\mathrm{N_2}$, $\mathrm{N_2^+}$, $\mathrm{O_2}$, $\mathrm{O_2^+}$?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Fill MOs and identify the partly filled HOMO. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{N_2}$: $\sigma 2p_z^2$ HOMO $\implies 0$; $\mathrm{N_2^+}$: $\sigma 2p_z^1 \implies 1$; $\mathrm{O_2}$: $\pi^*2p_x^1 = \pi^*2p_y^1 \implies 2$; $\mathrm{O_2^+}$: $\pi^*2p_x^1 \implies 1$.

questions.text: Identify the CORRECT statements. A. The dipole moment of $\mathrm{NF_3}$ is higher than that of $\mathrm{NH_3}$. B. The dipole moment of $\mathrm{BeH_2}$ is zero. C. The bond order of $\mathrm{O_2^{2-}}$ and $\mathrm{F_2}$ is same. D. The formal charge on the central oxygen atom of ozone is $-1$. E. In $\mathrm{NO_2}$, all three atoms satisfy the octet rule, hence it is very stable.

options.text: A, B, C, D and E

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Compare dipoles, bond orders and formal charges. // 📝 Solution: A ✗; B ✓ (linear); C ✓ (BO $= 1$ each); D ✗ (central O $= +1$); E ✗ (odd electron) $\implies$ option (3).
questions.topic: Dipole moment, bond order, formal charge

questions.text: In the Lewis dot structure for $\mathrm{NO_2^-}$, total number of valence electrons around nitrogen is ____.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Count lone-pair and bonding electrons around N in the drawn Lewis structure. // 📝 Solution: Lone pair $2$ + double bond $4$ + single bond $2$ $\implies 2 + 4 + 2 \; = \; 8$.

questions.text: The linear combination of atomic orbitals to form molecular orbitals takes place only when the combining atomic orbitals: A. have the same energy; B. have the minimum overlap; C. have same symmetry about the molecular axis; D. have different symmetry about the molecular axis. Choose the most appropriate option.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: LCAO needs similar energy, maximum overlap and matching symmetry. // 📝 Solution: A ✓, C ✓; B ✗, D ✗ $\implies$ option (2).

questions.text: The number of $\sigma$ and $\pi$ bonds in hex-1-en-4-yne are respectively:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Write the condensed structure and count bonds: single is one $\sigma$, double adds one $\pi$, triple adds two $\pi$. // 📝 Solution: $CH_2{=}CH{-}CH_2{-}C{\equiv}C{-}CH_3 \;\implies\; \sigma \;=\; 5 + 8 \;=\; 13,\; \pi \;=\; 1 + 2 \;=\; 3$

questions.text: Number of molecules from the following which can exhibit hydrogen bonding is ____ (nearest integer): $\mathrm{CH_3OH}$, $\mathrm{H_2O}$, $\mathrm{C_2H_6}$, $\mathrm{C_6H_6}$, o-nitrophenol, $\mathrm{HF}$, $\mathrm{NH_3}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: H-bonding needs H bonded to F, O or N. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{CH_3OH}$, $\mathrm{H_2O}$, o-nitrophenol, $\mathrm{HF}$, $\mathrm{NH_3}$ $\implies 5$; $\mathrm{C_2H_6}$ and $\mathrm{C_6H_6}$ cannot.

questions.text: The incorrect statement regarding ethyne is:

options.text: The C$-$C bond in ethyne is shorter than that in ethene.
The C$-$C bond in ethyne is weaker than that in ethene.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Compare triple and double C$-$C bonds. // 📝 Solution: Triple bond is shorter and stronger than double bond; (4) is false $\implies$ option (4).

questions.text: According to MO theory the bond orders for $\mathrm{O_2^{2-}}$, $\mathrm{CO}$ and $\mathrm{NO^+}$ respectively, are:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Bond order $= (\text{bonding} - \text{antibonding})/2$. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{O_2^{2-}}$: $\frac{10-8}{2} \; = \; 1$; $\mathrm{CO}$: $\frac{10-4}{2} \; = \; 3$; $\mathrm{NO^+}$: $\frac{10-4}{2} \; = \; 3$.

questions.text: Which of the following is least ionic?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Polarising power of the cation (small size, high charge, pseudo-inert configuration) increases covalency. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{AgCl} \; < \; \mathrm{CoCl_2} \; < \; \mathrm{BaCl_2} \; < \; \mathrm{KCl}$ (ionic character) $\implies$ AgCl least ionic.

questions.text: Statement-I: Since fluorine is more electronegative than nitrogen, the net dipole moment of $\mathrm{NF_3}$ is greater than $\mathrm{NH_3}$. Statement-II: In $\mathrm{NH_3}$, the orbital dipole due to lone pair and the dipole moment of N$-$H bonds are in opposite direction, but in $\mathrm{NF_3}$ the orbital dipole due to lone pair and dipole moments of N$-$F bonds are in same direction. Choose the most appropriate option.

options.text: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Compare lone-pair direction relative to bond dipoles in each molecule. // 📝 Solution: $\mu_{\mathrm{NH_3}} \; > \; \mu_{\mathrm{NF_3}}$ so I ✗; II reverses the directions ✗ $\implies$ option (2).

questions.text: The correct increasing order for bond angles among $\mathrm{BF_3}$, $\mathrm{PF_3}$ and $\mathrm{ClF_3}$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Lone pairs compress bond angles. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{BF_3}$ $\approx 120^\circ$; $\mathrm{PF_3}$ $\approx 97^\circ$; $\mathrm{ClF_3}$ $\approx 87.5^\circ$ $\implies \mathrm{ClF_3} \; < \; \mathrm{PF_3} \; < \; \mathrm{BF_3}$.

questions.text: Select the compound from the following that will show intramolecular hydrogen bonding.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Intramolecular H-bond needs donor and acceptor groups in ortho positions of one molecule. // 📝 Solution: o-nitrophenol forms an O$-$H$\cdots$O bond within the molecule $\implies$ option (4).

questions.text: Arrange the bonds in order of increasing ionic character in the molecules $\mathrm{LiF}$, $\mathrm{K_2O}$, $\mathrm{N_2}$, $\mathrm{SO_2}$ and $\mathrm{ClF_3}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Ionic character grows with electronegativity difference. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{N_2}$ ($\Delta\chi \; = \; 0$) $<$ $\mathrm{SO_2}$ $<$ $\mathrm{ClF_3}$ $<$ $\mathrm{K_2O}$ $<$ $\mathrm{LiF}$ $\implies$ option (3).

questions.text: The number of species from the following in which the central atom uses $\mathrm{sp^3}$ hybrid orbitals in its bonding is ____. $\mathrm{NH_3}$, $\mathrm{SO_2}$, $\mathrm{SiO_2}$, $\mathrm{BeCl_2}$, $\mathrm{CO_2}$, $\mathrm{H_2O}$, $\mathrm{CH_4}$, $\mathrm{BF_3}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mathrm{sp^3}$ means four electron domains on the central atom. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{NH_3}$, $\mathrm{SiO_2}$, $\mathrm{H_2O}$, $\mathrm{CH_4}$ $\implies 4$; $\mathrm{SO_2}$ and $\mathrm{BF_3}$ are sp$^2$; $\mathrm{BeCl_2}$ and $\mathrm{CO_2}$ are sp.

questions.text: Identify the molecule $X$ with maximum number of lone pairs (Lewis structure) among $\mathrm{HNO_3}$, $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$, $\mathrm{NF_3}$ and $\mathrm{O_3}$. Choose the correct bond angle made by the central atom of $X$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Official key identifies $X = \mathrm{NF_3}$. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{NF_3}$ has one lone pair on N (sp$^3$) $\implies$ bond angle $\approx 102^\circ$ $\implies$ option (2).

questions.text: Statement (I): A $\pi$ bonding MO has lower electron density above and below the inter-nuclear axis. Statement (II): The $\pi^*$ antibonding MO has a node between the nuclei. Choose the most appropriate answer.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\pi$ MOs have density above and below the axis; $\pi^*$ has a nodal plane between nuclei. // 📝 Solution: (I) ✗ (higher density above/below); (II) ✓ $\implies$ option (3).

questions.text: Which of the following linear combinations of atomic orbitals will form molecular orbitals (internuclear axis is z)? A. $2p_z + 2p_x$; B. $2s + 2p_x$; C. $3d_{xy} + 3d_{x^2-y^2}$; D. $2s + 2p_z$; E. $2p_z + 3d_{x^2-y^2}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Orbitals combine only if they have the same symmetry about the internuclear axis and non-zero overlap. // 📝 Solution: $2s + 2p_z \;\implies\; \text{both } \sigma \text{-symmetric, net overlap} \neq 0;\; \text{A, B, C, E} \;\implies\; \text{zero net overlap}$

questions.text: For $\mathrm{OF_2}$ molecule consider the following: (A) Number of lone pairs on oxygen is 2. (B) FOF angle is less than $104.5^\circ$. (C) Oxidation state of O is $-2$. (D) Molecule is bent V shaped. (E) Molecular geometry is linear. Correct options are:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Check each statement with VSEPR and oxidation-state rules. // 📝 Solution: A ✓ (2 lone pairs); B ✓ ($\angle \approx 103^\circ$); C ✗ (O is $+2$); D ✓ (bent); E ✗ $\implies$ A, B, D.

questions.text: In which one of the following pairs the central atoms exhibit $\mathrm{sp^2}$ hybridization?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mathrm{sp^2}$ means three electron domains. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{BF_3}$ $\mathrm{sp^2}$; $\mathrm{NO_2^-}$ $\mathrm{sp^2}$ $\implies$ option (2).

questions.text: The total number of species from the following in which one unpaired electron is present is ____. $\mathrm{N_2}$, $\mathrm{O_2}$, $\mathrm{C_2^-}$, $\mathrm{O_2^-}$, $\mathrm{O_2^{2-}}$, $\mathrm{H_2^+}$, $\mathrm{CN^-}$, $\mathrm{He_2^+}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Write MO configurations and count unpaired electrons. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{C_2^-}$, $\mathrm{O_2^-}$, $\mathrm{H_2^+}$, $\mathrm{He_2^+}$ have one unpaired e$^-$ each; $\mathrm{N_2}$, $\mathrm{O_2^{2-}}$, $\mathrm{CN^-}$ have none; $\mathrm{O_2}$ has two $\implies 4$.

questions.text: The number of paramagnetic species among $O_2$, $O_2^{+}$, $O_2^{-}$, $NO$, $NO_2$, $CO$, $K_2\left[NiCl_4\right]$, $\left[Co\left(NH_3\right)_6\right]Cl_3$ and $K_2\left[Ni\left(CN\right)_4\right]$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Count unpaired electrons using MO theory and crystal field theory for the complexes. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Paramagnetic} \;=\; O_2,\, O_2^{+},\, O_2^{-},\, NO,\, NO_2,\, \left[NiCl_4\right]^{2-} \;\implies\; 6$; $CO,\, \left[Co\left(NH_3\right)_6\right]^{3+},\, \left[Ni\left(CN\right)_4\right]^{2-} \;\text{diamagnetic}$

questions.text: When $\psi_A$ and $\psi_B$ are the wave functions of atomic orbitals, then $\sigma^*$ is represented by:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Antibonding MO arises from out-of-phase combination. // 📝 Solution: $\sigma^* = \psi_A - \psi_B$ (nodal plane between nuclei) $\implies$ option (2).

questions.text: The shape of carbocation (CH$_3^+$) is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Carbocation carbon has three bonding pairs and no lone pair. // 📝 Solution: sp$^2$ carbon with three bonds $\implies$ trigonal planar $\implies$ option (2).

questions.text: Number of molecules/species from the following having one unpaired electron is: $\mathrm{O_2}$, $\mathrm{O_2^-}$, $\mathrm{NO}$, $\mathrm{CN^-}$, $\mathrm{O_2^{2-}}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Write MO configurations and count unpaired electrons. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{O_2}$: 2 (excluded); $\mathrm{O_2^-}$: 1 ✓; $\mathrm{NO}$: 1 ✓; $\mathrm{CN^-}$: 0; $\mathrm{O_2^{2-}}$: 0 $\implies 2$.

questions.text: Which statements are NOT TRUE about $\mathrm{XeO_2F_2}$? A. It has a see-saw shape. B. Xe has 5 electron pairs in its valence shell. C. The O$-$Xe$-$O bond angle is close to $180^\circ$. D. The F$-$Xe$-$F bond angle is close to $180^\circ$. E. Xe has 16 valence electrons in $\mathrm{XeO_2F_2}$. Choose the correct answer.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Count electron pairs on Xe (4 bonding + 2 lone) to get the geometry. // 📝 Solution: See-saw (A ✓); B ✗ (six pairs); C ✗ (O$-$Xe$-$O $\approx 120^\circ$); D ✓ (F$-$Xe$-$F $\approx 180^\circ$); E ✗ (8 valence e$^-$) $\implies$ option (1).

questions.text: The number of species from the following which are paramagnetic and with bond order equal to one is ____. $\mathrm{H_2}$, $\mathrm{He_2^+}$, $\mathrm{O_2^+}$, $\mathrm{N_2^{2-}}$, $\mathrm{O_2^{2-}}$, $\mathrm{F_2}$, $\mathrm{Ne_2^+}$, $\mathrm{B_2}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Paramagnetic means unpaired electrons; BO must equal 1. // 📝 Solution: Only $\mathrm{B_2}$ is paramagnetic with BO $= 1$; $\mathrm{H_2}$, $\mathrm{O_2^{2-}}$, $\mathrm{F_2}$ have BO 1 but are diamagnetic $\implies 1$.

questions.text: Consider $H_2O$, $NH_3$ and $CH_4$. A. The central atoms are sp$^3$ hybridised. B. The H–O–H, H–N–H and H–C–H bond angles are $104.5^\circ$, $107.5^\circ$ and $109.5^\circ$ respectively. C. The dipole moment increases in the order $CH_4 < NH_3 < H_2O$. D. $H_2O$ and $NH_3$ are Lewis acids and $CH_4$ is a Lewis base. E. $NH_3$ in $H_2O$ is basic, with $NH_3$ and $H_2O$ acting as Brønsted acid and base respectively. Choose the correct answer.

options.text: A, B, C and E only

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Check lone pair repulsion for the angles, and the acid-base behaviour of each species. // 📝 Solution: $sp^3$ in all (A true); $104.5^\circ < 107.5^\circ < 109.5^\circ$ (B true); $0 < 1.47 < 1.85\text{ D}$ (C true); $H_2O,\, NH_3 \;\text{are Lewis bases}$ (D false); $NH_3$ accepts $H^+$ (E false)
questions.topic: Structure, bond angle and dipole of hydrides

questions.text: The total number of anti-bonding molecular orbitals, formed from 2s and 2p atomic orbitals in a diatomic molecule is ____.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Each pair of AOs gives one bonding and one antibonding MO. // 📝 Solution: 2s: 1 antibonding; 2p: 3 antibonding ($\sigma^*2p_z$, $\pi^*2p_x$, $\pi^*2p_y$) $\implies 1 + 3 \; = \; 4$.

questions.text: Match List-I (molecule) with List-II (shape): A. $\mathrm{BrF_5}$; B. $\mathrm{H_2O}$; C. $\mathrm{ClF_3}$; D. $\mathrm{SF_4}$. I. T-shape; II. See saw; III. Bent; IV. Square pyramidal.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use VSEPR shapes from lone-pair count. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{BrF_5}$ square pyramidal (IV); $\mathrm{H_2O}$ bent (III); $\mathrm{ClF_3}$ T-shape (I); $\mathrm{SF_4}$ see-saw (II) $\implies$ option (4).

questions.text: Choose the polar molecule from the following:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Polar molecules have net dipole $\neq 0$. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{CHCl_3}$ has $\mu \neq 0$; $\mathrm{CCl_4}$, $\mathrm{CO_2}$, $\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH_2}$ have $\mu = 0$ $\implies$ option (4).

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II according to shape: A. $\mathrm{XeO_3}$; B. $\mathrm{XeF_2}$; C. $\mathrm{XeO_2F_2}$; D. $\mathrm{XeOF_4}$. List-II: I. $\mathrm{BrF_5}$; II. $\mathrm{NH_3}$; III. $\mathrm{[I_3]^-}$; IV. $\mathrm{SF_4}$. Choose the correct answer.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Match each Xe species to a shape with the same lone-pair arrangement. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{XeO_3}$ pyramidal ($\mathrm{NH_3}$, II); $\mathrm{XeF_2}$ linear ($\mathrm{I_3^-}$, III); $\mathrm{XeO_2F_2}$ see-saw ($\mathrm{SF_4}$, IV); $\mathrm{XeOF_4}$ square pyramidal ($\mathrm{BrF_5}$, I) $\implies$ option (3).

questions.text: The sum of the number of $\sigma$ and $\pi$ bonds in hexa-1,3-dien-5-yne is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Draw $CH_2{=}CH{-}CH{=}CH{-}C{\equiv}CH$ and count each bond type. // 📝 Solution: $\sigma \;=\; 5 + 6 \;=\; 11,\; \pi \;=\; 2 + 2 \;=\; 4 \;\implies\; 11 + 4 \;=\; 15$

questions.text: Match List I (molecule) with List II (shape): A. $\mathrm{NH_3}$; B. $\mathrm{BrF_5}$; C. $\mathrm{PCl_5}$; D. $\mathrm{CH_4}$. I. Square pyramid; II. Tetrahedral; III. Trigonal pyramidal; IV. Trigonal bipyramidal. Choose the correct answer.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Count bonding and lone pairs for each molecule. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{NH_3}$ trigonal pyramidal (III); $\mathrm{BrF_5}$ square pyramid (I); $\mathrm{PCl_5}$ trigonal bipyramid (IV); $\mathrm{CH_4}$ tetrahedral (II) $\implies$ option (2).

questions.text: Statement I: Dipole moment is a vector quantity and by convention it is depicted by a small arrow with tail on the negative centre and head pointing towards the positive centre. Statement II: The crossed arrow of the dipole moment symbolizes the direction of the shift of charges in the molecules. Choose the most appropriate answer.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Check the dipole arrow convention and the meaning of the crossed arrow. // 📝 Solution: Official key: Statement I correct, Statement II incorrect $\implies$ option (4).

questions.text: The correct statement/s about hydrogen bonding is/are: A. H-bonding exists when H is covalently bonded to a highly electronegative atom. B. Intermolecular H-bonding is present in o-nitrophenol. C. Intramolecular H-bonding is present in HF. D. The magnitude of H-bonding depends on the physical state of the compound. E. H-bonding has powerful effect on the structure and properties of compounds.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Intramolecular H-bond occurs within one molecule (o-nitrophenol); HF is intermolecular. // 📝 Solution: A ✓; B ✗; C ✗; D ✓ (solid $>$ liquid); E ✓ $\implies$ A, D, E.

questions.text: The correct increasing order of $C-H(A)$, $C-O(B)$, $C=O(C)$ and $C\equiv N(D)$ bonds in terms of covalent bond length is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Higher bond order and smaller atoms give shorter bonds. // 📝 Solution: C$-$H ($1.09$ Å) $<$ C$\equiv$N ($1.16$ Å) $<$ C$=$O ($1.23$ Å) $<$ C$-$O ($1.43$ Å) $\implies$ A $<$ D $<$ C $<$ B.

questions.text: The formal charges on the atoms marked (1) to (4) in the Lewis representation of $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ respectively are: [FIGURE]

Match List I (complexes) with List II (hybridisation): (A) $\mathrm{[Ni(CO)_4]}$, (B) $\mathrm{[Cu(NH_3)_4]^{2+}}$, (C) $\mathrm{[Fe(NH_3)_6]^{2+}}$, (D) $\mathrm{[Fe(H_2O)_6]^{2+}}$. List II: I. $\mathrm{sp^3}$, II. $\mathrm{dsp^2}$, III. $\mathrm{sp^3d^2}$, IV. $\mathrm{d^2sp^3}$. Choose the correct answer.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Strong-field ligands (NH$_3$) give inner-orbital $\mathrm{d^2sp^3}$; weak-field (H$_2$O) gives outer $\mathrm{sp^3d^2}$. // 📝 Solution: A $\to$ I; B $\to$ II; C $\to$ IV; D $\to$ III $\implies$ option (4).

questions.text: The number of molecules/ions having trigonal bipyramidal shape is ____. $\mathrm{PF_5}$, $\mathrm{BrF_5}$, $\mathrm{PCl_5}$, $\mathrm{\left[ PtCl_4 \right]^{2-}}$, $\mathrm{BF_3}$, $\mathrm{Fe(CO)_5}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: TBP needs five electron domains and no lone pair. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{PF_5}$, $\mathrm{PCl_5}$, $\mathrm{Fe(CO)_5}$ are TBP; $\mathrm{BrF_5}$ square pyramidal; $\mathrm{\left[ PtCl_4 \right]^{2-}}$ square planar; $\mathrm{BF_3}$ trigonal planar $\implies 3$.

questions.text: The number of given orbitals which have electron density along the axis is ____. Orbitals: $p_x, p_y, p_z, d_{xy}, d_{yz}, d_{xz}, d_{z^2}, d_{x^2-y^2}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Orbitals with lobes along the x, y or z axes are axial. // 📝 Solution: $p_x, p_y, p_z, d_{z^2}, d_{x^2-y^2}$ $\implies 5$.

questions.text: Number of molecules from the following which are exceptions to the octet rule is ____. $\mathrm{CO_2}$, $\mathrm{NO_2}$, $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$, $\mathrm{BF_3}$, $\mathrm{CH_4}$, $\mathrm{SiF_4}$, $\mathrm{ClO_2}$, $\mathrm{PCl_5}$, $\mathrm{BeF_2}$, $\mathrm{C_2H_6}$, $\mathrm{CHCl_3}$, $\mathrm{CBr_4}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Odd-electron, incomplete-octet and expanded-octet species are exceptions. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{NO_2}$, $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$, $\mathrm{BF_3}$, $\mathrm{ClO_2}$, $\mathrm{PCl_5}$, $\mathrm{BeF_2}$ $\implies 6$.

questions.text: Sum of bond order of $\mathrm{CO}$ and $\mathrm{NO^+}$ is ____.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Compute bond order for each species from MO configuration. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{CO}$: 3; $\mathrm{NO^+}$: 3 $\implies 3 + 3 \; = \; 6$.

questions.text: Match List I (shapes) with List II for molecules: (A) $\mathrm{IF_7}$ type shapes, pentagonal bipyramidal, see the source list: (A) $\mathrm{IF_7}$ (B) $\mathrm{SF_4}$ (C) $\mathrm{NH_4^+}$ (D) $\mathrm{XeF_4}$ with shapes I. See-saw, II. Square planar, III. Bent T-shaped, IV. Tetrahedral.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use VSEPR shapes for each species. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{XeF_4}$ square planar (II); $\mathrm{SF_4}$ see-saw (I); $\mathrm{NH_4^+}$ tetrahedral (IV); $\mathrm{BrF_3}$ bent T (III) $\implies$ option (4).

questions.text: Match List I (molecule) with List II (colour/shape): A. $\mathrm{Fe_4[Fe(CN)_6]_3 \cdot xH_2O}$; B. $\mathrm{\left[ Fe(CN)_5NOS \right]^{4-}}$; C. $\mathrm{\left[ Fe(SCN) \right]^{2+}}$; D. $\mathrm{(NH_4)_3PO_4 \cdot 12MoO_3}$. I. Violet; II. Blood Red; III. Prussian Blue; IV. Yellow. Choose the correct answer.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall the colours of common Fe complexes. // 📝 Solution: Prussian blue (A-III); $\mathrm{\left[ Fe(CN)_5NOS \right]^{4-}}$ violet (B-I); $\mathrm{\left[ Fe(SCN) \right]^{2+}}$ blood red (C-II); phosphomolybdate yellow (D-IV) $\implies$ option (1).

questions.text: A diatomic molecule has a dipole moment of 1.2 D. If the bond distance is 1 Å, then the fractional charge on each atom is ____ $\times 10^{-1}$ esu. (Given $1 \; \mathrm{D} = 10^{-18}$ esu cm.)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $\mu = q \times d$ with unit conversion (1 Å $= 10^{-8}$ cm). // 📝 Solution: $\mu = 1.2 \times 10^{-10}$ esu Å $\implies q = \frac{\mu}{d} = 1.2 \times 10^{-10}$ esu $= 1.2 \times 10^{-9} \times 10^{-1}$ esu $\implies 0$ (official key).

questions.text: Given below are two statements. Statement I: The correct order in terms of bond dissociation enthalpy is $\mathrm{Cl_2} > \mathrm{Br_2} > \mathrm{F_2} > \mathrm{I_2}$. Statement II: The correct trend in covalent character of metal halides is $[\mathrm{SnCl_4} > \mathrm{SnCl_2}]$, $[\mathrm{PbCl_4} > \mathrm{PbCl_2}]$ and $[\mathrm{UF_4} > \mathrm{UF_6}]$. Choose the correct answer.

options.text: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Check the $\mathrm{F_2}$ anomaly and Fajans' rule with oxidation states. // 📝 Solution: I ✓ ($\mathrm{F_2}$ lone-pair repulsion); II ✗ since $\mathrm{UF_6}$ (+6) is more covalent than $\mathrm{UF_4}$ $\implies$ option (3).

questions.text: The total number of molecular orbitals formed from 2s and 2p atomic orbitals of a diatomic molecule is ____.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: MOs formed equal the number of AOs combined. // 📝 Solution: 2s$_A$, 2s$_B$ $\to$ 2 MOs; 2p (6 AOs) $\to$ 6 MOs $\implies 2 + 6 \; = \; 8$.

questions.text: Match List I with List II. List I: (A) Molecules obeying the octet rule; (B) Molecules with incomplete octet; (C) Molecules with incomplete octet with odd electron; (D) Molecules with expanded octet. List II: (I) NO, NO$_2$; (II) BCl$_3$, AlCl$_3$; (III) H$_2$SO$_4$, PCl$_5$; (IV) CCl$_4$, CO$_2$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Count valence electrons around the central atom in each molecule. // 📝 Solution: $CCl_4,\, CO_2 \;\implies\; 8e^{-};\; BCl_3,\, AlCl_3 \;\implies\; 6e^{-};\; NO,\, NO_2 \;\implies\; \text{odd } e^{-};\; H_2SO_4,\, PCl_5 \;\implies\; >8e^{-}$

questions.text: Match List I with List II: (A) ICl, (B) ICl$_3$, (C) ClF$_5$, (D) IF$_7$. List II: (I) T-shape, (II) pyramidal, (III) pentagonal bipyramidal, (IV) linear. Choose the correct answer.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Count electron domains and lone pairs on the central atom. // 📝 Solution: ICl linear (IV); ICl$_3$ T-shape (I); ClF$_5$ square pyramidal (II); IF$_7$ pentagonal bipyramidal (III) $\implies$ option (1).

questions.text: The correct increasing order of dipole moment of HBr, H$_2$S, NF$_3$ and CHCl$_3$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall experimental dipole moments; in NF$_3$ the lone pair dipole opposes the N–F bond dipoles. // 📝 Solution: $\mu:\; NF_3\left(0.24\right) \;<\; HBr\left(0.78\right) \;<\; H_2S\left(0.95\right) \;<\; CHCl_3\left(1.01\right)\text{ D}$

questions.text: Identify the molecule with maximum number of lone pairs of electrons among $\mathrm{HNO_3}$, $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$, $\mathrm{NF_3}$ and $\mathrm{O_3}$ (molecule $X$). Choose the correct bond angle made by the central atom of $X$. Options as listed: 116°, 102°, 107°, 120°.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Official key identifies $X = \mathrm{NF_3}$ (one lone pair on N, sp$^3$). // 📝 Solution: F$-$N$-$F angle $\approx 102^\circ$ $\implies$ option (2).

questions.text: Assertion (A): $\mathrm{NH_3}$ and $\mathrm{NF_3}$ have pyramidal shape with a lone pair on nitrogen. The resultant dipole moment of $\mathrm{NH_3}$ is greater than that of $\mathrm{NF_3}$. Reason (R): In $\mathrm{NH_3}$, the orbital dipole due to the lone pair is in the same direction as the resultant dipole moment of the N$-$H bonds. F is the most electronegative element. Choose the correct option.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Lone-pair dipole adds to bond dipoles in NH$_3$ but opposes them in NF$_3$. // 📝 Solution: $\mu_{\mathrm{NH_3}} \approx 1.47$ D $>$ $\mu_{\mathrm{NF_3}} \approx 0.23$ D; (R) explains this $\implies$ option (1).

questions.text: Number of compounds/species from the following with non-zero dipole moment is ____. $\mathrm{BeCl_2}$, $\mathrm{BCl_3}$, $\mathrm{NF_3}$, $\mathrm{XeF_4}$, $\mathrm{CCl_4}$, $\mathrm{H_2O}$, $\mathrm{H_2S}$, $\mathrm{HBr}$, $\mathrm{CO_2}$, $\mathrm{H_2}$, $\mathrm{HCl}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Polar molecules have net dipole $\neq 0$. // 📝 Solution: Polar: $\mathrm{NF_3}, \mathrm{H_2O}, \mathrm{H_2S}, \mathrm{HBr}, \mathrm{HCl}$ $\implies 5$.

questions.text: Which of the following pairs of molecules have square pyramidal geometry?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Square pyramidal means $sp^3d^2$ with five bond pairs and one lone pair. // 📝 Solution: $BrF_5 \;\implies\; 5\,bp + 1\,lp;\; XeOF_4 \;\implies\; 5\,bp + 1\,lp \;\implies\; \text{square pyramidal};\; PCl_5,\, SbF_5 \;\implies\; \text{trigonal bipyramidal}$

questions.text: Which one of the following molecules has maximum dipole moment?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Symmetric molecules have zero dipole; compare the remaining two. // 📝 Solution: $\mu_{\mathrm{CH_4}} = \mu_{\mathrm{PF_5}} = 0$; lone pair adds to bond dipoles in $\mathrm{NH_3}$ but opposes them in $\mathrm{NF_3}$ $\implies \mu_{\mathrm{NH_3}} \; > \; \mu_{\mathrm{NF_3}}$.

questions.text: Amongst the following, the number of species having the linear shape is ____. $\mathrm{XeF_2}$, $\mathrm{I_3^+}$, $\mathrm{C_3O_2}$, $\mathrm{I_3^-}$, $\mathrm{CO_2}$, $\mathrm{SO_2}$, $\mathrm{BeCl_2}$, $\mathrm{BCl_2^-}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Linear species have no lone pairs on the central atom (or are symmetric triatomics). // 📝 Solution: Linear: $\mathrm{XeF_2}, \mathrm{C_3O_2}, \mathrm{I_3^-}, \mathrm{CO_2}, \mathrm{BeCl_2}$ $\implies 5$.

questions.text: Assertion (A): $\mathrm{PH_3}$ has lower boiling point than $\mathrm{NH_3}$. Reason (R): In liquid state $\mathrm{NH_3}$ molecules are associated through van der Waals forces, but $\mathrm{PH_3}$ molecules are associated through hydrogen bonding. Choose the most appropriate answer.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mathrm{NH_3}$ forms H-bonds; $\mathrm{PH_3}$ does not. // 📝 Solution: (A) ✓; (R) ✗ (roles reversed) $\implies$ option (4).

questions.text: The total number of lone pairs of electrons on oxygen atoms of ozone ($\mathrm{O_3}$) is ____.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Draw the Lewis structure and count lone pairs on each O. // 📝 Solution: Terminal $\mathrm{O}$ (double bond) $= 2$; terminal $\mathrm{O}^-$ $= 3$; central $\mathrm{O}$ $= 1$ $\implies 2 + 3 + 1 \; = \; 6$.

questions.text: Pair of species among the following having same bond order as well as paramagnetic character will be:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Compute bond order and unpaired electrons for each species. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{O_2^+}$: BO $= 2.5$, paramagnetic; $\mathrm{N_2^-}$: BO $= 2.5$, paramagnetic $\implies$ option (4).

questions.text: Match List I (molecule/species) with List II (property/shape): A. $\mathrm{SO_2Cl_2}$; B. NO; C. $\mathrm{NO_2^-}$; D. $\mathrm{I_3^-}$. I. Paramagnetic; II. Diamagnetic; III. Tetrahedral; IV. Linear. Choose the correct answer.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Check geometry for molecules and unpaired electrons for species. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{SO_2Cl_2}$ tetrahedral (III); NO paramagnetic (I); $\mathrm{NO_2^-}$ diamagnetic (II); $\mathrm{I_3^-}$ linear (IV) $\implies$ option (2).

questions.text: Two p-block elements X and Y form fluorides of the type $\mathrm{EF_3}$. The fluoride $\mathrm{XF_3}$ is a Lewis acid and $\mathrm{YF_3}$ is a Lewis base. The hybridizations of the central atoms of $\mathrm{XF_3}$ and $\mathrm{YF_3}$ respectively are:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Lewis acid is electron-deficient (BF$_3$); Lewis base has a lone pair (NF$_3$). // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{BF_3}$ sp$^2$; $\mathrm{NF_3}$ sp$^3$ $\implies$ option (1).

questions.text: The number of molecules or ions with linear geometry among $SO_2$, $BeCl_2$, $CO_2$, $N_3^{-}$, $NO_2$, $F_2O$, $XeF_2$, $NO_2^{+}$, $I_3^{-}$ and $O_3$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use VSEPR; species with no bent distortion (sp or sp$^3$d with three lone pairs) are linear. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Linear} \;=\; BeCl_2,\, CO_2,\, N_3^{-},\, XeF_2,\, NO_2^{+},\, I_3^{-} \;\implies\; 6$

questions.text: The total number of $\sigma$ and $\pi$ bonds in 2-formylhex-4-enoic acid is ____.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Count every single, double and triple bond in the structure. // 📝 Solution: Total bonds (σ + π) in the drawn structure $\implies 22$.

questions.text: Among the following, the CORRECT combinations are: A. $\mathrm{IF_3}$ T-shaped ($\mathrm{sp^3d}$); B. $\mathrm{IF_5}$ square pyramidal ($\mathrm{sp^3d^2}$); C. $\mathrm{IF_7}$ pentagonal bipyramidal ($\mathrm{sp^3d^3}$); D. $\mathrm{ClO_4^-}$ square planar ($\mathrm{sp^2d}$). Choose the correct answer.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Check each shape against its electron-domain count. // 📝 Solution: A ✓; B ✓; C ✓; D ✗ ($\mathrm{ClO_4^-}$ tetrahedral, sp$^3$) $\implies$ option (3).

questions.text: Number of compounds from the following with zero dipole moment is ____. $\mathrm{HF}$, $\mathrm{H_2}$, $\mathrm{H_2S}$, $\mathrm{CO_2}$, $\mathrm{NH_3}$, $\mathrm{BF_3}$, $\mathrm{CH_4}$, $\mathrm{CHCl_3}$, $\mathrm{SiF_4}$, $\mathrm{H_2O}$, $\mathrm{BeF_2}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Symmetric molecules have zero net dipole moment. // 📝 Solution: Zero: $\mathrm{H_2}, \mathrm{CO_2}, \mathrm{BF_3}, \mathrm{CH_4}, \mathrm{SiF_4}, \mathrm{BeF_2}$ $\implies 6$.

questions.text: Number of molecules/ions from the following in which the central atom is involved in $\mathrm{sp^3}$ hybridization is: $\mathrm{NO_3^-}$, $\mathrm{BCl_3}$, $\mathrm{ClO_2^-}$, $\mathrm{ClO_3}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mathrm{sp^3}$ means four electron domains on the central atom. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{NO_3^-}$ $\mathrm{sp^2}$; $\mathrm{BCl_3}$ $\mathrm{sp^2}$; $\mathrm{ClO_2^-}$ $\mathrm{sp^3}$; $\mathrm{ClO_3}$ $\mathrm{sp^3}$ $\implies 2$.

questions.text: Statement I: The first ionisation enthalpy of Pb is greater than that of Sn. Statement II: The first ionisation enthalpy of Ge is greater than that of Si. Choose the correct option.

options.text: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Poor shielding by d and f electrons raises the IE of heavier group 14 members. // 📝 Solution: $IE_1\left(Pb\right) \;=\; 716 \;>\; IE_1\left(Sn\right) \;=\; 709$ (true); $IE_1\left(Ge\right) \;=\; 762 \;<\; IE_1\left(Si\right) \;=\; 786$ (false)

questions.text: The total number of molecules with zero dipole moment among $\mathrm{CH_4}$, $\mathrm{BF_3}$, $\mathrm{H_2O}$, $\mathrm{HF}$, $\mathrm{NH_3}$, $\mathrm{CO_2}$ and $\mathrm{SO_2}$ is ____.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Symmetric molecules have zero net dipole. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{CH_4}$, $\mathrm{BF_3}$, $\mathrm{CO_2}$ have $\mu = 0$; $\mathrm{H_2O}$, $\mathrm{HF}$, $\mathrm{NH_3}$, $\mathrm{SO_2}$ polar $\implies 3$.

questions.text: The number of species from the following that have pyramidal geometry around the central atom is ____. $\mathrm{S_2O_3^{2-}}$, $\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}$, $\mathrm{SO_3^{2-}}$, $\mathrm{S_2O_7^{2-}}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Pyramidal needs three bonding pairs and one lone pair on the central atom. // 📝 Solution: Only $\mathrm{SO_3^{2-}}$ has a lone pair on S; the others are tetrahedral $\implies 1$.

questions.text: Among $\mathrm{H_2S}$, $\mathrm{H_2O}$, $\mathrm{NF_3}$, $\mathrm{NH_3}$ and $\mathrm{CHCl_3}$, identify the molecule $X$ with lowest dipole moment. The number of lone pairs on the central atom of $X$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mathrm{NF_3}$ has the lowest dipole moment. // 📝 Solution: $X = \mathrm{NF_3}$ ($\mu \approx 0.23$ D); central N has one lone pair $\implies 1$.

questions.text: Match List I (compound/species) with List II (shape/geometry): A. $\mathrm{SF_4}$; B. $\mathrm{BrF_3}$; C. $\mathrm{BrO_3^-}$; D. $\mathrm{NH_4^+}$. I. Tetrahedral; II. Pyramidal; III. See saw; IV. Bent T-shape. Choose the correct answer.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use VSEPR shapes from lone pairs on the central atom. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{SF_4}$ see-saw (III); $\mathrm{BrF_3}$ bent T (IV); $\mathrm{BrO_3^-}$ pyramidal (II); $\mathrm{NH_4^+}$ tetrahedral (I) $\implies$ option (3).

questions.text: Total number of electrons present in $(\pi^*)$ molecular orbitals of $\mathrm{O_2}$, $\mathrm{O_2^+}$ and $\mathrm{O_2^-}$ is ____.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Fill the MO diagram for each species and count electrons in $\pi^*$. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{O_2}$: 2; $\mathrm{O_2^+}$: 1; $\mathrm{O_2^-}$: 3 $\implies 2 + 1 + 3 \; = \; 6$.

questions.text: Statement I: Ozone has equal O–O bond lengths, which are longer than the O=O bond but shorter than the O–O single bond. Statement II: Lone pair–lone pair repulsion is solely responsible for the shape and bond length of ozone. Choose the correct option.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Resonance equalises the two bonds, so repulsion alone cannot explain them. // 📝 Solution: $\text{resonance} \;\implies\; \text{bond order} \;=\; 1.5 \;\implies\; \text{I true};\; \text{II false since resonance also contributes}$

questions.text: Statement I: The number of species among $\mathrm{BF_4^-}$, $\mathrm{SiF_4}$, $\mathrm{XeF_4}$ and $\mathrm{SF_4}$ with unequal E$-$F bond lengths is two (E is the central atom). Statement II: Among $\mathrm{O_2^-}$, $\mathrm{O_2^{2-}}$, $\mathrm{F_2}$ and $\mathrm{O_2^+}$, $\mathrm{O_2^-}$ has the highest bond order. Choose the correct answer.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Only $\mathrm{SF_4}$ has unequal bonds; $\mathrm{O_2^+}$ has the highest bond order. // 📝 Solution: Count $= 1$ (I ✗); BO: $\mathrm{O_2^+}$ $= 2.5$ $>$ $\mathrm{O_2^-}$ $= 1.5$ (II ✗) $\implies$ option (1).

questions.text: Statement I: The number of species among $\mathrm{SF_4}$, $\mathrm{NH_4^+}$, $\mathrm{\left[ NiCl_4 \right]^{2-}}$, $\mathrm{XeF_4}$, $\mathrm{\left[ PtCl_4 \right]^{2-}}$, $\mathrm{SeF_4}$ and $\mathrm{\left[ Ni(CN)_4 \right]^{2-}}$ that have tetrahedral geometry is 3. Statement II: In the set $[\mathrm{NO_2}, \mathrm{BeH_2}, \mathrm{BF_3}, \mathrm{AlCl_3}]$, all molecules have incomplete octet around the central atom. Choose the correct answer.

options.text: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Tetrahedral needs sp$^3$ with no lone pairs. // 📝 Solution: Tetrahedral: $\mathrm{NH_4^+}$, $\mathrm{\left[ NiCl_4 \right]^{2-}}$ $\implies 2 \neq 3$ (I ✗); all four have incomplete octets (II ✓) $\implies$ option (2).

questions.text: Statement I: $\mathrm{N(CH_3)_3}$ and $\mathrm{P(CH_3)_3}$ can act as ligands to form transition metal complexes. Statement II: As N and P are from the same group, the nature of bonding of $\mathrm{N(CH_3)_3}$ and $\mathrm{P(CH_3)_3}$ is always the same with transition metals. Choose the most appropriate answer.

options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mathrm{P(CH_3)_3}$ shows $\pi$-acceptor character; $\mathrm{N(CH_3)_3}$ does not. // 📝 Solution: Both are Lewis bases (I ✓); bonding differs (II ✗) $\implies$ option (1).

questions.text: Arrange the following molecules in the correct increasing order of their dipole moments: $\mathrm{HBr}$, $\mathrm{H_2S}$, $\mathrm{NF_3}$, $\mathrm{CHCl_3}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Compare experimental dipole moments; in $\mathrm{NF_3}$ the N–F bond dipoles oppose the lone-pair dipole. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{NF_3} \;=\; 0.24\;\mathrm{D}$, $\mathrm{HBr} \;=\; 0.78\;\mathrm{D}$, $\mathrm{H_2S} \;=\; 0.95\;\mathrm{D}$, $\mathrm{CHCl_3} \;=\; 1.01\;\mathrm{D} \;\implies\; \mathrm{NF_3} \;<\; \mathrm{HBr} \;<\; \mathrm{H_2S} \;<\; \mathrm{CHCl_3}$

questions.text: Choose the correct option for the melting points of the pairs of d-block elements Mn/Fe, Tc/Ru and Re/Os.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Melting point depends on the strength of metallic bonding, i.e. the number of unpaired d-electrons contributing to bonding. // 📝 Solution: Melting points: $\mathrm{Mn} \;<\; \mathrm{Fe}$, $\mathrm{Tc} \;<\; \mathrm{Ru}$, $\mathrm{Os} \;<\; \mathrm{Re} \;\implies\;$ option B
questions.topic: Metallic Bonding and Melting Point Trends

questions.text: During Kinetic study of reaction $2\text{A} \;+\; \text{B} \rightarrow \text{C} \;+\; \text{D}$, the following results were obtained : I: $\left[\text{A}\right] \;=\; 0.1\;\text{M}, \left[\text{B}\right] \;=\; 0.1\;\text{M}$, initial rate $= 6.0 \;\times\; 10^{-3}$; II: $\left[\text{A}\right] \;=\; 0.3\;\text{M}, \left[\text{B}\right] \;=\; 0.2\;\text{M}$, initial rate $= 7.20 \;\times\; 10^{-2}$; III: $\left[\text{A}\right] \;=\; 0.3\;\text{M}, \left[\text{B}\right] \;=\; 0.4\;\text{M}$, initial rate $= 2.88 \;\times\; 10^{-1}$; IV: $\left[\text{A}\right] \;=\; 0.4\;\text{M}, \left[\text{B}\right] \;=\; 0.1\;\text{M}$, initial rate $= 2.40 \;\times\; 10^{-2}$. Based on above data, overall order of the reaction is _____
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Write $\text{rate} \;=\; k\left[\text{A}\right]^x\left[\text{B}\right]^y$ and take ratios of experiments with constant concentration of one reactant. // 📝 Solution: From (IV)/(I): $\frac{2.4 \;\times\; 10^{-2}}{6.0 \;\times\; 10^{-3}} \;=\; \left(\frac{0.4}{0.1}\right)^x \implies 4 \;=\; 4^x \implies x \;=\; 1$. From (III)/(II): $\frac{2.88 \;\times\; 10^{-1}}{7.20 \;\times\; 10^{-2}} \;=\; \left(\frac{0.4}{0.2}\right)^y \implies 4 \;=\; 2^y \implies y \;=\; 2 \implies \text{Overall order} \;=\; x \;+\; y \;=\; 1 \;+\; 2 \;=\; 3$.

questions.text: Observe the following reactions at $T(\text{K})$. I. $\text{A} \rightarrow \text{products}$. II. $5\text{Br}^-(\text{aq}) \;+\; \text{BrO}_3^-(\text{aq}) \;+\; 6\text{H}^+(\text{aq}) \rightarrow 3\text{Br}_2(\text{aq}) \;+\; 3\text{H}_2\text{O}(\text{l})$. Both the reactions are started at $10.00\;\text{am}$. The rates of these reactions at $10.10\;\text{am}$ are same. The value of $-\frac{\Delta\left[\text{Br}^-\right]}{\Delta t}$ at $10.10\;\text{am}$ is $2 \;\times\; 10^{-4}\;\text{mol L}^{-1}\;\text{min}^{-1}$. The concentration of A at $10.10\;\text{am}$ is $10^{-2}\;\text{mol L}^{-1}$. What is the first order rate constant (in $\text{min}^{-1}$) of reaction I ?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Rate of reaction II is $r_{\text{II}} \;=\; -\frac{1}{5}\frac{\Delta\left[\text{Br}^-\right]}{\Delta t}$, which equals $r_{\text{I}} \;=\; k\left[\text{A}\right]$. // 📝 Solution: $r_{\text{II}} \;=\; \frac{1}{5} \;\times\; 2 \;\times\; 10^{-4} \;=\; 4 \;\times\; 10^{-5}\;\text{mol L}^{-1}\;\text{min}^{-1} \implies r_{\text{I}} \;=\; k\left[\text{A}\right] \;=\; 4 \;\times\; 10^{-5} \implies k \;=\; \frac{4 \;\times\; 10^{-5}}{10^{-2}} \;=\; 4 \;\times\; 10^{-3}\;\text{min}^{-1}$.

questions.text: $\text{NO}_2$ required for a reaction is produced by decomposition of $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ in $\text{CCl}_4$ as by equation $2\text{N}_2\text{O}_5(\text{g}) \rightarrow 4\text{NO}_2(\text{g}) \;+\; \text{O}_2(\text{g})$. The initial concentration of $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ is $3\;\text{mol L}^{-1}$ and it is $2.75\;\text{mol L}^{-1}$ after $30\;\text{minutes}$. The rate of formation of $\text{NO}_2$ is $x \;\times\; 10^{-3}\;\text{mol L}^{-1}\;\text{min}^{-1}$, value of $x$ is _____
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: From stoichiometry, $\frac{\Delta\left[\text{NO}_2\right]}{\Delta t} \;=\; 2 \;\times\; \left(-\frac{\Delta\left[\text{N}_2\text{O}_5\right]}{\Delta t}\right)$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{\Delta\left[\text{NO}_2\right]}{\Delta t} \;=\; 2 \;\times\; \frac{3 \;-\; 2.75}{30} \;=\; \frac{0.5}{30} \;=\; 16.67 \;\times\; 10^{-3}\;\text{mol L}^{-1}\;\text{min}^{-1} \;\approx\; 17 \;\times\; 10^{-3}\;\text{mol L}^{-1}\;\text{min}^{-1} \implies x \;=\; 17$.

questions.text: In a reaction $\mathrm{A+B\to C}$, the initial concentrations satisfy $[A]_0=8[B]_0$. The half-lives of A and B are $10$ min and $40$ min respectively. Both follow first-order kinetics and start to disappear at the same time. After how much time will the concentrations of both reactants be the same?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Equal concentrations require $[A]_0e^{-k_At}=[B]_0e^{-k_Bt}$. // 📝 Solution: $8=e^{(k_A-k_B)t}$ with $k_A=\dfrac{\ln2}{10}$, $k_B=\dfrac{\ln2}{40}$ $\implies3\ln2=\ln2\cdot\dfrac{3}{40}\,t\implies t=40\;\text{min}$.

questions.text: For a reaction $\text{A} \xrightarrow{K_1} \text{B} \xrightarrow{K_2} \text{C}$. If the rate of formation of B is set to be zero then the concentration of B is given by :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Apply steady-state approximation: $\frac{d\left[\text{B}\right]}{dt} \;=\; K_1\left[\text{A}\right] \;-\; K_2\left[\text{B}\right] \;=\; 0$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{d\left[\text{B}\right]}{dt} \;=\; K_1\left[\text{A}\right] \;-\; K_2\left[\text{B}\right] \;=\; 0 \implies \left[\text{B}\right] \;=\; \left(\frac{K_1}{K_2}\right)\left[\text{A}\right]$.

questions.text: The reaction $\mathrm{A(g)\to 2B(g)+C(g)}$ is first order and starts with pure A. The total pressure of the system is $160$ mm Hg at $t=10$ min and $240$ mm Hg at $t=\infty$. Which of the following options is incorrect?

options.text: Initial pressure of A is $80$ mm Hg
The reaction never goes to completion
Rate constant of the reaction is $1.693\;\text{min}^{-1}$
Partial pressure of A after $10$ minutes is $40$ mm Hg

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For $\mathrm{A\to2B+C}$, $P_t=P_0+2x$ and $P_\infty=3P_0$. // 📝 Solution: $P_0=\dfrac{240}{3}=80$ mm Hg; at $10$ min $x=40\implies P_A=40$ mm Hg $\implies k=\dfrac{1}{10}\ln2=0.0693\;\text{min}^{-1}\neq1.693$ $\implies$ option (3).
questions.topic: First-order gaseous reactions, integrated rate law

questions.text: Integrated rate law equation for a first order gas phase reaction is given by (where $P_i$ is initial pressure and $P_t$ is total pressure at time $t$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For $\text{A}(\text{g}) \rightarrow \text{B}(\text{g}) \;+\; \text{C}(\text{g})$, total pressure at time $t$ is $P_t \;=\; P_i \;+\; x$. // 📝 Solution: $P_t \;=\; P_i \;+\; x \implies x \;=\; P_t \;-\; P_i \implies P_{\text{A}} \;=\; P_i \;-\; x \;=\; 2P_i \;-\; P_t \implies k \;=\; \frac{2.303}{t} \;\times\; \log \frac{P_i}{\left(2P_i \;-\; P_t\right)}$.

questions.text: In a first-order decomposition reaction, the time taken for the decomposition of reactant to one-fourth and one-eighth of its initial concentration are $t_1$ and $t_2$ (s), respectively. The ratio $t_1/t_2$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: In first-order kinetics each half-life halves the remaining amount. // 📝 Solution: Remaining $\tfrac{1}{4}$ requires $2t_{1/2}$, so $t_1=2t_{1/2}$; remaining $\tfrac{1}{8}$ requires $3t_{1/2}$, so $t_2=3t_{1/2}$ $\implies\dfrac{t_1}{t_2}=\dfrac{2}{3}$.

questions.text: Consider an elementary reaction $A\left(g\right)+B\left(g\right)\rightarrow C\left(g\right)+D\left(g\right)$. If the volume of the reaction mixture is suddenly reduced to $\frac{1}{3}$ of its initial volume, the reaction rate will become $x$ times of the original reaction rate. The value of $x$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For an elementary reaction, rate law follows stoichiometry and concentration varies inversely with volume. // 📝 Solution: $Rate\;=\;k\left[A\right]\left[B\right]\;\implies\;\left[A\right],\left[B\right]\;\times3\;\implies\;Rate\;\times\left(3\times3\right)\;=\;9$

questions.text: Consider the energy profile [FIGURE] showing reactant, activated complex, product and energies $E_1$ and $E_2$. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The activation energy of both forward and backward reactions is $E_1 + E_2$ and the reactant is more stable than the product
The activation energy of the forward reaction is $E_1 + E_2$ and the product is less stable than the reactant
The activation energy of the backward reaction is $E_1$ and the product is more stable than the reactant
The activation energy of the forward reaction is $E_1 + E_2$ and the product is more stable than the reactant

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Compare reactant and product levels, and read forward and backward barriers from the profile. // 📝 Solution: $E_{a,f} \;=\; E_1 + E_2 \;\implies\; \text{product lies above reactant} \;\implies\; \text{endothermic, product less stable than reactant}$
questions.topic: Energy profile diagram and activation energy

questions.text: $\text{A} \rightarrow \text{product}$ (First order reaction). Three sets of experiment were performed for a reaction under similar experimental conditions: Run 1 $\implies 100\;\text{mL}$ of $10\;\text{M}$ solution of reactant A; Run 2 $\implies 200\;\text{mL}$ of $10\;\text{M}$ solution of reactant A; Run 3 $\implies 100\;\text{mL}$ of $10\;\text{M}$ solution of reactant A $+ 100\;\text{mL}$ of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ added. The correct variation of rate of reaction is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Rate of reaction depends on molar concentration $\left[\text{A}\right]$, not on total volume of the solution. // 📝 Solution: In Run 1 and Run 2, $\left[\text{A}\right] \;=\; 10\;\text{M}$, whereas in Run 3, dilution halves the concentration to $\left[\text{A}\right] \;=\; \frac{10 \;\times\; 100}{200} \;=\; 5\;\text{M} \implies \text{Rate of Run 3} \;<\; \text{Rate of Run 1} \;=\; \text{Rate of Run 2}$.

questions.text: Reactant A converts to product D through the mechanism (with net evolution of heat): $\mathrm{A\to B}$ slow, $\Delta H=+ve$; $\mathrm{B\to C}$ fast, $\Delta H=-ve$; $\mathrm{C\to D}$ fast, $\Delta H=-ve$. Which energy profile represents this mechanism? [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The slow step has the highest barrier; the endothermic first step raises energy and the exothermic later steps lower it. // 📝 Solution: $A\to B$ has the highest barrier $E_{a1}$, followed by lower barriers for the exothermic steps, ending at the lowest level for D $\implies$ option (1).

questions.text: Consider the following single step reaction in gas phase at constant temperature. $2\text{A}(\text{g}) \;+\; \text{B}(\text{g}) \rightarrow \text{C}(\text{g})$. The initial rate of the reaction is recorded as $r_1$ when the reaction starts with $1.5\;\text{atm}$ pressure of A and $0.7\;\text{atm}$ pressure of B. After some time, the rate $r_2$ is recorded when the pressure of C becomes $0.5\;\text{atm}$. The ratio $r_1 : r_2$ is _____ $\times\; 10^{-1}$. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For an elementary reaction, orders equal stoichiometric coefficients: $r \;=\; k P_{\text{A}}^2 P_{\text{B}}$. // 📝 Solution: Initially $r_1 \;=\; k\left(1.5\right)^2\left(0.7\right)$. When $P_{\text{C}} \;=\; 0.5\;\text{atm}$, $P_{\text{A}} \;=\; 1.5 \;-\; 2\left(0.5\right) \;=\; 0.5\;\text{atm}$ and $P_{\text{B}} \;=\; 0.7 \;-\; 0.5 \;=\; 0.2\;\text{atm} \implies r_2 \;=\; k\left(0.5\right)^2\left(0.2\right) \implies \frac{r_1}{r_2} \;=\; \frac{2.25 \;\times\; 0.7}{0.25 \;\times\; 0.2} \;=\; 31.5 \;=\; 315 \;\times\; 10^{-1}$.

questions.text: For the first order reaction $\text{A} \rightarrow \text{B}$ the half life is $30\;\text{min}$. The time taken for $75\%$ completion of the reaction is _____ $\text{min}$. (Nearest integer) Given : $\log 2 \;=\; 0.3010, \log 3 \;=\; 0.4771, \log 5 \;=\; 0.6989$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For a first-order reaction, time for $75\%$ completion is twice the half-life $\left(t_{75\%} \;=\; 2 \;\times\; t_{1/2}\right)$. // 📝 Solution: $t_{1/2} \;=\; 30\;\text{min} \implies t_{75\%} \;=\; 2 \;\times\; t_{1/2} \;=\; 2 \;\times\; 30 \;=\; 60\;\text{min}$.

questions.text: At $27^\circ\text{C}$ in presence of a catalyst, activation energy of a reaction is lowered by $10\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. The logarithm of ratio of $\frac{k\;\text{(catalysed)}}{k\;\text{(uncatalysed)}}$ is.... (Consider that the frequency factor for both the reactions is same)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $\log_{10}\left(\frac{k_{\text{cat}}}{k_{\text{uncat}}}\right) \;=\; \frac{\Delta E_a}{2.303RT}$. // 📝 Solution: $\log_{10}\left(\frac{k_{\text{cat}}}{k_{\text{uncat}}}\right) \;=\; \frac{10 \;\times\; 10^3}{2.303 \;\times\; 8.314 \;\times\; 300} \;=\; \frac{10000}{5744.14} \;\approx\; 1.741$.
questions.topic: Effect of Catalyst on Activation Energy

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: List-I: (A) Physisorption, (B) Chemisorption, (C) $\text{N}_2(\text{g}) \;+\; 3\text{H}_2(\text{g}) \xrightarrow{\text{Fe(s)}} 2\text{NH}_3(\text{g})$, (D) Analytical Application of Adsorption. List-II: I. Single layer adsorption, II. $20\text{--}40\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, III. Chromatography, IV. Heterogeneous catalysis. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Match enthalpy and layer properties of physisorption/chemisorption and catalysis/chromatography applications. // 📝 Solution: Physisorption has enthalpy $20\text{--}40\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ (A-II); Chemisorption is unimolecular/single layer (B-I); Haber's process is heterogeneous catalysis (C-IV); Chromatography is an analytical application of adsorption (D-III).

questions.text: Pre-exponential factors of two different reactions of same order are identical. Let activation energy of first reaction exceeds the activation energy of second reaction by $20\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. If $k_1$ and $k_2$ are the rate constants of first and second reaction respectively at $300\;\text{K}$, then $\ln \frac{k_2}{k_1}$ will be _____. (nearest integer) $\left[R \;=\; 8.3\;\text{J K}^{-1}\;\text{mol}^{-1}\right]$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For identical pre-exponential factors $A_1 \;=\; A_2$, $\ln\left(\frac{k_2}{k_1}\right) \;=\; \frac{E_{a1} \;-\; E_{a2}}{RT}$. // 📝 Solution: $\ln\left(\frac{k_2}{k_1}\right) \;=\; \frac{20 \;\times\; 10^3}{8.3 \;\times\; 300} \;=\; \frac{20000}{2490} \;=\; 8.03 \;\approx\; 8$.

questions.text: Consider the following data for the given reaction $2\text{HI}(\text{g}) \rightarrow \text{H}_2(\text{g}) \;+\; \text{I}_2(\text{g})$. Exp 1: $\left[\text{HI}\right] \;=\; 0.005\;\text{mol L}^{-1}$, $\text{Rate} \;=\; 7.5 \;\times\; 10^{-4}\;\text{mol L}^{-1}\;\text{s}^{-1}$; Exp 2: $\left[\text{HI}\right] \;=\; 0.01\;\text{mol L}^{-1}$, $\text{Rate} \;=\; 3.0 \;\times\; 10^{-3}\;\text{mol L}^{-1}\;\text{s}^{-1}$; Exp 3: $\left[\text{HI}\right] \;=\; 0.02\;\text{mol L}^{-1}$, $\text{Rate} \;=\; 1.2 \;\times\; 10^{-2}\;\text{mol L}^{-1}\;\text{s}^{-1}$. The order of the reaction is _____
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $\frac{\text{Rate}_2}{\text{Rate}_1} \;=\; \left(\frac{\left[\text{HI}\right]_2}{\left[\text{HI}\right]_1}\right)^n$ to find the order $n$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{3.0 \;\times\; 10^{-3}}{7.5 \;\times\; 10^{-4}} \;=\; \left(\frac{0.01}{0.005}\right)^n \implies 4 \;=\; 2^n \implies n \;=\; 2$.

questions.text: For the thermal decomposition of reactant $\text{AB}(\text{g})$, the following plot is constructed. [FIGURE] The half life of the reaction is '$x$' $\text{min}$. $x \;=\;$ _____ $\text{min}$. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A linear decrease of $\left[\text{AB}\right]$ vs time indicates zero-order kinetics with slope $-k$. // 📝 Solution: From the graph, $\left[\text{AB}\right]_0 \;=\; 0.6\;\text{M}$ and at $t \;=\; 200\;\text{s}$, $\left[\text{AB}\right] \;=\; 0.5\;\text{M} \implies k \;=\; \frac{0.6 \;-\; 0.5}{200} \;=\; 5 \;\times\; 10^{-4}\;\text{M s}^{-1} \implies t_{1/2} \;=\; \frac{0.6}{2 \;\times\; 5 \;\times\; 10^{-4}} \;=\; 600\;\text{s} \;=\; 10\;\text{min}$.

questions.text: An organic compound undergoes first order decomposition. If the time taken for the $60\%$ decomposition is $540\;\text{s}$, then the time required for $90\%$ decomposition will be _____ $\text{s}$. (Nearest integer). Given : $\ln 10 \;=\; 2.3; \log 2 \;=\; 0.3$
Which of the following statements is not true for radioactive decay?

options.text: Decay constant increases with increase in temperature
Amount of radioactive substance remaining after three half lives is $\frac{1}{8}$th of the original amount
Decay constant does not depend upon temperature
Half life is $\ln 2$ times of $\frac{1}{\text{rate constant}}$

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Radioactive decay has zero activation energy. // 📝 Solution: $E_a\;=\;0\;\implies\;k$ is independent of $T$; also $\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^3\;=\;\frac{1}{8}$ and $t_{1/2}\;=\;\frac{\ln2}{k}$, so only statement (1) is false

questions.text: $\text{A} \rightarrow \text{B}$. The rate constants of the above reaction at $200\;\text{K}$ and $300\;\text{K}$ are $0.03\;\text{min}^{-1}$ and $0.05\;\text{min}^{-1}$ respectively. The activation energy for the reaction is _____ $\text{J}$ (Nearest integer) (Given : $\ln 10 \;=\; 2.3, R \;=\; 8.3\;\text{J K}^{-1}\;\text{mol}^{-1}, \log 5 \;=\; 0.70, \log 3 \;=\; 0.48, \log 2 \;=\; 0.30$)
