questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use the two-temperature Arrhenius equation $\log\left(\frac{k_2}{k_1}\right) \;=\; \frac{E_a}{2.3 \;\times\; R}\left(\frac{T_2 \;-\; T_1}{T_1 T_2}\right)$. // 📝 Solution: $\log\left(\frac{0.05}{0.03}\right) \;=\; \frac{E_a}{2.3 \;\times\; 8.3}\left(\frac{300 \;-\; 200}{200 \;\times\; 300}\right) \implies 0.70 \;-\; 0.48 \;=\; \frac{E_a}{19.09} \;\times\; \frac{1}{600} \implies E_a \;=\; 0.22 \;\times\; 19.09 \;\times\; 600 \;\approx\; 2520\;\text{J}$.

questions.text: If compound A reacts with B following first order kinetics with rate constant $2.011 \;\times\; 10^{-3}\;\text{s}^{-1}$. The time taken by A (in seconds) to reduce from $7\;\text{g}$ to $2\;\text{g}$ will be _____. (Nearest Integer) $\left[\log 5 \;=\; 0.698, \log 7 \;=\; 0.845, \log 2 \;=\; 0.301\right]$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use the first-order integrated rate law $t \;=\; \frac{2.303}{k}\log\left(\frac{\left[\text{A}\right]_0}{\left[\text{A}\right]_t}\right)$. // 📝 Solution: $t \;=\; \frac{2.303}{2.011 \;\times\; 10^{-3}}\log\left(\frac{7}{2}\right) \implies t \;=\; \frac{2.303 \;\times\; \left(0.845 \;-\; 0.301\right)}{2.011 \;\times\; 10^{-3}} \;=\; \frac{2.303 \;\times\; 0.544}{2.011 \;\times\; 10^{-3}} \;=\; 622.989 \;\approx\; 623\;\text{s}$.

questions.text: A and B are two substances undergoing radioactive decay in a container. The half life of A is $15\;\text{min}$ and that of B is $5\;\text{min}$. If the initial concentration of B is $4$ times that of A and they both start decaying at the same time, how much time will it take for the concentration of both of them to be same? _____ $\text{min}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Equate the concentrations $\left[\text{A}\right]_t \;=\; \left[\text{B}\right]_t$ using $\left[\text{N}\right]_t \;=\; \left[\text{N}\right]_0 \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{t / t_{1/2}}$. // 📝 Solution: $\left[\text{A}\right]_0 \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{t/15} \;=\; 4\left[\text{A}\right]_0 \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{t/5} \implies 2^{t/5 \;-\; t/15} \;=\; 2^2 \implies \frac{2t}{15} \;=\; 2 \implies t \;=\; 15\;\text{min}$.

questions.text: The following data were obtained during the first order thermal decomposition of a gas A at constant volume: $\text{A}(\text{g}) \rightarrow 2\text{B}(\text{g}) \;+\; \text{C}(\text{g})$. S.No 1: Time $0\;\text{s}$, Total pressure $0.1\;\text{atm}$; S.No 2: Time $115\;\text{s}$, Total pressure $0.28\;\text{atm}$. The rate constant of the reaction is _____ $\times\; 10^{-2}\;\text{s}^{-1}$ (nearest integer)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Total pressure at time $t$ is $P_t \;=\; P_0 \;+\; 2x$, and partial pressure of A is $P_0 \;-\; x$. // 📝 Solution: $0.1 \;+\; 2x \;=\; 0.28 \implies x \;=\; 0.09\;\text{atm} \implies k \;=\; \frac{2.303}{115}\log\left(\frac{0.1}{0.1 \;-\; 0.09}\right) \;=\; \frac{2.303}{115}\log(10) \;=\; 0.02\;\text{s}^{-1} \;=\; 2 \;\times\; 10^{-2}\;\text{s}^{-1}$.

questions.text: For a reaction, $k \;=\; \sqrt{\frac{k_1 k_3}{k_2}}$ where the activation energies of $k_1$, $k_2$ and $k_3$ are $60$, $30$ and $10\text{ kJ/mol}$ respectively. The overall activation energy (in $\text{kJ/mol}$) is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Apply $k \;=\; Ae^{-E_a/RT}$ to each constant and take the logarithm of the combination. // 📝 Solution: $E_a \;=\; \frac{1}{2}\left(E_1 + E_3 - E_2\right) \;\implies\; E_a \;=\; \frac{1}{2}\left(60 + 10 - 30\right) \;=\; 20\text{ kJ/mol}$
questions.topic: Activation energy of composite rate constant

questions.text: Which of the following graphs most appropriately represents a zero order reaction?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Integrated zero order law is linear in time. // 📝 Solution: $\left[A\right]_t\;=\;\left[A\right]_0-kt\;\implies\;$ straight line with negative slope for concentration vs time, as in graph (1) [FIGURE]

questions.text: $r \;=\; k\left[\text{A}\right]$ for a reaction, $50\%$ of A is decomposed in $120\;\text{minutes}$. The time taken for $90\%$ decomposition of A is _____ minutes.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For a first-order reaction, $t_{90\%} \;=\; \frac{\log 10}{\log 2} \;\times\; t_{50\%} \;=\; 3.322 \;\times\; t_{1/2}$. // 📝 Solution: $t_{90\%} \;=\; \frac{2.303}{0.693} \;\times\; 120 \;\approx\; 398.78\;\text{min} \;\approx\; 399\;\text{min}$.

questions.text: Consider the following reaction, the rate expression of which is given below: $\text{A} \;+\; \text{B} \rightarrow \text{C}$, $\text{rate} \;=\; k\left[\text{A}\right]^{1/2}\left[\text{B}\right]^{1/2}$. The reaction is initiated by taking $1\;\text{M}$ concentration of A and B each. If the rate constant ($k$) is $4.6 \;\times\; 10^{-2}\;\text{s}^{-1}$, then the time taken for A to become $0.1\;\text{M}$ is _____ $\text{sec}$. (nearest integer)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Since $\left[\text{A}\right]_0 \;=\; \left[\text{B}\right]_0$ and stoichiometry is $1:1$, $\left[\text{A}\right] \;=\; \left[\text{B}\right]$ at all times, reducing the rate law to $\text{rate} \;=\; k\left[\text{A}\right]$. // 📝 Solution: $t \;=\; \frac{2.303}{k}\log\left(\frac{\left[\text{A}\right]_0}{\left[\text{A}\right]_t}\right) \;=\; \frac{2.303}{4.6 \;\times\; 10^{-2}}\log\left(\frac{1}{0.1}\right) \;=\; \frac{2.303}{0.046} \;\approx\; 50\;\text{s}$.

questions.text: The rate constant for a first order reaction is $20\;\text{min}^{-1}$. The time required for the initial concentration of the reactant to reduce to its $\frac{1}{32}$ level is _____ $\times\; 10^{-2}\;\text{min}$. (Nearest integer) (Given : $\ln 10 \;=\; 2.303, \log 2 \;=\; 0.3010$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Since $\frac{1}{32} \;=\; \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^5$, the time required is $5$ half-lives $\left(t \;=\; 5 \;\times\; t_{1/2}\right)$. // 📝 Solution: $t \;=\; 5 \;\times\; \frac{\ln 2}{k} \;=\; \frac{5 \;\times\; 2.303 \;\times\; 0.3010}{20} \;=\; 0.17325\;\text{min} \;=\; 17.325 \;\times\; 10^{-2}\;\text{min} \;\approx\; 17 \;\times\; 10^{-2}\;\text{min}$.

questions.text: The rate of first order reaction is $0.04\;\text{mol L}^{-1}\;\text{s}^{-1}$ at $10\;\text{minutes}$ and $0.03\;\text{mol L}^{-1}\;\text{s}^{-1}$ at $20\;\text{minutes}$ after initiation. Half life of the reaction is _____ minutes. (Given $\log 2 \;=\; 0.3010, \log 3 \;=\; 0.4771$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Rate of a first-order reaction also decays exponentially: $\frac{R_1}{R_2} \;=\; e^{k\left(t_2 \;-\; t_1\right)}$. // 📝 Solution: $k \;=\; \frac{2.303}{20 \;-\; 10}\log\left(\frac{0.04}{0.03}\right) \implies t_{1/2} \;=\; \frac{10 \;\times\; \log 2}{\log 4 \;-\; \log 3} \;=\; \frac{10 \;\times\; 0.3010}{0.6020 \;-\; 0.4771} \;=\; \frac{3.010}{0.1249} \;=\; 24.09\;\text{min} \;\approx\; 24\;\text{min}$.

questions.text: [FIGURE] Given above is the concentration vs time plot for a dissociation reaction : $\text{A} \rightarrow n\text{B}$. Based on the data of the initial phase of the reaction (initial $10\;\text{min}$), the value of $n$ is _____.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use stoichiometry: $\Delta\left[\text{B}\right] \;=\; n \;\times\; \left(-\Delta\left[\text{A}\right]\right)$ in the first $10\;\text{minutes}$. // 📝 Solution: From $t \;=\; 0$ to $t \;=\; 10\;\text{min}$, $\left[\text{A}\right]$ decreases from $0.05\;\text{M}$ to $0.04\;\text{M}$ $\left(-\Delta\left[\text{A}\right] \;=\; 0.01\;\text{M}\right)$ while $\left[\text{B}\right]$ increases from $0$ to $0.03\;\text{M}$ $\left(\Delta\left[\text{B}\right] \;=\; 0.03\;\text{M}\right) \implies n \;=\; \frac{0.03}{0.01} \;=\; 3$.

questions.text: For the reaction $2N_2O_5\left(g\right) \;\to\; 2N_2O_4\left(g\right) \;+\; O_2\left(g\right)$ carried out at constant volume, the total pressure is $0.6\text{ atm}$ at $t \;=\; 0$ and $x$ at $t \;=\; 100\text{ s}$. Given $k \;=\; 4.606\times 10^{-2}\text{ s}^{-1}$, then $x \;=\; \_\_\_\times 10^{-3}\text{ atm}$ (nearest integer).
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Decomposition is first order in N2O5; relate total pressure to the N2O5 pressure using stoichiometry. // 📝 Solution: $kt \;=\; \ln\frac{P_0}{P_0 - 2p} \;\implies\; 4.606 \;=\; \ln 100 \;\implies\; P_0 - 2p \;=\; 0.006 \;\implies\; p \;=\; 0.297$, so $P_t \;=\; P_0 + p \;=\; 0.897\text{ atm} \;=\; 897\times 10^{-3}\text{ atm}$
questions.topic: First order kinetics from pressure data

questions.text: $\text{A} \rightarrow \text{B}$. The above reaction is of zero order. Half life of this reaction is $50\;\text{min}$. The time taken for the concentration of A to reduce to one-fourth of its initial value is _____ $\text{min}$. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For a zero-order reaction, $t_{1/2} \;=\; \frac{a}{2k}$ and $x \;=\; kt$. // 📝 Solution: $t_{1/2} \;=\; \frac{a}{2k} \;=\; 50 \implies \frac{a}{k} \;=\; 100\;\text{min} \implies t_{3/4} \;=\; \frac{3a}{4k} \;=\; \frac{3}{4} \;\times\; 100 \;=\; 75\;\text{min}$.

questions.text: The graph of concentration of A (g L$^{-1}$) versus time (s) for $\mathrm{A\to B}$ is given: [FIGURE]. Assuming first-order kinetics and $\log2=0.3010$, the time (in seconds) for the concentration of A to reduce from $50\;\text{g L}^{-1}$ to $2.5\;\text{g L}^{-1}$ is ______ (nearest integer).
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: From $40\to20$ g L$^{-1}$ in $10$ s, $t_{1/2}\approx10$ s, so $k=\dfrac{\ln2}{10}$. // 📝 Solution: $t=\dfrac{1}{k}\ln\dfrac{50}{2.5}=\dfrac{10\log20}{\log2}=\dfrac{10(1.3010)}{0.3010}\approx43\;\text{s}$.

questions.text: Correct statements regarding Arrhenius equation among the following are : A. Factor $e^{-E_a / RT}$ corresponds to fraction of molecules having kinetic energy less than $E_a$. B. At a given temperature, lower the $E_a$, faster is the reaction. C. Increase in temperature by about $10^\circ\text{C}$ doubles the rate of reaction. D. Plot of $\log k$ vs $\frac{1}{T}$ gives a straight line with $\text{slope} \;=\; -\frac{E_a}{R}$. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall the physical meaning of the Boltzmann factor $e^{-E_a / RT}$ and the base-$10$ logarithmic form of the Arrhenius equation. // 📝 Solution: $e^{-E_a / RT}$ is the fraction of molecules with kinetic energy $\ge\; E_a$ (A is false); lower $E_a$ means larger $k$ and faster reaction (B is true); a $10^\circ\text{C}$ rise approximately doubles the rate (C is true); plot of $\log k$ vs $\frac{1}{T}$ has slope $-\frac{E_a}{2.303R}$ (D is false). Thus, B and C only are correct.

questions.text: For bacterial growth in a cell culture, the growth law is very similar to the law of radioactive decay. Which of the following graphs is most suitable to represent bacterial colony growth? ($N$ - number of bacteria at any time, $N_0$ - initial number of bacteria.)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Growth follows an exponential law with positive rate constant. // 📝 Solution: $N\;=\;N_0e^{Kt}\;\implies\;\frac{N}{N_0}$ rises exponentially with time, as in graph (3) [FIGURE]

questions.text: A wound was exposed to bacteria, and bacterial growth began at the same place. Later the wound was treated with an antibacterial medicine, and the rate of bacterial decay $r$ was found to be proportional to the square of the existing number of bacteria $N$. Before treatment, growth follows first-order kinetics. Which set of graphs correctly represents the "before" and "after" situations? [Given: $N$ = number of bacteria, $t$ = time] [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: First-order growth gives $N=N_0e^{kt}$; second-order decay gives $r=KN^2$. // 📝 Solution: $N/N_0=e^{kt}$ rises exponentially from 1, and $r=KN^2$ rises parabolically from zero with $N$ $\implies$ option (2).

questions.text: Consider the following first order gas phase reaction at constant temperature $\text{A}(\text{g}) \rightarrow 2\text{B}(\text{g}) \;+\; \text{C}(\text{g})$. If the total pressure of the gases is found to be $200\;\text{torr}$ after $23\;\text{sec}$. and $300\;\text{torr}$ upon the complete decomposition of A after a very long time, then the rate constant of the given reaction is _____ $\times\; 10^{-2}\;\text{s}^{-1}$ (nearest integer) $\left[\text{Given} : \log_{10}(2) \;=\; 0.301\right]$

Consider $\text{A} \xrightarrow{k_1} \text{B}$ and $\text{C} \xrightarrow{k_2} \text{D}$ are two reactions. If the rate constant $\left(k_1\right)$ of the $\text{A} \rightarrow \text{B}$ reaction can be expressed by the following equation $\log_{10} k \;=\; 14.34 \;-\; \frac{1.5 \times 10^4}{T/\text{K}}$ and activation energy of $\text{C} \rightarrow \text{D}$ reaction $\left(E_{a2}\right)$ is $\frac{1}{5}\text{th}$ of the $\text{A} \rightarrow \text{B}$ reaction $\left(E_{a1}\right)$, then the value of $\left(E_{a2}\right)$ is _____ $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. (Nearest Integer)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Compare the given equation with $\log_{10} k_1 \;=\; \log_{10} A \;-\; \frac{E_{a1}}{2.303RT}$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{E_{a1}}{2.303R} \;=\; 1.5 \;\times\; 10^4\;\text{K} \implies E_{a1} \;=\; 1.5 \;\times\; 10^4 \;\times\; 2.303 \;\times\; 8.314\;\text{J mol}^{-1} \;=\; 287.2\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1} \implies E_{a2} \;=\; \frac{287.2}{5} \;=\; 57.44 \;\approx\; 57\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$.

questions.text: $\text{A} \rightarrow \text{B}$ (first reaction), $\text{C} \rightarrow \text{D}$ (second reaction). Consider the above two first-order reactions. The rate constant for first reaction at $500\;\text{K}$ is double of the same at $300\;\text{K}$. At $500\;\text{K}$, $50\%$ of the reaction becomes complete in $2\;\text{hour}$. The activation energy of the second reaction is half of that of first reaction. If the rate constant at $500\;\text{K}$ of the second reaction becomes double of the rate constant of first reaction at the same temperature; then rate constant for the second reaction at $300\;\text{K}$ is _____ $\times\; 10^{-1}\;\text{hour}^{-1}$ (nearest integer).
questions.topic: Arrhenius Equation and First Order Kinetics

questions.text: The half-life of a zero-order reaction $\mathrm{A\to product}$ is $1$ hour when the initial concentration of A is $2.0\;\text{mol L}^{-1}$. The time required to decrease the concentration of A from $0.50$ to $0.25\;\text{mol L}^{-1}$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For zero order, $t_{1/2}=\dfrac{[A]_0}{2k}$. // 📝 Solution: $k=\dfrac{2.0}{2(1\;\text{h})}=1\;\text{mol L}^{-1}\text{h}^{-1}\implies t=\dfrac{0.50-0.25}{1}=0.25\;\text{h}=15\;\text{min}$.

questions.text: The molecule $A$ changes into its isomeric form $B$ by following first order kinetics at a temperature of $1000\;K$. If the energy barrier with respect to reactant energy for such isomeric transformation is $191.48\;kJ\;mol^{-1}$ and the frequency factor is $10^{20}$, the time required for $50\%$ molecules of $A$ to become $B$ is ______ picoseconds (nearest integer). [$R\;=\;8.314\;J\;K^{-1}\;mol^{-1}$]

Consider the following statements related to temperature dependence of rate constants. A. The Arrhenius equation holds true only for an elementary homogeneous reaction. B. The unit of A is the same as that of k in the Arrhenius equation. C. At a given temperature, a low activation energy means a fast reaction. D. A and $E_a$ depend on temperature. E. When $E_a\gg RT$, A and $E_a$ become interdependent. Choose the correct answer.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Check each statement against $k=Ae^{-E_a/RT}$. // 📝 Solution: A is false (it applies to complex reactions too), B and C are true, D is false ($A$ and $E_a$ are temperature independent), E is false $\implies$ option (3).

questions.text: The temperature at which the rate constants of the given below two gaseous reactions become equal is _____ $\text{K}$. (Nearest integer) $\text{X} \rightarrow \text{Y}, k_1 \;=\; 10^6 e^{-\frac{30000}{T}}$; $\text{P} \rightarrow \text{Q}, k_2 \;=\; 10^4 e^{-\frac{24000}{T}}$. Given: $\ln 10 \;=\; 2.303$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Equate $k_1 \;=\; k_2$ and solve for $T$ by taking natural logarithm. // 📝 Solution: $10^6 e^{-30000 / T} \;=\; 10^4 e^{-24000 / T} \implies 10^2 \;=\; e^{6000 / T} \implies 2\ln 10 \;=\; \frac{6000}{T} \implies T \;=\; \frac{6000}{2 \;\times\; 2.303} \;=\; 1302.65\;\text{K} \;\approx\; 1303\;\text{K}$.

questions.text: An organic compound undergoes first order decomposition. The time taken for decomposition to $\left(\frac{1}{8}\right)^{\text{th}}$ and $\left(\frac{1}{10}\right)^{\text{th}}$ of its initial concentration are $t_{1/8}$ and $t_{1/10}$ respectively. What is the value of $\frac{t_{1/8}}{t_{1/10}} \;\times\; 10$ ? $\left(\log 2 \;=\; 0.3\right)$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $t \;=\; \frac{2.303}{k}\log\left(\frac{\left[\text{A}\right]_0}{\left[\text{A}\right]_t}\right)$ for $\left[\text{A}\right]_t \;=\; \frac{\left[\text{A}\right]_0}{8}$ and $\frac{\left[\text{A}\right]_0}{10}$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{t_{1/8}}{t_{1/10}} \;\times\; 10 \;=\; \frac{\log 8}{\log 10} \;\times\; 10 \;=\; \frac{3\log 2}{1} \;\times\; 10 \;=\; 3 \;\times\; 0.3 \;\times\; 10 \;=\; 9$.

questions.text: $\mathrm{A(g)\to B(g)+C(g)}$ is a first-order reaction started with reactant A only. The total pressure is $P_t$ at time $t$ and $P_\infty$ at $t=\infty$. Which of the following expressions is correct for the rate constant $k$?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Here $P_0=P_\infty/2$ and $P_t=P_0+x$. // 📝 Solution: Remaining A $=P_0-x=P_\infty-P_t$ $\implies k=\dfrac{1}{t}\ln\dfrac{P_0}{P_\infty-P_t}=\dfrac{1}{t}\ln\dfrac{P_\infty}{2(P_\infty-P_t)}$ $\implies$ option (3).

questions.text: For the reaction $\mathrm{A\to products}$, the plot of $t_{1/2}$ versus $[A]_0$ has slope $76.92$ (appropriate units) [FIGURE]. The reaction is started with $2.5\;\text{mol L}^{-1}$ of A. The concentration of A at $10$ minutes is ______ $\times10^{-3}\;\text{mol L}^{-1}$ (nearest integer).
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $t_{1/2}\propto[A]_0$ indicates zero-order kinetics with $t_{1/2}=\dfrac{[A]_0}{2K}$. // 📝 Solution: Slope $=\dfrac{1}{2K}=76.92\implies K=6.5\times10^{-3}\;\text{mol L}^{-1}\text{min}^{-1}$ $\implies[A]_{10}=2.5-(6.5\times10^{-3})(10)=2.435\;\text{mol L}^{-1}=2435\times10^{-3}$.

questions.text: Given below are two statements : Statement I: The rate law for the reaction $\text{A} \;+\; \text{B} \rightarrow \text{C}$ is $\text{rate}\;(r) \;=\; k\left[\text{A}\right]^2\left[\text{B}\right]$. When the concentration of both A and B is doubled, the reaction rate is increased "$x$" times. Statement II : [FIGURE] The figure is showing "the variation in concentration against time plot" for a "$y$" order reaction. The value of $x \;+\; y$ is _____
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find $x$ by substituting $2\left[\text{A}\right]$ and $2\left[\text{B}\right]$ in the rate law, and find $y$ from the linear $\left[\text{R}\right]$ vs $t$ plot. // 📝 Solution: $r' \;=\; k\left(2\left[\text{A}\right]\right)^2\left(2\left[\text{B}\right]\right) \;=\; 8r \implies x \;=\; 8$. Linear concentration vs time plot with slope $-k$ represents a zero-order reaction $\implies y \;=\; 0 \implies x \;+\; y \;=\; 8 \;+\; 0 \;=\; 8$.
questions.topic: Rate Law and Zero Order Graph

questions.text: For $\mathrm{A_2+B_2\rightleftharpoons 2AB}$, the activation energies of the forward and backward reactions are $180$ and $200\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ respectively. A catalyst lowers the activation energy of both reactions by $100\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Catalyst does not alter the Gibbs energy change of a reaction
Catalyst can cause non-spontaneous reactions to occur
The enthalpy change for the reaction is $+20\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$
The enthalpy change for the catalysed reaction is different from that of the uncatalysed reaction

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A catalyst changes only activation energies, not $\Delta H$ or $\Delta G$. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta H=E_f-E_b=180-200=-20\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ (not $+20$); the catalysed $\Delta H$ is unchanged $\implies$ option (1).

questions.text: The half-life of radioisotopic bromine-82 is $36\;\text{hours}$. The fraction which remains after one day is _____ $\times\; 10^{-2}$. (Given $\text{antilog}\;0.2006 \;=\; 1.587$)

The rate law for a reaction between A and B is $R=k[A]^n[B]^m$. If the concentration of A is doubled and that of B is halved from their initial values, the ratio $\dfrac{r_2}{r_1}$ of the new rate to the initial rate is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Substitute the new concentrations into the rate law. // 📝 Solution: $\dfrac{r_2}{r_1}=\dfrac{k(2[A])^n(\tfrac{1}{2}[B])^m}{k[A]^n[B]^m}=2^{n}\cdot2^{-m}=2^{(n-m)}$ $\implies$ option (1).

questions.text: Statement I: The plot of half-life $t_{1/2}$ versus initial concentration $\left[R\right]_0$ is a line parallel to the concentration axis [FIGURE], which is valid for a first order reaction. Statement II: The plot of $\log\frac{\left[R\right]}{\left[R\right]_0}$ versus time is a straight line with slope $\frac{k}{2.303}$ [FIGURE], which is valid for a first order reaction. Choose the correct option.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For first order, $t_{1/2}$ is independent of $\left[R\right]_0$ and $\log\left[R\right]$ is linear in $t$. // 📝 Solution: $t_{1/2} \;=\; \frac{0.693}{k} \;\implies\; \text{independent of } \left[R\right]_0$; $\log\frac{\left[R\right]}{\left[R\right]_0} \;=\; -\frac{k}{2.303}t \;\implies\; \text{straight line, so both are true}$
questions.topic: Graphical analysis of first order kinetics

questions.text: A student has studied the decomposition of a gas $\text{AB}_3$ at $25^\circ\text{C}$. He obtained the following data: $p\;(\text{mm Hg})$: $50, 100, 200, 400$; Relative $t_{1/2}\;(\text{s})$: $4, 2, 1, 0.5$. The order of the reaction is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Half-life of an $n^{\text{th}}$ order reaction is related to initial pressure as $t_{1/2} \;\propto\; \left(P_0\right)^{1-n}$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{\left(t_{1/2}\right)_1}{\left(t_{1/2}\right)_2} \;=\; \left(\frac{P_{0,1}}{P_{0,2}}\right)^{1-n} \implies \frac{4}{2} \;=\; \left(\frac{50}{100}\right)^{1-n} \implies 2 \;=\; 2^{n-1} \implies n \;-\; 1 \;=\; 1 \implies n \;=\; 2$.

questions.text: For certain chemical reaction $\text{X} \rightarrow \text{Y}$, the rate of formation of product is plotted against the time as shown in the figure. [FIGURE] The number of Correct statement/s from the following is _____. (A) Over all order of this reaction is one (B) Order of this reaction can't be determined (C) In region-I and III, the reaction is of first and zero order respectively (D) In region-II, the reaction is of first order (E) In region-II, the order of reaction is in the range of $0.1$ to $0.9$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Examine the rate of formation of product vs time across the three regions for a complex reaction. // 📝 Solution: Since the rate increases with time initially and then becomes constant, it is a complex reaction whose overall order cannot be determined from this plot alone (Official NTA key gives $2$).

questions.text: The variation of the rate of an enzyme catalyzed reaction with substrate concentration is correctly represented by graph [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Enzyme-catalyzed reactions follow Michaelis-Menten kinetics (first order at low substrate concentration, zero order at high concentration). // 📝 Solution: At low substrate concentration $[S]$, rate increases linearly with $[S]$ (first order), and at high $[S]$, active sites saturate and rate becomes constant (zero order), which corresponds to graph c.

questions.text: Time required for completion of $99.9\%$ of a First order reaction is _____ times of half life $\left(t_{1/2}\right)$ of the reaction.

For a reaction taking place in three steps at same temperature, overall rate constant $K \;=\; \frac{K_1 K_2}{K_3}$. If $E_{a1}, E_{a2}$ and $E_{a3}$ are $40, 50$ and $60\;\text{kJ/mol}$ respectively, the overall $E_a$ is _____ $\text{kJ/mol}$.

The ratio of $\frac{^{14}\text{C}}{^{12}\text{C}}$ in a piece of wood is $\frac{1}{8}$ part that of atmosphere. If half life of $^{14}\text{C}$ is $5730\;\text{years}$, the age of wood sample is _____ years.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Since $\frac{1}{8} \;=\; \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^3$, the wood sample has undergone $3$ half-lives. // 📝 Solution: $\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{t / t_{1/2}} \;=\; \frac{1}{8} \;=\; \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^3 \implies t \;=\; 3 \;\times\; t_{1/2} \;=\; 3 \;\times\; 5730 \;=\; 17190\;\text{years}$.

questions.text: Decomposition of A is a first order reaction at $T(\text{K})$ and is given by $\text{A}(\text{g}) \rightarrow \text{B}(\text{g}) \;+\; \text{C}(\text{g})$. In a closed $1\;\text{L}$ vessel, $1\;\text{bar}$ $\text{A}(\text{g})$ is allowed to decompose at $T(\text{K})$. After $100\;\text{minutes}$, the total pressure was $1.5\;\text{bar}$. What is the rate constant (in $\text{min}^{-1}$) of the reaction ? $\left(\log 2 \;=\; 0.3\right)$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $P_t \;=\; P_0 \;+\; x$ to find the remaining partial pressure of A after $100\;\text{minutes}$. // 📝 Solution: $P_t \;=\; 1 \;+\; x \;=\; 1.5 \implies x \;=\; 0.5\;\text{bar} \implies P_{\text{A}} \;=\; 1 \;-\; 0.5 \;=\; 0.5\;\text{bar} \implies k \;=\; \frac{2.303}{100}\log\left(\frac{1}{0.5}\right) \;=\; \frac{2.303 \;\times\; 0.3}{100} \;\approx\; 6.9 \;\times\; 10^{-3}\;\text{min}^{-1}$.

questions.text: For conversion of compound $\text{A} \rightarrow \text{B}$, the rate constant of the reaction was found to be $4.6 \;\times\; 10^{-5}\;\text{L mol}^{-1}\;\text{s}^{-1}$. The order of the reaction is _____.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The unit of rate constant for an $n^{\text{th}}$ order reaction is $\left(\text{mol L}^{-1}\right)^{1-n}\text{s}^{-1}$. // 📝 Solution: Comparing $\text{L mol}^{-1}\;\text{s}^{-1} \;=\; \left(\text{mol L}^{-1}\right)^{1-n}\text{s}^{-1} \implies 1 \;-\; n \;=\; -1 \implies n \;=\; 2$.

questions.text: Consider the following transformation involving first order elementary reaction in each step at constant temperature as shown below. $\text{A} \;+\; \text{B} \underset{\text{Step 3}}{\overset{\text{Step 1}}{\rightleftharpoons}} \text{C} \xrightarrow{\text{Step 2}} \text{P}$. Some details of the above reactions are listed below: Step 1: Rate constant $k_1$, Activation energy $300\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$; Step 2: Rate constant $k_2$, Activation energy $200\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$; Step 3: Rate constant $k_3$, Activation energy $E_{a3}\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$. If the overall rate constant of the above transformation ($k$) is given as $k \;=\; \frac{k_1 k_2}{k_3}$ and the overall activation energy ($E_a$) is $400\;\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$, then the value of $E_{a3}$ is _____ $\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$ (nearest integer)
Time required for $99.9\%$ completion of a first order reaction is _____ times the time required for completion of $90\%$ reaction. (nearest integer)

The number of correct statement/s from the following is _____. A. Larger the activation energy, smaller is the value of the rate constant. B. The higher is the activation energy, higher is the value of the temperature coefficient. C. At lower temperatures, increase in temperature causes more change in the value of $k$ than at higher temperature. D. A plot of $\ln k$ vs $\frac{1}{T}$ is a straight line with slope equal to $-\frac{E_a}{R}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use the Arrhenius equation $k \;=\; A e^{-E_a / RT}$ and its logarithmic form $\ln k \;=\; \ln A \;-\; \frac{E_a}{RT}$. // 📝 Solution: From $k \;=\; A e^{-E_a / RT}$, as $E_a$ increases, $k$ decreases (A is correct) $\implies \ln \left(\frac{k_2}{k_1}\right) \;=\; \frac{E_a}{R}\left(\frac{1}{T_1} \;-\; \frac{1}{T_2}\right)$, so higher $E_a$ gives a higher temperature coefficient (B is correct) $\implies \ln k \;=\; \ln A \;-\; \frac{E_a}{R}\left(\frac{1}{T}\right)$ has slope $-\frac{E_a}{R}$ (D is correct), whereas statement C is incorrect. Thus, $3$ statements are correct.

questions.text: The half-life of $^{65}\text{Zn}$ is $245\;\text{days}$. After $x\;\text{days}$, $75\%$ of original activity remained. The value of $x$ in days is _____. (Nearest integer) (Given: $\log 3 \;=\; 0.4771$ and $\log 2 \;=\; 0.3010$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use the radioactive decay relation $A \;=\; A_0\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{x / t_{1/2}}$. // 📝 Solution: $0.75 \;=\; \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{x / 245} \implies \frac{x}{245}\log 2 \;=\; \log 4 \;-\; \log 3 \implies x \;=\; \frac{245 \;\times\; \left(0.6020 \;-\; 0.4771\right)}{0.3010} \;=\; \frac{245 \;\times\; 0.1249}{0.3010} \;=\; 101.66 \;\approx\; 102\;\text{days}$.

questions.text: A drug X becomes ineffective after 50% decomposition. The drug in a $16\text{ mg/mL}$ sample decomposes to $4\text{ mg/mL}$ in 12 months following first order kinetics. The shelf life of the drug (in months) is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Going from 16 to 4 takes a whole number of half-lives. // 📝 Solution: $16 \;\to\; 8 \;\to\; 4 \;\implies\; 2\,t_{1/2} \;=\; 12 \;\implies\; t_{1/2} \;=\; 6\text{ months}$, and ineffective at 50% decomposition $\implies$ shelf life $\;=\; 6$ months

questions.text: For $A_2 + B_2 \;\to\; 2AB$ the mechanism is: $A_2 \;\rightleftharpoons\; A + A$ (fast, $k_1$, $k_{-1}$); $A + B_2 \;\to\; AB + B$ (slow, $k_2$); $A + B \;\to\; AB$ (fast). The overall order of the reaction is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The rate is set by the slow step; eliminate the intermediate A using the fast equilibrium. // 📝 Solution: $\text{rate} \;=\; k_2\left[A\right]\left[B_2\right],\; \left[A\right] \;=\; \sqrt{\frac{k_1}{k_{-1}}\left[A_2\right]} \;\implies\; \text{rate} \;=\; k_2\sqrt{\frac{k_1}{k_{-1}}}\left[A_2\right]^{1/2}\left[B_2\right] \;\implies\; \text{order} \;=\; 1.5$

questions.text: The graph which represents the following reaction is : $\left(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\right)_3\text{C}-\text{Cl} \xrightarrow[\text{Pyridine}]{\text{OH}^-} \left(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\right)_3\text{C}-\text{OH}$ [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Hydrolysis of triphenylmethyl chloride proceeds via the $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$ mechanism due to high stability of the $\left(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\right)_3\text{C}^+$ carbocation. // 📝 Solution: Since it is an $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$ reaction, $\text{rate} \;=\; k\left[\left(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\right)_3\text{C}-\text{Cl}\right]$ (first order with respect to alkyl halide only and independent of $\left[\text{OH}^-\right]$ and $\left[\text{Pyridine}\right]$), giving a straight line passing through the origin in plot (3).

questions.text: A first order reaction has the rate constant, $k \;=\; 4.6 \;\times\; 10^{-3}\;\text{s}^{-1}$. The number of correct statement/s from the following is/are _____. Given : $\log 3 \;=\; 0.48$. A. Reaction completes in $1000\;\text{s}$. B. The reaction has a half-life of $500\;\text{s}$. C. The time required for $10\%$ completion is $25$ times the time required for $90\%$ completion. D. The degree of dissociation is equal to $\left(1 \;-\; e^{-kt}\right)$. E. The rate and the rate constant have the same unit.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use first-order integrated rate law $\left[\text{A}\right] \;=\; \left[\text{A}\right]_0 e^{-kt}$ and $t \;=\; \frac{2.303}{k}\log\left(\frac{a}{a \;-\; x}\right)$. // 📝 Solution: Degree of dissociation $\alpha \;=\; \frac{x}{a} \;=\; 1 \;-\; e^{-kt}$ (D is correct) $\implies \frac{t_{90\%}}{t_{10\%}} \;=\; \frac{\log\left(100 / 10\right)}{\log\left(100 / 90\right)} \;=\; \frac{1}{1 \;-\; 2\left(0.48\right)} \;=\; \frac{1}{0.04} \;=\; 25$ (C and D are counted in the official key as $2$).

questions.text: Consider the following plots of $\log k$ versus $\dfrac{1}{T}$ for three different reactions: [FIGURE]. The correct order of activation energies of these reactions is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: From the Arrhenius plot, $\text{slope}=-\dfrac{E_a}{2.303R}$, so a steeper line means larger $E_a$. // 📝 Solution: Steepness order is line (2) > line (1) > line (3) $\implies E_{a2}>E_{a1}>E_{a3}$ $\implies$ option (1).

questions.text: Consider the following reaction $\text{A} \;+\; \text{B} \rightarrow \text{C}$. The time taken for A to become $1/4^{\text{th}}$ of its initial concentration is twice the time taken to become $1/2$ of the same. Also, when the change of concentration of B is plotted against time, the resulting graph gives a straight line with a negative slope and a positive intercept on the concentration axis. The overall order of the reaction is _____
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Determine the order with respect to A from half-life relation and with respect to B from the concentration vs time graph. // 📝 Solution: Since $t_{3/4} \;=\; 2 \;\times\; t_{1/2}$ for A, order with respect to A is $1$. Since $\left[\text{B}\right]$ vs $t$ is a straight line with negative slope, order with respect to B is $0 \implies \text{Overall order} \;=\; 1 \;+\; 0 \;=\; 1$.

questions.text: For the reaction $R \;\to\; P$, the half-life $t_{1/2}$ is $200\text{ min}$ for $\left[A\right]_0 \;=\; 0.100\text{ M}$ and $100\text{ min}$ for $\left[A\right]_0 \;=\; 0.025\text{ M}$ ($\log 2 \;=\; 0.30$). Statements: A. The order of the reaction is $\frac{1}{2}$. B. For $\left[A\right]_0 \;=\; 1\text{ M}$, $t_{1/2} \;=\; 200\sqrt{10}\text{ min}$. C. The order becomes 1 if the concentration is changed from $0.100\text{ M}$ to $0.500\text{ M}$. D. $t_{1/2} \;=\; 800\text{ min}$ for $\left[A\right]_0 \;=\; 1.6\text{ M}$. Choose the correct answer.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $t_{1/2} \;\propto\; \left[A\right]_0^{\,1-n}$ for an nth-order reaction. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{200}{100} \;=\; 4^{\,1-n} \;\implies\; n \;=\; \frac{1}{2} \;\implies\; t_{1/2}\left(1\text{ M}\right) \;=\; 200\sqrt{10},\; t_{1/2}\left(1.6\text{ M}\right) \;=\; 200\sqrt{16} \;=\; 800$; order is constant, so C is false

questions.text: Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A) : An aqueous solution of $\text{KOH}$ when for volumetric analysis, its concentration should be checked before the use. Reason (R) : On aging, $\text{KOH}$ solution absorbs atmospheric $\text{CO}_2$. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.

options.text: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\text{KOH}$ is a secondary standard because it reacts with acidic atmospheric gases like $\text{CO}_2$. // 📝 Solution: $\text{KOH}$ absorbs atmospheric $\text{CO}_2$ on aging ($2\text{KOH} \;+\; \text{CO}_2 \;\rightarrow\; \text{K}_2\text{CO}_3 \;+\; \text{H}_2\text{O}$), which alters its concentration; hence its concentration must be standardized before volumetric use.

questions.text: $2\text{MnO}_4^- \;+\; b\text{I}^- \;+\; c\text{H}_2\text{O} \;\rightarrow\; x\text{I}_2 \;+\; y\text{MnO}_2 \;+\; z\text{OH}^-$. If the above equation is balanced with integer coefficients, the value of $z$ is _______
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Balance the redox reaction in neutral/alkaline medium using the ion-electron method, keeping the coefficient of $\text{MnO}_4^-$ as $2$. // 📝 Solution: Reduction half: $2\text{MnO}_4^- \;+\; 4\text{H}_2\text{O} \;+\; 6\text{e}^- \;\rightarrow\; 2\text{MnO}_2 \;+\; 8\text{OH}^-$. Oxidation half: $6\text{I}^- \;\rightarrow\; 3\text{I}_2 \;+\; 6\text{e}^-$. Adding both gives $2\text{MnO}_4^- \;+\; 6\text{I}^- \;+\; 4\text{H}_2\text{O} \;\rightarrow\; 3\text{I}_2 \;+\; 2\text{MnO}_2 \;+\; 8\text{OH}^- \;\implies\; z \;=\; 8$.

questions.text: Only $2\;\text{mL}$ of $\text{KMnO}_4$ solution of unknown molarity is required to reach the end point of a titration of $20\;\text{mL}$ of oxalic acid ($2\;\text{M}$) in acidic medium. The molarity of $\text{KMnO}_4$ solution should be _______ $\text{M}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Equate the gram equivalents of $\text{KMnO}_4$ ($n$-factor $= 5$) and oxalic acid ($n$-factor $= 2$) at the equivalence point. // 📝 Solution: $\text{eq. of KMnO}_4 \;=\; \text{eq. of H}_2\text{C}_2\text{O}_4 \;\implies\; M \;\times\; 2 \;\times\; 5 \;=\; 2 \;\times\; 20 \;\times\; 2 \;\implies\; M \;=\; 8\;\text{M}$.

questions.text: $25\;\text{mL}$ of an aqueous solution of $\text{KCl}$ was found to require $20\;\text{mL}$ of $1\;\text{M}\;\text{AgNO}_3$ solution when titrated using $\text{K}_2\text{CrO}_4$ as an indicator. What is the depression in freezing point of $\text{KCl}$ solution of the given concentration? _________ (Nearest integer). (Given : $K_f \;=\; 2.0\;\text{K kg mol}^{-1}$) Assume 1) $100\%$ ionization and 2) density of the aqueous solution as $1\;\text{g mL}^{-1}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find moles of $\text{KCl}$ from precipitation titration with $\text{AgNO}_3$, calculate molality $m$, and use $\Delta T_f \;=\; i K_f m$. // 📝 Solution: $\text{mmol of KCl} \;=\; \text{mmol of AgNO}_3 \;=\; 20 \;\times\; 1 \;=\; 20\;\text{mmol} \;\implies\; \text{Mass of solvent} \;=\; 25 \;-\; \left(0.02 \;\times\; 74.5\right) \;=\; 23.51\;\text{g} \;\implies\; m \;=\; \frac{0.02}{0.02351} \;=\; 0.85\;\text{mol kg}^{-1} \;\implies\; \Delta T_f \;=\; i K_f m \;=\; 2 \;\times\; 2.0 \;\times\; 0.85 \;=\; 3.4\;\text{K} \;\approx\; 3\;\text{K}$.

questions.text: Given below are two statements : Statement I: $\text{S}_8$ solid undergoes disproportionation reaction under alkaline conditions to form $\text{S}^{2-}$ and $\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-}$. Statement II: $\text{ClO}_4^-$ can undergo disproportionation reaction under acidic condition. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

options.text: Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
Both statement I and statement II are correct

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Check whether chlorine in $\text{ClO}_4^-$ is in its highest possible oxidation state. // 📝 Solution: Statement I is correct: $\text{S}_8 \;+\; 12\text{OH}^- \;\rightarrow\; 4\text{S}^{2-} \;+\; 2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-} \;+\; 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Statement II is incorrect: in $\text{ClO}_4^-$, chlorine is in its maximum oxidation state ($+7$), so it cannot be oxidized further and cannot disproportionate.

questions.text: $200\;\text{cc}$ of $x \;\times\; 10^{-3}\;\text{M}$ potassium dichromate is required to oxidise $750\;\text{cc}$ of $0.6\;\text{M}$ Mohr's salt solution in acidic medium. Here $x \;=\; $ ____.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Equate the milliequivalents of $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ ($n$-factor $= 6$) and Mohr's salt ($n$-factor $= 1$). // 📝 Solution: $\text{meq of K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7 \;=\; \text{meq of Mohr's salt} \;\implies\; 200 \;\times\; \left(x \;\times\; 10^{-3}\right) \;\times\; 6 \;=\; 750 \;\times\; 0.6 \;\times\; 1 \;\implies\; 1.2x \;=\; 450 \;\implies\; x \;=\; 375$.

questions.text: Compounds that should not be used as primary standards in titrimetric analysis are: A. $\text{Na}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ B. Oxalic acid C. NaOH D. $\text{FeSO}_4\cdot6\text{H}_2\text{O}$ E. Sodium tetraborate. Choose the most appropriate answer.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A primary standard is pure, stable, non-hygroscopic and of exactly known composition. // 📝 Solution: NaOH is hygroscopic, $\text{FeSO}_4\cdot6\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is easily oxidised, and $\text{Na}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ is treated as hygroscopic in the key $\implies$ A, C and D are unsuitable $\implies$ D.

questions.text: Identify the incorrect statements regarding primary standard of titrimetric analysis. (A) It should be purely available in dry form. (B) It should not undergo chemical change in air. (C) It should be hygroscopic and should react with another chemical instantaneously and stoichiometrically. (D) It should be readily soluble in water. (E) $\text{KMnO}_4$ & $\text{NaOH}$ can be used as primary standard. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A primary standard must be non-hygroscopic, pure, stable in air, and have a high molar mass. // 📝 Solution: A primary standard should not be hygroscopic (so statement C is incorrect), and $\text{KMnO}_4$ and $\text{NaOH}$ are secondary standards (so statement E is incorrect) $\implies$ (C) and (E) only.

questions.text: The density of a monobasic strong acid (Molar mass $24.2\;\text{g mol}^{-1}$) is $1.21\;\text{kg L}^{-1}$. The volume of its solution required for the complete neutralization of $25\;\text{mL}$ of $0.24\;\text{M}\;\text{NaOH}$ is _______ $\times\; 10^{-2}\;\text{mL}$ (Nearest integer)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Equate millimoles of monobasic strong acid to millimoles of $\text{NaOH}$ and use density to find volume. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Millimoles of acid} \;=\; \text{Millimoles of NaOH} \;=\; 0.24 \;\times\; 25 \;=\; 6\;\text{mmol} \;\implies\; \text{Mass of acid} \;=\; 6 \;\times\; 10^{-3} \;\times\; 24.2\;\text{g} \;\implies\; \text{Volume } V \;=\; \frac{\text{Mass}}{\text{Density}} \;=\; \frac{6 \;\times\; 10^{-3} \;\times\; 24.2}{1.21}\;\text{mL} \;=\; 0.12\;\text{mL} \;=\; 12 \;\times\; 10^{-2}\;\text{mL}$.

questions.text: Thiosulphate reacts differently with iodine and bromine in the reactions given below: $2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-} \;+\; \text{I}_2 \;\rightarrow\; \text{S}_4\text{O}_6^{2-} \;+\; 2\text{I}^-$; $\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-} \;+\; 5\text{Br}_2 \;+\; 5\text{H}_2\text{O} \;\rightarrow\; 2\text{SO}_4^{2-} \;+\; 4\text{Br}^- \;+\; 10\text{H}^+$. Which of the following statement justifies the above dual behaviour of thiosulphate?

options.text: Bromine is a stronger oxidant than iodine
Thiosulphate undergoes oxidation by bromine and reduction by iodine in these reaction
Bromine is a weaker oxidant than iodine
Bromine undergoes oxidation and iodine undergoes reduction in these reactions

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Compare the change in average oxidation state of sulfur in $\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-}$ when oxidized by $\text{I}_2$ versus $\text{Br}_2$. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Br}_2$ oxidizes sulfur from $+2$ in $\text{S}_2\text{O}_3^{2-}$ to $+6$ in $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$, whereas $\text{I}_2$ only oxidizes it to $+2.5$ in $\text{S}_4\text{O}_6^{2-}$ $\implies$ Bromine is a stronger oxidant than iodine.

questions.text: Chlorine undergoes disproportionation in alkaline medium as shown below : $a\;\text{Cl}_{2\left(\text{g}\right)} \;+\; b\;\text{OH}^-_{\left(\text{aq}\right)} \;\rightarrow\; c\;\text{ClO}^-_{\left(\text{aq}\right)} \;+\; d\;\text{Cl}^-_{\left(\text{aq}\right)} \;+\; e\;\text{H}_2\text{O}_{\left(\text{l}\right)}$. The values of $a$, $b$, $c$ and $d$ in a balanced redox reaction are respectively:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Balance the disproportionation of $\text{Cl}_2$ in cold dilute alkaline medium to $\text{ClO}^-$ and $\text{Cl}^-$. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Cl}_2 \;+\; 2\text{OH}^- \;\rightarrow\; \text{ClO}^- \;+\; \text{Cl}^- \;+\; \text{H}_2\text{O} \;\implies\; a \;=\; 1, b \;=\; 2, c \;=\; 1 \text{ and } d \;=\; 1$.

questions.text: The species which does not undergo disproportionation reaction is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Disproportionation needs an intermediate oxidation state. // 📝 Solution: In $\text{ClO}_4^-$, $x\;+\;4\left(-2\right)\;=\;-1\implies\;x\;=\;+7$ (maximum) $\implies$ it cannot be oxidised further and cannot disproportionate

questions.text: $500\;\text{mL}$ of $1.2\;\text{M}\;\text{KI}$ solution is mixed with $500\;\text{mL}$ of $0.2\;\text{M}\;\text{KMnO}_4$ solution in basic medium. The liberated iodine was titrated with standard $0.1\;\text{M}\;\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3$ solution in the presence of starch indicator till the blue color disappeared. The volume (in $\text{L}$) of $\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3$ consumed is ____. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Equate the gram equivalents of limiting reagent $\text{KMnO}_4$ ($n$-factor $= 3$ in basic medium) with $\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3$ ($n$-factor $= 1$). // 📝 Solution: $\text{eq. of KMnO}_4 \;=\; \text{eq. of I}_2 \;=\; \text{eq. of Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3 \;\implies\; 0.2 \;\times\; \frac{500}{1000} \;\times\; 3 \;=\; 0.1 \;\times\; V \;\times\; 1 \;\implies\; V \;=\; 3\;\text{L}$.

questions.text: $0.1\;M$ solution of $KI$ reacts with excess of $H_2SO_4$ and $KIO_3$ solutions according to $5I^-\;+\;IO_3^-\;+\;6H^+\;\rightarrow\;3I_2\;+\;3H_2O$. Identify the correct statements: (A) $200\;mL$ of $KI$ solution reacts with $0.004\;mol$ of $KIO_3$ (B) $200\;mL$ of $KI$ solution reacts with $0.006\;mol$ of $H_2SO_4$ (C) $0.5\;L$ of $KI$ solution produced $0.005\;mol$ of $I_2$ (D) Equivalent weight of $KIO_3$ is $\frac{\text{Molecular weight}}{5}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use the mole ratio from the balanced equation and the $n$-factor of $IO_3^-$. // 📝 Solution: $n_{KI}\;=\;0.1\times0.2\;=\;0.02\;mol\;\implies\;n_{KIO_3}\;=\;\frac{0.02}{5}\;=\;0.004\;mol$ and $n\text{-factor}\;=\;5\;\implies\;E\;=\;\frac{M}{5}$, so only (A) and (D) are correct
questions.topic: Redox titrations and equivalent weight of KIO3

questions.text: Among the following halogens $\text{F}_2$, $\text{Cl}_2$, $\text{Br}_2$ and $\text{I}_2$, which can undergo disproportionation reactions?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: An element in $0$ oxidation state can disproportionate only if it can exhibit both negative and positive oxidation states. // 📝 Solution: $\text{F}_2$ being the most electronegative element shows only $-1$ oxidation state and never positive oxidation states, whereas $\text{Cl}_2$, $\text{Br}_2$, and $\text{I}_2$ can exhibit both $-1$ and positive oxidation states ($+1, +3, +5, +7$) and thus undergo disproportionation.

questions.text: Statement I: In the oxalic acid vs $\text{KMnO}_4$ (in presence of dil $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$) titration the solution needs to be heated initially to $60^\circ\text{C}$, but no heating is required in the Ferrous ammonium sulphate (FAS) vs $\text{KMnO}_4$ titration (in presence of dil $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$). Statement II: In oxalic acid vs $\text{KMnO}_4$ titration, the initial formation of $\text{MnSO}_4$ takes place at high temperature, which then acts as catalyst for further reaction. In the case of FAS vs $\text{KMnO}_4$, heating oxidizes $\text{Fe}^{2+}$ into $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ by oxygen of air and error may be introduced in the experiment. Choose the correct answer.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall autocatalysis by $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ and the air-oxidation of $\text{Fe}^{2+}$. // 📝 Solution: Oxalic acid reaction has high activation energy and is catalysed by $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ formed on heating; $\text{Fe}^{2+}\to\text{Fe}^{3+}$ in hot air gives error $\implies$ both statements true

questions.text: Total number of species from the following which can undergo disproportionation reaction _______. $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2, \text{ClO}_3^-, \text{P}_4, \text{Cl}_2, \text{Ag}, \text{Cu}^{+1}, \text{F}_2, \text{NO}_2, \text{K}^+$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Identify species containing an element in an intermediate oxidation state that can both increase and decrease. // 📝 Solution: Species with intermediate oxidation states that undergo disproportionation are $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ ($\text{O}$ in $-1$), $\text{ClO}_3^-$ ($\text{Cl}$ in $+5$), $\text{P}_4$ ($\text{P}$ in $0$), $\text{Cl}_2$ ($\text{Cl}$ in $0$), $\text{Cu}^{+1}$ ($\text{Cu}$ in $+1$), and $\text{NO}_2$ ($\text{N}$ in $+4$) $\implies$ Total $= 6$.

questions.text: The number of electrons involved in the reduction of permanganate to manganese dioxide in acidic medium is _______
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Calculate the change in oxidation state of $\text{Mn}$ from $\text{MnO}_4^-$ to $\text{MnO}_2$. // 📝 Solution: $\text{MnO}_4^- \;+\; 4\text{H}^+ \;+\; 3\text{e}^- \;\rightarrow\; \text{MnO}_2 \;+\; 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \;\implies\;$ Oxidation state of $\text{Mn}$ changes from $+7$ to $+4$, involving $3$ electrons.

questions.text: $X$ and $Y$ are the number of electrons involved, respectively during the oxidation of $\text{I}^-$ to $\text{I}_2$ and $\text{S}^{2-}$ to $\text{S}$ by acidified $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$. The value of $X \;+\; Y$ is ____.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: One mole of $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$ accepts $6$ moles of electrons in acidic medium during reduction to $2\text{Cr}^{3+}$. // 📝 Solution: Since $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} \;+\; 14\text{H}^+ \;+\; 6\text{e}^- \;\rightarrow\; 2\text{Cr}^{3+} \;+\; 7\text{H}_2\text{O}$ involves $6$ electrons, the balanced oxidation half-reactions are $6\text{I}^- \;\rightarrow\; 3\text{I}_2 \;+\; 6\text{e}^-$ ($X \;=\; 6$) and $3\text{S}^{2-} \;\rightarrow\; 3\text{S} \;+\; 6\text{e}^-$ ($Y \;=\; 6$) $\implies\; X \;+\; Y \;=\; 6 \;+\; 6 \;=\; 12$.

questions.text: Match List - I with List - II. List - I (Reaction): (A) $\text{N}_{2\left(\text{g}\right)} \;+\; \text{O}_{2\left(\text{g}\right)} \;\rightarrow\; 2\text{NO}_{\left(\text{g}\right)}$, (B) $2\text{Pb}\left(\text{NO}_3\right)_{2\left(\text{s}\right)} \;\rightarrow\; 2\text{PbO}_{\left(\text{s}\right)} \;+\; 4\text{NO}_{2\left(\text{g}\right)} \;+\; \text{O}_{2\left(\text{g}\right)}$, (C) $2\text{Na}_{\left(\text{s}\right)} \;+\; 2\text{H}_2\text{O}_{\left(\text{l}\right)} \;\rightarrow\; 2\text{NaOH}_{\left(\text{aq.}\right)} \;+\; \text{H}_{2\left(\text{g}\right)}$, (D) $2\text{NO}_{2\left(\text{g}\right)} \;+\; 2\text{OH}^-_{\left(\text{aq.}\right)} \;\rightarrow\; \text{NO}^-_{2\left(\text{aq.}\right)} \;+\; \text{NO}^-_{3\left(\text{aq.}\right)} \;+\; \text{H}_2\text{O}_{\left(\text{l}\right)}$. List - II (Type of redox reaction): (I) Decomposition, (II) Displacement, (III) Disproportionation, (IV) Combination. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Classify each redox reaction based on whether reactants combine, decompose, displace, or disproportionate. // 📝 Solution: (A) Two elements combine to form $\text{NO}$ $\rightarrow$ (IV) Combination; (B) Single compound breaks down on heating $\rightarrow$ (I) Decomposition; (C) $\text{Na}$ displaces $\text{H}_2$ from water $\rightarrow$ (II) Displacement; (D) $\text{N}$ in $\text{NO}_2$ ($+4$) is simultaneously reduced ($+3$) and oxidized ($+5$) $\rightarrow$ (III) Disproportionation.

questions.text: $\text{KMnO}_4$ decomposes on heating at $513\;\text{K}$ to form $\text{O}_2$ along with
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall the thermal decomposition reaction of potassium permanganate at $513\;\text{K}$. // 📝 Solution: $2\text{KMnO}_4 \;\xrightarrow{513\;\text{K}}\; \text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4 \;+\; \text{MnO}_2 \;+\; \text{O}_2 \;\implies\;$ Forms $\text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4$ and $\text{MnO}_2$ along with $\text{O}_2$.

questions.text: An indicator '$\text{X}$' is used for studying the effect of variation in concentration of iodide on the rate of reaction of iodide ion with $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ at room temp. The indicator '$\text{X}$' forms blue colored complex with compound '$\text{A}$' present in the solution. The indicator '$\text{X}$' and compound '$\text{A}$' respectively are
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Iodide is oxidized by $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ to $\text{I}_2$, which forms a deep blue complex with starch. // 📝 Solution: $2\text{I}^- \;+\; \text{H}_2\text{O}_2 \;+\; 2\text{H}^+ \;\rightarrow\; \text{I}_2\;\left(\text{A}\right) \;+\; 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \;\implies\; \text{I}_2 \;+\; \text{Starch}\;\left(\text{X}\right) \;\rightarrow\; \text{Blue complex}$. Thus, indicator '$\text{X}$' is starch and compound '$\text{A}$' is iodine.

questions.text: Given below are two statements : Statement (I) : Potassium hydrogen phthalate is a primary standard for standardisation of sodium hydroxide solution. Statement (II) : In this titration phenolphthalein can be used as indicator. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Potassium hydrogen phthalate (KHP) is a weak acid primary standard titrated against strong base $\text{NaOH}$ using phenolphthalein. // 📝 Solution: KHP is non-hygroscopic with a high molar mass, making it an ideal primary standard for $\text{NaOH}$. Since the equivalence point of this weak acid-strong base titration lies in the basic pH range ($8.3 - 10$), phenolphthalein is a suitable indicator.

questions.text: One mole of $\text{Cl}_{2\left(\text{g}\right)}$ was passed into $2\;\text{L}$ of cold $2\;\text{M}\;\text{KOH}$ solution. After the reaction, the concentrations of $\text{Cl}^-$, $\text{ClO}^-$ and $\text{OH}^-$ are respectively (assume volume remains constant)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use the stoichiometry of $\text{Cl}_2 \;+\; 2\text{OH}^- \;\rightarrow\; \text{Cl}^- \;+\; \text{ClO}^- \;+\; \text{H}_2\text{O}$ in cold $\text{KOH}$. // 📝 Solution: Initial moles: $n_{\text{Cl}_2} \;=\; 1\;\text{mol}$, $n_{\text{OH}^-} \;=\; 2 \;\times\; 2 \;=\; 4\;\text{mol}$. After reaction, $1\;\text{mol}\;\text{Cl}^-$ and $1\;\text{mol}\;\text{ClO}^-$ form, leaving $4 \;-\; 2 \;=\; 2\;\text{mol}\;\text{OH}^-$ in $2\;\text{L}$ solution $\implies\; \left[\text{Cl}^-\right] \;=\; 0.5\;\text{M}, \left[\text{ClO}^-\right] \;=\; 0.5\;\text{M}, \left[\text{OH}^-\right] \;=\; 1\;\text{M}$.

questions.text: Some $CO_2$ gas was kept in a sealed container at $1\;atm$ and $273\;K$. This entire amount of $CO_2$ was passed through aqueous $Ca(OH)_2$. The excess unreacted $Ca(OH)_2$ was neutralized with $40\;mL$ of $0.1\;M$ $HCl$. If the volume of the sealed container of $CO_2$ was $x$, then $x$ is ______ $cm^3$ (nearest integer). [The entire $CO_2$ reacted with exactly half the initial amount of $Ca(OH)_2$ present in the solution.]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Excess base equals the HCl used; $CO_2$ consumed half of the base, so $n_{CO_2}\;=\;n_{excess}$. // 📝 Solution: $2n_{excess}\;=\;0.1\times0.04\;=\;4\times10^{-3}\;mol\;\implies\;n_{CO_2}\;=\;2\times10^{-3}\;mol$ and $V\;=\;2\times10^{-3}\times22400\;=\;44.8\;cm^3\;\approx\;45$
questions.topic: Back titration and gas volume at STP

questions.text: If $50\;\text{mL}$ of $0.5\;\text{M}$ oxalic acid is required to neutralise $25\;\text{mL}$ of $\text{NaOH}$ solution, the amount of $\text{NaOH}$ in $50\;\text{mL}$ of given $\text{NaOH}$ solution is _______ $\text{g}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Equate gram equivalents of dibasic oxalic acid and monobasic $\text{NaOH}$ to find molarity of $\text{NaOH}$. // 📝 Solution: $\text{eq. of Oxalic acid} \;=\; \text{eq. of NaOH} \;\implies\; 50 \;\times\; 0.5 \;\times\; 2 \;=\; 25 \;\times\; M_{\text{NaOH}} \;\times\; 1 \;\implies\; M_{\text{NaOH}} \;=\; 2\;\text{M} \;\implies\; \text{Mass of NaOH in } 50\;\text{mL} \;=\; 2 \;\times\; \frac{50}{1000} \;\times\; 40 \;=\; 4\;\text{g}$.

questions.text: Identify the correct statements : A. Hydrated salts can be used as primary standard. B. Primary standard should not undergo any reaction with air. C. Reactions of primary standard with another substance should be instantaneous and stoichiometric. D. Primary standard should not be soluble in water. E. Primary standard should have low relative molar mass. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.text: A, B, C and E Only

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A primary standard must be soluble in water, stable in air, have a high relative molar mass, and can include stable hydrated salts like oxalic acid dihydrate or Mohr's salt. // 📝 Solution: Statements A, B, and C are correct, whereas D and E are incorrect because a primary standard must be readily soluble in water and have a high relative molar mass to minimize weighing errors.

questions.text: Which of the following cannot function as an oxidising agent?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A species in its lowest possible oxidation state cannot accept electrons (cannot be reduced) and hence cannot act as an oxidizing agent. // 📝 Solution: In $\text{N}^{3-}$, nitrogen is in its minimum possible oxidation state of $-3$, so it cannot be reduced further and cannot function as an oxidizing agent.

questions.text: The volume of $\text{HCl}$, containing $73\;\text{g L}^{-1}$, required to completely neutralise $\text{NaOH}$ obtained by reacting $0.69\;\text{g}$ of metallic sodium with water, is _______ $\text{mL}$. (Nearest Integer) (Given : molar Masses of $\text{Na}$, $\text{Cl}$, $\text{O}$, $\text{H}$ are $23$, $35.5$, $16$ and $1\;\text{g mol}^{-1}$ respectively)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find moles of $\text{NaOH}$ produced from $\text{Na}$ using stoichiometry, then equate equivalents with $\text{HCl}$. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Moles of Na} \;=\; \frac{0.69}{23} \;=\; 0.03\;\text{mol} \;=\; \text{Moles of NaOH} \;\implies\; \text{Molarity of HCl} \;=\; \frac{73}{36.5} \;=\; 2\;\text{M} \;\implies\; 2 \;\times\; V\;\left(\text{in L}\right) \;=\; 0.03 \;\implies\; V \;=\; 0.015\;\text{L} \;=\; 15\;\text{mL}$.

questions.text: $\text{KMnO}_4$ oxidises $\text{I}^-$ in acidic and neutral/faintly alkaline solution, respectively to
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall the standard redox reactions of $\text{KMnO}_4$ with $\text{KI}$ in acidic versus neutral/faintly alkaline media. // 📝 Solution: In acidic medium: $2\text{MnO}_4^- \;+\; 10\text{I}^- \;+\; 16\text{H}^+ \;\rightarrow\; 2\text{Mn}^{2+} \;+\; 5\text{I}_2 \;+\; 8\text{H}_2\text{O}$. In neutral/faintly alkaline medium: $2\text{MnO}_4^- \;+\; \text{I}^- \;+\; \text{H}_2\text{O} \;\rightarrow\; 2\text{MnO}_2 \;+\; 2\text{OH}^- \;+\; \text{IO}_3^-$.

questions.text: In acidic medium, $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ shows oxidising action as represented in the half reaction $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} \;+\; X\text{H}^+ \;+\; Y\text{e}^- \;\rightarrow\; 2\text{A} \;+\; Z\text{H}_2\text{O}$. $X$, $Y$, $Z$ and $\text{A}$ are respectively are:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Write the balanced reduction half-reaction of dichromate ion in acidic medium. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} \;+\; 14\text{H}^+ \;+\; 6\text{e}^- \;\rightarrow\; 2\text{Cr}^{3+} \;+\; 7\text{H}_2\text{O} \;\implies\; X \;=\; 14, Y \;=\; 6, Z \;=\; 7 \text{ and A} \;=\; \text{Cr}^{3+}$.

questions.text: Which will undergo deprotonation most readily in basic medium? [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The compound with the most acidic active methylene proton forms the most resonance-stabilized carbanion upon deprotonation. // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] Compound $\text{a}$ (a $\beta$-diketone) undergoes deprotonation most readily because the resulting conjugate base (carbanion) is stabilized by strong resonance delocalization over two keto groups without cross-conjugation from $-\text{OMe}$ ester groups.

questions.text: $5\;\text{g}$ of $\text{NaOH}$ was dissolved in deionized water to prepare a $450\;\text{mL}$ stock solution. What volume (in $\text{mL}$) of this solution would be required to prepare $500\;\text{mL}$ of $0.1\;\text{M}$ solution? Given : Molar Mass of $\text{Na}$, $\text{O}$ and $\text{H}$ is $23$, $16$ and $1\;\text{g mol}^{-1}$ respectively
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use the dilution law $M_1 V_1 \;=\; M_2 V_2$ after finding the molarity of the stock solution. // 📝 Solution: Molarity of stock solution $M_1 \;=\; \frac{5}{40} \;\times\; \frac{1000}{450}\;\text{M} \;\implies\; M_1 V_1 \;=\; M_2 V_2 \;\implies\; \left(\frac{5}{40} \;\times\; \frac{1000}{450}\right) \;\times\; V_1 \;=\; 0.1 \;\times\; 500 \;\implies\; V_1 \;=\; 180\;\text{mL}$.

questions.text: Which of the following reactions are disproportionation reactions? (A) $\text{Cu}^+ \;\rightarrow\; \text{Cu}^{2+} \;+\; \text{Cu}$, (B) $3\text{MnO}_4^{2-} \;+\; 4\text{H}^+ \;\rightarrow\; 2\text{MnO}_4^- \;+\; \text{MnO}_2 \;+\; 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$, (C) $2\text{KMnO}_4 \;\rightarrow\; \text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4 \;+\; \text{MnO}_2 \;+\; \text{O}_2$, (D) $2\text{MnO}_4^- \;+\; 3\text{Mn}^{2+} \;+\; 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \;\rightarrow\; 5\text{MnO}_2 \;+\; 4\text{H}^+$. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: In a disproportionation reaction, the same element in a single oxidation state is simultaneously oxidized and reduced. // 📝 Solution: In (A), $\text{Cu}^+$ ($+1$) changes to $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ ($+2$) and $\text{Cu}$ ($0$). In (B), $\text{MnO}_4^{2-}$ ($+6$) changes to $\text{MnO}_4^-$ ($+7$) and $\text{MnO}_2$ ($+4$). Reaction (C) is thermal decomposition and (D) is comproportionation $\implies$ (A), (B).

questions.text: Match LIST-I (Redox Reaction) with LIST-II (Type of Redox Reaction): (A) $\text{CH}_4\left(g\right)+2\text{O}_2\left(g\right)\xrightarrow{\Delta}\text{CO}_2\left(g\right)+2\text{H}_2\text{O}\left(l\right)$ (B) $2\text{NaH}\left(s\right)\xrightarrow{\Delta}2\text{Na}\left(s\right)+\text{H}_2\left(g\right)$ (C) $\text{V}_2\text{O}_5\left(s\right)+5\text{Ca}\left(s\right)\xrightarrow{\Delta}2\text{V}\left(s\right)+5\text{CaO}\left(s\right)$ (D) $2\text{H}_2\text{O}_2\left(aq\right)\xrightarrow{\Delta}2\text{H}_2\text{O}\left(l\right)+\text{O}_2\left(g\right)$ ; (I) Disproportionation reaction (II) Combination reaction (III) Decomposition reaction (IV) Displacement reaction
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Classify each reaction by how species combine, split, displace or both oxidise and reduce one element. // 📝 Solution: A $\to$ combination (II), B $\to$ decomposition (III), C $\to$ displacement (IV), D $\to$ disproportionation (I) $\implies$ A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I

questions.text: The wavelength of spectral line obtained in the spectrum of $\text{Li}^{2+}$ ion, when the transition takes place between two levels whose sum is $4$ and difference is $2$, is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Determine energy levels $n_1$ and $n_2$ and use $\frac{1}{\lambda} = R Z^2 \left(\frac{1}{n_1^2} - \frac{1}{n_2^2}\right)$. // 📝 Solution: $n_2 + n_1 = 4$ and $n_2 - n_1 = 2 \implies n_2 = 3, \; n_1 = 1$. For $\text{Li}^{2+}$ ($Z = 3$), $\frac{1}{\lambda} = R(3^2)\left(1 - \frac{1}{9}\right) = 8R \implies \lambda = \frac{1}{8 \times 1.097 \times 10^7} \approx 1.14 \times 10^{-6}\;\text{cm}$.

questions.text: Choose the Incorrect Statement about Dalton's Atomic Theory:

options.text: $\text{Compounds are formed when atoms of different elements combine in any ratio.}$
$\text{Compounds are formed when atoms of different elements combine in a fixed ratio. All the atoms of a given element have identical properties including identical mass.}$

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Dalton's theory incorporates the law of definite proportions. // 📝 Solution: According to Dalton's atomic theory, compounds are formed when atoms of different elements combine in fixed, simple whole-number ratios, not in any arbitrary ratio. Hence, statement (3) is incorrect.

questions.text: Heat treatment of muscular pain involves radiation of wavelength of about $900\;nm$. Which spectral line of H atom is suitable for this? Given : Rydberg constant $R_H \;=\; 10^5\;cm^{-1},\; h \;=\; 6.6 \times 10^{-34}\;J\;s,\; c \;=\; 3 \times 10^8\;m/s$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\frac{1}{\lambda} \;=\; R_H \left( \frac{1}{n_1^2} - \frac{1}{n_2^2} \right)$ // 📝 Solution: $\frac{1}{\lambda R_H} \;=\; \frac{1}{9 \times 10^{-5} \times 10^5} \;=\; \frac{1}{9} \implies n_1 \;=\; 3,\; n_2 \;=\; \infty \implies \text{Paschen}\;\infty \to 3$

questions.text: Which transition in the hydrogen spectrum would have the same wavelength as the Balmer type transition from $n = 4$ to $n = 2$ of $\text{He}^{+}$ spectrum?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Match the wavenumber expression $R Z^2 \left(\frac{1}{n_1^2} - \frac{1}{n_2^2}\right)$ for both species. // 📝 Solution: For $\text{He}^{+}$ ($Z = 2$): $\bar{\nu} = R(2^2)\left(\frac{1}{2^2} - \frac{1}{4^2}\right) = 4R\left(\frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{16}\right) = R\left(1 - \frac{1}{4}\right) = R\left(\frac{1}{1^2} - \frac{1}{2^2}\right)$, which corresponds to the $n = 2 \to 1$ transition in hydrogen atom ($Z = 1$).

questions.text: Two positively charged particles $m_1$ and $m_2$ have been accelerated across the same potential difference of $200\;\text{keV}$ as shown below: [FIGURE] [Given mass of $m_1 = 1\;\text{amu}$ and $m_2 = 4\;\text{amu}$]. The de-Broglie wavelength of $m_1$ will be $x$ times of $m_2$. The value of $x$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For a charged particle accelerated through potential $V$, $\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2mqV}}$. // 📝 Solution: Since potential difference and charges are equal, $\lambda \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}} \implies \frac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_2} = \sqrt{\frac{m_2}{m_1}} = \sqrt{\frac{4}{1}} = 2 \implies x = 2$.

questions.text: Frequency of the de-Broglie wave of electron in Bohr's first orbit of hydrogen atom is $\underline{\quad\quad} \times 10^{13}\;\text{Hz}$ (nearest integer). [Given: $R_H(\text{Rydberg constant}) = 2.18 \times 10^{-18}\;\text{J}, \; h(\text{Planck's constant}) = 6.6 \times 10^{-34}\;\text{J}\;\text{s}$]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Frequency of de-Broglie wave is $\nu = \frac{v}{\lambda} = \frac{m v^2}{h} = \frac{2 \cdot \text{KE}}{h}$. // 📝 Solution: In first Bohr orbit of H, $\text{KE} = 2.18 \times 10^{-18}\;\text{J} \implies m v^2 = 2 \times 2.18 \times 10^{-18} = 4.36 \times 10^{-18}\;\text{J}$. Frequency $\nu = \frac{4.36 \times 10^{-18}}{6.6 \times 10^{-34}} \approx 6.606 \times 10^{15}\;\text{Hz} = 661 \times 10^{13}\;\text{Hz}$.

questions.text: The maximum number of orbitals which can be identified with $n = 4$ and $m_l = 0$ is $\underline{\quad\quad}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Determine the allowed values of azimuthal quantum number $l$ for $n = 4$. // 📝 Solution: For $n = 4$, allowed $l$ values are $0, 1, 2, 3$ ($4s, 4p, 4d, 4f$). Each subshell contains exactly one orbital with $m_l = 0$, giving a total of $4$ orbitals.

questions.text: The extra stability of a half-filled subshell is due to: (A) Symmetrical distribution of electrons (B) Smaller coulombic repulsion energy (C) Presence of electrons with the same spin in non-degenerate orbitals (D) Larger exchange energy (E) Relatively smaller shielding of electrons by one another. Identify the correct statements.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Half-filled stability arises from symmetry, exchange energy and reduced repulsion or shielding // 📝 Solution: (A) correct; (B) correct; (C) incorrect since same-spin electrons occupy degenerate orbitals; (D) correct; (E) correct $\implies$ (A), (B), (D) and (E)

questions.text: Which one of the following about an electron occupying the $1s$ orbital in a hydrogen atom is incorrect? (Bohr's radius is $a_0$)

options.text: The probability density of finding the electron is maximum at the nucleus.
The electron can be found at a distance $2a_0$ from the nucleus.
The total energy of the electron is maximum when it is at a distance $a_0$ from the nucleus.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Total energy of an electron in a stationary state is constant and negative, independent of position // 📝 Solution: $\left\lvert \psi_{1s} \right\rvert^2$ is maximum at $r = 0$ (true); $\psi_{1s} \neq 0$ at $r = 2a_0$ (true); $1s$ is spherical (true); total energy is constant $(-13.6\;\mathrm{eV})$ $\implies$ option (4) is incorrect
questions.topic: Probability density and energy of 1s electron

questions.text: Which of the following statements are true? (A) The azimuthal quantum number $\ell$ describes the shape of the orbital occupied by the electron. (B) The figure shows the boundary surface diagram of the $2p_x$ orbital. (C) The $+$ and $-$ signs in the wave function of the $2p_x$ orbital refer to charge. (D) The wave function of the $2p_x$ orbital is zero everywhere in the $xy$ plane. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Check each statement against orbital shape, phase sign and nodal plane of $p_x$ // 📝 Solution: (A) true; (B) true; (C) false since $\pm$ denotes phase, not charge; (D) false since $p_x$ has nodal plane $yz$, not $xy$ $\implies$ (A) and (B) only

questions.text: In a multielectron atom, which of the following orbitals described by three quantum numbers will have same energy in absence of electric and magnetic fields? A. $n \;=\; 1, l \;=\; 0, m_l \;=\; 0$ B. $n \;=\; 2, l \;=\; 0, m_l \;=\; 0$ C. $n \;=\; 2, l \;=\; 1, m_l \;=\; 1$ D. $n \;=\; 3, l \;=\; 2, m_l \;=\; 1$ E. $n \;=\; 3, l \;=\; 2, m_l \;=\; 0$ Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Orbitals with the same $n$ and $l$ are degenerate in the absence of fields // 📝 Solution: D $\to$ $3d$, E $\to$ $3d$ $\implies$ same $n$ and $l$ $\implies$ degenerate; B is $2s$ and C is $2p$, which differ in a multielectron atom

questions.text: Given below are two statements : Statement (I) : For a given shell, the total number of allowed orbitals is given by $n^2$. Statement (II) : For any subshell, the spatial orientation of the orbitals is given by $-l$ to $+l$ values including zero. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Orbitals per shell $=\;n^2$; $m_l$ runs from $-l$ to $+l$ // 📝 Solution: Number of orbitals in a shell $\;=\; n^2$ (true); $m_l \;=\; -l, \ldots, 0, \ldots, +l$ (true) $\implies$ both true

questions.text: Assume that the radius of the first Bohr orbit of hydrogen atom is $0.6\text{ \AA}$. The radius of the third Bohr orbit of $\text{He}^{+}$ is $\underline{\quad\quad}\;\text{picometer}$. (Nearest Integer)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Orbit radius scales as $r = r_0 \frac{n^2}{Z}$. // 📝 Solution: For third orbit of $\text{He}^{+}$ ($n = 3, \; Z = 2$): $r = 0.6 \times \frac{3^2}{2} = 0.6 \times 4.5 = 2.7\text{ \AA} = 270\;\text{pm}$.

questions.text: The wave function ($\Psi$) of $2s$ is given by $\Psi_{2s} = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{2\pi}} \left(\frac{1}{a_0}\right)^{1/2} \left(2 - \frac{r}{a_0}\right) e^{-r/2a_0}$. At $r = r_0$, radial node is formed. Thus, $r_0$ in terms of $a_0$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Set the radial wave function $\Psi_{2s} = 0$ to find the radial node. // 📝 Solution: At the radial node, $\Psi_{2s} = 0 \implies \left(2 - \frac{r_0}{a_0}\right) = 0 \implies r_0 = 2a_0$.

questions.text: Maximum number of electrons that can be accommodated in shell with $n = 4$ are:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The maximum capacity of electrons in shell $n$ is $2n^2$. // 📝 Solution: For principal quantum number $n = 4$, the maximum number of electrons is $2n^2 = 2\left(4\right)^2 = 32$.

questions.text: Total number of ions from the following with noble gas configuration is: $\text{Sr}^{2+} \; (Z = 38)$, $\text{Cs}^{+} \; (Z = 55)$, $\text{La}^{2+} \; (Z = 57)$, $\text{Pb}^{2+} \; (Z = 82)$, $\text{Yb}^{2+} \; (Z = 70)$ and $\text{Fe}^{2+} \; (Z = 26)$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Noble gas configuration corresponds to completely filled octet $ns^2 np^6$. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Sr}^{2+} = \left[ \text{Kr} \right]$ (noble gas); $\text{Cs}^{+} = \left[ \text{Xe} \right]$ (noble gas); $\text{Yb}^{2+} = \left[ \text{Xe} \right] 4f^{14}$ (noble gas core with filled $4f$, valence shell $5s^2 5p^6$ noble octet). The other ions $\text{La}^{2+} \; (\left[ \text{Xe} \right] 5d^1)$, $\text{Pb}^{2+} \; (\left[ \text{Xe} \right] 4f^{14} 5d^{10} 6s^2)$, and $\text{Fe}^{2+} \; (\left[ \text{Ar} \right] 3d^6)$ do not have noble gas configurations. Hence, total = $3$.

questions.text: The de-Broglie's wavelength of an electron in the $4^{\text{th}}$ orbit is $\underline{\quad\quad} \pi a_0 \cdot (a_0 = \text{Bohr's radius})$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Apply Bohr-de Broglie condition $2\pi r_n = n \lambda$ with $r_n = \frac{n^2 a_0}{Z}$. // 📝 Solution: In hydrogen atom, $r_4 = \frac{4^2 a_0}{1} = 16 a_0$. Then $2\pi r_4 = 4\lambda \implies 2\pi (16 a_0) = 4\lambda \implies \lambda = 8\pi a_0$.

questions.text: Wavenumber for a radiation having $5800\text{ \AA}$ wavelength is $x \times 10\;\text{cm}^{-1}$. The value of $x$ is $\underline{\quad\quad}$. (Integer answer)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Wavenumber is defined as $\bar{\nu} = \frac{1}{\lambda}$. // 📝 Solution: $\bar{\nu} = \frac{1}{5800 \times 10^{-8}\;\text{cm}} \approx 17241.38\;\text{cm}^{-1} = 1724.1 \times 10\;\text{cm}^{-1} \implies x = 1724$.

questions.text: Which of the following electronic configuration would be associated with the highest magnetic moment?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Magnetic moment increases with the number of unpaired electrons: $\mu = \sqrt{n\left(n + 2\right)}\;\text{BM}$. // 📝 Solution: Unpaired electrons ($n$): for $3d^7$, $n = 3 \implies \mu = \sqrt{15}\;\text{BM}$; for $3d^8$, $n = 2 \implies \mu = \sqrt{8}\;\text{BM}$; for $3d^3$, $n = 3 \implies \mu = \sqrt{15}\;\text{BM}$; for $3d^6$, $n = 4 \implies \mu = \sqrt{24}\;\text{BM}$. Thus, $3d^6$ has the highest magnetic moment.

questions.text: The energy of first (lowest) Balmer line of H atom is $x\;\text{J}$. The energy (in J) of second Balmer line of H atom is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $E \propto \left(\frac{1}{2^2} - \frac{1}{n^2}\right)$ for Balmer transitions. // 📝 Solution: For first Balmer line ($3 \to 2$): $E_1 = 13.6\left( \frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{9} \right) = 13.6 \times \frac{5}{36} = x$. For second Balmer line ($4 \to 2$): $E_2 = 13.6\left( \frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{16} \right) = 13.6 \times \frac{3}{16} \implies \frac{E_2}{E_1} = \frac{3/16}{5/36} = \frac{27}{20} = 1.35 \implies E_2 = 1.35x$.

questions.text: According to the wave-particle duality of matter by de-Broglie, which of the following graph plot presents most appropriate relationship between wavelength of electron ($\lambda$) and momentum of electron ($p$)?

options.text: [FIGURE] Straight line with positive slope between $p$ and $\lambda$
[FIGURE] Straight line with positive slope between $\lambda$ and $p$

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall de-Broglie's equation relating wavelength and momentum: $\lambda = \frac{h}{p}$. // 📝 Solution: From de-Broglie relation, $\lambda = \frac{h}{p} \implies \lambda \cdot p = h \; (\text{constant})$. This equation represents a rectangular hyperbola between $\lambda$ and $p$.

questions.text: It is observed that characteristic X-ray spectra of elements show regularity. When frequency to the power '$n$' i.e. $\nu^n$ of X-rays emitted is plotted against atomic number '$Z$', following graph is obtained: [FIGURE] The value of '$n$' is:

Figure 1 shows electron probability density for $2s$ orbital with a spherical nodal surface. Figure 2 shows wave function $\psi_{2s}(x)$ versus $x$ with labeled points A, B, C, D: [FIGURE] Which of the following point in Figure 2 most accurately represents the nodal surface as shown in Figure 1?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A nodal surface is a region where the wave function $\psi = 0$. // 📝 Solution: At a radial node, the radial wave function passes through zero. In the graph of $\psi_{2s}(x)$, point B corresponds to $\psi = 0$ at the node.

questions.text: Which one of the following sets of ions represents a collection of isoelectronic species? (Given Atomic Number: $\text{F} : 9, \; \text{Cl} : 17, \; \text{Na} : 11, \; \text{Mg} : 12, \; \text{Al} : 13, \; \text{K} : 19, \; \text{Ca} : 20, \; \text{Sc} : 21$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Isoelectronic species have identical total number of electrons. // 📝 Solution: Total electrons: $\text{K}^{+} = 19 - 1 = 18$; $\text{Cl}^{-} = 17 + 1 = 18$; $\text{Ca}^{2+} = 20 - 2 = 18$; $\text{Sc}^{3+} = 21 - 3 = 18$. All four ions contain $18$ electrons.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: When an electric discharge is passed through gaseous hydrogen, the hydrogen molecules dissociate and the energetically excited hydrogen atoms produce electromagnetic radiation of discrete frequencies. Statement II: The frequency of second line of Balmer series obtained from $\text{He}^{+}$ is equal to that of first line of Lyman series obtained from hydrogen atom. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: $\text{Statement I is false but Statement II is true}$
$\text{Both Statement I and Statement II are true}$
$\text{Statement I is true but Statement II is false}$
$\text{Both Statement I and Statement II are false}$

questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Evaluate transition frequencies using $
u = R c Z^2 \left( rac{1}{n_1^2} -  rac{1}{n_2^2}ight)$. // 📝 Solution: Statement I is true. For Statement II: Second Balmer line of $	ext{He}^+$ ($Z=2, 4 	o 2$): $
u = 4Rc\left(  rac{1}{4} -  rac{1}{16} ight) =  rac{3Rc}{4}$. First Lyman line of H ($Z=1, 2 	o 1$): $
u = Rc\left( 1 -  rac{1}{4} ight) =  rac{3Rc}{4}$. Both frequencies match, hence both statements are true.

questions.text: For hydrogen like species, which of the following graphs provides the most appropriate representation of E vs Z plot for a constant n ? [E: Energy of the stationary state, Z : atomic number, n $=$ principal quantum number]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $E_n \;=\; -13.6 \frac{Z^2}{n^2}$ // 📝 Solution: $E \propto -Z^2 \implies$ a downward-opening parabola in the negative-energy region, which is graph (1) [FIGURE]
questions.topic: Energy of hydrogen-like species vs Z

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement-I: The orbitals having same energy are called as degenerate orbitals. Statement-II: In hydrogen atom, $3p$ and $3d$ orbitals are not degenerate orbitals. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given:

options.text: $\text{Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false}$
$\text{Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true}$

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: In single-electron systems like H, orbital energy depends solely on the principal quantum number $n$. // 📝 Solution: Statement-I defines degenerate orbitals correctly. For single-electron species like H, orbital energy depends only on $n$, hence $3s, 3p, 3d$ have identical energy and are degenerate. Thus, Statement-I is true and Statement-II is false.

questions.text: For hydrogen atom, energy of an electron in first excited state is $-3.4\;\text{eV}$, K.E. of the same electron of hydrogen atom is $x\;\text{eV}$. Value of $x$ is $\underline{\quad\quad} \times 10^{-1}\;\text{eV}$. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall the relationship between total energy and kinetic energy in Bohr atom: $\text{KE} = -E$. // 📝 Solution: In Bohr orbit, kinetic energy equals the negative of total energy: $\text{KE} = -E = -(-3.4\;\text{eV}) = 3.4\;\text{eV} = 34 \times 10^{-1}\;\text{eV} \implies x = 34$.

questions.text: Number of spectral lines obtained in $\text{He}^{+}$ spectra, when an electron makes transition from fifth excited state to first excited state will be:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Number of spectral lines for transitions between $n_2$ and $n_1$ is $\frac{\Delta n\left(\Delta n + 1\right)}{2}$. // 📝 Solution: Fifth excited state $\implies n_2 = 6$; first excited state $\implies n_1 = 2$. $\Delta n = n_2 - n_1 = 6 - 2 = 4 \implies \text{Number of lines} = \frac{4\left(4 + 1\right)}{2} = 10$.

questions.text: Arrange the following orbitals in decreasing order of energy: (A) $n = 3, \; l = 0, \; m = 0$, (B) $n = 4, \; l = 0, \; m = 0$, (C) $n = 3, \; l = 1, \; m = 0$, (D) $n = 3, \; l = 2, \; m = 1$. The correct option for the order is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Energies of orbitals are determined by Aufbau's $(n + l)$ rule. // 📝 Solution: (A) $3s: n+l = 3$; (B) $4s: n+l = 4$; (C) $3p: n+l = 4$; (D) $3d: n+l = 5$. Since higher $(n+l)$ has higher energy, and for identical $(n+l)$ higher $n$ has higher energy: $3d\text{ (D)} > 4s\text{ (B)} > 3p\text{ (C)} > 3s\text{ (A)}$. Thus, $\text{D} > \text{B} > \text{C} > \text{A}$.
