questions.text: The energy of an electron in the first Bohr orbit of H-atom is $-13.6\;\mathrm{eV}$. The magnitude of energy of an electron in the first excited state of $\mathrm{Be^{3+}}$ is ______ eV (nearest integer value).
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $E_n = -13.6\,\dfrac{Z^2}{n^2}\;\mathrm{eV}$ // 📝 Solution: For $\mathrm{Be^{3+}}$: $Z = 4$, first excited state $n = 2$ $\implies$ $E = -13.6 \times \dfrac{16}{4} = -54.4\;\mathrm{eV}$ $\implies$ magnitude $\approx 54\;\mathrm{eV}$

questions.text: Identify the INCORRECT statements from the following: A. Notation ${}^{24}_{12}\text{Mg}$ represents $24$ protons and $12$ neutrons. B. Wavelength of a radiation of frequency $4.5 \times 10^{15}\;\text{s}^{-1}$ is $6.7 \times 10^{-8}\;\text{m}$. C. One radiation has wavelength $\lambda_1 = 900\;\text{nm}$ and energy $E_1$. Other radiation has wavelength $\lambda_2 = 300\;\text{nm}$ and energy $E_2$. $E_1 : E_2 = 3 : 1$. D. Number of photons of light of wavelength $2000\;\text{pm}$ that provides $1\;\text{J}$ of energy is $1.006 \times 10^{16}$. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Note that atomic number gives protons, mass number gives nucleons, and $E \propto \frac{1}{\lambda}$. // 📝 Solution: A is incorrect: ${}^{24}_{12}\text{Mg}$ has $12$ protons and $12$ neutrons. C is incorrect: $E \propto \frac{1}{\lambda} \implies \frac{E_1}{E_2} = \frac{\lambda_2}{\lambda_1} = \frac{300}{900} = \frac{1}{3} \neq 3 : 1$. Statements B and D are correct. Thus, A and C are incorrect.

questions.text: The four quantum numbers for the electron in the outer most orbital of potassium (atomic no. $19$) are:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Potassium has electronic configuration $1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 4s^1$. // 📝 Solution: The outermost electron is in the $4s$ subshell. For this orbital, $n = 4$, $l = 0$, $m = 0$, and spin $s = +\frac{1}{2}$.

questions.text: If $a_0$ is denoted as the Bohr radius of hydrogen atom, then what is the de-Broglie wavelength $(\lambda)$ of the electron present in the second orbit of hydrogen atom? [n : any integer]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Bohr quantization $2\pi r \;=\; n\lambda$ and $r_n \;=\; a_0 n^2$ // 📝 Solution: $r_2 \;=\; 4a_0 \implies 2\pi \times 4a_0 \;=\; n\lambda \implies \lambda \;=\; \frac{8\pi a_0}{n}$
questions.topic: de Broglie wavelength in Bohr orbit

questions.text: How many of the following metal ions have similar value of spin only magnetic moment in gaseous state? $\text{V}^{3+}, \; \text{Cr}^{3+}, \; \text{Fe}^{2+}, \; \text{Ni}^{3+}$. (Given: Atomic number : $\text{V}, 23; \; \text{Cr}, 24; \; \text{Fe}, 26; \; \text{Ni}, 28$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Calculate number of unpaired electrons in $3d$ orbitals for each cation. // 📝 Solution: Configurations: $\text{V}^{3+} = 3d^2$ ($2$ unpaired $e^-$); $\text{Cr}^{3+} = 3d^3$ ($3$ unpaired $e^-$); $\text{Fe}^{2+} = 3d^6$ ($4$ unpaired $e^-$); $\text{Ni}^{3+} = 3d^7$ ($3$ unpaired $e^-$). Both $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ and $\text{Ni}^{3+}$ have $3$ unpaired electrons, so $2$ ions have identical magnetic moment.

questions.text: The incorrect postulates of the Dalton's atomic theory are: (A) Atoms of different elements differ in mass. (B) Matter consists of divisible atoms. (C) Compounds are formed when atoms of different element combine in a fixed ratio. (D) All the atoms of given element have different properties including mass. (E) Chemical reactions involve reorganisation of atoms. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Dalton postulated that atoms are indivisible and identical for a given element. // 📝 Solution: Dalton's postulates state that atoms are indivisible (so B is incorrect) and that atoms of the same element are identical in mass and properties (so D is incorrect). Thus, (B) and (D) are incorrect postulates.

questions.text: Given, (A) $n = 5, \; m_l = -1$, (B) $n = 3, \; l = 2, \; m_l = -1, \; m_s = +\frac{1}{2}$. The maximum number of electron(s) in an atom that can have the quantum numbers as given in (A) and (B) respectively are:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Each allowed orbital accommodates up to $2$ electrons; if spin is fixed, only $1$ electron is allowed. // 📝 Solution: For (A), $n = 5$ has $l = 1, 2, 3, 4$ containing $m_l = -1$, yielding $4$ orbitals $\implies 4 \times 2 = 8$ electrons. For (B), all four quantum numbers are fixed, specifying exactly $1$ electron.

questions.text: The energy required by electrons, present in the first Bohr orbit of hydrogen atom to be excited to second Bohr orbit is $\underline{\quad\quad}\;\text{J}\;\text{mol}^{-1}$. Given: $R_H = 2.18 \times 10^{-11}\;\text{ergs}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Calculate excitation energy per atom $\Delta E = R_H \left(1 - \frac{1}{4}\right)$, convert ergs to J, and multiply by $N_A$. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta E_{\text{atom}} = \frac{3}{4} R_H = \frac{3}{4} \times 2.18 \times 10^{-18}\;\text{J} = 1.635 \times 10^{-18}\;\text{J}$. For $1\text{ mole}$, $\Delta E = 1.635 \times 10^{-18} \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} \approx 9.835 \times 10^5\;\text{J}\;\text{mol}^{-1}$.

questions.text: Consider the following complex ions: $P = \left[ \text{FeF}_{6} \right]^{3-}$, $Q = \left[ \text{V}\left( \text{H}_{2}\text{O} \right)_{6} \right]^{2+}$, $R = \left[ \text{Fe}\left( \text{H}_{2}\text{O} \right)_{6} \right]^{2+}$. The correct order of the complex ions, according to their spin only magnetic moment values (in B.M.) is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Calculate the number of unpaired electrons for each metal ion considering weak field ligands. // 📝 Solution: In $\left[ \text{FeF}_6 \right]^{3-}$, $\text{Fe}^{3+} \; (3d^5)$ has $5$ unpaired electrons $\implies \mu = \sqrt{35}\;\text{BM}$. In $\left[ \text{V}\left( \text{H}_2\text{O} \right)_6 \right]^{2+}$, $\text{V}^{2+} \; (3d^3)$ has $3$ unpaired electrons $\implies \mu = \sqrt{15}\;\text{BM}$. In $\left[ \text{Fe}\left( \text{H}_2\text{O} \right)_6 \right]^{2+}$, $\text{Fe}^{2+} \; (3d^6)$ has $4$ unpaired electrons $\implies \mu = \sqrt{24}\;\text{BM}$. Hence, $Q < R < P$.

questions.text: Given below are two statements about X-ray spectra of elements : Statement (I) : A plot of $\sqrt{v}$ ($v$ $=$ frequency of $X$-rays emitted) vs atomic mass is a straight line. Statement (II) : A plot of $v$ ($v$ $=$ frequency of $X$-rays emitted) vs atomic number is a straight line. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Moseley's law: $\sqrt{v} \;=\; a(Z - b)$ // 📝 Solution: $\sqrt{v}$ is linear in $Z$, not in atomic mass $\implies$ I false; $v$ vs $Z$ is parabolic, not linear $\implies$ II false

questions.text: Consider the following spectral lines for atomic hydrogen: A. First line of Paschen series, B. Second line of Balmer series, C. Third line of Paschen series, D. Fourth line of Brackett series. The correct arrangement of the above lines in ascending order of energy is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Transition energy is proportional to $\left(\frac{1}{n_1^2} - \frac{1}{n_2^2}\right)$. // 📝 Solution: $E_A = 13.6\left( \frac{1}{9} - \frac{1}{16} \right) \approx 0.66\;\text{eV}$; $E_B = 13.6\left( \frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{16} \right) = 2.55\;\text{eV}$; $E_C = 13.6\left( \frac{1}{9} - \frac{1}{36} \right) \approx 1.13\;\text{eV}$; $E_D = 13.6\left( \frac{1}{16} - \frac{1}{64} \right) \approx 0.6375\;\text{eV}$. Thus, $E_D < E_A < E_C < E_B$.

questions.text: Given below are two statements : Statement (I) : A spectral line will be observed for a $2p_x \to 2p_y$ transition. Statement (II) : $2p_x$ and $2p_y$ are degenerate orbitals. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A spectral line needs an energy difference between the two levels // 📝 Solution: $2p_x$ and $2p_y$ have equal energy (degenerate) $\implies \Delta E \;=\; 0 \implies$ no spectral line; I false, II true

questions.text: Correct statements for an element with atomic number 9 are: A. There can be 5 electrons for which $m_s = +\tfrac{1}{2}$ and 4 electrons for which $m_s = -\tfrac{1}{2}$. B. There is only one electron in the $p_z$ orbital. C. The last electron goes to an orbital with $n = 2$ and $\ell = 1$. D. The sum of angular nodes of all the atomic orbitals is 1. Choose the correct answer.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Write the configuration $1s^2\,2s^2\,2p^5$ and count spins and angular nodes // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{F}: 1s^2\,2s^2\,2p^5$ $\implies$ 5 up and 4 down spins $\implies$ A true; unpaired electron can be in any $p$ orbital $\implies$ B false; last electron has $n = 2,\ \ell = 1$ $\implies$ C true; nodes $= \ell$ summed $= 0 + 0 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 3 \neq 1$ $\implies$ D false $\implies$ A and C only
questions.topic: Fluorine electronic configuration and quantum numbers

questions.text: The electronic configuration of Einsteinium is: (Given atomic number of Einsteinium = $99$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Einsteinium is an actinoid with atomic number $99$; its valence shell fills $5f$ and $7s$. // 📝 Solution: Radon core has $Z = 86$. The remaining $13$ electrons configure into $7s$ and $5f$: $\left[ \text{Rn} \right] 5f^{11} 6d^0 7s^2$.

questions.text: The value of Rydberg constant ($R_H$) is $2.18 \times 10^{-18}\;\text{J}$. The velocity of electron having mass $9.1 \times 10^{-31}\;\text{kg}$ in Bohr's first orbit of hydrogen atom = $\underline{\quad\quad} \times 10^{5}\;\text{m}\;\text{s}^{-1}$ (nearest integer).
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Velocity in the $n^{\text{th}}$ Bohr orbit is $v_n = 2.18 \times 10^6 \frac{Z}{n}\;\text{m}\;\text{s}^{-1}$. // 📝 Solution: For first orbit of H-atom ($n = 1, \; Z = 1$), $v_1 = 2.18 \times 10^6 \times \frac{1}{1}\;\text{m}\;\text{s}^{-1} = 21.8 \times 10^5\;\text{m}\;\text{s}^{-1} \approx 22 \times 10^5\;\text{m}\;\text{s}^{-1}$.

questions.text: According to Bohr's model of hydrogen atom, which of the following statement is incorrect?

options.text: Radius of $3^{\text{rd}}$ orbit is nine times larger than that of $1^{\text{st}}$ orbit.
Radius of $8^{\text{th}}$ orbit is four times larger than that of $4^{\text{th}}$ orbit.
Radius of $6^{\text{th}}$ orbit is three times larger than that of $4^{\text{th}}$ orbit.
Radius of $4^{\text{th}}$ orbit is four times larger than that of $2^{\text{nd}}$ orbit.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: In Bohr's model the radius is proportional to $n^2$ // 📝 Solution: $r_3/r_1 = 9$ (correct) $\implies$ $r_8/r_4 = 64/16 = 4$ (correct) $\implies$ $r_6/r_4 = 36/16 = 9/4 \neq 3$ (incorrect) $\implies$ $r_4/r_2 = 4$ (correct) $\implies$ option (3) is incorrect

questions.text: Compare the energies of following sets of quantum numbers for multielectron system: (A) $n = 4, \; l = 1$, (B) $n = 4, \; l = 2$, (C) $n = 3, \; l = 1$, (D) $n = 3, \; l = 2$, (E) $n = 4, \; l = 0$. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use the Aufbau $(n + l)$ rule to rank subshell energies. // 📝 Solution: Calculate $(n+l)$: (A) $4p \implies 4+1=5$; (B) $4d \implies 4+2=6$; (C) $3p \implies 3+1=4$; (D) $3d \implies 3+2=5$; (E) $4s \implies 4+0=4$. Ranking gives: $3p\text{ (C)} < 4s\text{ (E)} < 3d\text{ (D)} < 4p\text{ (A)} < 4d\text{ (B)}$.

questions.text: Which of the following postulates of Bohr's model of hydrogen atom is not in agreement with the quantum mechanical model of an atom?

options.text: An atom in a stationary state does not emit electromagnetic radiation as long as it stays in the same state.
An atom can take only certain distinct energies $E_1, E_2, E_3$, etc. These allowed states are called stationary states.
When an electron moves from a higher to a lower stationary state, it emits a photon of light.
The electron in a H atom's stationary state moves in a circle around the nucleus.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Quantum mechanics replaces fixed circular paths with probability distributions (orbitals) // 📝 Solution: Options (1) to (3) remain valid in quantum mechanics $\implies$ the fixed circular path postulate contradicts the quantum model $\implies$ option (4)
questions.topic: Bohr model vs quantum mechanical model

questions.text: The shortest wavelength of hydrogen atom in Lyman series is $\lambda$. The longest wavelength in Balmer series of $\text{He}^{+}$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Apply Rydberg formula $\frac{1}{\lambda} = R Z^2 \left(\frac{1}{n_1^2} - \frac{1}{n_2^2}\right)$. // 📝 Solution: Shortest Lyman for H ($n_1 = 1, \; n_2 = \infty, \; Z = 1$): $\frac{1}{\lambda} = R \implies R = \frac{1}{\lambda}$. Longest Balmer for $\text{He}^{+}$ ($n_1 = 2, \; n_2 = 3, \; Z = 2$): $\frac{1}{\lambda'} = R(2^2)\left(\frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{9}\right) = \frac{5R}{9} = \frac{5}{9\lambda} \implies \lambda' = \frac{9\lambda}{5}$.

questions.text: Electrons in a cathode ray tube have been emitted with a velocity of $1000\;\text{m}\;\text{s}^{-1}$. The number of following statements which is/are true about the emitted radiation is: [Given: $h = 6 \times 10^{-34}\;\text{J}\;\text{s}, \; m_e = 9 \times 10^{-31}\;\text{kg}$] (A) The deBroglie wavelength of the electron emitted is $666.67\;\text{nm}$. (B) The characteristic of electrons emitted depend upon the material of the electrodes of the cathode ray tube. (C) The cathode rays start from cathode and move towards anode. (D) The nature of the emitted electrons depends on the nature of the gas present in cathode ray tube.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Calculate $\lambda = \frac{h}{mv}$ and recall cathode ray fundamental properties. // 📝 Solution: (A) $\lambda = \frac{6 \times 10^{-34}}{9 \times 10^{-31} \times 1000} \approx 6.667 \times 10^{-7}\;\text{m} = 666.67\;\text{nm}$ (True). (B) False (independent of electrode). (C) True (travel cathode to anode). (D) False (electrons are universal). Exactly $2$ statements (A and C) are true.

questions.text: The hydrogen spectrum consists of several spectral lines in Lyman series ($L_1, L_2, L_3 \dots$; $L_1$ has lowest energy among Lyman series). Similarly it consists of several spectral lines in Balmer series ($B_1, B_2, B_3 \dots$; $B_1$ has lowest energy among Balmer lines). The energy of $L_1$ is $x$ times the energy of $B_1$. The value of $x$ is $\underline{\quad\quad} \times 10^{-1}$. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Lowest energy line corresponds to transition between adjacent levels ($2 \to 1$ for Lyman, $3 \to 2$ for Balmer). // 📝 Solution: $E(L_1) = 13.6\left(1 - \frac{1}{4}\right) = 13.6 \times \frac{3}{4}$; $E(B_1) = 13.6\left(\frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{9}\right) = 13.6 \times \frac{5}{36} \implies x = \frac{E(L_1)}{E(B_1)} = \frac{3/4}{5/36} = 5.4 = 54 \times 10^{-1}$.

questions.text: For an electron in $2s$ and $2p$ orbitals, the orbital angular momentum values, respectively, are:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Orbital angular momentum $= \sqrt{\ell(\ell+1)}\,\dfrac{h}{2\pi}$ // 📝 Solution: For $2s$: $\ell = 0 \implies L = 0$; for $2p$: $\ell = 1 \implies L = \sqrt{1(1+1)}\,\dfrac{h}{2\pi} = \sqrt{2}\,\dfrac{h}{2\pi}$

questions.text: Which of the following is/are not correct with respect to energy of atomic orbitals of hydrogen atom? (A) $1s < 2p < 3d < 4s$ (B) $1s < 2s = 2p < 3s = 3p$ (C) $1s < 2s < 2p < 3s < 3p$ (D) $1s < 2s < 4s < 3d$ Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: In H atom, $E$ depends only on $n$, so same-$n$ orbitals are degenerate // 📝 Solution: (A) true, (B) true; (C) wrong since $2s \;=\; 2p$ and $3s \;=\; 3p$; (D) wrong since $3d < 4s$ ($n \;=\; 3 < 4$)
questions.topic: Energy order of orbitals in H atom

questions.text: The wavelength of photon 'A' is $400\;\text{nm}$. The frequency of photon 'B' is $10^{16}\;\text{s}^{-1}$. The wave number of photon 'C' is $10^{4}\;\text{cm}^{-1}$. The correct order of energy of these photons is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Convert all quantities to photon energy using $E = \frac{hc}{\lambda} = h\nu = hc\bar{\nu}$. // 📝 Solution: $E_A = \frac{hc}{400 \times 10^{-9}} \approx 4.97 \times 10^{-19}\;\text{J}$; $E_B = h \times 10^{16} \approx 6.63 \times 10^{-18}\;\text{J}$; $E_C = hc \times 10^{6} \approx 1.99 \times 10^{-19}\;\text{J} \implies E_B > E_A > E_C$.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List - I (Element): A. $\text{N}$, B. $\text{S}$, C. $\text{Br}$, D. $\text{Kr}$; List - II (Electronic configuration): I. $\left[ \text{Ar} \right] 3d^{10} 4s^{2} 4p^{5}$, II. $\left[ \text{Ne} \right] 3s^{2} 3p^{4}$, III. $\left[ \text{He} \right] 2s^{2} 2p^{3}$, IV. $\left[ \text{Ar} \right] 3d^{10} 4s^{2} 4p^{6}$. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Write the ground-state electronic configurations for elements with $Z = 7, 16, 35, 36$. // 📝 Solution: $\text{N} \; (Z=7) \implies \left[\text{He}\right] 2s^2 2p^3$ (III); $\text{S} \; (Z=16) \implies \left[\text{Ne}\right] 3s^2 3p^4$ (II); $\text{Br} \; (Z=35) \implies \left[\text{Ar}\right] 3d^{10} 4s^2 4p^5$ (I); $\text{Kr} \; (Z=36) \implies \left[\text{Ar}\right] 3d^{10} 4s^2 4p^6$ (IV). Match is $\text{A-III}, \text{B-II}, \text{C-I}, \text{D-IV}$.

questions.text: The work functions of two metals ($M_A$ and $M_B$) are in the $1 : 2$ ratio. When these metals are exposed to photons of energy $6\;\text{eV}$, the kinetic energy of liberated electrons of $M_A : M_B$ is in the ratio of $2.642 : 1$. The work functions (in eV) of $M_A$ and $M_B$ are respectively:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Apply Einstein's photoelectric equation $\text{KE} = h\nu - W$ for both metals. // 📝 Solution: Let $W_A = W$ and $W_B = 2W$. $\frac{\text{KE}_A}{\text{KE}_B} = \frac{6 - W}{6 - 2W} = 2.642 \implies 6 - W = 15.852 - 5.284W \implies 4.284W = 9.852 \implies W \approx 2.3\;\text{eV}$. Thus, $W_A = 2.3\;\text{eV}$ and $W_B = 4.6\;\text{eV}$.

questions.text: The radius of the $2^{\text{nd}}$ orbit of $\text{Li}^{2+}$ is $x$. The expected radius of the $3^{\text{rd}}$ orbit of $\text{Be}^{3+}$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Bohr orbit radius satisfies $r \propto \frac{n^2}{Z}$. // 📝 Solution: For $\text{Li}^{2+}$ ($n = 2, \; Z = 3$), $r_1 = k \frac{2^2}{3} = \frac{4k}{3} = x \implies k = \frac{3x}{4}$. For $\text{Be}^{3+}$ ($n = 3, \; Z = 4$), $r_2 = k \frac{3^2}{4} = \frac{9k}{4} = \frac{9}{4} \left( \frac{3x}{4} \right) = \frac{27}{16}x$.

questions.text: Consider the ground state of chromium atom ($Z = 24$). How many electrons are present with azimuthal quantum number $\ell = 1$ and $\ell = 2$ respectively?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\ell = 1, 2$ correspond to $p$ and $d$ subshells; count electrons in each // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{Cr}: 1s^2\,2s^2\,2p^6\,3s^2\,3p^6\,3d^5\,4s^1$ $\implies$ $p$-electrons $= 6 + 6 = 12$ and $d$-electrons $= 5$

questions.text: Consider the following reactions: $\text{NiS} + \text{HNO}_3 + \text{HCl} \to A + \text{NO} + \text{S} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$; $A + \text{NH}_4\text{OH} + \text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{C}(=\text{N}-\text{OH})-\text{C}(=\text{N}-\text{OH})-\text{CH}_3 \to B + \text{NH}_4\text{Cl} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$. The number of protons that do not involve in hydrogen bonding in the product $B$ is $\underline{\quad\quad}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Identify product $B$ as bis(dimethylglyoximato)nickel(II) [FIGURE] and count the non-H-bonded methyl protons. // 📝 Solution: Product $B$ is $\left[\text{Ni}(\text{dmg})_2\right]$. Out of $14$ hydrogen atoms in the complex, $2$ oxime protons form intramolecular $\text{O}-\text{H}\cdots\text{O}$ hydrogen bonds, while the $12$ protons of the four methyl ($-\text{CH}_3$) groups do not participate in hydrogen bonding.

questions.text: In an atom, total number of electrons having quantum numbers $n = 4, \; \left\lvert m_l \right\rvert = 1$ and $m_s = -\frac{1}{2}$ is $\underline{\quad\quad}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Count orbitals having $m_l = +1$ or $-1$ for $n = 4$, each having one electron with $m_s = -\frac{1}{2}$. // 📝 Solution: In $n = 4$, subshells with $\left\lvert m_l \right\rvert = 1$ are $4p$ ($m_l = \pm 1$, $2$ orbitals), $4d$ ($m_l = \pm 1$, $2$ orbitals), and $4f$ ($m_l = \pm 1$, $2$ orbitals), giving $6$ orbitals. Each can hold $1$ electron with $m_s = -\frac{1}{2}$, yielding $6$ electrons.

questions.text: Given below are two statements : Statement (I): The radii of isoelectronic species increases in the order. $Mg^{2+} < Na^{+} < F^{-} < O^{2-}$ Statement (II): The magnitude of electron gain enthalpy of halogen decreases in the order. $Cl > F > Br > I$ In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

options.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For isoelectronic species $r \propto \frac{1}{Z_{eff}}$ ($\propto \frac{1}{\text{nuclear charge}}$) // 📝 Solution: Higher nuclear charge gives smaller radius, so $Mg^{2+} < Na^+ < F^- < O^{2-}$ is correct; electron gain enthalpy magnitude $Cl > F > Br > I$ is correct $\implies$ both true
questions.topic: Ionic radii and electron gain enthalpy

questions.text: Radius of the first excited state of Helium ion is given as : $a_0 \to$ radius of first stationary state of hydrogen atom.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $r_n \;=\; a_0 \frac{n^2}{Z}$ // 📝 Solution: First excited state $n \;=\; 2,\; Z \;=\; 2 \implies r \;=\; a_0 \frac{4}{2} \;=\; 2a_0$

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I (Spectral Series for Hydrogen): A. Lyman, B. Balmer, C. Paschen, D. Pfund; List II (Spectral Region): I. Infrared region, II. UV region, III. Infrared region, IV. Visible region. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Transitions to $n_1 = 1$ give UV, $n_1 = 2$ give visible, and $n_1 \ge 3$ give IR radiation. // 📝 Solution: Lyman series lies in the UV region ($\text{A-II}$); Balmer series lies in the visible region ($\text{B-IV}$); Paschen series lies in the IR region ($\text{C-III}$); Pfund series lies in the far-IR region ($\text{D-I}$). Thus, $\text{A-II}, \text{B-IV}, \text{C-III}, \text{D-I}$.

questions.text: The number of electrons present in all the completely filled subshells having $n = 4$ and $s = +\frac{1}{2}$ is (Where $n = \text{principal quantum number}$ and $s = \text{spin quantum number}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For principal energy level $n$, total electrons is $2n^2$, and half have spin $s = +\frac{1}{2}$. // 📝 Solution: Subshells for $n = 4$ are $4s, 4p, 4d, 4f$ containing $2 + 6 + 10 + 14 = 32$ electrons. Exactly half of them possess $s = +\frac{1}{2} \implies \frac{32}{2} = 16$.

questions.text: Which of the following statements regarding the energy of the stationary state is true in the following one-electron systems?

options.text: $-1.09 \times 10^{-18}\;\text{J}\text{ for second orbit of H atom}$

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For a one-electron system, $E_n = -2.18 \times 10^{-18} \times \frac{Z^2}{n^2}\;\text{J}$. // 📝 Solution: For $\text{Li}^{2+}$ ($Z = 3, \; n = 3$), $E = -2.18 \times 10^{-18} \times \frac{3^2}{3^2} = -2.18 \times 10^{-18}\;\text{J}$, which correctly matches statement B.

questions.text: For hydrogen atom, the orbital/s with lowest energy is/are: (A) $4s$ (B) $3p_x$ (C) $3d_{x^2-y^2}$ (D) $3d_{z^2}$ (E) $4p_z$ Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: In hydrogen, energy depends only on the principal quantum number $n$ // 📝 Solution: $3p_x,\; 3d_{x^2-y^2},\; 3d_{z^2}$ all have $n \;=\; 3$ and are lower than $n \;=\; 4$ orbitals $\implies$ (B), (C), (D)
questions.topic: Energy of orbitals in hydrogen atom

questions.text: If wavelength of the first line of the Paschen series of hydrogen atom is $720\;\text{nm}$, then the wavelength of the second line of this series is $\underline{\quad\quad}\;\text{nm}$. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Apply Rydberg's formula $\frac{1}{\lambda} = R\left(\frac{1}{3^2} - \frac{1}{n^2}\right)$ for $n = 4$ and $n = 5$. // 📝 Solution: For first line ($4 \to 3$): $\frac{1}{\lambda_1} = R\left(\frac{1}{9} - \frac{1}{16}\right) = \frac{7R}{144}$. For second line ($5 \to 3$): $\frac{1}{\lambda_2} = R\left(\frac{1}{9} - \frac{1}{25}\right) = \frac{16R}{225} \implies \lambda_2 = \lambda_1 \times \frac{7/144}{16/225} = 720 \times \frac{1575}{2304} \approx 492\;\text{nm}$.

questions.text: Based on Heisenberg's uncertainty principle, the uncertainty in the velocity of the electron to be found within an atomic nucleus of diameter $10^{-15}\;\text{m}$ is $\underline{\quad\quad} \times 10^{9}\;\text{m}\;\text{s}^{-1}$ (nearest integer). [Given: mass of electron = $9.1 \times 10^{-31}\;\text{kg}$, Planck's constant ($h$) = $6.626 \times 10^{-34}\;\text{J}\;\text{s}$, value of $\pi = 3.14$]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use Heisenberg's uncertainty relation $\Delta x \cdot m \Delta v \ge \frac{h}{4\pi}$. // 📝 Solution: Take $\Delta x = 10^{-15}\;\text{m}$. Then $\Delta v = \frac{h}{4\pi m \Delta x} = \frac{6.626 \times 10^{-34}}{4 \times 3.14 \times 9.1 \times 10^{-31} \times 10^{-15}} \approx 57.97 \times 10^9\;\text{m}\;\text{s}^{-1} \approx 58 \times 10^9\;\text{m}\;\text{s}^{-1}$.

questions.text: The energy of one mole of photons of radiation of frequency $2 \times 10^{12}\;\text{Hz}$ in $\text{J}\;\text{mol}^{-1}$ is $\underline{\quad\quad}$. (Nearest integer) (Given: $h = 6.626 \times 10^{-34}\;\text{J}\;\text{s}, \; N_A = 6.022 \times 10^{23}\;\text{mol}^{-1}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Total energy of one mole of photons is $E = N_A h \nu$. // 📝 Solution: $E = 6.022 \times 10^{23} \times 6.626 \times 10^{-34} \times 2 \times 10^{12} \approx 798.16\;\text{J}\;\text{mol}^{-1} \approx 798\;\text{J}\;\text{mol}^{-1}$.

questions.text: The ionization energy of sodium in $\text{kJ}\;\text{mol}^{-1}$, if electromagnetic radiation of wavelength $242\;\text{nm}$ is just sufficient to ionize sodium atom, is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $E = \frac{N_A h c}{\lambda}$ to calculate the threshold energy per mole. // 📝 Solution: Energy per photon $E = \frac{h c}{\lambda} = \frac{6.626 \times 10^{-34} \times 3 \times 10^{8}}{242 \times 10^{-9}} = 8.214 \times 10^{-19}\;\text{J}$. For $1\text{ mole}$, $E = 8.214 \times 10^{-19} \times 6.022 \times 10^{23}\;\text{J}\;\text{mol}^{-1} \approx 494.6\;\text{kJ}\;\text{mol}^{-1} \approx 494\;\text{kJ}\;\text{mol}^{-1}$.

questions.text: The electronic configuration for Neodymium is: [Atomic Number for Neodymium = 60]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Lanthanoids fill the $4f$ subshell; Neodymium ($Z = 60$) has $4$ electrons in $4f$. // 📝 Solution: Xenon core has $Z = 54$. For Neodymium ($Z = 60$), valence electrons enter $6s$ and $4f$, yielding $\left[ \text{Xe} \right] 4f^4 6s^2$.

questions.text: The number of radial node/s for $3p$ orbital is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The number of radial nodes is given by $n - l - 1$. // 📝 Solution: For a $3p$ orbital, $n = 3$ and $l = 1 \implies \text{Radial nodes} = n - l - 1 = 3 - 1 - 1 = 1$.

questions.text: Given below are two statements : Statement (I) : It is impossible to specify simultaneously with arbitrary precision, both the linear momentum and the position of a particle. Statement (II) : If the uncertainty in the measurement of position and uncertainty in measurement of momentum are equal for an electron, then the uncertainty in the measurement of velocity is $\geqslant \sqrt{\frac{h}{\pi}} \times \frac{1}{2m}$. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.text: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\Delta x \cdot \Delta p \;\geq\; \frac{h}{4\pi}$ // 📝 Solution: $\Delta x \;=\; \Delta p \implies (\Delta p)^2 \;\geq\; \frac{h}{4\pi} \implies m\Delta v \;\geq\; \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\frac{h}{\pi}} \implies \Delta v \;\geq\; \sqrt{\frac{h}{\pi}} \times \frac{1}{2m}$; both true

questions.text: A hypothetical electromagnetic wave is shown below: [FIGURE] The frequency of the wave is $x \times 10^{19}\;\text{Hz}$. $x = \underline{\quad\quad}$ (nearest integer).
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: One complete cycle corresponds to four quarter-wavelength intervals: $\lambda = 4 \times (\text{quarter cycle})$. // 📝 Solution: From the graph, one quarter wavelength is $1.5\;\text{pm} \implies \lambda = 4 \times 1.5\;\text{pm} = 6 \times 10^{-12}\;\text{m}$. Frequency $\nu = \frac{c}{\lambda} = \frac{3 \times 10^8}{6 \times 10^{-12}} = 5 \times 10^{19}\;\text{Hz} \implies x = 5$.

questions.text: The correct set of four quantum numbers for the valence electron of rubidium atom ($Z = 37$) is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Identify the outermost orbital from the electron configuration of Rubidium ($Z = 37$). // 📝 Solution: Electronic configuration of $\text{Rb} \; (Z = 37) = \left[ \text{Kr} \right] 5s^1$. For the valence electron in $5s$, the quantum numbers are $n = 5, \; l = 0, \; m = 0, \; s = +\frac{1}{2}$.

questions.text: The number of $s$-electrons present in an ion with $55$ protons in its unipositive state is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Cesium ($Z = 55$) loses $1$ electron to form $\text{Cs}^{+}$. Count electrons in all $s$ orbitals. // 📝 Solution: The ion is $\text{Cs}^{+} \; (54\text{ electrons}) = \left[ \text{Xe} \right] = 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2 3p^6 3d^{10} 4s^2 4p^6 4d^{10} 5s^2 5p^6$. The $s$-subshells present are $1s, 2s, 3s, 4s, 5s$, each with $2$ electrons $\implies 5 \times 2 = 10$.

questions.text: The threshold frequency of caesium is $5.16 \times 10^{14}\;\mathrm{Hz}$. Which of the following statements are correct? [FIGURE: visible spectrum] A. With yellow light focused on Cs in a vacuum chamber connected to an ammeter, current is shown. B. Dimming the yellow light reduces the ammeter current. C. Red light instead of yellow gives higher current. D. Blue light shows current formation. E. White light shows current formation.

A, B, D and E only

questions.text: The candela is the luminous intensity, in a given direction, of a source that emits monochromatic radiation of frequency '$A$' $\times 10^{12}\;\text{hertz}$ and that has a radiant intensity in that direction of $\frac{1}{B}\;\text{watt per steradian}$. '$A$' and '$B$' are respectively:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Refer to the standard SI definition of the luminous intensity unit (candela). // 📝 Solution: By the SI definition of candela, the monochromatic radiation has frequency $540 \times 10^{12}\;\text{Hz}$ and radiant intensity of $\frac{1}{683}\;\text{W}\;\text{sr}^{-1} \implies A = 540$ and $B = 683$.

questions.text: The wave numbers of three spectral lines of H atom are considered. Identify the set of spectral lines belonging to Balmer series. ($R = \text{Rydberg constant}$)
In the given reactions identify $A$ and $B$. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Hydrogenation of an alkyne over $\text{Pd/C}$ gives the cis-alkene (syn-addition), whereas reduction with $\text{Na / Liquid NH}_3$ gives the trans-alkene (anti-addition). // 📝 Solution: $\text{H}_2 + \text{CH}_3-\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\;\left(2\text{-pentyne, A}\right) \;\xrightarrow{\text{Pd/C}}\; \text{cis-pent-}2\text{-ene}$ $\implies$ $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-\text{CH}_3 + \text{H}_2 \;\xrightarrow{\text{Na / Liquid NH}_3}\; \text{trans-}2\text{-butene}\;\left(\text{B}\right)$ [FIGURE].

questions.text: [FIGURE] Consider the given reaction. The total number of oxygen atoms present per molecule of the product $\left(\text{P}\right)$ is _______
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Reductive ozonolysis cleaves the $\text{C}=\text{C}$ double bond of trans-but-2-ene to form two molecules of ethanal. // 📝 Solution: $\text{trans-CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3 \;\xrightarrow[\left(\text{ii}\right)\;\text{Zn/H}_2\text{O}]{\left(\text{i}\right)\;\text{O}_3}\; 2\;\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{O}\;\left(\text{P}\right)$ [FIGURE] $\implies \text{Number of oxygen atoms per molecule of product } \left(\text{P}\right) \;=\; 1$.

questions.text: [FIGURE] Identify (P)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Zinc dust with heat dehalogenates a vicinal dibromide to an alkene, which then undergoes $\text{HBr}$ addition with carbocation rearrangement ($1,2\text{-hydride}$ shift). // 📝 Solution: Heating the vicinal dibromide with $\left(\text{i}\right)\;\text{Zn}, \Delta$ causes elimination of $\text{Br}_2$ to form the cycloalkene $\implies$ Treatment with $\left(\text{ii}\right)\;\text{HBr}$ forms a secondary carbocation that undergoes a $1,2\text{-hydride}$ shift to form the more stable tertiary carbocation, followed by $\text{Br}^-$ attack to give the tertiary alkyl bromide ($\text{P}$) [FIGURE].

questions.text: Consider the following reaction of benzene. [FIGURE] In compound (Q), the percentage of oxygen is ____ %. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Friedel-Crafts acylation of benzene with $4\text{-oxopentanoyl chloride}$ gives a $1,4\text{-diketone}$ ($\text{P}$), which undergoes intramolecular aldol condensation with $\text{aq. NaOH}, \Delta$ to form a cyclic $\alpha,\beta\text{-unsaturated}$ ketone ($\text{Q}$). // 📝 Solution: Benzene reacts with $\text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{COCl}$ and anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ to give $\text{Ph}-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CO}-\text{CH}_3$ ($\text{P}$, $\text{C}_{11}\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_2$) $\implies$ Intramolecular aldol condensation with $\text{aq. NaOH}, \Delta$ eliminates $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ to give $\text{Q}$ ($\text{C}_{11}\text{H}_{10}\text{O}$, molar mass $\approx\; 157-158\;\text{g/mol}$) $\implies \text{Percentage of oxygen in Q} \;=\; \frac{16}{157} \;\times\; 100 \;=\; 10.19\% \;\approx\; 10\%$.

questions.text: The arenium ion which is not involved in the bromination of Aniline is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The $-\text{NH}_2$ group is strongly ortho- and para-directing, so electrophilic attack does not occur at the meta position. // 📝 Solution: Since the $-\text{NH}_2$ group directs incoming electrophiles ($\text{Br}^+$) exclusively to the ortho and para positions, the arenium ion formed by meta attack [FIGURE] is not involved in the bromination of aniline.

questions.text: $17\;\text{mg}$ of a hydrocarbon (M.F. $\text{C}_{10}\text{H}_{16}$) takes up $8.40\;\text{mL}$ of the $\text{H}_2$ gas measured at $0^\circ\text{C}$ and $760\;\text{mm of Hg}$. Ozonolysis of the same hydrocarbon yields [FIGURE]. The number of double bond/s present in the hydrocarbon is _______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Calculate the moles of $\text{H}_2$ gas consumed per mole of the hydrocarbon at STP to determine the number of double bonds. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Moles of hydrocarbon} \;=\; \frac{17 \;\times\; 10^{-3}\;\text{g}}{136\;\text{g/mol}} \;=\; 1.25 \;\times\; 10^{-4}\;\text{mol} \implies \text{Moles of } \text{H}_2\;\text{gas} \;=\; \frac{1 \;\times\; \left(8.40 / 1000\right)}{0.0821 \;\times\; 273} \;=\; 3.75 \;\times\; 10^{-4}\;\text{mol} \implies \text{Number of double bonds per molecule} \;=\; \frac{3.75 \;\times\; 10^{-4}}{1.25 \;\times\; 10^{-4}} \;=\; 3$.

questions.text: In the given reactions identify the reagent $A$ and reagent $B$ [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Oxidation of toluene to benzaldehyde can be carried out using $\text{CrO}_3$ in acetic anhydride or using chromyl chloride ($\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2$) in $\text{CS}_2$ (Etard reaction). // 📝 Solution: Toluene reacts with $\text{CrO}_3$ ($\text{A}$) and $\left(\text{CH}_3\text{CO}\right)_2\text{O}$ at $273-283\;\text{K}$ to form benzylidene diacetate $\text{PhCH(OCOCH}_3\text{)}_2$, and reacts with $\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2$ ($\text{B}$) in $\text{CS}_2$ to form the Etard complex $\text{PhCH}\left(\text{OCrCl}_2\text{OH}\right)_2$; both intermediates hydrolyze to benzaldehyde [FIGURE].

questions.text: Major product of the following reaction is - [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Electrophilic addition of $\text{D}-\text{Cl}$ to an unsymmetrical cycloalkene follows Markovnikov's rule via the more stable tertiary carbocation. // 📝 Solution: The double bond of $1\text{-methylcyclobutene}$ attacks $\text{D}^+$ to place $-\text{D}$ at the less substituted carbon and generate a stable tertiary carbocation at the methyl-bearing carbon $\implies$ Nucleophilic attack by $\text{Cl}^-$ at the tertiary carbon yields $1\text{-chloro-}2\text{-deuterio-}1\text{-methylcyclobutane}$ [FIGURE].

questions.text: [FIGURE] Product P is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Dehydrohalogenation of an alkyl bromide using alcoholic $\text{KOH}$ and heat yields the more stable conjugated alkene as the major product. // 📝 Solution: Heating with $\text{KOH(alc)}$ induces $\text{E}2$ elimination of $\text{HBr}$ towards the benzylic carbon so that the newly formed double bond is conjugated with the benzene ring [FIGURE].

questions.text: [FIGURE] In the above chemical reaction sequence "A" and "B" respectively are
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Reductive ozonolysis cleaves $1\text{-methylcyclopentene}$ to a keto-aldehyde, and the haloform reaction selectively oxidizes the methyl ketone without affecting the aldehyde group. // 📝 Solution: $1\text{-Methylcyclopentene}$ reacts with reagent $\text{A}$ ($\text{O}_3, \text{Zn/H}_2\text{O}$) via reductive ozonolysis to give $5\text{-oxohexanal}$ $\implies$ Treatment with reagent $\text{B}$ ($\text{NaOH/I}_2$) oxidizes the $-\text{COCH}_3$ group via haloform cleavage to $-\text{COO}^-\text{Na}^+$ and $\text{CHI}_3$ while leaving $-\text{CHO}$ intact [FIGURE].

questions.text: Method used for separation of mixture of products (B and C) obtained in the following reaction is [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Bromination of benzene followed by nitration produces ortho- and para-bromonitrobenzene, which have different boiling points. // 📝 Solution: Benzene reacts with $\text{Br}_2/\text{FeBr}_3$ to give bromobenzene ($\text{A}$), which on nitration with $\text{Conc. HNO}_3 / \text{Conc. H}_2\text{SO}_4$ gives a mixture of $o\text{-bromonitrobenzene}$ and $p\text{-bromonitrobenzene}$ ($\text{B}$ and $\text{C}$) $\implies$ These two isomers are separated by fractional distillation due to their different boiling points.
questions.topic: Separation of Ortho and Para Isomers

questions.text: $3\text{-Methylhex-}2\text{-ene}$ on reaction with $\text{HBr}$ in presence of peroxide forms an addition product (A). The number of possible stereoisomers for 'A' is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: In the presence of peroxide, $\text{HBr}$ adds to an unsymmetrical alkene via an anti-Markovnikov free-radical mechanism, creating chiral centers. // 📝 Solution: $3\text{-Methylhex-}2\text{-ene}$ reacts with $\text{HBr / Peroxide}$ to give $2\text{-bromo-}3\text{-methylhexane}$ ($\text{CH}_3-\text{C}^*\text{H(Br)}-\text{C}^*\text{H(CH}_3\text{)}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$), which contains $2$ dissimilar chiral centres [FIGURE] $\implies \text{Number of stereoisomers} \;=\; 2^2 \;=\; 4$.

questions.text: $\text{Ph}-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 \;\xrightarrow[\text{HBr}]{\left(\text{PhCOO}\right)_2}\; \text{Product}$ Consider the above reaction A. The reaction proceeds through a more stable radical intermediate. B. The role of peroxide is to generate $\text{H}^\bullet$ (Hydrogen radical). C. During this reaction, benzene is formed as a byproduct. D. 1-Bromo-2-phenylethane is formed as the minor product. E. The same reaction in absence of peroxide proceeds via carbocation intermediate. Identify the correct statements. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Benzoyl peroxide decomposes to give phenyl radicals ($\text{Ph}^\bullet$), which abstract $\text{H}^\bullet$ from $\text{HBr}$ to produce benzene and $\text{Br}^\bullet$ for anti-Markovnikov radical addition. // 📝 Solution: $\left(\text{PhCOO}\right)_2 \;\longrightarrow\; 2\;\text{PhCOO}^\bullet \;\longrightarrow\; 2\;\text{Ph}^\bullet + 2\;\text{CO}_2$, and $\text{Ph}^\bullet + \text{HBr} \;\longrightarrow\; \text{Ph}-\text{H}\;\left(\text{benzene, C}\right) + \text{Br}^\bullet$ $\implies$ $\text{Br}^\bullet$ adds to $\text{Ph}-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$ to give the more stable benzylic radical $\text{Ph}-\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}-\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$ (A), forming $1\text{-bromo-}2\text{-phenylethane}$ as the major product, while in the absence of peroxide it proceeds via a carbocation intermediate (E) $\implies$ A, C & E Only are correct.

questions.text: Consider the following compounds [FIGURE] Arrange these compounds in the increasing order of reactivity with nitrating mixture.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Electron-donating groups ($+\text{M}$) activate the benzene ring towards electrophilic nitration, whereas electron-withdrawing groups ($-\text{M}, -\text{I}$) deactivate it. // 📝 Solution: Nitrobenzene ($\text{b}$) has a strongly deactivating $-\text{NO}_2$ group ($-\text{M}, -\text{I}$), chlorobenzene ($\text{a}$) has a weakly deactivating $-\text{Cl}$ group ($-\text{I} \;>\; +\text{M}$), and anisole ($\text{c}$) has a strongly activating $-\text{OCH}_3$ group ($+\text{M} \;>\; -\text{I}$) $\implies$ Increasing order of reactivity with nitrating mixture is $\text{b} \;<\; \text{a} \;<\; \text{c}$.

questions.text: The major product of the following reaction is $P$. $\text{CH}_3\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-\text{CH}_3 \;\xrightarrow[\left(\text{ii}\right)\;\text{dil. KMnO}_4, 273\;\text{K}]{\left(\text{i}\right)\;\text{Na / liq. NH}_3}\; P$. Number of oxygen atoms present in product '$P$' is _______ (nearest integer)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Birch reduction converts the alkyne to a trans-alkene, and cold dilute $\text{KMnO}_4$ performs syn-dihydroxylation to yield a vicinal diol. // 📝 Solution: $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-\text{CH}_3 \;\xrightarrow{\text{Na / liq. NH}_3}\; \text{trans-CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3 \;\xrightarrow{\text{dil. KMnO}_4, 273\;\text{K}}\; \text{CH}_3-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{CH}_3\;\left(\text{Product } P\right)$ [FIGURE] $\implies \text{Number of oxygen atoms in product } P \;=\; 2$.

questions.text: The major product (P) in the following reaction is [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Excess concentrated $\text{HBr}$ with heat cleaves the aryl alkyl ether to a phenol and adds across the vinyl double bond according to Markovnikov's rule. // 📝 Solution: Protonation of the alkene group forms a resonance-stabilized benzylic carbocation which is attacked by $\text{Br}^-$ to give $-\text{CH(Br)}\text{CH}_3$ $\implies$ Protonation of the $-\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ oxygen followed by $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ attack of $\text{Br}^-$ on the ethyl carbon yields $4\text{-(}1\text{-bromoethyl)phenol}$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$ [FIGURE].

questions.text: The final product $A$ formed in the following multistep reaction sequence is [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Hydration followed by $\text{CrO}_3$ oxidation converts the alkene into a ketone, which is then completely reduced to a methylene group under Wolff-Kishner conditions. // 📝 Solution: Acid-catalyzed hydration ($\text{H}_2\text{O}, \text{H}^+$) converts the double bond to a secondary alcohol $\implies$ Oxidation with $\text{CrO}_3$ gives the corresponding ketone ($\alpha\text{-tetralone}$) $\implies$ Wolff-Kishner reduction ($\text{H}_2\text{N}-\text{NH}_2, \text{KOH}, \text{Heating}$) reduces the $\text{C}=\text{O}$ group to $-\text{CH}_2-$, yielding $1,2,3,4\text{-tetrahydronaphthalene}$ [FIGURE].

questions.text: Total number of deactivating groups in aromatic electrophilic substitution reaction among the following is [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Groups in which the atom directly attached to the benzene ring is bonded to a more electronegative atom by a double or triple bond exert a $-\text{M}$ effect and deactivate the ring. // 📝 Solution: $-\text{COOCH}_3$ ($-\text{M}$ group) and $-\text{C}\equiv\text{N}$ ($-\text{M}$ group) withdraw electron density from the ring and are deactivating, whereas $-\text{NHCOCH}_3$, $-\text{NHCH}_3$, and $-\text{OCH}_3$ exert a $+\text{M}$ effect and are activating [FIGURE] $\implies \text{Number of deactivating groups} \;=\; 2$.

questions.text: Find out the major product for the following reaction. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Acid-catalyzed dehydration of an alcohol adjacent to a strained $4\text{-membered}$ ring proceeds via carbocation rearrangement and ring expansion. // 📝 Solution: Protonation of the $-\text{OH}$ group and loss of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ generates a secondary carbocation adjacent to the cyclobutane ring $\implies$ $1,2\text{-bond}$ shift expands the $4\text{-membered}$ ring to a $5\text{-membered}$ cyclopentyl carbocation, followed by methyl shift and deprotonation to form $1,2\text{-dimethylcyclopentene}$ [FIGURE].

questions.text: Among the following, total number of meta directing functional groups is (Integer based): $-\text{OCH}_3, -\text{NO}_2, -\text{CN}, -\text{CH}_3, -\text{NHCOCH}_3, -\text{COR}, -\text{OH}, -\text{COOH}, -\text{Cl}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Functional groups that withdraw electrons by resonance ($-\text{M}$ effect) direct incoming electrophiles to the meta position. // 📝 Solution: Among the given groups, $-\text{NO}_2, -\text{C}\equiv\text{N}, -\text{COR}$, and $-\text{COOH}$ are meta-directing groups, whereas $-\text{OCH}_3, -\text{CH}_3, -\text{NHCOCH}_3, -\text{OH}$, and $-\text{Cl}$ are ortho/para-directing $\implies \text{Total meta-directing groups} \;=\; 4$.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I : Nitration of benzene involves the following step - [FIGURE] Statement II : Use of Lewis base promotes the electrophilic substitution of benzene. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Nitration generates the electrophile $\text{NO}_2^+$ via dehydration of protonated nitric acid, and Lewis acids (not Lewis bases) catalyze electrophilic aromatic substitution. // 📝 Solution: In nitration of benzene, $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ protonates $\text{HNO}_3$ to form $\text{H}_2\text{O}^+-\text{NO}_2$, which dissociates into $\text{H}_2\text{O} \;+\; \text{NO}_2^+$ (Statement I is correct) $\implies$ Lewis acids promote the generation of electrophiles in electrophilic substitution of benzene, whereas Lewis bases do not (Statement II is incorrect) [FIGURE].

questions.text: Product A and B formed in the following set of reactions are: [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Acid-catalyzed hydration of $1\text{-methylcyclohexene}$ gives the Markovnikov tertiary alcohol, whereas hydroboration-oxidation gives the anti-Markovnikov secondary alcohol. // 📝 Solution: Reaction of $1\text{-methylcyclohexene}$ with $\text{H}^+/\text{H}_2\text{O}$ proceeds via a tertiary carbocation to form $1\text{-methylcyclohexan-}1\text{-ol}$ ($\text{A}$) $\implies$ Reaction with $\text{B}_2\text{H}_6$ followed by $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2, \text{NaOH(aq.)}$ gives the anti-Markovnikov product $2\text{-methylcyclohexan-}1\text{-ol}$ ($\text{B}$) [FIGURE].

questions.text: Choose the correct set of reagents for the following conversion: $\text{trans }\left(\text{Ph}-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3\right) \;\longrightarrow\; \text{cis }\left(\text{Ph}-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3\right)$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Bromination followed by double dehydrohalogenation converts the trans-alkene into an alkyne, which upon syn-hydrogenation with Lindlar's catalyst gives the cis-alkene. // 📝 Solution: $\text{trans-Ph}-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3 \;\xrightarrow{\text{Br}_2}\; \text{Ph}-\text{CH(Br)}-\text{CH(Br)}-\text{CH}_3 \;\xrightarrow{\left(1\right)\;\text{Alc. KOH}, \left(2\right)\;\text{NaNH}_2}\; \text{Ph}-\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-\text{CH}_3 \;\xrightarrow{\text{H}_2, \text{Lindlar's Catalyst}}\; \text{cis-Ph}-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3$ [FIGURE].

questions.text: Identify the product A and product B in the following set of reactions. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Acid-catalyzed hydration of propene follows Markovnikov's rule to give propan-2-ol, whereas hydroboration-oxidation follows anti-Markovnikov addition to give propan-1-ol. // 📝 Solution: $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 \;\xrightarrow{\text{H}_2\text{O}, \text{H}^+}\; \text{CH}_3-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{CH}_3\;\left(\text{A}\right)$ via the more stable secondary carbocation $\implies$ $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2 \;\xrightarrow{\left(\text{BH}_3\right)_2 / \text{H}_2\text{O}_2, \text{OH}^-}\; \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{OH}\;\left(\text{B}\right)$ [FIGURE].

questions.text: A hydrocarbon 'X' with formula $\text{C}_6\text{H}_8$ uses two moles of $\text{H}_2$ on catalytic hydrogenation of its one mole. On ozonolysis, 'X' yields two moles of methane dicarbaldehyde. The hydrocarbon 'X' is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Consuming $2$ moles of $\text{H}_2$ for formula $\text{C}_6\text{H}_8$ ($\text{DBE} \;=\; 3$) indicates a cyclic diene, and symmetrical cleavage to two $3\text{-carbon}$ dialdehydes confirms $1,4$-diene geometry. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Cyclohexa-}1,4\text{-diene}$ ($\text{C}_6\text{H}_8$) absorbs $2$ moles of $\text{H}_2$ on catalytic hydrogenation $\implies$ Reductive ozonolysis ($\text{O}_3, \text{Zn/H}_2\text{O}$) cleaves both double bonds symmetrically to yield $2$ moles of $\text{OHC}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CHO}$ (methane dicarbaldehyde) [FIGURE].

questions.text: Compound A formed in the following reaction reacts with $B$ gives the product $C$. Find out $A$ and $B$. $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}\equiv\text{CH} + \text{Na} \;\longrightarrow\; \text{A} \;\xrightarrow{\text{B}}\; \text{CH}_3-\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3\;\left(\text{C}\right) + \text{NaBr}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Terminal alkynes are acidic and react with sodium metal to form sodium alkynides, which act as nucleophiles in $\text{S}_\text{N}2$ reactions with primary alkyl halides. // 📝 Solution: $\text{CH}_3-\text{C}\equiv\text{CH} \;\xrightarrow{\text{Na}}\; \text{CH}_3-\text{C}\equiv\text{C}^-\text{Na}^+\;\left(\text{A}\right) \;\xrightarrow{\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2-\text{Br}\;\left(\text{B}\right)}\; \text{CH}_3-\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3\;\left(\text{C}\right) \;+\; \text{NaBr}$.

questions.text: Identify A in the following reaction. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Oxidative cleavage of a conjugated cyclohexadiene ring with hot $\text{KMnO}_4$ yields oxalic acid ($\text{HOOC}-\text{COOH}$) from the $-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-$ unit between the two double bonds. // 📝 Solution: Compound $\text{A}$ absorbs $2\;\text{H}_2/\text{Pt}$ to form decalin, showing two double bonds in one ring $\implies$ Oxidative cleavage with $\text{KMnO}_4, \Delta$ gives cyclohexane-$1,2$-dicarboxylic acid and oxalic acid ($\text{HOOC}-\text{COOH}$), confirming the $1,3\text{-conjugated}$ diene structure in option B [FIGURE].

questions.text: Total number of isomeric compounds (including stereoisomers) formed by monochlorination of $2\text{-methylbutane}$ is _______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Determine all constitutional isomers obtained by replacing each type of non-equivalent hydrogen with $-\text{Cl}$ and count enantiomeric pairs for chiral products. // 📝 Solution: Monochlorination of $2\text{-methylbutane}$ ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CH(CH}_3\text{)}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$) with $\text{Cl}_2/h\nu$ gives $1\text{-chloro-}2\text{-methylbutane}$ ($1$ chiral center $\implies 2$ isomers), $2\text{-chloro-}2\text{-methylbutane}$ (achiral $\implies 1$ isomer), $2\text{-chloro-}3\text{-methylbutane}$ ($1$ chiral center $\implies 2$ isomers), and $1\text{-chloro-}3\text{-methylbutane}$ (achiral $\implies 1$ isomer) [FIGURE] $\implies \text{Total isomers} \;=\; 2 \;+\; 1 \;+\; 2 \;+\; 1 \;=\; 6$.

questions.text: The compound which will have the lowest rate towards nucleophilic aromatic substitution on treatment with $\text{OH}^-$ is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Electron-withdrawing groups ($-\text{NO}_2$) facilitate nucleophilic aromatic substitution ($\text{S}_\text{N}\text{Ar}$) primarily when located at ortho and para positions via resonance stabilization of the carbanion intermediate. // 📝 Solution: Electron-withdrawing groups are ineffective at the meta position in stabilizing the negative charge of the Meisenheimer complex by resonance $\implies$ $m\text{-chloronitrobenzene}$ [FIGURE] has the lowest rate towards nucleophilic aromatic substitution.

questions.text: [FIGURE] Identify (B) and (C) and how are (A) and (C) related ?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Alcoholic $\text{NaOH}$ causes $\text{E}2$ dehydrohalogenation of the primary aliphatic bromide (leaving the aryl bromide intact), followed by Markovnikov addition of $\text{HBr}$. // 📝 Solution: Compound $\text{A}$ undergoes $\text{E}2$ elimination on the side chain with $\text{NaOH(alc)}$ to form $3\text{-bromostyrene}$ ($\text{B}$) $\implies$ Electrophilic addition of $\text{HBr}$ in ether gives the Markovnikov adduct $1\text{-bromo-}3\text{-(}1\text{-bromoethyl)benzene}$ ($\text{C}$) $\implies$ $\text{A}$ and $\text{C}$ differ in the position of $-\text{Br}$ on the ethyl chain and are position isomers [FIGURE].

questions.text: But-2-yne and hydrogen (one mole each) are separately treated with (i) $\text{Pd/C}$ and (ii) $\text{Na/liq. NH}_3$ to give the products X and Y respectively. [FIGURE] Identify the incorrect statements. A. $X$ and $Y$ are stereoisomers. B. Dipole moment of X is zero. C. Boiling point of $X$ is higher than $Y$. D. X and Y react with $\text{O}_3/\text{Zn} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$ to give different products. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\text{X}$ is cis-but-2-ene ($\mu \;\neq\; 0$) and $\text{Y}$ is trans-but-2-ene ($\mu \;=\; 0$), and geometrical isomers differing only in configuration about the double bond give identical ozonolysis products. // 📝 Solution: Partial hydrogenation of but-2-yne with $\text{Pd/C}$ gives cis-but-2-ene ($\text{X}$, $\mu \;\neq\; 0$) and with $\text{Na/liq. NH}_3$ gives trans-but-2-ene ($\text{Y}$, $\mu \;=\; 0$), so Statement B is incorrect $\implies$ Both $\text{X}$ and $\text{Y}$ undergo reductive ozonolysis ($\text{O}_3/\text{Zn} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$) to yield the same product ethanal ($\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$), so Statement D is also incorrect.

questions.text: Identify the correct statements : The presence of $-\text{NO}_2$ group in benzene ring A. activates the ring towards electrophilic substitutions. B. deactivates the ring towards electrophilic substitutions. C. activates the ring towards nucleophilic substitutions. D. deactivates the ring towards nucleophilic substitutions. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A strong electron-withdrawing group ($-\text{M}, -\text{I}$) makes the benzene ring electron-deficient, disfavouring electrophilic attack while stabilizing the negatively charged intermediate in nucleophilic attack. // 📝 Solution: The $-\text{NO}_2$ group withdraws electron density from the benzene ring via $-\text{M}$ and $-\text{I}$ effects, which deactivates the ring towards electrophilic substitution (B) and activates the ring towards nucleophilic substitution (C) $\implies$ B and C Only are correct.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement (I) : The $\text{NH}_2$ group in Aniline is ortho and para directing and a powerful activating group. Statement (II) : Aniline does not undergo Friedel-Craft's reaction (alkylation and acylation). In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $-\text{NH}_2$ shows a strong $+\text{M}$ effect, but as a Lewis base it forms a strongly deactivating salt with the Lewis acid catalyst $\text{AlCl}_3$. // 📝 Solution: Statement I is correct because the $-\text{NH}_2$ group has a strong $+\text{M}$ effect that increases electron density at ortho and para positions $\implies$ Statement II is also correct because aniline reacts with $\text{AlCl}_3$ to form a complex that deactivates the benzene ring towards Friedel-Crafts alkylation and acylation.

questions.text: Number of isomeric products formed by monochlorination of $2\text{-methylbutane}$ in presence of sunlight is _______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Count all constitutional monochloro isomers and include both enantiomers for each isomer that contains a chiral carbon center. // 📝 Solution: Photochemical chlorination ($\text{Cl}_2 / h\nu$) of $2\text{-methylbutane}$ gives $1\text{-chloro-}2\text{-methylbutane}$ (chiral, $2$ enantiomers), $2\text{-chloro-}2\text{-methylbutane}$ (achiral, $1$ isomer), $2\text{-chloro-}3\text{-methylbutane}$ (chiral, $2$ enantiomers), and $1\text{-chloro-}3\text{-methylbutane}$ (achiral, $1$ isomer) [FIGURE] $\implies \text{Total number of isomeric products} \;=\; 2 \;+\; 1 \;+\; 2 \;+\; 1 \;=\; 6$.

questions.text: Which of the following compound will most easily be attacked by an electrophile?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The higher the electron density on the benzene ring due to electron-donating substituents, the faster the electrophilic attack. // 📝 Solution: The $-\text{OH}$ group in phenol donates electrons strongly into the benzene ring via its $+\text{M}$ effect, giving phenol the highest electron density among benzene, toluene, chlorobenzene, and phenol $\implies$ Phenol [FIGURE] is most easily attacked by an electrophile.

questions.text: 'X' is : [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Protonation of the alkene by $\text{HF}$ forms a tertiary carbocation, which acts as an electrophile for Friedel-Crafts alkylation of benzene. // 📝 Solution: Protonation of methylenecyclopentane by $\text{HF}$ yields the stable tertiary $1\text{-methylcyclopentyl}$ carbocation $\implies$ Electrophilic aromatic substitution (EAS) on the benzene ring gives $1\text{-methyl-}1\text{-phenylcyclopentane}$ [FIGURE].

questions.text: The product (C) in the below mentioned reaction is: $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{Br} \;\xrightarrow[\Delta]{\text{KOH}_{\left(\text{alc}\right)}}\; \text{A} \;\xrightarrow{\text{HBr}}\; \text{B} \;\xrightarrow[\text{KOH}_{\left(\text{aq}\right)}]{\Delta}\; \text{C}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Alcoholic $\text{KOH}$ promotes dehydrohalogenation to an alkene, $\text{HBr}$ adds according to Markovnikov's rule, and aqueous $\text{KOH}$ performs nucleophilic substitution. // 📝 Solution: $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{Br} \;\xrightarrow[\Delta]{\text{KOH}_{\left(\text{alc}\right)}}\; \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2\;\left(\text{A}\right) \;\xrightarrow{\text{HBr}}\; \text{CH}_3-\text{CH(Br)}-\text{CH}_3\;\left(\text{B}\right) \;\xrightarrow[\Delta]{\text{KOH}_{\left(\text{aq}\right)}}\; \text{CH}_3-\text{CH(OH)}-\text{CH}_3\;\left(\text{Propan-2-ol, C}\right)$.

questions.text: Find out the major products from the following reactions. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Hydroboration-oxidation gives the anti-Markovnikov alcohol, while oxymercuration-demercuration gives the Markovnikov alcohol without rearrangement. // 📝 Solution: Reaction with $\text{BH}_3\cdot\text{THF}$ followed by $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2 / \text{OH}^-$ results in anti-Markovnikov syn-hydration to give primary alcohol $\text{A}$ $\implies$ Reaction with $\text{Hg(OAc)}_2, \text{H}_2\text{O}$ followed by $\text{NaBH}_4$ results in Markovnikov hydration to give tertiary alcohol $\text{B}$ [FIGURE].

questions.text: The final product A, formed in the following reaction sequence is: [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Hydroboration-oxidation gives $\text{PhCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, which with $\text{HBr}$ and $\text{Mg}$ forms a Grignard reagent that attacks $\text{HCHO}$ to add one $-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ unit. // 📝 Solution: $\text{PhCH}=\text{CH}_2 \;\xrightarrow{\text{B}_2\text{H}_6 / \text{H}_2\text{O}_2, \text{OH}^-}\; \text{PhCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \;\xrightarrow{\text{HBr}}\; \text{PhCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br} \;\xrightarrow{\text{Mg / dry ether}}\; \text{PhCH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{MgBr} \;\xrightarrow{\left(\text{i}\right)\;\text{HCHO}, \left(\text{ii}\right)\;\text{H}_3\text{O}^+}\; \text{Ph}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{OH}$ [FIGURE].

questions.text: Identify A and B in the following reaction sequence. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Nitration of bromobenzene with excess fuming/conc. $\text{HNO}_3$ introduces nitro groups at the $2, 4,$ and $6$ positions, which strongly activate the $\text{C}-\text{Br}$ bond towards nucleophilic aromatic substitution by $\text{NaOH}$. // 📝 Solution: Bromobenzene reacts with conc. $\text{HNO}_3$ to form $2\text{-bromo-}1,3,5\text{-trinitrobenzene}$ ($\text{A}$) $\implies$ Treatment with $\left(\text{i}\right)\;\text{NaOH}$ and $\left(\text{ii}\right)\;\text{HCl}$ replaces $-\text{Br}$ with $-\text{OH}$ via $\text{S}_\text{N}\text{Ar}$ to yield $2,4,6\text{-trinitrophenol}$ (picric acid, $\text{B}$) [FIGURE].

questions.text: Consider the given chemical reaction : [FIGURE] Product "A" is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Oxidative cleavage of cyclohexene with hot acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$ oxidizes both $\text{sp}^2$ ring carbons to carboxylic acid groups. // 📝 Solution: Cyclohexene upon heating with $\text{KMnO}_4 / \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ undergoes ring-opening oxidative cleavage of the double bond to yield hexanedioic acid (adipic acid, $\text{HOOC}-\left(\text{CH}_2\right)_4-\text{COOH}$) [FIGURE].

questions.text: Identify product A and product B : [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\text{Cl}_2$ in the presence of light ($h\nu$) causes free-radical allylic substitution, whereas $\text{Cl}_2$ in $\text{CCl}_4$ causes electrophilic addition across the double bond. // 📝 Solution: Cyclohexene reacts with $\text{Cl}_2 / h\nu$ via a free-radical mechanism at the allylic position to form $3\text{-chlorocyclohex-}1\text{-ene}$ ($\text{A}$) $\implies$ With $\text{Cl}_2 / \text{CCl}_4$, it undergoes electrophilic addition across the double bond to give $1,2\text{-dichlorocyclohexane}$ ($\text{B}$) [FIGURE].

questions.text: Number of alkanes obtained on electrolysis of a mixture of $\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}$ and $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{COONa}$ is _______
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Kolbe's electrolysis of a mixture of two carboxylate salts produces free radicals that undergo both self-coupling and cross-coupling. // 📝 Solution: Electrolysis generates $\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_3$ and $\dot{\text{C}}_2\text{H}_5$ radicals at the anode $\implies$ Radical coupling yields $2\;\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_3 \;\longrightarrow\; \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_3$, $2\;\dot{\text{C}}_2\text{H}_5 \;\longrightarrow\; \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$, and $\dot{\text{C}}\text{H}_3 + \dot{\text{C}}_2\text{H}_5 \;\longrightarrow\; \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$ $\implies \text{Total number of alkanes} \;=\; 3$.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Benzene is nitrated to give nitrobenzene, which on further treatment with $\text{CH}_3\text{COCl}/\text{AlCl}_3$ will give [FIGURE] Statement II: $-\text{NO}_2$ group is a $m$-directing, and deactivating group. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below

options.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Strongly deactivated aromatic rings such as nitrobenzene do not undergo Friedel-Crafts alkylation or acylation. // 📝 Solution: Nitrobenzene does not react with $\text{CH}_3\text{COCl}/\text{AlCl}_3$ because the strongly deactivating $-\text{NO}_2$ group prevents Friedel-Crafts acylation (Statement I is incorrect) $\implies$ The $-\text{NO}_2$ group withdraws electron density from ortho and para positions via $-\text{M}$ and $-\text{I}$ effects, making it a meta-directing and deactivating group (Statement II is correct).

questions.text: The major products 'A' and 'B', respectively, are [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $2\text{-Methylpropene}$ reacts with cold $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to give an alkyl hydrogen sulphate addition product, while heating with $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ at $80^\circ\text{C}$ induces acid-catalyzed dimerization. // 📝 Solution: With cold $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, protonation of $\text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{C(CH}_3\text{)}=\text{CH}_2$ forms $\left(\text{CH}_3\right)_3\text{C}^+$, which combines with $\text{HSO}_4^-$ to give $\left(\text{CH}_3\right)_3\text{C}-\text{OSO}_3\text{H}$ ($\text{A}$) $\implies$ At $80^\circ\text{C}$, $\left(\text{CH}_3\right)_3\text{C}^+$ attacks another monomer molecule followed by deprotonation to give the more substituted alkene dimer $2,4,4\text{-trimethylpent-}2\text{-ene}$ ($\text{B}$) [FIGURE].

questions.text: Consider the following reaction : [FIGURE] The product Y formed is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Vicinal dibromide undergoes double dehydrohalogenation with $2\;\text{NaNH}_2$ to give a terminal alkyne ($\text{X}$), which is then deprotonated and alkylated. // 📝 Solution: $1,2\text{-Dibromobutane}$ reacts with $2\;\text{NaNH}_2$ via $\text{E}2$ elimination to form $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}$ ($\text{X}$) $\implies$ Treatment with $\left(\text{i}\right)\;\text{NaNH}_2$ forms the alkynide ion $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C}\equiv\text{C}^-\text{Na}^+$, which reacts with $\left(\text{ii}\right)$ isopropyl bromide to yield $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-\text{CH}\left(\text{CH}_3\right)_2$ ($2\text{-methylhex-}3\text{-yne}$, $\text{Y}$) [FIGURE].

questions.text: The one giving maximum number of isomeric alkenes on dehydrohalogenation reaction is (excluding rearrangement)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Dehydrohalogenation ($\beta$-elimination) yields both positional isomers and geometrical (cis/trans) isomers when two distinct $\beta$-carbons carry hydrogen atoms. // 📝 Solution: $2\text{-Bromopentane}$ ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH(Br)}-\text{CH}_3$) undergoes $\beta\text{-elimination}$ to give pent-$1$-ene, cis-pent-$2$-ene, and trans-pent-$2$-ene (total $3$ isomeric alkenes), whereas all other options produce only $1$ alkene each [FIGURE].

questions.text: Given below are two statements for the following reaction sequence. [FIGURE] Statement I: Compound 'Z' will give yellow precipitate with $\text{NaOI}$. Statement II: Compound 'Q' has two different types of 'H' atoms (aromatic : aliphatic) in the ratio $1 : 3$. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Dehydrohalogenation of $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{Cl}_2$ gives propyne ($\text{Y}$), which hydrates to acetone ($\text{Z}$) and trimerizes in a red-hot iron tube to mesitylene ($\text{Q}$). // 📝 Solution: $\text{C}_3\text{H}_6\text{Cl}_2\;\left(\text{X}\right) \;\xrightarrow{\text{excess NaNH}_2}\; \text{CH}_3-\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}\;\left(\text{Y}\right)$ $\implies$ Hydration of $\text{Y}$ with $\text{dil. H}_2\text{SO}_4, \text{Hg}^{2+}$ gives $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$ ($\text{Z}$), which gives a yellow precipitate of $\text{CHI}_3$ with $\text{NaOI}$ (Statement I is true) $\implies$ Cyclic trimerization of $\text{Y}$ in a red hot iron tube gives mesitylene ($1,3,5\text{-trimethylbenzene}$, $\text{Q}$), which has $3$ aromatic and $9$ aliphatic $\text{H}$ atoms in the ratio $3 : 9 \;=\; 1 : 3$ (Statement II is true) [FIGURE].

questions.text: Number of compounds from the following which cannot undergo Friedel-Crafts reactions is: ________. toluene, nitrobenzene, xylene, cumene, aniline, chlorobenzene, $m$-nitroaniline, $m$-dinitrobenzene
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Aromatic rings bearing strongly deactivating $-\text{NO}_2$ groups or basic $-\text{NH}_2$ groups (which coordinate with $\text{AlCl}_3$) fail to undergo Friedel-Crafts reactions. // 📝 Solution: Nitrobenzene, aniline, $m\text{-nitroaniline}$, and $m\text{-dinitrobenzene}$ do not undergo Friedel-Crafts reactions due to strong ring deactivation [FIGURE] $\implies \text{Total number of compounds} \;=\; 4$.

questions.text: Identify $A$ and $B$ in the given chemical reaction sequence : [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Friedel-Crafts acylation of benzene with succinic anhydride gives a $\gamma$-keto acid ($A$), which undergoes Clemmensen reduction of the ketone carbonyl to give $4\text{-phenylbutanoic acid}$ ($B$). // 📝 Solution: Benzene undergoes Friedel-Crafts acylation with succinic anhydride in the presence of $\text{AlCl}_3$ to form $4\text{-oxo-}4\text{-phenylbutanoic acid}$ ($\text{A}$) $\implies$ Clemmensen reduction ($\text{Zn-Hg / HCl}$) reduces the ketonic $\text{C}=\text{O}$ group to $-\text{CH}_2-$, yielding $4\text{-phenylbutanoic acid}$ ($\text{B}$) [FIGURE].

questions.text: The major product 'P' for the following sequence of reactions is: [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\text{Zn/Hg}$ with $\text{HCl}$ selectively reduces the ketone group to a methylene group, and $\text{LiAlH}_4$ reduces the amide group to a primary amine. // 📝 Solution: Step 1: Clemmensen reduction ($\text{Zn/Hg, HCl}$) selectively reduces the ketone carbonyl ($-\text{CO}-$) to $-\text{CH}_2-$, giving $\text{Ph}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CONH}_2$ $\implies$ Step 2: Reduction with $\text{LiAlH}_4$ followed by $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$ converts the amide group ($-\text{CONH}_2$) into $-\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$, yielding $\text{Ph}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{NH}_2$ [FIGURE].

questions.text: Given below are two statements : Statement I : [FIGURE] under Clemmensen reduction conditions will give [FIGURE]. Statement II : [FIGURE] under Wolff-Kishner reduction condition will give [FIGURE]. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.text: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Clemmensen reduction uses hot acidic conditions ($\text{Zn-Hg / conc. HCl}$) which also hydrolyzes amides, whereas Wolff-Kishner reduction uses strongly basic conditions ($\text{NH}_2\text{NH}_2 / \text{OH}^-$) which causes elimination of alkyl halides. // 📝 Solution: In Statement I, under acidic Clemmensen conditions ($\text{Zn-Hg / conc. HCl}$), the ketone carbonyl is reduced to $-\text{CH}_2-$ and the amide group ($-\text{CONH}_2$) undergoes acid hydrolysis to $-\text{COOH}$ (True) $\implies$ In Statement II, under strongly basic Wolff-Kishner conditions ($\text{NH}_2\text{NH}_2 / \text{OH}^-, \text{glycol}$), the $-\text{Cl}$ group undergoes dehydrohalogenation (elimination) along with carbonyl reduction (False) [FIGURE].

questions.text: But-2-yne is reacted separately with one mole of Hydrogen as shown below: $\text{B} \;\xleftarrow[\text{liq NH}_3]{\text{Na}}\; \text{CH}_3-\text{C}\equiv\text{C}-\text{CH}_3 \;\xrightarrow[\Delta]{\text{Pd/C, }+\text{H}_2}\; \text{A}$. Identify the incorrect statements from the options given below: A. A is more soluble than B. B. The boiling point & melting point of A are higher and lower than B respectively. C. A is more polar than B because dipole moment of A is zero. D. $\text{Br}_2$ adds easily to B than A.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\text{A}$ is cis-but-2-ene ($\mu \;\neq\; 0$) and $\text{B}$ is trans-but-2-ene ($\mu \;=\; 0$). // 📝 Solution: Hydrogenation with $\text{Pd/C}$ gives cis-but-$2$-ene ($\text{A}$, $\mu \;\neq\; 0$, higher boiling point, lower melting point, more reactive with $\text{Br}_2$) and Birch reduction ($\text{Na/liq. NH}_3$) gives trans-but-$2$-ene ($\text{B}$, $\mu \;=\; 0$) $\implies$ Statements C and D are definitely incorrect, matching option B as the closest official choice.

questions.text: The cycloalkene $\left(\text{X}\right)$ on bromination consumes one mole of bromine per mole of $\left(\text{X}\right)$ and gives the product $\left(\text{Y}\right)$ in which $\text{C} : \text{Br}$ ratio is $3 : 1$. The percentage of bromine in the product $\left(\text{Y}\right)$ is ____%. (Nearest integer) (Given : molar mass in $\text{g mol}^{-1}$ $\text{H} : 1, \text{C} : 12, \text{O} : 16, \text{Br} : 80$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Addition of $1\;\text{mol}$ of $\text{Br}_2$ adds $2$ bromine atoms per molecule, which fixes the number of carbon atoms at $2 \;\times\; 3 \;=\; 6$. // 📝 Solution: Since product $\text{Y}$ contains $2\;\text{Br}$ atoms and the atomic ratio $\text{C} : \text{Br} \;=\; 3 : 1$, the number of $\text{C}$ atoms is $6$ $\implies \text{Molar mass of dibromo adduct} \;=\; 6\left(12\right) \;+\; 12\left(1\right) \;+\; 2\left(80\right) \;=\; 244\;\text{g/mol} \implies \text{Percentage of Br} \;=\; \frac{160}{244} \;\times\; 100 \;=\; 65.57\% \;\approx\; 66\%$.

questions.text: In the following given reaction 'A' is [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Electrophilic addition of $\text{HBr}$ to an alkene adjacent to a cyclobutane ring proceeds via carbocation formation followed by ring expansion to relieve strain. // 📝 Solution: Protonation of the double bond forms a tertiary carbocation adjacent to the $4\text{-membered}$ ring $\implies$ $1,2\text{-alkyl}$ shift causes ring expansion to a $5\text{-membered}$ cyclopentane ring $\implies$ $1,2\text{-methyl}$ shift followed by nucleophilic attack of $\text{Br}^-$ gives $1\text{-bromo-}1,2\text{-dimethylcyclopentane}$ [FIGURE].

questions.text: Which of the following is strongest Bronsted base?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Availability of the lone pair on N decides basic strength // 📝 Solution: (1) aniline and (2) diphenylamine have delocalised lone pairs, and (3) pyrrole has the lone pair in the aromatic sextet, so all are weakly basic $\implies$ (4) pyrrolidine has a localised lone pair on $sp^3$ N and is the strongest base

questions.text: A 1 L buffer is prepared with 0.10 mol each of $\text{NH}_3$ and $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$. On adding 0.05 mol HCl, the change in pH is ____ $\times10^{-2}$ (nearest integer). Given $\text{p}K_b(\text{NH}_3)=4.745$ and $\log_{10}3 = 0.477$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use the basic buffer equation before and after the HCl addition. // 📝 Solution: After HCl, $[\text{NH}_3]=0.05$ and $[\text{NH}_4^+]=0.15$ $\implies$ $\text{pOH}' = 4.745+\log3 = 5.222$ $\implies$ $\Delta\text{pH}=0.477\approx48\times10^{-2}$.

questions.text: An aqueous HCl solution of pH 1.0 is diluted by adding an equal volume of water (ignore dissociation of water). The pH of the solution would: (Given $\log 2 = 0.30$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Equal-volume dilution halves $[\text{H}^+]$. // 📝 Solution: $[\text{H}^+]_{\text{new}} = \dfrac{10^{-1}}{2}$ $\implies$ $\text{pH} = -\log(0.05) = 1+\log2 = 1.3$.

questions.text: The pH at which $\mathrm{Mg(OH)_2}$ $\left[ K_{sp} \; = \; 1 \times 10^{-11} \right]$ begins to precipitate from a solution containing $0.10$ M $\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}$ ions is ______
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Precipitation begins when $Q_{sp} \; = \; K_{sp}$ // 📝 Solution: $0.1 \times \left[ \mathrm{OH^-} \right]^2 \; = \; 10^{-11} \implies \left[ \mathrm{OH^-} \right] \; = \; 10^{-5} \implies \mathrm{pOH} \; = \; 5 \implies \mathrm{pH} \; = \; 9$

questions.text: The first and second ionization constants of $\mathrm{H_2X}$ are $2.5 \times 10^{-8}$ and $1.0 \times 10^{-13}$ respectively. The concentration of $\mathrm{X^{2-}}$ in $0.1$ M $\mathrm{H_2X}$ solution is ______ $\times 10^{-15}$ M. (Nearest Integer)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: If $K_{a1} \gg K_{a2}$, then $\left[ \mathrm{HX^-} \right] \approx \left[ \mathrm{H^+} \right]$ and $\left[ \mathrm{X^{2-}} \right] \approx K_{a2}$ // 📝 Solution: $\left[ \mathrm{H^+} \right] \; = \; \sqrt{2.5 \times 10^{-8} \times 0.1} \; = \; 5 \times 10^{-5} \; = \; \left[ \mathrm{HX^-} \right] \implies \left[ \mathrm{X^{2-}} \right] \; = \; K_{a2} \; = \; 1.0 \times 10^{-13} \; = \; 100 \times 10^{-15}\;\mathrm{M}$

questions.text: A weak acid HA has degree of dissociation $x$. Which option gives the correct expression of $\left(\text{pH}-\text{p}K_a\right)$?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Write $K_a\;=\;\frac{\left[\text{H}^+\right]x}{1-x}$ and take negative logs. // 📝 Solution: $\left[\text{H}^+\right]\;=\;K_a\frac{1-x}{x}\implies\;\text{pH}\;=\;\text{p}K_a\;-\;\log\frac{1-x}{x}\implies\;\text{pH}-\text{p}K_a\;=\;\log\frac{x}{1-x}$

questions.text: Total number of non-bonded electrons present in the $\text{NO}_2^-$ ion based on Lewis theory is ______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Draw the Lewis structure and count lone-pair electrons on all atoms. // 📝 Solution: $\text{O=N-O}^-$ has $2$ lone pairs on $\text{O}$ (double bond), $3$ on $\text{O}^-$, $1$ on $\text{N}\implies\;12$ non-bonding electrons

questions.text: At $298$ K, the solubility of silver chloride in water is $1.434 \times 10^{-3}\;\mathrm{g\,L^{-1}}$. The value of $-\log K_{sp}$ for silver chloride is ______. (Given mass of Ag is $107.9\;\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$ and mass of Cl is $35.5\;\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For AgCl, $K_{sp} \; = \; S^2$ with $S$ in mol per litre // 📝 Solution: $M \; = \; 143.4 \implies S \; = \; \frac{1.434 \times 10^{-3}}{143.4} \; = \; 10^{-5}\;\mathrm{M} \implies K_{sp} \; = \; 10^{-10} \implies -\log K_{sp} \; = \; 10$

questions.text: Match List I with List II. List I (Amines): A. Aniline; B. Ethanamine; C. N-Ethylethanamine; D. N,N-Diethylethanamine. List II ($\mathrm{p}K_b$): I. $3.25$; II. $3.00$; III. $9.38$; IV. $3.29$. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Basic strength is proportional to $\frac{1}{\mathrm{p}K_b}$, and in aqueous medium $2^\circ$ amine is the most basic // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] $\mathrm{p}K_b$ order: $\text{Aniline} \; > \; \text{Ethanamine} \; > \; \text{N,N-Diethylethanamine} \; > \; \text{N-Ethylethanamine} \implies 9.38 \; > \; 3.29 \; > \; 3.25 \; > \; 3.00 \implies \text{A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I}$

questions.text: The pH of water is $7$ at $25^\circ\text{C}$. If water is heated to $80^\circ\text{C}$, its pH will:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Ionisation of water is endothermic, so $K_w$ increases with temperature. // 📝 Solution: $T\;\uparrow\implies\;K_w\;\uparrow\implies\;\left[\text{H}^+\right]\;\uparrow\implies\;\text{pH}\;\approx\;6.93$ (decreases) while the water stays neutral

questions.text: $x$ mg of pure HCl was used to make an aqueous solution. $25.0$ mL of $0.1$ M $\mathrm{Ba(OH)_2}$ solution is used when the HCl solution was titrated against it. The numerical value of $x$ is ______ $\times 10^{-1}$. (Nearest integer) Given: Molar mass of HCl and $\mathrm{Ba(OH)_2}$ are $36.5$ and $171.0\;\mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$ respectively.
