questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $2\,\mathrm{HCl} \; + \; \mathrm{Ba(OH)_2} \; \rightarrow \; \mathrm{BaCl_2} \; + \; 2\,\mathrm{H_2O}$, so $n_{\mathrm{HCl}} \; = \; 2\,n_{\mathrm{Ba(OH)_2}}$ // 📝 Solution: $n_{\mathrm{Ba(OH)_2}} \; = \; 0.1 \times 0.025 \; = \; 0.0025\;\text{mol} \implies n_{\mathrm{HCl}} \; = \; 0.005\;\text{mol} \implies m \; = \; 0.005 \times 36.5 \; = \; 182.5\;\text{mg} \; = \; 1825 \times 10^{-1}$

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement (I): Aqueous solution of ammonium carbonate is basic. Statement (II): Acidic/basic nature of salt solution of a salt of weak acid and weak base depends on $K_a$ and $K_b$ value of acid and the base forming it. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For a weak acid + weak base salt, $\mathrm{pH} \; = \; \frac{\mathrm{p}K_w \; + \; \mathrm{p}K_a \; - \; \mathrm{p}K_b}{2}$ // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{pH}$ depends on $K_a$ and $K_b \implies$ Statement II is correct $\implies$ for $\left( \mathrm{NH_4} \right)_2\mathrm{CO_3}$, $K_b \; > \; K_a$ so the solution is basic $\implies$ Statement I is correct

questions.text: Consider two Group IV metal ions $\mathrm{X^{2+}}$ and $\mathrm{Y^{2+}}$. A solution containing $0.01$ M $\mathrm{X^{2+}}$ and $0.01$ M $\mathrm{Y^{2+}}$ is saturated with $\mathrm{H_2S}$. The pH at which the metal sulphide YS will form as a precipitate is ______. (Nearest integer) (Given: $K_{sp}(\mathrm{XS}) \; = \; 1 \times 10^{-22}$ at $25^\circ \mathrm{C}$, $K_{sp}(\mathrm{YS}) \; = \; 4 \times 10^{-16}$ at $25^\circ \mathrm{C}$, $\left[ \mathrm{H_2S} \right] \; = \; 0.1$ M in solution, $K_{a1} \times K_{a2}(\mathrm{H_2S}) \; = \; 1.0 \times 10^{-21}$, $\log 2 \; = \; 0.30$, $\log 3 \; = \; 0.48$, $\log 5 \; = \; 0.70$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: YS precipitates when $\left[ \mathrm{Y^{2+}} \right] \left[ \mathrm{S^{2-}} \right] \; \ge \; K_{sp}$ and $\left[ \mathrm{S^{2-}} \right] \; = \; \frac{K_{a1} K_{a2} \left[ \mathrm{H_2S} \right]}{\left[ \mathrm{H^+} \right]^2}$ // 📝 Solution: $\left[ \mathrm{S^{2-}} \right] \; \ge \; \frac{4 \times 10^{-16}}{10^{-2}} \; = \; 4 \times 10^{-14} \implies \frac{10^{-21} \times 0.1}{\left[ \mathrm{H^+} \right]^2} \; \ge \; 4 \times 10^{-14} \implies \left[ \mathrm{H^+} \right] \; \le \; \frac{1}{2} \times 10^{-4} \implies \mathrm{pH} \; \ge \; 4.3 \; \approx \; 4$

questions.text: 10 mL of 2 M NaOH is added to 20 mL of 1 M HCl kept in a beaker. 10 mL of this mixture is poured into a 100 mL volumetric flask already containing 2 mol HCl, and the volume is made up to the mark with distilled water. The solution in the flask is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Equal moles of NaOH and HCl neutralise completely before the dilution step. // 📝 Solution: $0.2$ mol NaOH and $0.2$ mol HCl react fully, so the mixture is neutral $\implies$ the flask holds $2$ mol HCl in $0.1\,\text{L}$ $\implies$ $M = \dfrac{2}{0.1} = 20\,\text{M}$.

questions.text: The pH of an aqueous solution containing $1$ M benzoic acid $\left( \mathrm{p}K_a \; = \; 4.20 \right)$ and $1$ M sodium benzoate is $4.5$. The volume of benzoic acid solution in $300$ mL of this buffer solution is ______ mL.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mathrm{pH} \; = \; \mathrm{p}K_a \; + \; \log \frac{V_s}{V_a}$ for equimolar stock solutions // 📝 Solution: $4.5 \; = \; 4.2 \; + \; \log \frac{V_s}{V_a} \implies \frac{V_s}{V_a} \; = \; 2$ and $V_s \; + \; V_a \; = \; 300 \implies V_a \; = \; 100$ mL

questions.text: If a $1\;\text{mM}$ solution of ethylamine produces $\text{pH}\;=\;9$, then the ionization constant $K_b$ of ethylamine is $10^{-x}$. The value of $x$ is ______ (nearest integer). [The degree of ionization of ethylamine can be neglected with respect to unity.]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Get $\left[\text{OH}^-\right]$ from pOH, then use $K_b\;=\;\frac{\left[\text{OH}^-\right]^2}{C}$. // 📝 Solution: $\text{pOH}\;=\;5\implies\;\left[\text{OH}^-\right]\;=\;10^{-5}\implies\;K_b\;=\;\frac{10^{-10}}{10^{-3}}\;=\;10^{-7}\implies\;x\;=\;7$
questions.topic: Ionization constant of a weak base

questions.text: Which of the following mixture gives a buffer solution with pH $= 9.25$? Given: $\mathrm{p}K_b(\mathrm{NH_4OH}) \; = \; 4.75$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mathrm{pH} \; = \; 9.25 \implies \mathrm{pOH} \; = \; 4.75 \; = \; \mathrm{p}K_b$, so $[\text{salt}] \; = \; [\text{base}]$ // 📝 Solution: Option (1): $\mathrm{NH_4OH} \; = \; 100$ mmol, $\mathrm{HCl} \; = \; 50$ mmol $\implies$ remaining $\mathrm{NH_4OH} \; = \; 50$ mmol, $\mathrm{NH_4Cl} \; = \; 50$ mmol $\implies \mathrm{pOH} \; = \; 4.75 \; + \; \log 1 \; = \; 4.75$

questions.text: Millimoles of calcium hydroxide required to produce $100$ mL of the aqueous solution of pH $12$ is $x \times 10^{-1}$. The value of $x$ is ______ (Nearest integer). Assume complete dissociation.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mathrm{pOH} \; = \; 14 \; - \; \mathrm{pH}$ and $\left[ \mathrm{Ca(OH)_2} \right] \; = \; \frac{\left[ \mathrm{OH^-} \right]}{2}$ // 📝 Solution: $\left[ \mathrm{OH^-} \right] \; = \; 10^{-2}\;\mathrm{M} \implies \left[ \mathrm{Ca(OH)_2} \right] \; = \; 5 \times 10^{-3}\;\mathrm{M} \implies \text{mmol} \; = \; 5 \times 10^{-3} \times 100 \; = \; 0.5 \; = \; 5 \times 10^{-1} \implies x \; = \; 5$

questions.text: The dissociation constant of acetic acid is $x \times 10^{-5}$. When $25$ mL of $0.2$ M $\mathrm{CH_3COONa}$ solution is mixed with $25$ mL of $0.02$ M $\mathrm{CH_3COOH}$ solution, the pH of the resultant solution is found to be equal to $5$. The value of $x$ is ______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Buffer equation $\mathrm{pH} \; = \; \mathrm{p}K_a \; + \; \log \frac{[\text{salt}]}{[\text{acid}]}$ // 📝 Solution: $\text{salt} : \text{acid} \; = \; 5 : 0.5 \; = \; 10 \implies 5 \; = \; \mathrm{p}K_a \; + \; 1 \implies \mathrm{p}K_a \; = \; 4 \implies K_a \; = \; 10^{-4} \; = \; 10 \times 10^{-5} \implies x \; = \; 10$

questions.text: Solubility of calcium phosphate (molecular mass, $M$) in water is $W$ g per $100$ mL at $25^\circ \mathrm{C}$. Its solubility product at $25^\circ \mathrm{C}$ will be approximately.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For $\mathrm{Ca_3(PO_4)_2}$, $K_{sp} \; = \; 108\,S^5$ // 📝 Solution: $S \; = \; \frac{W \times 1000}{M \times 100} \; = \; \frac{10\,W}{M} \implies K_{sp} \; = \; \left( 3S \right)^3 \left( 2S \right)^2 \; = \; 108 \times 10^{5} \left( \frac{W}{M} \right)^5 \; \approx \; 10^{7}\left( \frac{W}{M} \right)^{5}$

questions.text: $600$ mL of $0.01$ M HCl is mixed with $400$ mL of $0.01$ M $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$. The pH of the mixture is ______ $\times 10^{-2}$. (Nearest integer) [Given: $\log 2 \; = \; 0.30$, $\log 3 \; = \; 0.48$, $\log 5 \; = \; 0.69$, $\log 7 \; = \; 0.84$, $\log 11 \; = \; 1.04$]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Add total millimoles of $\mathrm{H^+}$ and divide by total volume // 📝 Solution: $n_{\mathrm{H^+}} \; = \; 600 \times 0.01 \; + \; 400 \times 0.01 \times 2 \; = \; 14\;\text{mmol} \implies \left[ \mathrm{H^+} \right] \; = \; \frac{14}{1000} \; = \; 14 \times 10^{-3} \implies \mathrm{pH} \; = \; 3 \; - \; \log 14 \; = \; 3 \; - \; 1.14 \; = \; 1.86 \; = \; 186 \times 10^{-2}$
questions.topic: pH of Mixture of Strong Acids

questions.text: The pH of a $0.01\,\text{M}$ weak acid HX ($K_a = 4\times10^{-10}$) is found to be 5. On dilution with excess water the pH changes to 6. The new concentration of the diluted acid is $x\times10^{-4}\,\text{M}$. The value of $x$ is ____ (nearest integer).
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: At pH 6, $[\text{H}^+]=10^{-6}$; use $K_a = \dfrac{[\text{H}^+]^2}{C-[\text{H}^+]}$. // 📝 Solution: $4\times10^{-10} = \dfrac{10^{-12}}{C-10^{-6}}$ $\implies$ $C\approx2.5\times10^{-3} = 25\times10^{-4}\,\text{M}$ $\implies$ $x=25$ (the source flags the data as inconsistent).

questions.text: A litre of buffer solution contains $0.1$ mole of each of $\mathrm{NH_3}$ and $\mathrm{NH_4Cl}$. On the addition of $0.02$ mole of HCl by dissolving gaseous HCl, the pH of the solution is found to be ______ $\times 10^{-3}$ (Nearest integer). [Given: $\mathrm{p}K_b(\mathrm{NH_3}) \; = \; 4.745$, $\log 2 \; = \; 0.301$, $\log 3 \; = \; 0.477$, $T \; = \; 298$ K]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Basic buffer: $\mathrm{pOH} \; = \; \mathrm{p}K_b \; + \; \log \frac{[\mathrm{NH_4^+}]}{[\mathrm{NH_3}]}$ // 📝 Solution: $n_{\mathrm{NH_3}} \; = \; 0.08,\; n_{\mathrm{NH_4^+}} \; = \; 0.12 \implies \mathrm{pOH} \; = \; 4.745 \; + \; \log \frac{3}{2} \; = \; 4.921 \implies \mathrm{pH} \; = \; 14 \; - \; 4.921 \; = \; 9.079 \; = \; 9079 \times 10^{-3}$

questions.text: The correct order of $\mathrm{p}K_a$ values for the following compounds is: (a) phenol, (b) p-N,N-dimethylaminophenol, (c) p-nitrophenol, (d) p-isopropylphenol. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $-M$ and $-I$ groups increase acidity, while $+M$ and $+H$ groups decrease acidity // 📝 Solution: $-\mathrm{NO_2}$ increases acidity, $+M$ of $-\mathrm{N(CH_3)_2}$ decreases it strongly, and isopropyl (hyperconjugation) decreases it slightly $\implies$ acidity: $c \; > \; a \; > \; d \; > \; b \implies \mathrm{p}K_a: b \; > \; d \; > \; a \; > \; c$

questions.text: $K_{sp}$ for $\text{Cr}\left(\text{OH}\right)_3$ is $1.6\times 10^{-30}$. What is the molar solubility of this salt in water?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For $\text{AB}_3$ type salt, $K_{sp}\;=\;s\left(3s\right)^3$. // 📝 Solution: $K_{sp}\;=\;27s^4\implies\;s\;=\;\sqrt[4]{\frac{1.6\times 10^{-30}}{27}}$

questions.text: The equilibrium constant for $\text{H}_2\text{O(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{H}_2\text{(g)} + \tfrac12\text{O}_2\text{(g)}$ ($\Delta G^\circ = 92.34\,\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$) is $8.0\times10^{-3}$ at 2300 K with total equilibrium pressure 1 bar. The degree of dissociation $\alpha$ of water is ____ $\times10^{-2}$ (nearest integer). Assume $\alpha$ is negligible compared with 1.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: With $\alpha\ll1$, $n_{\text{total}}\approx1$, so $P_{\text{H}_2}=\alpha$, $P_{\text{O}_2}=\alpha/2$, $P_{\text{H}_2\text{O}}\approx1$. // 📝 Solution: $K_p = \dfrac{\alpha\,(\alpha/2)^{1/2}}{1} = 8\times10^{-3}$ $\implies$ $\alpha^{3} = 128\times10^{-6}$ $\implies$ $\alpha\approx5.03\times10^{-2}$.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: On passing $\mathrm{HCl_{(g)}}$ through a saturated solution of $\mathrm{BaCl_2}$, at room temperature white turbidity appears. Statement II: When HCl gas is passed through a saturated solution of NaCl, sodium chloride is precipitated due to common ion effect. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Common ion effect lowers the solubility of a salt in a saturated solution // 📝 Solution: Passing $\mathrm{HCl(g)}$ raises $\left[ \mathrm{Cl^-} \right]$, so $\mathrm{BaCl_2}$ precipitates as white turbidity $\implies$ Statement I is correct $\implies$ per the official answer key Statement II is marked incorrect $\implies$ Option (2)

questions.text: $x$ mg of $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ (molar mass $58\,\text{g mol}^{-1}$) must be dissolved in 1.0 L of water to produce a pH of 10.0 at 298 K. The value of $x$ is ____ mg (nearest integer). Assume $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ dissociates completely in water.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $[\text{OH}^-] = 10^{-4}$ and each $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ releases two $\text{OH}^-$ ions. // 📝 Solution: $n = \dfrac{10^{-4}}{2} = 5\times10^{-5}\,\text{mol}$ $\implies$ mass $= 5\times10^{-5}\times58\times10^{3}\,\text{mg} = 2.9\,\text{mg}\approx3$.

questions.text: Consider a weak base 'B' of $\mathrm{p}K_b \; = \; 5.699$. '$x$' mL of $0.02$ M HCl and '$y$' mL of $0.02$ M weak base 'B' are mixed to make $100$ mL of a buffer of pH $9$ at $25^\circ \mathrm{C}$. The values of '$x$' and '$y$' respectively are: [Given: $\log 2 \; = \; 0.3010$, $\log 3 \; = \; 0.4771$, $\log 5 \; = \; 0.699$]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Basic buffer after partial neutralisation: $\mathrm{pOH} \; = \; \mathrm{p}K_b \; + \; \log \frac{\text{salt}}{\text{base}}$ // 📝 Solution: $\text{salt} \; = \; 0.02x,\; \text{base} \; = \; 0.02\left( y - x \right),\; \mathrm{pOH} \; = \; 5 \implies 5 \; = \; 5.699 \; + \; \log \frac{x}{y-x} \implies \frac{x}{y-x} \; = \; \frac{1}{5} \implies y \; = \; 6x$, and $x \; + \; y \; = \; 100 \implies x \; = \; \frac{100}{7} \; = \; 14.3,\; y \; = \; \frac{600}{7} \; = \; 85.7$

questions.text: When the hydrogen ion concentration $\left[ \mathrm{H^+} \right]$ changes by a factor of $1000$, the value of pH of the solution ______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mathrm{pH} \; = \; -\log \left[ \mathrm{H^+} \right]$, so a factor of $10^3$ shifts pH by $3$ units // 📝 Solution: $\Delta \mathrm{pH} \; = \; -\log \left( 10^{3} \right) \; = \; -3 \implies$ pH decreases by $3$ units (Option 2). Note: the source answer key lists 4, which contradicts its own worked solution, so please verify.

questions.text: For a sparingly soluble salt $\mathrm{AB_2}$, the equilibrium concentrations of $\mathrm{A^{2+}}$ ions and $\mathrm{B^-}$ ions are $1.2 \times 10^{-4}\;\mathrm{M}$ and $0.24 \times 10^{-3}\;\mathrm{M}$, respectively. The solubility product of $\mathrm{AB_2}$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $K_{sp} \; = \; \left[ \mathrm{A^{2+}} \right] \left[ \mathrm{B^-} \right]^2$ // 📝 Solution: $K_{sp} \; = \; 1.2 \times 10^{-4} \times \left( 2.4 \times 10^{-4} \right)^2 \; = \; 6.91 \times 10^{-12}\;\mathrm{M^3}$

questions.text: The logarithm of equilibrium constant for the reaction $\mathrm{Pd^{2+}} \; + \; 4\mathrm{Cl^-} \; \rightleftharpoons \; \mathrm{PdCl_4^{2-}}$ is ______ (Nearest integer). Given: $\frac{2.303\,RT}{F} \; = \; 0.06$ V; $\mathrm{Pd^{2+}_{(aq)}} \; + \; 2e^- \; \rightleftharpoons \; \mathrm{Pd(s)}$, $E^\circ \; = \; 0.83$ V; $\mathrm{PdCl_4^{2-}(aq)} \; + \; 2e^- \; \rightleftharpoons \; \mathrm{Pd(s)} \; + \; 4\mathrm{Cl^-(aq)}$, $E^\circ \; = \; 0.65$ V
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\log K \; = \; \frac{n\,E^\circ_{\text{cell}}}{0.06}$ // 📝 Solution: $E^\circ_{\text{cell}} \; = \; 0.83 \; - \; 0.65 \; = \; 0.18\;\mathrm{V},\; n \; = \; 2 \implies \log K \; = \; \frac{2 \times 0.18}{0.06} \; = \; 6$

questions.text: Arrange the following in increasing order of solubility product: $\text{Ca}\left(\text{OH}\right)_2$, $\text{AgBr}$, $\text{PbS}$, $\text{HgS}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall the $K_{sp}$ values used in salt analysis group separation. // 📝 Solution: $\text{HgS}\;\left(4\times 10^{-53}\right)\;<\;\text{PbS}\;\left(8\times 10^{-28}\right)\;<\;\text{AgBr}\;\left(5\times 10^{-13}\right)\;<\;\text{Ca}\left(\text{OH}\right)_2\;\left(5.5\times 10^{-6}\right)$

questions.text: Incorrect statement for the use of indicators in acid-base titration is:

options.text: Methyl orange may be used for a weak acid vs weak base titration.
Methyl orange is a suitable indicator for a strong acid vs weak base titration
Phenolphthalein is a suitable indicator for a weak acid vs strong base titration
Phenolphthalein may be used for a strong acid vs strong base titration.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Indicator pH range must cover the pH at the equivalence point // 📝 Solution: $\text{Methyl orange} : 3.2 - 4.5,\; \text{Phenolphthalein} : 8.3 - 10.5 \implies$ weak acid vs weak base has no sharp pH jump, so methyl orange is unsuitable $\implies$ statement (1) is incorrect

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement (I): A Buffer solution is the mixture of a salt and an acid or a base mixed in any particular quantities. Statement (II): Blood is naturally occurring buffer solution whose pH is maintained by $\mathrm{H_2CO_3} / \mathrm{HCO_3^-}$ concentrations. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A buffer needs a weak acid or base with its conjugate in suitable proportions // 📝 Solution: Buffer $=$ weak acid or weak base $+$ its conjugate, not any quantities $\implies$ Statement I is false $\implies$ Blood is a $\mathrm{H_2CO_3} / \mathrm{HCO_3^-}$ buffer $\implies$ Statement II is true

questions.text: The molar solubility $s$ of zirconium phosphate with molecular formula $\left(\text{Zr}^{4+}\right)_3\left(\text{PO}_4^{3-}\right)_4$ is given by the relation:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For $\text{A}_3\text{B}_4$ write $K_{sp}\;=\;\left(3s\right)^3\left(4s\right)^4$. // 📝 Solution: $K_{sp}\;=\;27\times 256\,s^7\;=\;6912\,s^7\implies\;s\;=\;\left(\frac{K_{sp}}{6912}\right)^{1/7}$

questions.text: $K_a$ for $\mathrm{CH_3COOH}$ is $1.8 \times 10^{-5}$ and $K_b$ for $\mathrm{NH_4OH}$ is $1.8 \times 10^{-5}$. The pH of ammonium acetate solution will be
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Salt of weak acid and weak base: $\mathrm{pH} \; = \; \frac{\mathrm{p}K_w \; + \; \mathrm{p}K_a \; - \; \mathrm{p}K_b}{2}$ // 📝 Solution: $K_a \; = \; K_b \implies \mathrm{p}K_a \; = \; \mathrm{p}K_b \implies \mathrm{pH} \; = \; \frac{\mathrm{p}K_w}{2} \; = \; 7$

questions.text: Consider the dissociation equilibrium of the following weak acid $\mathrm{HA} \; \rightleftharpoons \; \mathrm{H^+(aq)} \; + \; \mathrm{A^-(aq)}$. If the $\mathrm{p}K_a$ of the acid is $4$, then the pH of $10$ mM HA solution is ______. (Nearest integer) [Given: The degree of dissociation can be neglected with respect to unity]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For a weak acid with $\alpha \ll 1$, $\left[ \mathrm{H^+} \right] \; = \; \sqrt{K_a\,C}$ // 📝 Solution: $K_a \; = \; 10^{-4},\; C \; = \; 0.01\;\mathrm{M} \implies \left[ \mathrm{H^+} \right]^2 \; = \; 10^{-4} \times 10^{-2} \; = \; 10^{-6} \implies \left[ \mathrm{H^+} \right] \; = \; 10^{-3} \implies \mathrm{pH} \; = \; 3$

questions.text: If the $\mathrm{p}K_a$ of lactic acid is $5$, then the pH of $0.005$ M calcium lactate solution at $25^\circ \mathrm{C}$ is ______ $\times 10^{-1}$ (Nearest integer). Lactic acid: [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Salt of weak acid and strong base: $\mathrm{pH} \; = \; 7 \; + \; \frac{1}{2}\left( \mathrm{p}K_a \; + \; \log C \right)$ // 📝 Solution: $C_{\text{lactate}} \; = \; 2 \times 0.005 \; = \; 0.01\;\mathrm{M} \implies \mathrm{pH} \; = \; 7 \; + \; \frac{1}{2}\left( 5 \; - \; 2 \right) \; = \; 8.5 \; = \; 85 \times 10^{-1}$

questions.text: Which of the following happens when $\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$ is added gradually to a solution containing $1\;\text{M}\;\text{A}^{2+}$ and $1\;\text{M}\;\text{B}^{3+}$ ions? Given: $K_{sp}\left[\text{A}\left(\text{OH}\right)_2\right]\;=\;9\times 10^{-10}$ and $K_{sp}\left[\text{B}\left(\text{OH}\right)_3\right]\;=\;27\times 10^{-18}$ at $298\;\text{K}$.

options.text: Both $\text{A}\left(\text{OH}\right)_2$ and $\text{B}\left(\text{OH}\right)_3$ do not show precipitation with $\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Precipitation starts when $Q_{ip}\;>\;K_{sp}$; compare the minimum $\left[\text{OH}^-\right]$ needed. // 📝 Solution: $\text{A}$: $\left[\text{OH}^-\right]\;>\;\sqrt{9\times 10^{-10}}\;=\;3\times 10^{-5}$; $\text{B}$: $\left[\text{OH}^-\right]\;>\;\sqrt[3]{27\times 10^{-18}}\;=\;3\times 10^{-6}\implies\;\text{B}\left(\text{OH}\right)_3$ first

questions.text: Equal volumes of $\text{AB}_2$ and XY (both salt) aqueous solutions are mixed. Which combination will give a precipitate of $\text{AY}_2$ at 300 K? Given $K_{sp}(\text{AY}_2)=5.2\times10^{-7}$ at 300 K.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Precipitation occurs when $Q_{sp} > K_{sp}$; equal-volume mixing halves each concentration. // 📝 Solution: For C, $[\text{A}^{2+}]=10^{-2}$ and $[\text{Y}^-]=10^{-2}$ $\implies$ $Q_{sp} = 10^{-2}(10^{-2})^2 = 10^{-6} > 5.2\times10^{-7}$; the other options give $Q_{sp} < K_{sp}$.

questions.text: Among the group 14 elements with atomic numbers $Z \;=\; 6$, $14$, $50$ and $82$, the element having the lowest melting point is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Melting points of group 14 do not vary regularly down the group; compare actual values. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{C} \;>\; \mathrm{Si} \;>\; \mathrm{Pb} \;>\; \mathrm{Sn}$ in melting point ($\mathrm{Sn} \;=\; 505\;\mathrm{K}$, $\mathrm{Pb} \;=\; 600\;\mathrm{K}$) $\;\implies\;$ lowest is Sn

questions.text: Among the elements $\mathrm{Ga}$, $\mathrm{Ge}$, $\mathrm{In}$ and $\mathrm{Sn}$, the elements having the highest and the lowest first ionisation enthalpy, along with their most stable oxidation states, are respectively
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Compare $\mathrm{IE_1}$ values of group 13 and 14 elements, and recall the inert pair effect. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{IE_1}$ order: $\mathrm{Ge} \;>\; \mathrm{Sn} \;>\; \mathrm{Ga} \;>\; \mathrm{In} \;\implies\;$ $\mathrm{Ge}$ highest, $\mathrm{In}$ lowest $\;\implies\;$ stable states $+4$ for $\mathrm{Ge}$ and $+3$ for $\mathrm{In}$
questions.topic: Periodic Trends in Group 13 and 14, Ionisation Enthalpy

questions.text: The Lassaigne's extract is boiled with dil $\text{HNO}_3$ before testing for halogens because,
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Nitric acid decomposes interfering cyanide and sulphide ions before silver nitrate addition. // 📝 Solution: Boiling with dil. $\text{HNO}_3$ expels $\text{CN}^-$ and $\text{S}^{2-}$ as $\text{HCN}\uparrow$ and $\text{H}_2\text{S}\uparrow$ respectively ($\text{NaCN} + \text{HNO}_3 \rightarrow \text{NaNO}_3 + \text{HCN}\uparrow$; $\text{Na}_2\text{S} + 2\,\text{HNO}_3 \rightarrow 2\,\text{NaNO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{S}\uparrow$), preventing false $\text{AgCN}$ or $\text{Ag}_2\text{S}$ precipitates.

questions.text: In the wet tests for identification of various cations by precipitation, which transition element cation doesn't belong to group IV in qualitative inorganic analysis?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Group III cations precipitate as hydroxides using $\text{NH}_4\text{OH} + \text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ belongs to Group III cations, whereas $\text{Zn}^{2+},\;\text{Co}^{2+}$, and $\text{Ni}^{2+}$ belong to Group IV.

questions.text: On passing a gas, '$\text{X}$', through Nessler's reagent, a brown precipitate is obtained. The gas '$\text{X}$' is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Nessler's reagent tests specifically for ammonia to form iodide of Millon's base. // 📝 Solution: $2\,\text{K}_2\left[\text{HgI}_4\right] + \text{NH}_3 + 3\,\text{KOH} \rightarrow \text{HgO}\cdot\text{Hg}(\text{NH}_2)\text{I}\downarrow\;(\text{iodide of Millon's base, brown ppt}) + 7\,\text{KI} + 2\,\text{H}_2\text{O} \implies \text{X} = \text{NH}_3$.

questions.text: During the detection of acidic radical present in a salt, a student gets a pale yellow precipitate soluble with difficulty in $\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$ solution when sodium carbonate extract was first acidified with dil. $\text{HNO}_3$ and then $\text{AgNO}_3$ solution was added. This indicates presence of :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\text{AgBr}$ is pale yellow and sparingly soluble in ammonium hydroxide. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Ag}^+ + \text{Br}^- \rightarrow \text{AgBr}\downarrow$ (pale yellow precipitate), which is soluble with difficulty (sparingly soluble) in excess aqueous $\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$.

questions.text: A student has been given $0.314\;\text{g}$ of an organic compound and asked to estimate Sulphur. During the experiment, the student has obtained $0.4813\;\text{g}$ of barium sulphate. The percentage of sulphur present in the compound is _______. (Given Molar mass in $\text{g}\,\text{mol}^{-1}: \text{S} : 32,\;\text{BaSO}_4 : 233$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Carius method: $\% \text{S} = \frac{32}{233} \times \frac{w_{\text{BaSO}_4}}{w_{\text{compound}}} \times 100$. // 📝 Solution: $\% \text{S} = \frac{32}{233} \times \frac{0.4813}{0.314} \times 100 = \frac{15.4016}{73.162} \times 100 \approx 21.05\%$.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement-I: The gas liberated on warming a salt with dil $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, turns a piece of paper dipped in lead acetate into black, it is a confirmatory test for sulphide ion.
Statement-II: In statement-I the colour of paper turns black because of formation of lead sulphite.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are false
Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true
Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The black color on lead acetate paper is due to $\text{PbS}$. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Na}_2\text{S} + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4 + \text{H}_2\text{S}\uparrow$, and $(\text{CH}_3\text{COO})_2\text{Pb} + \text{H}_2\text{S} \rightarrow \text{PbS}\downarrow\;(\text{black}) + 2\,\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$. Black colour is due to lead sulphide, not lead sulphite. Thus, Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false.

questions.text:
[FIGURE]
In a borax bead test under hot condition, a metal salt (one from the given) is heated at point B of the flame, resulted in green colour salt bead. The spin-only magnetic moment value of the salt is _______ $\text{BM}$ (Nearest integer)
[Given atomic number of $\text{Cu} = 29,\;\text{Ni} = 28,\;\text{Mn} = 25,\;\text{Fe} = 26$]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Identify the cation producing a green bead at reducing flame point B and compute $\mu = \sqrt{n(n + 2)}$. // 📝 Solution: Point B represents the reducing flame zone. $\text{Fe}^{3+}$ under reducing hot flame gives a green bead $\implies \text{Fe}^{3+} : 3d^5 \implies n = 5\text{ unpaired electrons} \implies \mu = \sqrt{5(5 + 2)} = \sqrt{35} \approx 5.92\;\text{BM} \approx 6\;\text{BM}$.

questions.text: In the Group analysis of cations, $\text{Ba}^{2+}\;\&\;\text{Ca}^{2+}$ are precipitated respectively as
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Group V cations precipitate as carbonates using $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{CO}_3$. // 📝 Solution: Group V cations ($\text{Ba}^{2+},\;\text{Ca}^{2+}$) precipitate as $\text{BaCO}_3$ (white) and $\text{CaCO}_3$ (white) upon adding $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{CO}_3$ in the presence of $\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$ and $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$.

questions.text: The compound that is white in color is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Sulphates of heavy metals like lead and barium are insoluble white precipitates. // 📝 Solution: $\text{PbSO}_4$ is a white solid; $\text{PbI}_2$ is bright yellow; ammonium arsenomolybdate is canary yellow; $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{S}$ is a soluble colourless/yellowish solution.

questions.text:
The number of white coloured salts among the following is
(A) $\text{SrSO}_4$
(B) $\text{Mg}(\text{NH}_4)\text{PO}_4$
(c) $\text{BaCrO}_4$
(D) $\text{Mn}(\text{OH})_2$
(E) $\text{PbSO}_4$
(F) $\text{PbCrO}_4$
(G) $\text{AgBr}$
(H) $\text{PbI}_2$
(I) $\text{CaC}_2\text{O}_4$
(J) $[\text{Fe}(\text{OH})_2(\text{CH}_3\text{COO})]$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Chromates, halides of heavy metals, and basic acetates are typically coloured precipitates. // 📝 Solution: White salts are: $\text{SrSO}_4$, $\text{Mg}(\text{NH}_4)\text{PO}_4$, $\text{Mn}(\text{OH})_2$, $\text{PbSO}_4$, and $\text{CaC}_2\text{O}_4$ (Total = $5$). Coloured salts: $\text{BaCrO}_4$ (yellow), $\text{PbCrO}_4$ (yellow), $\text{AgBr}$ (pale yellow), $\text{PbI}_2$ (yellow), $[\text{Fe}(\text{OH})_2(\text{CH}_3\text{COO})]$ (brown-red).

questions.text:
Match List I with List II
List - I (Precipitating reagent and conditions):
A. $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl} + \text{NH}_4\text{OH}$
B. $\text{NH}_4\text{OH} + \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$
C. $\text{NH}_4\text{OH} + \text{NH}_4\text{Cl} + \text{H}_2\text{S}\text{ gas}$
D. $\text{dilute HCl}$
List - II (Cation):
I. $\text{Mn}^{2+}$
II. $\text{Pb}^{2+}$
III. $\text{Al}^{3+}$
IV. $\text{Sr}^{2+}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Identify cation group numbers: $\text{Pb}^{2+}$ (Grp I), $\text{Al}^{3+}$ (Grp III), $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ (Grp IV), $\text{Sr}^{2+}$ (Grp V). // 📝 Solution: $\text{Al}^{3+}$ precipitates with $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl} + \text{NH}_4\text{OH} \implies \text{A-III}$; $\text{Sr}^{2+}$ with $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{CO}_3/\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3 \implies \text{B-IV}$; $\text{Mn}^{2+}$ with $\text{H}_2\text{S} + \text{NH}_4\text{OH} \implies \text{C-I}$; $\text{Pb}^{2+}$ with $\text{dil. HCl} \implies \text{D-II}$.

questions.text: Formulae for Nessler's reagent is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Nessler's reagent is potassium tetraiodomercurate(II). // 📝 Solution: Nessler's reagent is an alkaline solution of potassium tetraiodomercurate(II), represented by the formula $\text{K}_2\left[\text{HgI}_4\right]$ or $\text{K}_2\text{HgI}_4$.

questions.text: A reagent which gives brilliant red precipitate with Nickel ions in basic medium is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Dimethylglyoxime ($\text{DMG}$) forms an insoluble scarlet red bis-chelate with $\text{Ni}^{2+}$. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Ni}^{2+} + 2\,\text{dmg}^- \xrightarrow{\text{NH}_4\text{OH}} \left[\text{Ni}(\text{dmg})_2\right]\downarrow$ (brilliant/rosy red precipitate stabilized by hydrogen bonding).

questions.text:
Match the List-I with List-II:
List-I (Cations):
$\text{P}\rightarrow\text{Pb}^{2+},\;\text{Cu}^{2+}$
$\text{Q}\rightarrow\text{Al}^{3+},\;\text{Fe}^{3+}$
$\text{R}\rightarrow\text{Co}^{2+},\;\text{Ni}^{2+}$
$\text{S}\rightarrow\text{Ba}^{2+},\;\text{Ca}^{2+}$
List-II (Group reaction):
(i) $\text{H}_2\text{S}\text{ gas in presence of dilute HCl}$
(ii) $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{CO}_3\text{ in presence of }\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$
(iii) $\text{NH}_4\text{OH}\text{ in presence of }\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$
(iv) $\text{H}_2\text{S}\text{ in presence of }\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall qualitative analysis group separation reagents for cations. // 📝 Solution: Group II ($\text{Pb}^{2+},\;\text{Cu}^{2+}$) precipitates with $\text{H}_2\text{S} + \text{dil. HCl} \implies \text{P}\rightarrow\text{i}$; Group III ($\text{Al}^{3+},\;\text{Fe}^{3+}$) with $\text{NH}_4\text{OH} + \text{NH}_4\text{Cl} \implies \text{Q}\rightarrow\text{iii}$; Group IV ($\text{Co}^{2+},\;\text{Ni}^{2+}$) with $\text{H}_2\text{S} + \text{NH}_4\text{OH} \implies \text{R}\rightarrow\text{iv}$; Group V ($\text{Ba}^{2+},\;\text{Ca}^{2+}$) with $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{CO}_3 + \text{NH}_4\text{OH} \implies \text{S}\rightarrow\text{ii}$.

questions.text:
Consider the following test for a group-IV cation.
$\text{M}^{2+} + \text{H}_2\text{S} \rightarrow \text{A}\;(\text{Black precipitate}) + \text{byproduct}$
$\text{A} + \text{aqua regia} \rightarrow \text{B} + \text{NOCl} + \text{S} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$
$\text{B} + \text{KNO}_2 + \text{CH}_3\text{COOH} \rightarrow \text{C} + \text{byproduct}$
The spin-only magnetic moment value of the metal complex $\text{C}$ is ______ $\text{BM}$ (Nearest integer)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For $\text{Co}^{3+}$ with strong field ligand $\text{NO}_2^-$, pairing occurs completely. // 📝 Solution: $\text{M}^{2+} = \text{Co}^{2+}$; $\text{CoS} + \text{aqua regia} \rightarrow \text{CoCl}_2 (\text{B}) \xrightarrow{\text{KNO}_2,\;\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}} \text{K}_3\left[\text{Co}(\text{NO}_2)_6\right] (\text{C}) \implies \text{Co}^{3+} : 3d^6$ with strong-field $\text{NO}_2^- \implies t_{2g}^6 e_g^0 \implies n = 0 \implies \mu = \sqrt{0(0 + 2)} = 0\;\text{BM}$.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : Upon heating a borax bead dipped in cupric sulphate in a luminous flame, the colour of the bead becomes green.
Statement II : The green colour observed is due to the formation of copper(I) metaborate.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Cupric metaborate $\text{Cu}(\text{BO}_2)_2$ is blue-green in non-luminous (oxidizing) flame, but reduced in luminous flame. // 📝 Solution: In an oxidizing flame, $\text{CuSO}_4 + \text{B}_2\text{O}_3 \rightarrow \text{Cu}(\text{BO}_2)_2$ (blue-green). In a luminous (reducing) flame, it reduces to colorless cuprous metaborate $\text{CuBO}_2$ or red metallic $\text{Cu}$. Thus, both Statement I and Statement II are false.

questions.text:
Match List I with List II
List-I (Name of the test):
A. Borax bead test
B. Charcoal cavity test
C. Cobalt nitrate test
D. Flame test
List-II (Reaction sequence involved) [$\text{M}$ is metal]:
I. $\text{MCO}_3 \rightarrow \text{MO} \xrightarrow[\Delta]{\text{Co(NO}_3)_2} \text{CoO}\cdot\text{MO}$
II. $\text{MCO}_3 \rightarrow \text{MCl}_2 \rightarrow \text{M}^{2+}$
III. $\text{MSO}_4 \xrightarrow[\Delta]{\text{Na}_2\text{B}_4\text{O}_7} \text{M}(\text{BO}_2)_2 \rightarrow \text{MBO}_2 \rightarrow \text{M}$
IV. $\text{MSO}_4 \xrightarrow[\Delta]{\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3} \text{MCO}_3 \rightarrow \text{MO} \rightarrow \text{M}$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Link each dry test name to its corresponding characteristic reaction reagents. // 📝 Solution: Borax bead test involves metaborate formation $\implies \text{A-III}$; Charcoal cavity test reduces salt to metal $\implies \text{B-IV}$; Cobalt nitrate forms mixed oxide $\text{CoO}\cdot\text{MO} \implies \text{C-I}$; Flame test involves conversion to volatile metal chloride $\implies \text{D-II}$.

questions.text: Consider three metal chlorides $\text{x},\;\text{y}$ and $\text{z}$, where $\text{x}$ is water soluble at room temperature, $\text{y}$ is sparingly soluble in water at room temperature and $\text{z}$ is soluble in hot water. $\text{x},\;\text{y}$ and $\text{z}$ are respectively
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Lead(II) chloride dissolves selectively in hot water; silver chloride is insoluble at room temperature. // 📝 Solution: $\text{CuCl}_2$ is readily soluble in water at room temperature ($\text{x}$); $\text{AgCl}$ is insoluble/sparingly soluble at room temperature ($\text{y}$); $\text{PbCl}_2$ is sparingly soluble in cold water but completely soluble in boiling/hot water ($\text{z}$).

questions.text: By usual analysis, $1.00\;\text{g}$ of compound $(\text{X})$ gave $1.79\;\text{g}$ of magnesium pyrophosphate. The percentage of phosphorus in compound $(\text{X})$ is : (nearest integer) (Given, molar mass in $\text{g}\,\text{mol}^{-1}: \text{O} = 16,\;\text{Mg} = 24,\;\text{P} = 31$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\% \text{P} = \frac{2 \times M_{\text{P}}}{M_{\text{Mg}_2\text{P}_2\text{O}_7}} \times \frac{w_{\text{precipitate}}}{w_{\text{organic}}} \times 100$. // 📝 Solution: Molar mass of $\text{Mg}_2\text{P}_2\text{O}_7 = 2(24) + 2(31) + 7(16) = 222\;\text{g}\,\text{mol}^{-1} \implies \% \text{P} = \frac{62}{222} \times \frac{1.79}{1.00} \times 100 = \frac{110.98}{222} \times 100 \approx 50\%$.

questions.text: The oxidation number of iron in the compound formed during brown ring test for $\text{NO}_3^-$ ion is _______
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The brown ring complex contains $\text{NO}$ in the form of nitrosonium ion ($\text{NO}^+$). // 📝 Solution: The brown complex is $\left[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_5(\text{NO})\right]\text{SO}_4 \implies \left[\text{Fe}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_5(\text{NO})\right]^{2+}$. With neutral $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{NO}^+$, we have: $x + 5(0) + (+1) = +2 \implies x = +1$.

questions.text:
Number of metal ions characterized by flame test among the following is _______.
$\text{Sr}^{2+},\;\text{Ba}^{2+},\;\text{Ca}^{2+},\;\text{Cu}^{2+},\;\text{Zn}^{2+},\;\text{Co}^{2+},\;\text{Fe}^{2+}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Group 2 cations ($\text{Ca}^{2+},\;\text{Sr}^{2+},\;\text{Ba}^{2+}$) and $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ impart characteristic flame colours. // 📝 Solution: Metal ions characterized by flame test: $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ (brick-red), $\text{Sr}^{2+}$ (crimson red), $\text{Ba}^{2+}$ (apple green), $\text{Cu}^{2+}$ (greenish-blue). Ions $\text{Zn}^{2+},\;\text{Co}^{2+},\;\text{Fe}^{2+}$ do not impart characteristic flame colors $\implies$ Total = $4$.

questions.text: In the precipitation of the iron group (III) in qualitative analysis, ammonium chloride is added before adding ammonium hydroxide to :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Common ion effect suppresses the degree of dissociation of a weak electrolyte. // 📝 Solution: Addition of $\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$ suppresses the dissociation of weak base $\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$ due to common $\text{NH}_4^+$ ions $\implies \left[\text{OH}^-\right]$ decreases sufficiently so that only Group III hydroxides with very low $K_{sp} \approx 10^{-38}$ precipitate.

questions.text: Molar mass of the salt from $\text{NaBr},\;\text{NaNO}_3,\;\text{KI}$ and $\text{CaF}_2$ which does not evolve coloured vapours on heating with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is _______ $\text{g}\,\text{mol}^{-1}$, (Molar mass in $\text{g}\,\text{mol}^{-1}$: $\text{Na} : 23,\;\text{N} : 14,\;\text{K} : 39,\;\text{O} : 16,\;\text{Br} : 80,\;\text{I} : 127,\;\text{F} : 19,\;\text{Ca} : 40$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Fluoride yields colorless $\text{HF}$ gas upon treatment with concentrated sulphuric acid. // 📝 Solution: $\text{NaBr} \rightarrow \text{Br}_2\uparrow$ (reddish brown); $\text{NaNO}_3 \rightarrow \text{NO}_2\uparrow$ (brown); $\text{KI} \rightarrow \text{I}_2\uparrow$ (violet); $\text{CaF}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{CaSO}_4 + 2\,\text{HF}\uparrow$ (colorless). Molar mass of $\text{CaF}_2 = 40 + 2(19) = 78\;\text{g}\,\text{mol}^{-1}$.

questions.text: Observe the following equilibrium in a $1\text{ L}$ flask. $\text{A(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{B(g)}$. At $T(\text{K})$, the equilibrium concentrations of $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ are $0.5\text{ M}$ and $0.375\text{ M}$ respectively. $0.1\text{ moles}$ of $\text{A}$ is added into the flask and heated to $T(\text{K})$ to establish the equilibrium again. The new equilibrium concentrations (in $\text{M}$) of $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ are respectively
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $K_c$ is constant at fixed temperature; find $K_c$ and solve for new equilibrium moles. // 📝 Solution: $K_c = \frac{[\text{B}]}{[\text{A}]} = \frac{0.375}{0.5} = 0.75$. On adding $0.1\text{ mol A}$, $[\text{A}] = 0.6\text{ M}$. Let $x\text{ mol}$ react: $\frac{0.375+x}{0.6-x} = 0.75 \implies 0.375 + x = 0.45 - 0.75x \implies 1.75x = 0.075 \implies x \approx 0.0429\text{ M} \implies [\text{A}] = 0.6 - 0.0429 = 0.557\text{ M},\; [\text{B}] = 0.375 + 0.0429 = 0.418\text{ M}$.

questions.text: Statement I: A catalyst cannot alter the equilibrium constant $K_c$ of a reaction at constant temperature. Statement II: A homogeneous catalyst can change the equilibrium composition of a system at constant temperature. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer.

options.text: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A catalyst lowers $E_a$ for both directions equally, so $K$ is unchanged. // 📝 Solution: $K_c$ is fixed at constant $T$ $\implies$ I is true; the key marks II true, though strictly a catalyst cannot shift equilibrium composition, so II is contestable and the key is B.

questions.text: The ratio $\frac{K_p}{K_c}$ for the reaction : $\text{CO(g)} + \frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{CO}_2\text{(g)}$ is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Apply $K_p = K_c(RT)^{\Delta n_g}$. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta n_g = 1 - \left(1 + \frac{1}{2}\right) = -\frac{1}{2} \implies \frac{K_p}{K_c} = (RT)^{-1/2} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{RT}}$.

questions.text: For reaction: $\text{SO}_2\text{(g)} + \frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{SO}_3\text{(g)}$, $K_p = 2 \times 10^{12}$ at $27^\circ\text{C}$ and $1\text{ atm}$ pressure. The $K_c$ for the same reaction is $\underline{\quad} \times 10^{13}$ (Nearest integer). [Given: $R = 0.082\text{ L atm K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $K_p = K_c(RT)^{\Delta n_g}$. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta n_g = 1 - \left(1 + \frac{1}{2}\right) = -\frac{1}{2} \implies K_c = K_p(RT)^{1/2} = 2 \times 10^{12} \times \sqrt{0.082 \times 300} = 2 \times 10^{12} \times \sqrt{24.6} \approx 9.92 \times 10^{12} = 0.992 \times 10^{13} \approx 1 \times 10^{13}$.

questions.text: For the reaction $\text{H}_2\left(g\right)+\text{I}_2\left(g\right)\rightleftharpoons 2\text{HI}\left(g\right)$, attainment of equilibrium is predicted correctly by:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Reactants fall and the product rises until all concentrations become constant. // 📝 Solution: $\left[\text{H}_2\right]$ and $\left[\text{I}_2\right]$ decrease while $\left[\text{HI}\right]$ increases, then all three plateau $\implies$ graph (2) is correct

questions.text: For the given hypothetical reactions, the equilibrium constants are as follows : $\text{X} \rightleftharpoons \text{Y};\; K_1 = 1.0$, $\text{Y} \rightleftharpoons \text{Z};\; K_2 = 2.0$, $\text{Z} \rightleftharpoons \text{W};\; K_3 = 4.0$. The equilibrium constant for the reaction $\text{X} \rightleftharpoons \text{W}$ is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: When chemical reactions are added, their equilibrium constants are multiplied. // 📝 Solution: Adding the three equations: $\text{X} \rightleftharpoons \text{Y}$, $\text{Y} \rightleftharpoons \text{Z}$, $\text{Z} \rightleftharpoons \text{W}$ gives $\text{X} \rightleftharpoons \text{W} \implies K = K_1 \cdot K_2 \cdot K_3 = 1.0 \times 2.0 \times 4.0 = 8.0$.

questions.text: At $25^\circ\text{C}$, the enthalpy of the following processes are given: $\text{H}_2\text{(g)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow 2\text{OH(g)},\; \Delta H^\circ = 78\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$; $\text{H}_2\text{(g)} + \frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{O(g)},\; \Delta H^\circ = -242\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$; $\text{H}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow 2\text{H(g)},\; \Delta H^\circ = 436\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$; $\frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{O(g)},\; \Delta H^\circ = 249\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$. What would be the value of $X$ for the following reaction? (Nearest integer) $\text{H}_2\text{O(g)} \rightarrow \text{H(g)} + \text{OH(g)},\; \Delta H^\circ = X\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Apply Hess's Law by combining the given equations to yield $\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{H} + \text{OH}$. // 📝 Solution: Target: $\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{H} + \text{OH}$. Reversing Eq (2): $\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{H}_2 + \frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2$ ($\Delta H_1 = +242\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$). Taking $\frac{1}{2}\text{Eq}(1)$: $\frac{1}{2}\text{H}_2 + \frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{OH}$ ($\Delta H_2 = 39\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$). Taking $\frac{1}{2}\text{Eq}(3)$: $\frac{1}{2}\text{H}_2 \rightarrow \text{H}$ ($\Delta H_3 = 218\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$). Summing gives $\Delta H^\circ = 242 + 39 + 218 = 499\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.

questions.text: The equilibrium $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{CrO}_4^{2-}$ is shifted to the right in :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Dichromate reacts with hydroxide ions to form chromate ions. // 📝 Solution: In basic medium: $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-} + 2\text{OH}^- \rightleftharpoons 2\text{CrO}_4^{2-} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$. Adding $\text{OH}^-$ drives the reaction toward the right, forming yellow $\text{CrO}_4^{2-}$.

questions.text: Consider the following reaction approaching equilibrium at $27^\circ\text{C}$ and $1\text{ atm}$ pressure: $\text{A} + \text{B} \underset{K_b = 10^2}{\overset{K_f = 10^3}{\rightleftharpoons}} \text{C} + \text{D}$. The standard Gibb's energy change $\left( \Delta_r G^\circ \right)$ at $27^\circ\text{C}$ is $(-) \underline{\quad}\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ (Nearest integer). [Given: $R = 8.3\text{ J K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$ and $\ln 10 = 2.3$]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $K_{\text{eq}} = \frac{K_f}{K_b}$ and $\Delta_r G^\circ = -RT \ln K_{\text{eq}}$. // 📝 Solution: $K_{\text{eq}} = \frac{10^3}{10^2} = 10 \implies \Delta_r G^\circ = -RT \ln 10 = -(8.3 \times 300 \times 2.3) = -5727\text{ J mol}^{-1} \approx -6\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$.
questions.topic: Gibbs Free Energy and Equilibrium Constant

questions.text: For the given reaction, choose the correct expression of $K_c$ from the following :- $\text{Fe}^{3+}(\text{aq}) + \text{SCN}^-(\text{aq}) \rightleftharpoons [\text{FeSCN}]^{2+}(\text{aq})$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $K_c$ is defined as the concentration of products divided by reactants, raised to stoichiometric powers. // 📝 Solution: For $\text{Fe}^{3+}(\text{aq}) + \text{SCN}^-(\text{aq}) \rightleftharpoons [\text{FeSCN}]^{2+}(\text{aq})$, the expression for equilibrium constant is $K_c = \frac{\left[ \text{FeSCN}^{2+} \right]}{\left[ \text{Fe}^{3+} \right]\left[ \text{SCN}^- \right]}$.

questions.text: $\text{X}_2\text{(g)} + \text{Y}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{Z(g)}$. $\text{X}_2\text{(g)}$ and $\text{Y}_2\text{(g)}$ are added to a $1\text{ L}$ flask and it is found that the system attains the above equilibrium at $T(\text{K})$ with the number of moles of $\text{X}_2\text{(g)}$, $\text{Y}_2\text{(g)}$ and $\text{Z(g)}$ being $3$, $3$ and $9\text{ mol}$ respectively (equilibrium moles). Under this condition of equilibrium, $10\text{ mol}$ of $\text{Z(g)}$ is added to the flask and the temperature is maintained at $T(\text{K})$. Then the number of moles of $\text{Z(g)}$ in the flask when the new equilibrium is established is ____. (Nearest integer)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Compute $K_c$ from initial state and equate to new equilibrium expression. // 📝 Solution: $K_c = \frac{[\text{Z}]^2}{[\text{X}_2][\text{Y}_2]} = \frac{9^2}{3 \times 3} = 9$. When $10\text{ mol Z}$ is added, moles of $\text{Z} = 19$. Let $x\text{ mol Z}$ dissociate $\implies [\text{Z}] = 19 - x,\; [\text{X}_2] = [\text{Y}_2] = 3 + \frac{x}{2} \implies \frac{(19-x)^2}{\left(3+\frac{x}{2}\right)^2} = 9 \implies \frac{19-x}{3+\frac{x}{2}} = 3 \implies 19 - x = 9 + \frac{3x}{2} \implies 10 = \frac{5x}{2} \implies x = 4$. New moles of $\text{Z} = 19 - 4 = 15$.

questions.text: For the following gas phase equilibrium reaction at constant temperature, $\text{NH}_3\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons \frac{1}{2}\text{N}_2\text{(g)} + \frac{3}{2}\text{H}_2\text{(g)}$, if the total pressure is $\sqrt{3}\text{ atm}$ and the pressure equilibrium constant $(K_p)$ is $9\text{ atm}$, then the degree of dissociation is given as $\left( x \times 10^{-2} \right)^{-1/2}$. The value of $x$ is ____. (nearest integer)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Express $K_p$ in terms of $\alpha$ and $P_T$. // 📝 Solution: Equilibrium moles: $n_{\text{NH}_3} = 1-\alpha,\; n_{\text{N}_2} = \frac{\alpha}{2},\; n_{\text{H}_2} = \frac{3\alpha}{2} \implies n_T = 1+\alpha$. $K_p = \frac{(\alpha/2)^{1/2}(3\alpha/2)^{3/2}}{1-\alpha}\frac{P_T}{1+\alpha} = \frac{3\sqrt{3}\alpha^2}{4(1-\alpha^2)} P_T$. Substitute $P_T = \sqrt{3}\text{ atm}$ and $K_p = 9\text{ atm} \implies 9 = \frac{9\alpha^2}{4(1-\alpha^2)} \implies 4 - 4\alpha^2 = \alpha^2 \implies 5\alpha^2 = 4 \implies \alpha = (0.8)^{1/2} = \left(\frac{1}{0.8}\right)^{-1/2} = (1.25)^{-1/2} = \left(125 \times 10^{-2}\right)^{-1/2} \implies x = 125$.

questions.text: The equilibrium constant for the reaction $\text{SO}_3\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{SO}_2\text{(g)} + \frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2\text{(g)}$ is $K_c = 4.9 \times 10^{-2}$. The value of $K_c$ for the reaction given below is $2\text{SO}_2\text{(g)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3\text{(g)}$ is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Inverting a reaction reciprocates its equilibrium constant, and multiplying coefficients by $n$ raises it to power $n$. // 📝 Solution: The target reaction is obtained by reversing the given reaction and multiplying by $2 \implies K_c' = \left(\frac{1}{K_c}\right)^2 = \left(\frac{1}{4.9 \times 10^{-2}}\right)^2 = \left(\frac{100}{4.9}\right)^2 \approx (20.41)^2 \approx 416.49 \approx 416$.

questions.text: For the reaction $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NO}_2\text{(g)}$, $K_p = 0.492\text{ atm}$ at $300\text{ K}$. $K_c$ for the reaction at same temperature is _______ $\times 10^{-2}$. (Given : $R = 0.082\text{ L atm mol}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $K_p = K_c(RT)^{\Delta n_g}$. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta n_g = 2 - 1 = 1 \implies K_c = \frac{K_p}{RT} = \frac{0.492}{0.082 \times 300} = \frac{0.492}{24.6} = 0.02 = 2 \times 10^{-2} \implies \text{Answer} = 2$.

questions.text: For $\text{CO(g)} + 2\text{H}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{CH}_3\text{OH(g)}$, 0.1 mol CO with a catalyst is placed in a $2\,\text{dm}^3$ flask at 500 K. H$_2$ is introduced until the total pressure is 5 bar and 0.04 mol CH$_3$OH is formed. $K_p^\circ = $ ____ $\times10^{-3}$ (nearest integer). Given $R = 0.08\,\text{dm}^3\,\text{bar K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Build the equilibrium table, then use mole fractions with $K_p = \dfrac{X_{\text{CH}_3\text{OH}}}{X_{\text{CO}}X_{\text{H}_2}^2\,P^2}$. // 📝 Solution: Equilibrium moles: CO $=0.06$, H$_2=0.15$, CH$_3$OH $=0.04$, total $=0.25$ $\implies$ $X = 0.24,\;0.60,\;0.16$ $\implies$ $K_p = \dfrac{0.16}{0.24\times0.36\times25}\approx0.074 = 74\times10^{-3}$.

questions.text: Dissociation of a gas $\text{A}_2$ takes place according to the following chemical reaction. At equilibrium, the total pressure is $1\text{ bar}$ at $300\text{ K}$. $\text{A}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{A(g)}$. Given standard Gibbs energies of formation: $\Delta G^\circ_f(\text{A}_2) = -100.00\text{ kJ mol}^{-1},\; \Delta G^\circ_f(\text{A}) = -50.832\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$. The degree of dissociation of $\text{A}_2\text{(g)}$ is given by $\left( x \times 10^{-2} \right)^{1/2}$ where $x = \underline{\quad}$. (Nearest integer). [Given: $R = 8\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1},\; \log 2 = 0.3010,\; \log 3 = 0.48$]. Assume degree of dissociation is not negligible.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find $\Delta_r G^\circ$ to get $K_p$, then use $K_p = \frac{4\alpha^2}{1-\alpha^2} P$. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta_r G^\circ = 2(-50.832) - (-100.00) = -1.664\text{ kJ mol}^{-1} = -1664\text{ J mol}^{-1} \implies -1664 = -8 \times 300 \ln K_p \implies \ln K_p = 0.6933 \implies K_p = 2$. For $\text{A}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{A}$ at $P = 1\text{ bar}$: $K_p = \frac{4\alpha^2}{1-\alpha^2} = 2 \implies 4\alpha^2 = 2 - 2\alpha^2 \implies \alpha^2 = \frac{1}{3} \approx 0.333 \implies \alpha = \left(33.3 \times 10^{-2}\right)^{1/2} \implies x \approx 33$.

questions.text: For $\text{A(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{B(g)} + \text{C(g)}$ at constant temperature, with total pressure $p$, pressure equilibrium constant $K_p$ and degree of dissociation $\alpha$, which statement is true at equilibrium?

options.text: If $p$ is extremely high compared to $K_p$, then $\alpha\approx1$
If $K_p$ is extremely high compared to $p$, $\alpha$ becomes much less than unity

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Express $K_p$ in terms of $\alpha$ and $p$. // 📝 Solution: $K_p = \dfrac{\alpha^2 p}{1-\alpha^2}$ $\implies$ $\alpha^2 = \dfrac{K_p}{K_p+p}$ $\implies$ $\alpha$ decreases as $p$ increases $\implies$ B.

questions.text: At $-20^\circ\text{C}$ and $1\text{ atm}$ pressure, a cylinder is filled with equal number of $\text{H}_2$, $\text{I}_2$ and $\text{HI}$ molecules for the reaction $\text{H}_2\text{(g)} + \text{I}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{HI(g)}$, the $K_p$ for the process is $x \times 10^{-1}$. $x = \underline{\quad}$. [Given : $R = 0.082\text{ L atm K}^{-1}\text{ mol}^{-1}$]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Since $\Delta n_g = 0$, $K_p$ depends only on the mole ratio. // 📝 Solution: Equal number of molecules means $n_{\text{H}_2} = n_{\text{I}_2} = n_{\text{HI}} = n \implies K_p = \frac{n_{\text{HI}}^2}{n_{\text{H}_2} n_{\text{I}_2}} = \frac{n^2}{n \times n} = 1$. Given $K_p = x \times 10^{-1} \implies 1 = x \times 10^{-1} \implies x = 10$.

questions.text: The effect of addition of helium gas to the following reaction in equilibrium state, is: $\text{PCl}_5\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{PCl}_3\text{(g)} + \text{Cl}_2\text{(g)}$

options.text: the equilibrium will shift in the forward direction and more of $\text{Cl}_2$ and $\text{PCl}_3$ gases will be produced.
the equilibrium will go backward due to suppression of dissociation of $\text{PCl}_5$.
helium will deactivate $\text{PCl}_5$ and reaction will stop.
addition of helium will not affect the equilibrium.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: At constant pressure, inert gas addition increases volume and shifts equilibrium toward greater number of gaseous moles. // 📝 Solution: Under constant pressure conditions, addition of an inert gas increases total volume $\implies$ partial pressures of reactants and products decrease $\implies$ equilibrium shifts toward the side with more moles of gas ($\Delta n_g > 0$), which is the forward direction.

questions.text: A vessel at $1000\;\text{K}$ contains $\text{CO}_2$ with a pressure of $0.5\;\text{atm}$. Some of the $\text{CO}_2$ is converted into $\text{CO}$ on addition of graphite. If the total pressure at equilibrium is $0.8\;\text{atm}$, then $K_p$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For $\text{CO}_2+\text{C}\rightleftharpoons 2\text{CO}$, the total pressure is $0.5+x$. // 📝 Solution: $0.5\;+\;x\;=\;0.8\implies\;x\;=\;0.3\implies\;K_p\;=\;\frac{\left(0.6\right)^2}{0.2}\;=\;1.8\;\text{atm}$

questions.text: $\text{A(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{B(g)} + \frac{\text{C}}{2}\text{(g)}$. The correct relationship between $K_p$, $\alpha$ and equilibrium pressure $P$ is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Determine equilibrium moles and partial pressures: $p_i = \frac{n_i}{n_{\text{total}}} P$. // 📝 Solution: At eq: $n_A = 1 - \alpha,\; n_B = \alpha,\; n_C = \frac{\alpha}{2} \implies n_T = 1 + \frac{\alpha}{2} = \frac{2+\alpha}{2}$. Partial pressures: $p_A = \frac{1-\alpha}{n_T}P,\; p_B = \frac{\alpha}{n_T}P,\; p_C = \frac{\alpha/2}{n_T}P \implies K_p = \frac{p_B \cdot p_C^{1/2}}{p_A} = \frac{\left(\frac{\alpha P}{n_T}\right)\left(\frac{\alpha P}{2 n_T}\right)^{1/2}}{\frac{(1-\alpha)P}{n_T}} = \frac{\alpha^{3/2} P^{1/2}}{(2+\alpha)^{1/2}(1-\alpha)}$.

questions.text: Consider the equilibria: (i) $\text{X(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{Y(g)} + \text{Z(g)},\; K_{p_1} = 3$; (ii) $\text{A(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{B(g)},\; K_{p_2} = 1$. If the degree of dissociation and initial concentration of both the reactants $\text{X(g)}$ and $\text{A(g)}$ are equal, then the ratio of the total pressure at equilibrium $\left( \frac{p_1}{p_2} \right)$ is equal to $x : 1$. The value of $x$ is ____ (Nearest integer).
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Express $K_p$ for both dissociation reactions in terms of $\alpha$ and total pressure. // 📝 Solution: For (i): $K_{p_1} = \frac{\alpha^2}{1-\alpha^2} p_1 = 3$. For (ii): $K_{p_2} = \frac{4\alpha^2}{1-\alpha^2} p_2 = 1$. Dividing the two expressions: $\frac{K_{p_1}}{K_{p_2}} = \frac{p_1}{4p_2} = \frac{3}{1} \implies \frac{p_1}{p_2} = 12 \implies x = 12$.

questions.text: Consider the following equation: $2\text{SO}_2\text{(g)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{SO}_3\text{(g)},\; \Delta H = -190\text{ kJ}$. The number of factors which will increase the yield of $\text{SO}_3$ at equilibrium from the following is ____. A. Increasing temperature, B. Increasing pressure, C. Adding more $\text{SO}_2$, D. Adding more $\text{O}_2$, E. Addition of catalyst.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Apply Le Chatelier's principle for exothermic reaction with $\Delta n_g < 0$. // 📝 Solution: For an exothermic reaction ($\Delta H < 0$) with $\Delta n_g = -1$: B (increasing pressure shifts to fewer moles), C (adding reactant $\text{SO}_2$), and D (adding reactant $\text{O}_2$) shift the equilibrium forward. Factor A shifts it backward and factor E only changes rate. Hence, exactly $3$ factors increase the yield.

questions.text: The following concentrations were observed at $500\text{ K}$ for the formation of $\text{NH}_3$ from $\text{N}_2$ and $\text{H}_2$. At equilibrium : $[\text{N}_2] = 2 \times 10^{-2}\text{ M}$, $[\text{H}_2] = 3 \times 10^{-2}\text{ M}$ and $[\text{NH}_3] = 1.5 \times 10^{-2}\text{ M}$. Equilibrium constant for the reaction is _______
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $K_c = \frac{[\text{NH}_3]^2}{[\text{N}_2][\text{H}_2]^3}$ for $\text{N}_2 + 3\text{H}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3$. // 📝 Solution: $K_c = \frac{\left(1.5 \times 10^{-2}\right)^2}{\left(2 \times 10^{-2}\right)\left(3 \times 10^{-2}\right)^3} = \frac{2.25 \times 10^{-4}}{2 \times 10^{-2} \times 27 \times 10^{-6}} = \frac{2.25 \times 10^{-4}}{5.4 \times 10^{-7}} \approx 416.67 \approx 417$.

questions.text: For $\text{PCl}_5\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{PCl}_3\text{(g)} + \text{Cl}_2\text{(g)}$ at equilibrium, xenon gas is added at constant $T$ and $p$. Upon addition, the concentration of:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: At constant $T$ and $p$, an inert gas raises the volume and favours the side with more moles. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta n = +1$ $\implies$ forward shift $\implies$ $[\text{PCl}_5]\downarrow$, $[\text{PCl}_3]\uparrow$, $[\text{Cl}_2]\uparrow$; the printed key B conflicts with the $\text{Cl}_2$ rise, while D matches the direction.
questions.topic: Le Chatelier's principle and inert gas

questions.text: $37.8\;\text{g}$ of $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ was taken in a $1\;\text{L}$ reaction vessel and allowed to undergo the reaction $2\text{N}_2\text{O}_5\left(g\right)\rightleftharpoons 2\text{N}_2\text{O}_4\left(g\right)+\text{O}_2\left(g\right)$ at $500\;\text{K}$. The total pressure at equilibrium was found to be $18.65\;\text{bar}$. Then $K_p\;=\;$ ______ $\times 10^{-2}$ (nearest integer). Assume $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ behaves ideally. Given $R\;=\;0.082\;\text{bar L mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find the initial pressure from $PV\;=\;nRT$, then use a pressure table with total pressure $P_0+P$. // 📝 Solution: $P_0\;=\;\frac{37.8}{108}\times 0.082\times 500\;=\;14.35\implies\;14.35+P\;=\;18.65\implies\;P\;=\;4.3\implies\;K_p\;=\;\frac{\left(8.6\right)^2\left(4.3\right)}{\left(5.75\right)^2}\;\approx\;962\times 10^{-2}$

questions.text: At temperature $T$, compound $\text{AB}_2\left(g\right)$ dissociates as $\text{AB}_2\left(g\right)\rightleftharpoons\text{AB}\left(g\right)+\frac{1}{2}\text{B}_2\left(g\right)$ having degree of dissociation $x$ (small compared to unity). The correct expression for $x$ in terms of $K_p$ and $p$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Express partial pressures via mole fractions and neglect $x$ against unity. // 📝 Solution: $K_p\;=\;\frac{p^{1/2}x^{3/2}}{2^{1/2}}\implies\;x\;=\;\sqrt[3]{\frac{2K_p^2}{p}}$

questions.text: Consider the equilibrium $\text{CO}\left(g\right)+3\text{H}_2\left(g\right)\rightleftharpoons\text{CH}_4\left(g\right)+\text{H}_2\text{O}\left(g\right)$. If the pressure applied over the system increases by two fold at constant temperature then: (A) Concentration of reactants and products increases. (B) Equilibrium will shift in forward direction. (C) Equilibrium constant increases since concentration of products increases. (D) Equilibrium constant remains unchanged as concentration of reactants and products remain same. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Le Chatelier's principle with $\Delta n_g\;=\;-2$. // 📝 Solution: Pressure $\uparrow\implies$ shift to fewer moles (forward); all concentrations rise but products rise more; statements C and D are not correct as stated $\implies$ (A) and (B) only

questions.text: Consider the reaction $\text{X}_2\text{Y}\left(g\right)\rightleftharpoons\text{X}_2\left(g\right)+\frac{1}{2}\text{Y}_2\left(g\right)$. The equation representing the correct relationship between the degree of dissociation $x$ of $\text{X}_2\text{Y}\left(g\right)$ and its equilibrium constant $K_p$ is ______. Assume $x$ to be very very small.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Write $K_p$ in terms of mole fractions with $1-x\approx 1$ and $1+\frac{x}{2}\approx 1$. // 📝 Solution: $K_p\;=\;\frac{x^{3/2}p^{1/2}}{2^{1/2}}\implies\;x^3\;=\;\frac{2K_p^2}{p}$

questions.text: For the reaction, $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4 \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NO}_2$, graph is plotted as shown below [FIGURE]. Identify correct statements. A. Standard free energy change for the reaction is $-5.40\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$. B. As $\Delta G^\ominus$ in graph is positive, $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$ will not dissociate into $\text{NO}_2$ at all. C. Reverse reaction will go to completion. D. When $1\text{ mole}$ of $\text{N}_2\text{O}_4$ changes into equilibrium mixture, value of $\Delta G^\ominus = -0.84\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$. E. When $2\text{ mole}$ of $\text{NO}_2$ changes into equilibrium mixture, $\Delta G^\ominus$ for equilibrium mixture is $-6.24\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For $G$ vs extent of reaction, $\Delta G = G_{\text{eq}} - G_{\text{initial}}$. // 📝 Solution: From graph: $G(\text{N}_2\text{O}_4) = 0,\; G_{\text{eq}} = -0.84\text{ kJ mol}^{-1},\; G(2\text{NO}_2) = 5.40\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$. For Statement D: $\Delta G = G_{\text{eq}} - G(\text{N}_2\text{O}_4) = -0.84 - 0 = -0.84\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ (True). For Statement E: $\Delta G = G_{\text{eq}} - G(2\text{NO}_2) = -0.84 - 5.40 = -6.24\text{ kJ mol}^{-1}$ (True). Hence, D and E are correct.
questions.topic: Free Energy and Extent of Reaction

questions.text: At $298\text{ K}$, $\text{N}_2\text{(g)} + 3\text{H}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NH}_3\text{(g)},\; K_1 = 4 \times 10^5$; $\text{N}_2\text{(g)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NO(g)},\; K_2 = 1.6 \times 10^{12}$; $\text{H}_2\text{(g)} + \frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{H}_2\text{O(g)},\; K_3 = 1.0 \times 10^{-13}$. Based on above equilibria, the equilibrium constant of the reaction, $2\text{NH}_3\text{(g)} + \frac{5}{2}\text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NO(g)} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O(g)}$ is $\underline{\quad} \times 10^{-33}$ (Nearest integer).
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use the relation $\text{Target Equation} = -\text{Eq}(1) + \text{Eq}(2) + 3 \times \text{Eq}(3)$. // 📝 Solution: $K_{\text{eq}} = \frac{K_2 \times K_3^3}{K_1} = \frac{1.6 \times 10^{12} \times \left(1.0 \times 10^{-13}\right)^3}{4 \times 10^5} = \frac{1.6 \times 10^{-27}}{4 \times 10^5} = 4 \times 10^{-33} \implies \text{Answer} = 4$.

questions.text: For independent processes at $300\text{ K}$: Process A ($\Delta H = -25\text{ kJ mol}^{-1},\; \Delta S = -80\text{ J K}^{-1}$), Process B ($\Delta H = -22\text{ kJ mol}^{-1},\; \Delta S = 40\text{ J K}^{-1}$), Process C ($\Delta H = 25\text{ kJ mol}^{-1},\; \Delta S = -50\text{ J K}^{-1}$), Process D ($\Delta H = 22\text{ kJ mol}^{-1},\; \Delta S = 20\text{ J K}^{-1}$). The number of non-spontaneous processes from the following is ____.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A process is non-spontaneous when $\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S > 0$. // 📝 Solution: At $T = 300\text{ K}$: $\Delta G_A = -25 \times 10^3 - 300(-80) = -1000\text{ J} < 0$ (spontaneous); $\Delta G_B = -22 \times 10^3 - 300(40) = -34000\text{ J} < 0$ (spontaneous); $\Delta G_C = 25 \times 10^3 - 300(-50) = +40000\text{ J} > 0$ (non-spontaneous); $\Delta G_D = 22 \times 10^3 - 300(20) = +16000\text{ J} > 0$ (non-spontaneous). Hence, $2$ processes (C and D) are non-spontaneous.

questions.text: Consider the general reaction given below at $400\text{ K}$: $x\text{A(g)} \rightleftharpoons y\text{B(g)}$. The values of $K_p$ and $K_c$ are studied under the same condition of temperature but variation in $x$ and $y$. (i) $K_p = 85.87$ and $K_c = 2.586$ appropriate units; (ii) $K_p = 0.862$ and $K_c = 28.62$ appropriate units. The values of $x$ and $y$ in (i) and (ii) respectively are:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\frac{K_p}{K_c} = (RT)^{\Delta n_g}$ where $\Delta n_g = y - x$ and $RT = 0.0821 \times 400 = 32.84$. // 📝 Solution: For (i): $\frac{K_p}{K_c} = \frac{85.87}{2.586} \approx 33.2 \approx (32.84)^1 \implies y - x = 1 \implies x = 1,\; y = 2$. For (ii): $\frac{K_p}{K_c} = \frac{0.862}{28.62} \approx 0.0301 \approx (32.84)^{-1} \implies y - x = -1 \implies x = 2,\; y = 1$.

questions.text: Water decomposes at $2300\text{ K}$: $\text{H}_2\text{O(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{H}_2\text{(g)} + \frac{1}{2}\text{O}_2\text{(g)}$. The percent of water decomposing at $2300\text{ K}$ and $1\text{ bar}$ is _____ (Nearest integer). Equilibrium constant for the reaction is $2 \times 10^{-3}$ at $2300\text{ K}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Express $K_p$ in terms of degree of dissociation $\alpha$ and total pressure $P$. // 📝 Solution: Let $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ dissociate with degree $\alpha \ll 1$. Total moles $= 1 + \frac{\alpha}{2} \approx 1$. Partial pressures: $p_{\text{H}_2\text{O}} \approx P$, $p_{\text{H}_2} = \alpha P$, $p_{\text{O}_2} = \frac{\alpha}{2} P \implies K_p = \frac{(\alpha P)\left( \frac{\alpha P}{2} \right)^{1/2}}{P} = \frac{\alpha^{3/2} P^{1/2}}{\sqrt{2}}$. For $P = 1\text{ bar}$ and $K_p = 2 \times 10^{-3} \implies \alpha^{3/2} = 2\sqrt{2} \times 10^{-3} = 2^{3/2} \times 10^{-3} \implies \alpha = 2 \times 10^{-2} \implies \%\alpha = 2\%$.

questions.text: The following reaction occurs in the Blast furnace where iron ore is reduced to iron metal: $\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3\text{(s)} + 3\text{CO(g)} \rightleftharpoons \text{Fe(l)} + 3\text{CO}_2\text{(g)}$. Using the Le-chatelier's principle, predict which one of the following will not disturb the equilibrium.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Pure solids and liquids have constant active mass (activity $= 1$) and do not perturb the equilibrium position. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3\text{(s)}$ is a pure solid; its concentration is constant, so adding or removing it does not alter the reaction quotient $Q$, leaving the equilibrium undisturbed.

questions.text: Consider the following gaseous equilibrium in a closed container of volume '$V$' at $T(\text{K})$. $\text{P}_2\text{(g)} + \text{Q}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{PQ(g)}$. $2\text{ moles}$ each of $\text{P}_2\text{(g)}$, $\text{Q}_2\text{(g)}$ and $\text{PQ(g)}$ are present at equilibrium. Now one mole each of '$\text{P}_2$' and '$\text{Q}_2$' are added to the equilibrium keeping the temperature at $T(\text{K})$. The number of moles of $\text{P}_2$, $\text{Q}_2$ and $\text{PQ}$ at the new equilibrium, respectively, are
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Determine $K_c$, then express new equilibrium concentrations after adding reactants. // 📝 Solution: $K_c = \frac{[\text{PQ}]^2}{[\text{P}_2][\text{Q}_2]} = \frac{2^2}{2 \times 2} = 1$. When $1\text{ mol}$ of $\text{P}_2$ and $\text{Q}_2$ are added, initial moles are $3, 3, 2$. At new eq: $(3-x), (3-x), (2+2x) \implies \frac{(2+2x)^2}{(3-x)^2} = 1 \implies 2+2x = 3-x \implies 3x = 1 \implies x = \frac{1}{3} \approx 0.33 \implies \text{moles} = 2.67,\; 2.67,\; 2.67$.

questions.text: The correct arrangement for decreasing order of electrophilic substitution for the above compounds (I) to (IV) is: [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Activating $+M/+I$ groups increase $S_E$ rate; $-I$ groups decrease it. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{OMe}\,(+M) > \mathrm{CH_3}\,(+I) > \mathrm{H} > \mathrm{CF_3}\,(-I)$ $\implies$ (III) > (I) > (II) > (IV).
questions.topic: Activating and deactivating groups in SESE​

questions.text: 2-chlorobutane $+\,\mathrm{Cl_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{C_4H_8Cl_2}$ (isomers). The total number of optically active isomers shown by $\mathrm{C_4H_8Cl_2}$ obtained in the above reaction is ______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Optically active isomers are chiral stereoisomers; meso forms are excluded. // 📝 Solution: 1,2- ($\mathrm{C_2}$ chiral) $\implies$ 2; 1,3- ($\mathrm{C_3}$ chiral) $\implies$ 2; 2,3- (meso + $\pm$ pair) $\implies$ 2 $\implies$ total $= 6$.

questions.text: Which of the following reaction is NOT correctly represented? [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Ring halogenation needs a Lewis acid in the dark, while side-chain halogenation needs light. // 📝 Solution: (1) Fe/dark gives ring bromination, (2) Sandmeyer gives bromobenzene, (3) hν gives benzylic bromide, all conventional. (4) is the representation flagged as incorrect in the key, since $\mathrm{Br_2}$/hν on a ring alkene favours addition over the drawn allylic substitution $\implies$ D

questions.text: The correct statement regarding nucleophilic substitution reaction in a chiral alkyl halide is:

options.text: Retention occurs in $S_N1$ reaction and inversion occurs in $S_N2$ reaction
Racemisation occurs in $S_N1$ reaction and retention occurs in $S_N2$ reaction
Racemisation occurs in both $S_N1$ and $S_N2$ reactions
Racemisation occurs in $S_N1$ reaction and inversion occurs in $S_N2$ reaction

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $S_N1$ goes through a planar carbocation; $S_N2$ goes through backside attack. // 📝 Solution: $S_N1 \implies$ racemisation; $S_N2 \implies$ inversion $\implies$ option (4).

questions.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Haloalkanes react with $\mathrm{KCN}$ to form alkyl cyanides as the main product while with $\mathrm{AgCN}$ they form isocyanide as the main product. Reason (R): $\mathrm{KCN}$ and $\mathrm{AgCN}$ are both highly ionic compounds. Choose the most appropriate answer.

options.text: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mathrm{AgCN}$ is largely covalent, so the nitrogen end attacks. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{KCN}$ (ionic) $\implies$ C-attack $\implies$ $\mathrm{R{-}CN}$; $\mathrm{AgCN}$ (covalent) $\implies$ N-attack $\implies$ $\mathrm{R{-}NC}$; R is false.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other as Reason R. Assertion A: Aryl halides cannot be prepared by replacement of the hydroxyl group of phenol by a halogen atom. Reason R: Phenols react with halogen acids violently. Choose the most appropriate answer.

options.text: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The $C{-}O$ bond in phenol has partial double-bond character; phenols do not react with HX. // 📝 Solution: A is true (C–OH replacement not feasible) $\implies$ R is false (phenol gives no reaction with HX).

questions.text: Given below are two statements. Statement I: High concentration of a strong nucleophilic reagent with secondary alkyl halides lacking bulky substituents follows the $S_N2$ mechanism. Statement II: A secondary alkyl halide treated with a large excess of ethanol follows the $S_N1$ mechanism. Choose the most appropriate answer.

options.text: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Strong nucleophile with low steric hindrance gives $S_N2$; solvolysis in a protic solvent gives $S_N1$. // 📝 Solution: Statement I $\implies$ $S_N2$ true; Statement II (solvolysis) $\implies$ $S_N1$ true.

questions.text: Number of moles of $\mathrm{AgCl}$ formed in the following reaction is ______. [FIGURE] $\xrightarrow{\mathrm{AgNO_3}}$ (A) + X $\mathrm{AgCl}\downarrow$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Only ionisable alkyl $\mathrm{Cl}$ gives $\mathrm{Cl^-}$ with $\mathrm{Ag^+}$; vinylic $\mathrm{Cl}$ is inert. // 📝 Solution: Vinylic $\mathrm{Cl}$ does not ionise $\implies$ two alkyl $\mathrm{Cl}$ ionise $\implies$ $X = 2$ $\implies$ 2 mol $\mathrm{AgCl}$.

questions.text: The correct order of reactivity of the benzyl halides (a), (b), (c), (d) towards reaction with KCN is: [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Electron-donating groups stabilise the benzylic transition state, while nitro groups withdraw electron density. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{p\text{-}NH_2} > \mathrm{p\text{-}OH} \;\implies\; \mathrm{m\text{-}NO_2} > \mathrm{p\text{-}NO_2}$ (resonance withdrawal is strongest at para) $\;\implies\; b > a > d > c$
questions.topic: Substituent effects on substitution rate of benzyl halides

questions.text: Which among the following compounds will undergo fastest $S_N2$ reaction? [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $S_N2$ rate falls with steric hindrance: $\mathrm{Me} > 1^\circ > 2^\circ > 3^\circ$. // 📝 Solution: Least hindered primary halide $\implies$ fastest $S_N2$ $\implies$ option (1).

questions.text: Statement I: The $\mathrm{C{-}Cl}$ bond is stronger in $\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH{-}Cl}$ than in $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2Cl}$. Statement II: The optically active molecule [FIGURE] on hydrolysis gives a solution that can rotate plane-polarised light. Choose the correct option.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Bond strength depends on carbon hybridisation, and $S_N1$ hydrolysis gives a racemic product. // 📝 Solution: I: $\mathrm{sp^2}$ C–Cl is shorter and stronger than $\mathrm{sp^3}$ C–Cl $\implies$ I true; II: $S_N1$ hydrolysis gives a racemic mixture $\implies$ no net rotation $\implies$ II false

questions.text: The correct set of reagents or reaction conditions 'X' and 'Y' in the following transformation is: $\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH_2{-}CH_2{-}Br} \xrightarrow{\text{'X'}} \text{Product} \xrightarrow{\text{'Y'}} \mathrm{CH_3{-}CH(Br){-}CH_3}$

options.text: X = dil. aq. NaOH, 20 $^\circ$C; Y = Br$_2$/CHCl$_3$
X = conc. alc. NaOH, 80 $^\circ$C; Y = Br$_2$/CHCl$_3$
X = dil. aq. NaOH, 20 $^\circ$C; Y = HBr/acetic acid
X = conc. alc. NaOH, 80 $^\circ$C; Y = HBr/acetic acid

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Alcoholic base gives dehydrohalogenation; HBr without peroxide gives Markovnikov addition. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2CH_2Br} \xrightarrow{\text{conc. alc. NaOH}} \mathrm{CH_3CH{=}CH_2} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{HBr}} \mathrm{CH_3CHBrCH_3}$ $\implies$ option (4).

questions.text: A dibromo compound P ($\mathrm{C_9H_{10}Br_2}$) is heated with excess $\mathrm{NaNH_2}$, followed by dilute HCl, to give Q. Warming Q with $\mathrm{HgSO_4}$/dilute $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ gives R, which gives a positive iodoform test and a negative Tollens test. P is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Gem-dihalides give alkynes with strong base, and alkynes hydrate to methyl ketones by Markovnikov addition. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{p\text{-}CH_3C_6H_4CBr_2CH_3} \implies \mathrm{p\text{-}CH_3C_6H_4C{\equiv}CH} \implies \mathrm{p\text{-}CH_3C_6H_4COCH_3}$ (iodoform positive, Tollens negative)

questions.text: The correct order of reactivity in electrophilic substitution reaction of the following compounds is: A = benzene, B = toluene, C = chlorobenzene, D = nitrobenzene [FIGURE]

questions.text: The number of halobenzenes from the following that can be prepared by Sandmeyer's reaction is ______. [FIGURE]

questions.text: $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2Br} + \mathrm{NaOH} \xrightarrow[\mathrm{H_2O}]{\mathrm{C_2H_5OH}}$ Products $A$ and $B$. The total number of hydrogen atoms in product $A$ and product $B$ is ______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Count hydrogens in each product. // 📝 Solution: $A = \mathrm{CH_2{=}CH_2}$ (4 H); $B = \mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH}$ (6 H) $\implies$ total $= 10$.
questions.topic: Elimination vs substitution products of C2H5BrC2​H5​Br

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (A) vinyl chloride, (B) benzyl chloride, (C) alkyl chloride, (D) allyl chloride. List-II: (I) $\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH{-}CH_2Cl}$, (II) $\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH(Cl){-}CH_3}$, (III) $\mathrm{CH_2{=}CHCl}$, (IV) [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Classify each chloride by whether Cl sits on a vinyl, allyl, benzyl or saturated carbon. // 📝 Solution: Vinyl (A) $\implies$ III; allyl (D) $\implies$ I; alkyl (C) $\implies$ II (2-chloropropane); benzyl-type (B) $\implies$ IV as drawn $\implies$ option (4)
questions.topic: Classification of alkyl, allyl, vinyl and benzyl halides

questions.text: In the following sequence of reaction, the major products $B$ and $C$ respectively are: [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Wurtz coupling joins two C–X ends; Grignard with $\mathrm{D_2O}$ gives C–D; Swarts ($\mathrm{CoF_2}$) gives C–F. // 📝 Solution: Wurtz $\implies$ dimer $A$ (Cl at both ends) $\implies$ Mg then $\mathrm{D_2O}$ gives $B$ (D at both ends); $\mathrm{CoF_2}$ gives $C$ (F at both ends).

questions.text: A Grignard reagent $\mathrm{RMgBr}$ (P) reacts with water to form gas Q. One gram of Q occupies $1.4\;\mathrm{dm^3}$ at STP. (P) reacts with dry ice in dry ether, then $\mathrm{H_3O^+}$, to form Z. 0.1 mole of Z weighs ____ g (nearest integer).
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Grignard reagents react as carbanions, giving an alkane with water and a carboxylic acid with CO$_2$. // 📝 Solution: $M_Q = \frac{22.4}{1.4} = 16$ $\implies$ Q = $\mathrm{CH_4}$; $\mathrm{CH_3MgBr} + \mathrm{CO_2} \implies \mathrm{CH_3COOH}$ (Z, 60 g/mol) $\implies$ $0.1 \times 60 = 6\;\mathrm{g}$
questions.topic: Grignard reagents with water and carbon dioxide

questions.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R). Assertion (A): $S_N2$ reaction of $\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2Br}$ occurs more readily than the $S_N2$ reaction of $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2Br}$. Reason (R): The partially bonded unhybridized p-orbital in the trigonal bipyramidal transition state is stabilized by conjugation with the phenyl ring. Choose the most appropriate answer.

options.text: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Conjugation of the benzene $\pi$ system with the $S_N2$ transition state lowers $E_a$. // 📝 Solution: Benzylic TS p-orbital overlaps with ring $\pi$ $\implies$ lower $E_a$ $\implies$ faster; R explains A.

questions.text: Assertion A : Hydrolysis of an alkyl chloride is a slow reaction but in the presence of $\mathrm{NaI}$, the rate of hydrolysis increases. Reason R : $\mathrm{I^-}$ is a good nucleophile as well as a good leaving group. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer.

options.text: A is false but R is true
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\mathrm{I^-}$ is both a strong nucleophile and a good leaving group. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{R{-}Cl} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{I^-}} \mathrm{R{-}I} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Nu^-}} \mathrm{R{-}Nu}$ (fast) $\implies$ A true, R true and R explains A.
questions.topic: Nucleophilicity and leaving group ability in SN2SN​2

questions.text: Alkyl halide is converted into alkyl isocyanide by reaction with:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A covalent metal cyanide attacks through nitrogen. // 📝 Solution: $\mathrm{R{-}X} + \mathrm{AgCN} \implies \mathrm{R{-}NC}$ (isocyanide) since $\mathrm{AgCN}$ is covalent.

questions.text: The major products from the following reaction sequence are product $A$ and product $B$. [FIGURE] The total sum of $\pi$ electrons in product $A$ and product $B$ are ______ (nearest integer).
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Each $\pi$ bond contributes 2 $\pi$ electrons. // 📝 Solution: $A$ has one $\mathrm{C{\equiv}C}$ (2 $\pi$ bonds) $\implies$ 4 $\pi$ e$^-$; $B$ = cyclohexa-1,3-diene (2 $\mathrm{C{=}C}$) $\implies$ 4 $\pi$ e$^-$ $\implies$ total $= 8$.
