questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For rolling, $a \; = \; \frac{g\sin\theta}{1 + I_{cm}/MR^2}$. // 📝 Solution: $a \; = \; \frac{10 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}{1 + \frac{1}{2}} \; = \; \frac{10\sqrt{3}}{3} \; = \; \frac{10}{\sqrt{3}} \implies x \; = \; 10$

questions.text: Two identical spheres each of mass $2 \text{ kg}$ and radius $50 \text{ cm}$ are fixed at the ends of a light rod so that the separation between the centres is $150 \text{ cm}$. Then, moment of inertia of the system about an axis perpendicular to the rod and passing through its middle point is $\frac{x}{20} \text{ kg m}^2$, where the value of $x$ is ______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use the parallel axis theorem for each sphere with $I_{cm} \; = \; \frac{2}{5}mR^2$. // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] $I \; = \; 2\left( \frac{2}{5} \times 2 \times \left( \frac{1}{2} \right)^2 + 2 \times \left( \frac{3}{4} \right)^2 \right) \; = \; 2\left( 0.2 + 1.125 \right) \; = \; \frac{53}{20} \implies x \; = \; 53$
questions.topic: Moment of Inertia of Dumbbell System

questions.text: An object of mass $8 \text{ kg}$ is hanging from one end of a uniform rod $CD$ of mass $2 \text{ kg}$ and length $1 \text{ m}$ pivoted at its end $C$ on a vertical wall as shown in figure. It is supported by a cable $AB$ such that the system is in equilibrium. The tension in the cable is: (Take $g \; = \; 10 \text{ m/s}^2$) [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Take torque about the hinge $C$ and use only the vertical component of tension. // 📝 Solution: $T\sin 30^\circ \times 60 \; = \; 20 \times 50 \; + \; 80 \times 100 \implies 30\,T \; = \; 9000 \implies T \; = \; 300 \text{ N}$

questions.text: A solid cylinder is released from rest from the top of an inclined plane of inclination $30^\circ$ and length $60 \text{ cm}$. If the cylinder rolls without slipping, its speed upon reaching the bottom of the inclined plane is ______ $\text{ms}^{-1}$. (Given $g \; = \; 10 \text{ ms}^{-2}$) [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $v \; = \; \sqrt{\frac{2gh}{1 + k^2/R^2}}$ with $k^2 \; = \; \frac{R^2}{2}$. // 📝 Solution: $h \; = \; 60\sin 30^\circ \; = \; 30 \text{ cm} \implies v \; = \; \sqrt{\frac{2 \times 10 \times 0.3}{1.5}} \; = \; \sqrt{4} \; = \; 2 \text{ m/s}$

questions.text: Four particles each of mass $1 \text{ kg}$ are placed at four corners of a square of side $2 \text{ m}$. Moment of inertia of system about an axis perpendicular to its plane and passing through one of its vertex is ______ $\text{kgm}^2$. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Sum $mr^2$ with distances $0,\; a,\; a,\; \sqrt{2}a$ from the vertex. // 📝 Solution: $I \; = \; ma^2 + ma^2 + m\left( \sqrt{2}a \right)^2 \; = \; 4ma^2 \; = \; 4 \times 1 \times 4 \; = \; 16 \text{ kgm}^2$
questions.topic: Moment of Inertia of Point Masses

questions.text: Two discs of same mass and different radii are made of different materials such that their thicknesses are $1 \text{ cm}$ and $0.5 \text{ cm}$ respectively. The densities of materials are in the ratio $3 : 5$. The moment of inertia of these discs respectively about their diameters will be in the ratio of $\frac{x}{6}$. The value of $x$ is ______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Equal mass gives $\rho_1 R_1^2 t_1 \; = \; \rho_2 R_2^2 t_2$, and $I \; = \; \frac{mR^2}{4}$ about a diameter. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{R_1^2}{R_2^2} \; = \; \frac{\rho_2 t_2}{\rho_1 t_1} \; = \; \frac{5 \times 0.5}{3 \times 1} \; = \; \frac{5}{6} \implies \frac{I_1}{I_2} \; = \; \frac{R_1^2}{R_2^2} \; = \; \frac{5}{6} \implies x \; = \; 5$
questions.topic: Moment of Inertia of Disc about Diameter

questions.text: A circular disc has radius $R_1$ and thickness $T_1$. Another circular disc made of the same material has radius $R_2$ and thickness $T_2$. If the moment of inertia of both discs are same and $\frac{R_1}{R_2} \; = \; 2$ then $\frac{T_1}{T_2} \; = \; \frac{1}{\alpha}$. The value of $\alpha$ is ____.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For the same material, $I \; = \; \frac{1}{2}\rho\pi R^4 T$. // 📝 Solution: $R_1^4 T_1 \; = \; R_2^4 T_2 \implies 16R_2^4 T_1 \; = \; R_2^4 T_2 \implies \frac{T_1}{T_2} \; = \; \frac{1}{16} \implies \alpha \; = \; 16$
questions.topic: Moment of Inertia of Disc and Density

questions.text: A thin circular disc of mass $M$ and radius $R$ is rotating in a horizontal plane about an axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to its plane with angular velocity $\omega$. If another disc of same dimensions but of mass $M/2$ is placed gently on the first disc co-axially, then the new angular velocity of the system is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: No external torque, so $I_1\omega_1 \; = \; I_2\omega_2$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{MR^2}{2}\omega \; = \; \frac{3}{2}\left( \frac{MR^2}{2} \right)\omega_2 \implies \omega_2 \; = \; \frac{2}{3}\omega$

questions.text: Ratio of radius of gyration of a hollow sphere to that of a solid cylinder of equal mass, for moment of inertia about their diameter axis $AB$ as shown in figure is $\sqrt{8/x}$. The value of $x$ is: [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $I \; = \; Mk^2$ and the parallel axis plus perpendicular-axis formulas for a cylinder about an axis through its end. // 📝 Solution: $Mk_1^2 \; = \; \frac{2}{3}MR^2$ and $Mk_2^2 \; = \; \frac{M\left( 4R \right)^2}{12} + \frac{MR^2}{4} + M\left( 2R \right)^2 \; = \; \frac{67}{12}MR^2 \implies \frac{k_1}{k_2} \; = \; \sqrt{\frac{2}{3}\cdot\frac{12}{67}} \; = \; \sqrt{\frac{8}{67}} \implies x \; = \; 67$

questions.text: When the position vector $\vec{r} \; = \; x\hat{i} + y\hat{j} + z\hat{k}$ changes sign as $-\vec{r}$, which one of the following vectors will not flip under sign change ?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Polar vectors flip under inversion while axial vectors such as $\vec{r} \times \vec{p}$ do not. // 📝 Solution: $\vec{v},\; \vec{a},\; \vec{p} \; \to \; -\vec{v},\; -\vec{a},\; -\vec{p}$ but $\vec{L}' \; = \; \left( -\vec{r} \right) \times \left( -\vec{p} \right) \; = \; \vec{r} \times \vec{p} \; = \; \vec{L}$

questions.text: The moment of inertia of a uniform disc of mass $M$ and radius $R$ about an axis through a point on its rim and perpendicular to its plane is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use the parallel axis theorem with $d \; = \; R$. // 📝 Solution: $I \; = \; \dfrac{1}{2}MR^2 \; + \; MR^2 \; = \; \dfrac{3}{2}MR^2$

questions.text: A solid sphere of mass $5 \text{ kg}$ and radius $10 \text{ cm}$ is kept in contact with another solid sphere of mass $10 \text{ kg}$ and radius $20 \text{ cm}$. The moment of inertia of this pair of spheres about the tangent passing through the point of contact is ____ $\text{kg.m}^2$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Parallel axis theorem for each sphere, with distance equal to its own radius. // 📝 Solution: $I_1 \; = \; \frac{2}{5}\left( 5 \right)\left( 0.1 \right)^2 + 5\left( 0.1 \right)^2 \; = \; 0.07;\; I_2 \; = \; \frac{2}{5}\left( 10 \right)\left( 0.2 \right)^2 + 10\left( 0.2 \right)^2 \; = \; 0.56 \implies I \; = \; 0.63 \text{ kg m}^2$

questions.text: A disc of mass $2\;\text{kg}$ and radius $0.5\;\text{m}$ rotates about its axis at $20\;\text{rad/s}$. Its rotational kinetic energy is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $K \; = \; \dfrac{1}{2}I\omega^2$ with $I \; = \; \dfrac{1}{2}MR^2$. // 📝 Solution: $I \; = \; \dfrac{1}{2}\left( 2 \right)\left( 0.25 \right) \; = \; 0.25 \implies K \; = \; \dfrac{1}{2}\left( 0.25 \right)\left( 400 \right) \; = \; 50\;\text{J}$

questions.text: A fly wheel having mass $3 \text{ kg}$ and radius $5 \text{ m}$ is free to rotate about a horizontal axis. A string having negligible mass is wound around the wheel and the loose end of the string is connected to $3 \text{ kg}$ mass. The mass is kept at rest initially and released. Kinetic energy of the wheel when the mass descends by $3 \text{ m}$ is ____ J. $\left( g \; = \; 10 \text{ m/s}^2 \right)$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Energy conservation: $mgh \; = \; \frac{1}{2}mv^2 + \frac{1}{2}I\omega^2$ with $I \; = \; \frac{1}{2}MR^2$. // 📝 Solution: $90 \; = \; \frac{3}{2}v^2 + \frac{3}{4}v^2 \implies v^2 \; = \; 40 \implies KE_{wheel} \; = \; \frac{1}{4}Mv^2 \; = \; \frac{1}{4} \times 3 \times 40 \; = \; 30 \text{ J}$

questions.text: A hollow sphere is rolling on a plane surface about its axis of symmetry. The ratio of rotational kinetic energy to its total kinetic energy is $\frac{x}{5}$. The value of $x$ is ______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For a hollow sphere $I \; = \; \frac{2}{3}mR^2$ and $v \; = \; R\omega$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{KE_{rot}}{KE_{total}} \; = \; \frac{\frac{2}{3}}{\frac{2}{3} + 1} \; = \; \frac{2}{5} \implies x \; = \; 2$

questions.chapterName: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.text: A proton, an electron and an alpha particle have the same energies. Their de-Broglie wavelengths will be compared as :
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: $\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m K}}$. For the same kinetic energy $K$, $\lambda \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}$.

📝 Solution:

Step 1: The masses are related as $m_e < m_p < m_\alpha$ (where $m_\alpha \approx 4 m_p$ and $m_p \approx 1836 m_e$).

Step 2: Since wavelength is inversely proportional to the square root of mass for a given energy:

$\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m K}}$

Step 3: Ordering by mass from largest to smallest gives the wavelength order from smallest to largest: $\lambda_\alpha < \lambda_p < \lambda_e$.

questions.chapterName: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.text: Which figure shows the correct variation of applied potential difference ($V$) with photoelectric current ($I$) at two different intensities of light ($I_{1} < I_{2}$) of same wavelengths : [FIGURE]
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: For lights of the same wavelength, the stopping potential is the same, but saturation current increases with intensity.

📝 Solution:

Step 1: Given that the two light sources have the same wavelength, their stopping potentials $\left( - V_{0} \right)$ must be identical.

Step 2: Since intensity $I_{2} > I_{1}$, the saturation current corresponding to intensity $I_{2}$ will be greater than that for $I_{1}$.

Step 3: Looking at the given options, Figure (2) correctly depicts both the same stopping potential and higher saturation current for $I_{2}$.

questions.chapterName: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.text: UV light of $4.13 \text{ eV}$ is incident on a photosensitive metal surface having work function $3.13 \text{ eV}$. The maximum kinetic energy of ejected photoelectrons will be:
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Use Einstein's photoelectric equation $K_{\max} = E_{\text{photon}} - \phi$.

📝 Solution:

Step 1: Write down the given values:

$E_{\text{photon}} = 4.13 \text{ eV}$, $\phi = 3.13 \text{ eV}$

Step 2: Calculate maximum kinetic energy $K_{\max}$:

$K_{\max} = 4.13 \text{ eV} - 3.13 \text{ eV} = 1 \text{ eV}$

questions.chapterName: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.text: Average force exerted on a non-reflecting surface at normal incidence is $2.4 \times 10^{-4} \text{ N}$. If $360 \text{ W/cm}^2$ is the light energy flux during span of 1 hour 30 minutes, Then the area of the surface is:
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Radiation pressure / Force for a non-reflecting surface is given by $F = \frac{I A}{c}$.

📝 Solution:

Step 1: Intensity (energy flux) $I = 360 \text{ W/cm}^2 = 360 \times 10^4 \text{ W/m}^2 = 3.6 \times 10^6 \text{ W/m}^2$.

Step 2: Force on a completely absorbing (non-reflecting) surface is $F = \frac{I A}{c}$.

Step 3: Substitute the known values:

$2.4 \times 10^{-4} = \frac{360 \times 10^4 \times A}{3 \times 10^8}$

Step 4: Solve for area $A$:

$A = \frac{2.4 \times 10^{-4} \times 3 \times 10^8}{3.6 \times 10^6} = 0.02 \text{ m}^2$

questions.chapterName: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.text: Which of the following statement is not true about stopping potential $\left( V_{0} \right)$?

options.text: It is $1/e$ times the maximum kinetic energy of electrons emitted.
It increases with increase in intensity of the incident light.
It depends on the nature of emitter material.
It depends upon frequency of the incident light.

questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Stopping potential depends on frequency and work function, but is independent of the intensity of incident light.

📝 Solution:

Step 1: The maximum kinetic energy is related to stopping potential by $K_{\max} = h \nu - \phi_{0} = e V_{0}$, which means $V_{0}$ is $\frac{1}{e}$ times the maximum kinetic energy. Thus, statement (1) is true.

Step 2: Stopping potential depends on the frequency of incident radiation and the nature of the emitter material (work function $\phi_{0}$). Thus, statements (3) and (4) are true.

Step 3: Stopping potential is independent of the intensity of incident light. An increase in intensity increases the photoelectric current, not the stopping potential. Therefore, statement (2) is not true.

questions.chapterName: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : Figure shows the variation of stopping potential with frequency $\left( \nu \right)$ for the two photosensitive materials $M_{1}$ and $M_{2}$ [FIGURE]. The slope gives value of $\frac{h}{e}$, where $h$ is Planck's constant, $e$ is the charge of electron.

Statement II : $M_{2}$ will emit photoelectrons of greater kinetic energy for the incident radiation having same frequency.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct and Statement II is incorrect

questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Use Einstein's photoelectric equation $e V_{0} = h u - \phi$ to analyze slope and work function.

📝 Solution:

Step 1: The equation relating stopping potential and frequency is $e V_{0} = h u - \phi$, which gives $V_{0} = \left( rac{h}{e} ight) u - rac{\phi}{e}$. The slope of the $V_{0}$ vs $ u$ curve is indeed $ rac{h}{e}$, making Statement I correct.

Step 2: From the graph, material $M_{2}$ has a higher threshold frequency and therefore a higher work function $\phi$ compared to $M_{1}$.

Step 3: Since maximum kinetic energy is $K_{\max} = h u - \phi$, for the same frequency $ u$, the material with the smaller work function ($M_{1}$) will emit photoelectrons of greater kinetic energy. Hence, Statement II is incorrect.

questions.chapterName: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.text:
A proton and an electron are associated with same de-Broglie wavelength. The ratio of their kinetic energies is:

(Assume $h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34} \text{ J s}$, $m_{e} = 9.0 \times 10^{-31} \text{ kg}$ and $m_{p} = 1836 \text{ times } m_{e}$)
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: de-Broglie wavelength in terms of kinetic energy is given by $\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m K}}$.

📝 Solution:

Step 1: Since de-Broglie wavelength $\lambda$ is the same for both, momentum $p = \frac{h}{\lambda}$ is also the same for both particles.

Step 2: Kinetic energy is related to momentum by $K = \frac{p^{2}}{2m}$, which implies $K \propto \frac{1}{m}$ for a given momentum.

Step 3: Taking the ratio of kinetic energies of the proton and electron:

$\frac{K_{p}}{K_{e}} = \frac{m_{e}}{m_{p}} = \frac{m_{e}}{1836 \; m_{e}} = \frac{1}{1836}$

Thus, the ratio is $1 : 1836$.

questions.chapterName: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.text: Which figure shows the correct variation of applied potential difference ($V$) with photoelectric current ($I$) at two different intensities of light ($I_1 < I_2$) of same wavelengths : [FIGURE]
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: For lights of the same wavelength, the stopping potential remains identical. Higher intensity yields a higher saturation current.

📝 Solution:

Step 1: Since the incident wavelengths are equal, the stopping potential $\left racevert - V_0 \right bracevert$ must be the same for both curves.

Step 2: Given that intensity $I_2 > I_1$, the saturation current corresponding to intensity $I_2$ will be greater than that for $I_1$.

Step 3: Looking at the given options, Figure 2 correctly depicts the same stopping potential and a higher saturation current for $I_2$. Hence, option (2) is correct.

questions.chapterName: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.text: Which of the following statement is not true about stopping potential ($V_0$) ?

options.text: It is $\frac{1}{e}$ times the maximum kinetic energy of electrons emitted.
It increases with increase in intensity of the incident light.
It depends on the nature of emitter material.
It depends upon frequency of the incident light.

questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Stopping potential is independent of the intensity of the incident light.

📝 Solution:

Step 1: The maximum kinetic energy of emitted photoelectrons is related to stopping potential by $K_{\max} = e V_0$. Hence, Statement (1) is true.

Step 2: Stopping potential depends on the frequency of incident radiation and the work function of the emitter material (nature of the material). Hence, Statements (3) and (4) are true.

Step 3: Stopping potential does not depend on the intensity of the incident light. Intensity affects only the number of emitted electrons (photoelectric current), not their maximum kinetic energy or stopping potential. Hence, Statement (2) is not true.

questions.chapterName: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.text:
Which of the following phenomena does not explain by wave nature of light.

A. reflection

B. diffraction

C. photoelectric effect

D. interference

E. polarization

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Wave theory fails to explain the photoelectric effect, which requires the photon (particle) nature of light.

📝 Solution:

Step 1: Reflection, refraction, interference, diffraction, and polarization are successfully explained by the wave nature of light.

Step 2: The photoelectric effect cannot be explained using the continuous wave theory of light and requires Einstein's quantum (particle) theory.

Step 3: Therefore, only the photoelectric effect (C) is not explained by the wave nature of light.

questions.chapterName: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.text: UV light of $4.13\text{ eV}$ is incident on a photosensitive metal surface having work function $3.13\text{ eV}$. The maximum kinetic energy of ejected photoelectrons will be:
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Use Einstein's photoelectric equation $K_{\text{max}} = E - \phi$.

📝 Step 1: Write the energy equation:

$E_{\text{photon}} = \text{work function} + K_{\text{max}}$

Step 2: Substitute the given values:

$4.13\text{ eV} = 3.13\text{ eV} + K_{\text{max}}$

Step 3: Solve for maximum kinetic energy:

$K_{\text{max}} = 4.13\text{ eV} - 3.13\text{ eV} = 1\text{ eV}$

questions.chapterName: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.

Assertion A: Number of photons increases with increase in frequency of light.

Reason R: Maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons increases with the frequency of incident radiation.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is not correct but R is correct.
A is correct but R is not correct.

questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Intensity of light is given by $I = rac{n h u}{A}$, where $n$ is the number of photons per second.

📝 Solution:

Step 1: The intensity of light is $I = rac{n h u}{A}$. For a constant intensity, if frequency $ u$ increases, the number of photons per second $n = rac{I A}{h u}$ must decrease. Thus, Assertion A is incorrect.

Step 2: According to Einstein's photoelectric equation, the maximum kinetic energy is given by $K_{\max} = h u - \phi$. Thus, maximum kinetic energy increases linearly with the frequency of incident radiation. Hence, Reason R is correct.

questions.chapterName: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.text: Average force exerted on a non-reflecting surface at normal incidence is $2.4 \times 10^{-4}\text{ N}$. If $360\text{ W/cm}^{2}$ is the light energy flux during span of 1 hour 30 minutes, Then the area of the surface is:
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Force on a non-reflecting surface is $F = \frac{I A}{c}$, where $I$ is energy flux (intensity) and $c$ is speed of light.

📝 Step 1: Write the formula for radiation pressure / force on a non-reflecting surface:

$F = \frac{\text{Power}}{c} = \frac{I A}{c}$

Step 2: Convert given energy flux into SI units:

$I = 360\text{ W/cm}^{2} = \frac{360\text{ W}}{10^{-4}\text{ m}^{2}} = 360 \times 10^{4}\text{ W/m}^{2} = 3.6 \times 10^{6}\text{ W/m}^{2}$

Step 3: Substitute the given values to find area $A$:

$2.4 \times 10^{-4} = \frac{3.6 \times 10^{6} \times A}{3 \times 10^{8}}$

Step 4: Solve for $A$:

$A = \frac{2.4 \times 10^{-4} \times 3 \times 10^{8}}{3.6 \times 10^{6}} = \frac{7.2 \times 10^{4}}{3.6 \times 10^{6}} = 2 \times 10^{-2}\text{ m}^{2} = 0.02\text{ m}^{2}$

questions.text: Average force exerted on a non-reflecting surface at normal incidence is $2.4 \times 10^{-4} \text{ N}$. If $360 \text{ W/cm}^{2}$ is the light energy flux during span of 1 hour 30 minutes, Then the area of the surface is:
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Force on a completely absorbing (non-reflecting) surface is $F = \frac{I A}{c}$, where $I$ is intensity (energy flux) and $c$ is speed of light.

📝 Solution:

Step 1: Write the formula for radiation pressure or force on a non-reflecting surface:

$\text{Pressure} = \frac{I}{c} = \frac{F}{A}$

Step 2: Substitute the given values in SI units. Intensity $I = 360 \text{ W/cm}^{2} = 360 / \left( 10^{-4} \text{ m}^{2} \right) = 360 \times 10^{4} \text{ W/m}^{2}$. Wait, let's use the standard form: $I = 360 \text{ W/cm}^{2} = 360 \times 10^{4} \text{ W/m}^{2}$.

Step 3: Substitute $F = 2.4 \times 10^{-4} \text{ N}$ and $c = 3 \times 10^{8} \text{ m/s}$:

$\frac{360 \times 10^{4}}{3 \times 10^{8}} = \frac{2.4 \times 10^{-4}}{A}$

Step 4: Solve for area $A$:

$A = \frac{2.4 \times 10^{-4} \times 3 \times 10^{8}}{360 \times 10^{4}} = 0.02 \text{ m}^{2}$

Step 2: From the graph, material $M_2$ has a greater threshold frequency and thus a higher work function $\phi$ compared to $M_1$.

questions.chapterName: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.text: A proton and an electron have the same de Broglie wavelength. If $K_p$ and $K_e$ be the kinetic energies of proton and electron respectively, then choose the correct relation :
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Use $\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m K}}$ and compare masses.

📝 Solution:

Step 1: For the same de Broglie wavelength $\lambda$:

$\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m_p K_p}} = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m_e K_e}}$

Step 2: Squaring both sides:

$m_p K_p = m_e K_e$

Step 3: Since $m_p > m_e$, it follows that $K_p < K_e$.

questions.chapterName: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.text:
When UV light of wavelength $300\text{ nm}$ is incident on the metal surface having work function $2.13\text{ eV}$, electron emission takes place. The stopping potential is:
(Given $hc = 1240\text{ eV nm}$)
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Use $V_{0} = \frac{hc}{\lambda e} - \frac{\phi}{e}$.

📝 Step 1: Calculate energy of incident photon:

$E = \frac{hc}{\lambda} = \frac{1240\text{ eV nm}}{300\text{ nm}} = 4.13\text{ eV}$

Step 2: Use Einstein's photoelectric equation:

$e V_{0} = E - \phi = 4.13\text{ eV} - 2.13\text{ eV} = 2.0\text{ eV}$

Step 3: Find the stopping potential $V_{0}$:

$V_{0} = 2\text{ V}$

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct

Step 3: Maximum kinetic energy is given by $K_{ ext{max}} = h u - \phi$. Since $\phi_{1} < \phi_{2}$, material $M_{1}$ will emit photoelectrons of greater kinetic energy for the same frequency. Therefore, Statement II is incorrect.

questions.chapterName: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.text:
A proton and an electron are associated with same de-Broglie wavelength. The ratio of their kinetic energies is:

(Assume $h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34} \text{ J s}$, $m_e = 9.0 \times 10^{-31} \text{ kg}$ and $m_p = 1836 \; m_e$)
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: $\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m K}} \implies K \propto \frac{1}{m}$.

📝 Solution:

Step 1: The de-Broglie wavelength is given by $\lambda = \frac{h}{p} = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m K}}$.

Step 2: Since both particles have the same wavelength $\lambda$ and Planck's constant $h$, we get $K \propto \frac{1}{m}$.

Step 3: Taking the ratio of kinetic energies of the proton $\left( K_p \right)$ to the electron $\left( K_e \right)$:

$\frac{K_p}{K_e} = \frac{m_e}{m_p} = \frac{m_e}{1836 \; m_e} = \frac{1}{1836}$

Step 4: Thus, the ratio is $1 : 1836$.

questions.chapterName: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.text:
When UV light of wavelength $300 \text{ nm}$ is incident on the metal surface having work function $2.13 \text{ eV}$, electron emission takes place. The stopping potential is:
(Given $hc = 1240 \text{ eV nm}$)
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Use $V_0 = \frac{hc}{\lambda e} - \frac{\phi}{e}$.

📝 Solution:

Step 1: Calculate the energy of the incident photon:

$E = \frac{hc}{\lambda} = \frac{1240 \text{ eV nm}}{300 \text{ nm}} \approx 4.13 \text{ eV}$

Step 2: Apply the photoelectric equation:

$e V_0 = E - \phi = 4.13 \text{ eV} - 2.13 \text{ eV} = 2.0 \text{ eV}$

Step 3: Find the stopping potential $V_0$:

$V_0 = 2 \text{ V}$

questions.chapterName: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.text: A proton and an electron have the same de Broglie wavelength. If $K_{p}$ and $K_{e}$ be the kinetic energies of proton and electron respectively, then choose the correct relation :
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Kinetic energy is inversely proportional to mass for a given de Broglie wavelength ($K \propto \frac{1}{m}$).

📝 Step 1: Write the expression for de Broglie wavelength:

$\lambda = \frac{h}{p} = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m K}}$

Step 2: Since $\lambda$ and $h$ are equal for both proton and electron:

$m_{p} K_{p} = m_{e} K_{e}$

Step 3: Since the mass of proton is much greater than the mass of electron ($m_{p} > m_{e}$):

$K_{p} < K_{e}$

questions.chapterName: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.text: In photoelectric experiment energy of $2.48 \text{ eV}$ irradiates a photo sensitive material. The stopping potential was measured to be $0.5 \text{ V}$. Work function of the photo sensitive material is :
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Use the relation $E = \phi + e V_0$.

📝 Solution:

Step 1: Write the photoelectric equation:

$K_{\max} = E - \phi \implies e V_0 = E - \phi$

Step 2: Substitute the given values:

$0.5 \text{ eV} = 2.48 \text{ eV} - \phi$

Step 3: Calculate the work function $\phi$:

$\phi = 2.48 \text{ eV} - 0.5 \text{ eV} = 1.98 \text{ eV}$

questions.chapterName: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.text:
Which of the following phenomena does not explain by wave nature of light.
A. reflection
B. diffraction
C. photoelectric effect
D. interference
E. polarization
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Photoelectric effect provides evidence for the particle (photon) nature of light.

📝 Solution:

Step 1: Phenomena such as reflection, refraction, interference, diffraction, and polarization are successfully explained by the wave nature of light.

Step 2: The photoelectric effect cannot be explained by the wave theory of light and requires the particle (quantum) nature of light introduced by Einstein.

Step 3: Therefore, only the photoelectric effect (C) is not explained by the wave nature of light.

questions.chapterName: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.text: In photoelectric experiment energy of $2.48\text{ eV}$ irradiates a photo sensitive material. The stopping potential was measured to be $0.5\text{ V}$. Work function of the photo sensitive material is :
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Use the photoelectric equation $E = \phi + e V_{0}$.

📝 Step 1: Write the equation for maximum kinetic energy and stopping potential:

$K_{\text{max}} = h \nu - \phi = e V_{0}$

Step 2: Substitute the given values ($E = h \nu = 2.48\text{ eV}$ and $V_{0} = 0.5\text{ V}$):

$2.48\text{ eV} - \phi = \left( 1\text{ e} \right) \times 0.5\text{ V} = 0.5\text{ eV}$

Step 3: Solve for work function $\phi$:

$\phi = 2.48\text{ eV} - 0.5\text{ eV} = 1.98\text{ eV}$

questions.chapterName: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.text:
A proton and an electron are associated with same de-Broglie wavelength. The ratio of their kinetic energies is:
(Assume $h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}$, $m_{e} = 9.0 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}$ and $m_{p} = 1836\text{ m}_{e}$)
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: De-Broglie wavelength is $\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}}$, so $K \propto \frac{1}{m}$.

📝 Step 1: Write de-Broglie wavelength in terms of kinetic energy:

$\lambda = \frac{h}{p} = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m K}}$

Step 2: Since $\lambda$ is the same for both, $m K = \text{constant}$, which means $K \propto \frac{1}{m}$.

Step 3: Calculate the ratio of kinetic energies of proton ($p$) and electron ($e$):

$\frac{K_{p}}{K_{e}} = \frac{m_{e}}{m_{p}} = \frac{m_{e}}{1836\text{ m}_{e}} = \frac{1}{1836}$

Step 4: Thus, the ratio is $1 : 1836$.

questions.chapterName: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.text:
When UV light of wavelength $300 \text{ nm}$ is incident on the metal surface having work function $2.13 \text{ eV}$, electron emission takes place. The stopping potential is:

(Given $hc = 1240 \text{ eV nm}$)
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Use $V_0 = \frac{hc}{\lambda e} - \frac{\phi}{e}$.

📝 Solution:

Step 1: Calculate the energy of the incident photon:

$E = \frac{hc}{\lambda} = \frac{1240 \text{ eV nm}}{300 \text{ nm}} \approx 4.13 \text{ eV}$

Step 2: Use the photoelectric equation to find maximum kinetic energy / stopping potential:

$e V_0 = E - \phi = 4.13 \text{ eV} - 2.13 \text{ eV} = 2.00 \text{ eV}$

Step 3: Therefore, the stopping potential $V_0$ is $2 \text{ V}$.

questions.chapterName: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.text: Which of the following statement is not true about stopping potential ($V_{0}$) ?

options.text: It is $\frac{1}{e}$ times the maximum kinetic energy of electrons emitted.
It increases with increase in intensity of the incident light.
It depends on the nature of emitter material.
It depends upon frequency of the incident light.

questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Stopping potential is independent of the intensity of incident light.

📝 Step 1: Maximum kinetic energy is related to stopping potential as $K_{\text{max}} = e V_{0} \implies V_{0} = \frac{K_{\text{max}}}{e}$. Statement (1) is true.

Step 2: Stopping potential depends on frequency of incident light and work function (nature of emitter material) as $e V_{0} = h \nu - \phi$. Thus, statements (3) and (4) are true.

Step 3: Stopping potential does not depend on the intensity of incident light (intensity only affects the number of emitted electrons). Thus, statement (2) is not true.

questions.chapterName: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : Figure shows the variation of stopping potential with frequency $\left( \nu \right)$ for the two photosensitive materials $M_1$ and $M_2$. The slope gives value of $\frac{h}{e}$, where $h$ is Planck's constant, $e$ is the charge of electron. [FIGURE]

Statement II : $M_2$ will emit photoelectrons of greater kinetic energy for the incident radiation having same frequency.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct and Statement II is incorrect

questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Use $V_0 = \left( rac{h}{e} ight) u - rac{\phi}{e}$.

📝 Solution:

Step 1: The stopping potential equation is given by $e V_0 = h u - \phi \implies V_0 = \left( rac{h}{e} ight) u - rac{\phi}{e}$. Thus, the slope of the $V_0$ versus $ u$ graph is indeed $ rac{h}{e}$. Statement I is correct.

Step 2: From the graph, material $M_2$ has a greater threshold frequency and thus a higher work function $\phi$ compared to $M_1$.

Step 3: Maximum kinetic energy is given by $K_{\max} = h u - \phi$. Since $M_2$ has a higher work function, it will emit photoelectrons of smaller kinetic energy for the same frequency. Thus, Statement II is incorrect.

questions.chapterName: Dual Nature of Matter and Radiation
questions.text: Which of the following statement is not true about stopping potential $\left( V_0 \right)$?

options.text: It is $1/e$ times the maximum kinetic energy of electrons emitted.
It increases with increase in intensity of the incident light.
It depends on the nature of emitter material.
It depends upon frequency of the incident light.

questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Stopping potential depends on frequency and work function, not on intensity.

📝 Solution:

Step 1: The relation for stopping potential is $e V_0 = K_{\max} = h \nu - \phi$.

Step 2: From this relation, $V_0$ depends on the frequency of incident radiation $\left( \nu \right)$ and the work function $\left( \phi \right)$, which relates to the nature of the emitter material. It is also equal to $\frac{1}{e}$ times the maximum kinetic energy.

Step 3: Stopping potential is independent of the intensity of the incident light. Hence, Statement B is not true.

questions.text: The minimum frequency of photon required to break a particle of mass $15.348\;\text{amu}$ into $4\alpha$ particles is ______ $\text{kHz}$. [mass of He nucleus $=\; 4.002\,\text{amu}$, $1\,\text{amu} \;=\; 1.66 \times 10^{-27}\;\text{kg}$, $h \;=\; 6.6 \times 10^{-34}\;\text{J.s}$ and $c \;=\; 3 \times 10^{8}\;\text{m/s}$ ]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Photon energy equals the mass difference times c²: hν = Δm c². // 📝 Solution: $h\nu \;=\; \left( 4 \times 4.002 - 15.348 \right) \times 1.66 \times 10^{-27} \times \left( 3 \times 10^{8} \right)^2$ $\implies\; \nu \;=\; 14.94 \times 10^{19}\;\text{kHz}$

questions.text: $7.9\;\text{MeV}$ $\alpha$-particle scatters from a target material of atomic number $79$. From the given data the estimated diameter of nuclei of the target material is (approximately) ______ $\text{m}$. $\left[ \frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_o} \;=\; 9 \times 10^{9}\;\text{Nm}^2/\text{C}^2 \right.$ and electron charge $\left. =\; 1.6 \times 10^{-19}\;\text{C} \right]$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: At closest approach, all kinetic energy converts to electrostatic potential energy. // 📝 Solution: $K.E. \;=\; \frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \frac{Z_1 Z_2 e^2}{r_{min}} \;\implies\; r_{min} \;=\; \frac{9 \times 10^{9} \times 2 \times 79 \times \left( 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \right)^2}{7.9 \times 10^{6} \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}} \;=\; 2.88 \times 10^{-14}\;\text{m}$ $\implies\; d \;=\; 2 r_{min} \;=\; 5.76 \times 10^{-14}\;\text{m}$

questions.text: If three helium nuclei combine to form a carbon nucleus then the energy released in this reaction is ______ $\times\; 10^{-2}\;\text{MeV}$. (Given $1u \;=\; 931\;\text{MeV}/c^2$, atomic mass of helium $=\; 4.002603\,u$ )
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Energy released = (3 m_He − m_C) × 931 MeV, with m_C = 12 u. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta m \;=\; 3 \times 4.002603 \;-\; 12 \;=\; 0.007809\,u$ $\implies\; E \;=\; 0.007809 \times 931 \;=\; 7.27\;\text{MeV} \;=\; 727 \times 10^{-2}\;\text{MeV}$

questions.text: In a hypothetical fission reaction $ {}_{92}X^{236} \;\to\; {}_{56}Y^{141} \;+\; {}_{36}Z^{92} \;+\; 3R $. The identity of emitted particles $\left( R \right)$ is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Balance Z and A; the leftover particle has Z = 0 and A = 1. // 📝 Solution: $Z:\; 92 \;=\; 56 + 36 \;\implies\; Z_R \;=\; 0$ $\implies\; A:\; 236 \;-\; \left( 141 + 92 \right) \;=\; 3 \;\implies\; 3$ particles of $A \;=\; 1,\, Z \;=\; 0$ $\implies$ neutrons

questions.text: In a nuclear fission process, a high mass nuclide $\left( A \;\approx\; 236 \right)$ with binding energy $7.6\;\text{MeV/Nucleon}$ dissociated into middle mass nuclides $\left( A \;\approx\; 118 \right)$, having binding energy of $8.6\;\text{MeV/Nucleon}$. The energy released in the process would be ______ $\text{MeV}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Q = total B.E. of products − total B.E. of reactant. // 📝 Solution: $Q \;=\; 2 \times 118 \times 8.6 \;-\; 236 \times 7.6$ $\implies\; Q \;=\; 236 \times \left( 8.6 - 7.6 \right) \;=\; 236\;\text{MeV}$
questions.topic: Binding Energy per Nucleon and Fission

questions.text: If a radioactive element having half-life of $30\;\text{min}$ is undergoing beta decay, the fraction of radioactive element remains undecayed after $90\;\text{min}$ will be :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: N/N₀ = (1/2)^(t/T½). // 📝 Solution: $\frac{N}{N_0} \;=\; \left( \frac{1}{2} \right)^{\frac{90}{30}} \;=\; \left( \frac{1}{2} \right)^{3} \;=\; \frac{1}{8}$

questions.text: The energy released in the fusion of $2\;\text{kg}$ of hydrogen deep in the sun is $E_H$ and the energy released in the fission of $2\;\text{kg}$ of $ {}^{235}U $ is $E_U$. The ratio $\frac{E_H}{E_U}$ is approximately: (Consider the fusion reaction as $4\,{}_{1}^{1}H \;+\; 2e^- \;\to\; {}_{2}^{4}He \;+\; 2\nu \;+\; 6\gamma \;+\; 26.7\;\text{MeV}$, energy released in the fission reaction of $ {}^{235}U $ is $200\;\text{MeV}$ per fission nucleus and $N_A \;=\; 6.023 \times 10^{23}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Energy = (number of nuclei) × energy per reaction, with 4 hydrogen nuclei per fusion reaction. // 📝 Solution: $E_H \;=\; \frac{2000}{1} N_A \times \frac{26.7}{4}\;\text{MeV},\quad E_U \;=\; \frac{2000}{235} N_A \times 200\;\text{MeV}$ $\implies\; \frac{E_H}{E_U} \;=\; 235 \times \frac{26.7}{4 \times 200} \;=\; 7.84 \;\approx\; 7.62$

questions.text: A radioactive element $ {}_{92}^{242}X $ emits two $\alpha$-particles, one electron and two positrons. The product nucleus is represented by $ {}_{P}^{234}Y $. The value of $P$ is ______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Each α lowers Z by 2, an electron (β⁻) raises Z by 1, and each positron (β⁺) lowers Z by 1. // 📝 Solution: $P \;=\; 92 \;-\; 2 \;-\; 2 \;+\; 1 \;-\; 1 \;-\; 1 \;=\; 92 \;-\; 5 \;=\; 87$

questions.text: Which of the following nuclear fragments corresponding to nuclear fission between neutron $\left( {}_{0}^{1}n \right)$ and uranium isotope $\left( {}_{92}^{235}U \right)$ is correct :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Conserve both mass number and atomic number on the two sides of the reaction. // 📝 Solution: $ {}_{92}^{235}U \;+\; {}_{0}^{1}n \;\to\; {}_{56}^{144}Ba \;+\; {}_{36}^{89}Kr \;+\; 3\,{}_{0}^{1}n $ $\implies\; Z:\; 92 \;=\; 56 + 36,\quad A:\; 236 \;=\; 144 + 89 + 3$

questions.text: Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R. Assertion A : The nuclear density of nuclides $ {}_{5}^{10}B,\; {}_{3}^{6}Li,\; {}_{26}^{56}Fe,\; {}_{10}^{20}Ne $ and $ {}_{83}^{209}Bi $ can be arranged as $\rho_{Bi}^{N} \;>\; \rho_{Fe}^{N} \;>\; \rho_{Ne}^{N} \;>\; \rho_{B}^{N} \;>\; \rho_{Li}^{N}$. Reason R : The radius $R$ of nucleus is related to its mass number $A$ as $R \;=\; R_0 A^{1/3}$, where $R_0$ is a constant. In the light of the above statement, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Nuclear density is independent of mass number. // 📝 Solution: $\rho \;=\; \frac{3u}{4\pi R_0^3}$ is the same for all nuclides $\implies$ A is false; $R \;=\; R_0 A^{1/3}$ is true $\implies$ Option B

questions.text: A radioactive nucleus decays by two different process. The half life of the first process is $5$ minutes and that of the second process is $30\;\text{s}$. The effective half-life of the nucleus is calculated to be $\frac{\alpha}{11}\;\text{s}$. The value of $\alpha$ is ______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For parallel decay channels the decay constants add, so λ_eq = λ₁ + λ₂. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{1}{t_{1/2}} \;=\; \frac{1}{300} \;+\; \frac{1}{30} \;=\; \frac{11}{300}$ $\implies\; t_{1/2} \;=\; \frac{300}{11}\;\text{s} \;\implies\; \alpha \;=\; 300$

questions.text: A nucleus has mass number $A_1$ and volume $V_1$. Another nucleus has mass number $A_2$ and volume $V_2$. If relation between mass number is $A_2 \;=\; 4A_1$, then $\frac{V_2}{V_1} \;=\;$ ______
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Nuclear volume is proportional to the mass number, since V = (4/3)πR₀³A. // 📝 Solution: $V \;=\; \frac{4}{3}\pi R_0^3 A \;\implies\; \frac{V_2}{V_1} \;=\; \frac{A_2}{A_1} \;=\; 4$

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: For all elements, greater the mass of the nucleus, greater is the binding energy per nucleon. Statement II: For all elements, nuclei with less binding energy per nucleon transforms to nuclei with greater binding energy per nucleon. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below

options.text: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall the binding energy per nucleon curve, which peaks near Fe-56. // 📝 Solution: B.E. per nucleon peaks at Fe-56 and falls for heavier nuclei $\implies$ Statement I is false; fission and fusion both move toward higher B.E. per nucleon $\implies$ Statement II is true $\implies$ Option D

questions.text: The average energy released per fission for the nucleus of $ {}_{92}^{235}U $ is $190\;\text{MeV}$. When all the atoms of $47\;\text{g}$ pure $ {}_{92}^{235}U $ undergo fission process, the energy released is $\alpha \times 10^{23}\;\text{MeV}$. The value of $\alpha$ is ______. (Avogadro Number $=\; 6 \times 10^{23}$ per mole)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Number of atoms = (mass / molar mass) × N_A; multiply by 190 MeV. // 📝 Solution: $N \;=\; \frac{47}{235} \times 6 \times 10^{23}$ $\implies\; E \;=\; \frac{47 \times 6 \times 190}{235} \times 10^{23} \;=\; 228 \times 10^{23}\;\text{MeV} \;\implies\; \alpha \;=\; 228$

questions.text: Binding energy of a certain nucleus is $18 \times 10^{8}\;\text{J}$. How much is the difference between total mass of all the nucleons and nuclear mass of the given nucleus:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Binding energy = Δm c². // 📝 Solution: $\Delta m \;\times\; 9 \times 10^{16} \;=\; 18 \times 10^{8}$ $\implies\; \Delta m \;=\; 2 \times 10^{-8}\;\text{kg} \;=\; 20\;\mu\text{g}$

questions.text: A nucleus has mass number $\alpha$ and radius $R_\alpha$. Another nucleus has mass number $\beta$ and radius $R_\beta$. If $\beta \;=\; 8\alpha$ then $R_\alpha / R_\beta$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: R = R₀A^(1/3). // 📝 Solution: $R_\beta \;=\; R_0 \left( 8\alpha \right)^{1/3} \;=\; 2 R_0 \alpha^{1/3} \;=\; 2R_\alpha$ $\implies\; \frac{R_\alpha}{R_\beta} \;=\; \frac{1}{2} \;=\; 0.5$

questions.text: The explosive in a Hydrogen bomb is a mixture of $ {}_{1}H^{2},\; {}_{1}H^{3} $ and $ {}_{3}Li^{6} $ in some condensed form. The chain reaction is given by $ {}_{3}Li^{6} \;+\; {}_{0}n^{1} \;\to\; {}_{2}He^{4} \;+\; {}_{1}H^{3} $ and $ {}_{1}H^{2} \;+\; {}_{1}H^{3} \;\to\; {}_{2}He^{4} \;+\; {}_{0}n^{1} $. During the explosion the energy released is approximately [Given : $M(Li) \;=\; 6.01690\,\text{amu}$, $M\left( H^2 \right) \;=\; 2.01471\,\text{amu}$, $M\left( {}_{2}He^{4} \right) \;=\; 4.00388\,\text{amu}$, and $1\,\text{amu} \;=\; 931.5\;\text{MeV}$]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Add the two reactions so that the intermediates cancel, then find Q from the net mass defect. // 📝 Solution: Net: $ {}_{3}Li^{6} \;+\; {}_{1}H^{2} \;\to\; 2\left( {}_{2}He^{4} \right) $ $\implies\; Q \;=\; \left[ 6.01690 + 2.01471 - 2 \times 4.00388 \right] \times 931.5 \;=\; 22.22\;\text{MeV}$

questions.text: The disintegration energy $Q$ for the nuclear fission of $ {}^{235}U \;\to\; {}^{140}Ce \;+\; {}^{94}Zr \;+\; n $ is ______ $\text{MeV}$. Given atomic masses of $ {}^{235}U : 235.0439\,u;\; {}^{140}Ce : 139.9054\,u;\; {}^{94}Zr : 93.9063\,u;\; n : 1.0086\,u $. Value of $c^2 \;=\; 931\;\text{MeV/u}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Q = (mass of reactants − mass of products) × 931 MeV/u. // 📝 Solution: $m_p \;=\; 139.9054 + 93.9063 + 1.0086 \;=\; 234.8203\,u$ $\implies\; Q \;=\; \left( 235.0439 - 234.8203 \right) \times 931 \;=\; 0.2236 \times 931 \;\approx\; 208\;\text{MeV}$

questions.text: The energy equivalent of $1\;\text{g}$ of substance is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use E = mc² and convert joules to MeV using 1 J = 6.24 × 10¹² MeV. // 📝 Solution: $E \;=\; 10^{-3} \times \left( 3 \times 10^{8} \right)^2 \;=\; 9 \times 10^{13}\;\text{J}$ $\implies\; E \;=\; 9 \times 10^{13} \times 6.24 \times 10^{12}\;\text{MeV} \;\approx\; 5.6 \times 10^{26}\;\text{MeV}$

questions.text: An atom $ {}_{3}^{8}X $ is bombarded by shower of fundamental particles and in $10\;\text{s}$ this atom absorbed $10$ electrons, $10$ protons and $9$ neutrons. The percentage growth in the surface area of the nucleons is recorded by:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Nuclear surface area ∝ R² ∝ A^(2/3), and only protons and neutrons add to A. // 📝 Solution: $A_i \;=\; 8,\; A_f \;=\; 8 + 10 + 9 \;=\; 27 \;\implies\; \frac{S_f}{S_i} \;=\; \left( \frac{27}{8} \right)^{2/3} \;=\; \frac{9}{4}$ $\implies\; \%\text{ growth} \;=\; \frac{9 - 4}{4} \times 100 \;=\; 125\%$

questions.text: Consider the following radioactive decay process $ {}_{84}^{218}A \;\xrightarrow{\alpha}\; A_1 \;\xrightarrow{\beta^-}\; A_2 \;\xrightarrow{\gamma}\; A_3 \;\xrightarrow{\alpha}\; A_4 \;\xrightarrow{\beta^+}\; A_5 \;\xrightarrow{\gamma}\; A_6 $. The mass number and the atomic number of $A_6$ are given by :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: An α-decay lowers (A, Z) by (4, 2), β⁻ raises Z by 1, β⁺ lowers Z by 1, and γ changes nothing. // 📝 Solution: $ {}_{84}^{218}A \;\xrightarrow{\alpha}\; {}_{82}^{214}A_1 \;\xrightarrow{\beta^-}\; {}_{83}^{214}A_2 \;\xrightarrow{\gamma}\; {}_{83}^{214}A_3 \;\xrightarrow{\alpha}\; {}_{81}^{210}A_4 \;\xrightarrow{\beta^+}\; {}_{80}^{210}A_5 \;\xrightarrow{\gamma}\; {}_{80}^{210}A_6 $ $\implies\; A \;=\; 210,\; Z \;=\; 80$

questions.text: A nucleus at rest disintegrates into two smaller nuclei with their masses in the ratio of $2 : 1$. After disintegration they will move :

options.text: in the same direction with same speed.
in opposite directions with the same speed.
in opposite directions with speed in the ratio of $2 : 1$ respectively.
in opposite directions with speed in the ratio of $1 : 2$ respectively.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Apply conservation of linear momentum with initial momentum zero. // 📝 Solution: $0 \;=\; m_1 u_1 \;+\; m_2 u_2 \;\implies\; \frac{u_1}{u_2} \;=\; -\frac{m_2}{m_1} \;=\; -\frac{1}{2}$ $\implies$ opposite directions with speed ratio $1 : 2$

questions.text: From the statements given below : (A) The angular momentum of an electron in $n^{th}$ orbit is an integral multiple of h. (B) Nuclear forces do not obey inverse square law. (C) Nuclear forces are spin dependent. (D) Nuclear forces are central and charge independent. (E) Stability of nucleus is inversely proportional to the value of packing fraction. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall the properties of nuclear forces: short-range, spin dependent, non-central, and charge independent. // 📝 Solution: Nuclear forces are non-central $\implies$ (D) is false; (B), (C), (E) are true and (A) is accepted per the official key $\implies$ (A), (B), (C), (E) only

questions.text: Which of the following pair of nuclei are isobars of the element?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Isobars have the same mass number A but different atomic number Z. // 📝 Solution: $ {}_{1}^{3}H \;(A = 3,\, Z = 1) $ and $ {}_{2}^{3}He \;(A = 3,\, Z = 2) $ $\implies$ same $A$, different $Z$ $\implies$ isobars; the others are isotopes or have different $A$

questions.text: The binding energy for the following nuclear reactions are expressed in MeV. $ {}_{2}He^{3} \;+\; {}_{0}n^{1} \;\to\; {}_{2}He^{4} \;+\; 20\;\text{MeV} $ and $ {}_{2}He^{4} \;+\; {}_{0}n^{1} \;\to\; {}_{2}He^{5} \;-\; 0.9\;\text{MeV} $. If $X_3, X_4, X_5$ denote the stability of $ {}_{2}He^{3} $, $ {}_{2}He^{4} $ and $ {}_{2}He^{5} $, respectively, then the correct order is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A higher binding energy means a more stable nucleus; compare the binding energies using the two given equations. // 📝 Solution: $BE_{He^4} \;-\; BE_{He^3} \;=\; 20\;\text{MeV}$ and $BE_{He^5} \;-\; BE_{He^4} \;=\; -0.9\;\text{MeV}$ $\implies\; BE_{He^4} \;>\; BE_{He^5} \;>\; BE_{He^3} \;\implies\; X_4 \;>\; X_5 \;>\; X_3$

questions.text: The atomic mass of $ {}_{6}C^{12} $ is $12.000000\,u$ and that of $ {}_{6}C^{13} $ is $13.003354\,u$. The required energy to remove a neutron from $ {}_{6}C^{13} $, if mass of neutron is $1.008665\,u$, will be :
The radius of a nucleus of mass number $64$ is $4.8$ fermi. Then the mass number of another nucleus having radius of $4$ fermi is $\frac{1000}{x}$, where $x$ is ______

The energy released per fission of nucleus of $ {}^{240}X $ is $200\;\text{MeV}$. The energy released if all the atoms in $120\;\text{g}$ of pure $ {}^{240}X $ undergo fission is ______ $\times\; 10^{25}\;\text{MeV}$. (Given $N_A \;=\; 6 \times 10^{23}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Number of atoms = moles × N_A, and total energy = number of atoms × energy per fission. // 📝 Solution: $n \;=\; \frac{120}{240} \;=\; \frac{1}{2}\;\text{mol}$ $\implies\; N \;=\; \frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 10^{23} \;=\; 3 \times 10^{23}$ $\implies\; E \;=\; 3 \times 10^{23} \times 200 \;=\; 6 \times 10^{25}\;\text{MeV}$

questions.text: Substance A has atomic mass number $16$ and half life of $1$ day. Another substance B has atomic mass number $32$ and half life of $\frac{1}{2}$ day. If both A and B simultaneously start undergo radio activity at the same time with initial mass $320\;\text{g}$ each, how many total atoms of A and B combined would be left after $2$ days.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find the initial moles of each, halve them once per half-life, then multiply by N_A. // 📝 Solution: $N_{0A} \;=\; \frac{320}{16} \;=\; 20\;\text{mol},\; N_A \;=\; \frac{20}{2^2} \;=\; 5$ and $N_{0B} \;=\; \frac{320}{32} \;=\; 10\;\text{mol},\; N_B \;=\; \frac{10}{2^4} \;=\; 0.625$ $\implies\; N \;=\; 5.625 \times 6.023 \times 10^{23} \;=\; 3.38 \times 10^{24}$

questions.text: A star has $100\%$ helium composition. It starts to convert three $ {}^{4}He $ into one $ {}^{12}C $ via triple alpha process as $ {}^{4}He \;+\; {}^{4}He \;+\; {}^{4}He \;\to\; {}^{12}C \;+\; Q $. The mass of the star is $2.0 \times 10^{32}\;\text{kg}$ and it generates energy at the rate of $5.808 \times 10^{30}\;\text{W}$. The rate of converting these $ {}^{4}He $ to $ {}^{12}C $ is $n \times 10^{42}\;\text{s}^{-1}$, where $n$ is ______. [ Take, mass of $ {}^{4}He \;=\; 4.0026\,u $, mass of $ {}^{12}C \;=\; 12\,u $ ]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Reactions per second = Power / Q, and each reaction consumes 3 helium nuclei. // 📝 Solution: $Q \;=\; \left( 3 \times 4.0026 - 12 \right) \times 931.5 \;\approx\; 7.266\;\text{MeV}$ $\implies\; \frac{N}{t} \;=\; \frac{5.808 \times 10^{30}}{7.266 \times 10^{6} \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}} \;=\; 5 \times 10^{42}$ $\implies\; \text{rate of He converted} \;=\; 3 \times 5 \times 10^{42} \;=\; 15 \times 10^{42} \;\implies\; n \;=\; 15$

questions.text: If $M_o$ is the mass of isotope $ {}_{5}^{12}B $, $M_P$ and $M_n$ are the masses of proton and neutron, then nuclear binding energy of isotope is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: B.E. = (Zm_p + (A−Z)m_n − M_nucleus) c². // 📝 Solution: $Z \;=\; 5,\; N \;=\; 12 - 5 \;=\; 7$ $\implies\; B.E. \;=\; \left( 5M_p \;+\; 7M_n \;-\; M_o \right) C^2$

questions.text: In a nuclear fission reaction of an isotope of mass $M$, three similar daughter nuclei of same mass are formed. The speed of a daughter nuclei in terms of mass defect $\Delta M$ will be :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Energy released ΔMc² equals the total kinetic energy of the three equal-mass fragments. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta M c^2 \;=\; 3 \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{M}{3} \times V^2 \;=\; \frac{1}{2} M V^2$ $\implies\; V \;=\; c\sqrt{\frac{2\Delta M}{M}}$

questions.text: The mass number of nucleus having radius equal to half of the radius of nucleus with mass number $192$ is:
A free neutron decays into a proton but a free proton does not decay into neutron. This is because

options.text: neutron is a composite particle made of a proton and an electron
neutron has larger rest mass than proton

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A decay is possible only if the rest mass of the parent exceeds that of the products (Q > 0). // 📝 Solution: $m_n \;>\; m_p \;\implies\; n \;\to\; p \;+\; e^- \;+\; \bar{\nu}$ is energetically allowed $\implies$ a free proton would need energy supplied to convert into a neutron $\implies$ Option D

questions.text: The ratio of the density of oxygen nucleus $\left( {}_{8}^{16}O \right)$ and helium nucleus $\left( {}_{2}^{4}He \right)$ is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Nuclear density is independent of the mass number because R = R₀A^(1/3). // 📝 Solution: $\rho \;=\; \frac{A\,u}{\frac{4}{3}\pi R_0^3 A} \;=\; \frac{3u}{4\pi R_0^3}$ $\implies\; \rho_O \;:\; \rho_{He} \;=\; 1 : 1$

questions.text: A physical quantity $Q$ is related to four observables $a,\,b,\,c,\,d$ as follows : $Q\;=\;\frac{ab^4}{cd}$, where $a\;=\;\left(60\;\pm\;3\right)\text{Pa}$, $b\;=\;\left(20\;\pm\;0.1\right)\text{m}$, $c\;=\;\left(40\;\pm\;0.2\right)\text{Nsm}^{-2}$ and $d\;=\;\left(50\;\pm\;0.1\right)\text{m}$, then the percentage error in $Q$ is $\frac{x}{1000}$, where $x\;=$ ________.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Fractional error is the sum of power-weighted fractional errors of each observable. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{\Delta Q}{Q}\;\times\;100\;=\;\left[\frac{\Delta a}{a}\;+\;4\frac{\Delta b}{b}\;+\;\frac{\Delta c}{c}\;+\;\frac{\Delta d}{d}\right]\times 100$ $=\;\left[\frac{3}{60}\;+\;4\left(\frac{0.1}{20}\right)\;+\;\frac{0.2}{40}\;+\;\frac{0.1}{50}\right]\times 100\;=\;7.7\;=\;\frac{x}{1000}\;\implies\;x\;=\;7700$

questions.text: The maximum percentage error in the measurement of density of a wire is [Given, mass of wire $=\;\left(0.60\;\pm\;0.003\right)\text{g}$, radius of wire $=\;\left(0.50\;\pm\;0.01\right)\text{cm}$, length of wire $=\;\left(10.00\;\pm\;0.05\right)\text{cm}$]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Density $\rho\;=\;\frac{m}{\pi R^2 \ell}$, so $\frac{\Delta\rho}{\rho}\;=\;\frac{\Delta m}{m}\;+\;\frac{2\Delta R}{R}\;+\;\frac{\Delta \ell}{\ell}$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{\Delta\rho}{\rho}\;=\;\frac{0.003}{0.6}\;+\;\frac{2\left(0.01\right)}{0.5}\;+\;\frac{0.05}{10}\;=\;0.005\;+\;0.04\;+\;0.005\;=\;0.05\;\implies\;5\%$

questions.text: For an experimental expression $y\;=\;\frac{32.3\;\times\;1125}{27.4}$, where all the digits are significant. Then to report the value of $y$ we should write
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A product or quotient is reported with the least number of significant figures among the inputs. // 📝 Solution: $y\;=\;\frac{32.3\;\times\;1125}{27.4}\;=\;1326.18$ $\implies$ least significant figures are 3 (from $32.3$ and $27.4$) $\implies\;y\;=\;1330$

questions.text: The energy of a system is given as $E\left(t\right)\;=\;\alpha^3 e^{-\beta t}$, where $t$ is the time and $\beta\;=\;0.3\;\text{s}^{-1}$. The errors in the measurement of $\alpha$ and $t$ are $1.2\%$ and $1.6\%$, respectively. At $t\;=\;5\;\text{s}$, maximum percentage error in the energy is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Take $\ln$ of $E$ and differentiate to get the fractional error. // 📝 Solution: $\ln E\;=\;3\ln\alpha\;-\;\beta t\;\implies\;\frac{\Delta E}{E}\;=\;3\frac{\Delta\alpha}{\alpha}\;+\;\beta t\frac{\Delta t}{t}$ $=\;3\left(1.2\%\right)\;+\;\left(0.3\;\times\;5\;\times\;1.6\right)\%\;=\;3.6\%\;+\;2.4\%\;=\;6\%$

questions.text: Two particles are located at equal distance from origin. The position vectors of those are represented by $\vec{A}\;=\;2\hat{i}\;+\;3n\hat{j}\;+\;2\hat{k}$ and $\vec{B}\;=\;2\hat{i}\;-\;2\hat{j}\;+\;4p\hat{k}$, respectively. If both the vectors are at right angle to each other, the value of $n^{-1}$ is _____.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Perpendicular vectors have zero dot product, and equal distance from origin means equal magnitudes. // 📝 Solution: $\vec{A}\cdot\vec{B}\;=\;0\;\implies\;4\;-\;6n\;+\;8p\;=\;0$ and $\left\lvert\vec{A}\right\rvert\;=\;\left\lvert\vec{B}\right\rvert\;\implies\;9n^2\;=\;16p^2\;\implies\;p\;=\;-\frac{3n}{4}$ $\implies\;4\;-\;12n\;=\;0\;\implies\;n\;=\;\frac{1}{3}\;\implies\;n^{-1}\;=\;3$

questions.text: The magnetic moment of a bar magnet is $0.5\;\text{A}\,\text{m}^{2}$. It is suspended in a uniform magnetic field of $8\times10^{-2}\;\text{T}$. The work done in rotating it from its most stable to most unstable position is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $U=-\vec{M}\cdot\vec{B}=-MB\cos\theta$ and work done equals the change in potential energy // 📝 Solution: $U_{\text{stable}}=-MB\cos0^{\circ}=-MB\;\implies\;U_{\text{unstable}}=-MB\cos180^{\circ}=+MB$ $\;\implies\;$ $W=\Delta U=2MB=2(0.5)(8\times10^{-2})=8\times10^{-2}\;\text{J}$
questions.topic: Work done on a magnetic dipole in a uniform field

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I (Y vs X): (A) $Y=$ magnetic susceptibility, $X=$ magnetising field; (B) $Y=$ magnetic field, $X=$ distance from centre of a current carrying wire for $x<a$ ($a$ = radius of wire); (C) $Y=$ magnetic field, $X=$ distance from centre of a current carrying wire for $x>a$; (D) $Y=$ magnetic field inside solenoid, $X=$ distance from centre. List-II: Shape of Graph (I) to (IV) [FIGURE]. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Match each graph with its physical variation: constant, linear through origin, $\propto\frac{1}{x}$, or uniform then falling // 📝 Solution: (A) $\chi_{m}$ is independent of $H$ $\implies$ horizontal line (III); (B) $B=\frac{\mu_{0}ix}{2\pi a^{2}}$ for $x<a$ $\implies$ straight line through origin (I); (C) $B=\frac{\mu_{0}i}{2\pi x}$ for $x>a$ $\implies$ decreasing curve (IV); (D) $B$ is uniform inside the solenoid and falls outside $\implies$ (II) $\implies$ [FIGURE] Option (4) matches
questions.topic: Graphs of magnetic quantities versus distance and field

questions.text: A ceiling fan having 3 blades of length $80\;\text{cm}$ each is rotating with an angular velocity of $1200\;\text{rpm}$. The magnetic field of earth in that region is $0.5\;\text{G}$ and angle of dip is $30^{\circ}$. The emf induced across the blades is $N\pi\times10^{-5}\;\text{V}$. The value of $N$ is ______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Motional emf across a rotating blade is $\varepsilon=\frac{1}{2}B_{V}\omega\ell^{2}$ with $B_{V}=B\sin\delta$ // 📝 Solution: $B_{V}=0.5\times10^{-4}\sin30^{\circ}=2.5\times10^{-5}\;\text{T}$ $\;\implies\;$ $\omega=2\pi\times\frac{1200}{60}=40\pi\;\text{rad/s}$ $\;\implies\;$ $\varepsilon=\frac{1}{2}\left(2.5\times10^{-5}\right)\left(40\pi\right)\left(0.8\right)^{2}=32\pi\times10^{-5}\;\text{V}$ $\;\implies\;$ $N=32$
questions.topic: Motional emf in rotating blades of a fan

questions.text: The horizontal component of earth's magnetic field at a place is $3.5\times10^{-5}\;\text{T}$. A very long straight conductor carrying current of $\sqrt{2}\;\text{A}$ in the direction from South-East to North-West is placed. The force per unit length experienced by the conductor is ______ $\times10^{-6}\;\text{N/m}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Force per unit length on a straight conductor is $\frac{F}{\ell}=iB\sin\theta$, where $\theta$ is the angle between current and field // 📝 Solution: The SE-NW current makes $\theta=45^{\circ}$ with the horizontal component $B_{H}$ $\implies$ $\frac{F}{\ell}=\sqrt{2}\times3.5\times10^{-5}\times\sin45^{\circ}=\sqrt{2}\times3.5\times10^{-5}\times\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ $\;\implies\;$ $\frac{F}{\ell}=3.5\times10^{-5}\;\text{N/m}=35\times10^{-6}\;\text{N/m}$
questions.topic: Force on a current carrying conductor in Earth's field

questions.text: Paramagnetic substances: A. align themselves along the directions of external magnetic field. B. attract strongly towards external magnetic field. C. has susceptibility little more than zero. D. move from a region of strong magnetic field to weak magnetic field. Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Paramagnetic materials have a small positive susceptibility, are weakly attracted, and move from weak to strong field // 📝 Solution: A: aligns along $\vec{B}$ $\implies$ true; B: attraction is weak, not strong $\implies$ false; C: $0<\chi_{m}\ll1$ $\implies$ true; D: moves from weak to strong field $\implies$ false $\implies$ A, C only

questions.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Consider a ferromagnetic material. Assertion (A): The individual atoms in a ferromagnetic material possess a magnetic dipole moment and interact with one another in such a way that they spontaneously align themselves forming domains. Reason (R): At high enough temperature, the domain structure of ferromagnetic material disintegrates. Thus, magnetization will disappear at high enough temperature known as Curie temperature. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Domains form through exchange interaction below the Curie temperature $T_{C}$, and thermal agitation destroys them above $T_{C}$ // 📝 Solution: (A) describes spontaneous domain formation $\implies$ true; (R) describes domain loss above $T_{C}$ $\implies$ true; (R) does not explain why domains form $\implies$ Option (2)

questions.text: The coercivity of a magnet is $5\times10^{3}\;\text{A/m}$. The amount of current required to be passed in a solenoid of length $30\;\text{cm}$ and number of turns $150$, so that the magnet gets demagnetised when inside the solenoid, is ______ A.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For a long solenoid $H=nI$ with $n=\frac{N}{L}$, and demagnetisation requires $H=H_{c}$ // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] $n=\frac{150}{0.3}=500\;\text{turns/m}$ $\;\implies\;$ $I=\frac{H_{c}}{n}=\frac{5\times10^{3}}{500}=10\;\text{A}$
questions.topic: Coercivity and demagnetisation in a solenoid

questions.text: A man carrying a monkey on his shoulder does cycling smoothly on a circular track of radius $9\;\mathrm{m}$ and completes $120$ revolutions in $3$ minutes. The magnitude of centripetal acceleration of monkey is (in $\mathrm{m/s^{2}}$):
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Centripetal acceleration is $a_c=\omega^{2}R$ with $\omega=\frac{\theta}{t}$. // 📝 Solution: $\omega=\frac{120\times2\pi}{3\times60}=\frac{4\pi}{3}\;\mathrm{rad\,s^{-1}}$ $\;\implies\;a_c=\left(\frac{4\pi}{3}\right)^{2}(9)=16\pi^{2}\;\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$

questions.text: A stone is projected at angle $30^\circ$ to the horizontal. The ratio of kinetic energy of the stone at point of projection to its kinetic energy at the highest point of flight will be:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: At the highest point only the horizontal velocity $u\cos\theta$ remains. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{KE_{\text{proj}}}{KE_{\text{top}}}=\frac{\frac{1}{2}mu^{2}}{\frac{1}{2}m(u\cos30^\circ)^{2}}=\frac{1}{\cos^{2}30^\circ}\;\implies\;\frac{1}{\frac{3}{4}}=\frac{4}{3}$

questions.text: A child stands on the edge of a cliff $10\;\mathrm{m}$ above the ground and throws a stone horizontally with an initial speed of $5\;\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. Neglecting air resistance, the speed with which the stone hits the ground will be ____ $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ (given $g=10\;\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$).
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use the vertical velocity from $v_y^{2}=2gh$ and combine it with the horizontal velocity. // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] $v_y=\sqrt{2gh}=\sqrt{200}\;\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ $\;\implies\;v=\sqrt{v_x^{2}+v_y^{2}}=\sqrt{25+200}=\sqrt{225}=15\;\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$

questions.text: A body of mass $M$ thrown horizontally with velocity $v$ from the top of the tower of height $H$ touches the ground at a distance of $100\;\mathrm{m}$ from the foot of the tower. A body of mass $2M$ thrown at a velocity $\frac{v}{2}$ from the top of the tower of height $4H$ will touch the ground at a distance of ____ m.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Horizontal range of a horizontal projection is $x=v\sqrt{\frac{2H}{g}}$, independent of mass. // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] $100=v\sqrt{\frac{2H}{g}}$ $\;\implies\;x=\frac{v}{2}\sqrt{\frac{2(4H)}{g}}=v\sqrt{\frac{2H}{g}}=100\;\mathrm{m}$

questions.text: A particle is projected with initial speed $u$ from ground. At the highest point of its motion, the speed of the projectile is $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}u$. The time of flight of the projectile is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: At the highest point speed equals the horizontal component $u\cos\theta$, and $T=\frac{2u\sin\theta}{g}$. // 📝 Solution: $u\cos\theta=\frac{\sqrt{3}u}{2}\;\implies\;\cos\theta=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\;\implies\;\theta=30^\circ$ $\;\implies\;T=\frac{2u\sin30^\circ}{g}=\frac{u}{g}$

questions.text: Two objects are projected with same velocity $u$ at different angles $\alpha$ and $\beta$ with the horizontal. If $\alpha+\beta=90^\circ$, the ratio of horizontal range of the first object to the 2nd object will be:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Horizontal range is $R=\frac{u^{2}\sin2\theta}{g}$, and complementary angles give equal $\sin2\theta$. // 📝 Solution: $R_1=\frac{u^{2}\sin2\alpha}{g}$, $R_2=\frac{u^{2}\sin2\beta}{g}$ $\;\implies\;\beta=90^\circ-\alpha$ $\;\implies\;\sin2\beta=\sin(180^\circ-2\alpha)=\sin2\alpha$ $\;\implies\;\frac{R_1}{R_2}=1:1$

questions.text: The position vector of a moving body at any instant of time is given as $\vec{r}\;=\;\left(5t^2\hat{i}\;-\;5t\hat{j}\right)\text{m}$. The magnitude and direction of velocity at $t\;=\;2\;\text{s}$ is,

options.text: $5\sqrt{15}\;\text{m/s}$, making an angle of $\tan^{-1}4$ with -ve $Y$ axis
$5\sqrt{15}\;\text{m/s}$, making an angle of $\tan^{-1}4$ with +ve $X$ axis
$5\sqrt{17}\;\text{m/s}$, making an angle of $\tan^{-1}4$ with +ve $X$ axis
$5\sqrt{17}\;\text{m/s}$, making an angle of $\tan^{-1}4$ with -ve $Y$ axis

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Differentiate position to get velocity. // 📝 Solution: $\vec{v}\;=\;10t\hat{i}\;-\;5\hat{j}\;\implies\;\vec{v}\left(2\right)\;=\;20\hat{i}\;-\;5\hat{j}$, $\left\lvert\vec{v}\right\rvert\;=\;\sqrt{425}\;=\;5\sqrt{17}$, $\tan\theta\;=\;\frac{20}{5}\;=\;4$ measured from -ve $Y$ axis

questions.text: The maximum height reached by a projectile is $64\;\mathrm{m}$. If the initial velocity is halved, the new maximum height of the projectile is ____ m.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Maximum height is $H=\frac{u^{2}\sin^{2}\theta}{2g}$, so $H\propto u^{2}$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{H_{\text{new}}}{H_{\text{old}}}=\frac{(u/2)^{2}}{u^{2}}=\frac{1}{4}\;\implies\;H_{\text{new}}=\frac{64}{4}=16\;\mathrm{m}$

questions.text: A ball of mass $100\;\text{g}$ is projected with velocity $20\;\text{m/s}$ at $60^\circ$ with horizontal. The decrease in kinetic energy of the ball during the motion from point of projection to highest point is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: At the highest point only the horizontal component $v\cos 60^\circ$ remains. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta K\;=\;\frac{1}{2}mv^2\left(1\;-\;\cos^2 60^\circ\right)\;=\;\frac{3}{8}\left(0.1\right)\left(400\right)\;=\;15\;\text{J}$

questions.text: A particle of mass $100\;\mathrm{g}$ is projected at time $t=0$ with a speed $20\;\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ at an angle $45^\circ$ to the horizontal as given in the figure [FIGURE]. The magnitude of the angular momentum of the particle about the starting point at time $t=2\;\mathrm{s}$ is found to be $\sqrt{K}\;\mathrm{kg\,m^{2}/s}$. The value of $K$ is ____. (Take $g=10\;\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Torque of gravity about the launch point is $\tau=mg\,x=mg\,v_x t$, so $\Delta L=\int\tau\,dt$. // 📝 Solution: $v_x=20\cos45^\circ=10\sqrt{2}\;\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ $\;\implies\;L=\int_{0}^{2}mg\,(v_x t)\,dt=\frac{mg\,v_x\,t^{2}}{2}\Big\rvert_{t=2}$ $\;\implies\;L=\frac{(0.1)(10)(10\sqrt{2})(4)}{2}=20\sqrt{2}=\sqrt{800}\;\implies\;K=800$

questions.text: A particle is projected at an angle of $30^\circ$ from horizontal at a speed of $60\;\text{m/s}$. The height traversed by the particle in the first second is $h_0$ and height traversed in the last second, before it reaches the maximum height, is $h_1$. The ratio $h_0\;:\;h_1$ is _________ [Take, $g\;=\;10\;\text{m/s}^2$]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $s\;=\;ut\;-\;\frac{1}{2}gt^2$ for the first second, and symmetry (equivalent to the first second of free fall) for the last second. // 📝 Solution: $u_y\;=\;30$, $h_0\;=\;30\;-\;5\;=\;25\;\text{m}$; time to top $=\;3\;\text{s}$, $h_1\;=\;\frac{1}{2}\left(10\right)\left(1\right)^2\;=\;5\;\text{m}\;\implies\;\frac{h_0}{h_1}\;=\;5$

questions.text: A particle of mass $m$ projected with a velocity $u$ making an angle of $30^\circ$ with the horizontal. The magnitude of angular momentum of the projectile about the point of projection when the particle is at its maximum height $h$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: At the top only horizontal velocity remains, so $L=m\,v_x\,h$. // 📝 Solution: $v_x=u\cos30^\circ=\frac{\sqrt{3}u}{2}$ and $h=\frac{u^{2}\sin^{2}30^\circ}{2g}=\frac{u^{2}}{8g}$ $\;\implies\;L=m\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}u}{2}\right)\left(\frac{u^{2}}{8g}\right)=\frac{\sqrt{3}\,mu^{3}}{16g}$

questions.text: A body starts falling freely from height $H$ and hits an inclined plane in its path at height $h$. As a result of this perfectly elastic impact, the direction of the velocity of the body becomes horizontal. The value of $\frac{H}{h}$ for which the body will take the maximum time to reach the ground is ____
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Total time is the sum of the two segment times, so set $\frac{dT}{dh}=0$. // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] $T=\sqrt{\frac{2h}{g}}+\sqrt{\frac{2(H-h)}{g}}$ $\;\implies\;\frac{dT}{dh}=0\;\implies\;\sqrt{H-h}=\sqrt{h}$ $\;\implies\;h=\frac{H}{2}\;\implies\;\frac{H}{h}=2$
questions.topic: Free fall with elastic inclined impact

questions.text: The angle of projection for a projectile to have same horizontal range and maximum height is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Equate $R=\frac{u^{2}\sin2\theta}{g}$ with $H=\frac{u^{2}\sin^{2}\theta}{2g}$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{u^{2}\sin2\theta}{g}=\frac{u^{2}\sin^{2}\theta}{2g}\;\implies\;4\sin\theta\cos\theta=\sin^{2}\theta\;\implies\;\tan\theta=4$

questions.text: A river of width $200\;\mathrm{m}$ is flowing from west to east with a speed of $18\;\mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}$. A boat, moving with speed of $36\;\mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}$ in still water, is made to travel one-round trip (bank to bank of the river). Minimum time taken by the boat for this journey and also the displacement along the river bank are ____ and ____ respectively.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For minimum crossing time, the boat heads perpendicular to the flow, so $t=\frac{d}{v_b}$. // 📝 Solution: $v_r=5\;\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $v_b=10\;\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ $\;\implies\;t=\frac{200}{10}=20\;\mathrm{s}$ $\;\implies\;T=2t=40\;\mathrm{s}$ $\;\implies\;\text{drift}=2(v_r t)=2(100)=200\;\mathrm{m}$

questions.text: Two projectiles are fired with same initial speed from same point on ground at angles of $\left(45^\circ\;-\;\alpha\right)$ and $\left(45^\circ\;+\;\alpha\right)$, respectively, with the horizontal direction. The ratio of their maximum heights attained is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $H_{max}\;=\;\frac{u^2\sin^2\theta}{2g}$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{H_1}{H_2}\;=\;\frac{\sin^2\left(45^\circ-\alpha\right)}{\sin^2\left(45^\circ+\alpha\right)}\;=\;\frac{\left(\cos\alpha-\sin\alpha\right)^2}{\left(\cos\alpha+\sin\alpha\right)^2}\;=\;\frac{1-\sin 2\alpha}{1+\sin 2\alpha}$

questions.text: A particle is projected with velocity $u$ so that its horizontal range is three times the maximum height attained by it. The horizontal range of the projectile is given as $\frac{nu^{2}}{25g}$, where the value of $n$ is: (Given $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $R = \frac{u^{2}\sin 2\theta}{g}$ and $H_{max} = \frac{u^{2}\sin^{2}\theta}{2g}$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{u^{2}\sin 2\theta}{g} = \frac{3u^{2}\sin^{2}\theta}{2g} \implies \tan\theta = \frac{4}{3} \implies R = \frac{24u^{2}}{25g} \implies n = 24$

questions.text: A river is flowing from west to east direction with a speed of $9\ \text{km h}^{-1}$. A boat capable of moving at a maximum speed of $27\ \text{km h}^{-1}$ in still water crosses the river in half a minute, while moving with maximum speed at an angle of $150^{\circ}$ to the direction of river flow. The width of the river is: [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Only the component of boat velocity perpendicular to the bank decides the crossing time. // 📝 Solution: $v_\perp = 27\cos 60^{\circ} = 13.5\ \text{km h}^{-1} = 3.75\ \text{m/s} \implies w = v_\perp t = 3.75 \times 30 = 112.5\ \text{m}$

questions.text: A particle moving in a circle of radius $R$ with uniform speed takes time $T$ to complete one revolution. If this particle is projected with the same speed at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal, the maximum height attained by it is equal to $4R$. The angle of projection $\theta$ is then given by:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $v=\frac{2\pi R}{T}$ and $H=\frac{v^{2}\sin^{2}\theta}{2g}$. // 📝 Solution: $4R=\frac{4\pi^{2}R^{2}\sin^{2}\theta}{2gT^{2}}\;\implies\;\sin^{2}\theta=\frac{2gT^{2}}{\pi^{2}R}\;\implies\;\theta=\sin^{-1}\left\lbrack\left(\frac{2gT^{2}}{\pi^{2}R}\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\right\rbrack$

questions.text: If the radius of curvature of the path of two particles of same mass are in the ratio $3:4$, then in order to have constant centripetal force, their velocities will be in the ratio of:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Centripetal force is $F=\frac{mv^{2}}{r}$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{m_1v_1^{2}}{r_1}=\frac{m_2v_2^{2}}{r_2}$ with $m_1=m_2$ $\;\implies\;\frac{v_1}{v_2}=\sqrt{\frac{r_1}{r_2}}=\sqrt{\frac{3}{4}}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

questions.text: Two projectiles are fired from ground with the same initial speed from the same point at angles $(45^{\circ} + \alpha)$ and $(45^{\circ} - \alpha)$ with the horizontal direction. The ratio of their times of flight is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Time of flight $T = \frac{2u\sin\theta}{g}$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{T_1}{T_2} = \frac{\sin(45^{\circ}+\alpha)}{\sin(45^{\circ}-\alpha)} = \frac{\cos\alpha + \sin\alpha}{\cos\alpha - \sin\alpha} = \frac{1+\tan\alpha}{1-\tan\alpha}$

questions.text: An object is projected with kinetic energy $K$ from a point $A$ at an angle $60^\circ$ with the horizontal. The ratio of the difference in kinetic energies at points $B$ and $C$ to that at point $A$ (see figure), in the absence of air friction is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: At the highest point $v=v\cos\theta$, and KE at the same level as projection is unchanged. // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] $KE_B=K\cos^{2}60^\circ=\frac{K}{4}$ and $KE_C=K$ $\;\implies\;\frac{\left\lvert KE_B-KE_C\right\rvert}{K}=\frac{\frac{3K}{4}}{K}=\frac{3}{4}$

questions.text: Projectiles A and B are thrown at angles of $45^\circ$ and $60^\circ$ with vertical respectively from top of a $400\;\mathrm{m}$ high tower. If their ranges and times of flight are same, the ratio of their speeds of projection $v_A:v_B$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Equal flight time fixes the vertical components, and equal range fixes the horizontal components. // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] Equal time $\implies v_A\cos45^\circ=v_B\cos60^\circ$; equal range $\implies v_A\sin45^\circ=v_B\sin60^\circ$, which cannot both hold. Note: official NTA key had no correct option; answer as per provided key $1:1$
questions.topic: Projectile from height with equal range and time

questions.text: Two balls with the same mass and initial velocity are projected at different angles such that the maximum height reached by the first ball is $8$ times that of the second ball. $T_1$ and $T_2$ are the total flying times of the first and second ball, respectively. The ratio $T_1 : T_2$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $H \propto \sin^{2}\theta$ and $T \propto \sin\theta$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{H_1}{H_2} = 8 \implies \frac{\sin^{2}\theta_1}{\sin^{2}\theta_2} = 8 \implies \frac{\sin\theta_1}{\sin\theta_2} = 2\sqrt{2} \implies \frac{T_1}{T_2} = 2\sqrt{2}$

questions.text: The co-ordinates of a particle moving in $x-y$ plane are given by $x=2+4t$ and $y=3t+8t^{2}$. The motion of the particle is:

options.text: Uniformly accelerated having motion along a parabolic path.
Uniform motion along a straight line.
Uniformly accelerated having motion along a straight line.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find $v_x,v_y,a_x,a_y$ and eliminate $t$ to identify the path. // 📝 Solution: $v_x=4$, $a_x=0$ and $v_y=3+16t$, $a_y=16$ $\;\implies\;$ constant acceleration $a=16\;\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$ $\;\implies\;t=\frac{x-2}{4}$ gives $y=3\left(\frac{x-2}{4}\right)+8\left(\frac{x-2}{4}\right)^{2}$, a parabola

questions.text: The speed of a swimmer is $4\;\mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}$ in still water. If the swimmer makes his strokes normal to the flow of river of width $1\;\mathrm{km}$, he reaches a point $750\;\mathrm{m}$ down the stream on the opposite bank. The speed of the river water is ____ $\mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Crossing time is $t=\frac{\text{width}}{v_{\text{swimmer}}}$ and drift $=v_{\text{river}}\times t$. // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] $t=\frac{1\;\mathrm{km}}{4\;\mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}}=0.25\;\mathrm{h}$ $\;\implies\;v_{\text{river}}=\frac{0.75\;\mathrm{km}}{0.25\;\mathrm{h}}=3\;\mathrm{km\,h^{-1}}$

questions.text: A projectile is thrown upward at an angle $60^\circ$ with the horizontal. The speed of the projectile is $20\;\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ when its direction of motion is $45^\circ$ with the horizontal. The initial speed of the projectile is ____ $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Horizontal velocity remains constant throughout projectile motion. // 📝 Solution: $u\cos60^\circ=20\cos45^\circ\;\implies\;\frac{u}{2}=\frac{20}{\sqrt{2}}\;\implies\;u=20\sqrt{2}\;\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$

questions.text: A ball rolls off the top of a stairway with horizontal velocity $u$. The steps are $0.1\;\mathrm{m}$ high and $0.1\;\mathrm{m}$ wide. The minimum velocity $u$ with which that ball just hits the step $5$ of the stairway will be $\sqrt{x}\;\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ where $x=$ ____ [use $g=10\;\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$].
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The ball just clears the corner of step 4, so use $R=ut$ and $h=\frac{1}{2}gt^{2}$. // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] Corner of step 4 at $R=0.4\;\mathrm{m}$, $h=0.4\;\mathrm{m}$ $\;\implies\;0.4=\frac{1}{2}(10)t^{2}\;\implies\;t=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{5}\;\mathrm{s}$ $\;\implies\;u=\frac{0.4}{\sqrt{2}/5}=\sqrt{2}\;\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ $\;\implies\;x=2$

questions.text: The maximum vertical height to which a man can throw a ball is $136\;\mathrm{m}$. The maximum horizontal distance up to which he can throw the same ball is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For the same projection speed, $H_{\max}=\frac{v^{2}}{2g}$ and $R_{\max}=\frac{v^{2}}{g}$. // 📝 Solution: $H_{\max}=\frac{v^{2}}{2g}=136\;\mathrm{m}\;\implies\;R_{\max}=\frac{v^{2}}{g}=2H_{\max}\;\implies\;R_{\max}=2(136)=272\;\mathrm{m}$
