questions.text: A boy throws a ball into air at $45^\circ$ from the horizontal to land it on a roof of a building of height $H$. If the ball attains maximum height in $2\;\mathrm{s}$ and lands on the building in $3\;\mathrm{s}$ after launch, then value of $H$ is ____ m. ($g=10\;\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Time to maximum height gives $u_y=gt_{\text{top}}$, and $y=u_yt-\frac{1}{2}gt^{2}$. // 📝 Solution: $u_y=10(2)=20\;\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ $\;\implies\;H=20(3)-\frac{1}{2}(10)(3)^{2}=60-45=15\;\mathrm{m}$

questions.text: The angle of projection of a particle is measured from the vertical axis as $\phi$ and the maximum height reached by the particle is $h_m$. Here $h_m$ as a function of $\phi$ can be represented as: Graph (1): [FIGURE], Graph (2): [FIGURE], Graph (3): [FIGURE], Graph (4): [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $h_m = \frac{u^{2}\cos^{2}\phi}{2g}$ when $\phi$ is measured from the vertical. // 📝 Solution: $h_m \propto \cos^{2}\phi \implies$ maximum at $\phi = 0$, zero at $\phi = 90^{\circ}$, monotonically decreasing $\implies$ Graph (3)

questions.text: Two bodies are projected from ground with same speeds $40\;\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ at two different angles with respect to horizontal. The bodies were found to have same range. If one of the bodies was projected at an angle of $60^\circ$ with horizontal, then sum of the maximum heights attained by the two projectiles is ____ m. (Given $g=10\;\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Equal ranges with the same speed require complementary angles, $\theta_2=90^\circ-\theta_1$. // 📝 Solution: $\theta_2=30^\circ$ $\;\implies\;H_1=\frac{u^{2}\sin^{2}60^\circ}{2g}=\frac{1600\cdot\frac{3}{4}}{20}=60\;\mathrm{m}$ and $H_2=\frac{u^{2}\sin^{2}30^\circ}{2g}=\frac{1600\cdot\frac{1}{4}}{20}=20\;\mathrm{m}$ $\;\implies\;H_1+H_2=80\;\mathrm{m}$

questions.text: Two coils have mutual inductance $0.002 \; \text{H}$. The current changes in the first coil according to the relation $i \; = \; i_0 \sin \omega t$, where $i_0 \; = \; 5 \; \text{A}$ and $\omega \; = \; 50\pi \; \text{rad/s}$. The maximum value of emf in the second coil is $\frac{\pi}{\alpha} \; \text{V}$. The value of $\alpha$ is _______
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Induced emf in the secondary coil is $\varepsilon \; = \; -M \frac{di}{dt} \; = \; -M i_0 \omega \cos \omega t$. // 📝 Solution: Maximum induced emf is $\varepsilon_{\text{max}} \; = \; M i_0 \omega \; = \; 0.002 \; \times \; 5 \; \times \; 50\pi \; = \; 0.5\pi \; = \; \frac{\pi}{2} \; \text{V} \implies \alpha \; = \; 2$.

questions.text: A coil of $200$ turns and area $0.20 \; \text{m}^2$ is rotated at half a revolution per second and is placed in uniform magnetic field of $0.01 \; \text{T}$ perpendicular to axis of rotation of the coil. The maximum voltage generated in the coil is $\frac{2\pi}{\beta} \; \text{volt}$. The value of $\beta$ is _______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Maximum induced emf in a rotating coil is $\varepsilon_{\text{max}} \; = \; N B A \omega$, where $\omega \; = \; 2\pi f$. // 📝 Solution: Given $N \; = \; 200$, $A \; = \; 0.20 \; \text{m}^2$, $B \; = \; 0.01 \; \text{T}$, and $f \; = \; 0.5 \; \text{rev/s} \implies \omega \; = \; 2\pi \left(0.5\right) \; = \; \pi \; \text{rad/s} \implies \varepsilon_{\text{max}} \; = \; N B A \omega \; = \; 200 \; \times \; 0.01 \; \times \; 0.20 \; \times \; \pi \; = \; \frac{2\pi}{5} \; \text{V} \implies \beta \; = \; 5$.

questions.text: $XPQY$ is a vertical smooth long loop having a total resistance $R$ where $PX$ is parallel to $QY$ and separation between them is $l$. A constant magnetic field $B$ perpendicular to the plane of the loop exists in the entire space. A rod $CD$ of length $L \left(L \; > \; l\right)$ and mass $m$ is made to slide down from rest under the gravity as shown in figure. The terminal speed acquired by the rod is _______ $\text{m/s}$. $\left(g \; = \; \text{acceleration due to gravity}\right)$ [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: At terminal velocity, downward gravitational force $mg$ balances the upward magnetic force $F_m \; = \; B I l \; = \; \frac{B^2 l^2 v_t}{R}$ acting on the active length $l$ between the rails. // 📝 Solution: Active length of the rod in the circuit between rails $PX$ and $QY$ is $l \implies \varepsilon \; = \; B l v$ and $I \; = \; \frac{B l v}{R}$. At terminal velocity $v_t$, net force is zero: $mg \; = \; B I l \; = \; \frac{B^2 l^2 v_t}{R} \implies v_t \; = \; \frac{mgR}{B^2 l^2}$.

questions.text: The current in an inductor is given by $I \; = \; \left(3t \; + \; 8\right)$ where $t$ is in second. The magnitude of induced emf produced in the inductor is $12 \; \text{mV}$. The self-inductance of the inductor _______ $\text{mH}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use the self-induced emf formula $\left\lvert \varepsilon \right\rvert \; = \; L \left\lvert \frac{dI}{dt} \right\rvert$. // 📝 Solution: Given $I \; = \; 3t \; + \; 8 \implies \frac{dI}{dt} \; = \; 3 \; \text{A/s} \implies \left\lvert \varepsilon \right\rvert \; = \; L \left\lvert \frac{dI}{dt} \right\rvert \implies 12 \; \times \; 10^{-3} \; = \; L \; \times \; 3 \implies L \; = \; 4 \; \times \; 10^{-3} \; \text{H} \; = \; 4 \; \text{mH}$.

questions.text: A $20 \; \text{m}$ long uniform copper wire held horizontally is allowed to fall under the gravity $\left(g \; = \; 10 \; \text{m/s}^2\right)$ through a uniform horizontal magnetic field of $0.5 \; \text{Gauss}$ perpendicular to the length of the wire. The induced EMF across the wire when it travells a vertical distance of $200 \; \text{m}$ is _______ $\text{mV}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find velocity after falling height $h$ using $v \; = \; \sqrt{2gh}$ and then substitute into $\varepsilon \; = \; B L v$. // 📝 Solution: Velocity after falling $h \; = \; 200 \; \text{m}$ is $v \; = \; \sqrt{2gh} \; = \; \sqrt{2 \; \times \; 10 \; \times \; 200} \; = \; 20\sqrt{10} \; \text{m/s}$. Given $B \; = \; 0.5 \; \text{Gauss} \; = \; 0.5 \; \times \; 10^{-4} \; \text{T}$ and $L \; = \; 20 \; \text{m} \implies \varepsilon \; = \; B L v \; = \; 0.5 \; \times \; 10^{-4} \; \times \; 20 \; \times \; 20\sqrt{10} \; = \; 0.02\sqrt{10} \; \text{V} \; = \; 20\sqrt{10} \; \text{mV}$.

questions.text: A conducting loop of radius $\frac{10}{\sqrt{\pi}} \; \text{cm}$ is placed perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of $0.5 \; \text{T}$. The magnetic field is decreased to zero in $0.5 \; \text{s}$ at a steady rate. The induced emf in the circular loop at $0.25 \; \text{s}$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction $\varepsilon \; = \; -\frac{d\phi}{dt} \; = \; -A \frac{dB}{dt}$. // 📝 Solution: Area of loop $A \; = \; \pi r^2 \; = \; \pi \left(\frac{0.1}{\sqrt{\pi}}\right)^2 \; = \; 0.01 \; \text{m}^2 \implies \text{Induced emf } \varepsilon \; = \; \left\lvert \frac{\Delta \phi}{\Delta t} \right\rvert \; = \; \frac{A \left(B_i \; - \; B_f\right)}{\Delta t} \; = \; \frac{0.01 \; \times \; \left(0.5 \; - \; 0\right)}{0.5} \; = \; 0.01 \; \text{V} \; = \; 10 \; \text{mV}$.

questions.text: A square loop of side $10 \; \text{cm}$ and resistance $0.7 \; \Omega$ is placed vertically in east-west plane. A uniform magnetic field of $0.20 \; \text{T}$ is set up across the plane in north east direction. The magnetic field is decreased to zero in $1 \; \text{s}$ at a steady rate. Then, magnitude of induced emf is $\sqrt{x} \; \times \; 10^{-3} \; \text{V}$. The value of $x$ is _______
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The angle between the normal to the east-west plane (North) and the north-east magnetic field is $\theta \; = \; 45^\circ$. // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] Area $A \; = \; \left(0.1\right)^2 \; = \; 0.01 \; \text{m}^2$, $B \; = \; 0.20 \; \text{T}$, and $\theta \; = \; 45^\circ \implies \left\lvert \varepsilon \right\rvert \; = \; \frac{B A \cos 45^\circ \; - \; 0}{\Delta t} \; = \; \frac{0.20 \; \times \; 0.01 \; \times \; \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}{1} \; = \; \sqrt{2} \; \times \; 10^{-3} \; \text{V} \implies x \; = \; 2$.

questions.text: Figure shows the circuit that contains three resistances $\left(9 \; \Omega \text{ each}\right)$ and two inductors $\left(4 \; \text{mH each}\right)$. The reading of ammeter at the moment switch $K$ is turned ON, is _______ $\text{A}$. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: At $t \; = \; 0^+$ (just after switch $K$ is turned ON), inductors act as open circuits. // 📝 Solution: At $t \; = \; 0^+$, both $4 \; \text{mH}$ inductors block current (open circuit). Only the $9 \; \Omega$ resistor branch without an inductor in series conducts directly across the $9 \; \text{V}$ source through the ammeter $\implies I \; = \; \frac{V}{R} \; = \; \frac{9}{9} \; = \; 1 \; \text{A}$.

questions.text: A conducting circular loop of area $1.0 \; \text{m}^2$ is placed perpendicular to a magnetic field which varies as $B \; = \; \sin\left(100t\right)$ Tesla. If the resistance of the loop is $100 \; \Omega$, then the average thermal energy dissipated in the loop in one period is _______ $\text{J}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find induced emf $\varepsilon \; = \; -A \frac{dB}{dt}$, then calculate thermal energy in one time period $T \; = \; \frac{2\pi}{\omega}$ using $E \; = \; P_{\text{avg}} T \; = \; \frac{\varepsilon_{\text{max}}^2}{2R} T$. // 📝 Solution: Flux $\phi \; = \; B A \; = \; \sin\left(100t\right) \; \text{Wb} \implies \varepsilon \; = \; -\frac{d\phi}{dt} \; = \; -100 \cos\left(100t\right) \; \text{V} \implies P_{\text{avg}} \; = \; \frac{\varepsilon_{\text{max}}^2}{2R} \; = \; \frac{100^2}{2 \; \times \; 100} \; = \; 50 \; \text{W}$. Time period $T \; = \; \frac{2\pi}{100} \; \text{s} \implies \text{Energy } E \; = \; P_{\text{avg}} \; \times \; T \; = \; 50 \; \times \; \frac{2\pi}{100} \; = \; \pi \; \text{J}$.

questions.text: The magnetic flux $\phi$ (in weber) linked with a closed circuit of resistance $8 \; \Omega$ varies with time (in seconds) as $\phi \; = \; 5t^2 \; - \; 36t \; + \; 1$. The induced current in the circuit at $t \; = \; 2 \; \text{s}$ is _______ $\text{A}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Induced emf is $\left\lvert \varepsilon \right\rvert \; = \; \left\lvert \frac{d\phi}{dt} \right\rvert$ and induced current is $i \; = \; \frac{\left\lvert \varepsilon \right\rvert}{R}$. // 📝 Solution: $\varepsilon \; = \; -\frac{d\phi}{dt} \; = \; -\left(10t \; - \; 36\right)$. At $t \; = \; 2 \; \text{s}$, $\left\lvert \varepsilon \right\rvert \; = \; \left\lvert 10\left(2\right) \; - \; 36 \right\rvert \; = \; 16 \; \text{V} \implies i \; = \; \frac{\left\lvert \varepsilon \right\rvert}{R} \; = \; \frac{16}{8} \; = \; 2 \; \text{A}$.

questions.text: A wire of length $1 \; \text{m}$ moving with velocity $8 \; \text{m/s}$ at right angles to a magnetic field of $2 \; \text{T}$. The magnitude of induced emf, between the ends of wire will be _______ : [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Motional emf across a straight conductor moving perpendicular to a magnetic field is $\varepsilon \; = \; B v \ell$. // 📝 Solution: Given $B \; = \; 2 \; \text{T}$, $v \; = \; 8 \; \text{m/s}$, and $\ell \; = \; 1 \; \text{m} \implies \text{Induced emf } \varepsilon \; = \; B v \ell \; = \; 2 \; \times \; 8 \; \times \; 1 \; = \; 16 \; \text{V}$.

questions.text: As per the given figure, if $\frac{dI}{dt} \; = \; -1 \; \text{A/s}$ then the value of $V_{AB}$ at this instant will be _______ $\text{V}$. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Apply Kirchhoff's voltage law along the path from $A$ to $B$ including the inductor emf $-L \frac{dI}{dt}$. // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] Applying KVL from $A$ to $B$: $V_A \; - \; I R \; - \; L \frac{dI}{dt} \; - \; 12 \; = \; V_B \implies V_A \; - \; 2\left(12\right) \; - \; 6\left(-1\right) \; - \; 12 \; = \; V_B \implies V_A \; - \; V_B \; = \; 24 \; - \; 6 \; + \; 12 \; = \; 30 \; \text{V}$.
questions.topic: Self Induction and Inductors in Circuits

questions.text: In a coil, the current changes from $-2 \; \text{A}$ to $+2 \; \text{A}$ in $0.2 \; \text{s}$ and induces an emf of $0.1 \; \text{V}$. The self inductance of the coil is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Magnitude of average self-induced emf is $\left\lvert \varepsilon \right\rvert \; = \; L \left\lvert \frac{\Delta I}{\Delta t} \right\rvert$. // 📝 Solution: $\left\lvert \varepsilon \right\rvert \; = \; L \frac{\left\lvert I_f \; - \; I_i \right\rvert}{\Delta t} \implies 0.1 \; = \; L \frac{\left\lvert 2 \; - \; \left(-2\right) \right\rvert}{0.2} \; = \; L \left(\frac{4}{0.2}\right) \implies L \; = \; \frac{0.1 \; \times \; 0.2}{4} \; = \; 5 \; \times \; 10^{-3} \; \text{H} \; = \; 5 \; \text{mH}$.

questions.text: Three identical coils $C_1, \; C_2$ and $C_3$ are closely placed such that they share a common axis. $C_2$ is exactly midway. $C_1$ carries current $I$ in anti-clockwise direction while $C_3$ carries current $I$ in clockwise direction. An induced current flows through $C_2$ will be in clockwise direction when

options.text: $C_1$ moves away from $C_2$ and $C_3$ moves towards $C_2$
$C_1$ and $C_3$ move with equal speeds away from $C_2$
$C_1$ moves towards $C_2$ and $C_3$ moves away from $C_2$
$C_1$ and $C_3$ move with equal speeds towards $C_2$

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Apply Lenz's law: to induce a clockwise current in $C_2$, the net anti-clockwise magnetic flux through $C_2$ must increase. // 📝 Solution: Let the axis from $C_1$ to $C_3$ be $+z$. Anti-clockwise current in $C_1$ produces magnetic field $\vec{B}_1$ along $+z$, while clockwise current in $C_3$ produces $\vec{B}_3$ along $-z$. A clockwise induced current in $C_2$ produces an induced magnetic field along $-z$, which by Lenz's law opposes an increasing flux along $+z$. Flux along $+z$ increases when $C_1$ moves towards $C_2$ ($B_1$ increases) and $C_3$ moves away from $C_2$ ($B_3$ decreases).

questions.text: A simple pendulum made of mass $10 \; \text{g}$ and a metallic wire of length $10 \; \text{cm}$ is suspended vertically in a uniform magnetic field of $2 \; \text{T}$. The magnetic field direction is perpendicular to the plane of oscillations of the pendulum. If the pendulum is released from an angle of $60^\circ$ with vertical, then maximum induced EMF between the point of suspension and point of oscillation is _______ $\text{mV}$. $\left(\text{Take } g \; = \; 10 \; \text{m/s}^2\right)$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Maximum angular speed $\omega_{\text{max}}$ occurs at the lowest point; find it by energy conservation $mg\ell\left(1 \; - \; \cos\theta\right) \; = \; \frac{1}{2} m \left(\ell \omega_{\text{max}}\right)^2$ and use $\varepsilon_{\text{max}} \; = \; \frac{1}{2} B \omega_{\text{max}} \ell^2$. // 📝 Solution: By conservation of mechanical energy for the simple pendulum bob: $mg\ell\left(1 \; - \; \cos 60^\circ\right) \; = \; \frac{1}{2} m \ell^2 \omega_{\text{max}}^2 \implies \omega_{\text{max}} \; = \; \sqrt{\frac{g}{\ell}} \; = \; \sqrt{\frac{10}{0.1}} \; = \; 10 \; \text{rad/s} \implies \varepsilon_{\text{max}} \; = \; \frac{1}{2} B \omega_{\text{max}} \ell^2 \; = \; \frac{1}{2} \; \times \; 2 \; \times \; 10 \; \times \; \left(0.1\right)^2 \; = \; 0.1 \; \text{V} \; = \; 100 \; \text{mV}$.

questions.text: A conducting circular loop is rotated about its diameter at a constant angular speed of $100 \; \text{rad/s}$ in a magnetic field of $0.5 \; \text{T}$ perpendicular to the axis of rotation. When the loop is rotated by $30^\circ$ from the horizontal position, the induced EMF is $15.4 \; \text{mV}$. The radius of the loop is _______ $\text{mm}$. $\left(\text{Take } \pi \; = \; \frac{22}{7}\right)$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use instantaneous induced emf in a rotating loop $\varepsilon \; = \; B \omega A \sin\theta$, where $A \; = \; \pi r^2$. // 📝 Solution: Given $\varepsilon \; = \; 15.4 \; \times \; 10^{-3} \; \text{V}$, $B \; = \; 0.5 \; \text{T}$, $\omega \; = \; 100 \; \text{rad/s}$, and $\theta \; = \; 30^\circ \implies 15.4 \; \times \; 10^{-3} \; = \; 0.5 \; \times \; 100 \; \times \; \left(\frac{22}{7} r^2\right) \; \times \; \sin 30^\circ \implies r^2 \; = \; \frac{15.4 \; \times \; 10^{-3} \; \times \; 28}{100 \; \times \; 22} \; = \; 1.96 \; \times \; 10^{-4} \; \text{m}^2 \implies r \; = \; 1.4 \; \times \; 10^{-2} \; \text{m} \; = \; 14 \; \text{mm}$.

questions.text: When a coil is connected across a $20 \; \text{V}$ dc supply, it draws a current of $5 \; \text{A}$. When it is connected across $20 \; \text{V}$, $50 \; \text{Hz}$ ac supply, it draws a current of $4 \; \text{A}$. The self inductance of the coil is _______ $\text{mH}$. $\left(\text{Take } \pi \; = \; 3\right)$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use the DC case to find resistance $R \; = \; \frac{V_{\text{dc}}}{I_{\text{dc}}}$ and the AC case to find impedance $Z \; = \; \sqrt{R^2 \; + \; X_L^2} \; = \; \frac{V_{\text{ac}}}{I_{\text{ac}}}$. // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] For DC: $R \; = \; \frac{20}{5} \; = \; 4 \; \Omega$. For AC: $Z \; = \; \frac{20}{4} \; = \; 5 \; \Omega \implies \sqrt{R^2 \; + \; X_L^2} \; = \; 5 \implies 4^2 \; + \; X_L^2 \; = \; 25 \implies X_L \; = \; 3 \; \Omega \implies 2\pi f L \; = \; 3 \implies L \; = \; \frac{3}{2 \; \times \; 3 \; \times \; 50} \; = \; 0.01 \; \text{H} \; = \; 10 \; \text{mH}$.

questions.text: A $1 \; \text{m}$ long metal rod $AB$ completes the circuit as shown in figure. The area of circuit is perpendicular to the magnetic field of $0.10 \; \text{T}$. If the resistance of the total circuit is $2 \; \Omega$ then the force needed to move the rod towards right with constant speed $\left(v\right)$ of $1.5 \; \text{m/s}$ is _______ $\text{N}$. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Force required to move the rod at constant speed equals the opposing magnetic force $F \; = \; \frac{B^2 \ell^2 v}{R}$. // 📝 Solution: Given $\ell \; = \; 1 \; \text{m}$, $B \; = \; 0.10 \; \text{T}$, $R \; = \; 2 \; \Omega$, and $v \; = \; 1.5 \; \text{m/s} \implies \text{Motional emf } \varepsilon \; = \; B \ell v \; = \; 0.10 \; \times \; 1 \; \times \; 1.5 \; = \; 0.15 \; \text{V} \implies I \; = \; \frac{\varepsilon}{R} \; = \; \frac{0.15}{2} \; = \; 0.075 \; \text{A} \implies F \; = \; B I \ell \; = \; 0.10 \; \times \; 0.075 \; \times \; 1 \; = \; 7.5 \; \times \; 10^{-3} \; \text{N}$.

questions.text: A rod of length $60 \; \text{cm}$ rotates with a uniform angular velocity $20 \; \text{rad s}^{-1}$ about its perpendicular bisector, in a uniform magnetic field $0.5 \; \text{T}$. The direction of magnetic field is parallel to the axis of rotation. The potential difference between the two ends of the rod is _______ $\text{V}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Both halves of the rod rotate identically about the centre $O$, inducing equal potential differences from the centre to each end. // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] Let $O$ be the midpoint and $A, \; B$ be the two ends $\implies V_O \; - \; V_A \; = \; \frac{1}{2} B \omega \left(\frac{\ell}{2}\right)^2$ and $V_O \; - \; V_B \; = \; \frac{1}{2} B \omega \left(\frac{\ell}{2}\right)^2 \implies V_A \; = \; V_B \implies V_A \; - \; V_B \; = \; 0 \; \text{V}$.

questions.text: Two insulated circular loop $A$ and $B$ radius '$a$' carrying a current of '$I$' in the anti clockwise direction as shown in figure. The magnitude of the magnetic induction at the centre will be : [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The two circular loops are in mutually perpendicular planes, so their magnetic fields at the common centre are perpendicular: $B_{\text{net}} \; = \; \sqrt{B_A^2 \; + \; B_B^2}$. // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] Magnetic field at the centre of each loop is $B_A \; = \; B_B \; = \; \frac{\mu_0 I}{2a}$ with $B_A \perp B_B \implies B_{\text{net}} \; = \; \sqrt{B_A^2 \; + \; B_B^2} \; = \; \sqrt{2} \left(\frac{\mu_0 I}{2a}\right) \; = \; \frac{\mu_0 I}{\sqrt{2}a}$.

questions.text: A certain elastic conducting material is stretched into a circular loop. It is placed with its plane perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field $B \; = \; 0.8 \; \text{T}$. When released the radius of the loop starts shrinking at a constant rate of $2 \; \text{cm s}^{-1}$. The induced emf in the loop at an instant when the radius of the loop is $10 \; \text{cm}$ will be _______ $\text{mV}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Apply Faraday's law $\varepsilon \; = \; \left\lvert \frac{d}{dt} \left(B \pi r^2\right) \right\rvert \; = \; 2 \pi B r \left\lvert \frac{dr}{dt} \right\rvert$. // 📝 Solution: Given $B \; = \; 0.8 \; \text{T}$, $r \; = \; 10 \; \text{cm} \; = \; 0.1 \; \text{m}$, and $\left\lvert \frac{dr}{dt} \right\rvert \; = \; 2 \; \times \; 10^{-2} \; \text{m/s} \implies \varepsilon \; = \; 2 \pi B r \left\lvert \frac{dr}{dt} \right\rvert \; = \; 2 \; \times \; \pi \; \times \; 0.8 \; \times \; 0.1 \; \times \; 2 \; \times \; 10^{-2} \; = \; 3.2\pi \; \times \; 10^{-3} \; \text{V} \; \approx \; 10.05 \; \text{mV} \; \approx \; 10 \; \text{mV}$.

questions.text: An inductor of $0.5 \; \text{mH}$, a capacitor of $20 \; \mu\text{F}$ and resistance of $20 \; \Omega$ are connected in series with a $220 \; \text{V}$ ac source. If the current is in phase with the emf, the amplitude of current of the circuit is $\sqrt{x} \; \text{A}$. The value of $x$ is -
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Current is in phase with emf at resonance, so impedance $Z \; = \; R$ and $I_{\text{max}} \; = \; \sqrt{2} I_{\text{rms}}$. // 📝 Solution: Since current is in phase with emf, $X_L \; = \; X_C \implies Z \; = \; R \; = \; 20 \; \Omega \implies I_{\text{rms}} \; = \; \frac{V_{\text{rms}}}{Z} \; = \; \frac{220}{20} \; = \; 11 \; \text{A} \implies I_{\text{max}} \; = \; 11\sqrt{2} \; = \; \sqrt{242} \; \text{A} \implies x \; = \; 242$.

questions.text: A rectangular loop of sides $12 \; \text{cm}$ and $5 \; \text{cm}$, with its sides parallel to the $x$-axis and $y$-axis respectively moves with a velocity of $5 \; \text{cm/s}$ in the positive $x$ axis direction, in a space containing a variable magnetic field in the positive $z$ direction. The field has a gradient of $10^{-3} \; \text{T/cm}$ along the negative $x$ direction and it is decreasing with time at the rate of $10^{-3} \; \text{T/s}$. If the resistance of the loop is $6 \; \text{m}\Omega$, the power dissipated by the loop as heat is _______ $\times \; 10^{-9} \; \text{W}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Total induced emf is the sum of emf due to spatial motion $\varepsilon_1 \; = \; A v \left\lvert \frac{\partial B}{\partial x} \right\rvert$ and emf due to time variation $\varepsilon_2 \; = \; A \left\lvert \frac{\partial B}{\partial t} \right\rvert$. // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] Area $A \; = \; 12 \; \times \; 5 \; \times \; 10^{-4} \; = \; 6 \; \times \; 10^{-3} \; \text{m}^2$, $\frac{\partial B}{\partial x} \; = \; -10^{-1} \; \text{T/m}$, and $\frac{\partial B}{\partial t} \; = \; -10^{-3} \; \text{T/s}$. Both motion in $+x$ direction and time variation decrease the flux, so emfs add up: $\varepsilon_{\text{motional}} \; = \; A v \left\lvert \frac{\partial B}{\partial x} \right\rvert \; = \; 6 \; \times \; 10^{-3} \; \times \; 0.05 \; \times \; 0.1 \; = \; 300 \; \times \; 10^{-7} \; \text{V}$ and $\varepsilon_{\text{time}} \; = \; A \left\lvert \frac{\partial B}{\partial t} \right\rvert \; = \; 6 \; \times \; 10^{-3} \; \times \; 10^{-3} \; = \; 60 \; \times \; 10^{-7} \; \text{V} \implies \varepsilon_{\text{net}} \; = \; 360 \; \times \; 10^{-7} \; \text{V} \implies P \; = \; \frac{\varepsilon_{\text{net}}^2}{R} \; = \; \frac{\left(360 \; \times \; 10^{-7}\right)^2}{6 \; \times \; 10^{-3}} \; = \; 216 \; \times \; 10^{-9} \; \text{W}$.

questions.text: A square loop of side $15 \; \text{cm}$ being moved towards right at a constant speed of $2 \; \text{cm/s}$ as shown in figure. The front edge enters the $50 \; \text{cm}$ wide magnetic field at $t \; = \; 0$. The value of induced emf in the loop at $t \; = \; 10 \; \text{s}$ will be : [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Check whether the loop is partially or completely inside the uniform magnetic field at $t \; = \; 10 \; \text{s}$. // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] Distance travelled by front edge in $t \; = \; 10 \; \text{s}$ is $d \; = \; v t \; = \; 2 \; \text{cm/s} \; \times \; 10 \; \text{s} \; = \; 20 \; \text{cm}$. Since side of loop is $15 \; \text{cm} \; < \; 20 \; \text{cm}$ and field width is $50 \; \text{cm}$, the entire loop is inside the uniform magnetic field at $t \; = \; 10 \; \text{s} \implies \frac{d\phi}{dt} \; = \; 0 \implies \varepsilon \; = \; 0$.

questions.text: A horizontal straight wire $5 \; \text{m}$ long extending from east to west falling freely at right angle to horizontal component of earth's magnetic field $0.60 \; \times \; 10^{-4} \; \text{Wb m}^{-2}$. The instantaneous value of emf induced in the wire when its velocity is $10 \; \text{m s}^{-1}$ is _______ $\times \; 10^{-3} \; \text{V}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use the motional emf formula $\varepsilon \; = \; B_H v \ell$. // 📝 Solution: Given $B_H \; = \; 0.60 \; \times \; 10^{-4} \; \text{Wb m}^{-2}$, $v \; = \; 10 \; \text{m/s}$, and $\ell \; = \; 5 \; \text{m} \implies \varepsilon \; = \; B_H v \ell \; = \; 0.60 \; \times \; 10^{-4} \; \times \; 10 \; \times \; 5 \; = \; 3 \; \times \; 10^{-3} \; \text{V}$.

questions.text: A rectangular loop of length $2.5 \; \text{m}$ and width $2 \; \text{m}$ is placed at $60^\circ$ to a magnetic field of $4 \; \text{T}$. The loop is removed from the field in $10 \; \text{sec}$. The average emf induced in the loop during this time is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Average induced emf is $\varepsilon_{\text{avg}} \; = \; -\frac{\Delta \phi}{\Delta t} \; = \; -\frac{0 \; - \; B A \cos\theta}{\Delta t}$. // 📝 Solution: Area $A \; = \; 2.5 \; \times \; 2 \; = \; 5 \; \text{m}^2 \implies \phi_i \; = \; B A \cos 60^\circ \; = \; 4 \; \times \; 5 \; \times \; \frac{1}{2} \; = \; 10 \; \text{Wb}$ and $\phi_f \; = \; 0 \implies \varepsilon_{\text{avg}} \; = \; -\frac{\phi_f \; - \; \phi_i}{\Delta t} \; = \; -\frac{0 \; - \; 10}{10} \; = \; +1 \; \text{V}$.

questions.text: A metallic rod of length '$L$' is rotated with an angular speed of '$\omega$' normal to a uniform magnetic field '$B$' about an axis passing through one end of rod as shown in figure. The induced emf will be : [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Consider a small element $dx$ at distance $x$ moving with speed $v \; = \; \omega x$, so $d\varepsilon \; = \; B v \, dx$. // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] Emf across element $dx$ at distance $x$ from axis is $d\varepsilon \; = \; B \left(\omega x\right) dx \implies \varepsilon \; = \; \int_{0}^{L} B \omega x \, dx \; = \; B \omega \left[\frac{x^2}{2}\right]_{0}^{L} \; = \; \frac{1}{2} B L^2 \omega$.

questions.text: A square loop $PQRS$ having $10$ turns, area $3.6 \; \times \; 10^{-3} \; \text{m}^2$ and resistance $100 \; \Omega$ is slowly and uniformly being pulled out of a uniform magnetic field of magnitude $B \; = \; 0.5 \; \text{T}$ as shown. Work done in pulling the loop out of the field in $1.0 \; \text{s}$ is _______ $\times \; 10^{-6} \; \text{J}$. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Work done at constant speed equals thermal energy dissipated $W \; = \; F \ell \; = \; \frac{\varepsilon^2}{R} t \; = \; \frac{\left(N B A\right)^2}{R t}$. // 📝 Solution: Induced emf $\varepsilon \; = \; N B \ell v$ and $v \; = \; \frac{\ell}{t} \implies W \; = \; F \ell \; = \; N i \ell B \ell \; = \; \frac{N^2 B^2 \ell^2 v}{R} \ell \; = \; \frac{N^2 B^2 A^2}{R t} \implies W \; = \; \frac{10^2 \; \times \; \left(0.5\right)^2 \; \times \; \left(3.6 \; \times \; 10^{-3}\right)^2}{100 \; \times \; 1.0} \; = \; 3.24 \; \times \; 10^{-6} \; \text{J} \; \approx \; 3 \; \times \; 10^{-6} \; \text{J}$.

questions.text: Suppose a long solenoid of $100 \; \text{cm}$ length, radius $2 \; \text{cm}$ having $500$ turns per unit length, carries a current $I \; = \; 10 \sin\left(\omega t\right) \; \text{A}$, where $\omega \; = \; 1000 \; \text{rad/s}$. A circular conducting loop $\left(B\right)$ of radius $1 \; \text{cm}$ coaxially slided through the solenoid at a speed $v \; = \; 1 \; \text{cm/s}$. The r.m.s. current through the loop when the coil $B$ is inserted $10 \; \text{cm}$ inside the solenoid is $\alpha / \sqrt{2} \; \mu\text{A}$. The value of $\alpha$ is _______. $\left[\text{Resistance of the loop} \; = \; 10 \; \Omega\right]$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Inside a long solenoid, the magnetic field is spatially uniform $B \; = \; \mu_0 n I\left(t\right)$, so emf is induced solely due to the time-varying current: $\varepsilon \; = \; -A \frac{dB}{dt}$. // 📝 Solution: Area of loop $A \; = \; \pi r^2 \; = \; \pi \left(10^{-2}\right)^2 \; = \; \pi \; \times \; 10^{-4} \; \text{m}^2 \implies \varepsilon\left(t\right) \; = \; A \mu_0 n I_0 \omega \cos\left(\omega t\right) \implies i_{\text{rms}} \; = \; \frac{\varepsilon_{\text{max}}}{\sqrt{2} R} \; = \; \frac{\pi \; \times \; 10^{-4} \; \times \; 4\pi \; \times \; 10^{-7} \; \times \; 500 \; \times \; 10 \; \times \; 1000}{\sqrt{2} \; \times \; 10} \; = \; \frac{20\pi^2}{\sqrt{2}} \; \times \; 10^{-6} \; \text{A} \; \approx \; \frac{197}{\sqrt{2}} \; \mu\text{A} \implies \alpha \; = \; 197$.

questions.text: A small square loop of wire of side $\ell$ is placed inside a large square loop of wire of side $L$ $\left(L \; = \; \ell^2\right)$. The loops are coplanar and their centers coincide. The value of the mutual inductance of the system is $\sqrt{x} \; \times \; 10^{-7} \; \text{H}$, where $x \; =$ _______
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find the magnetic field at the centre of the larger square loop of side $L$ carrying current $i$, and multiply by the area $\ell^2$ of the smaller loop. // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] Magnetic field at the centre of the large square loop of side $L$ is $B_{\text{centre}} \; = \; 4 \; \times \; \frac{\mu_0 i}{4\pi \left(L/2\right)} \left(\sin 45^\circ \; + \; \sin 45^\circ\right) \; = \; \frac{2\sqrt{2}\mu_0 i}{\pi L} \implies \text{Flux through inner loop } \phi \; = \; B_{\text{centre}} \ell^2 \; = \; \frac{2\sqrt{2}\mu_0 \ell^2}{\pi L} i \implies M \; = \; \frac{\phi}{i} \; = \; \frac{2\sqrt{2}\mu_0}{\pi} \left(\text{since } L \; = \; \ell^2\right) \; = \; \frac{2\sqrt{2} \; \times \; 4\pi \; \times \; 10^{-7}}{\pi} \; = \; 8\sqrt{2} \; \times \; 10^{-7} \; \text{H} \; = \; \sqrt{128} \; \times \; 10^{-7} \; \text{H} \implies x \; = \; 128$.

questions.text: Two conducting circular loops $A$ and $B$ are placed in the same plane with their centers coinciding as shown in figure. The mutual inductance between them is : [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Assume current $i$ in the outer loop of radius $b$ and find the magnetic flux $\phi \; = \; M i \; = \; B_{\text{centre}} A_{\text{inner}}$ through the inner loop of radius $a \ll b$. // 📝 Solution: Magnetic field at centre due to outer loop of radius $b$ is $B \; = \; \frac{\mu_0 i}{2b} \implies \text{Flux through inner loop } \phi \; = \; B \left(\pi a^2\right) \; = \; \frac{\mu_0 \pi a^2}{2b} i \implies M \; = \; \frac{\phi}{i} \; = \; \frac{\mu_0 \pi a^2}{2b}$.

questions.text: A circular loop of radius $7 \; \text{cm}$ is placed in uniform magnetic field of $0.2 \; \text{T}$ directed perpendicular to plane of loop. The loop is converted into a square loop in $0.5 \; \text{s}$. The EMF induced in the loop is _______ $\text{mV}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Perimeter remains constant when converting the circle into a square: $4a \; = \; 2\pi r \implies a \; = \; \frac{\pi r}{2}$. // 📝 Solution: Initial area $A_1 \; = \; \pi r^2 \; = \; \frac{22}{7} \; \times \; \left(0.07\right)^2 \; = \; 0.0154 \; \text{m}^2$. Perimeter $2\pi r \; = \; 2 \; \times \; \frac{22}{7} \; \times \; 0.07 \; = \; 0.44 \; \text{m} \implies \text{Side of square } a \; = \; \frac{0.44}{4} \; = \; 0.11 \; \text{m} \implies \text{Final area } A_2 \; = \; a^2 \; = \; \left(0.11\right)^2 \; = \; 0.0121 \; \text{m}^2 \implies \varepsilon \; = \; \frac{B \left(A_1 \; - \; A_2\right)}{\Delta t} \; = \; \frac{0.2 \; \times \; \left(0.0154 \; - \; 0.0121\right)}{0.5} \; = \; 1.32 \; \times \; 10^{-3} \; \text{V} \; = \; 1.32 \; \text{mV}$.

questions.text: Inductance of a coil with $10^4$ turns is $10 \; \text{mH}$ and it is connected to a dc source of $10 \; \text{V}$ with internal resistance of $10 \; \Omega$. The energy density in the inductor when the current reaches $\left(\frac{1}{e}\right)$ of its maximum value is $\alpha\pi \; \times \; \frac{1}{e^2} \; \text{J/m}^3$. The value of $\alpha$ is _______. $\left(\mu_0 \; = \; 4\pi \; \times \; 10^{-7} \; \text{T m/A}\right)$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Magnetic energy density is $u_B \; = \; \frac{B^2}{2\mu_0} \; = \; \frac{1}{2} \mu_0 n^2 I^2$. // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] Maximum current $I_0 \; = \; \frac{V}{R} \; = \; \frac{10}{10} \; = \; 1 \; \text{A} \implies \text{Instantaneous current } I \; = \; \frac{I_0}{e} \; = \; \frac{1}{e} \; \text{A}$. Taking turn density $n \; = \; 10^4 \; \text{m}^{-1} \implies u_B \; = \; \frac{B^2}{2\mu_0} \; = \; \frac{1}{2} \mu_0 n^2 I^2 \; = \; \frac{1}{2} \left(4\pi \; \times \; 10^{-7}\right) \left(10^4\right)^2 \left(\frac{1}{e}\right)^2 \; = \; 20\pi \; \times \; \frac{1}{e^2} \; \text{J/m}^3 \implies \alpha \; = \; 20$.

questions.text: An object is allowed to fall from a height $R$ above the earth, where $R$ is the radius of earth. Its velocity when it strikes the earth's surface, ignoring air resistance, will be :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use conservation of energy with gravitational potential energy -GMm/r. // 📝 Solution: $ \left( - \frac{GMm}{2R} \right) \; - \; \left( - \frac{GMm}{R} \right) \; = \; \frac{1}{2} m v^2 \implies v^2 \; = \; \frac{GM}{R} \; = \; gR \implies v \; = \; \sqrt{gR} $
questions.topic: Fall from Large Height (Gravitation and Energy)

questions.text: Water drops fall from a tap on the floor, $5\;\text{m}$ below, at regular intervals of time, the first drop strikes the floor when the sixth drop begins to fall. The height at which the fourth drop will be from ground, at the instant when the first drop strikes the ground is ____ m. $\left( g \; = \; 10\;\text{m/s}^2 \right)$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find the fall time of the first drop, divide into 5 equal intervals, then find how long the fourth drop has fallen. // 📝 Solution: $ 5 \; = \; \frac{1}{2} \left( 10 \right) t^2 \implies t \; = \; 1\;\text{s}, \; T \; = \; 0.2\;\text{s} \implies t_4 \; = \; 1 \; - \; 3 \left( 0.2 \right) \; = \; 0.4\;\text{s} \implies s_4 \; = \; \frac{1}{2} \left( 10 \right) \left( 0.4 \right)^2 \; = \; 0.8\;\text{m} \implies h \; = \; 5 \; - \; 0.8 \; = \; 4.2\;\text{m} $

questions.text: A particle moves along the $x$-axis and its displacement varies with time according to $x = c_0(t^{2} - 2) + c(t - 2)^{2}$, where $c_0$ and $c$ are constants of appropriate dimensions. Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: The acceleration of the particle is $2c_0$
The acceleration of the particle is $2c$
The initial velocity of the particle is $4c$
The acceleration of the particle is $2(c + c_0)$

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $v = \frac{dx}{dt}$ and $a = \frac{dv}{dt}$. // 📝 Solution: $v = 2c_0 t + 2c(t-2) \implies a = \frac{dv}{dt} = 2c_0 + 2c = 2(c + c_0)$

questions.text: A person travelling on a straight line moves with a uniform velocity $v_1$ for a distance $x$ and with a uniform velocity $v_2$ for the next $\frac{3}{2}x$ distance. The average velocity in this motion is $\frac{50}{7}\ \text{m/s}$. If $v_1$ is $5\ \text{m/s}$, then $v_2 =$ ______ $\text{m/s}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Average velocity $=\frac{\text{total distance}}{\text{total time}}$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{\frac{5x}{2}}{\frac{x}{5} + \frac{3x}{2v_2}} = \frac{50}{7} \implies \frac{1}{5} + \frac{3}{2v_2} = \frac{7}{20} \implies \frac{3}{2v_2} = \frac{3}{20} \implies v_2 = 10\ \text{m/s}$

questions.text: A sportsman runs around a circular track of radius $r$ such that he traverses the path $ABAB$, where $A$ and $B$ are diametrically opposite points. [FIGURE] The distance travelled and displacement, respectively, are:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Distance is the total path length; displacement is the straight line from start to end. // 📝 Solution: Distance $= \pi r + \pi r + \pi r = 3\pi r$; displacement $= AB = 2r$

questions.text: Match Column-I with Column-II : Column-I (x-t graphs): A. [FIGURE] B. [FIGURE] C. [FIGURE] D. [FIGURE]. Column-II (v-t graphs): I. [FIGURE] II. [FIGURE] III. [FIGURE] IV. [FIGURE]. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The slope of the x-t graph gives the v-t graph. // 📝 Solution: $ \text{A} \; \text{(slope increasing steadily)} \implies \text{II} $, $ \text{B} \; \text{(slope negative}, \; \to 0 \text{)} \implies \text{IV} $, $ \text{C} \; \text{(slope} \; + \; \text{then} \; - \text{)} \implies \text{III} $, $ \text{D} \; \text{(constant slope)} \implies \text{I} $

questions.text: A body starts moving from rest with constant acceleration covers displacement $S_1$ in first $\left( p \; - \; 1 \right)$ seconds and $S_2$ in first $p$ seconds. The displacement $S_1 \; + \; S_2$ will be made in time :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use s = (1/2)at^2 from rest for each displacement. // 📝 Solution: $ S_1 \; = \; \frac{1}{2} a \left( p \; - \; 1 \right)^2, \; S_2 \; = \; \frac{1}{2} a p^2, \; S_1 \; + \; S_2 \; = \; \frac{1}{2} a t^2 \implies t^2 \; = \; \left( p \; - \; 1 \right)^2 \; + \; p^2 \implies t \; = \; \sqrt{2p^2 \; - \; 2p \; + \; 1} $

questions.text: The distance travelled by a particle is related to time $t$ as $x \; = \; 4t^2$. The velocity of the particle at $t \; = \; 5\;\text{s}$ is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Velocity is the time derivative of position. // 📝 Solution: $ v \; = \; \frac{dx}{dt} \; = \; 8t \implies v \left( 5 \right) \; = \; 8 \; \times \; 5 \; = \; 40\;\text{m/s} $

questions.text: The maximum speed of a boat in still water is $27\;\text{km/h}$. Now this boat is moving downstream in a river flowing at $9\;\text{km/h}$. A man in the boat throws a ball vertically upwards with speed of $10\;\text{m/s}$. Range of the ball as observed by an observer at rest on the river bank, is _______ cm. (Take $g\;=\;10\;\text{m/s}^2$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Horizontal velocity of the ball w.r.t. ground equals the boat speed downstream; use time of flight $\frac{2u}{g}$. // 📝 Solution: $v_x\;=\;27\;+\;9\;=\;36\;\text{km/h}\;=\;10\;\text{m/s}$, $T\;=\;\frac{2\;\times\;10}{10}\;=\;2\;\text{s}\;\implies\;R\;=\;10\;\times\;2\;=\;20\;\text{m}\;=\;2000\;\text{cm}$

questions.text: For a train engine moving with speed of $20\;\text{ms}^{-1}$, the driver must apply brakes at a distance of $500\;\text{m}$ before the station for the train to come to rest at the station. If the brakes were applied at half of this distance, the train engine would cross the station with speed $\sqrt{x}\;\text{ms}^{-1}$. The value of $x$ is ____. (Assuming same retardation is produced by brakes)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use v^2 = u^2 - 2as twice with the same retardation. // 📝 Solution: $ 0 \; = \; 20^2 \; - \; 2a \left( 500 \right) \implies a \; = \; 0.4\;\text{m/s}^2 \implies v^2 \; = \; 20^2 \; - \; 2 \left( 0.4 \right) \left( 250 \right) \; = \; 200 \implies x \; = \; 200 $

questions.text: A vehicle travels $4\;\text{km}$ with speed of $3\;\text{km/h}$ and another $4\;\text{km}$ with speed of $5\;\text{km/h}$, then its average speed is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For equal distances, average speed is the harmonic mean. // 📝 Solution: $ \frac{2}{V_{av}} \; = \; \frac{1}{3} \; + \; \frac{1}{5} \; = \; \frac{8}{15} \implies V_{av} \; = \; \frac{15}{4} \; = \; 3.75\;\text{km/h} $

questions.text: A particle starts from origin at $t \; = \; 0$ with a velocity $5 \hat{i}\;\text{m/s}$ and moves in $x \; - \; y$ plane under action of a force which produces a constant acceleration of $\left( 3 \hat{i} \; + \; 2 \hat{j} \right)\;\text{m/s}^2$. If the $x$-coordinate of the particle at that instant is $84\;\text{m}$, then the speed of the particle at this time is $\sqrt{\alpha}\;\text{m/s}$. The value of $\alpha$ is ______
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Treat x and y motions independently with constant acceleration. // 📝 Solution: $ v_x^2 \; = \; 25 \; + \; 2 \left( 3 \right) \left( 84 \right) \; = \; 529 \implies v_x \; = \; 23, \; t \; = \; \frac{23 \; - \; 5}{3} \; = \; 6\;\text{s} \implies v_y \; = \; 2 \; \times \; 6 \; = \; 12 \implies v^2 \; = \; 23^2 \; + \; 12^2 \; = \; 673 $
questions.topic: Motion in a Plane with Constant Acceleration

questions.text: A particle starts moving from time $t \; = \; 0$ and its coordinate is given as $x \left( t \right) \; = \; 4t^3 \; - \; 3t$. A. The particle returns to its original position (origin) $0.866$ units later. B. The particle is 1 unit away from origin at its turning point. C. Acceleration of the particle is non-negative. D. The particle is $0.5$ units away from origin at its turning point. E. Particle never turns back as acceleration is non-negative. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find v = dx/dt and a = dv/dt, then check the zeros of x and v for t >= 0. // 📝 Solution: $ v \; = \; 12t^2 \; - \; 3, \; a \; = \; 24t \; \ge \; 0 \implies \text{C true} $ ; $ x \; = \; 0 \implies t \; = \; \sqrt{\frac{3}{4}} \; = \; 0.866 \implies \text{A true} $ ; $ v \; = \; 0 \implies t \; = \; 0.5, \; x \; = \; 0.5 \; - \; 1.5 \; = \; -1 \implies \text{B true, D false, E false} $

questions.text: A particle is moving in a straight line. The variation of position $x$ as a function of time $t$ is given as $x \; = \; \left( t^3 \; - \; 6t^2 \; + \; 20t \; + \; 15 \right)\;\text{m}$. The velocity of the body when its acceleration becomes zero is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Differentiate x twice, set a = 0 and find t, then v. // 📝 Solution: $ v \; = \; 3t^2 \; - \; 12t \; + \; 20, \; a \; = \; 6t \; - \; 12 \; = \; 0 \implies t \; = \; 2\;\text{s} \implies v \; = \; 12 \; - \; 24 \; + \; 20 \; = \; 8\;\text{m/s} $

questions.text: A tennis ball is dropped on to the floor from a height of $9.8\;\text{m}$. It rebounds to a height $5.0\;\text{m}$. Ball comes in contact with the floor for $0.2\;\text{s}$. The average acceleration during contact is ____ $\text{ms}^{-2}$. [Given $g \; = \; 10\;\text{ms}^{-2}$]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find the speeds just before and after impact using v = sqrt(2gh), then a = change in velocity / time. // 📝 Solution: $ v_i \; = \; \sqrt{2 \; \times \; 10 \; \times \; 9.8} \; = \; 14\;\text{m/s} \; \downarrow $, $ v_f \; = \; \sqrt{2 \; \times \; 10 \; \times \; 5} \; = \; 10\;\text{m/s} \; \uparrow \implies \Delta v \; = \; 24 \implies a \; = \; \frac{24}{0.2} \; = \; 120\;\text{m/s}^2 $

questions.text: A body is moving with constant speed, in a circle of radius $10\;\text{m}$. The body completes one revolution in $4\;\text{s}$. At the end of $3^{rd}$ second, the displacement of body (in m) from its starting point is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find the angle covered in 3 s and use chord length = 2r sin(theta/2). // 📝 Solution: $ \theta \; = \; \frac{3}{4} \; \times \; 2\pi \; = \; \frac{3\pi}{2} \implies \text{displacement} \; = \; 2 r \sin \left( \frac{3\pi}{4} \right) \; = \; 10 \sqrt{2}\;\text{m} $

questions.text: Train A is moving along two parallel rail tracks towards north with speed $72\;\text{km/h}$ and train B is moving towards south with speed $108\;\text{km/h}$. Velocity of train B with respect to A and velocity of ground with respect to B are (in $\text{ms}^{-1}$) :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Convert km/h to m/s and use v_AB = v_A - v_B with north as positive. // 📝 Solution: $ v_A \; = \; 20\;\text{m/s}, \; v_B \; = \; -30\;\text{m/s} \implies v_{B/A} \; = \; -30 \; - \; 20 \; = \; -50, \; v_{G/B} \; = \; 0 \; - \; \left( -30 \right) \; = \; 30 $

questions.text: The velocity-time graph of an object moving along a straight line is shown in figure. What is the distance covered by the object between $t\;=\;0$ to $t\;=\;4\;\text{s}$ ? [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Distance equals the area under the v-t graph; velocity does not change sign. // 📝 Solution: $d\;=\;\frac{1}{2}\left(2\right)\left(10\right)\;+\;\left(10\right)\left(2\right)\;=\;10\;+\;20\;=\;30\;\text{m}$

questions.text: A particle is moving in a circle of radius $50\;\text{cm}$ in such a way that at any instant the normal and tangential components of its acceleration are equal. If its speed at $t \; = \; 0$ is $4\;\text{m/s}$, the time taken to complete the first revolution will be $\frac{1}{\alpha} \left[ 1 \; - \; e^{-2\pi} \right]\;\text{s}$, where $\alpha \; = \;$ _____ .
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Equate v^2/r with dv/dt, integrate to get v(t), then integrate v dt over one circumference. // 📝 Solution: $ \frac{v^2}{r} \; = \; \frac{dv}{dt} \implies v \; = \; \frac{4}{1 \; - \; 8t} \implies 4 \int_0^t \frac{dt}{1 \; - \; 8t} \; = \; \pi \implies t \; = \; \frac{1}{8} \left( 1 \; - \; e^{-2\pi} \right) \implies \alpha \; = \; 8 $
questions.topic: Circular Motion with Equal Normal and Tangential Acceleration

questions.text: The relation between time $t$ and distance $x$ is $t \; = \; \alpha x^2 \; + \; \beta x$, where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are constants. The relation between acceleration $\left( a \right)$ and velocity $\left( v \right)$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Differentiate t with respect to x to get 1/v, then differentiate again with respect to time. // 📝 Solution: $ \frac{dt}{dx} \; = \; \frac{1}{v} \; = \; 2 \alpha x \; + \; \beta \implies - \frac{1}{v^2} \frac{dv}{dt} \; = \; 2 \alpha v \implies a \; = \; -2 \alpha v^3 $

questions.text: The motion of an airplane is represented by velocity-time graph as shown below. The distance covered by airplane in the first 30.5 second is _______ km. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Distance equals the area under the velocity-time graph. // 📝 Solution: $d\;=\;\frac{200\;+\;400}{2}\left(2\right)\;+\;400\left(28.5\right)\;=\;600\;+\;11400\;=\;12000\;\text{m}\;=\;12\;\text{km}$

questions.text: The velocity $\left( v \right)$ - Distance $\left( x \right)$ graph is shown in figure. Which graph represents acceleration $\left( a \right)$ versus distance $\left( x \right)$ variation of this system? [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use a = v dv/dx with v linear in x. // 📝 Solution: $ v \; = \; v_0 \; - \; kx \implies a \; = \; v \frac{dv}{dx} \; = \; -k \left( v_0 \; - \; kx \right) \; = \; -k v_0 \; + \; k^2 x $ , so a is linear in x with positive slope (Option A).

questions.text: Two cars $P$ and $Q$ are moving on a road in the same direction. Acceleration of car $P$ increases linearly with time whereas car $Q$ moves with a constant acceleration. Both cars cross each other at time $t\;=\;0$, for the first time. The maximum possible number of crossing(s) (including the crossing at $t\;=\;0$) is ________.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Work in the frame of $P$ and use the relative acceleration $a_{QP}\;=\;a\;-\;kt$. // 📝 Solution: $a_{QP}\;=\;a\;-\;kt$ changes sign once $\implies$ if $u_{QP}$ and $a_{QP}$ are in the same direction, there are $2$ crossings; if opposite, there are $3$ crossings $\implies\;\text{maximum}\;=\;3$

questions.text: The displacement and the increase in the velocity of a moving particle in the time interval of $t$ to $\left( t \; + \; 1 \right)\text{s}$ are $125\;\text{m}$ and $50\;\text{m/s}$, respectively. The distance travelled by the particle in $\left( t \; + \; 2 \right)^{th}\;\text{s}$ is_____ m.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Assume constant acceleration with the interval starting at t = 0 and use the nth-second formula. // 📝 Solution: $ a \; = \; \frac{50}{1} \; = \; 50\;\text{m/s}^2, \; 125 \; = \; u \; + \; \frac{a}{2} \implies u \; = \; 100\;\text{m/s} \implies S_{2nd} \; = \; u \; + \; \frac{a}{2} \left( 2 \; \times \; 2 \; - \; 1 \right) \; = \; 175\;\text{m} $

questions.text: A helicopter flying horizontally with a speed of $360\ \text{km/h}$ at an altitude of $2\ \text{km}$ drops an object at an instant. The object hits the ground at a point $O$, $20\ \text{s}$ after it is dropped. The displacement of $O$ from the position of the helicopter where the object was released is (use $g = 10\ \text{m/s}^{2}$ and neglect air resistance):
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Horizontal motion is uniform; vertical motion is free fall from rest. // 📝 Solution: $x = 100 \times 20 = 2000\ \text{m}$; $H = \frac{1}{2}(10)(20)^{2} = 2000\ \text{m} \implies s = \sqrt{x^{2} + H^{2}} = 2000\sqrt{2}\ \text{m} = 2\sqrt{2}\ \text{km}$

questions.text: A car travels a distance of $x$ with speed $V_1$ and then same distance $x$ with speed $V_2$ in the same direction. The average speed of the car is: [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Average speed = total distance / total time. // 📝 Solution: $ v_{avg} \; = \; \frac{x \; + \; x}{\frac{x}{v_1} \; + \; \frac{x}{v_2}} \; = \; \frac{2 v_1 v_2}{v_1 \; + \; v_2} $

questions.text: The velocity-time graph of a body moving in a straight line is shown in figure. [FIGURE] The ratio of displacement to distance travelled by the body in time $0$ to $10\;\text{s}$ is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Displacement is the signed area under the v-t graph, while distance is the sum of the absolute areas. // 📝 Solution: $ \text{Displacement} \; = \; 16 \; - \; 8 \; + \; 16 \; - \; 8 \; = \; 16\;\text{m} $ and $ \text{Distance} \; = \; 16 \; + \; 8 \; + \; 16 \; + \; 8 \; = \; 48\;\text{m} \implies \text{ratio} \; = \; \frac{16}{48} \; = \; 1 \; : \; 3 $

questions.text: A paratrooper jumps from an aeroplane and opens a parachute after $2\;\text{s}$ of free fall and starts deaccelerating with $3\;\text{m/s}^2$. At $10\;\text{m}$ height from ground, while descending with the help of parachute, the speed of paratrooper is $5\;\text{m/s}$. The initial height of the airplane is ____ m. $\left( g \; = \; 10\;\text{m/s}^2 \right)$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Split the motion into free fall, parachute deceleration, and the final 10 m. // 📝 Solution: $ v_1 \; = \; 20\;\text{m/s}, \; h_1 \; = \; \frac{1}{2} \left( 10 \right) \left( 4 \right) \; = \; 20\;\text{m} ; \; 5^2 \; = \; 20^2 \; - \; 2 \left( 3 \right) h_2 \implies h_2 \; = \; 62.5\;\text{m} \implies H \; = \; 20 \; + \; 62.5 \; + \; 10 \; = \; 92.5\;\text{m} $

questions.text: Which of the following curves possibly represent one-dimensional motion of a particle? [FIGURE] (A) Phase versus time, (B) Velocity versus displacement, (C) Velocity versus time, (D) Total distance versus time.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Check whether each curve can be realised with motion along a single line and valid time values. // 📝 Solution: (A) $\phi = kt + C$ gives SHM-type motion $\implies$ possible; (B) $v^{2} + x^{2} = $ const $\implies$ possible; (C) time axis is circular, so negative time $\implies$ not possible; (D) distance never decreases $\implies$ possible

questions.text: A horse rider covers half the distance with $5\;\text{m/s}$ speed. The remaining part of the distance was travelled with speed $10\;\text{m/s}$ for half the time and with speed $15\;\text{m/s}$ for other half of the time. The mean speed of the rider averaged over the whole time of motion is $\frac{x}{7}\;\text{m/s}$. The value of $x$ is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Mean speed = total distance / total time; for equal time halves the speed is the arithmetic mean. // 📝 Solution: $ \text{Second half speed} \; = \; \frac{10 \; + \; 15}{2} \; = \; 12.5\;\text{m/s} \implies v_{avg} \; = \; \frac{2d}{\frac{d}{5} \; + \; \frac{d}{12.5}} \; = \; \frac{2 \; \times \; 25}{5 \; + \; 2} \; = \; \frac{50}{7} \implies x \; = \; 50 $

questions.text: An object moves with speed $v_1$, $v_2$, and $v_3$ along a line segment AB, BC and CD respectively as shown in figure. Where $AB \; = \; BC$ and $AD \; = \; 3 AB$, then average speed of the object will be : [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Equal segments imply average speed is the harmonic mean. // 📝 Solution: $ AB \; = \; BC \; = \; CD \; = \; x \implies \langle v \rangle \; = \; \frac{3x}{\frac{x}{v_1} \; + \; \frac{x}{v_2} \; + \; \frac{x}{v_3}} \; = \; \frac{3 v_1 v_2 v_3}{v_1 v_2 \; + \; v_2 v_3 \; + \; v_3 v_1} $

questions.text: A body falling under gravity covers two points $A$ and $B$ separated by $80\;\text{m}$ in $2\;\text{s}$. The distance of upper point $A$ from the starting point is _____ m (use $g \; = \; 10\;\text{ms}^{-2}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find the speed at A from s = ut + (1/2)gt^2 between A and B, then use v^2 = 2gh. // 📝 Solution: $ 80 \; = \; 2 v_A \; + \; \frac{1}{2} \left( 10 \right) \left( 4 \right) \implies v_A \; = \; 30\;\text{m/s} \implies h \; = \; \frac{v_A^2}{2g} \; = \; \frac{900}{20} \; = \; 45\;\text{m} $

questions.text: A body of mass $2\ \text{kg}$ moving with velocity $\vec{v}_{in} = 3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}\ \text{m/s}$ enters a constant force field of $6\ \text{N}$ directed along the positive $z$-axis. If the body remains in the field for $\frac{5}{3}\ \text{s}$, the velocity of the body when it emerges from the force field is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\vec{a} = \frac{\vec{F}}{m}$ and $\vec{v} = \vec{u} + \vec{a}t$. // 📝 Solution: $a = \frac{6}{2} = 3\ \text{m/s}^{2}\,\hat{k} \implies \vec{v} = (3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}) + 3\cdot\frac{5}{3}\hat{k} = 3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 5\hat{k}$

questions.text: A particle is moving in one dimension (along $x$ axis) under the action of a variable force. Its initial position was $16\;\text{m}$ right of origin. The variation of its position $\left( x \right)$ with time $\left( t \right)$ is given as $x \; = \; -3t^3 \; + \; 18t^2 \; + \; 16t$, where $x$ is in $\text{m}$ and $t$ is in $\text{s}$. The velocity of the particle when its acceleration becomes zero is ____ $\text{m/s}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Differentiate x twice, set a = 0 to get t, then substitute into v. // 📝 Solution: $ v \; = \; -9t^2 \; + \; 36t \; + \; 16, \; a \; = \; -18t \; + \; 36 \; = \; 0 \implies t \; = \; 2\;\text{s} \implies v \; = \; -36 \; + \; 72 \; + \; 16 \; = \; 52\;\text{m/s} $

questions.text: A particle initially at rest starts moving from reference point $x \; = \; 0$ along $x$-axis, with velocity $v$ that varies as $v \; = \; 4 \sqrt{x}\;\text{m/s}$. The acceleration of the particle is ____ $\text{ms}^{-2}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use a = v dv/dx. // 📝 Solution: $ a \; = \; v \frac{dv}{dx} \; = \; 4 \sqrt{x} \; \times \; 4 \; \times \; \frac{1}{2} x^{-1/2} \; = \; 8\;\text{m/s}^2 $

questions.text: The displacement $x$ versus time graph is shown below. [FIGURE] (A) The average velocity during $0$ to $3$ s is $10$ m/s. (B) The average velocity during $3$ to $5$ s is $0$ m/s. (C) The instantaneous velocity at $t = 2$ s is $5$ m/s. (D) The average velocity during $5$ to $7$ s and the instantaneous velocity at $t = 6.5$ s are equal. (E) The average velocity from $t = 0$ to $t = 9$ s is zero. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Average velocity $=\frac{\Delta x}{\Delta t}$; instantaneous velocity $=$ slope of $x$-$t$ graph. // 📝 Solution: (A) $\frac{5-0}{3} = \frac{5}{3}$ ✗; (B) $\frac{5-5}{2} = 0$ ✓; (C) slope on $2$–$3$ s $= 5$ ✓; (D) $\frac{0-5}{2} = -2.5$ vs slope at $6.5$ s $= -10$ ✗; (E) $\frac{0}{9} = 0$ ✓
questions.topic: x–t graph: average and instantaneous velocity

questions.text: A bullet is fired into a fixed target looses one third of its velocity after travelling $4\;\text{cm}$. It penetrates further $D \; \times \; 10^{-3}\;\text{m}$ before coming to rest. The value of D is : [We changed options. In official NTA paper no option was correct.]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Apply v^2 = u^2 - 2as for both stages with the same retardation. // 📝 Solution: $ \left( \frac{2u}{3} \right)^2 \; = \; u^2 \; - \; 2a \left( 4 \; \times \; 10^{-2} \right) \implies \frac{5u^2}{9} \; = \; 2a \left( 4 \; \times \; 10^{-2} \right), \; \frac{4u^2}{9} \; = \; 2ax \implies x \; = \; \frac{4}{5} \; \times \; 4 \; \times \; 10^{-2} \; = \; 32 \; \times \; 10^{-3}\;\text{m} $

questions.text: A small steel ball is dropped into a long cylinder containing glycerine. Which one of the following is the correct representation of the velocity time graph for the transit of the ball?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Drag increases with speed, so the ball approaches terminal velocity exponentially. // 📝 Solution: $ mg \; - \; F_B \; - \; 6 \pi \eta r v \; = \; m \frac{dv}{dt} \implies \frac{dv}{dt} \; = \; K_1 \; - \; K_2 v \implies v \; = \; \frac{K_1}{K_2} \left[ 1 \; - \; e^{-K_2 t} \right] $ , so the graph rises with decreasing slope and saturates (Option B).

questions.chapterName: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision
questions.text: In a system two particles of masses $m_{1} = 3 \; \text{kg}$ and $m_{2} = 2 \; \text{kg}$ are placed at certain distance from each other. The particle of mass $m_{1}$ is moved towards the center of mass of the system through a distance $2 \; \text{cm}$. In order to keep the center of mass of the system at the original position, the particle of mass $m_{2}$ should move towards the center of mass by the distance _____ cm.
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: $\Delta X_{\text{C.O.M.}} = \frac{m_{1} \Delta x_{1} + m_{2} \Delta x_{2}}{m_{1} + m_{2}} = 0$

📝 Solution:

Step 1: Using the center of mass shift formula for a stationary center of mass: $\Delta X_{\text{C.O.M.}} = \frac{m_{1} \Delta x_{1} + m_{2} \Delta x_{2}}{m_{1} + m_{2}} = 0$

Step 2: Substitute the given values: $\frac{3 \times 2 + 2 \left( - x \right)}{3 + 2} = 0$

Step 3: Solving for $x$: $6 - 2x = 0 \implies x = 3 \; \text{cm}$

questions.chapterName: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision
questions.text: [FIGURE] A simple pendulum of length $1\;\text{m}$ has a wooden bob of mass $1\;\text{kg}$. It is struck by a bullet of mass $10^{-2}\;\text{kg}$ moving with a speed of $2 \times 10^{2}\;\text{ms}^{-1}$. The bullet gets embedded into the bob. The height to which the bob rises before swinging back is. (use $g = 10\;\text{m/s}^{2}$)
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Use the principle of conservation of linear momentum during the collision followed by conservation of mechanical energy.

📝 Step 1: By conservation of linear momentum, $m u = \left( M + m \right) V$.

Step 2: Substitute the given values: $10^{-2} \times 2 \times 10^{2} \approx \left( 1 \right) V \implies V \approx 2\;\text{m/s}$.

Step 3: The height to which the combined mass rises is given by $h = \frac{V^{2}}{2 g} = \frac{2^{2}}{2 \times 10} = 0.2\;\text{m}$.

questions.chapterName: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision
questions.text:
A ball of mass $200 \; \text{g}$ rests on a vertical post of height $20 \; \text{m}$. A bullet of mass $10 \; \text{g}$, travelling in horizontal direction, hits the centre of the ball. After collision both travels independently. The ball hits the ground at a distance $30 \; \text{m}$ and the bullet at a distance of $120 \; \text{m}$ from the foot of the post. The value of initial velocity of the bullet will be $\left( \text{if} \; g \; = \; 10 \; \text{m/s}^2 \right)$:
(1) $120 \; \text{m/s}$
(2) $60 \; \text{m/s}$
(3) $400 \; \text{m/s}$
(4) $360 \; \text{m/s}$
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Determine the horizontal velocities of ball and bullet using projectile motion formulas, then apply conservation of linear momentum.

📝 Solution:

Step 1: Time of fall for both ball and bullet from height $h = 20 \; \text{m}$ is:

$t \; = \; \sqrt{\frac{2h}{g}} \; = \; \sqrt{\frac{2 \times 20}{10}} \; = \; 2 \; \text{s}$

Step 2: Velocity of ball after collision ($V_1$) and velocity of bullet after collision ($V_2$):

$V_1 \; = \; \frac{30}{t} \; = \; \frac{30}{\sqrt{\frac{2h}{g}}}$ and $V_2 \; = \; \frac{120}{\sqrt{\frac{2h}{g}}}$

Step 3: Applying conservation of momentum in the horizontal direction:

$m_{\text{bullet}} \cdot u \; = \; m_{\text{ball}} V_1 \; + \; m_{\text{bullet}} V_2$

$(0.01) u \; = \; (0.2) \frac{30 \sqrt{g}}{\sqrt{2h}} \; + \; (0.01) \frac{120 \sqrt{g}}{\sqrt{2h}}$

Step 4: Solving for $u$:

$u \; = \; 300 \; + \; 60 \; = \; 360 \; \text{ms}^{-1}$

questions.chapterName: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision
questions.text: 100 balls each of mass m moving with speed v simultaneously strike a wall normally and reflected back with same speed, in time t s. The total force exerted by the balls on the wall is
questions.solution: The initial momentum of 100 balls moving towards the wall is $\vec{P}_i = 100mv\hat{i}$. Since they are reflected back normally with the same speed, the final momentum is $\vec{P}_f = -100mv\hat{i}$. The change in momentum of the balls is $\Delta \vec{P} = \vec{P}_f - \vec{P}_i = -200mv\hat{i}$. The magnitude of force exerted on the wall by the balls is equal to the rate of change of momentum: $F = \frac{|\Delta \vec{P}|}{\Delta t} = \frac{200mv}{t}$.

questions.chapterName: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision
questions.text: A nucleus disintegrates into two smaller parts, which have their velocities in the ratio $3 \; : \; 2$. The ratio of their nuclear sizes will be $\left( \frac{1}{3} \right)^{\frac{1}{x}}$. The value of 'x' is :
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Use conservation of linear momentum to find mass ratio, and nuclear radius formula $R \propto A^{1/3}$.

📝 Solution:

Step 1: By conservation of linear momentum for the disintegrating nucleus:

$m_1 v_1 \; = \; m_2 v_2 \implies \frac{m_1}{m_2} \; = \; \frac{v_2}{v_1} \; = \; \frac{2}{3}$

Step 2: Since nuclear mass density is constant, mass is proportional to volume ($m \propto R^3$):

$\frac{m_1}{m_2} \; = \; \frac{\frac{4}{3} \pi r_1^3}{\frac{4}{3} \pi r_2^3} \; = \; \left( \frac{r_1}{r_2} \right)^{3}$

Step 3: Substituting the mass ratio:

$\left( \frac{r_1}{r_2} \right)^{3} \; = \; \frac{2}{3} \implies \frac{r_1}{r_2} \; = \; \left( \frac{2}{3} \right)^{\frac{1}{3}} \; = \; \left( \frac{1}{\frac{3}{2}} \right)^{\frac{1}{3}}$ wait, matching standard format $\left( \frac{1}{3} \right)^{\frac{1}{x}}$, we have $\frac{r_1}{r_2} \; = \; \left( \frac{1}{3} \right)^{\frac{1}{2}}$. Thus, $x = 2$.

questions.chapterName: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision
questions.text: If the total energy transferred to a surface in time $t$ is $6.48 \times 10^{5}\;\text{J}$, then the magnitude of the total momentum delivered to this surface for complete absorption will be :
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: For complete absorption of electromagnetic radiation, momentum $p$ is related to energy $E$ by $p = \frac{E}{c}$.

📝 Step 1: Substitute the given values of energy $E = 6.48 \times 10^{5}\;\text{J}$ and speed of light $c = 3 \times 10^{8}\;\text{m/s}$.

Step 2: Calculate momentum: $p = \frac{6.48 \times 10^{5}}{3 \times 10^{8}} = 2.16 \times 10^{-3}\;\text{kg}\;\text{m/s}$.

questions.chapterName: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision
questions.text:
Four particles $A, B, C, D$ of mass $\frac{m}{2}, m, 2m, 4m$, have same momentum, respectively. The particle with maximum kinetic energy is :
[FIGURE]
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Kinetic energy $KE = \frac{P^{2}}{2m}$ for a given momentum $P$.

📝 Solution:

Step 1: The relation between kinetic energy and momentum is given by $KE = \frac{P^{2}}{2m}$.

Step 2: Since all particles have the same momentum $P$, kinetic energy is inversely proportional to mass: $KE \propto \frac{1}{m}$.

Step 3: The particle with the minimum mass will have the maximum kinetic energy. Mass of particle $A$ is $\frac{m}{2}$, which is the smallest among all four, so particle $A$ has maximum kinetic energy.

questions.chapterName: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision
questions.text: Four particles A, B, C, D of mass $\frac{m}{2}$, m, 2m, 4m, have same momentum, respectively. The particle with maximum kinetic energy is :
questions.solution: Kinetic energy ($KE$) is given by $KE = \frac{p^2}{2m}$. Since all particles have the same momentum ($p$), the kinetic energy is inversely proportional to the mass ($KE \propto \frac{1}{m}$). Therefore, the particle with the least mass ($\frac{m}{2}$, which is particle A) will have the maximum kinetic energy.

questions.chapterName: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision
questions.text: [FIGURE] A uniform rod AB of mass $2\;\text{kg}$ and Length $30\;\text{cm}$ at rest on a smooth horizontal surface. An impulse of force $0.2\;\text{Ns}$ is applied to end B. The time taken by the rod to turn through at right angles will be $\frac{\pi}{x}\;\text{s}$, where $x =$_____
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Use the relation between impulse and angular momentum, $\vec{M} = \int \vec{\tau}\, dt$, and rotational kinematic equations.

📝 Step 1: Angular impulse $\vec{M}_{c} = \int \tau\, dt = \int \left( \frac{L}{2} \right) F\, dt = \frac{L}{2} \times J = \frac{0.3}{2} \times 0.2 = 0.03$.

Step 2: The moment of inertia of the rod about its center of mass is $I_{\text{cm}} = \frac{L^{2}}{12} = \frac{2 \times \left( 0.3 \right)^{2}}{12} = \frac{0.09}{6}$.

Step 3: Using $M = I_{\text{cm}} \omega_{f}$, we get $0.03 = \frac{0.09}{6} \omega_{f} \implies \omega_{f} = 2\;\text{rad/s}$.

Step 4: The time taken to turn through $\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}$ is $t = \frac{\theta}{\omega} = \frac{\pi / 2}{2} = \frac{\pi}{4}\;\text{s}$. Thus, $x = 4$.

questions.chapterName: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision
questions.text: As per the given figure, a small ball P slides down the quadrant of a circle and hits the other ball Q of equal mass which is initially at rest. Neglecting the effect of friction and assume the collision to be elastic, the velocity of ball Q after collision will be : ($g=10\text{ m/s}^2$)
questions.solution: When a small ball slides down a frictionless quadrant of a circle of radius $r = 20\text{ cm} = 0.2\text{ m}$, its velocity just before collision at the bottom is given by $v = \sqrt{2gh} = \sqrt{2 \times 10 \times 0.2} = \sqrt{4} = 2\text{ m/s}$. Since the collision is head-on and perfectly elastic ($e=1$) between two identical masses, their velocities get completely interchanged. Thus, ball P comes to rest, and ball Q moves with the velocity that ball P had before collision, which is $2\text{ m/s}$.

questions.chapterName: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision
questions.text: Three bodies A, B and C have equal kinetic energies and their masses are $400 \; \text{g}$, $1.2 \; \text{kg}$ and $1.6 \; \text{kg}$ respectively. The ratio of their linear momenta is :
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: $P = \sqrt{2mK}$ so $P \propto \sqrt{m}$ for equal kinetic energy.

📝 Solution:

Step 1: The relation between momentum and mass for equal kinetic energy is $P \propto \sqrt{m}$.

Step 2: Substitute the given masses in grams: $m_{A} = 400 \; \text{g}$, $m_{B} = 1200 \; \text{g}$, $m_{C} = 1600 \; \text{g}$.

Step 3: Taking the ratio of their momenta: $P_{A} : P_{B} : P_{C} = \sqrt{400} : \sqrt{1200} : \sqrt{1600} = 20 : 20\sqrt{3} : 40 = 1 : \sqrt{3} : 2$.

questions.chapterName: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision
questions.text: Three bodies A, B and C have equal kinetic energies and their masses are 400 g, 1.2 kg and 1.6 kg respectively. The ratio of their linear momenta is :
questions.solution: Kinetic energy is given by $KE = \frac{P^2}{2m} \implies P = \sqrt{2m \cdot KE}$. Since the kinetic energies are equal, the momentum is directly proportional to the square root of the mass ($P \propto \sqrt{m}$). Given the masses are $m_A = 0.4\text{ kg}$, $m_B = 1.2\text{ kg}$, and $m_C = 1.6\text{ kg}$, their ratio is $m_A : m_B : m_C = 400 : 1200 : 1600 = 1 : 3 : 4$. Thus, the ratio of their linear momenta is $P_A : P_B : P_C = \sqrt{1} : \sqrt{3} : \sqrt{4} = 1 : \sqrt{3} : 2$.

questions.chapterName: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision
questions.text: A body of mass $14\;\mathrm{kg}$ initially at rest explodes and breaks into three fragments of masses in the ratio $2 : 2 : 3$. The two pieces of equal masses fly off perpendicular to each other with a speed of $18\;\mathrm{m/s}$ each. The velocity of the heavier fragment is $\underline{\quad\quad\quad\quad}$ $\mathrm{m/s}$.
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Apply the law of conservation of linear momentum for an explosion in vector form.

📝 Solution:

Step 1: From mass ratio $2 : 2 : 3$ with total mass $14\;\mathrm{kg}$: individual masses are $\frac{2}{7} \times 14 = 4\;\mathrm{kg}$, $\frac{2}{7} \times 14 = 4\;\mathrm{kg}$, and $\frac{3}{7} \times 14 = 6\;\mathrm{kg}$.

Step 2: Setting coordinate axes along the motion directions of the two equal fragments: fragment 1 has momentum $\vec{p}_{1} = 4 \times 18 \; \hat{i} = 72 \; \hat{i}\;\mathrm{kg\cdot m/s}$, and fragment 2 has momentum $\vec{p}_{2} = 4 \times 18 \; \hat{j} = 72 \; \hat{j}\;\mathrm{kg\cdot m/s}$.

Step 3: By momentum conservation, initially at rest: $\vec{p}_{1} + \vec{p}_{2} + \vec{p}_{3} = 0$, so $\vec{p}_{3} = -72 \; \hat{i} - 72 \; \hat{j}\;\mathrm{kg\cdot m/s}$.

Step 4: Velocity of $6\;\mathrm{kg}$ fragment: $\vec{v}_{3} = \frac{\vec{p}_{3}}{6} = -12 \; \hat{i} - 12 \; \hat{j}\;\mathrm{m/s}$.

Step 5: Speed: $\left\lvert \vec{v}_{3} \right\rvert = \sqrt{144 + 144} = \sqrt{288} = 12 \sqrt{2}\;\mathrm{m/s}$.

questions.chapterName: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision
questions.text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I: For a mechanical system of many particles total kinetic energy is the sum of kinetic energies of all the particles.

Statement II: The total kinetic energy can be the sum of kinetic energy of the center of mass w.r.t to the origin and the kinetic energy of all the particles w.r.t. the center of mass as the reference.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.text: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true

questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Use the fundamental definition of total kinetic energy and Koenig's theorem (energy decomposition theorem).

📝 Solution:

Step 1: Statement I: Total kinetic energy of a system equals $\sum_{i} \frac{1}{2} m_{i} v_{i}^{2}$. This is TRUE by definition.

Step 2: Statement II: Total KE can be decomposed as $KE_{\text{total}} = \frac{1}{2} M v_{\text{cm}}^{2} + \sum_{i} \frac{1}{2} m_{i} {v^{\prime}_{i}}^{2}$, where the first term is kinetic energy of center of mass motion and the second is kinetic energy of particles relative to the center of mass. This is TRUE by the energy decomposition theorem (Koenig's theorem).

Step 3: Hence, both statements are true.

questions.chapterName: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision
questions.text: A player caught a cricket ball of mass 150 g moving at a speed of $20\text{ m/s}$. If the catching process is completed in 0.1 s, the magnitude of force exerted by the ball on the hand of the player is:
questions.solution: The magnitude of the average force exerted is given by Newton's second law: $F = \frac{\Delta P}{\Delta t} = \frac{mv - 0}{\Delta t}$. Substituting the given values: $F = \frac{150 \times 10^{-3}\text{ kg} \times 20\text{ m/s}}{0.1\text{ s}} = 30\text{ N}$.

questions.chapterName: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision
questions.text:
A uniform thin metal plate of mass $10 \; \text{kg}$ with dimensions is shown. The ratio of $x$ and $y$ coordinates of center of mass of plate in $\frac{n}{9}$. The value of $n$ is ________
[FIGURE]
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Divide the composite metal plate into simpler geometric shapes and apply $X_{\text{cm}} = \frac{\sum m_{i} x_{i}}{\sum m_{i}}$ and $Y_{\text{cm}} = \frac{\sum m_{i} y_{i}}{\sum m_{i}}$.

📝 Solution:

Step 1: Let the surface mass density be $\sigma$. The plate can be divided into parts where $m_{1} = \sigma \times 5 = 10 \; \text{kg}$, $m_{2} = \sigma \times 1 = 2 \; \text{kg}$, and total mass $m_{3} = m_{1} + m_{2} = 12 \; \text{kg}$ considering the completed block minus the cutout.

Step 2: Calculating $x$-coordinate of center of mass: $m_{1}x_{1} + m_{2}x_{2} = m_{3}x_{3} \implies 10x_{1} + 2(1.5) = 12(1.5) \implies x_{1} = 1.5 \; \text{cm}$.

Step 3: Calculating $y$-coordinate of center of mass: $m_{1}y_{1} + m_{2}y_{2} = m_{3}y_{3} \implies 10y_{1} + 2(1.5) = 12 \times 1 \implies y_{1} = 0.9 \; \text{cm}$.

Step 4: Taking the ratio $\frac{x_{1}}{y_{1}} = \frac{1.5}{0.9} = \frac{15}{9}$, which gives $n = 15$.
questions.topic: Center of Mass of Continuous Bodies

questions.chapterName: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision
questions.text: A ball of mass 200 g rests on a vertical post of height 20 m. A bullet of mass 10 g, travelling in a horizontal direction, hits the centre of the ball. After collision both travels independently. The ball hits the ground at a distance 30 m and the bullet at a distance of 120 m from the foot of the post. The value of initial velocity of the bullet will be (if $g=10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.solution: The time taken for both objects to reach the ground after colliding on top of the vertical post of height $h=20\text{ m}$ is $t = \sqrt{\frac{2h}{g}} = \sqrt{\frac{2 \times 20}{10}} = 2\text{ s}$. The horizontal velocity of the ball after collision is $v_1 = \frac{30\text{ m}}{2\text{ s}} = 15\text{ m/s}$. The horizontal velocity of the bullet after collision is $v_2 = \frac{120\text{ m}}{2\text{ s}} = 60\text{ m/s}$. Applying linear momentum conservation along the horizontal direction: $m_{bullet} u = m_{ball} v_1 + m_{bullet} v_2 \implies (0.01)u = (0.2)(15) + (0.01)(60) \implies 0.01u = 3 + 0.6 = 3.6 \implies u = 360\text{ m/s}$.

questions.chapterName: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision
questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: For a mechanical system of many particles total kinetic energy is the sum of kinetic energies of all the particles.
Statement II: The total kinetic energy can be the sum of kinetic energy of the center of mass w.r.t to the origin and the kinetic energy of all the particles w.r.t. the center of mass as the reference.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true

questions.solution: Statement I is true by definition since the total kinetic energy of a multi-particle system is given by $\sum \frac{1}{2}m_i v_i^2$. Statement II is true according to Koenig's theorem (energy decomposition theorem), which states that $KE_{total} = \frac{1}{2}M v_{cm}^2 + \sum \frac{1}{2}m_i v_i'^2$, where the first term is the kinetic energy of the center of mass motion and the second term is the kinetic energy of the particles relative to the center of mass.

questions.chapterName: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision
questions.text: A body of mass $2\;\text{kg}$ moving at $5\;\text{m/s}$ collides head-on with a stationary body of mass $3\;\text{kg}$ and they stick together. The common velocity is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Apply conservation of momentum. // 📝 Solution: $2\left( 5 \right) \; + \; 3\left( 0 \right) \; = \; \left( 2 \; + \; 3 \right)v \implies v \; = \; 2\;\text{m/s}$

questions.chapterName: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision
questions.text: A spherical body of mass $100\;\text{g}$ is dropped from a height of $10\;\text{m}$ from the ground. After hitting the ground, the body rebounds to a height of $5\;\text{m}$. The impulse of force imparted by the ground to the body is given by: (given $g = 9.8\;\text{m/s}^{2}$)
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Impulse is equal to the change in linear momentum, $\vec{I} = \Delta \vec{P} = \vec{P}_{f} - \vec{P}_{i}$.

📝 Step 1: Identify mass $M = 0.1\;\text{kg}$, velocity just before impact $v_{i} = -\sqrt{2 g h_{1}} = -\sqrt{2 \times 9.8 \times 10}$, and velocity just after impact $v_{f} = \sqrt{2 g h_{2}} = \sqrt{2 \times 9.8 \times 5}$.

Step 2: Substitute into the impulse formula: $I = \Delta P = 0.1 \left( \sqrt{2 \times 9.8 \times 5} - \left( -\sqrt{2 \times 9.8 \times 10} \right) \right)$.

Step 3: Simplify the expression: $I = 0.1 \left( 14 + 7\sqrt{2} \right) \approx 2.39\;\text{kg}\;\text{ms}^{-1}$.

questions.chapterName: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision
questions.text: Figures (a), (b), (c) and (d) show variation of force with time. The impulse is highest in figure:
questions.solution:
Impulse is equal to the area under the Force-time ($F-t$) curve. Let's calculate the area for each figure:
(a) Area = $\frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} \times 1.0 \times 0.5 = 0.25\text{ N}\cdot\text{s}$
(b) Area = $\text{width} \times \text{height} = 2.0 \times 0.5 = 1.0\text{ N}\cdot\text{s}$
(c) Area = $\frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} \times 1.0 \times 0.75 = 0.375\text{ N}\cdot\text{s}$
(d) Area = $\frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} \times 2.0 \times 0.5 = 0.5\text{ N}\cdot\text{s}$
Comparing the values, Fig (b) yields the highest impulse ($1.0\text{ N}\cdot\text{s}$).

questions.chapterName: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision
questions.text: A ball is dropped from a height of $20\;\text{m}$ onto a floor. If the coefficient of restitution is $0.5$, the height reached after the first rebound is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Rebound height scales as $e^2$. // 📝 Solution: $h' \; = \; e^2 h \; = \; \left( 0.5 \right)^2\left( 20 \right) \; = \; 5\;\text{m}$

questions.chapterName: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision
questions.text: In a perfectly inelastic collision, two spheres made of the same material with masses 15 kg and 25 kg, moving in opposite directions with speeds of $10\text{ m/s}$ and $30\text{ m/s}$ respectively, strike each other and stick together. The rise in temperature (in Â°C), if all the heat produced during the collision is retained by these spheres, is: (specific heat of sphere material $31\text{ cal/kg} \cdot \text{Â°C}$ and 1 cal = $4.2\text{ J}$)
questions.solution: Using conservation of linear momentum: $m_1 v_1 + m_2 v_2 = (m_1 + m_2) v_f$. Taking the direction of the first sphere as positive: $15(10) + 25(-30) = 40 v_f \implies 150 - 750 = 40 v_f \implies v_f = -15\text{ m/s}$. The initial kinetic energy is $KE_i = \frac{1}{2}(15)(10)^2 + \frac{1}{2}(25)(30)^2 = 750 + 11250 = 12000\text{ J}$. The final kinetic energy is $KE_f = \frac{1}{2}(40)(-15)^2 = 4500\text{ J}$. The heat produced is the loss in kinetic energy: $Q = KE_i - KE_f = 12000 - 4500 = 7500\text{ J}$. Converting to calories: $Q = \frac{7500}{4.2} \approx 1785.71\text{ cal}$. The temperature rise is given by $\Delta T = \frac{Q}{m_{total} \cdot c} = \frac{1785.71}{40 \times 31} \approx 1.44\text{Â°C}$.

questions.chapterName: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision
questions.text: A solid circular disc of mass $50\;\text{kg}$ rolls along a horizontal floor so that its center of mass has a speed of $0.4\;\text{m/s}$. The absolute value of work done on the disc to stop it is_____ J.
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Use the work-energy theorem, $W = \Delta \text{KE} = \text{KE}_{f} - \text{KE}_{i}$.

📝 Step 1: Initial kinetic energy of rolling disc is $\text{KE}_{i} = \frac{1}{2} m v^{2} + \frac{1}{2} I \omega^{2} = \frac{1}{2} m v^{2} \left( 1 + \frac{K^{2}}{R^{2}} \right)$.

Step 2: For a solid disc, $\frac{K^{2}}{R^{2}} = \frac{1}{2}$. Substitute the values: $W = 0 - \frac{1}{2} \times 50 \times \left( 0.4 \right)^{2} \left( 1 + \frac{1}{2} \right) = -6\;\text{J}$.

Step 3: Taking the absolute value, $\left\lvert W \right\rvert = 6\;\text{J}$.

questions.chapterName: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision
questions.text: A machine gun of mass 10 kg fires 20 g bullets at the rate of 180 bullets per minute with a speed of 100 m s$^{-1}$ each. The recoil velocity of the gun is :
questions.solution: The rate of firing bullets is $n = \frac{180}{60} = 3\text{ bullets/second}$. By conservation of linear momentum, the momentum imparted per second to the bullets must be balanced by the momentum change per second of the gun: $M_{gun} V_{recoil} = n \cdot m_{bullet} \cdot v_{bullet} \implies 10 \times V_{recoil} = 3 \times (20 \times 10^{-3}\text{ kg}) \times 100\text{ m/s} \implies 10 \times V_{recoil} = 6 \implies V_{recoil} = 0.6\text{ m/s}$.

questions.chapterName: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision
