questions.text: A spherical body of mass 100 g is dropped from a height of 10 m from the ground. After hitting the ground, the body rebounds to a height of 5 m. The impulse of force imparted by the ground to the body is given by (given $g=9.8\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.solution: The velocity just before hitting the ground is $v_i = -\sqrt{2gh_1} = -\sqrt{2 \times 9.8 \times 10} = -\sqrt{196} = -14\text{ m/s}$. The velocity just after rebounding is $v_f = +\sqrt{2gh_2} = +\sqrt{2 \times 9.8 \times 5} = +\sqrt{98} = 7\sqrt{2}\text{ m/s} \approx 9.9\text{ m/s}$. The magnitude of the impulse is given by the change in momentum: $I = \Delta P = m(v_f - v_i) = 0.1\text{ kg} \times (14 + 7\sqrt{2}) \approx 0.1 \times (14 + 9.9) = 2.39\text{ kg ms}^{-1}$.

questions.chapterName: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision
questions.text: A body of mass $1 \; \text{kg}$ collides head on elastically with a stationary body of mass $3 \; \text{kg}$. After collision, the smaller body reverses its direction of motion and moves with a speed of $2 \; \text{m/s}$. The initial speed of the smaller body before collision is $\text{ms}^{-1}$.
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Use conservation of linear momentum and the restitution equation for elastic collisions.

📝 Solution:

Step 1: Let the initial speed of the $1 \; \text{kg}$ mass be $u_1$. Applying conservation of linear momentum:

$1 \times u_1 \; = \; -2 \; + \; 3v \implies u_1 \; = \; -2 \; + \; 3v \quad \text{--- (1)}$

Step 2: Using the coefficient of restitution $e = 1$ for an elastic collision:

$1 \; = \; \frac{\left( v \; - \; (-2) \right)}{u_1 - 0} \implies v \; + \; 2 \; = \; u_1 \quad \text{--- (2)}$

Step 3: Solving equations (1) and (2) simultaneously, we get:

$u_1 \; = \; 4 \; \text{m/s}$

questions.chapterName: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision
questions.text: In a perfectly inelastic collision, two spheres made of the same material with masses $15\;\mathrm{kg}$ and $25\;\mathrm{kg}$, moving in opposite directions with speeds of $10\;\mathrm{m/s}$ and $30\;\mathrm{m/s}$, respectively, strike each other and stick together. The rise in temperature (in $^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$), if all the heat produced during the collision is retained by these spheres, is : \left(\text{specific heat of sphere material } 31\;\mathrm{cal/kg}\cdot^{\circ}\mathrm{C} \text{ and } 1\;\mathrm{cal} = 4.2\;\mathrm{J}\right)
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: The heat produced in an inelastic collision is equal to the loss in kinetic energy, which then raises the temperature of the combined mass according to $Q = m c \Delta T$.

📝 Solution:

Step 1: Using conservation of momentum: $m_{1} v_{1} + m_{2} v_{2} = \left( m_{1} + m_{2} \right) v_{f}$, where $v_{2} = -30\;\mathrm{m/s}$ (opposite direction).

$15 \left( 10 \right) + 25 \left( -30 \right) = 40 v_{f} \implies v_{f} = -15\;\mathrm{m/s}$.

Step 2: Initial kinetic energy: $KE_{i} = \frac{1}{2} \left( 15 \right) \left( 10 \right)^{2} + \frac{1}{2} \left( 25 \right) \left( 30 \right)^{2} = 750 + 11250 = 12000\;\mathrm{J}$.

Final kinetic energy: $KE_{f} = \frac{1}{2} \left( 40 \right) \left( 15 \right)^{2} = 4500\;\mathrm{J}$.

Step 3: Heat produced: $Q = 12000 - 4500 = 7500\;\mathrm{J} = \frac{7500}{4.2} = 1785.71\;\mathrm{cal}$.

Temperature rise: $\Delta T = \frac{Q}{m_{\text{total}} \cdot c} = \frac{1785.71}{40 \times 31} = 1.44^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$.

questions.chapterName: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision
questions.text: A body of mass 14 kg initially at rest explodes and breaks into three fragments of masses in the ratio $2:2:3$. The two pieces of equal masses fly off perpendicular to each other with a speed of $18\text{ m/s}$ each. The velocity of the heavier fragment is ______ $m/s$.
questions.solution: From the mass ratio $2:2:3$ and total mass of $14\text{ kg}$, the individual masses are $4\text{ kg}$, $4\text{ kg}$, and $6\text{ kg}$. Let the directions of the two perpendicular equal fragments be along the x and y axes. Their respective momenta are $\vec{p}_1 = 4 \times 18\hat{i} = 72\hat{i}\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m/s}$ and $\vec{p}_2 = 4 \times 18\hat{j} = 72\hat{j}\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m/s}$. By conservation of momentum, since the body was initially at rest: $\vec{p}_1 + \vec{p}_2 + \vec{p}_3 = 0 \implies \vec{p}_3 = -72\hat{i} - 72\hat{j}$. The velocity of the $6\text{ kg}$ fragment is $\vec{v}_3 = \frac{\vec{p}_3}{6} = -12\hat{i} - 12\hat{j}\text{ m/s}$. The magnitude of this velocity (speed) is $|\vec{v}_3| = \sqrt{(-12)^2 + (-12)^2} = \sqrt{288} = 12\sqrt{2}\text{ m/s}$.

questions.chapterName: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision
questions.text: A shell at rest explodes into two fragments of masses in the ratio $1:2$. The ratio of the kinetic energy of the lighter fragment to that of the heavier fragment is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Momenta of the fragments are equal and opposite, and $K \; = \; \dfrac{p^2}{2m}$. // 📝 Solution: $K \; \propto \; \dfrac{1}{m} \implies \dfrac{K_1}{K_2} \; = \; \dfrac{m_2}{m_1} \; = \; \dfrac{2}{1}$

questions.chapterName: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision
questions.text: A player caught a cricket ball of mass $150 \; \text{g}$ moving at a speed of $20 \; \text{m/s}$. If the catching process is completed in $0.1 \; \text{s}$, the magnitude of force exerted by the ball on the hand of the player is:
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: $F = \frac{\Delta P}{\Delta t} = \frac{mv - 0}{\Delta t}$

📝 Solution:

Step 1: Force is equal to the rate of change of momentum: $F = \frac{\Delta P}{\Delta t} = \frac{mv - 0}{\Delta t}$.

Step 2: Substitute the given values: $m = 150 \times 10^{-3} \; \text{kg}$, $v = 20 \; \text{m/s}$, and $\Delta t = 0.1 \; \text{s}$.

Step 3: Calculate the force: $F = \frac{150 \times 10^{-3} \times 20}{0.1} = \frac{3}{0.1} = 30 \; \text{N}$.

questions.chapterName: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision
questions.text: When kinetic energy of a body becomes 36 times of its original value, the percentage increase in the momentum of the body will be:
questions.solution: Kinetic energy is given by $K = \frac{P^2}{2m} \implies P = \sqrt{2mK}$. If the final kinetic energy becomes 36 times the initial value ($K_f = 36K_i$), then the final momentum becomes $P_f = \sqrt{36} P_i = 6P_i$. The percentage increase in momentum is calculated as: $\frac{P_f - P_i}{P_i} \times 100\% = \frac{6P_i - P_i}{P_i} \times 100\% = 500\%$.

questions.chapterName: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision
questions.text: Two spherical bodies of masses $M$ and $5M$ and radii $R$ and $2R$ respectively are released in free space with an initial separation of $12R$ between their centres. If they attract each other due to gravity only, the distance travelled by the smaller body just before collision is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The centre of mass stays fixed, so the displacements are inversely proportional to the masses. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Centres meet at separation } 3R \implies \text{relative displacement} \; = \; 12R \; - \; 3R \; = \; 9R \implies x_{small} \; = \; \dfrac{5M}{6M}\left( 9R \right) \; = \; 7.5R$

questions.text: A bullet of mass $20\;\text{g}$ moving at $500\;\text{m/s}$ embeds in a wooden block of mass $4.98\;\text{kg}$ at rest on a smooth surface. The speed of the combined system just after impact is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Conserve linear momentum in a perfectly inelastic collision. // 📝 Solution: $0.02\left( 500 \right) \; = \; \left( 0.02 \; + \; 4.98 \right)v \implies v \; = \; \dfrac{10}{5} \; = \; 2\;\text{m/s}$

questions.text: Particles of masses $1\;\text{kg}$, $2\;\text{kg}$ and $3\;\text{kg}$ are placed at $\left( 0, 0 \right)$, $\left( 3, 0 \right)$ and $\left( 0, 2 \right)$ respectively (in metres). The coordinates of the centre of mass are
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $x_{cm} \; = \; \dfrac{\sum m_i x_i}{\sum m_i}$. // 📝 Solution: $x_{cm} \; = \; \dfrac{2\left( 3 \right)}{6} \; = \; 1, \; y_{cm} \; = \; \dfrac{3\left( 2 \right)}{6} \; = \; 1$

questions.chapterName: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision
questions.text: [FIGURE] The identical spheres each of mass $2M$ are placed at the corners of a right angled triangle with mutually perpendicular sides equal to $4\;\text{m}$ each. Taking point of intersection of these two sides as origin, the magnitude of position vector of the centre of mass of the system is $\frac{4\sqrt{2}}{x}$, where the value of $x$ is_____
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Use the position vector formula for the center of mass of a discrete system of particles: $\vec{r}_{\text{COM}} = \frac{m_{1}\vec{r}_{1} + m_{2}\vec{r}_{2} + m_{3}\vec{r}_{3}}{m_{1} + m_{2} + m_{3}}$.

📝 Step 1: Let the masses be located at $\left( 0, 0 \right)$, $\left( 4, 0 \right)$, and $\left( 0, 4 \right)$.

Step 2: Calculate the center of mass position vector: $\vec{r}_{\text{COM}} = \frac{2M \times 0 + 2M \times 4\hat{i} + 2M \times 4\hat{j}}{6M} = \frac{4}{3}\hat{i} + \frac{4}{3}\hat{j}$.

Step 3: Find the magnitude: $\left\lvert \vec{r} \right\rvert = \sqrt{\left( \frac{4}{3} \right)^{2} + \left( \frac{4}{3} \right)^{2}} = \frac{4\sqrt{2}}{3}$. Comparing with $\frac{4\sqrt{2}}{x}$, we get $x = 3$.

questions.chapterName: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision
questions.text: A simple pendulum of length 1 m has a wooden bob of mass 1 kg. It is struck by a bullet of mass $10^{-2}\text{ kg}$ moving with a speed of $2 \times 10^2\text{ ms}^{-1}$. The bullet gets embedded into the bob. The height to which the bob rises before swinging back is (use $g=10\text{ m/s}^2$):
questions.solution: Using the principle of conservation of linear momentum during the collision: $m u = (M + m) V \implies 10^{-2} \times (2 \times 10^2) = (1 + 10^{-2}) V$. Since $m \ll M$, we can approximate $M + m \approx 1\text{ kg}$, which gives $2 = 1 \times V \implies V \approx 2\text{ m/s}$. After the collision, applying conservation of mechanical energy as the bob rises to a height $h$: $(M+m)gh = \frac{1}{2}(M+m)V^2 \implies h = \frac{V^2}{2g} = \frac{2^2}{2 \times 10} = 0.20\text{ m}$.

questions.chapterName: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision
questions.text: If the total energy transferred to a surface in time t is $6.48 \times 10^5\text{ J}$, then the magnitude of the total momentum delivered to this surface for complete absorption will be :
questions.solution: For complete absorption of radiation/energy, the momentum delivered is given by the relation $p = \frac{E}{c}$, where $E$ is the total energy transferred and $c$ is the speed of light ($3 \times 10^8\text{ m/s}$). Substituting the values: $p = \frac{6.48 \times 10^5}{3 \times 10^8} = 2.16 \times 10^{-3}\text{ kg m/s}$.

questions.text: The angle between vector $\vec{Q}$ and the resultant of $(2\vec{Q}+2\vec{P})$ and $(2\vec{Q}-2\vec{P})$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Add the two vectors first; if the sum is parallel to $\vec{Q}$, the angle is zero. // 📝 Solution: $\vec{R}=\left(2\vec{Q}+2\vec{P}\right)+\left(2\vec{Q}-2\vec{P}\right)=4\vec{Q}\;\implies\;\theta=0^{\circ}$
questions.topic: Resultant of vectors and angle between vectors

questions.text: If two vectors $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ having equal magnitude $R$ are inclined at an angle $\theta$, then:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $\left\lvert\vec{A}+\vec{B}\right\rvert^{2}=A^{2}+B^{2}+2AB\cos\theta$ and the half-angle identity. // 📝 Solution: $\left\lvert\vec{A}+\vec{B}\right\rvert^{2}=2R^{2}+2R^{2}\cos\theta=4R^{2}\cos^{2}\frac{\theta}{2}\;\implies\;\left\lvert\vec{A}+\vec{B}\right\rvert=2R\cos\frac{\theta}{2}$

questions.text: Two forces $\vec{F}_{1}$ and $\vec{F}_{2}$ act on a body. One force has magnitude thrice that of the other and the resultant equals the force of larger magnitude. The angle between $\vec{F}_{1}$ and $\vec{F}_{2}$ is $\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{n}\right)$. The value of $\left\lvert n\right\rvert$ is ______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $R^{2}=F_{1}^{2}+F_{2}^{2}+2F_{1}F_{2}\cos\theta$. // 📝 Solution: Let $F_{1}=F,\;F_{2}=3F,\;R=3F$ $\;\implies\;9F^{2}=F^{2}+9F^{2}+6F^{2}\cos\theta$ $\;\implies\;\cos\theta=-\frac{1}{6}\;\implies\;n=-6\;\implies\;\left\lvert n\right\rvert=6$

questions.text: If $\vec{P}=3\hat{i}+\sqrt{3}\hat{j}+2\hat{k}$ and $\vec{Q}=4\hat{i}+\sqrt{3}\hat{j}+2.5\hat{k}$, then the unit vector in the direction of $\vec{P}\times\vec{Q}$ is $\frac{1}{x}\left(\sqrt{3}\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\sqrt{3}\hat{k}\right)$. The value of $x$ is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Evaluate the cross product by determinant, then divide by its magnitude. // 📝 Solution: $\vec{P}\times\vec{Q}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\hat{i}+\frac{1}{2}\hat{j}-\sqrt{3}\hat{k}$ $\;\implies\;\left\lvert\vec{P}\times\vec{Q}\right\rvert=\sqrt{\frac{3}{4}+\frac{1}{4}+3}=2$ $\;\implies\;\frac{\vec{P}\times\vec{Q}}{2}=\frac{1}{4}\left(\sqrt{3}\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\sqrt{3}\hat{k}\right)\;\implies\;x=4$

questions.text: Three vectors $\overrightarrow{OP}$, $\overrightarrow{OQ}$ and $\overrightarrow{OR}$, each of magnitude $A$, act as shown in the figure: [FIGURE]. The resultant of the three vectors is $A\sqrt{x}$. The value of $x$ is ______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Resolve each vector into x and y components and find the magnitude of the resultant. // 📝 Solution: $\overrightarrow{OP}=A\hat{i},\;\overrightarrow{OQ}=A\hat{j},\;\overrightarrow{OR}=\frac{A}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{i}-\frac{A}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{j}$ $\;\implies\;\vec{R}=\left(A+\frac{A}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\hat{i}+\left(A-\frac{A}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\hat{j}$ $\;\implies\;\left\lvert\vec{R}\right\rvert=\sqrt{3}A\;\implies\;x=3$

questions.text: A vector $\vec{N}$ has magnitude same as that of $\vec{A}=3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}$ and is parallel to $\vec{B}=4\hat{i}+3\hat{j}$. The $x$ and $y$ components of this vector in the first quadrant are $x$ and $3$, respectively, where $x=$ ______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A vector parallel to $\vec{B}$ with magnitude $\left\lvert\vec{A}\right\rvert$ equals $\left\lvert\vec{A}\right\rvert\hat{B}$. // 📝 Solution: $\left\lvert\vec{A}\right\rvert=\sqrt{9+16}=5$, $\hat{B}=\frac{4\hat{i}+3\hat{j}}{5}\;\implies\;\vec{N}=5\hat{B}=4\hat{i}+3\hat{j}\;\implies\;x=4$

questions.text: The resultant of two vectors $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{A}$ and its magnitude is half that of $\vec{B}$. The angle between vectors $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ is ______ $^{\circ}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Resolve $\vec{B}$ along the direction of the resultant, which is perpendicular to $\vec{A}$. // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] $\;\implies\;B\cos\theta=\frac{B}{2}\;\implies\;\theta=60^{\circ}$ $\;\implies\;$ angle between $\vec{A}$ and $\vec{B}$ $=90^{\circ}+60^{\circ}=150^{\circ}$

questions.text: If $\vec{P}=\hat{i}+2m\hat{j}+m\hat{k}$ and $\vec{Q}=4\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+m\hat{k}$ are perpendicular to each other, then the value of $m$ will be:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Perpendicular vectors satisfy $\vec{P}\cdot\vec{Q}=0$. // 📝 Solution: $\vec{P}\cdot\vec{Q}=4-4m+m^{2}=0\;\implies\;\left(m-2\right)^{2}=0\;\implies\;m=2$
questions.topic: Dot product condition for perpendicular vectors

questions.text: If $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ make an angle $\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{9}\right)$ with each other, then $\left\lvert\vec{a}+\vec{b}\right\rvert=\sqrt{2}\left\lvert\vec{a}-\vec{b}\right\rvert$ for $\left\lvert\vec{a}\right\rvert=n\left\lvert\vec{b}\right\rvert$. The integer value of $n$ is ______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Square both sides and expand using $\left\lvert\vec{a}\pm\vec{b}\right\rvert^{2}=a^{2}+b^{2}\pm2\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}$. // 📝 Solution: $6\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=a^{2}+b^{2}\;\implies\;\frac{10}{3}ab=a^{2}+b^{2}$ $\;\implies\;$ with $a=nb$: $3n^{2}-10n+3=0\;\implies\;n=3\;\text{or}\;\frac{1}{3}\;\implies\;n=3$
questions.topic: Magnitude of sum and difference of vectors

questions.text: Vectors $a\hat{i}+b\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ and $2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+4\hat{k}$ are perpendicular to each other when $3a+2b\;=\;7$. The ratio of $a$ to $b$ is $\frac{x}{2}$. The value of $x$ is ______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Perpendicular vectors have zero dot product, so solve the resulting pair of linear equations. // 📝 Solution: $\left(a\hat{i}+b\hat{j}+\hat{k}\right)\cdot\left(2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+4\hat{k}\right)=0\;\implies\;2a-3b=-4$ $\;\implies\;$ with $3a+2b=7$: $a=1,\;b=2$ $\;\implies\;\frac{a}{b}=\frac{x}{2}\;\implies\;x=\frac{2a}{b}=1$
questions.topic: Dot product and perpendicularity of vectors

questions.text: For three vectors $\vec{A}=\left(-x\hat{i}-6\hat{j}-2\hat{k}\right)$, $\vec{B}=\left(-\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\right)$ and $\vec{C}=\left(-8\hat{i}-\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\right)$, if $\vec{A}\cdot\left(\vec{B}\times\vec{C}\right)=0$, then the value of $x$ is ______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The scalar triple product equals the determinant of the component matrix. // 📝 Solution: $\vec{B}\times\vec{C}=15\hat{i}-21\hat{j}+33\hat{k}\;\implies\;\vec{A}\cdot\left(\vec{B}\times\vec{C}\right)=-15x+126-66=0$ $\;\implies\;15x=60\;\implies\;x=4$

questions.text: A particle moves in $x-y$ plane under the influence of a force $\vec{F}$ such that its linear momentum is $\vec{p}(t)=\hat{i}\cos(kt)-\hat{j}\sin(kt)$. If $k$ is constant, the angle between $\vec{F}$ and $\vec{p}$ will be:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Force is the time derivative of momentum; check the dot product of $\vec{F}$ and $\vec{p}$. // 📝 Solution: $\vec{F}=\frac{d\vec{p}}{dt}=-k\sin(kt)\hat{i}-k\cos(kt)\hat{j}$ $\;\implies\;\vec{F}\cdot\vec{p}=-k\sin(kt)\cos(kt)+k\cos(kt)\sin(kt)=0\;\implies\;\theta=\frac{\pi}{2}$
