questions.text: A mass $m$ is suspended from a spring of negligible mass and the system oscillates with a frequency $f_1$. The frequency of oscillations if a mass $9m$ is suspended from the same spring is $f_2$. The value of $\frac{f_1}{f_2}$ is _____.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $f\;=\;\frac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\frac{k}{m}}$, so $f\;\propto\;\frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{f_1}{f_2}\;=\;\sqrt{\frac{9m}{m}}\;=\;\sqrt{9}\;=\;3$

questions.text: Two blocks with masses $100\;\text{g}$ and $200\;\text{g}$ are attached to the ends of springs $A$ and $B$ as shown in figure. The energy stored in $A$ is $E$. The energy stored in $B$, when spring constants $k_A,\;k_B$ of $A$ and $B$, respectively satisfy the relation $4k_A\;=\;3k_B$, is : [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Static extension is $x\;=\;\frac{mg}{k}$ and stored energy is $\frac{1}{2}kx^{2}\;=\;\frac{m^{2}g^{2}}{2k}$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{U_B}{E}\;=\;\frac{m_B^{2}}{m_A^{2}}\cdot\frac{k_A}{k_B}\;=\;4\times\frac{3}{4}\;=\;3\;\implies\;U_B\;=\;3E$

questions.text: A ball suspended by a thread swings in a vertical plane so that its magnitude of acceleration in the extreme position and lowest position are equal. The angle $\left(\theta\right)$ of thread deflection in the extreme position will be :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Compare $\frac{v^{2}}{\ell}$ at the lowest point with $g\sin\theta$ at the extreme point, and use energy conservation. // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] $\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}\;=\;mg\ell\left(1\;-\;\cos\theta\right)\;\implies\;\frac{v^{2}}{\ell}\;=\;2g\left(1\;-\;\cos\theta\right)\;=\;g\sin\theta\;\implies\;\tan\frac{\theta}{2}\;=\;\frac{1}{2}\;\implies\;\theta\;=\;2\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$

questions.text: An object of mass $0.2\;\text{kg}$ executes simple harmonic motion along $x$ axis with frequency of $\left(\frac{25}{\pi}\right)\;\text{Hz}$. At the position $x\;=\;0.04\;\text{m}$ the object has kinetic energy $0.5\;\text{J}$ and potential energy $0.4\;\text{J}$. The amplitude of oscillation is _____ cm.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Total energy $E\;=\;KE\;+\;PE\;=\;\frac{1}{2}m\omega^{2}A^{2}$. // 📝 Solution: $E\;=\;0.9\;\text{J}\;,\;\omega\;=\;2\pi\times\frac{25}{\pi}\;=\;50\;\implies\;\frac{1}{2}\left(0.2\right)\left(2500\right)A^{2}\;=\;0.9\;\implies\;A\;=\;0.06\;\text{m}\;=\;6\;\text{cm}$

questions.text: A body of mass $200\;\text{g}$ is tied to a spring of spring constant $12.5\;\text{N/m}$, while the other end of spring is fixed at point O. If the body moves about O in a circular path on a smooth horizontal surface with constant angular speed $5\;\text{rad/s}$, then the ratio of extension in the spring to its natural length will be :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The spring force provides the centripetal force: $kx\;=\;m\left(L_0\;+\;x\right)\omega^{2}$. // 📝 Solution: $12.5\,x\;=\;\frac{1}{5}\left(L_0\;+\;x\right)\left(25\right)\;\implies\;12.5\,x\;=\;5\left(L_0\;+\;x\right)\;\implies\;1.5\,x\;=\;L_0\;\implies\;\frac{x}{L_0}\;=\;\frac{2}{3}$

questions.text: As shown in the figure, a spring is kept in a stretched position with some extension by holding the masses $1\;\text{kg}$ and $0.2\;\text{kg}$ with a separation more than spring natural length and are released. Assuming the horizontal surface to be frictionless, the angular frequency $\left(\text{in SI unit}\right)$ of the system is : $k\;=\;150\;\text{N/m}$ [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A two-body spring system oscillates with reduced mass $\mu\;=\;\frac{m_1 m_2}{m_1\;+\;m_2}$. // 📝 Solution: $\mu\;=\;\frac{1\times 0.2}{1.2}\;=\;\frac{1}{6}\;\text{kg}\;\implies\;\omega\;=\;\sqrt{\frac{k}{\mu}}\;=\;\sqrt{\frac{150}{1/6}}\;=\;\sqrt{900}\;=\;30\;\text{rad/s}$

questions.text: When the displacement of a simple harmonic oscillator is one third of its amplitude, the ratio of total energy to the kinetic energy is $\frac{x}{8}$, where $x\;=$ _____ .
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $PE\;\propto\;x^{2}$ and $KE\;=\;E\;-\;PE$. // 📝 Solution: $U\;=\;\frac{1}{2}K\left(\frac{A}{3}\right)^{2}\;=\;\frac{E}{9}\;\implies\;KE\;=\;\frac{8E}{9}\;\implies\;\frac{E}{KE}\;=\;\frac{9}{8}\;\implies\;x\;=\;9$

questions.text: The velocity of a particle executing SHM varies with displacement $x$ as $4v^{2}\;=\;50\;-\;x^{2}$. The time period of oscillations is $\frac{x}{7}\;\text{s}$. The value of $x$ is ........ $\left(\text{Take }\pi\;=\;\frac{22}{7}\right)$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Compare with $v\;=\;\omega\sqrt{A^{2}\;-\;x^{2}}$ to read off $\omega$. // 📝 Solution: $v\;=\;\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{50\;-\;x^{2}}\;\implies\;\omega\;=\;\frac{1}{2}\;\implies\;T\;=\;\frac{2\pi}{\omega}\;=\;4\pi\;=\;\frac{88}{7}\;\implies\;x\;=\;88$

questions.text: The position, velocity and acceleration of a particle executing simple harmonic motion are found to have magnitudes of $4\;\text{m},\;2\;\text{ms}^{-1}$ and $16\;\text{ms}^{-2}$ at a certain instant. The amplitude of the motion is $\sqrt{x}\;\text{m}$ where $x$ is ________
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $a\;=\;\omega^{2}x$ and $A^{2}\;=\;x^{2}\;+\;\frac{v^{2}}{\omega^{2}}$. // 📝 Solution: $16\;=\;\omega^{2}\left(4\right)\;\implies\;\omega\;=\;2\;\text{rad/s}\;\implies\;A\;=\;\sqrt{\frac{4}{4}\;+\;16}\;=\;\sqrt{17}\;\text{m}\;\implies\;x\;=\;17$

questions.text: A simple pendulum is placed at a place where its distance from the earth's surface is equal to the radius of the earth. If the length of the string is $4\;\text{m}$, then the time period of small oscillations will be _____ $\text{s}$. $\left[\text{take }g\;=\;\pi^{2}\;\text{ms}^{-2}\right]$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: At height $h\;=\;R$, $g'\;=\;\frac{g}{4}$; then use $T\;=\;2\pi\sqrt{\frac{\ell}{g'}}$. // 📝 Solution: $T\;=\;2\pi\sqrt{\frac{4\ell}{g}}\;=\;2\pi\sqrt{\frac{16}{\pi^{2}}}\;=\;2\pi\times\frac{4}{\pi}\;=\;8\;\text{s}$

questions.text: The time period of simple harmonic motion of mass $M$ in the given figure is $\pi\sqrt{\frac{\alpha M}{5K}}$, where the value of $\alpha$ is _____ [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find the equivalent spring constant using series and parallel combinations, then $T\;=\;2\pi\sqrt{\frac{M}{k_{eq}}}$. // 📝 Solution: $k_{eq}\;=\;\frac{2k\cdot k}{3k}\;+\;k\;=\;\frac{5k}{3}\;\implies\;T\;=\;2\pi\sqrt{\frac{3M}{5k}}\;=\;\pi\sqrt{\frac{12M}{5k}}\;\implies\;\alpha\;=\;12$

questions.text: The general displacement of a simple harmonic oscillator is $x\;=\;A\sin\omega t$. Let $T$ be its time period. The slope of its potential energy $\left(U\right)$ - time $\left(t\right)$ curve will be maximum when $t\;=\;\frac{T}{\beta}$. The value of $\beta$ is ____ .
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Slope of the $U$–$t$ curve is $\frac{dU}{dt}$, and it is maximum when $\sin 2\omega t\;=\;1$. // 📝 Solution: $U\;=\;\frac{1}{2}kx^{2}\;\implies\;\frac{dU}{dt}\;=\;\frac{kA^{2}\omega}{2}\sin 2\omega t\;\implies\;2\omega t\;=\;\frac{\pi}{2}\;\implies\;t\;=\;\frac{T}{8}\;\implies\;\beta\;=\;8$
questions.topic: Energy in SHM (Rate of Change of Potential Energy)

questions.text: For a simple harmonic motion in a mass spring system shown, the surface is frictionless. When the mass of the block is $1\;\text{kg}$, the angular frequency is $\omega_1$. When the mass block is $2\;\text{kg}$ the angular frequency is $\omega_2$. The ratio $\frac{\omega_2}{\omega_1}$ is : [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\omega\;=\;\sqrt{\frac{k}{m}}$, so $\omega\;\propto\;\frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{\omega_2}{\omega_1}\;=\;\sqrt{\frac{m_1}{m_2}}\;=\;\sqrt{\frac{1}{2}}\;=\;\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

questions.text: Choose the correct length $\left(L\right)$ versus square of time period $\left(T^{2}\right)$ graph for a simple pendulum executing simple harmonic motion. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $T\;=\;2\pi\sqrt{\frac{L}{g}}$ and look at how $T^{2}$ depends on $L$. // 📝 Solution: $T^{2}\;=\;\frac{4\pi^{2}}{g}\,L\;\implies\;T^{2}\;\propto\;L\;\implies\;\text{straight line through origin}\;\implies\;\text{option (3)}$

questions.text: A particle performs simple harmonic motion with amplitude $A$. Its speed is increased to three times at an instant when its displacement is $\frac{2A}{3}$. The new amplitude of motion is $\frac{nA}{3}$. The value of $n$ is _____
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $v\;=\;\omega\sqrt{A^{2}\;-\;x^{2}}$ before and after the speed change, with $\omega$ and $x$ unchanged. // 📝 Solution: $v\;=\;\omega\sqrt{A^{2}\;-\;\frac{4A^{2}}{9}}\;=\;\frac{\sqrt{5}A\omega}{3}\;\implies\;3v\;=\;\sqrt{5}A\omega\;=\;\omega\sqrt{A'^{2}\;-\;\frac{4A^{2}}{9}}\;\implies\;A'\;=\;\frac{7A}{3}\;\implies\;n\;=\;7$

questions.text: A particle of mass $0.50\;\text{kg}$ executes simple harmonic motion under force $F\;=\;-50\left(\text{Nm}^{-1}\right)x$. The time period of oscillation is $\frac{x}{35}\;\text{s}$. The value of $x$ is _______ $\left(\text{Given }\pi\;=\;\frac{22}{7}\right)$

A particle executes simple harmonic motion with an amplitude of $4\;\text{cm}$. At the mean position, velocity of the particle is $10\;\text{cm/s}$. The distance of the particle from the mean position when its speed becomes $5\;\text{cm/s}$ is $\sqrt{\alpha}\;\text{cm}$, where $\alpha\;=$ _____

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R. Assertion A: Number of photons increases with increase in frequency of light. Reason R: Maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons increases with the frequency of incident radiation. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: (1) Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
(2) Both A and R are correct and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
(3) A is not correct but R is correct.
(4) A is correct but R is not correct.

questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Intensity $I = rac{nh u}{A}$, where $n$ is the number of photons per unit time.

Step 1: From $n = rac{IA}{h u}$, if intensity $I$ is constant, increasing frequency $ u$ causes the number of photons $n$ to decrease. Thus, Assertion A is incorrect.

Step 2: According to Einstein's photoelectric equation, $K_{max} = h u - \phi$. Thus, increasing frequency $ u$ increases the maximum kinetic energy. Reason R is correct.

Step 3: Therefore, A is not correct but R is correct.

questions.text: Which of the following statement is not true about stopping potential $\left( V_0 \right)$?

options.text: It is $1/e$ times the maximum kinetic energy of electrons emitted.
It increases with increase in intensity of the incident light.
It depends on the nature of emitter material.
It depends upon frequency of the incident light.

questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Stopping potential depends on frequency and work function, but is independent of intensity.

📝 Step 1: The maximum kinetic energy is related to stopping potential by $K_{\max} = e V_0 \implies V_0 = \frac{K_{\max}}{e}$. Thus, Statement (1) is true.

Step 2: Stopping potential depends on frequency and the work function of the material (Statements 3 and 4 are true).

Step 3: Intensity determines the number of emitted photoelectrons (current) but has no effect on the stopping potential or maximum kinetic energy. Hence, Statement (2) is not true.

questions.text: Which figure [FIGURE] shows the correct variation of applied potential difference ($V$) with photoelectric current ($I$) at two different intensities of light ($I_{1} < I_{2}$) of same wavelengths :
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Stopping potential depends only on the frequency of incident light, whereas saturation current is directly proportional to the intensity of light.

📝 Step 1: Since the wavelengths of both light beams are identical, the frequency is the same. Therefore, the stopping potential $\left( - V_{0} \right)$ must be equal for both intensities.

Step 2: Given that $I_{1} < I_{2}$, the saturation current for intensity $I_{2}$ must be higher than that for $I_{1}$.

Step 3: Looking at the given figures, Figure (2) correctly shows the same stopping potential and a higher saturation current for $I_{2}$ compared to $I_{1}$. Hence, Option B is correct.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : Stopping potential in photoelectric effect does not depend on the power of the light source.
Statement II : For a given metal, the maximum kinetic energy of the photoelectron depends on the wavelength of the incident light.
In the light of above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.

options.text: Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Both statement I and statement II are correct

questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Stopping potential depends on frequency/wavelength, not intensity/power. Max kinetic energy depends on wavelength.

📝 Solution:

Step 1: Stopping potential $V_{S} = \frac{K E_{\max}}{e} = \frac{\frac{hc}{\lambda} - \phi}{e}$. It depends only on the frequency or wavelength of incident light, not on the power or intensity of the light source. Thus, Statement I is correct.

Step 2: The maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons is given by $K E_{\max} = \frac{hc}{\lambda} - \phi$, which clearly depends on the wavelength $\lambda$ of the incident light. Thus, Statement II is also correct.

questions.text: A proton and an electron have the same de Broglie wavelength. If Kp and Ke be the kinetic energies of proton and electron respectively, then choose the correct relation :
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: $\lambda = \frac{h}{p} \implies p = \frac{h}{\lambda}$.

Step 1: Since $\lambda$ is the same, $p_p = p_e$.

Step 2: $K = \frac{p^2}{2m}$. Since $m_p > m_e$, for the same momentum, $K_p < K_e$.

questions.text: When UV light of wavelength 300 nm is incident on the metal surface having work function 2.13eV, electron emission takes place. The stopping potential is: (Given hc = 1240eVnm)
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: $\frac{hc}{\lambda} - \phi = eV_s$.

Step 1: Energy of incident photon $E = \frac{1240 \text{ eVnm}}{300 \text{ nm}} = 4.13 \text{ eV}$.

Step 2: $4.13 \text{ eV} - 2.13 \text{ eV} = eV_s$.

Step 3: $2 \text{ eV} = eV_s \implies V_s = 2 \text{ V}$.

questions.text: In photoelectric experiment energy of $2.48\text{ eV}$ irradiates a photosensitive material. The stopping potential was measured to be $0.5\text{ V}$. Work function of the photosensitive material is :
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Use $E = \phi + e V_0$.

📝 Step 1: Apply Einstein's photoelectric equation:

$E = \phi + e V_0$

Step 2: Substitute the given values ($E = 2.48\text{ eV}$ and $e V_0 = 0.5\text{ eV}$):

$2.48\text{ eV} = \phi + 0.5\text{ eV}$

Step 3: Calculate the work function $\phi$:

$\phi = 2.48\text{ eV} - 0.5\text{ eV} = 1.98\text{ eV}$

questions.text: A proton, an electron and an alpha particle have the same energies. Their de-Broglie wavelengths will be compared as :
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: $\lambda \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}$ for same kinetic energy.

📝 Step 1: The de-Broglie wavelength for a particle of mass $m$ and energy $E$ is:

$\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m E}}$

Step 2: Since energy $E$ is the same for all three particles, $\lambda \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}$.

Step 3: Order of masses: $m_\alpha > m_p > m_e$.

Step 4: Consequently, the order of wavelengths is:

$\lambda_\alpha < \lambda_p < \lambda_e$

questions.text: A proton and an electron are associated with same de-Broglie wavelength. The ratio of their kinetic energies is: (Assume h=6.63 \times 10^{-34} J s, m_e = 9.0 \times 10^{-31} kg and m_p = 1836 m_e )
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: $\lambda = \frac{h}{p} = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}} \implies K = \frac{h^2}{2m\lambda^2}$.

Step 1: Since $\lambda$ is the same for both, $K \propto \frac{1}{m}$.

Step 2: $\frac{K_p}{K_e} = \frac{m_e}{m_p} = \frac{m_e}{1836 m_e} = \frac{1}{1836}$.

questions.text: Which figure shows the correct variation of applied potential difference (V) with photoelectric current (I) at two different intensities of light (I1 < I2) of same wavelengths : [FIGURE]
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Stopping potential depends on frequency, while saturation current depends on intensity.

Step 1: Since the wavelengths are the same, the stopping potential $V_0$ remains the same for both intensities.

Step 2: Since $I_2 > I_1$, the saturation current corresponding to $I_2$ must be greater than that corresponding to $I_1$.

Step 3: Figure (2) correctly shows the same stopping potential and higher saturation current for $I_2$.

questions.text: The ratio of de-Broglie wavelength of an $\alpha$-particle and a proton accelerated from rest by the same potential is $\frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}$, the value of m is
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: $\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m q V}}$

📝 Solution:

Step 1: The de-Broglie wavelength is given by $\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m q V}}$.

Step 2: For $\alpha$-particle and proton, taking the ratio: $\frac{\lambda_{\alpha}}{\lambda_{p}} = \sqrt{\frac{m_{p} q_{p}}{m_{\alpha} q_{\alpha}}}$

Step 3: Substituting $m_{\alpha} = 4 m_{p}$ and $q_{\alpha} = 2 q_{p}$, we get $\frac{\lambda_{\alpha}}{\lambda_{p}} = \sqrt{\frac{m_{p} q_{p}}{(4 m_{p})(2 q_{p})}} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{8}}$. Thus, $m = 8$.

questions.text: An electron accelerated through a potential difference $V_{1}$ has a de-Broglie wavelength of $\lambda$. When the potential is changed to $V_{2}$, its de-Broglie wavelength increases by $50\%$. The value of $\frac{V_{1}}{V_{2}}$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: $\lambda \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{V}}$

📝 Solution:

Step 1: Since $\lambda \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{V}}$, we can write $\frac{\lambda_{1}}{\lambda_{2}} = \sqrt{\frac{V_{2}}{V_{1}}}$

Step 2: The wavelength increases by $50\%$, so $\lambda_{2} = \lambda + 0.5\lambda = 1.5\lambda = \frac{3}{2}\lambda$.

Step 3: Therefore, $\frac{\lambda}{\frac{3}{2}\lambda} = \sqrt{\frac{V_{2}}{V_{1}}} \implies \frac{2}{3} = \sqrt{\frac{V_{2}}{V_{1}}} \implies \frac{V_{2}}{V_{1}} = \frac{4}{9} \implies \frac{V_{1}}{V_{2}} = \frac{9}{4}$.

questions.text:
Which of the following phenomena does not explain by wave nature of light.

A. reflection

B. diffraction

C. photoelectric effect

D. interference

E. polarization

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Photoelectric effect provides evidence for the particle nature of light (photons).

📝 Step 1: Reflection, diffraction, interference, and polarization are successfully explained by the wave theory of light.

Step 2: The photoelectric effect cannot be explained by wave theory because wave theory predicts that kinetic energy should depend on intensity rather than frequency, and time lag should occur at low intensities.

Step 3: Thus, photoelectric effect is exclusively explained by the particle nature of light.

questions.text: UV light of $4.13\text{ eV}$ is incident on a photosensitive metal surface having work function $3.13\text{ eV}$. The maximum kinetic energy of ejected photoelectrons will be:
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: $K_{\max} = E_{\text{photon}} - \phi$.

📝 Step 1: Write Einstein's photoelectric equation:

$E_{\text{photon}} = \text{Work Function} + K_{\max}$

Step 2: Substitute the given values:

$4.13\text{ eV} = 3.13\text{ eV} + K_{\max}$

Step 3: Solve for $K_{\max}$:

$K_{\max} = 4.13\text{ eV} - 3.13\text{ eV} = 1\text{ eV}$

questions.text: A small object at rest, absorbs a light pulse of power $20\text{ mW}$ and duration $300\text{ ns}$. Assuming speed of light as $3 \times 10^{8}\text{ m/s}$, the momentum of the object becomes equal to :
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: $\text{Momentum } p = \frac{\text{Energy}}{c} = \frac{\text{Power} \times \text{time}}{c}$

📝 Solution:

Step 1: Momentum imparted by an absorbed photon pulse is given by $p = \frac{E}{c} = \frac{P \times t}{c}$

Step 2: Substitute the given values: $P = 20 \times 10^{-3}\text{ W}$, $t = 300 \times 10^{-9}\text{ s}$, and $c = 3 \times 10^{8}\text{ m/s}$.

Step 3: $p = \frac{\left( 20 \times 10^{-3} \right) \left( 300 \times 10^{-9} \right)}{3 \times 10^{8}} = 2 \times 10^{-17}\text{ kg m/s}$.

questions.text: UV light of 4.13eV is incident on a photosensitive metal surface having work function 3.13eV. The maximum kinetic energy of ejected photoelectrons will be:
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: $E_{photon} = \phi + K_{max}$.

Step 1: $4.13 \text{ eV} = 3.13 \text{ eV} + K_{max}$.

Step 2: $K_{max} = 4.13 \text{ eV} - 3.13 \text{ eV} = 1 \text{ eV}$.

questions.text:
If a source of electromagnetic radiation having power $15\text{ kW}$ produces $10^{16}$ photons per second, the radiation belongs to a part of spectrum is.
(Take Planck constant $h = 6 \times 10^{-34}\text{ Js}$)
(1) Micro waves
(2) Ultraviolet rays
(3) Gamma rays
(4) Radio waves
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: $E = h\nu = \frac{\text{Power}}{\text{number of photons per second}}$

📝 Solution:

Step 1: Energy of one photon is $E = \frac{P}{n} = \frac{15 \times 10^{3}}{10^{16}} = 1.5 \times 10^{-12}\text{ J}$.

Step 2: Frequency $\nu = \frac{E}{h} = \frac{1.5 \times 10^{-12}}{6 \times 10^{-34}} = 2.5 \times 10^{21}\text{ Hz}$.

Step 3: A frequency of $2.5 \times 10^{21}\text{ Hz}$ falls in the range of Gamma rays.

questions.text: The threshold frequency of metal is $f_{0}$. When the light of frequency $2f_{0}$ is incident on the metal plate, the maximum velocity of photoelectron is $v_{1}$. When the frequency of incident radiation is increased to $5f_{0}$, the maximum velocity of photoelectrons emitted is $v_{2}$. The ratio of $v_{1}$ to $v_{2}$ is:
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: $\frac{1}{2} m v^{2} = hf - hf_{0}$

📝 Solution:

Step 1: For frequency $2f_{0}$, maximum kinetic energy is $\frac{1}{2} m v_{1}^{2} = h(2f_{0}) - hf_{0} = hf_{0}$.

Step 2: For frequency $5f_{0}$, maximum kinetic energy is $\frac{1}{2} m v_{2}^{2} = h(5f_{0}) - hf_{0} = 4hf_{0}$.

Step 3: Taking the ratio of velocities, $\frac{v_{1}^{2}}{v_{2}^{2}} = \frac{hf_{0}}{4hf_{0}} = \frac{1}{4}$, which gives $\frac{v_{1}}{v_{2}} = \frac{1}{2}$.

questions.text: Electron beam used in an electron microscope, when accelerated by a voltage of $20\text{ kV}$, has a de-Broglie wavelength of $\lambda_{0}$. If the voltage is increased to $40\text{ kV}$, then the de-Broglie wavelength associated with the electron beam would be:
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: $\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m e V}}$ so $\lambda \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{V}}$

📝 Solution:

Step 1: The de-Broglie wavelength for an electron accelerated through potential $V$ is $\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m e V}}$

Step 2: Therefore, $\lambda \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{V}}$

Step 3: Taking the ratio for $20\text{ kV}$ and $40\text{ kV}$, we get $\frac{\lambda}{\lambda_{0}} = \sqrt{\frac{20}{40}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$, which gives $\lambda = \frac{\lambda_{0}}{\sqrt{2}}$.

questions.text: A proton and an electron have the same de Broglie wavelength. If $K_p$ and $K_e$ be the kinetic energies of proton and electron respectively, then choose the correct relation :
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: $\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}}$ implies $K \propto \frac{1}{m}$.

📝 Step 1: The de Broglie wavelength formula containing kinetic energy is:

$\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m K}}$

Step 2: Since $\lambda$ and $h$ are equal for both particles:

$m_p K_p = m_e K_e$

Step 3: Since the mass of a proton is much greater than the mass of an electron ($m_p > m_e$):

$K_p < K_e$

questions.text: Average force exerted on a non-reflecting surface at normal incidence is $2.4 \times 10^{-4}\text{ N}$. If $360\text{ W/cm}^2$ is the light energy flux during span of 1 hour 30 minutes, Then the area of the surface is:
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Radiation pressure / force relation for a non-reflecting surface is $F = \frac{I A}{c}$.

📝 Step 1: Convert light intensity (flux) into SI units:

$I = 360\text{ W/cm}^2 = \frac{360\text{ W}}{10^{-4}\text{ m}^2} = 360 \times 10^4\text{ W/m}^2$

Step 2: Use the force formula for complete absorption:

$F = \frac{I A}{c} \implies 2.4 \times 10^{-4} = \frac{360 \times 10^4 \times A}{3 \times 10^8}$

Step 3: Solve for area $A$:

$A = \frac{2.4 \times 10^{-4} \times 3 \times 10^8}{3.6 \times 10^6} = \frac{7.2 \times 10^4}{3.6 \times 10^6} = 2 \times 10^{-2}\text{ m}^2 = 0.02\text{ m}^2$

questions.text: A proton moving with one tenth of velocity of light has a certain de Broglie wavelength of $\lambda$. An alpha particle having certain kinetic energy has the same de-Broglie wavelength $\lambda$. The ratio of kinetic energy of proton and that of alpha particle is:
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: $K E = \frac{p^{2}}{2m} = \frac{h^{2}}{2m\lambda^{2}}$

📝 Solution:

Step 1: Kinetic energy in terms of de-Broglie wavelength is $K E = \frac{h^{2}}{2m\lambda^{2}}$.

Step 2: Since $\lambda$ and $h$ are the same for both, $K E \propto \frac{1}{m}$.

Step 3: Taking the ratio, $\frac{K E_{p}}{K E_{\alpha}} = \frac{m_{\alpha}}{m_{p}} = \frac{4 m_{p}}{m_{p}} = \frac{4}{1}$.

questions.text: [FIGURE] A point source of light is placed at the centre of curvature of a hemispherical surface. The source emits a power of $24\text{ W}$. The radius of curvature of hemisphere is $10\text{ cm}$ and the inner surface is completely reflecting. The force on the hemisphere due to the light falling on it is $\_\_\_\_\_\_\_ \times 10^{-8}\text{ N}$.
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: $\text{Force } F = \int P dA \cos\theta$ for a completely reflecting surface.

📝 Solution:

Step 1: The radiation force on a completely reflecting surface element is given by $dF = \frac{2 I}{c} \cos\theta \, dA$ where $I = \frac{P}{4 \pi R^{2}}$

Step 2: Integrating over the hemisphere, $F = \frac{2P}{c \left( 4\pi R^{2} \right)} \int \cos\theta \, dA = \frac{2P}{c \left( 4\pi R^{2} \right)} (\pi R^{2}) = \frac{P}{2c}$

Step 3: Substituting $P = 24\text{ W}$ and $c = 3 \times 10^{8}\text{ m/s}$, we get $F = \frac{24}{2 \times 3 \times 10^{8}} = 4 \times 10^{-8}\text{ N}$.

questions.text: An $\alpha$-particle, a proton and an electron have the same kinetic energy. Which one of the following is correct in case of their De-Broglie wavelength:
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: $\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m K}}$

📝 Solution:

Step 1: The de-Broglie wavelength formula in terms of kinetic energy $K$ is given by $\lambda = \frac{h}{\sqrt{2 m K}}$

Step 2: Since $h$ and $K$ are the same for all three particles, we have $\lambda \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{m}}$

Step 3: Comparing the masses: $m_{\alpha} > m_{p} > m_{e}$, it follows that their de-Broglie wavelengths follow the order $\lambda_{\alpha} < \lambda_{p} < \lambda_{e}$.

questions.text: If the two metals A and B are exposed to radiation of wavelength $350\text{ nm}$. The work functions of metals A and B are $4.8\text{ eV}$ and $2.2\text{ eV}$. Then choose the correct option

options.text: Metal B will not emit photo-electrons
Both metals A and B will emit photo-electrons
Both metals A and B will not emit photo-electrons
Metal A will not emit photo-electrons

questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Calculate incident photon energy in eV and compare with work functions.

📝 Solution:

Step 1: Energy of incident photon is $E = \frac{12400}{\lambda\text{ in \AA}} = \frac{12400}{3500} \approx 3.54\text{ eV}$.

Step 2: Work function of metal A is $\phi_{A} = 4.8\text{ eV}$ and for metal B is $\phi_{B} = 2.2\text{ eV}$.

Step 3: Since $E < \phi_{A}$, metal A will not emit photoelectrons, whereas $E > \phi_{B}$, so metal B will emit photoelectrons.

questions.text:
The threshold wavelength for photoelectric emission from a material is $5500\;\mathring{\text{A}}$. Photoelectrons will be emitted, when this material is illuminated with monochromatic radiation from a
A. $75\text{ W}$ infra-red lamp
B. $10\text{ W}$ infra-red lamp
C. $75\text{ W}$ ultra-violet lamp
D. $10\text{ W}$ ultra-violet lamp
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: For emission, $\lambda < \lambda_{0}$ ($5500\;\mathring{\text{A}}$).

📝 Solution:

Step 1: Photoelectric emission takes place only when the wavelength of incident radiation is less than the threshold wavelength ($\lambda < \lambda_{0} = 5500\;\mathring{\text{A}}$).

Step 2: Ultra-violet rays have shorter wavelengths (typically $< 4000\;\mathring{\text{A}}$) compared to $5500\;\mathring{\text{A}}$, whereas infra-red rays have much longer wavelengths.

Step 3: Therefore, only ultra-violet lamps (C and D) will cause photoelectric emission regardless of power.

questions.text: Which figure shows the correct variation of applied potential difference ($V$) with photoelectric current ($I$) at two different intensities of light ($I_1 < I_2$) of same wavelengths : [FIGURE]
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: For lights of the same wavelength, the stopping potential remains identical. Higher intensity yields a higher saturation current.

📝 Step 1: Since the wavelengths are equal, the stopping potential $\left\lvert - V_0 \right vert$ must be the same for both curves.

Step 2: Given $I_1 < I_2$, the saturation current for $I_2$ is greater than that for $I_1$.

Step 3: Looking at the given options, figure (2) correctly depicts the same stopping potential and higher saturation current for $I_2$. Hence, option (2) is correct.

questions.text:
When UV light of wavelength $300\text{ nm}$ is incident on the metal surface having work function $2.13\text{ eV}$, electron emission takes place. The stopping potential is:

(Given $hc = 1240\text{ eV nm}$)
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Use $V_0 = \frac{hc}{e \lambda} - \frac{\phi}{e}$.

📝 Step 1: Calculate the energy of the incident photon:

$E = \frac{hc}{\lambda} = \frac{1240\text{ eV nm}}{300\text{ nm}} \approx 4.13\text{ eV}$

Step 2: Use Einstein's photoelectric equation to find maximum kinetic energy:

$e V_0 = E - \phi = 4.13\text{ eV} - 2.13\text{ eV} = 2.0\text{ eV}$

Step 3: Determine the stopping potential $V_0$:

$V_0 = 2\text{ V}$

questions.text: Which of the following statement is not true about stopping potential (V0)?

options.text: (1) It is 1/e times the maximum kinetic energy of electrons emitted.
(2) It increases with increase in intensity of the incident light.
(3) It depends on the nature of emitter material.
(4) It depends upon frequency of the incident light.

questions.solution:
💡 Hint: $K_{max} = h\nu - \phi_0 = eV_0$.

Step 1: Stopping potential $V_0$ is defined by $eV_0 = K_{max}$, so $V_0 = K_{max}/e$. Statement (1) is true.

Step 2: Stopping potential depends on the frequency of incident light and the work function of the material. It does not depend on the intensity of incident light. Statement (2) is not true.

questions.text: Which of the following phenomena does not explain by wave nature of light. A. reflection B. diffraction C. photoelectric effect D. interference
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Photoelectric effect demonstrates the particle nature of light.

Step 1: Reflection, diffraction, and interference are well-explained by the wave theory of light.

Step 2: The photoelectric effect cannot be explained by wave theory and requires the particle (photon) model of light.

questions.text: In photoelectric experiment energy of 2.48eV irradiates a photo sensitive material. The stopping potential was measured to be 0.5 V. Work function of the photo sensitive material is :
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: $eV_s = h\nu - \phi$.

Step 1: Given $h\nu = 2.48 \text{ eV}$ and $V_s = 0.5 \text{ V}$.

Step 2: $0.5 \text{ eV} = 2.48 \text{ eV} - \phi$.

Step 3: $\phi = 2.48 \text{ eV} - 0.5 \text{ eV} = 1.98 \text{ eV}$.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : Figure [FIGURE] shows the variation of stopping potential with frequency $\left( \nu \right)$ for the two photosensitive materials $M_{1}$ and $M_{2}$. The slope gives value of $\frac{h}{e}$, where $h$ is Planck's constant, $e$ is the charge of electron.

Statement II : $M_{2}$ will emit photoelectrons of greater kinetic energy for the incident radiation having same frequency.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct and Statement II is incorrect

questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Use Einstein's equation $e V_{0} = h u - \phi$ to find stopping potential $V_{0} = \left( rac{h}{e} ight) u - rac{\phi}{e}$.

📝 Step 1: From the equation, the slope of the $V_{0}$ versus $ u$ graph is indeed $ rac{h}{e}$. Hence, Statement I is correct.

Step 2: The intercept on the frequency axis gives the threshold frequency. From the graph, material $M_{2}$ has a higher threshold frequency and hence a higher work function $\phi$.

Step 3: Since $K_{ ext{max}} = h u - \phi$, for the same frequency $ u$, the material with the smaller work function ($M_{1}$) will emit photoelectrons of greater kinetic energy. Thus, Statement II is incorrect.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I : Figure shows the variation of stopping potential with frequency $(\nu)$ for the two photosensitive materials $M_1$ and $M_2$. The slope gives value of $\frac{h}{e}$, where $h$ is Planck's constant, $e$ is the charge of electron. [FIGURE]

Statement II : $M_2$ will emit photoelectrons of greater kinetic energy for the incident radiation having same frequency.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct and Statement II is incorrect

questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Einstein's equation gives $V_0 = \left( rac{h}{e} ight) u - rac{\phi}{e}$.

📝 Step 1: The stopping potential equation is $e V_0 = h u - \phi \implies V_0 = \left( rac{h}{e} ight) u - rac{\phi}{e}$. Thus, the slope of the $V_0$ versus $ u$ graph is indeed $ rac{h}{e}$. Statement I is correct.

Step 2: From the graph, material $M_2$ has a higher threshold frequency and therefore a higher work function $\phi$ than $M_1$.

Step 3: Since $K_{\max} = h u - \phi$, for the same frequency $ u$, material $M_1$ (having a smaller work function) will emit photoelectrons of greater kinetic energy. Thus, Statement II is incorrect.

questions.text:
A proton and an electron are associated with same de-Broglie wavelength. The ratio of their kinetic energies is:

(Assume $h = 6.63 \times 10^{-34}\text{ J s}$, $m_e = 9.0 \times 10^{-31}\text{ kg}$ and $m_p = 1836\text{ } m_e$)
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Kinetic energy $K = \frac{p^2}{2m}$ and $\lambda = \frac{h}{p}$.

📝 Step 1: Since both particles have the same de-Broglie wavelength $\lambda$, their momentum $p = \frac{h}{\lambda}$ is also the same.

Step 2: The kinetic energy is given by $K = \frac{p^2}{2m}$, which implies $K \propto \frac{1}{m}$.

Step 3: Taking the ratio for proton and electron:

$\frac{K_p}{K_e} = \frac{m_e}{m_p} = \frac{m_e}{1836 m_e} = \frac{1}{1836}$

Step 4: Thus, the ratio is $1 : 1836$.

questions.text: Average force exerted on a non-reflecting surface at normal incidence is 2.4 \times 10^{-4} N. If 360 W/cm^2 is the light energy flux during span of 1 hour 30 minutes, Then the area of the surface is:
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Pressure $P = \frac{I}{c} = \frac{F}{A}$.

Step 1: $I = 360 \text{ W/cm}^2 = 360 \times 10^4 \text{ W/m}^2$.

Step 2: $\frac{360 \times 10^4}{3 \times 10^8} = \frac{2.4 \times 10^{-4}}{A}$.

Step 3: $A = \frac{2.4 \times 10^{-4} \times 3 \times 10^8}{360 \times 10^4} = \frac{7.2 \times 10^4}{360 \times 10^4} = 0.02 \text{ m}^2$.

questions.text:
From the photoelectric effect experiment, following observations are made. Identify which of these are correct.
A. The stopping potential depends only on the work function of the metal.
B. The saturation current increases as the intensity of incident light increases.
C. The maximum kinetic energy of a photo electron depends on the intensity of the incident light.
D. Photoelectric effect can be explained using wave theory of light.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Saturation current is directly proportional to intensity and stopping potential depends on frequency and work function.

📝 Solution:

Step 1: Stopping potential depends on frequency of incident light and work function, not only on work function. So statement A is incorrect.

Step 2: Saturation current is directly proportional to the intensity of incident light. So statement B is correct.

Step 3: Maximum kinetic energy depends on frequency of incident light, not intensity. So statement C is incorrect. Photoelectric effect is explained by particle nature (Einstein), not wave theory. So statement D is incorrect. Thus, only B is correct.

questions.text: Given below are two statements : Statement I : Figure shows the variation of stopping potential with frequency (\nu) for the two photosensitive materials M1 and M2. The slope gives value of $\frac{h}{e}$, where h is Planck's constant, e is the charge of electron. Statement II : M2 will emit photoelectrons of greater kinetic energy for the incident radiation having same frequency. [FIGURE] In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.

options.text: (1) Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
(2) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
(3) Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
(4) Statement I is correct and Statement II is incorrect

questions.solution:
💡 Hint: $eV_0 = h u - \phi \implies V_0 = rac{h}{e} u - rac{\phi}{e}$.

Step 1: The slope of the $V_0$ vs $ u$ graph is indeed $ rac{h}{e}$. Statement I is correct.

Step 2: From the graph, M2 has a higher threshold frequency, meaning it has a higher work function $\phi$.

Step 3: Since $K_{max} = h u - \phi$, for the same frequency, the material with the higher work function (M2) will emit photoelectrons with lower kinetic energy. Thus, Statement II is incorrect.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.

Assertion A: Number of photons increases with increase in frequency of light.

Reason R: Maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons increases with the frequency of incident radiation.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is not correct but R is correct.
A is correct but R is not correct.

questions.solution:
💡 Hint: Intensity of light is given by $I = \left( n \, h u ight) / \left( A ight)$. For constant intensity, increasing frequency decreases the number of photons per second.

📝 Step 1: The number of photons per unit time $n$ is given by $n = \left( I \, A ight) / \left( h u ight)$. Thus, when the frequency $ u$ increases, the number of photons $n$ decreases (keeping intensity constant). Therefore, Assertion A is incorrect.

Step 2: According to Einstein's photoelectric equation, the maximum kinetic energy is given by $K_{ ext{max}} = h u - \phi$. Thus, maximum kinetic energy increases linearly with the frequency of incident radiation. Therefore, Reason R is correct.

Step 3: Conclusion: A is not correct but R is correct.

questions.text: Electromagnetic waves travel in a medium with speed of $1.5 \times 10^{8}\;\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$. The relative permeability of the medium is $2.0$. The relative permittivity will be:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $v \; = \; \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu \varepsilon}}$ so $\varepsilon_r \mu_r \; = \; \frac{c^2}{v^2}$ // 📝 Solution: $\varepsilon_r \times 2 \; = \; \frac{\left( 3 \times 10^{8} \right)^2}{\left( 1.5 \times 10^{8} \right)^2} \; = \; 4 \implies \varepsilon_r \; = \; 2$
questions.topic: Speed of EM Wave in Medium

questions.text: The equation of the electric field of an electromagnetic wave propagating through free space is given by : $E \; = \; \sqrt{377}\sin\left( 6.27 \times 10^{3}t \; - \; 2.09 \times 10^{-5}x \right)\;\mathrm{N/C}$. The average power of the electromagnetic wave is $\left( \frac{1}{\alpha} \right)\mathrm{W/m^2}$. The value of $\alpha$ is ____ (Take $\sqrt{\frac{\mu_0}{\varepsilon_o}} \; = \; 377$ in SI units)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $I_{avg} \; = \; \frac{E_0^2}{2Z_0}$ with $Z_0 \; = \; \sqrt{\frac{\mu_0}{\varepsilon_0}}$ // 📝 Solution: $E_0 \; = \; \sqrt{377} \implies I_{avg} \; = \; \frac{377}{2 \times 377} \; = \; \frac{1}{2}\;\mathrm{W/m^2} \implies \frac{1}{\alpha} \; = \; \frac{1}{2} \implies \alpha \; = \; 2$

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II : List-I (EM-Wave): A. Infra-red, B. Ultraviolet, C. X-rays, D. Gamma rays. List-II (Wavelength Range): I. $< \; 10^{-3}\;\mathrm{nm}$, II. $400\;\mathrm{nm}$ to $1\;\mathrm{nm}$, III. $1\;\mathrm{mm}$ to $700\;\mathrm{nm}$, IV. $1\;\mathrm{nm}$ to $10^{-3}\;\mathrm{nm}$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall standard wavelength ranges of EM spectrum // 📝 Solution: IR $\implies$ $1\;\mathrm{mm}$ to $700\;\mathrm{nm}$ (III) $\;;\;$ UV $\implies$ $400\;\mathrm{nm}$ to $1\;\mathrm{nm}$ (II) $\;;\;$ X-rays $\implies$ $1\;\mathrm{nm}$ to $10^{-3}\;\mathrm{nm}$ (IV) $\;;\;$ Gamma $\implies$ $< \; 10^{-3}\;\mathrm{nm}$ (I)

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Electromagnetic waves carry energy as they travel through space and this energy is equally shared by the electric and magnetic fields. Statement II: When electromagnetic waves strike a surface, a pressure is exerted on the surface. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\frac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0 E^2 \; = \; \frac{B^2}{2\mu_0}$ and EM waves carry momentum // 📝 Solution: $E \; = \; cB \;,\; c \; = \; \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0 \varepsilon_0}} \implies \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0 E^2 \; = \; \frac{B^2}{2\mu_0} \implies$ Statement I true $\;;\;$ EM waves have momentum $\implies$ radiation pressure exists $\implies$ Statement II true

questions.text: In a plane EM wave, the electric field oscillates sinusoidally at a frequency of $5 \times 10^{10}\;\mathrm{Hz}$ and an amplitude of $50\;\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$. The total average energy density of the electromagnetic field of the wave is : [Use $\varepsilon_0 \; = \; 8.85 \times 10^{-12}\;\mathrm{C^2/N\,m^2}$]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Average total energy density $u \; = \; \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0 E_0^2$ // 📝 Solution: $u \; = \; \frac{1}{2} \times 8.85 \times 10^{-12} \times \left( 50 \right)^2 \; = \; 1.106 \times 10^{-8}\;\mathrm{J/m^3}$

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: A. Microwaves, B. UV rays, C. Infra-red rays, D. X-rays. List-II: I. Physiotherapy, II. Treatment of cancer, III. Lasik eye surgery, IV. Aircraft navigation. Choose the correct answer from the option given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall the standard uses of each EM wave region // 📝 Solution: Microwaves $\implies$ aircraft navigation (IV) $\;;\;$ UV $\implies$ Lasik eye surgery (III) $\;;\;$ Infra-red $\implies$ physiotherapy (I) $\;;\;$ X-rays $\implies$ treatment of cancer (II) $\implies$ A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II

questions.text: Arrange the following in the ascending order of wavelength: A. Gamma rays ($\lambda_1$), B. $x$-rays ($\lambda_2$), C. Infrared waves ($\lambda_3$), D. Microwaves ($\lambda_4$). Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Higher energy $\implies$ smaller wavelength // 📝 Solution: Energy order $\implies$ gamma $>$ X-ray $>$ infrared $>$ microwave $\implies \lambda_1 \; < \; \lambda_2 \; < \; \lambda_3 \; < \; \lambda_4$

questions.text: In the given electromagnetic wave $E_y \; = \; 600 \sin\left( \omega t \; - \; kx \right)\;\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$, intensity of the associated light beam is (in $\mathrm{W/m^2}$) : (Given $\epsilon_0 \; = \; 9 \times 10^{-12}\;\mathrm{C^2\,N^{-1}\,m^{-2}}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $I \; = \; \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0 E_0^2 c$ // 📝 Solution: $I \; = \; \frac{1}{2} \times 9 \times 10^{-12} \times \left( 600 \right)^2 \times 3 \times 10^{8} \; = \; \frac{9}{2} \times 36 \times 3 \; = \; 486\;\mathrm{W/m^2}$

questions.text: The electric field and magnetic field components of an electromagnetic wave going through vacuum is described by $E_x \; = \; E_0 \sin\left( kz \; - \; \omega t \right)$ and $B_y \; = \; B_0 \sin\left( kz \; - \; \omega t \right)$. Then the correct relation between $E_0$ and $B_0$ is given by
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Wave speed $c \; = \; \frac{\omega}{k} \; = \; \frac{E_0}{B_0}$ // 📝 Solution: $c \; = \; \frac{\omega}{k} \; = \; \frac{E_0}{B_0} \implies kE_0 \; = \; \omega B_0$
questions.topic: Amplitude Relation of E and B

questions.text: A plane electromagnetic wave propagating in $x$-direction is described by $E_y \; = \; \left( 200\;\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}} \right)\sin\left[ 1.5 \times 10^{7}t \; - \; 0.05x \right]$. The intensity of the wave is : (Use $\epsilon_0 \; = \; 8.85 \times 10^{-12}\;\mathrm{C^2\,N^{-1}\,m^{-2}}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $I \; = \; \frac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0 E_0^2 c$ // 📝 Solution: $I \; = \; \frac{1}{2} \times 8.85 \times 10^{-12} \times 4 \times 10^{4} \times 3 \times 10^{8} \; = \; 53.1\;\mathrm{W/m^2}$

questions.text: Match the List-I with List-II: List-I: A. Microwaves, B. Gamma rays, C. Radio waves, D. X-rays. List-II: I. Radio active decay of the nucleus, II. Rapid acceleration and deceleration of electron in aerials, III. Inner shell electrons, IV. Klystron valve. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall the source of each EM wave // 📝 Solution: Microwaves $\implies$ Klystron valve (IV) $\;;\;$ Gamma rays $\implies$ radioactive decay (I) $\;;\;$ Radio waves $\implies$ acceleration of electrons in aerials (II) $\;;\;$ X-rays $\implies$ inner shell electrons (III) $\implies$ A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III

questions.text: The magnetic field in a plane electromagnetic wave is $B_y \; = \; \left( 3.5 \times 10^{-7} \right)\sin\left( 1.5 \times 10^{3}x \; + \; 0.5 \times 10^{11}t \right)\;\mathrm{T}$. The corresponding electric field will be :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $E_0 \; = \; cB_0$ and $\vec{E} \times \vec{B}$ points along propagation // 📝 Solution: $E_0 \; = \; 3 \times 10^{8} \times 3.5 \times 10^{-7} \; = \; 105\;\mathrm{V/m}$ $\;;\;$ wave moves along $-x$ and $\hat{B} \; = \; \hat{j} \implies \hat{E} \; = \; \hat{k}$ since $\hat{k} \times \hat{j} \; = \; -\hat{i} \implies E_z \; = \; 105 \sin\left( 1.5 \times 10^{3}x \; + \; 0.5 \times 10^{11}t \right)$

questions.text: An electromagnetic wave of frequency $100\;\mathrm{MHz}$ propagates through a medium of conductivity, $\sigma \; = \; 10\;\mathrm{mho/m}$. The ratio of maximum conduction current density to maximum displacement current density is ____. [Take $\frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \; = \; 9 \times 10^{9}\;\mathrm{N\,m^2/C^2}$]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $J_c \; = \; \sigma E_0$ and $J_d \; = \; \epsilon_0 \omega E_0$ // 📝 Solution: $\frac{J_{c,max}}{J_{d,max}} \; = \; \frac{\sigma}{\epsilon_0 \omega} \;;\; \omega \; = \; 2\pi \times 10^{8} \;,\; \epsilon_0 \; = \; \frac{10^{-9}}{36\pi} \implies \frac{10 \times 36\pi}{10^{-9} \times 2\pi \times 10^{8}} \; = \; 1800$

questions.text: Match List - I with List - II. List - I (Relation): A. $\oint \vec{E} \cdot d\vec{l} \; = \; -\frac{d}{dt}\oint \vec{B} \cdot d\vec{a}$, B. $\oint \vec{B} \cdot d\vec{l} \; = \; \mu_0\left( I \; + \; \epsilon_0 \frac{d\phi_E}{dt} \right)$, C. $\oint \vec{E} \cdot d\vec{a} \; = \; \frac{1}{\epsilon_0}\int_V \rho\,dv$, D. $\oint \vec{B} \cdot d\vec{l} \; = \; \mu_0 I$. List - II (Law): I. Ampere's circuital law, II. Faraday's laws of electromagnetic induction, III. Ampere - Maxwell law, IV. Gauss's law of electrostatics. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Identify each integral relation with its named law // 📝 Solution: A $\implies$ Faraday (II) $\;;\;$ B $\implies$ Ampere-Maxwell (III) $\;;\;$ C $\implies$ Gauss electrostatics (IV) $\;;\;$ D $\implies$ Ampere circuital (I)

questions.text: Match List I with List II. List-I: A. Gauss's law of magnetostatics, B. Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, C. Ampere's law, D. Gauss's law of electrostatics. List-II: I. $\oint \vec{E} \cdot d\vec{a} \; = \; \frac{1}{\varepsilon_0}\int \rho\,dV$, II. $\oint \vec{B} \cdot d\vec{a} \; = \; 0$, III. $\oint \vec{E} \cdot d\vec{l} \; = \; -\frac{d}{dt}\int \vec{B} \cdot d\vec{a}$, IV. $\oint \vec{B} \cdot d\vec{l} \; = \; \mu_0 I$. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall Maxwell's equations and their names // 📝 Solution: Gauss magnetism $\implies$ II $\;;\;$ Faraday $\implies$ III $\;;\;$ Ampere $\implies$ IV $\;;\;$ Gauss electrostatics $\implies$ I $\implies$ A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I

questions.text: A plane EM wave is propagating along $x$ direction. It has a wavelength of $4\;\mathrm{mm}$. If electric field is in $y$ direction with the maximum magnitude of $60\;\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}$, the equation for magnetic field is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $B_0 \; = \; \frac{E_0}{c}$, $k \; = \; \frac{2\pi}{\lambda}$ and $\hat{E} \times \hat{B} \; = \; \hat{v}$ // 📝 Solution: $B_0 \; = \; \frac{60}{3 \times 10^{8}} \; = \; 2 \times 10^{-7}\;\mathrm{T} \;;\; k \; = \; \frac{2\pi}{4 \times 10^{-3}} \; = \; \frac{\pi}{2} \times 10^{3} \;;\; \hat{j} \times \hat{k} \; = \; \hat{i} \implies \hat{B} \; = \; \hat{k} \implies B_z \; = \; 2 \times 10^{-7}\sin\left[ \frac{\pi}{2} \times 10^{3}\left( x \; - \; 3 \times 10^{8}t \right) \right]\hat{k}$

questions.text: The electric field in a plane electromagnetic wave is given by : $E_y \; = \; 69\sin\left[ 0.6 \times 10^{3}x \; - \; 1.8 \times 10^{11}t \right]\;\mathrm{V/m}$. The expression for magnetic field associated with this electromagnetic wave is ____ T.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $B_0 \; = \; \frac{E_0}{c}$ and $\hat{E} \times \hat{B} \; = \; \hat{v}$ // 📝 Solution: Wave along $+x$ with $\vec{E} \parallel \hat{j} \implies \hat{j} \times \hat{k} \; = \; \hat{i} \implies \vec{B} \parallel \hat{k} \;;\; B_0 \; = \; \frac{69}{3 \times 10^{8}} \; = \; 2.3 \times 10^{-7}\;\mathrm{T}$ and $\vec{E}$, $\vec{B}$ in phase

questions.text: An object is placed in a medium of refractive index $3$. An electromagnetic wave of intensity $6 \times 10^{8}\;\mathrm{W/m^2}$ falls normally on the object and it is absorbed completely. The radiation pressure on the object would be (speed of light in free space $= \; 3 \times 10^{8}\;\mathrm{m/s}$):
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Radiation pressure for complete absorption $P \; = \; \frac{I}{v}$ with $v \; = \; \frac{c}{\mu}$ // 📝 Solution: $P \; = \; \frac{I}{v} \; = \; \frac{I\mu}{c} \; = \; \frac{6 \times 10^{8} \times 3}{3 \times 10^{8}} \; = \; 6\;\mathrm{N/m^2}$

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I : Electromagnetic waves are not deflected by electric and magnetic field. Statement II : The amplitude of electric field and the magnetic field in electromagnetic waves are related to each other as $E_0 \; = \; \sqrt{\frac{\mu_0}{\varepsilon_0}}\,B_0$. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Statement I is true but statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: EM waves are neutral and $E_0 \; = \; cB_0$ // 📝 Solution: EM waves carry no charge $\implies$ Statement I true $\;;\;$ $E_0 \; = \; cB_0 \; = \; \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0 \varepsilon_0}}B_0 \; \ne \; \sqrt{\frac{\mu_0}{\varepsilon_0}}B_0 \implies$ Statement II false

questions.text: An alternating voltage of amplitude $40\;\mathrm{V}$ and frequency $4\;\mathrm{kHz}$ is applied directly across the capacitor of $12\;\mu\mathrm{F}$. The maximum displacement current between the plates of the capacitor is nearly :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Displacement current in capacitor equals conduction current $I_0 \; = \; \frac{V_0}{X_C}$ // 📝 Solution: $X_C \; = \; \frac{1}{2\pi f C} \; = \; \frac{1}{2\pi \times 4 \times 10^{3} \times 12 \times 10^{-6}} \; = \; 3.317\;\Omega \implies I_0 \; = \; \frac{40}{3.317} \; \approx \; 12\;\mathrm{A}$

questions.text: The electric field of an electromagnetic wave travelling through a medium is given by $\vec{E}\left( x,t \right) \; = \; 25\sin\left( 2.0 \times 10^{15}t \; - \; 10^{7}x \right)\hat{n}$ then the refractive index of the medium is ____. (All given measurement are in SI units)
If $\vec{E}$ and $\vec{K}$ represent electric field and propagation vectors of the EM waves in vacuum, then magnetic field vector is given by : ($\omega$ - angular frequency) :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\hat{B} \; = \; \hat{K} \times \hat{E}$ and $B \; = \; \frac{E}{c}$ // 📝 Solution: $\hat{B} \; \parallel \; \hat{K} \times \hat{E} \;,\; B \; = \; \frac{E}{c} \; = \; \frac{K}{\omega}E \implies \vec{B} \; = \; \frac{1}{\omega}\left( \vec{K} \times \vec{E} \right)$
questions.topic: Relation between E, B and K in EM Wave

questions.text: The electric field of a plane electromagnetic wave, travelling in an unknown nonmagnetic medium is given by, $E_y \; = \; 20\sin\left( 3 \times 10^{6}x \; - \; 4.5 \times 10^{14}t \right)\;\mathrm{V/m}$ (where $x$, $t$ and other values have S.I. units). The dielectric constant of the medium is ____ (speed of light in free space is $3 \times 10^{8}\;\mathrm{m/s}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $v \; = \; \frac{\omega}{k}$ and $n \; = \; \frac{c}{v} \; = \; \sqrt{\epsilon_r}$ for nonmagnetic medium // 📝 Solution: $v \; = \; \frac{4.5 \times 10^{14}}{3 \times 10^{6}} \; = \; 1.5 \times 10^{8} \implies n \; = \; \frac{3 \times 10^{8}}{1.5 \times 10^{8}} \; = \; 2 \implies \epsilon_r \; = \; n^2 \; = \; 4$
questions.topic: Speed of EM Wave in Medium

questions.text: The ratio of average electric energy density and total average energy density of electromagnetic wave is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\left\langle u_E \right\rangle \; = \; \left\langle u_B \right\rangle \; = \; \frac{1}{2}\left\langle u_{total} \right\rangle$ // 📝 Solution: $\left\langle u_E \right\rangle \; = \; \left\langle u_B \right\rangle \; = \; \frac{1}{2}\left\langle u_{total} \right\rangle \implies \frac{\left\langle u_E \right\rangle}{\left\langle u_{total} \right\rangle} \; = \; \frac{1}{2}$

questions.text: The ratio of speeds of electromagnetic waves in vacuum and a medium, having dielectric constant $k \; = \; 3$ and permeability of $\mu \; = \; 2\mu_0$, is ($\mu_0$ = permeability of vacuum)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $v \; = \; \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu \epsilon}}$ // 📝 Solution: $v \; = \; \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\mu_0 \times 3\epsilon_0}} \; = \; \frac{c}{\sqrt{6}} \implies \frac{c}{v} \; = \; \sqrt{6} \implies c : v \; = \; \sqrt{6} : 1$
questions.topic: Speed of EM Wave in Medium

questions.text: An electromagnetic wave is transporting energy in the negative z direction. At a certain point and certain time the direction of electric field of the wave is along positive y direction. What will be the direction of the magnetic field of the wave at that point and instant?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Poynting vector $\vec{S} \; \parallel \; \vec{E} \times \vec{B}$ gives energy flow direction // 📝 Solution: $\vec{S} \; \parallel \; \vec{E} \times \vec{B} \implies \left( -\hat{k} \right) \; = \; \left( +\hat{j} \right) \times \hat{B} \implies \hat{B} \; = \; +\hat{i}$ since $\hat{j} \times \hat{i} \; = \; -\hat{k}$
questions.topic: Poynting Vector and Direction of Fields

questions.text: The electric field of an electromagnetic wave in free space is represented as $\vec{E} \; = \; E_0 \cos\left( \omega t \; - \; kz \right)\hat{i}$. The corresponding magnetic induction vector will be :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $B_0 \; = \; \frac{E_0}{c}$ and $\hat{E} \times \hat{B} \; = \; \hat{v}$ // 📝 Solution: Wave moves along $+z \implies \hat{B} \; = \; \hat{k} \times \hat{i} \; = \; \hat{j} \;;\; B_0 \; = \; \frac{E_0}{C} \implies \vec{B} \; = \; \frac{E_0}{C}\cos\left( \omega t \; - \; kz \right)\hat{j}$
questions.topic: Direction and Magnitude of B in EM Wave

questions.text: A plane electromagnetic wave is moving in free space with velocity $c \; = \; 3 \times 10^{8}\;\mathrm{m/s}$ and its electric field is given as $\vec{E} \; = \; 54\sin\left( kz \; - \; \omega t \right)\hat{j}\;\mathrm{V/m}$, where $\hat{j}$ is the unit vector along $y$-axis. The magnetic field vector $\vec{B}$ of the wave is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $B_0 \; = \; \frac{E_0}{c}$ and $\vec{E} \times \vec{B}$ along $+z$ // 📝 Solution: $B_0 \; = \; \frac{54}{3 \times 10^{8}} \; = \; 1.8 \times 10^{-7}\;\mathrm{T} \;;\; \hat{j} \times \left( -\hat{i} \right) \; = \; \hat{k} \implies \vec{B} \; = \; -1.8 \times 10^{-7}\sin\left( kz \; - \; \omega t \right)\hat{i}\;\mathrm{T}$
questions.topic: Direction and Magnitude of B in EM Wave

questions.text: If frequency of electromagnetic wave is $60\;\mathrm{MHz}$ and it travels in air along $z$ direction then the corresponding electric and magnetic field vectors will be mutually perpendicular to each other and the wavelength of the wave (in $\mathrm{m}$) is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\lambda \; = \; \frac{c}{f}$ // 📝 Solution: $\lambda \; = \; \frac{3 \times 10^{8}}{60 \times 10^{6}} \; = \; 5\;\mathrm{m}$

questions.text: The electric field in an electromagnetic wave is given by $\vec{E} \; = \; \hat{i}\,40 \cos\omega\left( t \; - \; \frac{z}{c} \right)\;\mathrm{N\,C^{-1}}$. The magnetic field induction of this wave is (in SI unit) :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $B_0 \; = \; \frac{E_0}{c}$ and $\hat{E} \times \hat{B} \; = \; \hat{v}$ // 📝 Solution: $\hat{E} \; = \; \hat{i} \;,\; \hat{v} \; = \; \hat{k} \implies \hat{B} \; = \; \hat{k} \times \hat{i} \; = \; \hat{j} \;;\; B_0 \; = \; \frac{40}{c} \implies \vec{B} \; = \; \hat{j}\,\frac{40}{c}\cos\omega\left( t \; - \; \frac{z}{c} \right)$
questions.topic: Direction and Magnitude of B in EM Wave

questions.text: A plane electromagnetic wave of frequency $35\;\mathrm{MHz}$ travels in free space along the X-direction. At a particular point (in space and time) $\vec{E} \; = \; 9.6\,\hat{j}\;\mathrm{V/m}$. The value of magnetic field at this point is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $B \; = \; \frac{E}{c}$ and $\hat{B} \; = \; \hat{v} \times \hat{E}$ // 📝 Solution: $B \; = \; \frac{9.6}{3 \times 10^{8}} \; = \; 3.2 \times 10^{-8}\;\mathrm{T} \;;\; \hat{B} \; = \; \hat{i} \times \hat{j} \; = \; \hat{k} \implies \vec{B} \; = \; 3.2 \times 10^{-8}\,\hat{k}\;\mathrm{T}$
questions.topic: Direction and Magnitude of B in EM Wave

questions.text: Match the LIST-I with LIST-II. List-I: A. Radio-wave, B. Micro-wave, C. Infrared-wave, D. X-ray. List-II: I. is produced by Magnetron valve, II. due to change in the vibrational modes of atoms, III. due to inner shell electrons moving from higher to lower energy level, IV. due to rapid acceleration of electrons. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall the production mechanism of each EM wave // 📝 Solution: Radio $\implies$ rapid acceleration of electrons (IV) $\;;\;$ Micro $\implies$ Magnetron valve (I) $\;;\;$ IR $\implies$ vibrational modes of atoms (II) $\;;\;$ X-ray $\implies$ inner shell transitions (III) $\implies$ A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III

questions.text: Which of the following are true? A. Speed of light in vacuum is dependent on the direction of propagation. B. Speed of light in a medium is independent of the wavelength of light. C. The speed of light is independent of the motion of the source. D. The speed of light in a medium is independent of intensity. Choose the correct answer from the option given below :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Speed of light in vacuum is constant; speed in a medium depends on wavelength (dispersion) // 📝 Solution: A false $\implies$ $c$ is same in all directions $\;;\;$ B false $\implies$ $v \; = \; v\left( \lambda \right)$ in medium $\;;\;$ C true $\;;\;$ D true $\implies$ correct option is C and D only

questions.text: A laser beam has intensity of $4.0 \times 10^{14}\;\mathrm{W/m^2}$. The amplitude of magnetic field associated with beam is ____ T. (Take $\epsilon_o \; = \; 8.85 \times 10^{-12}\;\mathrm{C^2/N\,m^2}$ and $c \; = \; 3 \times 10^{8}\;\mathrm{m/s}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $I \; = \; \frac{1}{2}\epsilon_0 c E_0^2$ with $E_0 \; = \; cB_0$ // 📝 Solution: $I \; = \; \frac{1}{2}\epsilon_0 c^3 B_0^2 \implies B_0 \; = \; \sqrt{\frac{2I}{\epsilon_0 c^3}} \; = \; \sqrt{\frac{8 \times 10^{14}}{8.85 \times 10^{-12} \times 2.7 \times 10^{25}}} \; = \; \sqrt{3.347} \; = \; 1.83\;\mathrm{T}$

questions.text: In an experiment, a set of readings are obtained as follows - $1.24\;\text{mm}$, $1.25\;\text{mm}$, $1.23\;\text{mm}$, $1.21\;\text{mm}$. The expected least count of the instrument used in recording these readings is ____ $\text{mm}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The least count is the smallest difference the instrument can read, set by the last recorded decimal place. // 📝 Solution: All readings are recorded to two decimal places, and differences are as small as $1.25\;-\;1.24\;=\;0.01\;\text{mm}$. Hence $\text{LC}\;=\;0.01\;\text{mm}$

questions.text: Identify the physical quantity that cannot be measured using a spherometer :

options.text: Radius of curvature of concave surface
Radius of curvature of convex surface

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A spherometer measures small thicknesses and the curvature of surfaces. // 📝 Solution: A spherometer is used for the thickness of thin plates and the radius of curvature of concave and convex surfaces. Specific rotation of liquids is measured with a polarimeter, so option (2) is the answer.

questions.text: In a vernier calliper, when both jaws touch each other, the zero of the vernier scale shifts towards left and its $4^{\text{th}}$ division coincides exactly with a certain division on the main scale. If $50$ vernier scale divisions equal $49$ main scale divisions and the zero error in the instrument is $0.04\;\text{mm}$, then how many main scale divisions are there in $1\;\text{cm}$ ?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Zero error magnitude is $n\times\text{LC}$, and $\text{LC}\;=\;\frac{\text{MSD}}{50}$ for $50\;\text{VSD}\;=\;49\;\text{MSD}$. // 📝 Solution: $1\;\text{VSD}\;=\;\frac{49}{50}\;\text{MSD}\;\implies\;\text{LC}\;=\;\frac{\text{MSD}}{50}$. $\left\lvert \text{zero error} \right\rvert\;=\;4\;\text{LC}\;=\;0.04\;\implies\;\text{LC}\;=\;0.01\;\text{mm}$. $\frac{\text{MSD}}{50}\;=\;0.01\;\implies\;\text{MSD}\;=\;0.5\;\text{mm}$. $N\;=\;\frac{10\;\text{mm}}{0.5\;\text{mm}}\;=\;20$

questions.text: The diameter of a sphere is measured using a vernier caliper whose $9$ divisions of main scale are equal to $10$ divisions of vernier scale. The shortest division on the main scale is equal to $1\;\text{mm}$. The main scale reading is $2\;\text{cm}$ and the second division of the vernier scale coincides with a division on the main scale. If the mass of the sphere is $8.635\;\text{g}$, the density of the sphere is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find $\text{LC}\;=\;1\;\text{MSD}\;-\;1\;\text{VSD}$, then $d\;=\;\text{MSR}\;+\;\text{VSR}\times\text{LC}$ and $\rho\;=\;\frac{m}{\frac{4}{3}\pi\left( \frac{d}{2} \right)^3}$. // 📝 Solution: $9\;\text{MSD}\;=\;10\;\text{VSD}\;\implies\;\text{LC}\;=\;1\;\text{MSD}\;-\;\frac{9}{10}\;\text{MSD}\;=\;\frac{1}{10}\;\text{MSD}\;=\;0.01\;\text{cm}$. $d\;=\;2\;+\;0.01\times 2\;=\;2.02\;\text{cm}$. $V\;=\;\frac{4}{3}\pi\left( \frac{2.02}{2} \right)^3\;\approx\;4.32\;\text{cm}^3$. $\rho\;=\;\frac{8.635}{4.32}\;\approx\;2.0\;\text{g/cm}^3$

questions.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A) : In Vernier calliper if positive zero error exists, then while taking measurements, the reading taken will be more than the actual reading. Reason (R) : The zero error in Vernier Calliper might have happened due to manufacturing defect or due to rough handling. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Actual reading $=\;\text{observed reading}\;-\;\text{zero error}$. // 📝 Solution: With positive zero error, observed reading $=\;\text{actual}\;+\;e\;>\;\text{actual}$, so (A) is true. Zero error does arise from manufacturing defects or rough handling, so (R) is true. But (R) states the cause of zero error, not why the reading is larger, so it does not explain (A). Hence option (2).

questions.text: When both jaws of a vernier callipers touch each other, the zero mark of the vernier scale is to the right of the zero mark of the main scale, and the $4^{\text{th}}$ mark on the vernier scale coincides with a certain mark on the main scale. While measuring the length of a cylinder, the observer observes $15$ divisions on the main scale and the $5^{\text{th}}$ division of the vernier scale coincides with a main scale division. The measured length of the cylinder is ____ $\text{mm}$. (Least count of Vernier calliper $=\;0.1\;\text{mm}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\text{True length}\;=\;\text{MSR}\;+\;\text{VSR}\times\text{LC}\;-\;\text{zero error}$, with positive zero error $=\;+n\times\text{LC}$. // 📝 Solution: Zero error $e\;=\;+4\times 0.1\;=\;+0.4\;\text{mm}$. $\text{MSR}\;=\;15\;\text{mm}$ (taking $1\;\text{MSD}\;=\;1\;\text{mm}$). $\text{VSR}\;=\;5\times 0.1\;=\;0.5\;\text{mm}$. $\text{Observed}\;=\;15.5\;\text{mm}$. $\text{True length}\;=\;15.5\;-\;0.4\;=\;15.1\;\text{mm}$

questions.text: While measuring the diameter of a wire using a screw gauge the following readings were noted. Main scale reading is $1\;\text{mm}$ and circular scale reading is equal to $42$ divisions. Pitch of the screw gauge is $1\;\text{mm}$ and it has $100$ divisions on the circular scale. The diameter of the wire is $\frac{x}{50}\;\text{mm}$. The value of $x$ is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\text{LC}\;=\;\frac{\text{pitch}}{\text{no. of circular divisions}}$ and $\text{Diameter}\;=\;\text{MSR}\;+\;\text{CSR}\;\times\;\text{LC}$. // 📝 Solution: $\text{LC}\;=\;\frac{1}{100}\;=\;0.01\;\text{mm}$. $\text{Diameter}\;=\;1\;+\;\left( 0.01 \right)\times 42\;=\;1.42\;\text{mm}\;=\;\frac{x}{50}\;\implies\;x\;=\;71$

questions.text: In a screw gauge, the zero of the circular scale lies $3$ divisions above the horizontal pitch line when the metallic studs are brought in contact. Using this instrument the thickness of a sheet is measured. If the pitch scale reading is $1\;\text{mm}$ and the circular scale reading is $51$, then the correct thickness of the sheet is ____ $\text{mm}$. [Assume least count is $0.01\;\text{mm}$]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\text{Correct reading}\;=\;\text{PSR}\;+\;\text{CSR}\times\text{LC}\;-\;\text{zero error}$, and zero above the line gives negative zero error. // 📝 Solution: Zero error $=\;-3\times 0.01\;=\;-0.03\;\text{mm}$. $\text{Reading}\;=\;1\;+\;51\times 0.01\;-\;\left( -0.03 \right)\;=\;1\;+\;0.51\;+\;0.03\;=\;1.54\;\text{mm}$

questions.text: There are $100$ divisions on the circular scale of a screw gauge of pitch $1\;\text{mm}$. With no measuring quantity in between the jaws, the zero of the circular scale lies $5$ divisions below the reference line. The diameter of a wire is then measured using this screw gauge. It is found that $4$ linear scale divisions are clearly visible while $60$ divisions on the circular scale coincide with the reference line. The diameter of the wire is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Zero below the reference line means positive zero error, so $\text{Reading}\;=\;\text{MSR}\;+\;\text{CSR}\times\text{LC}\;-\;\text{zero error}$. // 📝 Solution: $\text{LC}\;=\;\frac{1}{100}\;=\;0.01\;\text{mm}$. Zero error $=\;+0.05\;\text{mm}$. $\text{Reading}\;=\;4\times 1\;+\;60\times 0.01\;-\;0.05\;=\;4.55\;\text{mm}$

questions.text: In a metre bridge experiment the balance point is obtained if the gaps are closed by $2\;\Omega$ and $3\;\Omega$. A shunt of $X\;\Omega$ is added to the $3\;\Omega$ resistor to shift the balancing point by $22.5\;\text{cm}$. The value of $X$ is ____
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Metre bridge balance condition is $\frac{P}{Q}\;=\;\frac{l}{100\;-\;l}$, and a shunt gives the parallel combination $\frac{3X}{3\;+\;X}$. // 📝 Solution: Initially $\frac{2}{3}\;=\;\frac{l}{100\;-\;l}\;\implies\;l\;=\;40\;\text{cm}$. After the shift the balance point is $40\;+\;22.5\;=\;62.5\;\text{cm}$. So $\frac{2}{\left( \frac{3X}{3\;+\;X} \right)}\;=\;\frac{62.5}{37.5}\;=\;\frac{5}{3}\;\implies\;\frac{3X}{3\;+\;X}\;=\;\frac{6}{5}\;\implies\;15X\;=\;18\;+\;6X\;\implies\;X\;=\;2\;\Omega$

questions.text: Least count of a vernier caliper is $\frac{1}{20\;N}\;\text{cm}$. The value of one division on the main scale is $1\;\text{mm}$. Then the number of divisions of main scale that coincide with $N$ divisions of vernier scale is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\text{LC}\;=\;1\;\text{MSD}\;-\;1\;\text{VSD}$ with $1\;\text{VSD}\;=\;\frac{x\times 1\;\text{mm}}{N}$. // 📝 Solution: Let $x$ MSD coincide with $N$ VSD. $\frac{1}{20N}\;\text{cm}\;=\;\frac{1}{2N}\;\text{mm}\;=\;1\;-\;\frac{x}{N}\;\implies\;x\;=\;N\left( 1\;-\;\frac{1}{2N} \right)\;=\;\frac{2N\;-\;1}{2}$

questions.text: A null point is found at $200\;\text{cm}$ in a potentiometer when the cell in the secondary circuit is shunted by $5\;\Omega$. When a resistance of $15\;\Omega$ is used for shunting, the null point moves to $300\;\text{cm}$. The internal resistance of the cell is ____ $\Omega$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Terminal voltage across the shunt is $V\;=\;\frac{\varepsilon R}{r\;+\;R}$ and it is proportional to the null length. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{5\varepsilon}{r\;+\;5}\;=\;k\left( 200 \right)$ and $\frac{15\varepsilon}{r\;+\;15}\;=\;k\left( 300 \right)$. Dividing, $\frac{5\left( r\;+\;15 \right)}{15\left( r\;+\;5 \right)}\;=\;\frac{2}{3}\;\implies\;r\;+\;15\;=\;2r\;+\;10\;\implies\;r\;=\;5\;\Omega$

questions.text: In a vernier callipers, $50$ vernier scale divisions are equal to $48$ main scale divisions. If one main scale division $=\;0.05\;\text{mm}$, then the least count of the vernier callipers is ____ $\text{mm}$.

If $50$ Vernier divisions are equal to $49$ main scale divisions of a travelling microscope and the smallest reading of the main scale is $0.5\;\text{mm}$, the Vernier constant of the travelling microscope is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Vernier constant $=\;S\;-\;V$ where $50V\;=\;49S$. // 📝 Solution: $50V\;=\;49S\;\implies\;S\;=\;50\left( S\;-\;V \right)\;\implies\;S\;-\;V\;=\;\frac{0.5}{50}\;=\;\frac{1}{100}\;=\;0.01\;\text{mm}$

questions.text: The measured value of the length of a simple pendulum is $20\;\text{cm}$ with $2\;\text{mm}$ accuracy. The time for $50$ oscillations was measured to be $40$ seconds with $1$ second resolution. From these measurements, the accuracy in the measurement of acceleration due to gravity is $N\%$. The value of $N$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: From $g\;=\;\frac{4\pi^2 \ell}{T^2}$, $\frac{\Delta g}{g}\;=\;\frac{\Delta \ell}{\ell}\;+\;2\frac{\Delta T}{T}$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{\Delta g}{g}\;=\;\frac{0.2}{20}\;+\;2\left( \frac{1}{40} \right)\;=\;0.01\;+\;0.05\;=\;0.06\;\implies\;N\;=\;6\%$

questions.text: Young's modulus of the material of a wire of length $L$ and cross-sectional area $A$ is $Y$. If the length of the wire is doubled and the cross-sectional area is halved, then Young's modulus will be :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Young's modulus is a material property and does not depend on dimensions. // 📝 Solution: $Y\;=\;\frac{FL}{A\Delta L}$ is fixed by the material, not by $L$ or $A$. Changing $L\;\to\;2L$ and $A\;\to\;\frac{A}{2}$ leaves $Y$ unchanged, so the modulus remains $Y$.

questions.text: In a screw gauge, there are $100$ divisions on the circular scale and the main scale moves by $0.5\;\text{mm}$ on a complete rotation of the circular scale. The zero of the circular scale lies $6$ divisions below the line of graduation when two studs are brought in contact with each other. When a wire is placed between the studs, $4$ linear scale divisions are clearly visible while the $46^{\text{th}}$ division of the circular scale coincides with the reference line. The diameter of the wire is ____ $\times\;10^{-2}\;\text{mm}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Diameter $=\;\text{MSR}\;+\;\left( \text{CSR}\;-\;\text{zero error divisions} \right)\times\text{LC}$, with $\text{LC}\;=\;\frac{\text{pitch}}{\text{no. of circular divisions}}$. // 📝 Solution: $\text{LC}\;=\;\frac{0.5}{100}\;=\;5\;\times\;10^{-3}\;\text{mm}$. Zero error $=\;+6\;\text{div}\;=\;+0.03\;\text{mm}$. $\text{MSR}\;=\;4\;\times\;0.5\;=\;2\;\text{mm}$. $\text{Diameter}\;=\;2\;+\;46\left( 5\;\times\;10^{-3} \right)\;-\;6\left( 5\;\times\;10^{-3} \right)\;=\;2.2\;\text{mm}$. Note: the answer key in the PDF lists $22$, which is marked here. Direct calculation gives $2.2\;\text{mm}$, so please verify the key against the original NTA paper.

questions.text: $10$ divisions on the main scale of a Vernier calliper coincide with $11$ divisions on the Vernier scale. If each division on the main scale is of $5$ units, the least count of the instrument is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\text{LC}\;=\;1\;\text{MSD}\;-\;1\;\text{VSD}$. // 📝 Solution: $10\;\text{MSD}\;=\;11\;\text{VSD}\;\implies\;1\;\text{VSD}\;=\;\frac{10}{11}\;\text{MSD}$. $\text{LC}\;=\;1\;\text{MSD}\;-\;\frac{10}{11}\;\text{MSD}\;=\;\frac{1\;\text{MSD}}{11}\;=\;\frac{5}{11}\;\text{units}$

questions.text: In an experiment to find emf of a cell using a potentiometer, the length of null point for a cell of emf $1.5\;\text{V}$ is found to be $60\;\text{cm}$. If this cell is replaced by another cell of emf $E$, the length of null point increases by $40\;\text{cm}$. The value of $E$ is $\frac{x}{10}\;\text{V}$. The value of $x$ is ____.

One main scale division of a vernier caliper is equal to $m$ units. If the $n^{\text{th}}$ division of the main scale coincides with the $\left( n\;+\;1 \right)^{\text{th}}$ division of the vernier scale, the least count of the vernier caliper is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\text{LC}\;=\;1\;\text{MSD}\;-\;1\;\text{VSD}$. // 📝 Solution: $n\;\text{MSD}\;=\;\left( n\;+\;1 \right)\text{VSD}\;\implies\;1\;\text{VSD}\;=\;\frac{n}{n\;+\;1}\;\text{MSD}$. $\text{LC}\;=\;m\;-\;m\left( \frac{n}{n\;+\;1} \right)\;=\;m\left( \frac{n\;+\;1\;-\;n}{n\;+\;1} \right)\;=\;\frac{m}{n\;+\;1}$

questions.text: A vernier callipers has $20$ divisions on the vernier scale, which coincides with the $19^{\text{th}}$ division on the main scale. The least count of the instrument is $0.1\;\text{mm}$. One main scale division is equal to ____ $\text{mm}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\text{LC}\;=\;1\;\text{MSD}\;-\;1\;\text{VSD}$. // 📝 Solution: $20\;\text{VSD}\;=\;19\;\text{MSD}\;\implies\;1\;\text{VSD}\;=\;\frac{19}{20}\;\text{MSD}$. $0.1\;\text{mm}\;=\;1\;\text{MSD}\;-\;\frac{19}{20}\;\text{MSD}\;=\;\frac{1}{20}\;\text{MSD}\;\implies\;1\;\text{MSD}\;=\;2\;\text{mm}$

questions.text: The equation of stationary wave is $y = 2a\sin\left( \frac{2\pi nt}{\lambda} \right)\cos\left( \frac{2\pi x}{\lambda} \right)$. Which of the following is NOT correct?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The argument $\frac{2\pi nt}{\lambda}$ is dimensionless, so $\frac{n}{\lambda}$ must have dimension $\left[ T^{-1} \right]$. // 📝 Solution: $\left[ \frac{n}{\lambda} \right] = \left[ \omega \right] = \left[ T^{-1} \right] \implies$ option A is wrong; $\left[ n \right] = \left[ \lambda\omega \right] = \left[ LT^{-1} \right]$; $\left[ x \right] = \left[ \lambda \right] = \left[ L \right]$; $\left[ nt \right] = \left[ \lambda \right] = \left[ L \right]$.
questions.topic: Dimensional analysis of stationary wave equation

questions.text: The equation of a circle is $x^{2} + y^{2} = a^{2}$, where $a$ is the radius. If the origin is shifted, the equation becomes $\left( x - At \right)^{2} + \left( y - \frac{t}{B} \right)^{2} = a^{2}$. Given that the dimension of $t$ is $\left[ T^{-1} \right]$, find the dimensions of $A$ and $B$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Each term inside the bracket must have the dimension of length. // 📝 Solution: $\left[ At \right] = L \implies \left[ A \right] = \frac{L}{T^{-1}} = LT$; $\left[ \frac{t}{B} \right] = L \implies \left[ B \right] = \frac{T^{-1}}{L} = L^{-1}T^{-1}$.
questions.topic: Dimensional analysis of shifted circle equation

questions.text: If $R$, $X_{L}$ and $X_{C}$ represent resistance, inductive reactance and capacitive reactance respectively, then which of the following is dimensionless?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $R$, $X_{L}$ and $X_{C}$ all have the dimension of resistance $\left[ ML^{2}T^{-3}A^{-2} \right]$. // 📝 Solution: $\left[ R \right] = \left[ X_{L} \right] = \left[ X_{C} \right] = \left[ ML^{2}T^{-3}A^{-2} \right] \implies \frac{\left[ R \right]}{\sqrt{\left[ X_{L} \right]\left[ X_{C} \right]}} = \frac{\left[ ML^{2}T^{-3}A^{-2} \right]}{\left[ ML^{2}T^{-3}A^{-2} \right]} = \left[ M^{0}L^{0}T^{0} \right]$.

questions.text: Applying the principle of homogeneity of dimensions, determine which one is correct, where $T$ is time period, $G$ is gravitational constant, $M$ is mass and $r$ is radius of orbit.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The dimension of $G$ is $\left[ M^{-1}L^{3}T^{-2} \right]$; both sides of the equation must match. // 📝 Solution: $\left[ T^{2} \right] = \frac{\left[ L^{3} \right]}{\left[ M^{-1}L^{3}T^{-2} \right]\left[ M \right]} = \left[ T^{2} \right] \implies$ option C is dimensionally correct.

questions.text: The electric flux is $\phi\;=\;\alpha\sigma\;+\;\beta\lambda$ where $\lambda$ and $\sigma$ are linear and surface charge density, respectively. $\left(\frac{\alpha}{\beta}\right)$ represents
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Each term has the dimensions of $\phi$, so $\left[\alpha\right]\;=\;\frac{\left[\phi\right]}{\left[\sigma\right]}$ and $\left[\beta\right]\;=\;\frac{\left[\phi\right]}{\left[\lambda\right]}$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{\alpha}{\beta}\;=\;\frac{\lambda}{\sigma}\;=\;\frac{C/m}{C/m^2}\;=\;m\;\implies$ displacement (length)

questions.text: Match List - I with List - II. List - I: (A) Magnetic induction (B) Magnetic intensity $\left(H\;=\;\frac{B}{\mu}\right)$ (C) Magnetic flux (D) Magnetic moment $\left(\vec{M}\;=\;i\vec{A}\right)$. List - II: (I) Ampere meter$^2$ (II) Weber (III) Gauss (IV) Ampere/meter
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall the units of $B$, $H$, $\Phi_B$ and magnetic moment. // 📝 Solution: $B\;\to\;\text{Gauss}$, $H\;\to\;\text{A/m}$, $\Phi_B\;\to\;\text{Weber}$, $M\;\to\;\text{A m}^2\;\implies\;\text{(A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(I)}$

questions.text: If $\mu_0$ and $\varepsilon_0$ are the permeability and permittivity of free space, respectively, then the dimension of $\frac{1}{\mu_0\varepsilon_0}$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\frac{1}{\mu_0\varepsilon_0} = c^{2}$, where $c$ is the speed of light. // 📝 Solution: $c = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0\varepsilon_0}} \implies \frac{1}{\mu_0\varepsilon_0} = c^{2} \implies [c^{2}] = L^{2}T^{-2}$

questions.text: If $\epsilon_0$ denotes the permittivity of free space and $\Phi_E$ is the electric flux through a closed surface, then the dimension of $\epsilon_0\frac{d\Phi_E}{dt}$ is that of:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Displacement current is $i_d = \varepsilon_0\frac{d\Phi_E}{dt}$. // 📝 Solution: $\varepsilon_0\frac{d\Phi_E}{dt} = i_d \implies$ dimension of current $= [A]$

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: A. Surface tension; B. Pressure; C. Viscosity; D. Impulse.
