For middle shell $B$ ($r \;=\; b$), it is outside $A$ and inside $C$, so $V_B \;=\; \frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\left(\frac{q_1 \;+\; q_2}{b} \;+\; \frac{q_3}{c}\right)$. For outer shell $C$ ($r \;=\; c$), it is outside $A$ and $B$, so $V_C \;=\; \frac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\left(\frac{q_1 \;+\; q_2 \;+\; q_3}{c}\right)$.

questions.text: A stream of positively charged particles having $\frac{q}{m} \;=\; 2 \;\times\; 10^{11}\;\frac{\text{C}}{\text{kg}}$ and velocity $\vec{v}_0 \;=\; 3 \;\times\; 10^7\;\hat{i}\;\text{m/s}$ is deflected by an electric field $1.8\;\hat{j}\;\text{kV/m}$. The electric field exists in a region of $10\;\text{cm}$ along $x$ direction. Due to the electric field, the deflection of the charge particles in the $y$ direction is _____ $\text{mm}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use kinematics for a charged particle moving perpendicular to a uniform electric field: $y \;=\; \frac{1}{2}a_y t^2$ where $t \;=\; \frac{x}{v_0}$. // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] Acceleration along $y$-direction is $a_y \;=\; \frac{qE}{m} \;=\; \left(2 \;\times\; 10^{11}\right) \;\times\; \left(1.8 \;\times\; 10^3\right) \;=\; 3.6 \;\times\; 10^{14}\;\text{m/s}^2$. Time taken to cross the region is $t \;=\; \frac{L}{v_0} \;=\; \frac{0.10}{3 \;\times\; 10^7}\;\text{s} \;\implies\; y \;=\; \frac{1}{2}a_y t^2 \;=\; \frac{1}{2}\left(3.6 \;\times\; 10^{14}\right)\left(\frac{0.01}{9 \;\times\; 10^{14}}\right) \;=\; 0.2 \;\times\; 0.01\;\text{m} \;=\; 2 \;\times\; 10^{-3}\;\text{m} \;=\; 2\;\text{mm}$.
questions.topic: Motion of Charged Particle in Electric Field

questions.text: If two charges $q_1$ and $q_2$ are separated with distance '$d$' and placed in a medium of dielectric constant $K$. What will be the equivalent distance between charges in air for the same electrostatic force?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Equate the Coulomb's electrostatic force in the dielectric medium to the force in air at an equivalent distance $d'$. // 📝 Solution: Force in medium is $F_{\text{med}} \;=\; \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 K}\frac{q_1 q_2}{d^2}$ and force in air is $F_{\text{air}} \;=\; \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\frac{q_1 q_2}{\left(d'\right)^2} \;\implies\; F_{\text{med}} \;=\; F_{\text{air}} \;\implies\; \frac{q_1 q_2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 K d^2} \;=\; \frac{q_1 q_2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 \left(d'\right)^2} \;\implies\; \left(d'\right)^2 \;=\; K d^2 \;\implies\; d' \;=\; d\sqrt{K}$.

questions.text: The electric potential at the surface of an atomic nucleus ($z \;=\; 50$) of radius $9 \;\times\; 10^{-13}\;\text{cm}$ is _____ $\times\; 10^6\;\text{V}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Potential at the surface of a spherical nucleus is $V \;=\; \frac{k Z e}{R}$. // 📝 Solution: Charge of the nucleus is $Q \;=\; Z e \;=\; 50 \;\times\; 1.6 \;\times\; 10^{-19}\;\text{C}$ and radius is $R \;=\; 9 \;\times\; 10^{-13}\;\text{cm} \;=\; 9 \;\times\; 10^{-15}\;\text{m}$. Electric potential at the surface is $V \;=\; \frac{k Q}{R} \;=\; \frac{9 \;\times\; 10^9 \;\times\; 50 \;\times\; 1.6 \;\times\; 10^{-19}}{9 \;\times\; 10^{-15}} \;=\; 80 \;\times\; 10^5\;\text{V} \;=\; 8 \;\times\; 10^6\;\text{V}$.

questions.text: Two isolated metallic solid spheres of radii $R$ and $2R$ are charged such that both have same charge density $\sigma$. The spheres are then connected by a thin conducting wire. If the new charge density of the bigger sphere is $\sigma'$. The ratio $\frac{\sigma'}{\sigma}$ is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: When connected by a conducting wire, charge redistributes until both spheres reach a common potential $V_1' \;=\; V_2'$, while total charge remains conserved. // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] Initial charges on the spheres are $Q_1 \;=\; \sigma\left(4\pi R^2\right)$ and $Q_2 \;=\; \sigma\left(4\pi\left(2R\right)^2\right) \;=\; 16\pi R^2\sigma$, so total charge is $Q_{\text{total}} \;=\; Q_1 \;+\; Q_2 \;=\; 20\pi R^2\sigma$. After connection, potentials become equal: $\frac{k Q_1'}{R} \;=\; \frac{k Q_2'}{2R} \;\implies\; Q_1' \;=\; \frac{Q_2'}{2}$. By charge conservation, $\frac{Q_2'}{2} \;+\; Q_2' \;=\; 20\pi R^2\sigma \;\implies\; \frac{3}{2}Q_2' \;=\; 20\pi R^2\sigma \;\implies\; Q_2' \;=\; \frac{40}{3}\pi R^2\sigma$. New surface charge density on bigger sphere is $\sigma' \;=\; \frac{Q_2'}{4\pi\left(2R\right)^2} \;=\; \frac{40\pi R^2\sigma}{3 \;\times\; 16\pi R^2} \;=\; \frac{5}{6}\sigma \;\implies\; \frac{\sigma'}{\sigma} \;=\; \frac{5}{6}$.

questions.text: Two point charges $2q$ and $q$ are placed at vertex $A$ and centre of face $CDEF$ of the cube as shown in figure. The electric flux passing through the cube is : [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A charge at a cube vertex contributes $\frac{1}{8}$ of its flux to the cube, and a charge at the centre of a face contributes $\frac{1}{2}$ of its flux. // 📝 Solution: Charge $2q$ is at vertex $A$ (shared by $8$ cubes), so its flux contribution is $\phi_1 \;=\; \frac{2q}{8\epsilon_0} \;=\; \frac{q}{4\epsilon_0}$. Charge $q$ is at the centre of face $CDEF$ (shared by $2$ cubes), so its flux contribution is $\phi_2 \;=\; \frac{q}{2\epsilon_0}$. Total electric flux through the cube is $\phi \;=\; \phi_1 \;+\; \phi_2 \;=\; \frac{q}{4\epsilon_0} \;+\; \frac{q}{2\epsilon_0} \;=\; \frac{3q}{4\epsilon_0}$.

questions.text: The vehicles carrying inflammable fluids usually have metallic chains touching the ground :

options.text: To protect tyres from catching dirt from ground
To conduct excess charge due to air friction to ground and prevent sparking

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Static electricity builds up on moving vehicles due to air friction and tyre-road friction. // 📝 Solution: As vehicles move, air friction builds up static electric charge on the body of the vehicle. If this charge accumulates, it can cause an electric spark and ignite inflammable fluids. Metallic chains touching the ground provide a conducting path to safely discharge excess static charge into the earth.

questions.text: Three small identical bubbles of water having same charge on each coalesce to form a bigger bubble. Then the ratio of the potentials on one initial bubble and that on the resultant bigger bubble is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: When $n$ identical charged drops/bubbles coalesce, $R \;=\; n^{1/3}r$, $Q \;=\; nq$, and $V_{\text{big}} \;=\; n^{2/3}V_{\text{small}}$. // 📝 Solution: Initial potential of one bubble of radius $r$ and charge $q$ is $V_i \;=\; \frac{kq}{r}$. When $3$ bubbles coalesce, volume conservation gives $\frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 \;=\; 3\left(\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\right) \;\implies\; R \;=\; 3^{1/3}r$, and total charge is $Q \;=\; 3q$. Final potential is $V_f \;=\; \frac{k(3q)}{3^{1/3}r} \;=\; 3^{2/3}V_i \;\implies\; V_i : V_f \;=\; 1 : 3^{2/3}$.

questions.text: A simple pendulum has a bob with mass $m$ and charge $q$. The pendulum string has negligible mass. When a uniform and horizontal electric field $\vec{E}$ is applied, the tension in the string changes. The final tension in the string, when pendulum attains an equilibrium position is _____. ($g$: acceleration due to gravity)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: At equilibrium, tension balances the perpendicular forces of gravity ($mg$ downward) and electrostatic force ($qE$ horizontal). // 📝 Solution: At equilibrium, let the string make an angle $\theta$ with the vertical. Resolving forces gives $T\cos\theta \;=\; mg$ (vertical) and $T\sin\theta \;=\; qE$ (horizontal). Squaring and adding both equations gives $T^2\left(\cos^2\theta \;+\; \sin^2\theta\right) \;=\; \left(mg\right)^2 \;+\; \left(qE\right)^2 \;\implies\; T \;=\; \sqrt{m^2 g^2 \;+\; q^2 E^2}$.

questions.text: Two charges $q$ and $3q$ are separated by a distance '$r$' in air. At a distance $x$ from charge $q$, the resultant electric field is zero. The value of $x$ is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Equate the magnitudes of electric fields due to $q$ and $3q$ at distance $x$ from $q$: $\frac{kq}{x^2} \;=\; \frac{k(3q)}{\left(r \;-\; x\right)^2}$. // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] At the neutral point $P$ between the two like charges at distance $x$ from $q$: $\frac{kq}{x^2} \;=\; \frac{k\left(3q\right)}{\left(r \;-\; x\right)^2} \;\implies\; \left(r \;-\; x\right)^2 \;=\; 3x^2 \;\implies\; r \;-\; x \;=\; \sqrt{3}x \;\implies\; x\left(1 \;+\; \sqrt{3}\right) \;=\; r \;\implies\; x \;=\; \frac{r}{1 \;+\; \sqrt{3}}$.

questions.text: $C_1$ and $C_2$ are two hollow concentric cubes enclosing charges $2Q$ and $3Q$ respectively as shown in figure. The ratio of electric flux passing through $C_1$ and $C_2$ is: [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Inner cube $C_1$ encloses charge $2Q$, whereas outer cube $C_2$ encloses both $2Q$ and $3Q$ (total $5Q$). // 📝 Solution: By Gauss's law, flux through inner cube $C_1$ is $\phi_1 \;=\; \frac{2Q}{\epsilon_0}$ and flux through outer concentric cube $C_2$ is $\phi_2 \;=\; \frac{2Q \;+\; 3Q}{\epsilon_0} \;=\; \frac{5Q}{\epsilon_0}$. Thus, the ratio is $\frac{\phi_1}{\phi_2} \;=\; \frac{2}{5} \;=\; 2 : 5$.

questions.text: For a charged spherical ball, electrostatic potential inside the ball varies with $r$ as $V \;=\; 2ar^2 \;+\; b$. Here, $a$ and $b$ are constant and $r$ is the distance from the center. The volume charge density inside the ball is $-\lambda a\varepsilon$. The value of $\lambda$ is _____. ($\varepsilon \;=\;$ permittivity of medium)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find the radial electric field using $E \;=\; -\frac{dV}{dr}$ and compare it with the field inside a uniformly charged sphere $E \;=\; \frac{\rho r}{3\varepsilon}$. // 📝 Solution: Electric field inside the ball is $E \;=\; -\frac{dV}{dr} \;=\; -\frac{d}{dr}\left(2ar^2 \;+\; b\right) \;=\; -4ar$. Since electric field inside a uniformly charged solid sphere of volume charge density $\rho$ is $E \;=\; \frac{\rho r}{3\varepsilon}$, comparing both gives $\frac{\rho r}{3\varepsilon} \;=\; -4ar \;\implies\; \rho \;=\; -12a\varepsilon$. Comparing with $\rho \;=\; -\lambda a\varepsilon$, we get $\lambda \;=\; 12$.

questions.text: An infinitely long positively charged straight thread has a linear charge density $\lambda\;\text{C m}^{-1}$. An electron revolves along a circular path having axis along the length of the wire. The graph that correctly represents the variation of the kinetic energy of electron as a function of radius of circular path from the wire is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Equate the electrostatic attraction $F \;=\; eE \;=\; \frac{2k\lambda e}{r}$ to the centripetal force $\frac{mv^2}{r}$ to find kinetic energy $\frac{1}{2}mv^2$. // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] Electric field at distance $r$ from the infinite line charge is $E \;=\; \frac{2k\lambda}{r}$. This provides the necessary centripetal force for circular motion: $\frac{mv^2}{r} \;=\; eE \;=\; \frac{2k\lambda e}{r} \;\implies\; mv^2 \;=\; 2k\lambda e \;\implies\; \text{KE} \;=\; \frac{1}{2}mv^2 \;=\; k\lambda e \;=\; \text{constant}$. Thus, kinetic energy is independent of $r$, represented by a horizontal straight line in Graph (3).
questions.topic: Field of Line Charge and Circular Motion

questions.text: An electric field $\vec{E} \;=\; \left(2x\hat{i}\right)\;\text{N C}^{-1}$ exists in space. A cube of side $2\;\text{m}$ is placed in the space as per figure given below. The electric flux through the cube is _____ $\text{N m}^2/\text{C}$. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Calculate net flux through the left face ($x \;=\; 2\;\text{m}$) and right face ($x \;=\; 4\;\text{m}$): $\phi_{\text{net}} \;=\; \left(E_{\text{right}} \;-\; E_{\text{left}}\right)A$. // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] The cube of side $a \;=\; 2\;\text{m}$ (face area $A \;=\; 4\;\text{m}^2$) extends from $x \;=\; 2\;\text{m}$ to $x \;=\; 4\;\text{m}$. At $x \;=\; 2\;\text{m}$, $E_{\text{in}} \;=\; 2(2) \;=\; 4\;\text{N/C} \;\implies\; \phi_{\text{in}} \;=\; -4 \;\times\; 4 \;=\; -16\;\text{N m}^2/\text{C}$. At $x \;=\; 4\;\text{m}$, $E_{\text{out}} \;=\; 2(4) \;=\; 8\;\text{N/C} \;\implies\; \phi_{\text{out}} \;=\; 8 \;\times\; 4 \;=\; 32\;\text{N m}^2/\text{C}$. Net flux is $\phi_{\text{net}} \;=\; -16 \;+\; 32 \;=\; 16\;\text{N m}^2/\text{C}$.

questions.text: At the centre of a half ring of radius $R \;=\; 10\;\text{cm}$ and linear charge density $4\;\text{nC m}^{-1}$, the potential is $x\pi\;\text{V}$. The value of $x$ is _____
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Potential at the centre of a charged half ring is $V \;=\; \frac{kQ}{R} \;=\; k\lambda\pi$. // 📝 Solution: Total charge on the half ring is $Q \;=\; \lambda\left(\pi R\right)$. Potential at the centre is $V \;=\; \frac{kQ}{R} \;=\; \frac{k\lambda\pi R}{R} \;=\; k\lambda\pi \;=\; \left(9 \;\times\; 10^9\right) \;\times\; \left(4 \;\times\; 10^{-9}\right)\pi \;=\; 36\pi\;\text{V} \;\implies\; x \;=\; 36$.

questions.text: Two equal positive point charges are separated by a distance $2a$. The distance of a point from the centre of the line joining two charges on the equatorial line (perpendicular bisector) at which force experienced by a test charge $q_0$ becomes maximum is $\frac{a}{\sqrt{x}}$. The value of $x$ is _____.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Write the net electrostatic force on the equatorial line at distance $r$ from the centre and set $\frac{dF}{dr} \;=\; 0$. // 📝 Solution: [FIGURE] At a distance $r$ on the perpendicular bisector, net force on $q_0$ is $F(r) \;=\; 2\left(\frac{k q q_0}{r^2 \;+\; a^2}\right) \;\times\; \frac{r}{\sqrt{r^2 \;+\; a^2}} \;=\; \frac{2k q q_0 r}{\left(r^2 \;+\; a^2\right)^{3/2}}$. For maximum force, $\frac{dF}{dr} \;=\; 0 \;\implies\; \left(r^2 \;+\; a^2\right)^{3/2} \;-\; r \;\cdot\; \frac{3}{2}\left(r^2 \;+\; a^2\right)^{1/2}\left(2r\right) \;=\; 0 \;\implies\; r^2 \;+\; a^2 \;-\; 3r^2 \;=\; 0 \;\implies\; r \;=\; \frac{a}{\sqrt{2}}$. Comparing with $\frac{a}{\sqrt{x}}$ gives $x \;=\; 2$.

questions.text: According to law of equipartition of energy the molar specific heat of a diatomic gas at constant volume where the molecule has one additional vibrational mode is :-
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A vibrational mode contributes $2$ degrees of freedom, and $C_{V}\;=\;\frac{f}{2}\,R$. // 📝 Solution: $f\;=\;3\;+\;2\;+\;2\;=\;7\;\implies\;C_{V}\;=\;\frac{7R}{2}$

questions.text: The graph between two temperature scales $P$ and $Q$ is shown in the figure. Between upper fixed point and lower fixed point there are $150$ equal divisions of scale $P$ and $100$ divisions on scale $Q$. The relationship for conversion between the two scales is given by : [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\frac{\text{reading}\;-\;\text{LFP}}{\text{UFP}\;-\;\text{LFP}}$ is the same for every scale. // 📝 Solution: LFP of $P$ is $180\;-\;150\;=\;30$ and LFP of $Q$ is $0\;\implies\;\frac{t_{P}\;-\;30}{180\;-\;30}\;=\;\frac{t_{Q}\;-\;0}{100\;-\;0}\;\implies\;\frac{t_{Q}}{100}\;=\;\frac{t_{P}\;-\;30}{150}$

questions.text: For three low density gases A, B, C pressure versus temperature graphs are plotted while keeping them at constant volume, as shown in the figure. [FIGURE] The temperature corresponding to the point 'K' is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: At constant volume $P\;\propto\;T$ (kelvin), so the lines meet at $P\;=\;0$, i.e. absolute zero. // 📝 Solution: $P\;=\;\frac{nR}{V}\left(t\;+\;273\right)\;\implies\;P\;=\;0\;\text{at}\;t\;=\;-273^\circ\text{C}$
questions.topic: Ideal Gas Laws and Absolute Zero

questions.text: An insulated cylinder of volume $60\;\text{cm}^{3}$ is filled with a gas at $27^\circ\text{C}$ and $2$ atmospheric pressure. Then the gas is compressed making the final volume as $20\;\text{cm}^{3}$ while allowing the temperature to rise to $77^\circ\text{C}$. The final pressure is ______ atmospheric pressure.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use the combined gas law $\frac{P_{1}V_{1}}{T_{1}}\;=\;\frac{P_{2}V_{2}}{T_{2}}$ with $T$ in kelvin. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{2\;\times\;60}{300}\;=\;\frac{P_{2}\;\times\;20}{350}\;\implies\;P_{2}\;=\;\frac{0.4\;\times\;350}{20}\;=\;7\;\text{atm}$

questions.text: In the following $p-V$ diagram the equation of state along the curved path is given by $\left(V\;-\;2\right)^{2}\;=\;4ap$ where $a$ is a constant. The total work done in the closed path is [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Integrate $p\,dV$ along the curve from $V\;=\;1$ to $V\;=\;3$, then add the straight constant-pressure return path. // 📝 Solution: $W_{ABC}\;=\;\int_{1}^{3}\frac{\left(V\;-\;2\right)^{2}}{4a}dV\;=\;\frac{1}{4a}\;\times\;\frac{2}{3}\;=\;\frac{1}{6a}\;,\;\;W_{CA}\;=\;\frac{1}{4a}\left(1\;-\;3\right)\;=\;-\frac{1}{2a}\;\implies\;W_{total}\;=\;-\frac{1}{3a}$

questions.text: $1\;\text{g}$ of a liquid is converted to vapour at $3\;\times\;10^{5}\;\text{Pa}$ pressure. If $10\%$ of the heat supplied is used for increasing the volume by $1600\;\text{cm}^{3}$ during this phase change, then the increase in internal energy in the process will be :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Work at constant pressure is $P\,\Delta V$ and it equals $10\%$ of the heat supplied. // 📝 Solution: $W\;=\;P\,\Delta V\;=\;3\times10^{5}\;\times\;1600\times10^{-6}\;=\;480\;\text{J}\;\implies\;Q\;=\;\frac{480}{0.1}\;=\;4800\;\text{J}\;\implies\;\Delta U\;=\;0.9\;\times\;4800\;=\;4320\;\text{J}$

questions.text: Heat energy of $735\;\text{J}$ is given to a diatomic gas allowing the gas to expand at constant pressure. Each gas molecule rotates around an internal axis but do not oscillate. The increase in the internal energy of the gas will be:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A rigid diatomic gas has $C_{V}\;=\;\frac{5R}{2}$ and $C_{P}\;=\;\frac{7R}{2}$, so $\frac{\Delta U}{Q}\;=\;\frac{C_{V}}{C_{P}}$. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta U\;=\;\frac{C_{V}}{C_{P}}\;Q\;=\;\frac{5}{7}\;\times\;735\;=\;525\;\text{J}$

questions.text: The pressure of a gas changes linearly with volume from A to B as shown in figure. If no heat is supplied to or extracted from the gas then change in the internal energy of the gas will be [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: With $\Delta Q\;=\;0$, $\Delta U\;=\;-W$, and $W$ equals the area under the P-V line. // 📝 Solution: $W_{A\to B}\;=\;-\frac{1}{2}\left(10\;+\;50\right)\times10^{3}\;\times\;150\times10^{-6}\;=\;-4.5\;\text{J}\;\implies\;\Delta U\;=\;-W\;=\;+4.5\;\text{J}$

questions.text: A real gas within a closed chamber at $27^\circ\text{C}$ undergoes the cyclic process as shown in figure. The gas obeys $PV^{3}\;=\;RT$ equation for the path $A$ to $B$. The net work done in the complete cycle is (assuming $R\;=\;8\;\text{J/molK}$): [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Add the work on each leg, with $W_{AB}\;=\;\int P\,dV\;=\;RT\int V^{-3}\,dV$ at constant $T$. // 📝 Solution: $W_{AB}\;=\;RT\int_{2}^{4}V^{-3}dV\;=\;2400\;\times\;\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{1}{4}\;-\;\frac{1}{16}\right]\;=\;225\;\text{J}\;,\;\;W_{BC}\;=\;10\left(2\;-\;4\right)\;=\;-20\;\text{J}\;,\;\;W_{CA}\;=\;0\;\implies\;W_{net}\;=\;205\;\text{J}$

questions.text: P-T diagram of an ideal gas having three different densities $\rho_{1},\;\rho_{2},\;\rho_{3}$ (in three different cases) is shown in the figure. Which of the following is correct : [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $P\;=\;\frac{\rho R T}{M}$, so the slope of a P-T line is proportional to density. // 📝 Solution: $P\;=\;\frac{\rho R}{M}\,T\;\implies\;\text{slope}\;\propto\;\rho\;\implies\;\rho_{1}\;>\;\rho_{2}\;>\;\rho_{3}$

questions.text: A total of $48\;\text{J}$ heat is given to one mole of helium kept in a cylinder. The temperature of helium increases by $2^\circ\text{C}$. The work done by the gas is: Given, $R\;=\;8.3\;\text{J K}^{-1}\;\text{mol}^{-1}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: First law $Q\;=\;\Delta U\;+\;W$ with $C_{V}\;=\;\frac{3R}{2}$ for helium. // 📝 Solution: $48\;=\;1\;\times\;\frac{3R}{2}\;\times\;2\;+\;W\;\implies\;W\;=\;48\;-\;3\times8.3\;=\;23.1\;\text{J}$

questions.text: A thermodynamic system is taken from an original state $A$ to an intermediate state $B$ by a linear process as shown in the figure. Its volume is then reduced to the original value from $B$ to $C$ by an isobaric process. The total work done by the gas from $A$ to $B$ and $B$ to $C$ would be : [FIGURE] [We changed options. In official NTA paper no option was correct.]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Work is the area under the P-V graph, positive for expansion and negative for compression. // 📝 Solution: $W_{AB}\;=\;\frac{1}{2}\left(8000\;+\;4000\right)\;\times\;4\;$ and $W_{BC}\;=\;-4000\;\times\;4$ in $\text{dyne/cm}^{2}\;\cdot\;\text{m}^{3}\;\implies\;W\;=\;2000\;\text{dyne/cm}^{2}\;\times\;4\;\text{m}^{3}\;=\;200\;\text{Pa}\;\times\;4\;\text{m}^{3}\;=\;800\;\text{J}$

questions.text: $10$ mole of an ideal gas is undergoing the process shown in the figure. The heat involved in the process from $P_{1}$ to $P_{2}$ is $\alpha$ Joule ($P_{1}\;=\;21.7\;\text{Pa}$ and $P_{2}\;=\;30\;\text{Pa}$, $C_{v}\;=\;21\;\text{J/K.mol}$, $R\;=\;8.3\;\text{J/mol.K}$). The value of $\alpha$ is ______. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The process from $P_{1}$ to $P_{2}$ is isochoric ($V\;=\;1\;\text{m}^{3}$), so $Q\;=\;nC_{v}\Delta T$ with $n\Delta T\;=\;\frac{V\Delta P}{R}$. // 📝 Solution: $W\;=\;0\;\implies\;Q\;=\;\Delta U\;=\;C_{v}\,\frac{V\left(P_{2}\;-\;P_{1}\right)}{R}\;=\;21\;\times\;\frac{1\;\times\;8.3}{8.3}\;=\;21\;\text{J}$

questions.text: The correct relation between $\gamma\;=\;\frac{C_{p}}{C_{v}}$ and temperature $T$ is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For an ideal gas $\gamma\;=\;1\;+\;\frac{2}{f}$, which does not involve $T$. // 📝 Solution: $\gamma\;=\;1\;+\;\frac{2}{f}\;\implies\;\gamma$ is independent of temperature $\implies\;\gamma\;\propto\;T^{0}$

questions.text: One mole of an ideal diatomic gas expands from volume $V$ to $2V$ isothermally at a temperature $27^\circ\text{C}$ and does $W$ joule of work. If the gas undergoes same magnitude of expansion adiabatically from $27^\circ\text{C}$ doing the same amount of work $W$, then its final temperature will be (close to) ______ $^\circ\text{C}$. $\left(\log_{e}2\;=\;0.693\right)$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Isothermal $W\;=\;RT\ln2$ and adiabatic $W\;=\;C_{V}\left(T_{i}\;-\;T_{f}\right)$ with $C_{V}\;=\;\frac{5R}{2}$. // 📝 Solution: $R\left(300\right)\ln2\;=\;\frac{5}{2}\,R\left(300\;-\;T_{f}\right)\;\implies\;207.9\;=\;2.5\left(300\;-\;T_{f}\right)\;\implies\;T_{f}\;\approx\;216.8\;\text{K}\;\approx\;-56^\circ\text{C}$

questions.text: The volume of an ideal gas $\left(\gamma\;=\;1.5\right)$ is changed adiabatically from $5$ litres to $4$ litres. The ratio of initial pressure to final pressure is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For an adiabatic process $P_{i}V_{i}^{\gamma}\;=\;P_{f}V_{f}^{\gamma}$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{P_{i}}{P_{f}}\;=\;\left(\frac{V_{f}}{V_{i}}\right)^{3/2}\;=\;\left(\frac{4}{5}\right)^{3/2}\;=\;\frac{8}{5\sqrt{5}}$

questions.text: The pressure and volume of an ideal gas are related as $PV^{3/2}\;=\;K$ (Constant). The work done by gas when the gas is taken from state $A\left(P_{1},\;V_{1},\;T_{1}\right)$ to state $B\left(P_{2},\;V_{2},\;T_{2}\right)$ is : [We modified question statement, In official NTA paper question was incomplete]
A sample of gas at temperature $T$ is adiabatically expanded to double its volume. The work done by the gas in the process is $\left(\text{given},\;\gamma\;=\;\frac{3}{2}\right)$ :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $TV^{\gamma-1}\;=\;\text{constant}$ and $W\;=\;\frac{R\left(T_{1}\;-\;T_{2}\right)}{\gamma\;-\;1}$ for $1$ mole. // 📝 Solution: $T\,V^{1/2}\;=\;T_{2}\left(2V\right)^{1/2}\;\implies\;T_{2}\;=\;\frac{T}{\sqrt{2}}\;\implies\;W\;=\;\frac{R\left(T\;-\;\frac{T}{\sqrt{2}}\right)}{\frac{1}{2}}\;=\;RT\left(2\;-\;\sqrt{2}\right)$

questions.text: A sample of $1$ mole gas at temperature $T$ is adiabatically expanded to double its volume. If adiabatic constant for the gas is $\gamma\;=\;\frac{3}{2}$, then the work done by the gas in the process is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $TV^{\gamma-1}\;=\;\text{constant}$ and $W\;=\;\frac{nR\Delta T}{1\;-\;\gamma}$. // 📝 Solution: $T_{f}\;=\;\frac{T}{\sqrt{2}}\;\implies\;W\;=\;\frac{R\left(\frac{T}{\sqrt{2}}\;-\;T\right)}{-\frac{1}{2}}\;=\;2RT\left[1\;-\;\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right]\;=\;RT\left[2\;-\;\sqrt{2}\right]$

questions.text: A diatomic gas $\left(\gamma\;=\;1.4\right)$ does $200\;\text{J}$ of work when it is expanded isobarically. The heat given to the gas in the process is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\gamma\;=\;1\;+\;\frac{2}{f}$ gives $f$, then $Q\;=\;\frac{f\;+\;2}{2}\,nR\Delta T$. // 📝 Solution: $1.4\;=\;1\;+\;\frac{2}{f}\;\implies\;f\;=\;5\;\implies\;Q\;=\;\frac{7}{2}\,nR\Delta T\;=\;\frac{7}{2}\;\times\;200\;=\;700\;\text{J}$

questions.text: A hypothetical gas expands adiabatically such that its volume changes from $8$ litres to $27$ litres. If the ratio of final pressure of the gas to initial pressure of the gas is $\frac{16}{81}$. Then the ratio of $\frac{C_{P}}{C_{V}}$ will be.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For an adiabatic process $PV^{\gamma}\;=\;\text{constant}$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{P_{f}}{P_{i}}\;=\;\left(\frac{V_{i}}{V_{f}}\right)^{\gamma}\;=\;\left(\frac{8}{27}\right)^{\gamma}\;=\;\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{3\gamma}\;=\;\frac{16}{81}\;=\;\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{4}\;\implies\;\gamma\;=\;\frac{4}{3}$

questions.text: Choose the correct statement for processes A & B shown in figure. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: On a P-V graph the adiabatic curve is steeper than the isothermal curve through the same point. // 📝 Solution: Steeper curve $B$ is adiabatic $\implies\;PV^{\gamma}\;=\;k\;$ (equivalently $\frac{T^{\gamma}}{P^{\gamma-1}}\;=\;k$), and curve $A$ is isothermal $\implies\;PV\;=\;k$.

questions.text: Match List I with List II : List I: A. Isothermal Process, B. Adiabatic Process, C. Isochoric Process, D. Isobaric Process. List II: I. Work done by the gas decreases internal energy, II. No change in internal energy, III. The heat absorbed goes partly to increase internal energy and partly to do work, IV. No work is done on or by the gas. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall $\Delta U\;=\;nC_{v}\Delta T$ and the first law $\Delta Q\;=\;\Delta U\;+\;\Delta W$ for each process. // 📝 Solution: Isothermal $\implies\;\Delta U\;=\;0$ (II). Adiabatic $\implies\;\Delta U\;=\;-\Delta W$ (I). Isochoric $\implies\;\Delta W\;=\;0$ (IV). Isobaric $\implies\;\Delta Q\;=\;\Delta U\;+\;P\Delta V$ (III). So A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

questions.text: The heat absorbed by a system in going through the given cyclic process is : [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For a cyclic process $\Delta U\;=\;0$, so $Q\;=\;W\;=\;$ area enclosed in the P-V diagram. // 📝 Solution: $Q\;=\;W\;=\;\pi\;\times\;\left(140\times10^{3}\;\text{Pa}\right)\;\times\;\left(140\times10^{-6}\;\text{m}^{3}\right)\;\implies\;Q\;\approx\;61.6\;\text{J}$

questions.text: In an isothermal change, the change in pressure and volume of a gas can be represented for three different temperatures $T_{3}\;>\;T_{2}\;>\;T_{1}$ as :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For an isothermal curve $PV\;=\;nRT$, so a higher temperature curve lies farther from the origin. // 📝 Solution: $PV\;=\;nRT\;\implies\;$ at fixed $P$, larger $T$ gives larger $V\;\implies\;$ the $T_{3}$ hyperbola is farthest from the axes and the $T_{1}$ hyperbola is nearest, which is option (4).

questions.text: Heat is given to an ideal gas in an isothermal process. A. Internal energy of the gas will decrease. B. Internal energy of the gas will increase. C. Internal energy of the gas will not change. D. The gas will do positive work. E. The gas will do negative work. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For an ideal gas, $U$ depends only on $T$, and $T$ is constant in an isothermal process. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta T\;=\;0\;\implies\;\Delta U\;=\;0\;\implies\;\Delta Q\;=\;\Delta W\;>\;0$, so the gas does positive work. Hence C and D.

questions.text: Two different adiabatic paths for the same gas intersect two isothermal curves as shown in P-V diagram. The relation between the ratio $\frac{V_{a}}{V_{d}}$ and the ratio $\frac{V_{b}}{V_{c}}$ is: [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Along an adiabatic path $TV^{\gamma-1}\;=\;\text{constant}$, and $a,b$ lie on one isotherm while $d,c$ lie on the other. // 📝 Solution: $\left(\frac{V_{a}}{V_{d}}\right)^{\gamma-1}\;=\;\frac{T_{d}}{T_{a}}\;,\;\;\left(\frac{V_{b}}{V_{c}}\right)^{\gamma-1}\;=\;\frac{T_{c}}{T_{b}}\;,\;\;T_{d}\;=\;T_{c}\;,\;T_{a}\;=\;T_{b}\;\implies\;\frac{V_{a}}{V_{d}}\;=\;\frac{V_{b}}{V_{c}}$

questions.text: $10$ mole of oxygen is heated at constant volume from $30^\circ\text{C}$ to $40^\circ\text{C}$. The change in the internal energy of the gas is ______ cal. (The molecular specific heat of oxygen at constant pressure, $C_{P}\;=\;7\;\text{cal/mol.}^\circ\text{C}$ and $R\;=\;2\;\text{cal/mol.}^\circ\text{C}$.)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $C_{V}\;=\;C_{P}\;-\;R$ and $\Delta U\;=\;nC_{V}\Delta T$. // 📝 Solution: $C_{V}\;=\;7\;-\;2\;=\;5\;\implies\;\Delta U\;=\;10\;\times\;5\;\times\;10\;=\;500\;\text{cal}$

questions.text: Density of water at $4^\circ\text{C}$ and $20^\circ\text{C}$ are $1000\;\text{kg/m}^{3}$ and $998\;\text{kg/m}^{3}$ respectively. The increase in internal energy of $4$ kg of water when it is heated from $4^\circ\text{C}$ to $20^\circ\text{C}$ is ______ J. (specific heat capacity of water $=\;4.2\;\text{kJ/kg}\,^\circ\text{C}$ and $1$ atmospheric pressure $=\;10^{5}\;\text{Pa}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\Delta U\;=\;Q\;-\;P\,\Delta V$, where $\Delta V$ comes from the density change. // 📝 Solution: $Q\;=\;4\;\times\;4200\;\times\;16\;=\;268800\;\text{J}\;,\;\;\Delta V\;=\;\frac{4}{998}\;-\;\frac{4}{1000}\;\approx\;8\times10^{-6}\;\text{m}^{3}\;\implies\;W\;\approx\;0.8\;\text{J}\;\implies\;\Delta U\;=\;268800\;-\;0.8\;=\;268799.2\;\text{J}$
questions.topic: First Law with Volume Expansion of Liquid

questions.text: A Carnot engine with efficiency $50\%$ takes heat from a source at $600\;\text{K}$. In order to increase the efficiency to $70\%$, keeping the temperature of sink same, the new temperature of the source will be :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\eta\;=\;1\;-\;\frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}$ with the sink temperature held fixed. // 📝 Solution: $0.5\;=\;1\;-\;\frac{T_{2}}{600}\;\implies\;T_{2}\;=\;300\;\text{K}\;\implies\;0.7\;=\;1\;-\;\frac{300}{T}\;\implies\;T\;=\;1000\;\text{K}$

questions.text: Heat energy of $184\;\text{kJ}$ is given to ice of mass $600\;\text{g}$ at $-12^\circ\text{C}$. Specific heat of ice is $2222.3\;\text{J kg}^{-1}\;{}^\circ\text{C}^{-1}$ and latent heat of ice is $336\;\text{kJ/kg}$. (A) Final temperature of system will be $0^\circ\text{C}$. (B) Final temperature of the system will be greater than $0^\circ\text{C}$. (C) The final system will have a mixture of ice and water in the ratio of $5:1$. (D) The final system will have a mixture of ice and water in the ratio of $1:5$. (E) The final system will have water only. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: First warm the ice to $0^\circ\text{C}$, then compare the remaining heat with $mL$. // 📝 Solution: $Q_{1}\;=\;0.6\times2222.3\times12\;\approx\;16000.56\;\text{J}\;\implies\;Q_{rem}\;=\;167999.44\;\text{J}\;<\;mL\;=\;201600\;\text{J}\;\implies\;m_{melted}\;=\;\frac{167999.44}{336000}\;\approx\;0.5\;\text{kg}\;\implies\;\text{ice}:\text{water}\;=\;0.1:0.5\;=\;1:5\;\text{at}\;0^\circ\text{C}$

questions.text: A bowl filled with very hot soup cools from $98^\circ\text{C}$ to $86^\circ\text{C}$ in $2$ minutes when the room temperature is $22^\circ\text{C}$. How long it will take to cool from $75^\circ\text{C}$ to $69^\circ\text{C}$ ?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use the average form of Newton's law of cooling, $\frac{\Delta\theta}{\Delta t}\;=\;k\left(\theta_{avg}\;-\;\theta_{0}\right)$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{12}{2}\;=\;k\left(92\;-\;22\right)\;\implies\;6\;=\;70k\;,\;\;\frac{6}{t}\;=\;k\left(72\;-\;22\right)\;=\;50k\;\implies\;t\;=\;\frac{70}{50}\;=\;1.4\;\text{min}$

questions.text: A diatomic gas $\left(\gamma\;=\;1.4\right)$ does $100\;\text{J}$ of work when it is expanded isobarically. Then the heat given to the gas is ______ J.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $Q\;=\;\Delta U\;+\;W$ with $\Delta U\;=\;nC_{V}\Delta T\;=\;\frac{5}{2}\,nR\Delta T$ and $W\;=\;nR\Delta T$. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta U\;=\;\frac{5}{2}\;\times\;100\;=\;250\;\text{J}\;\implies\;Q\;=\;250\;+\;100\;=\;350\;\text{J}$

questions.text: A body cools from $60^\circ\text{C}$ to $40^\circ\text{C}$ in $6$ minutes. If temperature of surroundings is $10^\circ\text{C}$. Then, after the next $6$ minutes, its temperature will be ______ $^\circ\text{C}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use the average form of Newton's law of cooling for both $6$-minute intervals. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{20}{6}\;=\;k\left(50\;-\;10\right)\;\implies\;k\;=\;\frac{1}{12}\;,\;\;\frac{40\;-\;T}{6}\;=\;k\left(\frac{40\;+\;T}{2}\;-\;10\right)\;\implies\;80\;-\;2T\;=\;10\;+\;\frac{T}{2}\;\implies\;T\;=\;28^\circ\text{C}$

questions.text: Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R. Assertion A : Efficiency of a reversible heat engine will be highest at $-273^\circ\text{C}$ temperature of cold reservoir. Reason R : The efficiency of Carnot's engine depends not only on temperature of cold reservoir but it depends on the temperature of hot reservoir too and is given as $\eta\;=\;\left(1\;-\;\frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}\right)$. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.text: A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\eta\;=\;1\;-\;\frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}$ is maximum when $T_{2}\;\to\;0\;\text{K}$. // 📝 Solution: $T_{2}\;=\;-273^\circ\text{C}\;=\;0\;\text{K}\;\implies\;\eta\;=\;1\;$ (maximum), so A is true and R gives exactly this formula, hence R explains A.

questions.text: A diatomic gas $\left(\gamma\;=\;1.4\right)$ does $100\;\text{J}$ of work in an isobaric expansion. The heat given to the gas is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: In an isobaric process $Q\;=\;\Delta U\;+\;W$ with $\Delta U\;=\;\frac{f}{2}\,nR\Delta T$. // 📝 Solution: $\gamma\;=\;1.4\;\implies\;f\;=\;5\;\implies\;Q\;=\;\left(\frac{5}{2}\;+\;1\right)nR\Delta T\;=\;\frac{7}{2}\;\times\;100\;=\;350\;\text{J}$

questions.text: The given figure represents two isobaric processes for the same mass of an ideal gas, then [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: On a V-T graph the slope of an isobar is $\frac{nR}{P}$. // 📝 Solution: $V\;=\;\left(\frac{nR}{P}\right)T\;\implies\;\text{slope}\;\propto\;\frac{1}{P}\;\implies\;\left(\text{slope}\right)_{2}\;>\;\left(\text{slope}\right)_{1}\;\implies\;P_{2}\;<\;P_{1}$

questions.text: Given below are two statements. One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R. Assertion A : If $dQ$ and $dW$ represent the heat supplied to the system and the work done on the system respectively. Then according to the first law of thermodynamics $dQ\;=\;dU\;-\;dW$. Reason R : First law of thermodynamics is based on law of conservation of energy. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the option given below :

options.text: A is correct but R is not correct
A is not correct but R is correct
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: With $dW$ as work done on the system, the first law reads $dU\;=\;dQ\;+\;dW$. // 📝 Solution: $dU\;=\;dQ\;+\;dW\;\implies\;dQ\;=\;dU\;-\;dW$ ($dW$ done on the system), so A is correct. R is the conservation of energy, which is the basis of the law, so R correctly explains A.

questions.text: A sample of gas at temperature $T$ is adiabatically expanded to double its volume. Adiabatic constant for the gas is $\gamma\;=\;3/2$. The work done by the gas in the process is: $\left(\mu\;=\;1\;\text{mole}\right)$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $TV^{\gamma-1}\;=\;\text{constant}$ and $W\;=\;\frac{nR\Delta T}{1\;-\;\gamma}$. // 📝 Solution: $T_{f}\;=\;T\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{1/2}\;=\;\frac{T}{\sqrt{2}}\;\implies\;W\;=\;\frac{R\left(\frac{T}{\sqrt{2}}\;-\;T\right)}{1\;-\;\frac{3}{2}}\;=\;RT\left(2\;-\;\sqrt{2}\right)$

questions.text: During an adiabatic process, the pressure of a gas is found to be proportional to the cube of its absolute temperature. The ratio of $\frac{C_{p}}{C_{v}}$ for the gas is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Rewrite $PV^{\gamma}\;=\;\text{constant}$ in terms of $P$ and $T$ using $V\;=\;\frac{nRT}{P}$. // 📝 Solution: $P^{1-\gamma}\,T^{\gamma}\;=\;\text{constant}\;\implies\;P\,T^{\frac{\gamma}{1-\gamma}}\;=\;\text{constant}\;\implies\;\frac{\gamma}{1\;-\;\gamma}\;=\;-3\;\implies\;\gamma\;=\;\frac{3}{2}$

questions.text: A bicycle tyre is filled with air having pressure of $270\;\text{kPa}$ at $27^\circ\text{C}$. The approximate pressure of the air in the tyre when the temperature increases to $36^\circ\text{C}$ is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: At constant volume $\frac{P_{1}}{T_{1}}\;=\;\frac{P_{2}}{T_{2}}$ with $T$ in kelvin. // 📝 Solution: $P_{2}\;=\;\frac{270\;\times\;309}{300}\;\approx\;278\;\text{kPa}$

questions.text: $0.08\;\text{kg}$ air is heated at constant volume through $5^\circ\text{C}$. The specific heat of air at constant volume is $0.17\;\text{kcal/kg}\,^\circ\text{C}$ and $J\;=\;4.18\;\text{joule/cal}$. The change in its internal energy is approximately.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: At constant volume $Q\;=\;\Delta U\;=\;m\,s\,\Delta T$. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta U\;=\;0.08\;\times\;\left(170\;\times\;4.18\right)\;\times\;5\;\approx\;284\;\text{J}$

questions.text: When $300\;\text{J}$ of heat given to an ideal gas with $C_{p}\;=\;\frac{7}{2}\,R$ its temperature raises from $20^\circ\text{C}$ to $50^\circ\text{C}$ keeping its volume constant. If $n$ is the number of moles of the gas, then what is the value of $100n$? $\left(R\;=\;8.314\;\text{J/mol.K}\right)$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: At constant volume $Q\;=\;nC_{V}\Delta T$ with $C_{V}\;=\;C_{P}\;-\;R$. // 📝 Solution: $C_{V}\;=\;\frac{5}{2}\,R\;\implies\;300\;=\;n\;\times\;\frac{5}{2}\;\times\;8.314\;\times\;30\;\implies\;n\;\approx\;0.48\;\implies\;100n\;\approx\;48$
questions.topic: Molar Specific Heat at Constant Volume

questions.text: A thermodynamic system is taken through the cyclic process $ABC$ as shown in the figure. The total work done by the system during the cycle $ABC$ is ______ J. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Work in a cycle is the area enclosed by the loop on the P-V diagram. // 📝 Solution: $A\left(2,100\right),\;B\left(5,300\right),\;C\left(5,100\right)\;\implies\;W\;=\;\frac{1}{2}\;\times\;\left(5\;-\;2\right)\;\times\;\left(300\;-\;100\right)\;=\;300\;\text{J}$

questions.text: Let $\gamma_{1}$ be the ratio of molar specific heat at constant pressure and molar specific heat at constant volume of a monoatomic gas and $\gamma_{2}$ be the similar ratio of diatomic gas. Considering the diatomic gas molecule as a rigid rotator, the ratio $\frac{\gamma_{1}}{\gamma_{2}}$ is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\gamma\;=\;1\;+\;\frac{2}{f}$ where $f$ is the number of degrees of freedom. // 📝 Solution: $\gamma_{1}\;=\;\frac{5}{3}\;,\;\gamma_{2}\;=\;\frac{7}{5}\;\implies\;\frac{\gamma_{1}}{\gamma_{2}}\;=\;\frac{5}{3}\;\times\;\frac{5}{7}\;=\;\frac{25}{21}$
questions.topic: Specific Heats and Degrees of Freedom

questions.text: The internal energy of a monoatomic gas is $3nRT$. One mole of helium is kept in a cylinder having internal cross section area of $17\;\text{cm}^{2}$ and fitted with a light movable frictionless piston. The gas is heated slowly by supplying $126\;\text{J}$ heat. If the temperature rises by $4^\circ\text{C}$, then the piston will move ______ cm. (atmospheric pressure $=\;10^{5}\;\text{Pa}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $Q\;=\;\Delta U\;+\;P\,A\,d$ at constant atmospheric pressure. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta U\;=\;3\;\times\;1\;\times\;8.314\;\times\;4\;\approx\;99.77\;\text{J}\;\implies\;W\;=\;126\;-\;99.77\;=\;26.23\;\text{J}\;\implies\;d\;=\;\frac{26.23}{10^{5}\;\times\;17\times10^{-4}}\;\approx\;0.154\;\text{m}\;\approx\;15.5\;\text{cm}$

questions.text: A Carnot engine operating between two reservoirs has efficiency $\frac{1}{3}$. When the temperature of cold reservoir raised by $x$, its efficiency decreases to $\frac{1}{6}$. The value of $x$, if the temperature of hot reservoir is $99^\circ\text{C}$, will be:

A soap bubble of surface tension $0.04\;\text{N/m}$ is blown to a diameter of $7\;\text{cm}$. If $\left(15000\;-\;x\right)\mu\text{J}$ of work is done in blowing it further to make its diameter $14\;\text{cm}$, then the value of $x$ is ____. $\left(\pi\;=\;22/7\right)$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Soap bubble has two surfaces: $W\;=\;T\times8\pi\left(r_f^2\;-\;r_i^2\right)$. // 📝 Solution: $W\;=\;0.04\times8\pi\left(0.07^2\;-\;0.035^2\right)\;=\;3.696\times10^{-3}\;\text{J}\;=\;3696\;\mu\text{J}\;\implies\;x\;=\;15000\;-\;3696\;=\;11304$
questions.topic: Work done in blowing soap bubble

questions.text: The surface of water in a water tank of cross section area $750\;\text{cm}^2$ on the top of a house is $h$ m above the tap level. The speed of water coming out through the tap of cross section area $500\;\text{mm}^2$ is $30\;\text{cm/s}$. At that instant, $\frac{dh}{dt}$ is $x\;\times\;10^{-3}\;\text{m/s}$. The value of $x$ will be ______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Equation of continuity $A_1v_1\;=\;A_2v_2$. // 📝 Solution: $750\times10^{-4}\;v_1\;=\;500\times10^{-6}\times0.3\;\implies\;v_1\;=\;2\times10^{-3}\;\text{m/s}\;\implies\;\frac{dh}{dt}\;=\;-2\times10^{-3}\;\text{m/s}\;\implies\;x\;=\;2$

questions.text: Given below are two statements : Statement I : When a capillary tube is dipped into a liquid, the liquid neither rises nor falls in the capillary. The contact angle may be $0^{\circ}$. Statement II : The contact angle between a solid and a liquid is a property of the material of the solid and liquid as well. In the light of the above statement, choose the correct answer from the options given below.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true and Statement II is false

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $h\;=\;\frac{2T\cos\theta}{\rho g r}$ and check the case $\theta\;=\;0^{\circ}$. // 📝 Solution: If $\theta\;=\;0^{\circ}$ then $h\;\ne\;0$ $\implies$ Statement I is incorrect $\implies$ Statement II is correct

questions.text: A spherical ball of radius $1\;\text{mm}$ and density $10.5\;\text{g/cc}$ is dropped in glycerine of coefficient of viscosity $9.8$ poise and density $1.5\;\text{g/cc}$. Viscous force on the ball when it attains constant velocity is $3696\;\times\;10^{-x}\;\text{N}$. The value of $x$ is (Given, $g\;=\;9.8\;\text{m/s}^2$ and $\pi\;=\;\frac{22}{7}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: At terminal velocity, viscous force = weight − buoyant force. // 📝 Solution: $F_v\;=\;mg\;-\;F_B\;=\;V\left(\sigma_b\;-\;\rho_l\right)g\;=\;\frac{4}{3}\pi\left(10^{-3}\right)^3\;\times\;9.8\;\times\;\left(10.5\;-\;1.5\right)\times 10^{3}\;=\;3696\;\times\;10^{-7}\;\text{N}\;\implies\;x\;=\;7$

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I : When speed of liquid is zero everywhere, pressure difference at any two points depends on equation $P_1\;-\;P_2\;=\;\rho g\left(h_2\;-\;h_1\right)$. Statement II : In ventury tube shown $2gh\;=\;v_1^2\;-\;v_2^2$ [FIGURE] In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Apply Bernoulli's equation between the two points of the venturi tube. // 📝 Solution: $V_1\;=\;V_2\;=\;0\;\implies\;P_1\;-\;P_2\;=\;\rho g\left(h_2\;-\;h_1\right)$, so I is correct $\implies$ Venturi: $P_1\;-\;P_2\;=\;\rho g h\;=\;\frac{1}{2}\rho\left(v_2^2\;-\;v_1^2\right)\;\implies\;2gh\;=\;v_2^2\;-\;v_1^2$, so II is incorrect

questions.text: Sixty four rain drops of radius $1\;\text{mm}$ each falling down with a terminal velocity of $10\;\text{cm/s}$ coalesce to form a bigger drop. The terminal velocity of bigger drop is ____ cm/s.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Volume conservation gives $R\;=\;4r$, and $v_t\;\propto\;r^2$. // 📝 Solution: $64\times\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\;=\;\frac{4}{3}\pi R^3\;\implies\;R\;=\;4r\;\implies\;v\;=\;16\times10\;=\;160\;\text{cm/s}$

questions.text: A mercury drop of radius $10^{-3}\;\text{m}$ is broken into $125$ equal size droplets. Surface tension of mercury is $0.45\;\text{N m}^{-1}$. The gain in surface energy is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Volume conservation gives $R_{new}\;=\;\frac{R}{5}$; gain = $T\left(A_f\;-\;A_i\right)$. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta E\;=\;0.45\times4\pi\left(10^{-3}\right)^2\left[\frac{125}{25}\;-\;1\right]\;=\;4\times0.45\times4\pi\times10^{-6}\;=\;2.26\times10^{-5}\;\text{J}$

questions.text: A spherical body of radius $r$ and density $\sigma$ falls freely through a viscous liquid having density $\rho$ and viscosity $\eta$ and attains a terminal velocity $v_0$. Estimated maximum error in the quantity $\eta$ is : (Ignore errors associated with $\sigma,\;\rho$ and $g$, gravitational acceleration)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Write $\eta\;\propto\;\frac{r^2}{v_0}$ and add relative errors. // 📝 Solution: $\eta\;=\;\frac{2r^2\left(\sigma\;-\;\rho\right)g}{9v_0}\;\implies\;\ln\eta\;=\;\ln k\;+\;2\ln r\;-\;\ln v_0\;\implies\;\frac{\Delta\eta}{\eta}\;=\;2\frac{\Delta r}{r}\;+\;\frac{\Delta v_0}{v_0}$

questions.text: Pressure inside a soap bubble is greater than the pressure outside by an amount : (given : $R\;=\;$ Radius of bubble, $S\;=\;$ Surface tension of bubble)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A soap bubble has two liquid-air surfaces. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta P\;=\;2\left(\frac{2S}{R}\right)\;=\;\frac{4S}{R}$

questions.text: Given below are two statements : Statement (I) : Viscosity of gases is greater than that of liquids. Statement (II) : Surface tension of a liquid decreases due to the presence of insoluble impurities. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Compare typical viscosities of gases and liquids, and recall the effect of impurities on surface tension. // 📝 Solution: Gases have lower viscosity than liquids, so I is incorrect $\implies$ Insoluble impurities such as detergent decrease surface tension, so II is correct

questions.text: A big drop is formed by coalescing $1000$ small identical drops of water. If $E_1$ be the total surface energy of $1000$ small drops of water and $E_2$ be the surface energy of single big drop of water, the $E_1\;:\;E_2$ is $x\;:\;1$ where $x\;=$ ______
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Volume conservation gives $R\;=\;10r$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{E_1}{E_2}\;=\;\frac{1000\times4\pi r^2 S}{4\pi\left(10r\right)^2 S}\;=\;\frac{10}{1}\;\implies\;x\;=\;10$

questions.text: The height of liquid column raised in a capillary tube of certain radius when dipped in liquid A vertically is $5\;\text{cm}$. If the tube is dipped in a similar manner in another liquid B of surface tension and density double the values of liquid A, the height of liquid column raised in liquid B would be ______ m.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Capillary rise $h\;=\;\frac{2S\cos\theta}{r\rho g}$, so $h\;\propto\;\frac{S}{\rho}$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{h_1}{h_2}\;=\;\frac{S_1}{S_2}\times\frac{\rho_2}{\rho_1}\;=\;\frac{1}{2}\times\frac{2}{1}\;=\;1\;\implies\;h_2\;=\;5\;\text{cm}\;=\;0.05\;\text{m}$

questions.text: Correct Bernoulli's equation is (symbols have their usual meaning) :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Bernoulli's equation is energy conservation per unit volume. // 📝 Solution: $P\;+\;\rho gh\;+\;\frac{1}{2}\rho v^2\;=\;\text{constant}$

questions.text: A cubical block of density $\rho_b\;=\;600\;\text{kg/m}^3$ floats in a liquid of density $\rho_e\;=\;900\;\text{kg/m}^3$. If the height of block is $H\;=\;8.0\;\text{cm}$ then height of the submerged part is ____ cm.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For floating, weight = buoyant force: $\rho_e h_s\;=\;\rho_b H$. // 📝 Solution: $h_s\;=\;\frac{600}{900}\times8.0\;=\;\frac{2}{3}\times8\;=\;5.33\;\text{cm}\;\approx\;5.3\;\text{cm}$

questions.text: Mercury is filled in a tube of radius $2\;\text{cm}$ up to a height of $30\;\text{cm}$. The force exerted by mercury on the bottom of the tube is ______ N. (Given, atmospheric pressure $=\;10^{5}\;\text{N m}^{-2}$, density of mercury $=\;1.36\;\times\;10^{4}\;\text{kg m}^{-3}$, $g\;=\;10\;\text{m s}^{-2}$, $\pi\;=\;\frac{22}{7}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Force on bottom = $\left(P_0\;+\;\rho g h\right)A$. // 📝 Solution: $A\;=\;\frac{22}{7}\left(2\times10^{-2}\right)^2\;=\;1.257\times10^{-3}\;\text{m}^2\;\implies\;F\;=\;10^{5}A\;+\;1.36\times10^{4}\times10\times0.3\times A\;=\;125.71\;+\;51.29\;=\;177\;\text{N}$

questions.text: An air bubble of volume $2.9\;\text{cm}^3$ rises from the bottom of a swimming pool of $5\;\text{m}$ deep. At the bottom of the pool water temperature is $17^{\circ}\text{C}$. The volume of the bubble when it reaches the surface, where the water temperature is $27^{\circ}\text{C}$, is ____ $\text{cm}^3$. $\left(g\;=\;10\;\text{m/s}^2,\;\text{density of water}\;=\;10^{3}\;\text{kg/m}^3,\;\text{and 1 atm pressure is}\;10^{5}\;\text{Pa}\right)$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Apply the ideal gas law $\frac{P_1V_1}{T_1}\;=\;\frac{P_2V_2}{T_2}$ with $P_1\;=\;P_0\;+\;\rho g h$. // 📝 Solution: $P_1\;=\;1.5\times10^{5}\;\text{Pa},\;P_2\;=\;10^{5}\;\text{Pa}\;\implies\;V_2\;=\;2.9\times\frac{1.5\times10^{5}}{10^{5}}\times\frac{300}{290}\;\approx\;4.5\;\text{cm}^3$

questions.text: A fully loaded boeing aircraft has a mass of $5.4\;\times\;10^{5}\;\text{kg}$. Its total wing area is $500\;\text{m}^2$. It is in level flight with a speed of $1080\;\text{km/h}$. If the density of air $\rho$ is $1.2\;\text{kg m}^{-3}$, the fractional increase in the speed of the air on the upper surface of the wing relative to the lower surface in percentage will be $\left(g\;=\;10\;\text{m/s}^2\right)$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Lift = pressure difference × area = $mg$, and $\Delta P\;=\;\frac{1}{2}\rho\left(v_1^2\;-\;v_2^2\right)$. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta P\;=\;\frac{5.4\times10^{5}\times10}{500}\;=\;1.08\times10^{4}\;\implies\;1.08\times10^{4}\;=\;\frac{1}{2}\left(1.2\right)\left(v_1\;-\;v_2\right)\left(600\right)\;\implies\;v_1\;-\;v_2\;=\;30\;\implies\;\frac{30}{300}\times100\;=\;10\%$

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I : If a capillary tube is immersed first in cold water and then in hot water, the height of capillary rise will be smaller in hot water. Statement II : If a capillary tube is immersed first in cold water and then in hot water, the height of capillary rise will be smaller in cold water. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate from the options given below

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Surface tension decreases with temperature and $h\;=\;\frac{2T\cos\theta}{\rho g r}$. // 📝 Solution: Hot water has lower $T$ $\implies$ smaller $h$ in hot water and larger $h$ in cold water $\implies$ I is true, II is false

questions.text: Given below are two statements : Statement I : The contact angle between a solid and a liquid is a property of the material of the solid and liquid as well. Statement II : The rise of a liquid in a capillary tube does not depend on the inner radius of the tube. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Capillary rise $h\;=\;\frac{2T\cos\theta}{\rho g r}$. // 📝 Solution: Contact angle depends on cohesive and adhesive forces, so I is true $\implies$ $h\;\propto\;\frac{1}{r}$, so II is false

questions.text: A big drop is formed by coalescing $1000$ small droplets of water. The surface energy will become :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Volume conservation gives $R\;=\;10r$. // 📝 Solution: $U_i\;=\;1000\left(4\pi r^2 S\right),\;U_f\;=\;4\pi\left(10r\right)^2 S\;=\;100\left(4\pi r^2 S\right)\;\implies\;U_f\;=\;\frac{1}{10}U_i$

questions.text: A small liquid drop of radius $R$ is divided into $27$ identical liquid drops. If the surface tension is $T$, then the work done in the process will be :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Work = $T\;\Delta A$ with volume conserved, $r\;=\;\frac{R}{3}$. // 📝 Solution: $W\;=\;T\left[27\times4\pi\frac{R^2}{9}\;-\;4\pi R^2\right]\;=\;T\;\times\;4\pi R^2\left(3\;-\;1\right)\;=\;8\pi R^2\,T$
questions.topic: Work done in splitting a drop

questions.text: The excess pressure inside a soap bubble is thrice the excess pressure inside a second soap bubble. The ratio between the volume of the first and the second bubble is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Excess pressure $\propto\;\frac{1}{r}$ and volume $\propto\;r^3$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{4T}{r_1}\;=\;3\times\frac{4T}{r_2}\;\implies\;r_2\;=\;3r_1\;\implies\;\frac{V_1}{V_2}\;=\;\left(\frac{r_1}{r_2}\right)^3\;=\;\frac{1}{27}$

questions.text: The reading of pressure metre attached with a closed pipe is $4.5\;\times\;10^{4}\;\text{N/m}^2$. On opening the valve, water starts flowing and the reading of pressure metre falls to $2.0\;\times\;10^{4}\;\text{N/m}^2$. The velocity of water is found to be $\sqrt{V}\;\text{m/s}$. The value of $V$ is ______
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Pressure drop = $\frac{1}{2}\rho v^2$ (Bernoulli's theorem). // 📝 Solution: $4.5\times10^{4}\;-\;2.0\times10^{4}\;=\;\frac{1}{2}\times10^{3}\times v^2\;\implies\;v^2\;=\;50\;\implies\;V\;=\;50$

questions.text: Water flows through a horizontal tube as shown in the figure. The difference in height between the water columns in vertical tubes is $5\;\text{cm}$ and the area of cross-sections at $A$ and $B$ are $6\;\text{cm}^2$ and $3\;\text{cm}^2$ respectively. The rate of flow will be ____ $\text{cm}^3/\text{s}$. (take $g\;=\;10\;\text{m/s}^2$) [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Combine continuity $A_1v_1\;=\;A_2v_2$ with Bernoulli's equation $\Delta P\;=\;\rho g h$. // 📝 Solution: $v_2\;=\;2v_1,\;\rho g h\;=\;\frac{1}{2}\rho\left(4v_1^2\;-\;v_1^2\right)\;\implies\;v_1\;=\;\sqrt{\frac{2\times1000\times5}{3}}\;=\;\frac{100}{\sqrt{3}}\;\text{cm/s}\;\implies\;Q\;=\;6\times\frac{100}{\sqrt{3}}\;=\;200\sqrt{3}\;\text{cm}^3/\text{s}$
questions.topic: Venturi meter and equation of continuity

questions.text: A sphere of relative density $\sigma$ and diameter $D$ has concentric cavity of diameter $d$. The ratio of $\frac{D}{d}$, if it just floats on water in a tank is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For just floating, weight = buoyant force on the full sphere volume. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{4}{3}\pi\left(\frac{D^3\;-\;d^3}{8}\right)\sigma g\;=\;\frac{4}{3}\pi\frac{D^3}{8}g\;\implies\;1\;-\;\frac{d^3}{D^3}\;=\;\frac{1}{\sigma}\;\implies\;\frac{D}{d}\;=\;\left(\frac{\sigma}{\sigma-1}\right)^{1/3}$

questions.text: In a test experiment on a model aeroplane in wind tunnel, the flow speeds on the upper and lower surfaces of the wings are $70\;\text{ms}^{-1}$ and $65\;\text{ms}^{-1}$ respectively. If the wing area is $2\;\text{m}^2$ the lift of the wing is ______ N. (Given density of air $=\;1.2\;\text{kg m}^{-3}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Lift $F\;=\;\frac{1}{2}\rho\left(v_1^2\;-\;v_2^2\right)A$. // 📝 Solution: $F\;=\;\frac{1}{2}\times1.2\times\left(70^2\;-\;65^2\right)\times2\;=\;810\;\text{N}$

questions.text: A small metallic sphere of diameter $2\;\text{mm}$ and density $10.5\;\text{g/cm}^3$ is dropped in glycerine having viscosity $10$ Poise and density $1.5\;\text{g/cm}^3$ respectively. The terminal velocity attained by the sphere is ____ cm/s. $\left(\pi\;=\;\frac{22}{7}\;\text{and}\;g\;=\;10\;\text{m/s}^2\right)$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Stokes' law: $v_t\;=\;\frac{2r^2 g\left(\rho_s\;-\;\rho_f\right)}{9\eta}$. // 📝 Solution: $v_t\;=\;\frac{2\times\left(0.1\right)^2\times1000\times\left(10.5\;-\;1.5\right)}{9\times10}\;=\;\frac{180}{90}\;=\;2.0\;\text{cm/s}$

questions.text: A metal block of base area $0.20\;\text{m}^2$ is placed on a table, as shown in figure. A liquid film of thickness $0.25\;\text{mm}$ is inserted between the block and the table. The block is pushed by a horizontal force of $0.1\;\text{N}$ and moves with a constant speed. If the viscosity of the liquid is $5.0\;\times\;10^{-3}\;\text{Pl}$, the speed of block is ______ $\times\;10^{-3}\;\text{m/s}$. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Viscous force $F\;=\;\eta A\frac{v}{h}$. // 📝 Solution: $0.1\;=\;5\times10^{-3}\;\times\;0.2\;\times\;\frac{v}{0.25\times10^{-3}}\;\implies\;v\;=\;0.025\;\text{m/s}\;=\;25\times10^{-3}\;\text{m/s}$

questions.text: A big drop is formed by coalescing $1000$ small droplets of water. The ratio of surface energy of $1000$ droplets to that of energy of big drop is $\frac{10}{x}$. The value of $x$ is __________
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Volume conservation gives $R\;=\;10r$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{1000\left(4\pi r^2\right)T}{4\pi R^2 T}\;=\;\frac{1000\,r^2}{\left(10r\right)^2}\;=\;10\;=\;\frac{10}{x}\;\implies\;x\;=\;1$

questions.text: When a part of a straight capillary tube is placed vertically in a liquid, the liquid raises upto certain height $h$. If the inner radius of the capillary tube, density of the liquid and surface tension of the liquid decrease by $1\%$ each, then the height of the liquid in the tube will change by ____ %.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $h\;\propto\;\frac{\sigma}{\rho r}$, so use percentage changes. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{\Delta h}{h}\;\approx\;-1\%\;+\;1\%\;+\;1\%\;=\;+1\%$

questions.text: A spherical ball of radius $1\;\times\;10^{-4}\;\text{m}$ and density $10^{5}\;\text{kg/m}^3$ falls freely under gravity through a distance $h$ before entering a tank of water. If after entering in water the velocity of the ball does not change, then the value of $h$ is approximately: (The coefficient of viscosity of water is $9.8\;\times\;10^{-6}\;\text{N s/m}^2$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Free-fall speed $\sqrt{2gh}$ equals the terminal velocity in water. // 📝 Solution: $v_T\;=\;\frac{2}{9}\frac{R^2\left(\rho_B\;-\;\rho_L\right)g}{\eta}\;=\;\frac{2}{9}\times\frac{10^{-8}\left(10^{5}\;-\;10^{3}\right)\times10}{9.8\times10^{-6}}\;\approx\;224.5\;\text{m/s}\;\implies\;h\;=\;\frac{v^2}{2g}\;\approx\;2518\;\text{m}$

questions.text: Small water droplets of radius $0.01\;\text{mm}$ are formed in the upper atmosphere and falling with a terminal velocity of $10\;\text{cm/s}$. Due to condensation, if $8$ such droplets are coalesced and formed a larger drop, the new terminal velocity will be ______ cm/s.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Terminal velocity $v_t\;\propto\;R^2$ and volume is conserved. // 📝 Solution: $8r^3\;=\;R^3\;\implies\;R\;=\;2r\;\implies\;v_t'\;=\;4\times10\;=\;40\;\text{cm/s}$

questions.text: A liquid column of height $0.04\;\text{cm}$ balances excess pressure of a soap bubble of certain radius. If density of liquid is $8\;\times\;10^{3}\;\text{kg m}^{-3}$ and surface tension of soap solution is $0.28\;\text{N m}^{-1}$, then diameter of the soap bubble is ______ cm. (if $g\;=\;10\;\text{m s}^{-2}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Excess pressure of soap bubble is $\frac{4S}{R}\;=\;\rho g h$. // 📝 Solution: $R\;=\;\frac{4\times0.28}{8\times10^{3}\times10\times4\times10^{-4}}\;=\;0.035\;\text{m}\;=\;3.5\;\text{cm}\;\implies\;\text{Diameter}\;=\;7\;\text{cm}$

questions.text: The terminal velocity of a metallic ball of radius $6\;\text{mm}$ in a viscous fluid is $20\;\text{cm/s}$. The terminal velocity of another ball of same material and having radius $3\;\text{mm}$ in the same fluid will be ____ cm/s.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Terminal velocity $v_t\;\propto\;r^2$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{20}{v_{t2}}\;=\;\frac{6^2}{3^2}\;=\;4\;\implies\;v_{t2}\;=\;5\;\text{cm/s}$

questions.text: A small spherical ball of radius $r$, falling through a viscous medium of negligible density has terminal velocity $v$. Another ball of the same mass but of radius $2r$, falling through the same viscous medium will have terminal velocity:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: With negligible buoyancy, $mg\;=\;6\pi\eta r v$, so $v\;\propto\;\frac{1}{r}$ for constant mass. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{v}{v'}\;=\;\frac{r'}{r}\;=\;2\;\implies\;v'\;=\;\frac{v}{2}$

questions.text: A cube of ice floats partly in water and partly in kerosene oil. The ratio of volume of ice immersed in water to that in kerosene oil (specific gravity of Kerosene oil $=\;0.8$, specific gravity of ice $=\;0.9$) [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Weight of ice = sum of the buoyant forces from water and kerosene. // 📝 Solution: $v_1\rho_w g\;+\;v_2\rho_o g\;=\;\left(v_1\;+\;v_2\right)\rho_c g\;\implies\;v_1\;+\;0.8v_2\;=\;0.9v_1\;+\;0.9v_2\;\implies\;0.1v_1\;=\;0.1v_2\;\implies\;v_1\;:\;v_2\;=\;1\;:\;1$

questions.text: A soap bubble is blown to a diameter of $7\;\text{cm}$. $36960\;\text{erg}$ of work is done in blowing it further. If surface tension of soap solution is $40\;\text{dyne/cm}$ then the new radius is ______ cm. Take $\left(\pi\;=\;\frac{22}{7}\right)$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Work = $S\;\Delta A$ with two surfaces, $\Delta A\;=\;8\pi\left(r^2\;-\;r_0^2\right)$. // 📝 Solution: $36960\;=\;40\times8\pi\left[r^2\;-\;\left(\frac{7}{2}\right)^2\right]\;\implies\;r^2\;-\;12.25\;=\;36.75\;\implies\;r^2\;=\;49\;\implies\;r\;=\;7\;\text{cm}$
questions.topic: Work done in blowing soap bubble

questions.text: Surface tension of a soap bubble is $2.0\;\times\;10^{-2}\;\text{N m}^{-1}$. Work done to increase the radius of soap bubble from $3.5\;\text{cm}$ to $7\;\text{cm}$ will be : [Take $\pi\;=\;\frac{22}{7}$]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A soap bubble has two surfaces, so work = $T\;\times\;8\pi\left(R_2^2\;-\;R_1^2\right)$. // 📝 Solution: $W\;=\;T\;\times\;8\pi\left(R_2^2\;-\;R_1^2\right)\;=\;2\times10^{-2}\;\times\;8\;\times\;\frac{22}{7}\;\times\;49\;\times\;\frac{3}{4}\times10^{-4}\;=\;18.48\;\times\;10^{-4}\;\text{J}$
questions.topic: Surface tension and work done in soap bubble

questions.text: If $1000$ droplets of water of surface tension $0.07\;\text{N/m}$, having same radius $1\;\text{mm}$ each, combine to form a single drop. In the process the released surface energy is- $\left(\text{Take}\;\pi\;=\;\frac{22}{7}\right)$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Volume conservation gives $R\;=\;10r$; released energy = $T\left(A_{initial}\;-\;A_{final}\right)$. // 📝 Solution: $R\;=\;10\;\text{mm}\;\implies\;\Delta E\;=\;T\times4\pi\left[1000\left(10^{-3}\right)^2\;-\;\left(10\times10^{-3}\right)^2\right]\;=\;4\times\frac{22}{7}\times7\times10^{-2}\times900\times10^{-6}\;=\;7.92\times10^{-4}\;\text{J}$

questions.text: A plane is in level flight at constant speed and each of its two wings has an area of $40\;\text{m}^2$. If the speed of the air is $180\;\text{km/h}$ over the lower wing surface and $252\;\text{km/h}$ over the upper wing surface, the mass of the plane is ______ kg. (Take air density to be $1\;\text{kg m}^{-3}$ and $g\;=\;10\;\text{ms}^{-2}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Lift = $\Delta P\times A_{total}$ = $mg$ with $\Delta P\;=\;\frac{1}{2}\rho\left(v_1^2\;-\;v_2^2\right)$. // 📝 Solution: $v_1\;=\;70\;\text{m/s},\;v_2\;=\;50\;\text{m/s},\;A\;=\;80\;\text{m}^2\;\implies\;mg\;=\;\frac{1}{2}\times1\times\left(70^2\;-\;50^2\right)\times80\;=\;96000\;\implies\;m\;=\;9600\;\text{kg}$

questions.text: A hydraulic press containing water has two arms with diameters as mentioned in the figure. A force of $10\;\text{N}$ is applied on the surface of water in the thinner arm. The force required to be applied on the surface of water in the thicker arm to maintain equilibrium of water is ______ N. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Pascal's law gives $\frac{F_1}{A_1}\;=\;\frac{F_2}{A_2}$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{F_1}{\pi\left(7\right)^2}\;=\;\frac{10}{\pi\left(0.7\right)^2}\;\implies\;F_1\;=\;1000\;\text{N}$

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Pressure of a fluid is exerted only on a solid surface in contact as the fluid-pressure does not exist everywhere in a still fluid. Statement II: Excess potential energy of the molecules on the surface of a liquid, when compared to interior, results in surface tension. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below

options.text: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Recall Pascal's law and the molecular origin of surface tension. // 📝 Solution: Pressure exists at every point in a still fluid, so I is false $\implies$ Surface molecules have excess potential energy, giving surface tension, so II is true

questions.text: A spherical drop of liquid splits into $1000$ identical spherical drops. If $u_i$ is the surface energy of the original drop and $u_f$ is the total surface energy of the resulting drops (ignoring evaporation), $\frac{u_f}{u_i}\;=\;\left(\frac{10}{x}\right)$. Then the value of $x$ is ______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Volume is conserved, so $R\;=\;n^{1/3}r$; surface energy is $T\;\times\;\text{area}$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{4}{3}\pi R^3\;=\;1000\;\times\;\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\;\implies\;R\;=\;10r\;\implies\;\frac{u_f}{u_i}\;=\;\frac{1000\,r^2}{R^2}\;=\;\frac{10}{1}\;\implies\;x\;=\;1$

questions.text: A small ball of mass $m$ and density $\rho$ is dropped in a viscous liquid of density $\rho_0$. After sometime, the ball falls with constant velocity. The viscous force on the ball is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: At constant velocity net force is zero: $mg\;=\;F_B\;+\;F_v$. // 📝 Solution: $F_v\;=\;mg\;-\;V\rho_0 g\;=\;mg\;-\;\frac{m}{\rho}\rho_0 g\;=\;mg\left(1\;-\;\frac{\rho_0}{\rho}\right)$

questions.text: Surface tension of two liquids (having same densities), $T_1$ and $T_2$, are measured using capillary rise method utilizing two tubes with inner radii of $r_1$ and $r_2$ where $r_1\;>\;r_2$. The measured liquid heights in these tubes are $h_1$ and $h_2$ respectively. [Ignore the weight of the liquid about the lowest point of miniscus]. The heights $h_1$ and $h_2$ and surfaces tensions $T_1$ and $T_2$ satisfy the relation:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Capillary rise $h\;=\;\frac{2T\cos\theta}{\rho g r}$, so $\frac{h_1}{h_2}\;=\;\frac{T_1}{T_2}\times\frac{r_2}{r_1}$. // 📝 Solution: Same density and angle give $\frac{h_1}{h_2}\;=\;\frac{T_1}{T_2}\times\frac{r_2}{r_1}$ $\implies$ as per the official key, $T_1\;=\;T_2$ and since $r_1\;>\;r_2$, $h_1\;<\;h_2$

questions.text: A particle of mass $m$ falls from rest through a resistive medium having resistive force $F = -kv$, where $v$ is the velocity of the particle and $k$ is a constant. Which of the following graphs represents velocity $\left( v \right)$ versus time $\left( t \right)$? (1) [FIGURE] (2) [FIGURE] (3) [FIGURE] (4) [FIGURE]

options.text: [FIGURE] Curve from origin rising and flattening
[FIGURE] Steep curve from origin concave up
[FIGURE] Decreasing curve from maximum at origin

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Write $m\dfrac{dv}{dt} = mg - kv$ and note the terminal velocity $mg/k$. // 📝 Solution: $m\dfrac{dv}{dt} = mg - kv$ with $v(0) = 0$ $\implies v = \dfrac{mg}{k}\left( 1 - e^{-kt/m} \right)$ $\implies$ $v$ rises from origin and saturates at $\dfrac{mg}{k}$

questions.text: The time taken by an object to slide down $45^{\circ}$ rough inclined plane is $n$ times as it takes to slide down a perfectly smooth $45^{\circ}$ incline plane. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the object and the incline plane is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Compare accelerations on rough and smooth incline using $s = \dfrac{1}{2}at^{2}$ with the same $s$. // 📝 Solution: $a_1 = g\sin 45^{\circ}$, $a_2 = g\sin 45^{\circ} - \mu g\cos 45^{\circ}$ $t_2 = nt_1 \implies a_2 = \dfrac{a_1}{n^{2}}$ $\implies \mu = 1 - \dfrac{1}{n^{2}}$
questions.topic: Rough incline, time ratio and friction

questions.text: A block is kept on an inclined plane (inclined at $45^{\circ}$) as shown in the figure. If the force required to just push it up the incline is 2 times the force required to just prevent it from sliding down, the coefficient of friction between the block and inclined plane ($\mu$) is equal to: [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Up-motion friction adds to $mg\sin\theta$ and down-motion friction subtracts from it. // 📝 Solution: $F_1 = mg\sin 45^{\circ} + \mu mg\cos 45^{\circ} = \dfrac{mg}{\sqrt{2}}\left( 1 + \mu \right)$ $F_2 = mg\sin 45^{\circ} - \mu mg\cos 45^{\circ} = \dfrac{mg}{\sqrt{2}}\left( 1 - \mu \right)$ $F_1 = 2F_2 \implies 1 + \mu = 2 - 2\mu \implies \mu = \dfrac{1}{3} \approx 0.33$
questions.topic: Friction on inclined plane, pushing and holding force

questions.text: A body of mass $10\;\text{kg}$ is moving with an initial speed of $20\;\text{m/s}$. The body stops after $5\;\text{s}$ due to friction between body and the floor. The value of the coefficient of friction is: (Take $g = 10\;\text{m s}^{-2}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Friction provides the retardation, so $\mu g = \lvert a \rvert$. // 📝 Solution: $a = \dfrac{0 - 20}{5} = -4\;\text{m s}^{-2}$ $\implies \mu g = 4 \implies \mu = \dfrac{4}{10} = 0.4$

questions.text: A light string passing over a smooth light pulley connects two blocks of masses $m_1$ and $m_2$ (where $m_2 > m_1$). If the acceleration of the system is $\dfrac{g}{\sqrt{2}}$, then the ratio of the masses $\dfrac{m_1}{m_2}$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For an Atwood machine, $a = \dfrac{\left( m_2 - m_1 \right)g}{m_1 + m_2}$. // 📝 Solution: $\dfrac{g}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{\left( m_2 - m_1 \right)g}{m_1 + m_2} \implies \sqrt{2}\,m_2 - \sqrt{2}\,m_1 = m_1 + m_2$ $\implies \dfrac{m_1}{m_2} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2} - 1}{\sqrt{2} + 1}$

questions.text: A body of mass $1\ \text{kg}$ is suspended with the help of two strings making angles as shown in the figure (take $g = 10\ \text{m/s}^{2}$). [FIGURE] The magnitudes of tensions $T_1$ and $T_2$, respectively, are (in N):
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Resolve tensions horizontally and vertically and balance with weight. // 📝 Solution: $T_1\cos 60^{\circ} = T_2\cos 30^{\circ} \implies T_1 = \sqrt{3}\,T_2$; $T_1\sin 60^{\circ} + T_2\sin 30^{\circ} = 10 \implies \frac{3T_2}{2} + \frac{T_2}{2} = 10 \implies T_2 = 5\ \text{N},\; T_1 = 5\sqrt{3}\ \text{N}$

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement (I): The limiting force of static friction depends on the area of contact and is independent of materials. Statement (II): The limiting force of kinetic friction is independent of the area of contact and depends on materials. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Limiting friction is $\mu N$, and $\mu$ depends on the pair of surfaces, not on contact area. // 📝 Solution: $f_{lim} = \mu N$ has no area term $\implies$ Statement I is false $\;\text{and}\;$ $\mu_k$ depends on materials $\implies$ Statement II is true
questions.topic: Laws of static and kinetic friction

questions.text: A spring of force constant $15\;\text{N/m}$ is cut into two pieces. If the ratio of their length is $1 : 3$, then the force constant of smaller piece is ____ N/m.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Force constant is inversely proportional to length for pieces of the same spring. // 📝 Solution: $k_1 \cdot \dfrac{L}{4} = k \cdot L \implies k_1 = 15 \times 4 = 60\;\text{N/m}$
questions.topic: Spring constant and cutting of springs

questions.text: A stone of mass $1\;\text{kg}$ is tied to end of a massless string of length $1\;\text{m}$. If the breaking tension of the string is $400\;\text{N}$, then maximum linear velocity the stone can have without breaking the string, while rotating in horizontal plane, is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Maximum tension supplies the centripetal force. // 📝 Solution: $T_{max} = \dfrac{mv_{max}^{2}}{r} \implies 400 = \dfrac{1 \times v_{max}^{2}}{1} \implies v_{max} = 20\;\text{m s}^{-1}$

questions.text: A stone of mass $900\;\text{g}$ is tied to a string and moved in a vertical circle of radius $1\;\text{m}$ making $10$ rpm. The tension in the string, when the stone is at the lowest point is (if $\pi^{2} = 9.8$ and $g = 9.8\;\text{m s}^{-2}$):
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: At the lowest point, tension minus weight supplies the centripetal force. // 📝 Solution: $\omega = \dfrac{2\pi \times 10}{60} = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\;\text{rad/s}$ $T = mg + mr\omega^{2} = \dfrac{9}{10}\times 9.8 + \dfrac{9}{10}\times 1 \times \dfrac{\pi^{2}}{9} = 8.82 + 0.98 = 9.8\;\text{N}$

questions.text: A block of mass $5\;\text{kg}$ is placed on a rough inclined surface as shown in the figure. If $\vec{F}_1$ is the force required to just move the block up the inclined plane and $\vec{F}_2$ is the force required to just prevent the block from sliding down, then the value of $\left\lvert \vec{F}_1 \right\rvert - \left\lvert \vec{F}_2 \right\rvert$ is: $\left[ \text{Use } g = 10\;\text{m s}^{-2} \right]$ [We changed options. In official NTA paper no option was correct.] [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Friction adds to $mg\sin\theta$ when pushing up and subtracts when preventing slide. // 📝 Solution: $f_K = \mu mg\cos\theta = 0.1 \times 50 \times \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 2.5\sqrt{3}\;\text{N}$ $F_1 = 25 + 2.5\sqrt{3}$ and $F_2 = 25 - 2.5\sqrt{3}$ $\implies F_1 - F_2 = 5\sqrt{3}\;\text{N}$

questions.text: An object with mass $500\ \text{g}$ moves along the $x$-axis with speed $v = 4\sqrt{x}\ \text{m/s}$. The force acting on the object is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $F = m\,v\frac{dv}{dx}$ for $v$ as a function of $x$. // 📝 Solution: $v^{2} = 16x \implies v\frac{dv}{dx} = 8\ \text{m/s}^{2} \implies F = 0.5 \times 8 = 4\ \text{N}$
questions.topic: Variable velocity and Newton's second law

questions.text: Three blocks $M_1$, $M_2$, $M_3$ having masses $4\;\text{kg}$, $6\;\text{kg}$ and $10\;\text{kg}$ respectively are hanging from a smooth pulley using rope $1$, $2$ and $3$ as shown in figure. The tension in the rope $1$, $T_1$, when they are moving upward with acceleration of $2\;\text{m s}^{-2}$ is ____ N (if $g = 10\;\text{m s}^{-2}$). [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Treat the whole hanging system as one body of total mass $20\;\text{kg}$. // 📝 Solution: $T_1 - \left( 4 + 6 + 10 \right)\left( 10 \right) = \left( 4 + 6 + 10 \right)\left( 2 \right)$ $\implies T_1 - 200 = 40 \implies T_1 = 240\;\text{N}$

questions.text: A light unstretchable string passing over a smooth light pulley connects two blocks of masses $m_1$ and $m_2$. If the acceleration of the system is $\dfrac{g}{8}$, then the ratio of the masses $\dfrac{m_2}{m_1}$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use the Atwood acceleration formula $a = \dfrac{\left( m_2 - m_1 \right)g}{m_1 + m_2}$. // 📝 Solution: $\dfrac{\left( m_2 - m_1 \right)g}{m_1 + m_2} = \dfrac{g}{8} \implies 8m_2 - 8m_1 = m_1 + m_2$ $\implies 7m_2 = 9m_1 \implies \dfrac{m_2}{m_1} = \dfrac{9}{7}$

questions.text: In the given arrangement of a doubly inclined plane two blocks of masses $M$ and $m$ are placed. The blocks are connected by a light string passing over an ideal pulley as shown. The coefficient of friction between the surface of the plane and the blocks is $0.25$. The value of $m$, for which $M = 10\;\text{kg}$ will move down with an acceleration of $2\;\text{m s}^{-2}$, is: (take $g = 10\;\text{m s}^{-2}$ and $\tan 37^{\circ} = \dfrac{3}{4}$) [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Apply Newton's second law to each block with kinetic friction opposing motion. // 📝 Solution: For $M$: $80 - 15 - T = 10 \times 2 \implies T = 45\;\text{N}$ For $m$: $T - mg\sin 37^{\circ} - \mu mg\cos 37^{\circ} = 2m \implies 45 = 10m \implies m = 4.5\;\text{kg}$

questions.text: A small block of mass $m$ slides down from the top of a frictionless inclined surface, while the inclined plane is moving towards left with constant acceleration $a_0$. The angle between the inclined plane and ground is $\theta$ and its base length is $L$. The time it takes to reach the lowest point of the inclined plane is ____. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: In the accelerating incline frame, the pseudo force adds a component along the incline. // 📝 Solution: $a_{eff} = g\sin\theta - a_0\cos\theta$ $\dfrac{L}{\cos\theta} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left( g\sin\theta - a_0\cos\theta \right)t^{2}$ $\implies t = \sqrt{\dfrac{4L}{g\sin 2\theta - a_0\left( 1 + \cos 2\theta \right)}}$

questions.text: Three blocks A, B and C of masses $5\;\text{kg}$, $3\;\text{kg}$ and $2\;\text{kg}$ are pulled on a horizontal smooth surface by a force of $80\;\text{N}$ as shown in figure. The tensions $T_1$ and $T_2$ in the string are respectively: [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find the common acceleration of the whole system first, then isolate the blocks. // 📝 Solution: $a = \dfrac{80}{5 + 3 + 2} = 8\;\text{m s}^{-2}$ $T_1 = 5 \times 8 = 40\;\text{N}$ and $T_2 - T_1 = 3 \times 8 \implies T_2 = 64\;\text{N}$

questions.text: A drum of radius $R$ is spinning around its axis with angular velocity $\omega$, as shown in figure. The minimum value of $\omega$ so that a body of mass $M$ remains stuck to the inner wall of the drum, taking the coefficient of friction between the drum surface and mass $M$ as $\mu$, is: [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Friction balances the weight, while the normal force supplies centripetal force. // 📝 Solution: $N = M\omega^{2}R$ and $f = Mg \le \mu N = \mu M\omega^{2}R$ $\implies \omega^{2} \ge \dfrac{g}{\mu R} \implies \omega_{min} = \sqrt{\dfrac{g}{\mu R}}$
questions.topic: Circular motion with friction on drum wall

questions.text: A block of mass $5\;\text{kg}$ is placed at rest on a table of rough surface. Now, if a force of $30\;\text{N}$ is applied in the direction parallel to surface of the table, the block slides through a distance of $50\;\text{m}$ in an interval of time $10\;\text{s}$. Coefficient of kinetic friction is (given $g = 10\;\text{m s}^{-2}$):
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find acceleration from kinematics, then apply $F - \mu mg = ma$. // 📝 Solution: $50 = \dfrac{1}{2}a\left( 10 \right)^{2} \implies a = 1\;\text{m s}^{-2}$ $30 - \mu\left( 5 \right)\left( 10 \right) = 5\left( 1 \right) \implies 50\mu = 25 \implies \mu = 0.5$

questions.text: A lift of mass $M = 500\;\text{kg}$ is descending with speed of $2\;\text{m s}^{-1}$. Its supporting cable begins to slip thus allowing it to fall with a constant acceleration of $2\;\text{m s}^{-2}$. The kinetic energy of the lift at the end of fall through to a distance of $6\;\text{m}$ will be ____ kJ.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $v^{2} = u^{2} + 2as$ and then $KE = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2}$. // 📝 Solution: $v^{2} = 2^{2} + 2\left( 2 \right)\left( 6 \right) = 28$ $\implies KE = \dfrac{1}{2}\left( 500 \right)\left( 28 \right) = 7000\;\text{J} = 7\;\text{kJ}$
questions.topic: Kinematics and kinetic energy of lift

questions.text: A massless spring gets elongated by amount $x_1$ under a tension of 5 N. Its elongation is $x_2$ under the tension of 7 N. For the elongation of $\left(5x_1\;-\;2x_2\right)$, the tension in the spring will be,
