questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Tension is proportional to elongation, $T\;=\;kx$. // 📝 Solution: $kx_1\;=\;5$, $kx_2\;=\;7\;\implies\;k\left(5x_1\;-\;2x_2\right)\;=\;5\left(5\right)\;-\;2\left(7\right)\;=\;11\;\text{N}$

questions.text: A coin is placed on a disc. The coefficient of friction between the coin and the disc is $\mu$. If the distance of the coin from the center of the disc is $r$, the maximum angular velocity which can be given to the disc, so that the coin does not slip away, is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Maximum static friction supplies the centripetal force on the coin. // 📝 Solution: $\mu mg = m\omega^{2}r \implies \omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{\mu g}{r}}$

questions.text: A car of mass $m$ moves on a banked road having radius $r$ and banking angle $\theta$. To avoid slipping from banked road, the maximum permissible speed of the car is $v_0$. The coefficient of friction $\mu$ between the wheels of the car and the banked road is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: At maximum speed friction acts down the incline; resolve forces along and perpendicular to the incline. // 📝 Solution: $N\;=\;mg\cos\theta\;+\;\frac{mv_0^2}{r}\sin\theta$, $\frac{mv_0^2}{r}\cos\theta\;=\;mg\sin\theta\;+\;\mu N\;\implies\;\mu\;=\;\frac{v_0^2-rg\tan\theta}{rg+v_0^2\tan\theta}$

questions.text: A light string passing over a smooth light fixed pulley connects two blocks of masses $m_1$ and $m_2$. If the acceleration of the system is $g/8$, then the ratio of masses is [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use the Atwood acceleration formula with $m_1$ as the heavier mass. // 📝 Solution: $\dfrac{\left( m_1 - m_2 \right)g}{m_1 + m_2} = \dfrac{g}{8} \implies 8m_1 - 8m_2 = m_1 + m_2$ $\implies 7m_1 = 9m_2 \implies \dfrac{m_1}{m_2} = \dfrac{9}{7}$

questions.text: A body of mass $1000\;\text{kg}$ is moving horizontally with a velocity $6\;\text{m s}^{-1}$. If $200\;\text{kg}$ extra mass is added, the final velocity (in $\text{m s}^{-1}$) is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Horizontal momentum is conserved when no external horizontal force acts. // 📝 Solution: $1000 \times 6 = 1200 \times v \implies v = 5\;\text{m s}^{-1}$
questions.topic: Conservation of momentum with mass addition

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: An elevator can go up or down with uniform speed when its weight is balanced with the tension of its cable. Statement II: Force exerted by the floor of an elevator on the foot of a person standing on it is more than his/her weight when the elevator goes down with increasing speed. Choose the correct answer.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: At uniform speed $a = 0$, while downward acceleration reduces the normal force. // 📝 Solution: $T = W \;\text{at uniform speed}$ $\implies$ Statement I is true $\;\text{and}\;$ $N = W\left( 1 - \dfrac{a}{g} \right) < W$ for downward $a$ $\implies$ Statement II is false

questions.text: A $2\;\text{kg}$ brick begins to slide over a surface which is inclined at an angle of $45^{\circ}$ with respect to horizontal axis. The co-efficient of static friction between their surfaces is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: At impending slip, $\tan\theta = \mu_s$ (angle of repose). // 📝 Solution: $mg\sin 45^{\circ} = \mu_s mg\cos 45^{\circ} \implies \mu_s = \tan 45^{\circ} = 1$
questions.topic: Static friction and angle of repose

questions.text: A block is sliding down on an inclined plane of slope $\theta$ and at an instant $t = 0$ this block is given an upward momentum so that it starts moving up on the inclined surface with velocity $u$. The distance $\left( S \right)$ travelled by the block before its velocity become zero, is ____. $\left( g = \text{gravitational acceleration} \right)$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $v^{2} = u^{2} - 2as$ with retardation $a = g\sin\theta$ along the incline. // 📝 Solution: $0 = u^{2} - 2\left( g\sin\theta \right)S \implies S = \dfrac{u^{2}}{2g\sin\theta}$
questions.topic: Motion on incline with upward velocity

questions.text: A body of mass $4\;\text{kg}$ experiences two forces $\vec{F}_1 = 5\hat{i} + 8\hat{j} + 7\hat{k}$ and $\vec{F}_2 = 3\hat{i} - 4\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}$. The acceleration acting on the body is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Add the force vectors first, then divide by mass. // 📝 Solution: $\vec{F}_{net} = \vec{F}_1 + \vec{F}_2 = 8\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$ $\implies \vec{a} = \dfrac{\vec{F}_{net}}{m} = \dfrac{8\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}}{4} = 2\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}$
questions.topic: Vector form of Newton's second law

questions.text: A stone tied to $180\;\text{cm}$ long string at its end is making $28$ revolutions in horizontal circle in every minute. The magnitude of acceleration of stone is $\dfrac{1936}{x}\;\text{m s}^{-2}$. The value of $x$ is: (Take $\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Centripetal acceleration is $a = \omega^{2}R$ with $\omega = \dfrac{2\pi N}{60}$. // 📝 Solution: $\omega = \dfrac{56}{60}\times\dfrac{22}{7}\;\text{rad/s}$ $\implies a = \left( \dfrac{44}{15} \right)^{2} \times 1.8 = \dfrac{1936 \times 1.8}{225}$ $\implies \dfrac{1936}{x} = \dfrac{1936 \times 1.8}{225} \implies x = 125$

questions.text: A force acts for $20\;\text{s}$ on a body of mass $20\;\text{kg}$, starting from rest, after which the force ceases and then the body describes $50\;\text{m}$ in the next $10\;\text{s}$. The value of force will be:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: After the force ceases, the body moves with constant velocity; use it to find the speed at $t = 20\;\text{s}$. // 📝 Solution: $50 = v \times 10 \implies v = 5\;\text{m/s}$ $v = 0 + a \times 20 \implies a = \dfrac{1}{4}\;\text{m/s}^{2}$ $F = ma = 20 \times \dfrac{1}{4} = 5\;\text{N}$

questions.text: A car of $800\;\text{kg}$ is taking turn on a banked road of radius $300\;\text{m}$ and angle of banking $30^{\circ}$. If coefficient of static friction is $0.2$, then the maximum speed with which car can negotiate the turn safely: $\left( g = 10\;\text{m s}^{-2},\; \sqrt{3} = 1.73 \right)$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Maximum safe speed on a banked road uses $\tan\theta + \mu$ over $1 - \mu\tan\theta$. // 📝 Solution: $v_{max} = \sqrt{Rg\dfrac{\tan\theta + \mu}{1 - \mu\tan\theta}} = \sqrt{300 \times 10 \times \dfrac{0.577 + 0.2}{1 - 0.2 \times 0.577}}$ $\implies v_{max} \approx 51.4\;\text{m s}^{-1}$

questions.text: A block and trolley system is shown in the figure. If the coefficient of kinetic friction between the trolley and the surface is $0.04$, the acceleration of the system in $\text{m s}^{-2}$ is: (Consider that the string is massless and unstretchable and the pulley is also massless and frictionless) [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Friction on the trolley is $\mu N$; apply $F_{net} = m_{total}a$ to the whole system. // 📝 Solution: $f_k = \mu N = 0.04 \times 20 \times 10 = 8\;\text{N}$ $a = \dfrac{60 - 8}{20 + 6} = \dfrac{52}{26} = 2\;\text{m s}^{-2}$

questions.text: A block of mass $m$ slides down the plane inclined at angle $30^{\circ}$ with an acceleration $\dfrac{g}{4}$. The value of coefficient of kinetic friction will be:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Apply Newton's second law along the incline with kinetic friction opposing motion. // 📝 Solution: $mg\sin 30^{\circ} - \mu mg\cos 30^{\circ} = m\dfrac{g}{4}$ $\implies \dfrac{g}{2} - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\mu g = \dfrac{g}{4}$ $\implies \mu = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{3}}$

questions.text: A flexible chain of mass $m$ hangs between two fixed points at the same level. The inclination of the chain with the horizontal at the two points of support is $30^{\circ}$. Considering the equilibrium of each half of the chain, the tension of the chain at the lowest point is ____.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Each half of the chain is in equilibrium under the support tension and the horizontal tension at the lowest point. // 📝 Solution: $T_1\sin 30^{\circ} = \dfrac{mg}{2} \implies T_1 = mg$ $T_0 = T_1\cos 30^{\circ} = mg \cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$
questions.topic: Equilibrium of a hanging flexible chain

questions.text: A heavy box of mass $50\;\text{kg}$ is moving on a horizontal surface. If the coefficient of kinetic friction between the box and horizontal surface is $0.3$, then force of kinetic friction is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Kinetic friction equals $\mu_k N$ with $N = mg$ on a horizontal surface. // 📝 Solution: $f_k = \mu_k N = 0.3 \times 50 \times 9.8 = 147\;\text{N}$

questions.text: A wooden block, initially at rest on the ground, is pushed by a force which increases linearly with time $t$. Which of the following curve best describes acceleration of the block with time? (1) [FIGURE] (2) [FIGURE] (3) [FIGURE] (4) [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Newton's second law makes acceleration proportional to the applied force. // 📝 Solution: $F = kt \implies a = \dfrac{F}{m} = \dfrac{kt}{m}$ $\implies$ acceleration versus time is a straight line through the origin

questions.text: A cricket player catches a ball of mass $120\;\text{g}$ moving with $25\;\text{m s}^{-1}$ speed. If the catching process is completed in $0.1\;\text{s}$, then the magnitude of force exerted by the ball on the hand of player will be (in SI unit):
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Force equals the change in momentum divided by the time taken. // 📝 Solution: $F = \dfrac{\Delta p}{\Delta t} = \dfrac{0.12 \times 25}{0.1} = 30\;\text{N}$

questions.text: A string of length $L$ is fixed at one end and carries a mass of $M$ at the other end. The mass makes $\left(\frac{3}{\pi}\right)$ rotations per second about the vertical axis passing through end of the string as shown. The tension in the string is ...... $ML$. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For a conical pendulum, $T\sin\theta\;=\;M\omega^2 L\sin\theta$. // 📝 Solution: $\omega\;=\;\frac{3}{\pi}\times 2\pi\;=\;6\;\text{rad/s}\;\implies\;T\;=\;M\omega^2L\;=\;36\,ML$

questions.text: A block of mass $1\;\text{kg}$ is pushed up a surface inclined to horizontal at an angle of $60^{\circ}$ by a force of $10\;\text{N}$ parallel to the inclined surface as shown in figure. When the block is pushed up by $10\;\text{m}$ along inclined surface, the work done against frictional force is: $\left[ g = 10\;\text{m s}^{-2} \right]$ [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Work against friction equals friction force times displacement, with $N = mg\cos\theta$. // 📝 Solution: $N = mg\cos 60^{\circ} = 5\;\text{N}$ $\implies W_f = \mu N \times s = 0.1 \times 5 \times 10 = 5\;\text{J}$
questions.topic: Work done against friction on incline

questions.text: A block of mass $5\;\text{kg}$ is moving on an inclined plane which makes an angle of $30^{\circ}$ with the horizontal. Friction coefficient between the block and inclined plane surface is $\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$. The force to be applied on the block so that the block will move down without acceleration is ____ N. $\left( g = 10\;\text{m s}^{-2} \right)$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For no acceleration, the net force along the incline must be zero, with friction opposing the downward motion. // 📝 Solution: $mg\sin 30^{\circ} = 25\;\text{N}$, $N = mg\cos 30^{\circ} = 25\sqrt{3}\;\text{N}$ $f = \mu N = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \times 25\sqrt{3} = 37.5\;\text{N}$ $\implies 25 + F = 37.5 \implies F = 12.5\;\text{N}$ (applied down the incline)

questions.text: A train is moving with a speed of $12\;\text{m s}^{-1}$ on rails which are $1.5\;\text{m}$ apart. To negotiate a curve of radius $400\;\text{m}$, the height by which the outer rail should be raised with respect to the inner rail is (Given $g = 10\;\text{m s}^{-2}$):
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For banking without friction, $\tan\theta = \dfrac{v^{2}}{Rg}$ and $\tan\theta = \dfrac{h}{\text{gauge}}$. // 📝 Solution: $\dfrac{h}{1.5} = \dfrac{144}{4000} \implies h = 0.054\;\text{m} = 5.4\;\text{cm}$

questions.text: A body of weight $200\;\text{N}$ is suspended from a tree branch through a chain of mass $10\;\text{kg}$. The branch pulls the chain by a force equal to (if $g = 10\;\text{m s}^{-2}$):
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The whole body-chain system is in equilibrium, so the support force equals total weight. // 📝 Solution: $T = 200 + 10 \times 10 = 300\;\text{N}$

questions.text: The figure represents the momentum-time $\left( p\text{-}t \right)$ curve for a particle moving along an axis under the influence of the force. Identify the regions on the graph where the magnitude of the force is maximum and minimum respectively? If $\left( t_3 - t_2 \right) < t_1$. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Force equals the rate of change of momentum, i.e. the slope of the $p\text{-}t$ curve. // 📝 Solution: $\left\lvert \vec{F} \right\rvert = \left\lvert \dfrac{d\vec{p}}{dt} \right\rvert$ $\implies$ maximum force at the steepest slope (region c) $\;\text{and}\;$ minimum force at the least slope (region b)

questions.text: In the given figure the blocks $A$, $B$ and $C$ weigh $4\;\text{kg}$, $6\;\text{kg}$ and $8\;\text{kg}$ respectively. The co-efficient of sliding friction between any two surfaces is $0.5$. The force $\vec{F}$ required to slide the block $C$ with constant speed is ____ N. $\left( g = 10\;\text{m s}^{-2} \right)$ [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Constant speed means zero net force; add all friction forces opposing the motion of $C$. // 📝 Solution: $f_{ground} = \mu\left( m_A + m_B + m_C \right)g = 0.5 \times 180 = 90\;\text{N}$ $f_{BC} = \mu\left( m_A + m_B \right)g = 50\;\text{N}$ $T = \mu m_A g + \mu\left( m_A + m_B \right)g = 20 + 50 = 70\;\text{N}$ $\implies F = 90 + 70 + 50 = 210\;\text{N}$
questions.topic: Friction in stacked blocks with constant speed

questions.text: A given object takes $n$ times the time to slide down $45^{\circ}$ rough inclined plane as it takes the time to slide down an identical perfectly smooth $45^{\circ}$ inclined plane. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the object and the surface of inclined plane is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Equal distances with different times give the ratio of accelerations. // 📝 Solution: $t_2 = nt_1 \implies a_{rough} = \dfrac{a_{smooth}}{n^{2}}$ $g\sin 45^{\circ} - \mu g\cos 45^{\circ} = \dfrac{g\sin 45^{\circ}}{n^{2}} \implies \mu = 1 - \dfrac{1}{n^{2}}$
questions.topic: Rough incline, time ratio and friction

questions.text: A block of $\sqrt{3}\;\text{kg}$ is attached to a string whose other end is attached to the wall. An unknown force $F$ is applied so that the string makes an angle of $30^{\circ}$ with the wall. The tension $T$ is: (Given $g = 10\;\text{m/s}^{2}$) [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The vertical component of tension balances the weight of the block. // 📝 Solution: $T\cos 30^{\circ} = \sqrt{3}\,g \implies T \cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 10\sqrt{3} \implies T = 20\;\text{N}$

questions.text: A heavy iron bar of weight $12\;\text{kg}$ is having its one end on the ground and the other on the shoulder of a man. The rod makes an angle $60^{\circ}$ with the horizontal, the weight experienced by the man is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Take torques about the ground contact point. // 📝 Solution: $N_2 \cdot L = 120\left( \dfrac{L}{2}\cos 60^{\circ} \right) \implies N_2 = 30\;\text{N} = 3\;\text{kg-wt}$

questions.text: A $4\;\text{kg}$ mass moves under the influence of a force $\vec{F} = \left( 4t^{3}\hat{i} - 3t\hat{j} \right)\;\text{N}$ where $t$ is the time in seconds. If mass starts from origin at $t = 0$, the velocity and position after $t = 2\;\text{s}$ will be:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Integrate acceleration to get velocity, then integrate velocity to get position with zero initial values. // 📝 Solution: $\vec{a} = t^{3}\hat{i} - \dfrac{3t}{4}\hat{j}$ $\implies \vec{v} = \dfrac{t^{4}}{4}\hat{i} - \dfrac{3t^{2}}{8}\hat{j} \implies \vec{v}(2) = 4\hat{i} - \dfrac{3}{2}\hat{j}$ $\vec{r} = \dfrac{t^{5}}{20}\hat{i} - \dfrac{t^{3}}{8}\hat{j} \implies \vec{r}(2) = \dfrac{8}{5}\hat{i} - \hat{j}$
questions.topic: Variable force and kinematics by integration

questions.text: As per the given figure, a weightless pulley $P$ is attached on a double inclined frictionless surface. The tension in the string (massless) will be (if $g = 10\;\text{m/s}^{2}$) [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Write Newton's second law for each block along its incline and eliminate $a$. // 📝 Solution: $4g\sin 60^{\circ} - T = 4a \;\text{and}\; T - g\sin 30^{\circ} = a$ $\implies 20\sqrt{3} - T = 4\left( T - 5 \right)$ $\implies 5T = 20\sqrt{3} + 20$ $\implies T = 4\left( \sqrt{3} + 1 \right)\;\text{N}$
questions.topic: Tension in strings over pulley on double incline

questions.text: A wooden block of mass $5\;\text{kg}$ rests on a soft horizontal floor. When an iron cylinder of mass $25\;\text{kg}$ is placed on the top of the block, the floor yields and the block and the cylinder together go down with an acceleration of $0.1\;\text{m s}^{-2}$. The action force of the system on the floor is equal to:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Apply Newton's second law to the combined mass; action force equals the normal reaction. // 📝 Solution: $\left( 5 + 25 \right)\left( 9.8 \right) - N = 30 \times 0.1 \implies 294 - N = 3$ $\implies N = 291\;\text{N}$

questions.text: As shown in figure, a $70\;\text{kg}$ garden roller is pushed with a force of $\vec{F} = 200\;\text{N}$ at an angle of $30^{\circ}$ with horizontal. The normal reaction on the roller is (Given $g = 10\;\text{m s}^{-2}$) [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Resolve the push vertically and add it to the weight. // 📝 Solution: $N = mg + F\sin 30^{\circ} = 700 + 200 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 800\;\text{N}$
questions.topic: Normal reaction with applied force at angle

questions.text: As shown in the figure a block of mass $10\;\text{kg}$ lying on a horizontal surface is pulled by a force $F$ acting at an angle $30^{\circ}$ with horizontal. For $\mu_s = 0.25$, the block will just start to move for the value of $F$: [Given $g = 10\;\text{m s}^{-2}$] [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: At impending motion, the horizontal component of $F$ equals limiting friction $\mu_s N$. // 📝 Solution: $N = mg - F\sin 30^{\circ} = 100 - \dfrac{F}{2}$ $F\cos 30^{\circ} = \mu_s N \implies \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}F = 0.25\left( 100 - \dfrac{F}{2} \right)$ $\implies 4\sqrt{3}F = 200 - F \implies F = \dfrac{200}{4\sqrt{3} + 1} \approx 25.2\;\text{N}$
questions.topic: Limiting static friction with inclined pull

questions.text: All surfaces shown in figure are assumed to be frictionless and the pulleys and the string are light. The acceleration of the block of mass $2\;\text{kg}$ is: [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use the pulley constraint that the $2\;\text{kg}$ block moves twice as fast as the $4\;\text{kg}$ block. // 📝 Solution: $40 - 2T = 4a$ and $T - 10 = 2\left( 2a \right) = 4a$ $\implies 20 = 12a \implies a = \dfrac{5}{3}$ $\implies 2a = \dfrac{10}{3} = \dfrac{g}{3}$

questions.text: A $1\;\text{kg}$ mass is suspended from the ceiling by a rope of length $4\;\text{m}$. A horizontal force $F$ is applied at the mid point of the rope so that the rope makes an angle of $45^{\circ}$ with respect to the vertical axis as shown in figure. The magnitude of $F$ is: (Assume that the system is in equilibrium and $g = 10\;\text{m s}^{-2}$) [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: At the midpoint, the horizontal force and the lower string tension balance the upper tension. // 📝 Solution: $T_1\sin 45^{\circ} = F$ and $T_1\cos 45^{\circ} = mg = 10\;\text{N}$ $\implies F = mg\tan 45^{\circ} = 10\;\text{N}$
questions.topic: Equilibrium of rope with horizontal force at midpoint

questions.text: A block of mass $m$ is placed on a surface having vertical cross section given by $y = \dfrac{x^{2}}{4}$. If coefficient of friction is $0.5$, the maximum height above the ground at which block can be placed without slipping is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: On a curved surface, the block stays put while $\tan\theta = \dfrac{dy}{dx} \le \mu$. // 📝 Solution: $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x}{2} = \mu = \dfrac{1}{2} \implies x = 1$ $\implies y = \dfrac{x^{2}}{4} = \dfrac{1}{4}\;\text{m}$

questions.text: A rigid wire consists of a semicircular portion of radius $R$ and two straight sections, and is partially immersed in a uniform magnetic field $\vec{B}=B_0\,\hat{j}$ [FIGURE]. The magnetic force acting on the wire, when it carries a current $i$, is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Force on a curved wire in a uniform field equals the force on the straight line joining its ends. // 📝 Solution: $\vec{F}\;=\;i\left( \vec{L}_{eff}\times\vec{B} \right)\;\implies\;L_{eff}\;=\;2R\;\implies\;\vec{F}\;=\;-2iRB\,\hat{j}$
questions.topic: Force on a current-carrying wire of arbitrary shape in a uniform field

questions.text: Two long parallel wires carrying currents $8\;A$ and $15\;A$ in opposite directions are placed at a distance of $7\;cm$ from each other. A point $P$ is at equidistant from both the wires such that the lines joining the point $P$ to the wires are perpendicular to each other. The magnitude of magnetic field at $P$ is ______ $\times 10^{-6}\;T$. (Given : $\sqrt{2}\;=\;1.4$) [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The two fields at $P$ are perpendicular, so $B\;=\;\sqrt{B_1^2 + B_2^2}$ // 📝 Solution: $d\;=\;\frac{7}{\sqrt{2}}\;cm\;=\;5\;cm\;\implies\;B\;=\;\frac{\mu_0}{2\pi d}\sqrt{8^2 + 15^2}\;=\;\frac{2\times 10^{-7}\times 17}{5\times 10^{-2}}\;=\;68\times 10^{-6}\;T$
questions.topic: Superposition of fields of two straight wires

questions.text: Two long straight wires carry equal currents of $10\;\text{A}$ in opposite directions and are separated by $5.0\;\text{cm}$ [FIGURE]. The magnetic field at the midpoint $P$ between the wires is ______ $\mu\text{T}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: At the midpoint the fields of the two opposite currents add. // 📝 Solution: $a\;=\;2.5\;\text{cm}\;\implies\;B\;=\;2\times\dfrac{\mu_0 i}{2\pi a}\;=\;\dfrac{\mu_0 i}{\pi a}\;\implies\;B\;=\;\dfrac{4\pi\times10^{-7}\times10}{\pi\times0.025}\;=\;1.6\times10^{-4}\;\text{T}\;=\;160\;\mu\text{T}$
questions.topic: Superposition of fields of two antiparallel wires

questions.text: A rod of circular cross-section of area $2\;\text{cm}^2$ and length $40\;\text{cm}$ is wound uniformly with $400$ turns of insulated wire. If a current of $0.4\;\text{A}$ flows in the wire, the total magnetic flux produced inside the windings is $4\pi\times10^{-6}\;\text{Wb}$. The relative permeability of the rod is: (Take $\mu_0=4\pi\times10^{-7}\;\text{N A}^{-2}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Flux φ = μr μ0 n I A with n = N / l. // 📝 Solution: $\phi\;=\;\mu_r\mu_0\,\dfrac{N}{l}\,I A\;\implies\;4\pi\times10^{-6}\;=\;\mu_r\times4\pi\times10^{-7}\times\dfrac{400}{0.4}\times0.4\times2\times10^{-4}\;\implies\;\mu_r\;=\;125$
questions.topic: Magnetic field in a solenoid with a core (relative permeability)

questions.text: A square loop of area $25\;\text{cm}^2$ and resistance $10\;\Omega$ is placed in a uniform magnetic field of $40.0\;\text{T}$, with its plane perpendicular to the field. The work done in pulling the loop out of the field slowly and uniformly in $1.0\;\text{s}$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Motional emf gives the current, then F = BiL and W = F·l. // 📝 Solution: $l\;=\;5\;\text{cm}\;\implies\;v\;=\;\dfrac{0.05}{1}\;=\;0.05\;\text{m/s}\;\implies\;i\;=\;\dfrac{Blv}{R}\;=\;\dfrac{40\times0.05\times0.05}{10}\;=\;0.01\;\text{A}\;\implies\;F\;=\;Bil\;=\;40\times0.01\times0.05\;=\;0.02\;\text{N}\;\implies\;W\;=\;F\,l\;=\;0.02\times0.05\;=\;1.0\times10^{-3}\;\text{J}$
questions.topic: Work done in pulling a loop out of a magnetic field

questions.text: Two long straight wires $P$ and $Q$ carrying equal current $10\;A$ each were kept parallel to each other at $5\;cm$ distance. Magnitude of magnetic force experienced by $10\;cm$ length of wire $P$ is $F_1$. If distance between wires is halved and currents on them are doubled, force $F_2$ on $10\;cm$ length of wire $P$ will be :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Force per unit length between parallel wires is $\frac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{2\pi d}$ // 📝 Solution: $\frac{F_2}{F_1}\;=\;\frac{\left(2I\right)\left(2I\right)}{I\cdot I}\times\frac{d}{d/2}\;=\;4\times 2\;=\;8\;\implies\;F_2\;=\;8\;F_1$

questions.text: A square coil of area $70\;\text{cm}^2$ with $600$ turns rotates in a magnetic field of $0.4\;\text{Wb m}^{-2}$ about an axis parallel to one side of the coil and perpendicular to the field. It completes $500$ revolutions per minute. The instantaneous emf, when the plane of the coil is inclined at $60^\circ$ with the field, is ______ V. (Take $\pi=\dfrac{22}{7}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: e = N A B ω sinθ, where θ is the angle between the coil normal and the field. // 📝 Solution: $\omega\;=\;\dfrac{2\pi\times500}{60}\;=\;\dfrac{50\pi}{3}\;\text{rad/s}\;\implies\;\theta\;=\;90^\circ-60^\circ\;=\;30^\circ\;\implies\;e\;=\;600\times70\times10^{-4}\times0.4\times\dfrac{50}{3}\times\dfrac{22}{7}\times\dfrac{1}{2}\;=\;44\;\text{V}$
questions.topic: Induced emf in a rotating coil

questions.text: A bar magnet of magnetic moment $5.0\;\text{A m}^2$ is placed parallel to a magnetic field of $0.4\;\text{T}$. The work done in turning the magnet from the parallel to the antiparallel orientation is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: W = MB(cosθ1 − cosθ2). // 📝 Solution: $W\;=\;MB\left( \cos 0^\circ\;-\;\cos 180^\circ \right)\;=\;2MB\;\implies\;W\;=\;2\times5\times0.4\;=\;4\;\text{J}$
questions.topic: Work done in rotating a magnetic dipole

questions.text: The magnetic field at the centre of a circular loop of radius $R$ is $16\;\mu\text{T}$. The magnetic field at a point on its axis at a distance $x=\sqrt{3}\,R$ from the centre is ______ $\mu\text{T}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Axial field is B = μ0 I R² / 2(R² + x²)^{3/2}, while the centre field is μ0 I / 2R. // 📝 Solution: $\dfrac{B_x}{B_0}\;=\;\dfrac{R^3}{\left( R^2+x^2 \right)^{3/2}}\;=\;\dfrac{R^3}{\left( 4R^2 \right)^{3/2}}\;=\;\dfrac{1}{8}\;\implies\;B_x\;=\;\dfrac{16}{8}\;=\;2\;\mu\text{T}$
questions.topic: Axial magnetic field of a circular current loop

questions.text: A single turn current loop in the shape of a right angle triangle with sides $5\;cm$, $12\;cm$, $13\;cm$ is carrying a current of $2\;A$. The loop is in a uniform magnetic field of magnitude $0.75\;T$ whose direction is parallel to the current in the $13\;cm$ side of the loop. The magnitude of the magnetic force on the $5\;cm$ side will be $\frac{x}{130}\;N$. The value of $x$ is ______ [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Force on a straight wire is $F\;=\;I\,L\,B\sin\theta$ // 📝 Solution: Angle between $5\;cm$ side and $B$ has $\sin\theta\;=\;\frac{12}{13}\;\implies\;F\;=\;2\times 5\times 10^{-2}\times 0.75\times\frac{12}{13}\;=\;\frac{9}{130}\;N\;\implies\;x\;=\;9$
questions.topic: Force on current-carrying conductor in uniform field

questions.text: Two parallel long wires carry currents $I$ and $2I$ and are separated by a distance $2r$ [FIGURE]. The ratio of the magnetic field at point $A$ to that at point $C$ is $\dfrac{x}{7}$. The value of $x$ is ______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Superposition of B = μ0 i / 2πd from each wire, with directions from the figure. // 📝 Solution: $B_A\;=\;\dfrac{\mu_0 i}{2\pi r}+\dfrac{\mu_0 \left( 2i \right)}{2\pi\left( 3r \right)}\;=\;\dfrac{5\mu_0 i}{6\pi r}\;,\;B_C\;=\;\dfrac{7\mu_0 i}{6\pi r}\;\implies\;\dfrac{B_A}{B_C}\;=\;\dfrac{5}{7}\;\implies\;x\;=\;5$
questions.topic: Superposition of fields of two parallel wires

questions.text: An electron moves in a magnetic field $\vec{B}=B_0\,\hat{i}+2B_0\,\hat{j}\;\text{T}$ with a velocity $\vec{v}=3\,\hat{i}+5\,\hat{j}\;\text{m s}^{-1}$. The force on it is $5e\,\hat{k}\;\text{N}$ (as given in the official key). The value of $B_0$ is ______ T.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Evaluate the cross product v×B and match the magnitude of the k̂ component with the given force. // 📝 Solution: $\vec{v}\times\vec{B}\;=\;\left( 3\times2B_0-5\times B_0 \right)\hat{k}\;=\;B_0\,\hat{k}\;\implies\;\left\lvert \vec{F} \right\rvert\;=\;e\,B_0\;=\;5e\;\implies\;B_0\;=\;5\;\text{T}\;\text{(sign convention as per official key)}$
questions.topic: Lorentz force on an electron (cross product)

questions.text: The magnitude of magnetic induction at mid-point $O$ due to current arrangement as shown in Fig will be : [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Semi-infinite wire starting at the foot of the perpendicular gives $\frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r}$ // 📝 Solution: Only $BC$ and $ET$ contribute, each at $r\;=\;\frac{a}{2}$, both outward at $O$ $\implies$ $B_0\;=\;\frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r}+\frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r}\;=\;\frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}\;=\;\frac{\mu_0 I}{\pi a}$

questions.text: A long straight wire of radius $a$ carries a steady current $I$ uniformly distributed over its cross-section. The ratio of the magnetic fields at distances $\dfrac{a}{2}$ and $2a$ from the axis of the wire is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Inside B = μ0 I r / 2πa², outside B = μ0 I / 2πr. // 📝 Solution: $B_1\;=\;\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi a^2}\cdot\dfrac{a}{2}\;=\;\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi a}\;,\;B_2\;=\;\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi\left( 2a \right)}\;=\;\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi a}\;\implies\;B_1:B_2\;=\;1:1$
questions.topic: Ampere's circuital law for a thick straight wire

questions.text: A current of $2\;\text{A}$ flows in a straight metal wire of resistance $R=1\;\Omega$, resistivity $\rho=2\times10^{-6}\;\Omega\,\text{m}$, cross-section area $A=10\;\text{mm}^2$ and mass $500\;\text{g}$. The wire is suspended horizontally by a uniform magnetic field $B$. The value of $B$ is ______ $\times10^{-1}\;\text{T}$. (Take $g=10\;\text{m s}^{-2}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find the wire length from R = ρℓ/A, then balance BiL with mg. // 📝 Solution: $\ell\;=\;\dfrac{RA}{\rho}\;=\;\dfrac{1\times10\times10^{-6}}{2\times10^{-6}}\;=\;5\;\text{m}\;\implies\;B i \ell\;=\;mg\;\implies\;B\;=\;\dfrac{0.5\times10}{2\times5}\;=\;0.5\;\text{T}\;=\;5\times10^{-1}\;\text{T}$
questions.topic: Magnetic levitation of a current-carrying wire

questions.text: A current of $5\;\text{A}$ flows in a square loop of side $1\;\text{m}$ placed in air. The magnetic field at the centre of the loop is $X\sqrt{2}\times10^{-7}\;\text{T}$. The value of $X$ is ______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Each side gives (μ0 i / 4πd)(sin45° + sin45°) with d = half the side. // 📝 Solution: $d\;=\;0.5\;\text{m}\;\implies\;B\;=\;4\times\dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4\pi d}\left( \sin45^\circ+\sin45^\circ \right)\;=\;4\times\dfrac{10^{-7}\times5}{0.5}\times\sqrt{2}\;=\;40\sqrt{2}\times10^{-7}\;\text{T}\;\implies\;X\;=\;40$
questions.topic: Magnetic field at the centre of a square loop

questions.text: Statement I: When currents vary with time, Newton's third law is valid only if the momentum carried by the electromagnetic field is taken into account. Statement II: Ampere's circuital law does not depend on Biot-Savart's law. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Field momentum restores Newton's third law for time-varying currents, and Ampere's law follows from Biot-Savart's law. // 📝 Solution: $\text{Statement I: true (field momentum must be included)}\;\implies\;\text{Statement II: false, since Ampere's law is derivable from Biot-Savart's law}\;\implies\;\text{Option B}$
questions.topic: Ampere's law, Biot-Savart law and conceptual statements

questions.text: The position of an ant $S$ (in metres) moving in the $Y$-$Z$ plane is given by $S=2t^2\hat{j}+5\hat{k}$, where $t$ is in seconds. The magnitude and direction of the velocity of the ant at $t=1\;\text{s}$ will be:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Velocity is the time derivative of position. // 📝 Solution: $\vec{v}\;=\;\dfrac{d\vec{S}}{dt}\;=\;4t\,\hat{j}\;\implies\;\vec{v}\left( t=1 \right)\;=\;4\,\hat{j}\;\text{m/s}\;\implies\;4\;\text{m/s along the }y\text{ direction}$

questions.text: Three long parallel wires $P$, $Q$ and $R$ carry currents of $3\;\text{A}$ (upward), $1\;\text{A}$ (downward) and $2\;\text{A}$ (downward) respectively [FIGURE]. The spacing between $P$ and $Q$ is $3\;\text{cm}$ and between $Q$ and $R$ is $2\;\text{cm}$. The magnetic force on a $15\;\text{cm}$ length of wire $Q$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Force per unit length between parallel wires is μ0 I1 I2 / 2πd, repulsive for opposite currents and attractive for the same direction. // 📝 Solution: $\dfrac{F_{PQ}}{L}\;=\;\dfrac{2\times10^{-7}\times3\times1}{0.03}\;=\;2\times10^{-5}\;\text{N/m}\;\text{(repulsion, towards }R\text{)}\;,\;\dfrac{F_{RQ}}{L}\;=\;\dfrac{2\times10^{-7}\times2\times1}{0.02}\;=\;2\times10^{-5}\;\text{N/m}\;\text{(attraction, towards }R\text{)}\;\implies\;F\;=\;4\times10^{-5}\times0.15\;=\;6\times10^{-6}\;\text{N towards }R$
questions.topic: Force between parallel current-carrying wires (three wires)

questions.text: A loop of two concentric semicircles of radii $R_1=2\pi\;\text{m}$ and $R_2=4\pi\;\text{m}$ carries a current $I=4\;\text{A}$ [FIGURE]. The magnetic field at the common centre is $\alpha\times10^{-7}\;\text{T}$. The value of $\alpha$ is ______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Each semicircle gives μ0 I / 4R and the straight segments pass through the centre, giving zero. // 📝 Solution: $B\;=\;\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4R_1}+\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4R_2}\;\implies\;B\;=\;4\pi\times10^{-7}\left( \dfrac{1}{2\pi}+\dfrac{1}{4\pi} \right)\;=\;\left( 2+1 \right)\times10^{-7}\;=\;3\times10^{-7}\;\text{T}$
questions.topic: Magnetic field at the centre of concentric semicircular arcs

questions.text: As shown in the figure, a current of $2\;\text{A}$ flows in an equilateral triangle of side $4\sqrt{3}\;\text{cm}$. The magnetic field at the centroid $O$ of the triangle is: [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Field of a finite wire is (μ0 i / 4πd)(sinα + sinβ), and the three sides add. // 📝 Solution: $d\;=\;\dfrac{a}{2\sqrt{3}}\;=\;2\;\text{cm}\;\implies\;B\;=\;3\times\dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4\pi d}\left( 2\sin 60^\circ \right)\;=\;3\times\dfrac{10^{-7}\times2}{0.02}\times\sqrt{3}\;=\;3\sqrt{3}\times10^{-5}\;\text{T}$
questions.topic: Magnetic field due to a finite straight wire (triangular loop)

questions.text: Two identical circular loops $P$ and $Q$ of radius $r$ share a common axis, with their centres separated by $2r$ and the point $O$ midway between them [FIGURE]. They carry currents $I$ and $4I$ respectively, both clockwise as seen from $O$. The net magnetic field at $O$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Axial field of a loop is B = μ0 I R² / 2(R² + x²)^{3/2} with x = R, and the two fields oppose. // 📝 Solution: $B_1\;=\;\dfrac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2\left( 2R^2 \right)^{3/2}}\;=\;\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\sqrt{2}\,R}\;,\;B_2\;=\;\dfrac{4\mu_0 I}{4\sqrt{2}\,R}\;\implies\;B_{net}\;=\;B_2-B_1\;=\;\dfrac{3\mu_0 I}{4\sqrt{2}\,R}\;\text{towards }Q$
questions.topic: Axial field of two coaxial current loops

questions.text: A current-carrying solenoid is placed vertically. A particle of mass $m$ and charge $Q$ is released from rest and moves along the axis of the solenoid. The acceleration $a$ of the particle satisfies:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Magnetic force q(v×B) is zero when v is parallel to B. // 📝 Solution: $\vec{v}\;\parallel\;\vec{B}\;\implies\;\vec{F}_{mag}\;=\;Q\left( \vec{v}\times\vec{B} \right)\;=\;0\;\implies\;\text{only gravity acts}\;\implies\;a\;=\;g$
questions.topic: Motion of a charged particle along a solenoid axis

questions.text: A coil is placed in a magnetic field such that the plane of the coil is perpendicular to the direction of the field. The magnetic flux through the coil can be changed by: A. changing the magnitude of the field within the coil; B. changing the area of the coil within the field; C. changing the angle between the direction of the magnetic field and the plane of the coil; D. reversing the magnetic field direction abruptly without changing its magnitude. Choose the most appropriate answer:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Flux φ = B A cosθ depends on B, A and θ. // 📝 Solution: $\phi\;=\;BA\cos\theta\;\implies\;\text{changing }B,\;A,\;\theta\;\text{alters }\phi\;\implies\;\text{A, B, C change flux}\;\implies\;\text{Most suitable answer is A, B and C only (official key option 2)}$
questions.topic: Magnetic flux and factors affecting it

questions.text: A circular loop of radius $r$ is carrying current $I\;A$. The ratio of magnetic field at the centre of circular loop and at a distance $r$ from the center of the loop on its axis is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Axial field of a loop is $B\;=\;\frac{\mu_0 I r^2}{2\left(r^2 + x^2\right)^{3/2}}$ // 📝 Solution: $B_1\;=\;\frac{\mu_0 I}{2r}$ and $B_2\;=\;\frac{\mu_0 I r^2}{2\left(2r^2\right)^{3/2}}\;=\;\frac{\mu_0 I}{4\sqrt{2}\,r}\;\implies\;\frac{B_1}{B_2}\;=\;2\sqrt{2}$
questions.topic: Axial magnetic field of circular loop

questions.text:
A proton moving with a constant velocity passes through a region of space without any change in its velocity. If $\vec{E}$ and $\vec{B}$ represent the electric and magnetic fields respectively, this region may have: A. $E=0,\;B=0$ B. $E=0,\;B
eq0$ C. $E
eq0,\;B=0$ D. $E
eq0,\;B
eq0$. Choose the most appropriate answer:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Velocity is unchanged only if the net Lorentz force is zero. // 📝 Solution: $\vec{F}\;=\;q\vec{E}+q\left( \vec{v}\times\vec{B} \right)\;=\;0\;\implies\;\text{A: }E=B=0\;\text{works}\;,\;\text{B: }\vec{v}\parallel\vec{B}\;\text{works}\;,\;\text{D: }q\vec{E}\;=\;-q\left( \vec{v}\times\vec{B} \right)\;\text{works}\;,\;\text{C: }F=qE\neq0\;\text{fails}\;\implies\;\text{A, B and D only}$
questions.topic: Charged particle in electric and magnetic fields (zero net force)

questions.text: A regular hexagon is formed by bending a wire of length $4\pi\;\text{m}$ and carries a current of $4\pi\sqrt{3}\;\text{A}$. The magnetic field at the centre of the hexagon is $x\times10^{-7}\;\text{T}$. The value of $x$ is ______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Each side gives (μ0 i / 4πd)(sin30° + sin30°), where d is the distance from the centre to the side. // 📝 Solution: $a\;=\;\dfrac{4\pi}{6}\;=\;\dfrac{2\pi}{3}\;\text{m}\;\implies\;d\;=\;\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\,a\;=\;\dfrac{\pi}{\sqrt{3}}\;\text{m}\;\implies\;B\;=\;6\times\dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4\pi d}\left( \sin30^\circ+\sin30^\circ \right)\;=\;6\times10^{-7}\times\dfrac{4\pi\sqrt{3}\times\sqrt{3}}{\pi}\;=\;72\times10^{-7}\;\text{T}$
questions.topic: Magnetic field at the centre of a regular polygon loop

questions.text: A long cylindrical conductor of large cross-section carries a current distributed uniformly over its cross-section. The magnetic field is: A. maximum at either end and minimum at the midpoint; B. maximum at the axis; C. minimum at the surface; D. minimum at the axis; E. the same at all points. Choose the correct answer:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Inside, B = μ0 I r / 2πR², which is zero at the axis and maximum at the surface. // 📝 Solution: $B\left( r \right)\;=\;\dfrac{\mu_0 I r}{2\pi R^2}\;\left( r<R \right)\;\implies\;B\left( 0 \right)\;=\;0\;\text{(minimum at the axis)}\;\implies\;B_{max}\;\text{at the surface}\;\implies\;\text{only D is correct}$
questions.topic: Ampere's circuital law for a thick cylindrical conductor

questions.text: Two circular coils $P$ and $Q$ of $100$ turns each and radius $\pi\;\text{cm}$ carry currents of $1\;\text{A}$ and $2\;\text{A}$ respectively. Their planes are mutually perpendicular and their centres coincide [FIGURE]. The resultant magnetic field at the common centre is $\sqrt{x}\;\text{mT}$. The value of $x$ is ______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Field at a coil centre is B = μ0 N I / 2R, and the perpendicular fields add as vectors. // 📝 Solution: $B_P\;=\;\dfrac{\mu_0 N I_P}{2R}\;=\;\dfrac{4\pi\times10^{-7}\times100\times1}{2\pi\times10^{-2}}\;=\;2\times10^{-3}\;\text{T}\;,\;B_Q\;=\;4\times10^{-3}\;\text{T}\;\implies\;B\;=\;\sqrt{B_P^2+B_Q^2}\;=\;\sqrt{4+16}\;\text{mT}\;=\;\sqrt{20}\;\text{mT}\;\implies\;x\;=\;20$
questions.topic: Superposition of fields of perpendicular coils

questions.text: An infinitely long straight wire carrying current $I$ is bent in a planar shape as shown in the figure [FIGURE: points $A$, $B$, $D$, $E$ on the line, circular part of radius $r$ with centre $O$, axes $\hat{x}$, $\hat{y}$, $\hat{z}$]. The magnetic field at the centre $O$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Add the two semi-infinite wires (μ0 i / 4πr each) and subtract the opposing circular loop field μ0 i / 2r. // 📝 Solution: $\vec{B}\;=\;\dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4\pi r}\hat{i}+\dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4\pi r}\hat{i}-\dfrac{\mu_0 i}{2r}\hat{i}\;\implies\;\vec{B}\;=\;\dfrac{\mu_0 i}{2\pi r}\left( 1-\pi \right)\hat{i}\;=\;-\dfrac{\mu_0}{2\pi}\dfrac{I}{r}\left( \pi-1 \right)\hat{i}$
questions.topic: Biot-Savart law for a loop with semi-infinite straight wires

questions.text: A coil is placed perpendicular to a magnetic field of $5000\;\text{T}$. When the field changes to $3000\;\text{T}$ in $2\;\text{s}$, an emf of $22\;\text{V}$ is induced. If the diameter of the coil is $0.02\;\text{m}$, the number of turns in the coil is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Faraday's law, emf = N A (ΔB / Δt). // 📝 Solution: $A\;=\;\pi\left( 0.01 \right)^2\;=\;\pi\times10^{-4}\;\text{m}^2\;\implies\;\varepsilon\;=\;N A\,\dfrac{\Delta B}{\Delta t}\;\implies\;22\;=\;N\times\pi\times10^{-4}\times\dfrac{2000}{2}\;\implies\;N\;=\;\dfrac{22}{0.1\pi}\;=\;70$

questions.text: A short bar magnet with its axis at $30^\circ$ to an external magnetic field of $800\;\text{Gauss}$ experiences a torque of $0.016\;\text{N m}$. The work done in moving it from its most stable to its most unstable position is $\alpha\times10^{-3}\;\text{J}$. The value of $\alpha$ is ______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Torque τ = mB sinθ gives m, and W = 2mB between the stable and unstable positions. // 📝 Solution: $B\;=\;800\;\text{G}\;=\;0.08\;\text{T}\;\implies\;m\;=\;\dfrac{\tau}{B\sin30^\circ}\;=\;\dfrac{0.016}{0.08\times0.5}\;=\;0.4\;\text{A m}^2\;\implies\;W\;=\;2mB\;=\;2\times0.4\times0.08\;=\;0.064\;\text{J}\;=\;64\times10^{-3}\;\text{J}$
questions.topic: Torque and work done on a bar magnet in a magnetic field

questions.text: In a coaxial cable, the central conductor and the outer conductor carry equal currents in opposite directions [FIGURE]. The magnetic field is zero:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Apply Ampere's circuital law on a circular loop coaxial with the cable. // 📝 Solution: $\oint\vec{B}\cdot d\vec{l}\;=\;\mu_0 I_{enc}\;\implies\;\text{outside: }I_{enc}\;=\;I-I\;=\;0\;\implies\;B\;=\;0\;\text{outside the cable}$
questions.topic: Ampere's circuital law for a coaxial cable

questions.text: Two particles $X$ and $Y$ having equal charges, after being accelerated through the same potential difference, enter a region of uniform magnetic field and describe circular paths of radii $R_1$ and $R_2$ respectively. The ratio of the mass of $X$ to that of $Y$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: qV = ½mv² and r = mv / qB give r = √(2mV/q) / B. // 📝 Solution: $R\;=\;\dfrac{1}{B}\sqrt{\dfrac{2mV}{q}}\;\implies\;R^2\;\propto\;m\;\implies\;\dfrac{m_X}{m_Y}\;=\;\left( \dfrac{R_1}{R_2} \right)^{2}$
questions.topic: Charged particle accelerated through a potential and deflected in a magnetic field

questions.text: A solenoid of length $0.5\;\text{m}$ and radius $1\;\text{cm}$ is made of $m$ turns. It carries a current of $5\;\text{A}$. If the magnitude of the magnetic field at its centre is $6.28\times10^{-3}\;\text{T}$, then the value of $m$ is ______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: B = μ0 (m / ℓ) i for a long solenoid. // 📝 Solution: $B\;=\;\mu_0\dfrac{m}{\ell}\,i\;\implies\;m\;=\;\dfrac{B\ell}{\mu_0 i}\;=\;\dfrac{6.28\times10^{-3}\times0.5}{4\pi\times10^{-7}\times5}\;=\;500$

questions.text: The electric current in a circular coil of four turns produces a magnetic induction of $32\;\text{T}$ at its centre. The coil is unwound and rewound into a single-turn circular coil. The magnetic induction at the centre of the new coil by the same current is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: B = μ0 N I / 2R, and the wire length 2πRN stays constant. // 📝 Solution: $N\left( 2\pi R \right)\;=\;2\pi R'\;\implies\;R'\;=\;4R\;\implies\;B\;=\;\dfrac{\mu_0 \left( 4 \right) I}{2R}\;,\;B'\;=\;\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\left( 4R \right)}\;\implies\;\dfrac{B'}{B}\;=\;\dfrac{1}{16}\;\implies\;B'\;=\;\dfrac{32}{16}\;=\;2\;\text{T}$
questions.topic: Magnetic field at the centre of a circular coil

questions.text: A magnetic field $\vec{B}=0.2\left( 1+2x \right)\hat{k}\;\text{T}$ exists in space. A square loop of edge $50\;\text{cm}$ carrying $0.5\;\text{A}$ lies in the $x$-$y$ plane with its edges parallel to the axes and its lower-left corner at $x=2\;\text{m},\;y=2\;\text{m}$ [FIGURE]. The net magnetic force on the loop is ______ mN.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Forces on the two horizontal sides cancel, so only the vertical sides at different x contribute. // 📝 Solution: $B\left( 2 \right)\;=\;0.2\times5\;=\;1.0\;\text{T}\;,\;B\left( 2.5 \right)\;=\;0.2\times6\;=\;1.2\;\text{T}\;\implies\;F_{net}\;=\;iL\left( 1.2-1.0 \right)\;=\;0.5\times0.5\times0.2\;=\;0.05\;\text{N}\;=\;50\;\text{mN}$
questions.topic: Force on a current loop in a non-uniform magnetic field

questions.text: A moving coil galvanometer has $100$ turns, each of area $2.0\;\text{cm}^2$, in a magnetic field of $0.01\;\text{T}$. It shows a deflection of $0.05\;\text{rad}$ for a current of $10\;\text{mA}$. The torsional constant of the spring is $x\times10^{-5}\;\text{N m rad}^{-1}$. The value of $x$ is ______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: At equilibrium NIAB = Cθ. // 📝 Solution: $C\theta\;=\;BINA\;\implies\;C\;=\;\dfrac{BINA}{\theta}\;=\;\dfrac{0.01\times10\times10^{-3}\times100\times2\times10^{-4}}{0.05}\;=\;4\times10^{-5}\;\text{N m rad}^{-1}$

questions.text: A massless square loop of resistance $10\;\Omega$ supports a mass of $1\;\text{g}$ and hangs vertically with one of its sides in a uniform magnetic field of $10^{3}\;\text{G}$, directed outwards in the shaded region [FIGURE]. A dc voltage $V$ is applied to the loop. For what value of $V$ does the magnetic force exactly balance the weight of the $1\;\text{g}$ mass? (Side of loop $=10\;\text{cm}$, $g=10\;\text{m s}^{-2}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Balance the magnetic force BiL with the weight mg, where i = V/R. // 📝 Solution: $B\;=\;10^{3}\;\text{G}\;=\;0.1\;\text{T}\;\implies\;B\,\dfrac{V}{R}\,L\;=\;mg\;\implies\;V\;=\;\dfrac{mgR}{BL}\;=\;\dfrac{10^{-3}\times10\times10}{0.1\times0.1}\;=\;10\;\text{V}$
questions.topic: Force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field

questions.text: A coil of $100$ turns and area $5\times10^{-3}\;\text{m}^2$ carries a current of $1\;\text{mA}$ in a uniform magnetic field of $0.20\;\text{T}$, with its plane perpendicular to the field. The work done in turning the coil through $90^\circ$ is ______ $\mu\text{J}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Plane perpendicular to B means M is parallel to B, so W = MB(1 − cos90°). // 📝 Solution: $M\;=\;NIA\;=\;100\times10^{-3}\times5\times10^{-3}\;=\;5\times10^{-4}\;\text{A m}^2\;\implies\;W\;=\;MB\;=\;5\times10^{-4}\times0.2\;=\;10^{-4}\;\text{J}\;=\;100\;\mu\text{J}$
questions.topic: Work done in rotating a current-carrying coil

questions.text: A long solenoid is formed by winding $70$ turns $cm^{-1}$. If $2.0\;A$ current flows, then the magnetic field produced inside the solenoid is ______ ($\mu_0\;=\;4\pi\times 10^{-7}\;TmA^{-1}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Field inside a solenoid is $B\;=\;\mu_0 n I$ // 📝 Solution: $n\;=\;70\times 10^{2}\;m^{-1}\;\implies\;B\;=\;4\pi\times 10^{-7}\times 70\times 10^{2}\times 2\;=\;56\pi\times 10^{-4}\;T\;\approx\;176\times 10^{-4}\;T$

questions.text: A current-carrying rectangular loop $PQRS$ is made of uniform wire, with $PR=QS=5\;\text{cm}$ and $PQ=RS=100\;\text{cm}$ [FIGURE]. If the current $I$ read by the ammeter changes to $2I$, the ratio of the magnetic forces per unit length on the wire $PQ$ due to the wire $RS$ in the two cases, $f_{PQ}^{1}:f_{PQ}^{2}$, is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Force per unit length between parallel wires is proportional to the product of their currents. // 📝 Solution: $f\;=\;\dfrac{\mu_0 I_1 I_2}{2\pi d}\;\implies\;f\;\propto\;I_1 I_2\;\propto\;I^2\;\implies\;\dfrac{f^{1}_{PQ}}{f^{2}_{PQ}}\;=\;\dfrac{I^2}{\left( 2I \right)^2}\;=\;\dfrac{1}{4}$

questions.text: A proton and a deuteron (charge $+e$, mass $2.0\;\text{u}$) with the same kinetic energy enter a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the field. The ratio of the radii of their circular paths, $r_d:r_p$, is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: r = √(2mK) / qB, so r ∝ √m for equal K and q. // 📝 Solution: $r\;=\;\dfrac{\sqrt{2mK}}{qB}\;\implies\;r\;\propto\;\sqrt{m}\;\implies\;\dfrac{r_d}{r_p}\;=\;\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{1}}\;=\;\sqrt{2}:1$
questions.topic: Circular motion of a charged particle in a magnetic field

questions.text: The magnetic potential due to a magnetic dipole at a point on its axis, at a distance of $20\;\text{cm}$ from it, is $1.5\times10^{-5}\;\text{T m}$. The magnetic moment of the dipole is ______ $\text{A m}^2$. (Given $\dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi}=10^{-7}\;\text{T m A}^{-1}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Axial magnetic potential is V = (μ0 / 4π) M / r². // 📝 Solution: $V\;=\;\dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\dfrac{M}{r^2}\;\implies\;M\;=\;\dfrac{V r^2}{10^{-7}}\;=\;\dfrac{1.5\times10^{-5}\times\left( 0.2 \right)^2}{10^{-7}}\;=\;6\;\text{A m}^2$

questions.text: For a moving coil galvanometer, the deflection in the coil is $0.05\;rad$ when a current of $10\;mA$ is passed through it. If the torsional constant of suspension wire is $4.0\times 10^{-5}\;Nm\,rad^{-1}$, the magnetic field is $0.01\;T$ and the number of turns in the coil is $200$, the area of each turn (in $cm^2$) is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Balance of torques $NiAB\;=\;K\theta$ // 📝 Solution: $A\;=\;\frac{K\theta}{NiB}\;=\;\frac{4\times 10^{-5}\times 0.05}{200\times 10\times 10^{-3}\times 0.01}\;=\;10^{-4}\;m^{2}\;=\;1\;cm^{2}$

questions.text: Find the magnetic field at the point $P$ in the figure. The curved portion is a semicircle of radius $r$ connected to two long straight wires, carrying current $i$. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Semicircle gives μ0 i / 4r, a semi-infinite straight wire gives μ0 i / 4πr, and the wire through P gives zero. // 📝 Solution: $B_P\;=\;\dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4r}\;+\;\dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4\pi r}\;\implies\;B_P\;=\;\dfrac{\mu_0 i}{2r}\left( \dfrac{1}{2}+\dfrac{1}{2\pi} \right)$
questions.topic: Biot-Savart law for a semicircular arc with straight wires

questions.text: The magnetic moments of two closely wound circular coils $A$ (radius $r_A=10\;\text{cm}$) and $B$ (radius $r_B=20\;\text{cm}$) are equal. If $N$ and $I$ denote the number of turns and the current respectively, then:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Magnetic moment of a coil is M = N I A with A = πr². // 📝 Solution: $M_A\;=\;M_B\;\implies\;N_A I_A\,\pi\left( 0.1 \right)^2\;=\;N_B I_B\,\pi\left( 0.2 \right)^2\;\implies\;N_A I_A\;=\;4N_B I_B$
questions.topic: Magnetic moment of a current-carrying coil

questions.text: An equilateral triangle of side $4\sqrt{3}\;\text{cm}$ carries a current of $2\;\text{A}$. The magnetic field at its centroid is $\alpha\times10^{-5}\;\text{T}$. The value of $\alpha$ is: (Take $\mu_0=4\pi\times10^{-7}\;\text{N A}^{-2}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Each side gives (μ0 i / 4πr)(sin60° + sin60°), where r is the inradius a / 2√3. // 📝 Solution: $r\;=\;\dfrac{a}{2\sqrt{3}}\;=\;2\;\text{cm}\;\implies\;B_1\;=\;\dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4\pi r}\left( 2\sin60^\circ \right)\;=\;\sqrt{3}\times10^{-5}\;\text{T}\;\implies\;B\;=\;3B_1\;=\;3\sqrt{3}\times10^{-5}\;\text{T}\;\implies\;\alpha\;=\;3\sqrt{3}$
questions.topic: Magnetic field due to a finite straight wire (triangular loop)

questions.text: A circular coil of $200$ turns and area $2.5\times10^{-4}\;\text{m}^2$ carries a current of $100\;\mu\text{A}$ in a uniform magnetic field of $1\;\text{T}$. The magnetic moment $\vec{M}$ is initially along $\vec{B}$. The work done to rotate the coil through $90^\circ$ is ______ $\mu\text{J}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: W = MB(cosθ1 − cosθ2) with M = N I A. // 📝 Solution: $M\;=\;NIA\;=\;200\times100\times10^{-6}\times2.5\times10^{-4}\;=\;5\times10^{-6}\;\text{A m}^2\;\implies\;W\;=\;MB\left( \cos0^\circ-\cos90^\circ \right)\;=\;5\times10^{-6}\;\text{J}\;=\;5\;\mu\text{J}$
questions.topic: Work done in rotating a current-carrying coil

questions.text: A charge of $4.0\;\mu\text{C}$ moves with a velocity of $4.0\times10^{6}\;\text{m s}^{-1}$ along the $+y$ axis in a uniform magnetic field $\vec{B}=2\,\hat{k}\;\text{T}$. The force acting on the charge is $x\,\hat{i}\;\text{N}$. The value of $x$ is ______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Magnetic force is F = q(v×B), and ĵ × k̂ = î. // 📝 Solution: $\vec{F}\;=\;q\left( \vec{v}\times\vec{B} \right)\;\implies\;\vec{F}\;=\;4\times10^{-6}\times4\times10^{6}\times2\left( \hat{j}\times\hat{k} \right)\;=\;32\,\hat{i}\;\text{N}\;\implies\;x\;=\;32$
questions.topic: Magnetic force on a moving charge

questions.text: A square loop of edge $2\;\text{m}$ carries a current of $2\;\text{A}$ and lies in the $x$-$y$ plane with its edges parallel to the axes [FIGURE]. The magnetic field is $\vec{B}=B_0\left( 1+4x \right)\hat{k}$ with $B_0=5\;\text{T}$. The net magnetic force on the loop is ______ N.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Forces on the two sides parallel to the x-axis cancel, so only the two sides along y contribute. // 📝 Solution: $B\left( x=0 \right)\;=\;B_0\;,\;B\left( x=2 \right)\;=\;9B_0\;\implies\;F_{net}\;=\;i\ell\left( 9B_0-B_0 \right)\;=\;8\,i\,\ell\,B_0\;\implies\;F_{net}\;=\;8\times2\times2\times5\;=\;160\;\text{N}$
questions.topic: Force on a current loop in a non-uniform magnetic field

questions.text: A solenoid of $1200$ turns is wound uniformly in a single layer on a glass tube $2\;m$ long and $0.2\;m$ in diameter. The magnetic intensity at the center of the solenoid when a current of $2\;A$ flows through it is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Magnetic intensity $H\;=\;\frac{B}{\mu_0}\;=\;nI$ // 📝 Solution: $H\;=\;nI\;=\;\left(\frac{1200}{2}\right)\left(2\right)\;=\;1.2\times 10^{3}\;A\,m^{-1}$

questions.text: An electron with kinetic energy $5\;\text{eV}$ enters a region of uniform magnetic field of $3\;\mu\text{T}$ perpendicular to its direction. An electric field $E$ is applied perpendicular to both the velocity and the magnetic field so that the electron moves undeflected. The value of $E$ is ______ $\text{N C}^{-1}$. (Given $m=9\times10^{-31}\;\text{kg}$, $e=1.6\times10^{-19}\;\text{C}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Velocity selector condition qE = qvB with v = √(2KE/m). // 📝 Solution: $v\;=\;\sqrt{\dfrac{2\times5\times1.6\times10^{-19}}{9\times10^{-31}}}\;=\;\dfrac{4}{3}\times10^{6}\;\text{m/s}\;\implies\;E\;=\;vB\;=\;\dfrac{4}{3}\times10^{6}\times3\times10^{-6}\;=\;4\;\text{N C}^{-1}$
questions.topic: Velocity selector (crossed E and B fields)

questions.text: A long conducting wire carrying current $I$ is bent into a circular coil of $N$ turns. It is then bent into a coil of $n$ turns, with the same current $I$. The ratio of the magnetic field at the centre of the coil in the first case to that in the second case is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The wire length is fixed, so R ∝ 1/N, and B = μ0 N I / 2R. // 📝 Solution: $L\;=\;N\left( 2\pi R \right)\;\implies\;R\;=\;\dfrac{L}{2\pi N}\;\implies\;B\;=\;\dfrac{\mu_0 N I}{2R}\;=\;\dfrac{\mu_0 I\pi N^2}{L}\;\implies\;B\;\propto\;N^2\;\implies\;\dfrac{B_1}{B_2}\;=\;\dfrac{N^2}{n^2}$
questions.topic: Magnetic field at the centre of a circular coil (fixed wire length)

questions.text: A long straight conductor with a semicircular arc of radius $\dfrac{\pi}{10}\;\text{m}$ carries a current $I=3\;\text{A}$ as shown in the figure. The magnetic field at the centre $O$ of the arc is: (Take $\mu_0=4\pi\times10^{-7}\;\text{N A}^{-2}$) [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Semicircular arc gives μ0 I / 4R at its centre, and the straight parts contribute nothing at O. // 📝 Solution: $B\;=\;\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4R}\;\implies\;B\;=\;\dfrac{4\pi\times10^{-7}\times3}{4\times\dfrac{\pi}{10}}\;=\;3\times10^{-6}\;\text{T}\;=\;3\;\mu\text{T}$
questions.topic: Magnetic field at the centre of a semicircular arc

questions.text: A uniform magnetic field of $2\times10^{-3}\;\text{T}$ acts along the $+Y$ direction. A rectangular loop of sides $20\;\text{cm}$ and $10\;\text{cm}$ carrying a current of $5\;\text{A}$ lies in the $Y$-$Z$ plane [FIGURE]. The current is anticlockwise with reference to the negative $X$ axis. The torque on the loop is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Torque is τ = M × B with M = iA along the loop normal. // 📝 Solution: $M\;=\;iA\;=\;5\times0.2\times0.1\;=\;0.1\;\text{A m}^2\;\text{along}\;-\hat{i}\;\implies\;\vec{\tau}\;=\;\vec{M}\times\vec{B}\;=\;0.1\left( -\hat{i} \right)\times2\times10^{-3}\,\hat{j}\;=\;2\times10^{-4}\left( -\hat{k} \right)\;\text{N m}$
questions.topic: Torque on a current loop in a uniform magnetic field

questions.text: Match List I with List II. List I (Current configuration): A. [FIGURE] circular loop of radius $r$ touching a long straight wire, with $O$ at the centre of the loop; B. [FIGURE] long wire bent into a semicircle of radius $r$ with two parallel semi-infinite straight arms, $O$ at the centre; C. [FIGURE] circular arc of radius $r$ joined to one semi-infinite straight wire, $O$ at the centre; D. [FIGURE] semicircle of radius $r$ joined to two collinear straight wires, $O$ at the centre. List II (Magnetic field at point $O$): I. $B_0\;=\;\frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r}\left[\pi + 2\right]$ II. $B_0\;=\;\frac{\mu_0}{4}\frac{I}{r}$ III. $B_0\;=\;\frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}\left[\pi - 1\right]$ IV. $B_0\;=\;\frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r}\left[\pi + 1\right]$. Choose the correct answer from the option given below :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Add arc field $\frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r}\theta$ and semi-infinite wire field $\frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r}$ with correct directions // 📝 Solution: A $\implies\;\frac{\mu_0 I}{2r}-\frac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi r}$ (III); B $\implies$ semicircle plus two semi-infinite wires $=\frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r}\left[\pi + 2\right]$ (I); C $\implies$ arc plus one semi-infinite wire $=\frac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi r}\left[\pi + 1\right]$ (IV); D $\implies$ only semicircle $=\frac{\mu_0 I}{4r}$ (II)
questions.topic: Biot-Savart law for arcs and semi-infinite wires

questions.text: An electron is projected with uniform velocity along the axis inside a current-carrying long solenoid. Then:

options.text: the electron will continue to move with uniform velocity along the axis of the solenoid
the electron will be accelerated along the axis
the electron path will be circular about the axis
the electron will experience a force at $45^\circ$ to the axis and hence execute a helical path

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Magnetic force is q(v×B), which vanishes when v is parallel to B. // 📝 Solution: $\vec{v}\;\parallel\;\vec{B}\;\implies\;\vec{F}\;=\;q\left( \vec{v}\times\vec{B} \right)\;=\;0\;\implies\;\text{no force}\;\implies\;\text{uniform velocity along the axis}$
questions.topic: Motion of a charged particle in a solenoid field

questions.text: An element $\Delta\vec{l}=\Delta x\,\hat{i}$ is placed at the origin and carries a large current $I=10\;\text{A}$ [FIGURE]. The magnetic field on the $y$-axis at a distance of $0.5\;\text{m}$ from the element, for $\Delta x=1\;\text{cm}$, is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Biot-Savart law dB = (μ0 / 4π) I Δl sinθ / r². // 📝 Solution: $\theta\;=\;90^\circ\;\implies\;dB\;=\;\dfrac{\mu_0}{4\pi}\dfrac{I\,\Delta x}{r^2}\;=\;\dfrac{10^{-7}\times10\times10^{-2}}{\left( 0.5 \right)^2}\;=\;4\times10^{-8}\;\text{T}$
questions.topic: Biot-Savart law for a current element

questions.text: A single current carrying loop of wire carrying current $I$ flowing in anticlockwise direction seen from $+$ve $z$ direction and lying in $xy$ plane is shown in figure. The plot of $\hat{j}$ component of magnetic field $\left(B_y\right)$ at a distance $a$ (less than radius of the coil) and on $yz$ plane vs $z$ coordinate looks like [FIGURE]

options.text: [FIGURE] Graph of $B_y\left(0,a,z\right)$ vs $z$: flat-topped symmetric curve, always positive
[FIGURE] Graph of $B_y\left(0,a,z\right)$ vs $z$: two symmetric positive humps meeting at a cusp at $z\;=\;0$
[FIGURE] Graph of $B_y\left(0,a,z\right)$ vs $z$: odd curve, negative for $z<0$, zero at $z\;=\;0$, positive for $z>0$, decaying at both ends
[FIGURE] Graph of $B_y\left(0,a,z\right)$ vs $z$: single sharp symmetric peak at $z\;=\;0$ decaying on both sides

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Off-axis field of a loop has a radial component that reverses sign on the two sides of the loop plane // 📝 Solution: $B_y\;=\;0$ in the plane of the coil $\left(z\;=\;0\right)\;\implies$ $B_y$ has opposite signs at $+z$ and $-z$ $\implies$ odd function of $z$ $\implies$ graph (3)
questions.topic: Off-axis magnetic field of a current loop

questions.text: A charge $q$ moving with velocity $\vec{v}$ in an electric field $\vec{E}$ and a magnetic field $\vec{B}$ experiences an electric force $\vec{F}_1$ and a magnetic force $\vec{F}_2$. Which of the following is correct?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Lorentz force is F = qE + q(v×B). // 📝 Solution: $\vec{F}\;=\;q\vec{E}+q\left( \vec{v}\times\vec{B} \right)\;\implies\;\vec{F}_1\;=\;q\vec{E}\;,\;\vec{F}_2\;=\;q\left( \vec{v}\times\vec{B} \right)$
questions.topic: Lorentz force on a moving charge

questions.text: A straight magnetic strip has a magnetic moment of $44\;\text{A m}^2$. If the strip is bent into a semicircular shape, its magnetic moment will be ______ $\text{A m}^2$. (Take $\pi=\dfrac{22}{7}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Magnetic moment is pole strength times the distance between the poles. // 📝 Solution: $M\;=\;m\,\ell\;=\;44\;,\;\ell\;=\;\pi r\;\implies\;M'\;=\;m\left( 2r \right)\;=\;\dfrac{2}{\pi}\,M\;\implies\;M'\;=\;\dfrac{2\times7}{22}\times44\;=\;28\;\text{A m}^2$
questions.topic: Magnetic moment of a bent magnetic strip

questions.text: Every planet revolves around the sun in an elliptical orbit: A. The force acting on a planet is inversely proportional to square of distance from sun. B. Force acting on planet is inversely proportional to product of the masses of the planet and the sun. C. The centripetal force acting on the planet is directed away from the sun. D. The square of time period of revolution of planet around sun is directly proportional to cube of semi-major axis of elliptical orbit. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Newton's law of gravitation and Kepler's third law // 📝 Solution: $F\;=\;\frac{Gm_1m_2}{r^{2}}\implies F\;\propto\;\frac{1}{r^{2}}$ (A true) $\implies F\;\propto\;m_1m_2$, not inverse (B false) $\implies$ force is centripetal, directed towards the sun (C false) $\implies T^{2}\;\propto\;a^{3}$ (D true) $\implies$ A and D only
questions.topic: Kepler's laws and Newton's law of gravitation

questions.text: If the gravitational field in the space is given as $\left(-\frac{K}{r^{2}}\right)$. Taking the reference point to be at $r\;=\;2\;cm$ with gravitational potential $V\;=\;10\;J/kg$. Find the gravitational potential at $r\;=\;3\;cm$ in SI unit (Given, that $K\;=\;6\;J\;cm/kg$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Field $E\;=\;-\frac{dV}{dr}$, so integrate between the two radii // 📝 Solution: $-\frac{dV}{dr}\;=\;-\frac{K}{r^{2}}\implies\int_{10}^{V}dV\;=\;\int_{2}^{3}\frac{K}{r^{2}}dr\implies V\;-\;10\;=\;K\left[\frac{1}{2}\;-\;\frac{1}{3}\right]\;=\;\frac{K}{6}\;=\;1\implies V\;=\;11$

questions.text: Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): The angular speed of the moon in its orbit about the earth is more than the angular speed of the earth in its orbit about the sun. Reason (R): The moon takes less time to move around the earth than the time taken by the earth to move around the sun. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

options.text: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Angular speed $\omega\;=\;\frac{2\pi}{T}\implies\omega\;\propto\;\frac{1}{T}$ // 📝 Solution: $T_{moon}\;=\;27$ days and $T_{earth}\;=\;365$ days $4$ hours $\implies\omega_{moon}\;>\;\omega_{earth}$ $\implies$ A is true and R is true, and R explains A

questions.text: A body weight $W$, is projected vertically upwards from earth's surface to reach a height above the earth which is equal to nine times the radius of earth. The weight of the body at that height will be:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $g'\;=\;\frac{g}{\left(1\;+\;\frac{h}{R}\right)^{2}}$ // 📝 Solution: $h\;=\;9R\implies g'\;=\;\frac{g}{\left(1\;+\;9\right)^{2}}\;=\;\frac{g}{100}\implies W'\;=\;\frac{W}{100}$

questions.text: A metal wire of uniform mass density having length $L$ and mass $M$ is bent to form a semicircular arc and a particle of mass $m$ is placed at the centre of the arc. The gravitational force on the particle by the wire is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Field at the centre of a semicircular arc of linear density $\lambda$ is $\frac{2G\lambda}{R}$ // 📝 Solution: $L\;=\;\pi R\implies R\;=\;\frac{L}{\pi}\implies g_0\;=\;\frac{2G\frac{M}{L}}{R}\;=\;\frac{2GM\pi}{L^{2}}\implies F\;=\;mg_0\;=\;\frac{2GMm\pi}{L^{2}}$ [FIGURE]

questions.text: At a certain depth "d" below surface of earth, value of acceleration due to gravity becomes four times that of its value at a height $3R$ above earth surface. Where $R$ is Radius of earth (Take $R\;=\;6400\;km$). The depth $d$ is equal to
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $g_{depth}\;=\;g\left(1\;-\;\frac{d}{R}\right)$ and $g_{height}\;=\;\frac{GM}{\left(R\;+\;h\right)^{2}}$ // 📝 Solution: $\frac{GM}{R^{2}}\left[1\;-\;\frac{d}{R}\right]\;=\;\frac{4\;GM}{\left(4R\right)^{2}}\implies1\;-\;\frac{d}{R}\;=\;\frac{1}{4}\implies d\;=\;\frac{3}{4}R\;=\;4800\;km$
questions.topic: Variation of g with depth and height

questions.text: Four identical particles of mass $m$ are kept at the four corners of a square. If the gravitational force exerted on one of the masses by the other masses is $\left(\frac{2\sqrt{2}\;+\;1}{32}\right)\frac{Gm^{2}}{L^{2}}$, the length of the sides of the square is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Add two equal perpendicular forces $F$ and the diagonal force $F'$ // 📝 Solution: $F\;=\;\frac{Gm^{2}}{a^{2}}$, $F'\;=\;\frac{Gm^{2}}{2a^{2}}\implies F_{net}\;=\;\sqrt{2}F\;+\;F'\;=\;\frac{Gm^{2}}{a^{2}}\left(\frac{2\sqrt{2}\;+\;1}{2}\right)\;=\;\frac{2\sqrt{2}\;+\;1}{32}\frac{Gm^{2}}{L^{2}}\implies a^{2}\;=\;16L^{2}\implies a\;=\;4L$ [FIGURE]

questions.text: The acceleration due to gravity on the surface of earth is $g$. If the diameter of earth reduces to half of its original value and mass remains constant, then acceleration due to gravity on the surface of earth would be :
If the distance of the earth from Sun is $1.5\;\times\;10^{6}\;km$. Then the distance of an imaginary planet from Sun, if its period of revolution is $2.83$ years is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Kepler's third law $T^{2}\;\propto\;R^{3}$ // 📝 Solution: $\left(\frac{T_1}{T_2}\right)^{2}\;=\;\left(\frac{R_1}{R_2}\right)^{3}\implies\left(\frac{1}{2.83}\right)^{2}\;=\;\left(\frac{1.5\;\times\;10^{6}}{R_2}\right)^{3}\implies R_2\;=\;\left[\left(2.83\right)^{2}\;\times\;\left(1.5\;\times\;10^{6}\right)^{3}\right]^{1/3}\;=\;8^{1/3}\;\times\;1.5\;\times\;10^{6}\;=\;3\;\times\;10^{6}\;km$

questions.text: The acceleration due to gravity at a height equal to the radius of the Earth above its surface is (where $g$ is the value at the surface)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $g' \; = \; \dfrac{g}{\left( 1 \; + \; h/R \right)^2}$. // 📝 Solution: $g' \; = \; \dfrac{g}{\left( 1 \; + \; 1 \right)^2} \; = \; \dfrac{g}{4}$

questions.text: Assume that the earth is a solid sphere of uniform density and a tunnel is dug along its diameter throughout the earth. It is found that when a particle is released in this tunnel, it executes a simple harmonic motion. The mass of the particle is $100\;g$. The time period of the motion of the particle will be (approximately) (take $g\;=\;10\;ms^{-2}$, radius of earth $=\;6400\;km$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Inside the earth $g_{in}\;=\;\frac{GM}{R^{3}}x$ gives SHM with $T\;=\;2\pi\sqrt{\frac{R}{g}}$ // 📝 Solution: $a\;=\;-\frac{GM}{R^{3}}x\implies\omega\;=\;\sqrt{\frac{g}{R}}\implies T\;=\;2\pi\sqrt{\frac{6400\;\times\;10^{3}}{10}}\;=\;2\;\times\;3.14\;\times\;800\;s\;\approx\;5024\;s\;\approx\;1\text{ hour }24\text{ minutes}$ [FIGURE]

questions.text: Initially a satellite of $100\;kg$ is in a circular orbit of radius $1.5R_E$. This satellite can be moved to a circular orbit of radius $3R_E$ by supplying $\alpha\;\times\;10^{6}\;J$ of energy. The value of $\alpha$ is ____. (Take Radius of Earth $R_E\;=\;6\;\times\;10^{6}\;m$ and $g\;=\;10\;m/s^{2}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Total energy of circular orbit $E\;=\;-\frac{GMm}{2r}\;=\;-\frac{gR_E^{2}m}{2r}$ // 📝 Solution: $E_1\;=\;-\frac{gR_Em}{3}$, $E_2\;=\;-\frac{gR_Em}{6}\implies\Delta E\;=\;E_2\;-\;E_1\;=\;\frac{gR_Em}{6}\;=\;\frac{10\;\times\;6\;\times\;10^{6}\;\times\;100}{6}\;=\;10^{9}\;J\;=\;1000\;\times\;10^{6}\;J\implies\alpha\;=\;1000$
questions.topic: Energy for change of satellite orbit

questions.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R. Assertion A: A pendulum clock when taken to Mount Everest becomes fast. Reason R: The value of g (acceleration due to gravity) is less at Mount Everest than its value on the surface of earth. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below

options.text: Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
A is not correct but R is correct
A is correct but R is not correct

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Time period of a pendulum $T\;\propto\;\frac{1}{\sqrt{g}}$ // 📝 Solution: At Mount Everest $g$ is less $\implies T\;\propto\;\frac{1}{\sqrt{g}}$ increases $\implies$ the clock runs slow, not fast $\implies$ A is incorrect and R is correct
questions.topic: Variation of g with height, pendulum clock

questions.text: The escape velocities of two planets A and B are in the ratio $1\;:\;2$. If the ratio of their radii respectively is $1\;:\;3$, then the ratio of acceleration due to gravity of planet A to the acceleration of gravity of planet B will be:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $v_e^{2}\;=\;2gR\implies g\;=\;\frac{v_e^{2}}{2R}$ // 📝 Solution: $\frac{g_A}{g_B}\;=\;\left(\frac{v_A}{v_B}\right)^{2}\frac{R_B}{R_A}\;=\;\frac{1}{4}\;\times\;3\;=\;\frac{3}{4}$

questions.text: Spherical insulating ball and a spherical metallic ball of same size and mass are dropped from the same height. Choose the correct statement out of the following {Assume negligible air friction}

options.text: Time taken by them to reach the earth's surface will be independent of the properties of their materials
Insulating ball will reach the earth's surface earlier than the metal ball
Both will reach the earth's surface simultaneously
Metal ball will reach the earth's surface earlier than the insulating ball.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: A moving conductor in a magnetic field develops eddy currents that oppose its motion // 📝 Solution: Metal ball falls through earth's magnetic field $\implies$ eddy currents are induced $\implies$ they oppose the motion (Lenz's law) $\implies$ the metal ball takes more time $\implies$ the insulating ball reaches earlier

questions.text: A simple pendulum doing small oscillations at a place $R$ height above earth surface has time period of $T_1\;=\;4\;s$. $T_2$ would be it's time period if it is brought to a point which is at a height $2R$ from earth surface. Choose the correct relation [$R\;=\;$ radius of earth] :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $T\;=\;2\pi\sqrt{\frac{\ell}{g'}}$ with $g'\;=\;\frac{GM}{\left(R\;+\;h\right)^{2}}$, so $T\;\propto\;\left(R\;+\;h\right)$ // 📝 Solution: $T_1\;=\;2\pi\sqrt{\frac{\ell}{GM}\left(2R\right)^{2}}$, $T_2\;=\;2\pi\sqrt{\frac{\ell}{GM}\left(3R\right)^{2}}\implies\frac{T_1}{T_2}\;=\;\frac{2}{3}\implies3\,T_1\;=\;2\,T_2$

questions.text: At what distance above and below the surface of the earth a body will have same weight, (take radius of earth as $R$.)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Equate $g_{above}\;=\;\frac{g}{\left(1\;+\;\frac{h}{R}\right)^{2}}$ and $g_{below}\;=\;g\left(1\;-\;\frac{h}{R}\right)$ // 📝 Solution: Let $x\;=\;\frac{h}{R}\implies\left(1\;+\;x\right)^{2}\left(1\;-\;x\right)\;=\;1\implies x\left(1\;-\;x\;-\;x^{2}\right)\;=\;0\implies x^{2}\;+\;x\;-\;1\;=\;0\implies x\;=\;\frac{\sqrt{5}\;-\;1}{2}\implies h\;=\;\frac{\sqrt{5}R\;-\;R}{2}$ [FIGURE]
questions.topic: Variation of g with height and depth

questions.text: The mass of the moon is $1/144$ times the mass of a planet and its diameter $1/16$ times the diameter of a planet. If the escape velocity on the planet is $v$, the escape velocity on the moon will be:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $v_e\;\propto\;\sqrt{\frac{M}{R}}$ // 📝 Solution: $v_{moon}\;=\;\sqrt{\frac{2G\left(\frac{M}{144}\right)}{\frac{R}{16}}}\;=\;\sqrt{\frac{16}{144}}\sqrt{\frac{2GM}{R}}\;=\;\frac{1}{3}v$

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: A satellite is moving around earth in the orbit very close to the earth surface. The time period of revolution of satellite depends upon the density of earth. Statement II: The time period of revolution of the satellite is $T\;=\;2\pi\sqrt{\frac{R_e}{g}}$ (for satellite very close to the earth surface), where $R_e$ radius of earth and $g$ acceleration due to gravity. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Express $g$ in terms of density: $g\;=\;\frac{4}{3}\pi G\rho R_e$ // 📝 Solution: $g\;=\;\frac{GM}{R_e^{2}}\;=\;\frac{4\pi G\rho R_e}{3}\implies T\;=\;2\pi\sqrt{\frac{R_e}{g}}\;=\;2\pi\sqrt{\frac{3}{4\pi G\rho}}\implies T$ depends on $\rho$ $\implies$ both statements are true

questions.text: Match List I with List II : List I: (A) Kinetic energy of planet, (B) Gravitation Potential energy of sun-planet system, (C) Total mechanical energy of planet, (D) Escape energy at the surface of planet for unit mass object. List II: (I) $-\frac{GMm}{a}$, (II) $\frac{GMm}{2a}$, (III) $\frac{Gm}{r}$, (IV) $-\frac{GMm}{2a}$. (Where $a\;=\;$ radius of planet orbit, $r\;=\;$ radius of planet, $M\;=\;$ mass of Sun, $m\;=\;$ mass of planet). Choose the correct answer from the options given below : [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For circular orbits $PE\;=\;-2KE$ and $TE\;=\;-KE$ // 📝 Solution: $KE\;=\;\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}\;=\;\frac{GMm}{2a}$ (II) $\implies PE\;=\;-2KE\;=\;-\frac{GMm}{a}$ (I) $\implies TE\;=\;-KE\;=\;-\frac{GMm}{2a}$ (IV) $\implies$ escape energy per unit mass $=\;\frac{Gm}{r}$ (III)

questions.text: A body of mass $m$ is taken from earth surface to the height $h$ equal to twice the radius of earth ($R_e$), the increase in potential energy will be: ($g\;=\;$ acceleration due to gravity on the surface of Earth)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $U\;=\;-\frac{GM_em}{r}$ and $GM_e\;=\;gR_e^{2}$ // 📝 Solution: $U_i\;=\;-\frac{GM_em}{R_e}$, $U_f\;=\;-\frac{GM_em}{R_e\;+\;2R_e}\;=\;-\frac{GM_em}{3R_e}\implies\Delta U\;=\;U_f\;-\;U_i\;=\;\frac{2}{3}\frac{GM_em}{R_e}\;=\;\frac{2}{3}\frac{GM_e}{R_e^{2}}mR_e\;=\;\frac{2}{3}mgR_e$

questions.text: Three masses $200\;kg,\;300\;kg$ and $400\;kg$ are placed at the vertices of an equilateral triangle with sides $20\;m$. They are rearranged on the vertices of a bigger triangle of side $25\;m$ and with the same centre. The work done in this process ____ $J$. (Gravitational constant $G\;=\;6.7\;\times\;10^{-11}\;N\,m^{2}/kg^{2}$)
For a body projected at an angle with the horizontal from the ground, choose the correct statement.

options.text: Gravitational potential energy is maximum at the highest point.
The horizontal component of velocity is zero at highest point.
The vertical component of momentum is maximum at the highest point.
The kinetic energy (K.E.) is zero at the highest point of projectile motion.

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: At the highest point $v_y\;=\;0$ but $v_x\;=\;u\cos\theta$ is unchanged // 📝 Solution: $v_y\;=\;0$ and $v_x\;=\;u\cos\theta\;\ne\;0$ at the top $\implies$ K.E. is minimum but not zero $\implies$ vertical momentum is zero $\implies U_g\;=\;mgh$ is maximum at $H_{max}$

questions.text: If $R$ is the radius of the earth and the acceleration due to gravity on the surface of earth is $g\;=\;\pi^{2}\;m/s^{2}$, then the length of the second's pendulum at a height $h\;=\;2R$ from the surface of earth will be,:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Second's pendulum has $T\;=\;2\;s$ and $g'\;=\;\frac{g}{\left(1\;+\;\frac{h}{R}\right)^{2}}$ // 📝 Solution: $g'\;=\;\frac{GM_e}{\left(3R\right)^{2}}\;=\;\frac{g}{9}\implies2\;=\;2\pi\sqrt{\frac{9\ell}{g}}\implies\ell\;=\;\frac{g}{9\pi^{2}}\;=\;\frac{1}{9}\;m$

questions.text: In hydrogen like system the ratio of coulombian force and gravitational force between an electron and a proton is in the order of :
To project a body of mass $m$ from earth's surface to infinity, the required kinetic energy is (assume, the radius of earth is $R_E$, $g\;=\;$ acceleration due to gravity on the surface of earth):
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Required KE equals the magnitude of potential energy at the surface // 📝 Solution: $K\;=\;\frac{GMm}{R_E}\;=\;\frac{GM}{R_E^{2}}mR_E\;=\;mgR_E$

questions.text: Two satellite $A$ and $B$ go round a planet in circular orbits having radii $4R$ and $R$ respectively. If the speed of A is $3v$, the speed of B will be :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Orbital speed $v\;=\;\sqrt{\frac{GM}{R}}$ // 📝 Solution: $\frac{v_A}{v_B}\;=\;\sqrt{\frac{R_B}{R_A}}\;=\;\sqrt{\frac{R}{4R}}\;=\;\frac{1}{2}\implies v_B\;=\;2v_A\;=\;6v$

questions.text: An astronaut takes a ball of mass $m$ from earth to space. He throws the ball into a circular orbit about earth at an altitude of $318.5\;km$. From earth's surface to the orbit, the change in total mechanical energy of the ball is $x\frac{GM_em}{21R_e}$. The value of $x$ is (take $R_e\;=\;6370\;km$) :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Orbit energy is $-\frac{GMm}{2r}$ and surface energy is $-\frac{GMm}{R_e}$ // 📝 Solution: $h\;=\;318.5\;\approx\;\frac{R_e}{20}\implies E_i\;=\;-\frac{GM_em}{R_e}$, $E_f\;=\;-\frac{GM_em}{2\left(R_e\;+\;\frac{R_e}{20}\right)}\;=\;-\frac{10\,GM_em}{21R_e}\implies\Delta E\;=\;\frac{GM_em}{R_e}\left[1\;-\;\frac{10}{21}\right]\;=\;\frac{11\,GM_em}{21R_e}\implies x\;=\;11$

questions.text: $T$ is the time period of simple pendulum on the earth's surface. Its time period becomes $x\,T$ when taken to a height $R$ (equal to earth's radius) above the earth's surface. Then, the value of $x$ will be:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $g'\;=\;\frac{g}{\left(1\;+\;\frac{h}{R}\right)^{2}}$ and $T\;=\;2\pi\sqrt{\frac{\ell}{g}}$ // 📝 Solution: $h\;=\;R\implies g'\;=\;\frac{g}{4}\implies xT\;=\;2\pi\sqrt{\frac{\ell}{g/4}}\;=\;2\;\times\;2\pi\sqrt{\frac{\ell}{g}}\;=\;2T\implies x\;=\;2$
questions.topic: Variation of g with height, pendulum

questions.text: The gravitational potential at a point above the surface of earth is $-5.12\;\times\;10^{7}\;J/kg$ and the acceleration due to gravity at that point is $6.4\;m/s^{2}$. Assume that the mean radius of earth to be $6400\;km$. The height of this point above the earth's surface is :
