questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Divide potential by $g$ at the point: $\frac{V}{g}\;=\;-r$ // 📝 Solution: $-\frac{GM_E}{R_E\;+\;h}\;=\;-5.12\;\times\;10^{7}$ and $\frac{GM_E}{\left(R_E\;+\;h\right)^{2}}\;=\;6.4\implies R_E\;+\;h\;=\;\frac{5.12\;\times\;10^{7}}{6.4}\;=\;8\;\times\;10^{6}\;m\implies h\;=\;1.6\;\times\;10^{6}\;m\;=\;1600\;km$

questions.text: The escape velocity from a spherical planet $A$ is $10\;km/s$. The escape velocity from another planet $B$ whose density and radius are $10\%$ of those of planet $A$, is ____ $m/s$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $v_e\;=\;R\sqrt{\frac{8\pi G\rho}{3}}\;\propto\;R\sqrt{\rho}$ // 📝 Solution: $\rho_B\;=\;0.1\rho_A$, $R_B\;=\;0.1R_A\implies\frac{v_B}{v_A}\;=\;0.1\sqrt{0.1}\;=\;\frac{1}{10\sqrt{10}}\implies v_B\;=\;\frac{10}{10\sqrt{10}}\;km/s\;=\;\frac{1000}{\sqrt{10}}\;m/s\;=\;100\sqrt{10}\;m/s$

questions.text: Correct formula for height of a satellite from earths surface is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Gravity provides centripetal force and $GM\;=\;gR^{2}$ // 📝 Solution: $\frac{GM}{\left(R\;+\;h\right)^{2}}\;=\;\left(R\;+\;h\right)\left(\frac{2\pi}{T}\right)^{2}\implies\left(R\;+\;h\right)^{3}\;=\;\frac{gR^{2}T^{2}}{4\pi^{2}}\implies h\;=\;\left(\frac{T^{2}R^{2}g}{4\pi^{2}}\right)^{1/3}\;-\;R$ [FIGURE]

questions.text: A $90\;kg$ body placed at $2R$ distance from surface of earth experiences gravitational pull of : ($R\;=\;$ Radius of earth, $g\;=\;10\;m\,s^{-2}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $g'\;=\;g\left(1\;+\;\frac{h}{R}\right)^{-2}$ // 📝 Solution: $h\;=\;2R\implies g'\;=\;g\left(1\;+\;2\right)^{-2}\;=\;\frac{g}{9}\implies F\;=\;90\;\times\;\frac{10}{9}\;=\;100\;N$

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement-I: Acceleration due to gravity is different at different places on the surface of earth. Statement-II: Acceleration due to gravity increases as we go down below the earth's surface. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Effective $g\;=\;g\;-\;\omega^{2}R_e\sin^{2}\theta$ on the surface, and $g_d\;=\;g\left(1\;-\;\frac{d}{R_e}\right)$ below it // 📝 Solution: Because of rotation and shape of earth, $g$ varies with latitude $\implies$ Statement I is true $\implies g_{d}\;=\;g\left(1\;-\;\frac{d}{R_e}\right)$ decreases with depth $\implies$ Statement II is false

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Acceleration due to earth's gravity decreases as you go 'up' or 'down' from earth's surface. Statement II: Acceleration due to earth's gravity is same at a height 'h' and depth 'd' from earth's surface, if $h\;=\;d$. In the light of above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below

options.text: Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and II are correct

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Compare $g'\;=\;\frac{g}{\left(1\;+\;\frac{h}{R}\right)^{2}}$ above the surface with $g'\;=\;g\left(1\;-\;\frac{d}{R}\right)$ below the surface // 📝 Solution: $g$ is maximum at the surface and decreases both above and below it $\implies$ Statement I is correct $\implies$ for small $h$, $g_{h}\;\approx\;g\left(1\;-\;\frac{2h}{R}\right)\;\ne\;g\left(1\;-\;\frac{d}{R}\right)$ at $h\;=\;d$ $\implies$ Statement II is incorrect
questions.topic: Variation of g with height and depth

questions.text: A planet has mass $9$ times that of the Earth and the same radius. The ratio $\dfrac{g_{planet}}{g_{earth}}$ is ______.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $g \; = \; \dfrac{GM}{R^2}$. // 📝 Solution: $\dfrac{g_p}{g_e} \; = \; \dfrac{M_p}{M_e} \cdot \dfrac{R_e^2}{R_p^2} \; = \; 9 \cdot 1 \; = \; 9$
questions.topic: Acceleration due to gravity of a planet

questions.text: A light planet is revolving around a massive star in a circular orbit of radius $R$ with a period of revolution $T$. If the force of attraction between planet and star is proportional to $R^{-3/2}$ then choose the correct option :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Force provides centripetal force $m\omega^{2}R$ // 📝 Solution: $F\;=\;\frac{GMm}{R^{3/2}}\;=\;m\omega^{2}R\implies\omega^{2}\;\propto\;\frac{1}{R^{5/2}}\implies T^{2}\;=\;\frac{4\pi^{2}}{\omega^{2}}\;\propto\;R^{5/2}$

questions.text: Two planets $A$ and $B$ having masses $m_1$ and $m_2$ move around the sun in circular orbits of $r_1$ and $r_2$ radii respectively. If angular momentum of $A$ is $L$ and that of $B$ is $3\,L$, the ratio of time period $\left(\frac{T_A}{T_B}\right)$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Angular momentum $L\;=\;mr^{2}\frac{2\pi}{T}$ combined with Kepler's law $T^{2}\;\propto\;r^{3}$ // 📝 Solution: $\frac{\pi r_1^{2}}{T_A}\;=\;\frac{L}{2m_1}$, $\frac{\pi r_2^{2}}{T_B}\;=\;\frac{3L}{2m_2}\implies\frac{T_A}{T_B}\;=\;3\;\frac{m_1}{m_2}\left(\frac{r_1}{r_2}\right)^{2}$ $\implies\left(\frac{r_1}{r_2}\right)^{2}\;=\;\left(\frac{T_A}{T_B}\right)^{4/3}\implies\frac{T_A}{T_B}\;=\;\frac{1}{27}\left(\frac{m_2}{m_1}\right)^{3}$

questions.text: Two particles of equal mass 'm' move in a circle of radius 'r' under the action of their mutual gravitational attraction. The speed of each particle will be: (Here $M$ in the options denotes the mass $m$ of each particle)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The particles are diametrically opposite, so separation is $2r$ and mutual force gives the centripetal force // 📝 Solution: $\frac{Gm^{2}}{\left(2r\right)^{2}}\;=\;\frac{mv^{2}}{r}\implies v^{2}\;=\;\frac{Gm}{4r}\implies v\;=\;\sqrt{\frac{Gm}{4r}}$ [FIGURE]

questions.text: A satellite revolving around a planet in stationary orbit has time period $6$ hours. The mass of planet is one-fourth the mass of earth. The radius orbit of planet is : (Given $=$ Radius of geo-stationary orbit for earth is $4.2\;\times\;10^{4}\;km$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $T\;=\;\frac{2\pi r^{3/2}}{\sqrt{GM}}$ // 📝 Solution: $\frac{T_1}{T_2}\;=\;\left(\frac{r_1}{r_2}\right)^{3/2}\left(\frac{M_2}{M_1}\right)^{1/2}\implies\frac{6}{24}\;=\;\frac{\left(r_1\right)^{3/2}}{\left(4.2\;\times\;10^{4}\right)^{3/2}}\left(\frac{M}{M/4}\right)^{1/2}\implies r_1\;=\;1.05\;\times\;10^{4}\;km$

questions.text: Net gravitational force at the center of a square is found to be $F_1$ when four particles having mass $M,\;2M,\;3M$ and $4M$ are placed at the four corners of the square as shown in figure and it is $F_2$ when the positions of $3M$ and $4M$ are interchanged. The ratio $\frac{F_1}{F_2}$ is $\frac{\alpha}{\sqrt{5}}$. The value of $\alpha$ is ____. [FIGURE: square with $4M$ at top-left, $3M$ at top-right, $M$ at bottom-left, $2M$ at bottom-right]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Resolve the field of each mass along the two axes, with equal distance $r$ from the centre // 📝 Solution: Take $k\;=\;\frac{G}{r^{2}}$, positions $4M\;(-,+)$, $3M\;(+,+)$, $M\;(-,-)$, $2M\;(+,-)$ $\implies g_x\;=\;k\left(-4M\;+\;3M\;-\;M\;+\;2M\right)\;=\;0$, $g_y\;=\;k\left(4M\;+\;3M\;-\;M\;-\;2M\right)\;=\;4kM\implies F_1\;=\;4kM$ $\implies$ after swapping $g_x\;=\;k\left(-3M\;+\;4M\;-\;M\;+\;2M\right)\;=\;2kM$, $g_y\;=\;k\left(3M\;+\;4M\;-\;M\;-\;2M\right)\;=\;4kM\implies F_2\;=\;kM\sqrt{4\;+\;16}\;=\;2\sqrt{5}\,kM\implies\frac{F_1}{F_2}\;=\;\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}}\implies\alpha\;=\;2$

questions.text: The weight of a body at the surface of earth is $18\;N$. The weight of the body at an altitude of $3200\;km$ above the earth's surface is (given, radius of earth $R_e\;=\;6400\;km$)

A satellite of $10^{3}\;kg$ mass is revolving in circular orbit of radius $2R$. If $\frac{10^{4}R}{6}\;J$ energy is supplied to the satellite, it would revolve in a new circular orbit of radius (use $g\;=\;10\;m/s^{2}$, $R\;=\;$ radius of earth)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Total energy of a circular orbit is $-\frac{GMm}{2r}$ with $GM\;=\;gR^{2}$ // 📝 Solution: $-\frac{GMm}{4R}\;+\;\frac{10^{4}R}{6}\;=\;-\frac{GMm}{2r}\implies-\frac{10^{3}\;\times\;10\;\times\;R}{4}\;+\;\frac{10^{4}R}{6}\;=\;-\frac{10^{3}\;\times\;10\;\times\;R^{2}}{2r}\implies-\frac{1}{4}\;+\;\frac{1}{6}\;=\;-\frac{R}{2r}\implies r\;=\;6R$ [FIGURE]
questions.topic: Change of satellite orbit and energy

questions.text: A planet takes $200$ days to complete one revolution around the Sun. If the distance of the planet from Sun is reduced to one fourth of the original distance, how many days will it take to complete one revolution?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Kepler's third law $T^{2}\;\propto\;r^{3}$ // 📝 Solution: $\frac{\left(200\right)^{2}}{r^{3}}\;=\;\frac{T_2^{2}}{\left(\frac{r}{4}\right)^{3}}\implies T_2^{2}\;=\;\frac{200\;\times\;200}{4\;\times\;4\;\times\;4}\implies T_2\;=\;\frac{200}{8}\;=\;25$ days

questions.text: Escape velocity of a body from earth is $11.2\;km/s$. If the radius of a planet be one-third the radius of earth and mass be one-sixth that of earth, the escape velocity from the plate is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $v_e\;=\;\sqrt{\frac{2GM}{R}}$ // 📝 Solution: $R_P\;=\;\frac{R_E}{3}$, $M_P\;=\;\frac{M_E}{6}\implies\frac{v_e}{v_P}\;=\;\sqrt{2}\implies v_P\;=\;\frac{11.2}{\sqrt{2}}\;\approx\;7.9\;km/s$

questions.text: If earth has a mass nine times and radius twice to the of a planet $P$. Then $\frac{v_e}{3}\sqrt{x}\;ms^{-1}$ will be the minimum velocity required by a rocket to pull out of gravitational force of $P$, where $v_e$ is escape velocity on earth. The value of $x$ is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $v_{esc}\;=\;\sqrt{\frac{2GM}{R}}$ // 📝 Solution: $v_P\;=\;\sqrt{\frac{2G\left(\frac{M_e}{9}\right)}{\left(\frac{R_e}{2}\right)}}\;=\;\sqrt{\frac{2}{9}}\sqrt{\frac{2GM_e}{R_e}}\;=\;\frac{v_e\sqrt{2}}{3}\implies x\;=\;2$

questions.text: The ratio of the escape velocity to the orbital velocity of a satellite revolving close to the Earth's surface is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Compare $v_e \; = \; \sqrt{2gR}$ and $v_o \; = \; \sqrt{gR}$. // 📝 Solution: $\dfrac{v_e}{v_o} \; = \; \dfrac{\sqrt{2gR}}{\sqrt{gR}} \; = \; \sqrt{2}$

questions.text: The time period of a satellite of earth is $24$ hours. If the separation between the earth and the satellite is decreased to one fourth of the previous value, then its new time period will become.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Kepler's third law $T^{2}\;\propto\;R^{3}$ // 📝 Solution: $\left(\frac{T_1}{T_2}\right)^{2}\;=\;\left(\frac{R}{R/4}\right)^{3}\;=\;64\implies T_2\;=\;\frac{24}{8}\;=\;3$ hours

questions.text: Assuming the earth to be a sphere of uniform mass density, a body weighed $300\;N$ on the surface of earth. How much it would weigh at $R/4$ depth under surface of earth ?
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $g_d\;=\;g\left(1\;-\;\frac{d}{R}\right)$ // 📝 Solution: $g_d\;=\;g\left(1\;-\;\frac{R}{4R}\right)\;=\;\frac{3g}{4}\implies W_d\;=\;\frac{3}{4}\;\times\;300\;=\;225\;N$

questions.text: Given below are two statements. Assertion (A): The property of a body by virtue of which it tends to regain its original shape when the external force is removed is elasticity. Reason (R): The restoring force depends upon the bonded inter-atomic and inter-molecular forces of solids. Choose the correct answer.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Elasticity is the tendency to regain shape; restoring force arises from interatomic bonds. // 📝 Solution: Definition of elasticity is correct $\implies$ A true; restoring force due to interatomic/intermolecular bonds explains elasticity $\implies$ R true and correct explanation $\implies$ Option C.

questions.text: Each of three blocks $P$, $Q$ and $R$ shown in the figure has a mass of $3\;\text{kg}$. Each of wires $A$ and $B$ has cross-sectional area $0.005\;\text{cm}^{2}$ and Young's modulus $2\;\times\;10^{11}\;\text{N}\,\text{m}^{-2}$. Neglecting friction, the longitudinal strain in wire $B$ is ____ $\times\;10^{-4}$. (Take $g\;=\;10\;\text{m}\,\text{s}^{-2}$) [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Treat $P$, $Q$, $R$ as one system and apply Newton's law to block $R$ for wire $B$ tension. // 📝 Solution: $a\;=\;\frac{m_{R}g}{3m}\;=\;\frac{30}{9}\;=\;\frac{10}{3}\;\text{m/s}^{2}\;\implies\;30-T_{B}\;=\;3a\;\implies\;T_{B}\;=\;20\;\text{N}$; $\epsilon_{B}\;=\;\frac{T_{B}}{AY}\;=\;\frac{20}{5\times10^{-7}\times2\times10^{11}}\;=\;2\times10^{-4}$
questions.topic: Strain in wire with connected blocks

questions.text: Two persons pull a wire towards themselves. Each person exerts a force of $200\;\text{N}$ on the wire. Young's modulus of the wire is $1\;\times\;10^{11}\;\text{N}\,\text{m}^{-2}$. Original length of the wire is $2\;\text{m}$ and area of cross-section is $2\;\text{cm}^{2}$. The wire will extend in length by ____ $\mu\text{m}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\Delta\ell\;=\;\frac{F\ell}{AY}$ where $F$ is the force from one person. // 📝 Solution: $A\;=\;2\;\text{cm}^{2}\;=\;2\times10^{-4}\;\text{m}^{2}\;\implies\;\Delta\ell\;=\;\frac{200\times2}{2\times10^{-4}\times10^{11}}\;=\;2\times10^{-5}\;\text{m}\;=\;20\;\mu\text{m}$
questions.topic: Elongation of wire under pulling forces

questions.text: An elastic spring under tension of $3\;\text{N}$ has a length $a$. Its length is $b$ under tension $2\;\text{N}$. For its length $(3a-2b)$, the value of tension will be ____ N.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Hooke's law $T\;=\;K\left(L-\ell\right)$ where $\ell$ is the natural length. // 📝 Solution: $3\;=\;K\left(a-\ell\right)$ and $2\;=\;K\left(b-\ell\right)\;\implies\;T\;=\;K\left(3a-2b-\ell\right)\;=\;3K\left(a-\ell\right)-2K\left(b-\ell\right)\;=\;9-4\;=\;5\;\text{N}$

questions.text: A thin rod of length $1\;\text{m}$ and cross-sectional area $3\;\times\;10^{-6}\;\text{m}^{2}$ is suspended vertically from one end. It is cooled from $210^\circ\text{C}$ to $160^\circ\text{C}$. A mass $M$ is then attached at the lower end so that the length again becomes $1\;\text{m}$. Given $Y\;=\;2\;\times\;10^{11}\;\text{N}\,\text{m}^{-2}$ and $\alpha\;=\;2\;\times\;10^{-5}\;\text{K}^{-1}$. The value of $M$ is ____ kg. (Take $g\;=\;10\;\text{m}\,\text{s}^{-2}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Thermal contraction $\ell\alpha\Delta T$ must be undone by mechanical stretch $\frac{Mg\,\ell}{AY}$. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta\ell\;=\;1\times2\times10^{-5}\times50\;=\;10^{-3}\;\text{m}\;\implies\;Mg\;=\;\frac{YA\,\Delta\ell}{\ell}\;=\;2\times10^{11}\times3\times10^{-6}\times10^{-3}\;=\;6\times10^{2}\;\text{N}\;\implies\;M\;=\;60\;\text{kg}$

questions.text: A force is applied to a steel wire $A$, rigidly clamped at one end. The elongation in the wire is $0.2\;\text{mm}$. The same force is applied to another steel wire $B$ of double the length and a diameter $2.4$ times that of wire $A$. The elongation in wire $B$ will be (uniform circular cross sections):
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $\Delta\ell\;=\;\frac{F\ell}{AY}$ with $A\;\propto\;d^{2}$. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta\ell\;\propto\;\frac{\ell}{d^{2}}\;\implies\;\Delta\ell_{B}\;=\;0.2\;\times\;\frac{2}{(2.4)^{2}}\;=\;\frac{0.4}{5.76}\;\implies\;\Delta\ell_{B}\;=\;6.9\;\times\;10^{-2}\;\text{mm}$
questions.topic: Elongation ratio with length and diameter

questions.text: In an experiment to determine Young's modulus of a wire, the extension-load curve is a straight line through the origin making an angle of $45^\circ$ with the load axis. The length of wire is $62.8\;\text{cm}$ and its diameter is $4\;\text{mm}$. The Young's modulus is $x\;\times\;10^{4}\;\text{N}\,\text{m}^{-2}$. The value of $x$ is ____. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $Y\;=\;\frac{FL}{A\,\Delta L}$ and the graph slope gives $\frac{\Delta L}{F}$. // 📝 Solution: $\tan45^\circ\;=\;\frac{\Delta L}{F}\;=\;1\;\implies\;Y\;=\;\frac{L}{A}\;=\;\frac{0.628}{\pi\left(2\times10^{-3}\right)^{2}}\;=\;5\times10^{4}\;\implies\;x\;=\;5$

questions.text: Assertion A: Steel is used in the construction of buildings and bridges. Reason R: Steel is more elastic and its elastic limit is high. Choose the most appropriate answer.

options.text: Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is not correct but R is correct
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
A is correct but R is not correct

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Consider the high tensile strength and elastic limit of steel under heavy loads. // 📝 Solution: Steel has high strength and large elastic limit $\implies$ it withstands heavy loads without permanent deformation $\implies$ R is true and explains A $\implies$ Option C.

questions.text: The density and breaking stress of a wire are $6\;\times\;10^{4}\;\text{kg}\,\text{m}^{-3}$ and $1.2\;\times\;10^{8}\;\text{N}\,\text{m}^{-2}$. The wire is suspended from a rigid support on a planet where $g$ is $\frac{1}{3}$ of its value on earth. The maximum length of the wire without breaking is ____ m (take $g\;=\;10\;\text{m}\,\text{s}^{-2}$).
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Stress at the top of a hanging wire equals $\rho\,\ell\,g_{p}$. // 📝 Solution: $\sigma\;=\;\rho\,\ell\,g_{p}\;\implies\;\ell\;=\;\frac{\sigma}{\rho\,g_{p}}\;=\;\frac{1.2\times10^{8}}{6\times10^{4}\times\frac{10}{3}}\;=\;\frac{3.6\times10^{8}}{6\times10^{5}}\;=\;600\;\text{m}$

questions.text: One end of a metal wire is fixed to a ceiling and a load of $2\;\text{kg}$ hangs from the other end. A similar wire is attached to the bottom of the load and another load of $1\;\text{kg}$ hangs from this lower wire. The ratio of longitudinal strain of upper wire to that of the lower wire will be ____. [Area of cross-section $=0.005\;\text{cm}^{2}$, $Y\;=\;2\;\times\;10^{11}\;\text{N}\,\text{m}^{-2}$, $g\;=\;10\;\text{m}\,\text{s}^{-2}$]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Strain $=\frac{F}{AY}$, so for identical wires strain is proportional to tension. // 📝 Solution: $T_{\text{upper}}\;=\;(2+1)\times10\;=\;30\;\text{N}$, $T_{\text{lower}}\;=\;1\times10\;=\;10\;\text{N}\;\implies\;\frac{\epsilon_{\text{upper}}}{\epsilon_{\text{lower}}}\;=\;\frac{30}{10}\;=\;3$

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (A) A force that restores an elastic body of unit area to its original state; (B) Two equal and opposite forces parallel to opposite faces; (C) Forces perpendicular everywhere to the surface per unit area, same everywhere; (D) Two equal and opposite forces perpendicular to opposite faces. List-II: (I) Bulk modulus; (II) Young's modulus; (III) Stress; (IV) Shear modulus. Choose the correct answer.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Link each definition to its type of stress and corresponding modulus. // 📝 Solution: (A) restoring force per unit area $\implies$ Stress (III); (B) tangential forces $\implies$ Shear modulus (IV); (C) uniform normal force per area $\implies$ Bulk modulus (I); (D) longitudinal forces $\implies$ Young's modulus (II) $\implies$ Option B.
questions.topic: Types of stress and elastic moduli

questions.text: The depth below the surface of sea to which a rubber ball must be taken so as to decrease its volume by $0.02\%$ is ____ m. (Take density of sea water $=10^{3}\;\text{kg}\,\text{m}^{-3}$, bulk modulus of rubber $=9\;\times\;10^{8}\;\text{N}\,\text{m}^{-2}$, $g\;=\;10\;\text{m}\,\text{s}^{-2}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $B\;=\;\frac{\Delta P}{\Delta V/V}$ with $\Delta P\;=\;\rho g h$. // 📝 Solution: $h\;=\;\frac{B\,(\Delta V/V)}{\rho g}\;=\;\frac{9\times10^{8}\times2\times10^{-4}}{10^{3}\times10}\;=\;\frac{1.8\times10^{5}}{10^{4}}\;=\;18\;\text{m}$
questions.topic: Bulk modulus and depth in sea

questions.text: Under the same load, wire $A$ of length $5.0\;\text{m}$ and cross-section $2.5\;\times\;10^{-5}\;\text{m}^{2}$ stretches uniformly by the same amount as wire $B$ of length $6.0\;\text{m}$ and cross-section $3.0\;\times\;10^{-5}\;\text{m}^{2}$. The ratio of the Young's modulus of $A$ to that of $B$ is:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $Y\;=\;\frac{FL}{A\,\Delta\ell}$ with $F$ and $\Delta\ell$ same for both wires. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{Y_{A}}{Y_{B}}\;=\;\frac{L_{A}}{A_{A}}\times\frac{A_{B}}{L_{B}}\;=\;\frac{5.0\times3.0\times10^{-5}}{2.5\times10^{-5}\times6.0}\;=\;\frac{15}{15}\;=\;1$
questions.topic: Ratio of Young's modulus from identical loading

questions.text: Two blocks of mass $2\;\text{kg}$ and $4\;\text{kg}$ are connected by a metal wire going over a smooth pulley as shown in the figure. The radius of the wire is $4.0\;\times\;10^{-5}\;\text{m}$ and Young's modulus is $2.0\;\times\;10^{11}\;\text{N}\,\text{m}^{-2}$. The longitudinal strain in the wire is $\frac{1}{\alpha\pi}$. The value of $\alpha$ is ____. (Use $g\;=\;10\;\text{m}\,\text{s}^{-2}$) [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Tension in an Atwood-type system is $T\;=\;\frac{2m_{1}m_{2}g}{m_{1}+m_{2}}$ and strain is $\frac{T}{AY}$. // 📝 Solution: $T\;=\;\frac{2\times2\times4\times10}{6}\;=\;\frac{80}{3}\;\text{N}$; $A\;=\;\pi r^{2}\;=\;16\pi\times10^{-10}\;\text{m}^{2}\;\implies\;\epsilon\;=\;\frac{T}{AY}\;=\;\frac{80/3}{320\pi}\;=\;\frac{1}{12\pi}\;\implies\;\alpha\;=\;12$

questions.text: The strain-stress plot for materials $A$, $B$, $C$ and $D$ is shown in the figure. Which material has the largest Young's modulus? [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Young's modulus is the reciprocal of the slope of the strain-stress graph. // 📝 Solution: $\text{slope}\;=\;\frac{\epsilon}{\sigma}\;=\;\frac{1}{Y}\;\implies\;$ smallest slope gives largest $Y$ $\implies$ material $C$ (flattest line) has the largest Young's modulus.

questions.text: Two wires $A$ and $B$ of different materials, lengths $6.0\;\text{cm}$ and $5.4\;\text{cm}$ and cross-sectional areas $3.0\;\times\;10^{-5}\;\text{m}^{2}$ and $4.5\;\times\;10^{-5}\;\text{m}^{2}$ respectively, are stretched by the same magnitude under a given load. The ratio of Young's modulus of $A$ to that of $B$ is $x:3$. The value of $x$ is ____.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For same $F$ and $\Delta L$, $Y\;=\;\frac{FL}{A\,\Delta L}\;\propto\;\frac{L}{A}$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{Y_{A}}{Y_{B}}\;=\;\frac{L_{A}}{A_{A}}\times\frac{A_{B}}{L_{B}}\;=\;\frac{6.0}{3.0\times10^{-5}}\times\frac{4.5\times10^{-5}}{5.4}\;=\;\frac{5}{3}\;\implies\;x:3\;=\;5:3\;\implies\;x\;=\;5$
questions.topic: Ratio of Young's moduli from wire dimensions

questions.text: A wire of length $L$ and radius $r$ is clamped at one end. If its other end is pulled by a force $F$, its length increases by $l$. If the radius and the applied force are both reduced to half of their original values, keeping the original length constant, the increase in length will become:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Extension $\Delta\ell\;=\;\frac{FL}{\pi r^{2}Y}$. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta\ell'\;=\;\frac{(F/2)\,L}{\pi(r/2)^{2}Y}\;=\;\frac{FL}{2}\cdot\frac{4}{\pi r^{2}Y}\;=\;2\,\Delta\ell\;\implies\;$ Option D.
questions.topic: Elongation dependence on radius and force

questions.text: If the average depth of an ocean is $4000\;\text{m}$ and the bulk modulus of water is $2\;\times\;10^{9}\;\text{N}\,\text{m}^{-2}$, then the fractional compression $\frac{\Delta V}{V}$ of water at the bottom is $\alpha\;\times\;10^{-2}$. The value of $\alpha$ is ____. (Given $g\;=\;10\;\text{m}\,\text{s}^{-2}$, $\rho\;=\;1000\;\text{kg}\,\text{m}^{-3}$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $B\;=\;\frac{\Delta P}{\Delta V/V}$ with $\Delta P\;=\;\rho g h$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{\Delta V}{V}\;=\;\frac{\rho g h}{B}\;=\;\frac{1000\times10\times4000}{2\times10^{9}}\;=\;2\times10^{-2}\;\implies\;\alpha\;=\;2$

questions.text: Two metallic wires $P$ and $Q$ have the same volume and are made of the same material. Their areas of cross-section are in the ratio $4:1$. Force $F_{1}$ applied to $P$ produces an extension $\Delta\ell$. The force $F_{2}$ required to produce the same extension in $Q$ gives $\frac{F_{1}}{F_{2}}$ equal to ____.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For equal volume, $\ell\;=\;\frac{V}{A}$ so extension depends on $A^{2}$. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta\ell\;=\;\frac{F\ell}{AY}\;=\;\frac{FV}{A^{2}Y}\;\implies\;\frac{F_{1}}{A_{P}^{2}}\;=\;\frac{F_{2}}{A_{Q}^{2}}\;\implies\;\frac{F_{1}}{F_{2}}\;=\;\left(\frac{4}{1}\right)^{2}\;=\;16$
questions.topic: Extension of wires of equal volume

questions.text: The Young's modulus of a steel wire of length $6\;\text{m}$ and cross-sectional area $3\;\text{mm}^{2}$ is $2\;\times\;10^{11}\;\text{N}\,\text{m}^{-2}$. The wire is suspended from its support on a planet where $g$ is $\frac{1}{4}$ of its value on earth. A block of mass $4\;\text{kg}$ is attached to the free end. The elongation of the wire is (take $g$ on earth $=10\;\text{m}\,\text{s}^{-2}$):
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Weight on the planet is $mg_{p}$ and elongation is $\frac{F\ell}{AY}$. // 📝 Solution: $g_{p}\;=\;\frac{10}{4}\;=\;2.5\;\text{m/s}^{2}\;\implies\;F\;=\;4\times2.5\;=\;10\;\text{N}\;\implies\;\Delta\ell\;=\;\frac{10\times6}{3\times10^{-6}\times2\times10^{11}}\;=\;10^{-4}\;\text{m}\;=\;0.1\;\text{mm}$

questions.text: Choose the correct relationship between Poisson ratio $\sigma$, bulk modulus $K$ and modulus of rigidity $\eta$ of a given solid object.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $Y\;=\;3K\left(1-2\sigma\right)\;=\;2\eta\left(1+\sigma\right)$. // 📝 Solution: $3K\left(1-2\sigma\right)\;=\;2\eta\left(1+\sigma\right)\;\implies\;3K-6K\sigma\;=\;2\eta+2\eta\sigma\;\implies\;\sigma\;=\;\frac{3K-2\eta}{6K+2\eta}$
questions.topic: Relation among elastic moduli and Poisson ratio

questions.text: A wire of cross-sectional area $A$, modulus of elasticity $2\;\times\;10^{11}\;\text{N}\,\text{m}^{-2}$ and length $2\;\text{m}$ is stretched between two vertical rigid supports. A mass $2\;\text{kg}$ is suspended at the middle, and it sags making angle $\theta\;=\;\frac{1}{100}\;\text{rad}$ at the supports. The value of $A$ is ____ $\times\;10^{-4}\;\text{m}^{2}$ (consider $x\;\ll\;L$, $g\;=\;10\;\text{m}\,\text{s}^{-2}$). [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use vertical equilibrium $2T\sin\theta\;=\;mg$ and $\Delta\ell\;\approx\;\frac{x^{2}}{L}$. // 📝 Solution: $2T\sin\theta\;=\;20$ with $\sin\theta\approx\theta\;\implies\;T\;=\;\frac{10}{\theta}\;=\;1000\;\text{N}$; $\Delta\ell\;=\;2\sqrt{x^{2}+L^{2}}-2L\;\approx\;\frac{x^{2}}{L}\;\implies\;Y\;=\;\frac{T/A}{\Delta\ell/2L}\;=\;\frac{2000\,L^{2}}{A\,x^{2}}$; with $x\;=\;L\theta\;=\;\frac{L}{100}$: $2\times10^{11}\;=\;\frac{2\times10^{7}}{A}\;\implies\;A\;=\;1\times10^{-4}\;\text{m}^{2}$

questions.text: A certain pressure $P$ is applied to $1$ litre of water and $2$ litre of a liquid separately. Water is compressed by $0.01\%$ whereas the liquid is compressed by $0.03\%$. The ratio of bulk modulus of water to that of the liquid is $\frac{3}{x}$. The value of $x$ is ____.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Bulk modulus $B\;=\;\frac{\Delta P}{\Delta V/V}$ with the same $\Delta P$ for both liquids. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{B_{w}}{B_{l}}\;=\;\frac{0.03}{0.01}\;=\;3\;\implies\;\frac{3}{x}\;=\;3\;\implies\;x\;=\;1$

questions.text: For a solid rod, the Young's modulus of elasticity is $3.2\;\times\;10^{11}\;\text{N}\,\text{m}^{-2}$ and density is $8\;\times\;10^{3}\;\text{kg}\,\text{m}^{-3}$. The velocity of longitudinal wave in the rod will be:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Speed of longitudinal waves in a solid rod is $v\;=\;\sqrt{\frac{Y}{\rho}}$. // 📝 Solution: $v\;=\;\sqrt{\frac{3.2\;\times\;10^{11}}{8\;\times\;10^{3}}}\;=\;\sqrt{4\;\times\;10^{7}}\;\implies\;v\;\approx\;6.32\;\times\;10^{3}\;\text{m/s}$

questions.text: Which of the following best describes the effect of temperature on the Young's modulus of elasticity? With rise in temperature, the Young's modulus of elasticity:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Think about how increasing thermal agitation affects interatomic bonding strength. // 📝 Solution: With rise in temperature, interatomic bonds weaken and atoms vibrate more $\implies$ Young's modulus decreases $\implies$ Option B.

questions.text: A $100\;\text{m}$ long wire having cross-sectional area $6.25\;\times\;10^{-4}\;\text{m}^{2}$ and Young's modulus $10^{10}\;\text{N}\,\text{m}^{-2}$ is subjected to a load of $250\;\text{N}$. The elongation in the wire will be:
questions.topic: Elongation of wire under load (Young's modulus)

questions.text: Two bodies of mass $4\;\text{g}$ and $25\;\text{g}$ are moving with equal kinetic energies. The ratio of magnitude of their linear momentum is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For equal kinetic energy, momentum is $p\;=\;\sqrt{2mK}\;\propto\;\sqrt{m}$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{p_1}{p_2}\;=\;\sqrt{\frac{m_1}{m_2}}\;=\;\sqrt{\frac{4}{25}}\;=\;\frac{2}{5}$

questions.text: A body of mass $2\;\text{kg}$ is initially at rest. It starts moving unidirectionally under the influence of a source of constant power $P$. Its displacement in $4\;\text{s}$ is $\frac{1}{3}\alpha^2\sqrt{P}\;\text{m}$. The value of $\alpha$ will be ......
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Constant power gives $\frac{1}{2}mv^2\;=\;Pt$, then integrate the speed to get displacement. // 📝 Solution: $v\;=\;\sqrt{\frac{2Pt}{m}}\;=\;\sqrt{Pt}\implies x\;=\;\sqrt{P}\cdot\frac{2}{3}\left[t^{3/2}\right]_0^4\;=\;\frac{16\sqrt{P}}{3}\implies\alpha^2\;=\;16\implies\alpha\;=\;4$

questions.text: A body is moving unidirectionally under the influence of a constant power source. Its displacement in time $t$ is proportional to :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Constant power means $P\;=\;Fv\;=\;mv\frac{dv}{dt}\;=\;\text{constant}$. // 📝 Solution: $\int_0^v v\,dv\;=\;C\int_0^t dt\implies v\;\propto\;t^{1/2}\implies\frac{ds}{dt}\;\propto\;t^{1/2}\implies s\;\propto\;t^{3/2}$

questions.text: A particle of mass $m$ moves on a straight line with its velocity increasing with distance according to the equation $v\;=\;\alpha\sqrt{x}$, where $\alpha$ is a constant. The total work done by all the forces applied on the particle during its displacement from $x\;=\;0$ to $x\;=\;d$, will be :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Total work done equals the change in kinetic energy. // 📝 Solution: $W\;=\;K_f\;-\;K_i\;=\;\frac{1}{2}m\left(\alpha\sqrt{d}\right)^2\;-\;0\implies W\;=\;\frac{m\alpha^2 d}{2}$

questions.text: Given below are two statements : Statement I: An object moves from position $r_1$ to position $r_2$ under a conservative force field $\vec{F}$. The work done by the force is $W\;=\;-\int_{r_1}^{r_2}\vec{F}\cdot d\vec{r}$. Statement II: Any object moving from one location to another location can follow infinite number of paths. Therefore, the amount of work done by the object changes with the path it follows for a conservative force. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true

questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Work done by a force is $\int\vec{F}\cdot d\vec{r}$, and for a conservative force it is path independent. // 📝 Solution: $W\;=\;+\int\vec{F}\cdot d\vec{r}$ while $\Delta U\;=\;-\int\vec{F}\cdot d\vec{r}\implies$ Statement I is false $\implies$ conservative force work is path independent $\implies$ Statement II is false

questions.text: A spherical body of mass $2\;\text{kg}$ starting from rest acquires a kinetic energy of $10000\;\text{J}$ at the end of $5^{th}$ second. The force acted on the body is ____ N.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Get the final speed from the kinetic energy, then use $v\;=\;at$ and $F\;=\;ma$. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{1}{2}\left(2\right)v^2\;=\;10000\implies v\;=\;100\implies a\;=\;\frac{100}{5}\;=\;20\implies F\;=\;ma\;=\;2\times 20\;=\;40\;\text{N}$
questions.topic: Kinetic Energy and Newton's Second Law

questions.text: In case of vertical circular motion of a particle by a thread of length $r$ if the tension in the thread is zero at an angle $30^\circ$ shown in figure, the velocity at the bottom point $\left(A\right)$ of the circular path is ( $g$ = gravitational acceleration) [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Set $T\;=\;0$ in the radial equation at the given point, then conserve energy from the bottom. // 📝 Solution: $mg\sin 30^\circ\;=\;\frac{mV^2}{r}\implies V^2\;=\;\frac{gr}{2}\implies\frac{1}{2}u^2\;=\;g\left(1.5r\right)\;+\;\frac{V^2}{2}\implies u^2\;=\;3gr\;+\;\frac{gr}{2}\;=\;\frac{7gr}{2}$
questions.topic: Vertical Circular Motion with Zero Tension

questions.text: The de-Broglie wavelength of an electron is the same as that of a photon. If velocity of electron is $25\%$ of the velocity of light, then the ratio of K.E. of electron and K.E. of photon will be:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Write $\lambda_e\;=\;\frac{h}{mv}\;=\;\frac{hv}{2K_e}$ and $\lambda_p\;=\;\frac{hc}{E_p}$, then equate them. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{hv}{2K_e}\;=\;\frac{hc}{E_p}\implies\frac{K_e}{E_p}\;=\;\frac{v}{2c}\;=\;\frac{0.25}{2}\;=\;\frac{1}{8}$

questions.text: The bob of a pendulum was released from a horizontal position. The length of the pendulum is $10\;\text{m}$. If it dissipates $10\%$ of its initial energy against air resistance, the speed with which the bob arrives at the lowest point is : [Use, $g\;:\;10\;\text{ms}^{-2}$]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Only $90\%$ of the initial potential energy $mg\ell$ is converted to kinetic energy. // 📝 Solution: $\frac{1}{2}mv^2\;=\;0.9\,mg\ell\implies v^2\;=\;1.8\times 10\times 10\;=\;180\implies v\;=\;6\sqrt{5}\;\text{m/s}$

questions.text: A body of mass $2\;\text{kg}$ is moving along $x$-direction such that its displacement as function of time is given by $x\left(t\right)\;=\;\alpha t^2\;+\;\beta t\;+\;\gamma\;\text{m}$, where $\alpha\;=\;1\;\text{m/s}^2\;,\;\beta\;=\;1\;\text{m/s}$ and $\gamma\;=\;1\;\text{m}$. The work done on the body during the time interval $t\;=\;2\;\text{s}$ to $t\;=\;3\;\text{s}$, is ____ J.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find the velocity by differentiating $x\left(t\right)$ and apply the work-energy theorem. // 📝 Solution: $v\;=\;2t\;+\;1\implies v_i\;=\;5\;,\;v_f\;=\;7\implies W\;=\;\frac{1}{2}\left(2\right)\left(49\;-\;25\right)\;=\;24\;\text{J}$

questions.text: A bob of mass $m$ is suspended by a light string of length $L$. It is imparted a minimum horizontal velocity at the lowest point A such that it just completes half circle reaching the top most position B. The ratio of kinetic energies $\frac{\left(\text{K.E.}\right)_A}{\left(\text{K.E.}\right)_B}$ is : [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For a string, the minimum speed at the top is $\sqrt{gL}$ and energy is conserved from A to B. // 📝 Solution: $v_B\;=\;\sqrt{gL}\;,\;\frac{1}{2}mv_A^2\;=\;\frac{1}{2}mv_B^2\;+\;mg\left(2L\right)\implies v_A\;=\;\sqrt{5gL}\implies\frac{K_A}{K_B}\;=\;\frac{5gL}{gL}\;=\;\frac{5}{1}$

questions.text: A block is fastened to a horizontal spring. The block is pulled to a distance $x\;=\;10\;\text{cm}$ from its equilibrium position (at $x\;=\;0$) on a frictionless surface from rest. The energy of the block at $x\;=\;5\;\text{cm}$ is $0.25\;\text{J}$. The spring constant of the spring is ____ $\text{Nm}^{-1}$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Total mechanical energy is conserved and equals $\frac{1}{2}kA^2$ at the extreme position. // 📝 Solution: $E\;=\;\frac{1}{2}kA^2\;=\;0.25\implies\frac{1}{2}k\left(0.1\right)^2\;=\;0.25\implies k\;=\;50\;\text{N/m}$
questions.topic: Spring Potential Energy and Energy Conservation

questions.text: A bullet of mass $50\;\text{g}$ is fired with a speed $100\;\text{m/s}$ on a plywood and emerges with $40\;\text{m/s}$. The percentage loss of kinetic energy is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Percentage loss is $\frac{K_i\;-\;K_f}{K_i}\times 100$ and the mass cancels. // 📝 Solution: $\%\text{ loss}\;=\;\frac{\frac{1}{2}m\left(100\right)^2\;-\;\frac{1}{2}m\left(40\right)^2}{\frac{1}{2}m\left(100\right)^2}\times 100\;=\;\frac{10000\;-\;1600}{10000}\times 100\;=\;84\%$

questions.text: A block of mass $100\;\text{kg}$ slides over a distance of $10\;\text{m}$ on a horizontal surface. If the co-efficient of friction between the surfaces is $0.4$, then the work done against friction (in $J$) is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Work against friction is $W\;=\;\mu mg\,s$. // 📝 Solution: $f\;=\;\mu mg\;=\;0.4\times 100\times 10\;=\;400\;\text{N}\implies W\;=\;f\,s\;=\;400\times 10\;=\;4000\;\text{J}$

questions.text: A ball is projected at an angle $60^\circ$ with the horizontal with kinetic energy $K$. The kinetic energy of the ball at the highest point of its path is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Only the horizontal component of velocity survives at the top. // 📝 Solution: $v_{top} \; = \; u\cos 60^\circ \; = \; \dfrac{u}{2} \implies KE_{top} \; = \; \dfrac{1}{2}m\left( \dfrac{u}{2} \right)^2 \; = \; \dfrac{K}{4}$

questions.text: A body of mass $2\;\text{kg}$ begins to move under the action of a time dependent force given by $\vec{F}\;=\;\left(6t\,\hat{i}\;+\;6t^2\,\hat{j}\right)\;\text{N}$. The power developed by the force at the time $t$ is given by:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Integrate acceleration to get velocity, then use $P\;=\;\vec{F}\cdot\vec{v}$. // 📝 Solution: $\vec{a}\;=\;3t\,\hat{i}\;+\;3t^2\,\hat{j}\implies\vec{v}\;=\;\frac{3t^2}{2}\hat{i}\;+\;t^3\hat{j}\implies P\;=\;\vec{F}\cdot\vec{v}\;=\;9t^3\;+\;6t^5$

questions.text: A particle is placed at the point $A$ of a frictionless track $ABC$ as shown in figure. It is gently pushed toward right. The speed of the particle when it reaches the point $B$ is : ( Take $g\;=\;10\;\text{m/s}^2$ ). [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Conserve mechanical energy between A and B using the height difference. // 📝 Solution: $mg\left(1\right)\;=\;\frac{1}{2}mv^2\;+\;mg\left(0.5\right)\implies v^2\;=\;g\;=\;10\implies v\;=\;\sqrt{10}\;\text{m/s}$

questions.text: A body of $m$ kg slides from rest along the curve of vertical circle from point $A$ to $B$ in friction less path. The velocity of the body at $B$ is: [FIGURE] (given, $R\;=\;14\;\text{m}\;,\;g\;=\;10\;\text{m/s}^2$ and $\sqrt{2}\;=\;1.4$)
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Apply the work-energy theorem from $A$ to $B$ using the vertical height dropped. // 📝 Solution: $h\;=\;\frac{R}{\sqrt{2}}\;+\;R\implies mg\left(\frac{R}{\sqrt{2}}\;+\;R\right)\;=\;\frac{1}{2}mv_B^2\implies v_B\;=\;\sqrt{\frac{2gR\left(\sqrt{2}\;+\;1\right)}{\sqrt{2}}}\;=\;\sqrt{\frac{10\times 14\times 2\times 2.4}{1.4}}\;\approx\;21.9\;\text{m/s}$

questions.text: A body falls freely from rest from a height $h$. When it has fallen through a distance $\dfrac{h}{4}$, the ratio of its kinetic energy to its potential energy (measured from the ground) is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Kinetic energy gained equals the loss in potential energy. // 📝 Solution: $KE \; = \; mg\dfrac{h}{4}, \; PE \; = \; mg\left( h \; - \; \dfrac{h}{4} \right) \; = \; \dfrac{3mgh}{4} \implies \dfrac{KE}{PE} \; = \; \dfrac{1}{3}$

questions.text: A circular table is rotating with an angular velocity of $\omega\;\text{rad/s}$ about its axis (see figure). There is a smooth groove along a radial direction on the table. A steel ball is gently placed at a distance of $1\;\text{m}$ on the groove. All the surfaces are smooth. If the radius of the table is $3\;\text{m}$, the radial velocity of the ball w.r.t. the table at the time ball leaves the table is $x\sqrt{2}\,\omega\;\text{m/s}$, where the value of $x$ is _____. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: In the rotating frame, the radial acceleration is $\omega^2 x$, so use $v\,dv\;=\;\omega^2x\,dx$. // 📝 Solution: $\int_0^v v\,dv\;=\;\int_1^3\omega^2x\,dx\implies\frac{v^2}{2}\;=\;\frac{\omega^2}{2}\left[9\;-\;1\right]\implies v\;=\;2\sqrt{2}\,\omega\implies x\;=\;2$

questions.text: An artillery piece of mass $M_1$ fires a shell of mass $M_2$ horizontally. Instantaneously after the firing, the ratio of kinetic energy of the artillery and that of the shell is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Momenta are equal in magnitude, and $K\;=\;\frac{p^2}{2m}$. // 📝 Solution: $K\;\propto\;\frac{1}{m}\implies\frac{K_1}{K_2}\;=\;\frac{p^2/2M_1}{p^2/2M_2}\;=\;\frac{M_2}{M_1}$

questions.text: Identify the correct statements from the following: (A) Work done by a man in lifting a bucket out of a well by means of a rope tied to the bucket is negative. (B) Work done by gravitational force in lifting a bucket out of a well by a rope tied to the bucket is negative. (C) Work done by friction on a body sliding down an inclined plane is positive. (D) Work done by an applied force on a body moving on a rough horizontal plane with uniform velocity is zero. (E) Work done by the air resistance on an oscillating pendulum in negative. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The sign of work depends on the angle between force and displacement. // 📝 Solution: Man's work is positive so A is false $\implies$ gravity opposes upward motion so B is true $\implies$ friction opposes sliding so C is false $\implies$ applied force balances friction so D is false $\implies$ air resistance opposes motion so E is true $\implies$ B and E only

questions.text: An object of mass $m$ initially at rest on a smooth horizontal plane starts moving under the action of force $F\;=\;2\;\text{N}$. In the process of its linear motion, the angle $\theta$ (as shown in figure) between the direction of force and horizontal varies as $\theta\;=\;kx$, where $k$ is a constant and $x$ is the distance covered by the object from its initial position. The expression of kinetic energy of the object will be $E\;=\;\frac{n}{k}\sin\theta$. The value of $n$ is ___. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use the work-energy theorem with $W\;=\;\int F\cos\theta\,dx$. // 📝 Solution: $K\;=\;\int_0^x 2\cos\left(kx\right)dx\;=\;\frac{2}{k}\sin\left(kx\right)\;=\;\frac{2}{k}\sin\theta\implies n\;=\;2$
questions.topic: Work Done by Variable Direction Force

questions.text: Potential energy $\left(V\right)$ versus distance $\left(x\right)$ is given by the graph. Rank various regions as per the magnitudes of the force (F) acting on a particle from high to low. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: The force magnitude equals the magnitude of the slope of the $V$-$x$ graph, $\left\lvert F\right\rvert\;=\;\left\lvert\frac{dV}{dx}\right\rvert$. // 📝 Solution: $\left\lvert F_{AB}\right\rvert\;=\;2\;,\;\left\lvert F_{BC}\right\rvert\;=\;6\;,\;\left\lvert F_{CD}\right\rvert\;=\;0\;,\;\left\lvert F_{DE}\right\rvert\;=\;1\implies F_{BC}\;>\;F_{AB}\;>\;F_{DE}\;>\;F_{CD}$

questions.text: A stationary particle breaks into two parts of masses $m_A$ and $m_B$ which move with velocities $v_A$ and $v_B$ respectively. The ratio of their kinetic energies $\left(K_B\;:\;K_A\right)$ is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Initial momentum is zero, so the two fragments have equal and opposite momenta. // 📝 Solution: $m_Av_A\;=\;m_Bv_B\implies\frac{K_B}{K_A}\;=\;\frac{\frac{1}{2}m_Bv_B^2}{\frac{1}{2}m_Av_A^2}\;=\;\frac{\left(m_Bv_B\right)v_B}{\left(m_Av_A\right)v_A}\;=\;\frac{v_B}{v_A}$

questions.text: A body of mass $1\;\text{kg}$ begins to move under the action of a time dependent force $\vec{F}\;=\;\left(t\,\hat{i}\;+\;3t^2\,\hat{j}\right)\;\text{N}$, where $\hat{i}$ and $\hat{j}$ are the unit vectors along $x$ and $y$ axis. The power developed by above force, at the time $t\;=\;2\;\text{s}$, will be ____ W.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Integrate $\vec{F}\;=\;m\frac{d\vec{v}}{dt}$ to get $\vec{v}$, then use $P\;=\;\vec{F}\cdot\vec{v}$. // 📝 Solution: $\vec{v}\;=\;\frac{t^2}{2}\hat{i}\;+\;t^3\hat{j}\implies P\;=\;\frac{t^3}{2}\;+\;3t^5\implies P\left(2\right)\;=\;4\;+\;96\;=\;100\;\text{W}$

questions.text: A body of mass $50\;\text{kg}$ is lifted to a height of $20\;\text{m}$ from the ground in the two different ways as shown in the figures. [FIGURE] The ratio of work done against the gravity in both the respective cases, will be :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Gravity is a conservative force, so its work depends only on the vertical displacement. // 📝 Solution: $W_g\;=\;mgh\;$ in both cases (same $m$ and same $h$) $\implies W_1\;:\;W_2\;=\;1\;:\;1$
questions.topic: Conservative Forces and Work Done by Gravity

questions.text: A bob of mass $m$ is suspended by a light string of length $L$. It is given the minimum horizontal velocity at the lowest point $A$ so that it just completes the vertical circle and reaches the top point $B$. The ratio of kinetic energies $\dfrac{KE_A}{KE_B}$ is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: At the top, the minimum condition is $mg \; = \; \dfrac{mv_B^2}{L}$, then use energy conservation. // 📝 Solution: $v_B^2 \; = \; gL, \; v_A^2 \; = \; v_B^2 \; + \; 4gL \; = \; 5gL \implies \dfrac{KE_A}{KE_B} \; = \; \dfrac{v_A^2}{v_B^2} \; = \; 5:1$
questions.topic: Vertical circular motion and energy conservation

questions.text: A block of mass $2\;\text{kg}$ is projected with speed $10\;\text{m/s}$ on a rough horizontal surface with $\mu \; = \; 0.2$. The distance covered before it stops is $\left( g \; = \; 10\;\text{m/s}^2 \right)$
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Work done by friction equals the loss of kinetic energy. // 📝 Solution: $\mu mg\,d \; = \; \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 \implies d \; = \; \dfrac{v^2}{2\mu g} \; = \; \dfrac{100}{2\left( 0.2 \right)\left( 10 \right)} \; = \; 25\;\text{m}$

questions.text: If the kinetic energy of a particle is doubled, its momentum becomes
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Use $p \; = \; \sqrt{2mK}$. // 📝 Solution: $p \; \propto \; \sqrt{K} \implies \dfrac{p'}{p} \; = \; \sqrt{\dfrac{2K}{K}} \; = \; \sqrt{2}$
questions.topic: Relation between momentum and kinetic energy

questions.text: A force $F \; = \; \left( 2x \; + \; 3 \right)\;\text{N}$ acts on a particle along the $x$-axis. The work done by the force in moving the particle from $x \; = \; 0$ to $x \; = \; 4\;\text{m}$ is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Work done by a variable force is $\int F\,dx$. // 📝 Solution: $W \; = \; \int_0^4 \left( 2x \; + \; 3 \right)dx \; = \; \left[ x^2 \; + \; 3x \right]_0^4 \; = \; 16 \; + \; 12 \; = \; 28\;\text{J}$
questions.topic: Work done by a variable force

questions.text: The work done in stretching a spring of force constant $400\;\text{N/m}$ from an extension of $5\;\text{cm}$ to $10\;\text{cm}$ is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Work done equals the change in elastic potential energy $\dfrac{1}{2}kx^2$. // 📝 Solution: $W \; = \; \dfrac{1}{2}k\left( x_2^2 \; - \; x_1^2 \right) \; = \; \dfrac{1}{2}\left( 400 \right)\left( 0.01 \; - \; 0.0025 \right) \; = \; 1.5\;\text{J}$
questions.topic: Elastic potential energy of a spring

questions.text: A bead $P$ sliding on a frictionless semi-circular string $\left(ACB\right)$ and it is at point $S$ at $t\;=\;0$ and at this instant the horizontal component of its velocity is $v$. Another bead $Q$ of the same mass as $P$ is ejected from point $A$ at $t\;=\;0$ along the horizontal string $AB$, with the speed $v$, friction between the beads and the respective strings may be neglected in both cases. Let $t_P$ and $t_Q$ be the respective times taken by beads $P$ and $Q$ to reach the point $B$, then the relation between $t_P$ and $t_Q$ is [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Compare the horizontal distances covered, since the horizontal velocity component is the same. // 📝 Solution: $t_P\;=\;\frac{x_P}{v}\;,\;t_Q\;=\;\frac{x_Q}{v}\;,\;x_Q\;>\;x_P\implies t_Q\;>\;t_P$

questions.text: The potential energy function (in $J$) of a particle in a region of space is given as $U\;=\;\left(2x^2\;+\;3y^3\;+\;2z\right)$. Here $x,\;y$ and $z$ are in meter. The magnitude of $x$ - component of force (in $N$) acting on the particle at point $P\left(1,\;2,\;3\right)\text{m}$ is :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Force is the negative gradient of potential energy, $F_x\;=\;-\frac{\partial U}{\partial x}$. // 📝 Solution: $F_x\;=\;-\frac{\partial U}{\partial x}\;=\;-4x\implies\left\lvert F_x\right\rvert_{x=1}\;=\;4\;\text{N}$

questions.text: A small particle moves to position $5\hat{i}\;-\;2\hat{j}\;+\;\hat{k}$ from its initial position $2\hat{i}\;+\;3\hat{j}\;-\;4\hat{k}$ under the action of force $5\hat{i}\;+\;2\hat{j}\;+\;7\hat{k}\;\text{N}$. The value of work done will be ____ J.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: For a constant force, $W\;=\;\vec{F}\cdot\left(\vec{r}_f\;-\;\vec{r}_i\right)$. // 📝 Solution: $\Delta\vec{r}\;=\;3\hat{i}\;-\;5\hat{j}\;+\;5\hat{k}\implies W\;=\;15\;-\;10\;+\;35\;=\;40\;\text{J}$

questions.text: A force $F\;=\;\left(5\;+\;3y^2\right)$ acts on a particle in the $y$-direction, where $F$ is newton and $y$ is in meter. The work done by the force during a displacement from $y\;=\;2\;\text{m}$ to $y\;=\;5\;\text{m}$ is ______ J.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Work by a variable force is $W\;=\;\int F\,dy$. // 📝 Solution: $W\;=\;\int_2^5\left(5\;+\;3y^2\right)dy\;=\;\left[5y\;+\;y^3\right]_2^5\;=\;150\;-\;18\;=\;132\;\text{J}$

questions.text: A force $\vec{F}\;=\;2\hat{i}\;+\;b\hat{j}\;+\;\hat{k}$ is applied on a particle and it undergoes a displacement $\hat{i}\;-\;2\hat{j}\;-\;\hat{k}$. What will be the value of $b$, if work done on the particle is zero.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Work $W\;=\;\vec{F}\cdot\vec{S}$. // 📝 Solution: $W\;=\;0\;\implies\;2\;-\;2b\;-\;1\;=\;0\;\implies\;b\;=\;\frac{1}{2}$

questions.text: A force $\left(3x^2\;+\;2x\;-\;5\right)\;\text{N}$ displaces a body from $x\;=\;2\;\text{m}$ to $x\;=\;4\;\text{m}$. Work done by this force is ________ $J$.
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Work done by a variable force is $W\;=\;\int F\,dx$. // 📝 Solution: $W\;=\;\int_2^4\left(3x^2\;+\;2x\;-\;5\right)dx\;=\;\left[x^3\;+\;x^2\;-\;5x\right]_2^4\implies W\;=\;60\;-\;2\;=\;58\;\text{J}$

questions.text: A force $\vec{f}\;=\;x^2y\,\hat{i}\;+\;y^2\hat{j}$ acts on a particle in a plane $x\;+\;y\;=\;10$. The work done by this force during a displacement from $\left(0,\,0\right)$ to $\left(4\;\text{m},\,2\;\text{m}\right)$ is ________ Joule (round off to the nearest integer)
A car of mass $1000\;\text{kg}$ accelerates uniformly from rest to $20\;\text{m/s}$ in $5\;\text{s}$. The average power delivered by the engine is
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Average power is work done (change in KE) divided by time. // 📝 Solution: $W \; = \; \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 \; = \; \dfrac{1}{2}\left( 1000 \right)\left( 400 \right) \; = \; 2\times 10^5\;\text{J} \implies P_{avg} \; = \; \dfrac{2\times 10^5}{5} \; = \; 40\;\text{kW}$

questions.text: If a rubber ball falls from a height $h$ and rebounds upto the height of $\frac{h}{2}$. The percentage loss of total energy of the initial system as well as velocity ball before it strikes the ground, respectively, are :
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Free-fall speed is $\sqrt{2gh}$ and energy lost is the difference of potential energies before and after the bounce. // 📝 Solution: $v\;=\;\sqrt{2gh}\;,\;\Delta E\;=\;mgh\;-\;mg\frac{h}{2}\;=\;\frac{mgh}{2}\implies\%\text{ loss}\;=\;\frac{mgh/2}{mgh}\times 100\;=\;50\%$

questions.text: A $0.4\;\text{kg}$ mass takes $8\;\text{s}$ to reach ground when dropped from a certain height $P$ above surface of earth. The loss of potential energy in the last second of fall is ____ J. [Take $g\;=\;10\;\text{m/s}^2$]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: Find the distance fallen in the $8^{th}$ second, then use $\Delta U\;=\;mgh$. // 📝 Solution: $S_8\;=\;\frac{1}{2}\times 10\times\left(2\times 8\;-\;1\right)\;=\;75\;\text{m}\implies\Delta U\;=\;0.4\times 10\times 75\;=\;300\;\text{J}$

questions.text: A force $F\;=\;\alpha\;+\;\beta x^2$ acts on an object in the $x$-direction. The work done by the force is $5\;\text{J}$ when the object is displaced by $1\;\text{m}$. If the constant $\alpha\;=\;1\;\text{N}$ then $\beta$ will be
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: $W\;=\;\int_0^1 F\,dx$. // 📝 Solution: $W\;=\;\int_0^1\left(\alpha\;+\;\beta x^2\right)dx\;=\;\alpha\;+\;\frac{\beta}{3}\;=\;5\;\implies\;\frac{\beta}{3}\;=\;4\;\implies\;\beta\;=\;12\;\text{N/m}^2$

questions.text: A small bob $A$ of mass $m$ is attached to a massless rigid rod of length $1\;\text{m}$ pivoted at point $P$ and kept at an angle of $60^\circ$ with vertical as shown in figure. At distance of $1\;\text{m}$ below point $P$, an identical bob $B$ is kept at rest on a smooth horizontal surface that extends to a circular track of radius $R$ as shown in figure. If bob $B$ just manages to complete the circular path of radius $R$ upto a point $Q$ after being hit elastically by bob $A$, then radius $R$ is ____ m. [FIGURE]
questions.solution: 💡 Hint: An elastic collision between equal masses exchanges velocities, and a loop needs $v^2\;=\;5gR$ at the bottom. // 📝 Solution: $h\;=\;1\left(1\;-\;\cos 60^\circ\right)\;=\;0.5\implies v_A\;=\;\sqrt{2gh}\;=\;\sqrt{10}\;=\;v_B\implies 10\;=\;5\times 10\times R\implies R\;=\;\frac{1}{5}\;\text{m}$
